2. Check whether the rock-drill-specific **SLU air valve** on the carrier receives control (is the LED on the valve cover lit?) [2, 5].
3. If the valve receives a control signal, measure the air pressure going to the pressure switch that monitors the shank lubrication [1, 2]. The pressure switch should be triggered at **2.8 bar** and inform the monitoring system that the air pressure is sufficient [1, 2].
4. If the air valve is working properly and the air pressure at the switch is sufficient (at or above 2.8 bar), the fault is either in the air pressure switch or in the SLU pump unit – i.e., in the oil flow [1, 6].

questions.question: When adjusting the boom circuit max LS pressure to its target of 230 bar at an engine speed of 1800 rpm, what specific pressure reducing/relieving valve must first be temporarily adjusted to 250 bar while monitoring measuring point M10?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the boom circuit max. LS pressure to its target of 230 bar at an engine speed of 1800 rpm, the **pressure reducing/relieving valve (210)** at the drilling control block must first be temporarily adjusted to 250 bar [1-3]. 

According to Section 4.5.1, "Adjusting boom circuit max. LS pressure" in the *SB20/SB20NV/SB40/SB40NV Booms* manual (Pages 41-42), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1-15]:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure relief valve for the max. LS-pressure.
2. Install a pressure gauge to the measuring point **M10** of the drilling control block.
3. Start the powerpack.
4. Run the boom zoom inwards or outwards (whichever is safest) and hold against the stopper to raise maximum pressure. 
5. Adjust the boom circuit max. pressure to **250 bar** with the **pressure reducing/relieving valve (210)** at the drilling control block. Read the pressure value in the gauge connected to the measuring point **M10**.
6. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the **pressure reducing/relieving valve (210)**.
7. Stop the powerpack.
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the max. LS-pressure pressure relief valve almost fully open (counterclockwise).
9. Start the carrier engine (diesel). *(Note: Check if the carrier's hydraulic circuit has a pressure relief valve restricting this adjustment. If so, temporarily adjust it approx. 10 bar higher than the boom circuit max. LS-pressure setting).*
10. Run the zoom cylinder inwards with the engine speed at **1800 rpm** and adjust at the same time the boom circuit max. LS pressure to **230 bar**, by turning the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure pressure relief valve clockwise. Read the pressure in the pressure gauge installed to the measuring point **M10** of the drilling control block.
11. Stop the diesel engine and lock the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure pressure relief valve.
12. Start the powerpack.
13. Run the boom control operating valve for zoom or feed transfer.
14. Adjust the boom circuit max. pressure back to **230 bar** with the **pressure reducing/relieving valve (210)**. Read the pressure value in the gauge connected to the measuring point **M10**.
15. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the **pressure reducing/relieving valve (210)**.
16. Stop the powerpack.
17. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **M10** of the drilling control block.

questions.question: What specific pressure value should be read on the rotation pressure gauge (51) when adjusting the maximum pressure of the rotation circuit using the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65)?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the maximum pressure of the rotation circuit using the **rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65)**, you should read a specific pressure value of **180 bar** on the **rotation pressure gauge (51)** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 5.1.4 ("Adjusting the max. pressure of rotation circuit") in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Page 91/138 of the standard manual and Page 98/144 of the constant feed speed manual), the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows [1-7]:

1. Start the power pack [3, 5].
2. Run the rock drill against the rear stopper [3, 5].
3. Stop the power pack [3, 5].
4. Loosen the locking nut of the **pressure relief valve (65)** mounted to the rotation control valve [1-3, 5].
5. Turn the **pressure relief valve (65)** adjusting screw almost fully open (counterclockwise) [1, 2].
6. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the hose support and plug the hose ends [1, 2].
7. Turn the **rotation speed regulating valve (59)** closed (clockwise) [1, 2].
8. Start the power pack [1, 2].
9. Lock the control lever of the **rotation pilot control valve (58)** in the back position [1, 2].
10. Adjust the rotation max. pressure to **180 bar** with the **pressure relief valve (65)**. Read the pressure in the **rotation pressure gauge (51)** [1, 2].
11. Lock the adjusting screw of the max. **rotation pressure relief valve (65)** [1, 6].
12. Release the control lever of the **rotation pilot control valve (58)** to the middle position [4, 6].
13. Stop the power pack [4, 6].
14. Reconnect the rotation hose to the hose support [4, 6].
15. Start the power pack [4, 6].
16. Turn drilling rotation on again by locking the control lever of the **rotation pilot control valve (58)** in the back position [4, 6].
17. Adjust the drill steel rotation speed to the desired value by turning the **rotation speed regulating valve (59)** counterclockwise [4, 6, 7].
18. Release the control lever of the **rotation pilot control valve (58)** to the middle position [7, 8].
19. Stop the power pack [7, 8].

questions.question: To adjust the minimum percussion pressure to 120 bar as read on gauge (11), what specific valve must be adjusted by turning its screw fully open counterclockwise and then closing it by exactly 3½ turns?
questions.answer:
To adjust the minimum percussion pressure to 120 bar as read on the percussion pressure gauge (11), you must adjust the **monitoring valve (18)** [1-3]. 

According to Section 5.1.7 ("Adjusting min. percussion pressure") in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Page 97/138 of the standard manual and Page 104/144 of the constant feed speed manual), the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the half-power pressure relief valve (6) [4, 5].
2. Turn the adjusting screw of the half-power pressure relief valve (6) almost fully closed (clockwise) [4, 5].
3. Loosen the locking nuts of the monitoring valve (18) [4, 5].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the monitoring valve (18) fully open (counterclockwise) and then close it by 3½ turns [4, 5].
5. Start the powerpack [4, 5].
6. Turn percussion half-power on by locking the control lever of the percussion pilot control valve (14) to the back position [2, 4, 5].
7. Adjust min. percussion pressure to 120 bar with the monitoring valve (18) [2, 6]. Read the pressure value from the percussion pressure gauge (11) [2, 6].
8. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw for the monitoring valve (18) [2, 6].
9. Adjust the percussion half-power pressure relief valve (6) according to the chapter "Adjusting percussion half-power" [2, 6].
10. Release the control lever of the percussion pilot control valve (14) [6, 7].
11. Stop the powerpack [6, 7].

questions.question: If the rig is equipped with a TFX 500 feed, what specific pressure value must the fast feed max pressure relief valve (30) be adjusted to while reading the feed pressure gauge (21)?
questions.answer:
If the rig is equipped with a TFX 500 feed, the fast feed max. pressure relief valve **(30)** must be adjusted to exactly **180 bar**, as read from the feed pressure gauge **(21)** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 5.1.11, "Adjusting fast feed max. pressure" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Page 103 of the standard manual and Pages 108–109 of the constant feed speed manual), the complete step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows [3, 4]:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the fast feed max. pressure relief valve **(30)** [3, 4].
2. Start the powerpack [3, 4].
3. Run the rock drill against the rear stopper by locking the control lever of the fast feed pilot control valve **(33)** into the front position and adjust at the same time the fast feed max. pressure to **180 bar** using the pressure relief valve **(30)** [1-4]. Read the pressure value from the feed pressure gauge **(21)** [1, 4]. 
4. Release the control lever of the fast feed pilot control valve **(33)** [1, 2].
5. Lock the adjusting screw of the fast feed max. pressure relief valve **(30)** [1, 2].
6. Stop the powerpack [1, 2].

questions.question: According to the accumulator filling pressure specifications for the RD520 and RD525 rock drills, what is the required nitrogen gas pre-charge pressure for the stabilizer accumulator?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, the required nitrogen (N2) gas pre-charge pressure for the **stabilizer accumulator (9)** on the RD520 and RD525 rock drills is exactly **30 bar** [1-3]. 

According to Section 4.1.1 ("Preparations") in the *RD520/RD525 Rock drill operation, maintenance and repair manual* and Section 3.8.2 ("Filling pressures of accumulators") in the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions*, this pressure must be set correctly prior to taking the rock drill into use [2-4].

If the accumulator needs to be filled, Section 3.8.1 ("Filling instruction") outlines the following step-by-step sequence. **Note:** You must strictly use nitrogen (N2) gas, as using any other type of gas creates an explosion hazard [5, 6]:

1. Remove the **cap (4)** from the accumulator [7].
2. Screw the **elbow adapter (15)** to the **filling valve (2)** [7].
3. Push the **quick coupling sleeve (6)** onto the **stem (5)** [7].
4. Undo the **locking nut (3)** [7].
5. Turn the **pressure regulating valve (11)** open [7].
6. Open the **nitrogen bottle valve (12)**. The **gas bottle pressure gauge (9)** will indicate the pressure in the bottle [7].
7. Adjust the pressure of the stabilizer accumulator with the **pressure regulating valve (11)** to the target of **30 bar** [2, 8]. The **accumulator pressure gauge (8)** indicates the pressure inside the accumulator [8]. 
8. Close the **filling valve (2)** by turning the **locking nut (3)** [8].
9. Close the **nitrogen bottle valve (12)** [8].
10. Turn the **pressure regulating valve (11)** open [8].
11. Disconnect the **quick coupling stem (5)** and **quick coupling sleeve (6)** [8].
12. Release the **elbow adapter (15)** from the **filling valve (2)** [8].
13. Tighten the **locking nut (3)** to a torque of **15 Nm** [9].
14. Refit the **cap (4)** [9].

questions.question: If the flow controller (A) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) deviates from the 22-30 bar set value and measuring points M1 and M2 on the anti-jamming and return automatics control block receive pressure simultaneously, which specific pilot control valve is likely sticking?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, if the flow controller **(A)** of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** deviates from the **22-30 bar** set value and measuring points **M1** and **M2** on the anti-jamming and return automatics control block receive pressure simultaneously, it is likely that the **feed pilot control valve (31)** is sticking [1, 2]. 

According to Section 6.3.1, "Flow controller (A) value deviates from the set value 22-30 bar" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Pages 116–117 of the standard manual and Pages 122–123 of the constant feed speed DD321 manual), the step-by-step sequence to inspect this issue is as follows:

1. Start the power pack [3].
2. Install a pressure gauge to the following measuring points alternately:
   * Measuring point **M9** of the feed and percussion control block [3]. 
   * Measuring points **M1**, **M2**, and **M3** of the anti-jamming and return automatics control block [3].
3. Check the pressure readings. If the measuring points **M1 and M2** (or M1 and M3) of the anti-jamming and return automatics control block receive pressure simultaneously, it indicates that the **feed pilot control valve (31)** is sticking [2].
4. Stop the power pack and replace the faulty valves [2].

questions.question: When testing the TFX feed cylinder intermediate piston seals on a test bench with the ball valve (3) closed, driving the piston rod completely in and applying a constant pressure of 250 bar will cause oil to leak from the hoses of which specific ports if the seals are damaged?
questions.answer:
When testing the TFX feed cylinder **(1)** on a test bench with a constant pressure of **250 bar**, damaged intermediate piston seals will cause oil to leak from specific ports depending on which exact test configuration is being run. 

According to Section 7.1.6 ("Checking oil leaks from the TFX feed intermediate piston and piston seals" in the *Cylinder feed TF500 / TFX500* manuals, pages 40–45), there are two different test setups for the intermediate piston seals:

1. **Testing the intermediate piston and piston seals:** If oil comes out from **port B**, it indicates that one of the intermediate piston seals is damaged [1]. *(Note: If oil leaks from port A during this test, a piston seal is damaged)* [1]. 
2. **Testing the intermediate piston and rear cover seals:** If oil comes out from **port C**, it indicates that one of the intermediate piston seals is damaged [2]. If oil comes out from **port B** during this test, it indicates that some of the intermediate piston and piston seals are damaged [2].

**Step-by-step Test Sequence:**
For both test configurations, the procedure to apply the pressure and check for these leaks is as follows [2-6]:
1. Connect the TFX feed cylinder **(1)** to the test bench so that the mechanical attachments from the cylinder tube and stem end are left unattached [3, 5].
2. Open the ball valve **(3)** (500 bar) [3, 5].
3. Turn the adjusting spool of the pressure limit **(4)** (250 bar) to the minimum value (counterclockwise) [3, 5].
4. Start the powerpack pump **(2)** [4, 6].
5. Close the ball valve **(3)** [4, 6].
6. Drive the piston rod of the feed cylinder in by turning the pressure limit **(4)** adjusting screw clockwise until the piston rod is completely in and the pressure value on the pressure gauge **(5)** (400 bar) shows a constant pressure value of **250 bar** [4, 6]. *During this step, be careful with oil coming out of port A, B, or C (depending on the test).*
7. Keep the pressure on for **2-5 minutes** [4, 6].
8. Check if there is oil leaking past the seals from the hoses of the ports to identify the damaged seals [1, 2, 4, 6]. 
9. After the test, turn the adjusting spool of the pressure limit valve **(4)** to the minimum value (counterclockwise), open the ball valve **(3)**, and stop the powerpack **(2)** [1, 2, 5, 7].

questions.question: When adjusting the water pressure before the water pump (501) using the pressure reducing valve (506), what is the absolute maximum pressure value that must never be exceeded on the water pressure gauge (510.06)?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, when adjusting the water pressure before the water pump **(501)** using the pressure reducing valve **(506)**, the absolute maximum pressure value that must never be exceeded on the water pressure gauge **(510.06)** is **25 bar** [1, 2].

According to Section 4.1 ("Operation of the pressure reducing valve (506)") and Section 7.2.2 ("Adjusting water pressure") in the *Water circuit NC7/DT821/DT1131* manual, the step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Adjust the pressure using the adjusting knob **(A)** on the pressure reducing valve **(506)** while the water pump **(501)** is running [2].
2. Read the pressure value on the water pressure gauge **(510.06)** [1].
3. Increase the pressure by turning the adjusting knob clockwise, and decrease the pressure by turning it counterclockwise [2]. *(Note: The normal adjusting range of the pressure reducing valve (506) is 1...7 bar)* [1, 2].
4. Strictly ensure that the value read on the gauge must never exceed **25 bar** [2]. *(Note: The flushing pressure is the combined total of the inlet pressure plus the pump pressure)* [2].

questions.question: While troubleshooting low drilling feed pressure, if the pressure at measuring point M1 reads approximately 19-21 bar but the pressure at connection P3 reads a different value, which specific regulating valve must be replaced?
questions.answer:
If the pressure at measuring point M1 is approximately 19-21 bar but the pressure at connection P3 reads a different value during troubleshooting, the specific component that must be replaced is the **feed speed regulating valve (150)** [1].

According to Section 6.11 ("Drilling feed pressure too low") in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics, constant feed speed DD321* manual (Pages 131-132), this diagnosis is determined through the following step-by-step sequence:

1. Install a pressure gauge to measuring point **M1** of the anti-jamming and return automatics block, and install another pressure gauge to the connection **P3** of the feed speed regulating valve **(150)** [1]. 
2. Remove the drill rod [1].
3. Lock the control lever of the feed pilot control valve **(31)** into the rear position and turn the feed speed regulating valve **(150)** fully closed (clockwise) [1].
4. Check the pressure readings. If the pressure at the measuring point **M1** is approx. **19-21 bar** and the pressure at the connection **P3** reads something else, it indicates that the feed speed regulating valve **(150)** is faulty [1]. *(Note: If the M1 pressure is something other than 19-21 bar, it instead indicates a faulty feed pilot control valve (31) [1])*
5. Stop the powerpack [2].
6. Replace the faulty feed speed regulating valve **(150)** [2].

questions.question: To achieve optimum damping performance and prevent cavitation, what specific mathematical relationship must the low-pressure accumulator's pre-charge gas pressure have compared to the return line pressure?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, to achieve optimum performance from a low-pressure accumulator (LP) and prevent cavitation in the return lines and channels, the gas pre-charge pressure of the accumulator must be exactly **half of the return line pressure** [1-3]. 

Normally, a low-pressure accumulator is pressurized to a specific value of **2 - 4 bars** [1-3]. 

This specification is detailed in the "Filling pressures of accumulators -> Low pressure accumulator (LP)" section of the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions* (found on pages 22 and 25) [1-6]. The manuals emphasize that overfilling a low-pressure accumulator significantly increases the risk of cavitation, so ensuring the pressure matches this mathematical relationship is critical to avoiding damage to the rock drill [4-6].

questions.question: During the calibration of the anti-jamming pressure for an RD314 rock drill, what specific pressure value must the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) be adjusted to before verifying that measuring point M3 receives 19-21 bar of feed pilot control pressure from the anti-jamming valve (34)?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, during the calibration of the anti-jamming pressure for an RD314 rock drill, the **rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65)** must be adjusted to a specific pressure value of **140 bar** [1-4]. 

According to the "Adjusting anti-jamming pressure" procedure in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Section 5.1.5, Pages 93-94 in the standard manual and Pages 100-101 in the constant feed speed manual), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the **anti-jamming valve (34)** adjusting screw [5, 6].
2. Turn the **anti-jamming valve (34)** adjusting screw first fully closed (clockwise), and open it then 2 turns (counterclockwise) [5, 6].
3. Start the powerpack [5, 6].
4. Run the rock drill against the rear stopper [5, 6].
5. Stop the powerpack [5, 6].
6. Loosen the locking nut of **rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65)** of the rotation control block adjusting screw [5, 6].
7. Turn the **LS-pressure relief valve (65)** adjusting screw almost fully open (counterclockwise) [5, 6].
8. Turn the **rotation speed regulating valve (59)** closed (clockwise) [6, 7].
9. Plug the pressure side hose of the feed cylinder [6, 7].
10. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the hose support and plug the hose ends [7, 8].
11. Install a pressure gauge to the **measuring point M3** of the anti-jamming/return automatics block [7, 8].
12. Start the powerpack [7, 8].
13. Lock the control levers of **rotation and feed pilot control valves (58) and (31)** to the back position [7, 8].
14. Adjust the desired anti-jamming activation pressure with the **rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65)** by turning the adjusting screw clockwise to **140 bar** (the factory setting for the RD314). Read the pressure value in the **rotation pressure gauge (51)** [2, 4, 7, 8].
15. Adjust the **anti-jamming valve (34)** so that it directs feed pilot control pressure at the set pressure to the **measuring point M3** of the anti-jamming/return automatics block. Read the feed pilot control pressure (approx. **19-21 bar**) in the pressure gauge installed in the **measuring point M3** [2, 4].
16. When the **anti-jamming valve (34)** is correctly adjusted, lock the adjusting screw of the valve **(34)** [2, 4].

*(Note: After verifying this pressure, the operator must re-adjust the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) back to its normal operating pressure of 180 bar before resuming drilling [9, 10].)*

questions.question: When calibrating the anti-jamming valve (34) with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) set to the 120 bar factory setting, what specific feed pilot control pressure range must be verified at measuring point M3?
questions.answer:
When calibrating the anti-jamming valve **(34)** with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** set to the factory setting of **120 bar**, the specific feed pilot control pressure range that must be verified at measuring point **M3** is **19-21 bar** [1, 2].

According to Section 5.1.5, "Adjusting anti-jamming pressure" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Pages 92–95 of the standard manual and Pages 100–102 of the constant feed speed manual) [3-6], the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the anti-jamming valve **(34)** adjusting screw [7, 8].
2. Turn the anti-jamming valve **(34)** adjusting screw first fully closed (clockwise), and open it then 2 turns (counterclockwise) [7, 8].
3. Start the powerpack [7, 8].
4. Run the rock drill against the rear stopper [7, 8].
5. Stop the powerpack [7, 8].
6. Loosen the locking nut of rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** of the rotation control block adjusting screw [7, 8].
7. Turn the LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** adjusting screw almost fully open (counterclockwise) [7, 8].
8. Turn the rotation speed regulating valve **(59)** closed (clockwise) [8, 9].
9. Plug the pressure side hose of the feed cylinder [8, 9].
10. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the hose support and plug the hose ends [9, 10].
11. Install a pressure gauge to the measuring point **M3** of the anti-jamming/return automatics block [9, 10].
12. Start the powerpack [9, 10].
13. Lock the control levers of the rotation and feed pilot control valves **(58)** and **(31)** to the back position [9, 10].
14. Adjust the desired anti-jamming activation pressure with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** by turning the adjusting screw clockwise to the factory setting of **120 bar** (RD314: 140 bar). Read the pressure value in the rotation pressure gauge **(51)** [1, 2, 9, 10].
15. Adjust the anti-jamming valve **(34)** so that it directs feed pilot control pressure at the set pressure to the measuring point **M3** of the anti-jamming/return automatics block. Read the feed pilot control pressure (**approx. 19-21 bar**) in the pressure gauge installed in the measuring point **M3** [1, 2].
16. When the anti-jamming valve **(34)** is correctly adjusted, lock the adjusting screw of the valve **(34)** [1, 2].
17. Adjust the rotation pressure with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** to **180 bar** by turning the adjusting screw clockwise. Read the pressure in the rotation pressure gauge **(51)** [1, 11, 12].
18. Lock the adjusting screw of the rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** [11, 12].
19. Release the control levers of the rotation and feed pilot control valves **(58)** and **(31)** [11, 12].
20. Stop the powerpack [11, 12].
21. Remove the plugs from the disconnected rotation hoses and reconnect the hoses together [4, 11, 12].
22. Remove the plugs from the feed cylinder pressure side feed line and reconnect the hose to the feed cylinder [4, 6, 12].
23. Start the powerpack [4, 6].
24. Turn drilling rotation on again by locking the control lever of rotation pilot control valve **(58)** in the back position [4, 6].
25. Adjust the drill rod rotation speed to the desired value by turning the rotation speed regulating valve **(59)** counterclockwise [4, 6].
26. Release the control lever of the rotation pilot control valve **(58)** [4, 6].
27. Stop the powerpack [4, 6].
28. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **M3** for the anti-jamming/return automatics [4, 6, 13, 14].

questions.question: If the water pressure drops below 2.8 bar for more than one minute, triggering indicator H601 and stopping the water pump, what specific switch must the operator use to restart the pump after pressing the acknowledgement button (S505)?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, if the water pressure drops below **2.8 bar** for more than one minute, the pressure control system stops the drilling water pump and the "low water pressure" indicator light **(H601)** remains on [1, 2]. 

To restart the pump, the operator must use the water booster pump start/stop switch **(S501)** [1, 2].

According to the "Water pressure low (H601)" and "Pressure control functions" sections of the manuals (e.g., *Maintenance Manual DD321*, Page 150, and *DT821 Electric System*, Pages 31-32), the step-by-step sequence to restore operation is as follows:

1. The water pump is automatically stopped by the system, and indicator light **(H601)** is illuminated [1, 2].
2. The operator must press the pressure control reset/acknowledgement button **(S505)** [2]. This will turn off the indicator light and enable the system for a restart [1]. *(Note: Resetting the fault with S505 alone will not restart the pump, even if the power packs are on and the water pump switch is in the "automatic" position [1]).*
3. The operator must then restart the water pump by setting the water booster pump operation switch **(S501)** to the "start" position [1, 2].
4. After the water pump is successfully restarted, automatic drilling is enabled once again [1].

questions.question: If an operator chooses to perform collaring by locking the rotation (58), percussion (14), and feed (31) pilot control levers into the back position, what specific physical adjustment must first be made to the feed pressure regulating valve (20) to ensure drilling starts at half power?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, to ensure drilling starts at half power when performing collaring by locking the rotation, percussion, and feed control levers into the back position, you must first **turn the feed pressure regulating valve (20) fully open (counterclockwise)** [1].

According to Section 4.2.7, "Operation of the collaring" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manual (Page 48/138), the step-by-step sequence for this alternative collaring method is as follows:

1. Turn the **feed pressure regulating valve (20)** fully open (counterclockwise) [1].
2. Lock all three control levers—the **rotation pilot control valve (58)**, **percussion pilot control valve (14)**, and **feed pilot control valve (31)**—into the back position [1, 2]. 
3. Drilling will now start at half power [1]. 
4. Drilling continues at half power until the drilling values are returned to correspond to full-power drilling by turning the **feed pressure regulating valve (20)** [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (1) for a cable with a cross-sectional area of 35 mm², what is the specified maximum pressure P1 target in bar?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, when adjusting the cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve **(1)** for a cable with a cross-sectional area of **35 mm²**, the specified maximum pressure P1 target is **80 bar** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 3.1 ("Adjusting the cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (1)") in the *Basic adjustment of the cable reel and water hose reel* manual (Page 15), the step-by-step sequence to achieve this adjustment is as follows:

1. Start the diesel engine and let it idle [1].
2. Deactivate the directional valve **Y450 (8)** by disconnecting the coil from the cartridge or by disconnecting the connector from the coil [1].
3. Connect a pressure gauge to the cable reel measuring point **(5)** of the rear carrier control block [1].
4. Loosen the cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve **(1)** locking nut by turning it counterclockwise [1].
5. Activate the "reeling out the cable" function, which controls the coil **Y173a** in the rear carrier control block [1, 2].
6. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve **(1)** clockwise/counterclockwise to adjust the pressure to **80 bar**, as specified in the "Reeling the cable in" table for 35 mm² cables [2].
7. Stop the "reeling out the cable" function [2].
8. Lock the adjustment screw [2].
9. Activate the directional valve **Y450 (8)** by connecting the coil back to the cartridge or connecting the connector back to the coil [2].
10. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **(5)** [3].

*(Note: Depending on the specific reel control block version used, alternative instructions in Section 3 of the "Basic adjustment and max force control of reels" manual, pages 20–25, indicate you may instead connect the pressure gauge to measuring point **MB1** (Version A) or **MB** (Version B) while utilizing the same 80 bar target limit for a 35 mm² cable)* [4-7].

questions.question: During the calibration of the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15), what exact target pressure must be read at measuring connector MCR while the diesel engine is running at maximum rpm?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, during the calibration of the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve **(10.15)**, the exact target pressure that must be read at the measuring connector **MCR** while the diesel engine is running at maximum rpm is **160 bars** [1].

According to Section 4.7.8, "Adjusting brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15)" in the *Drill carrier C400, C900* manual (Pages 93–94), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Unplug the electrical connectors of the brake circuit retarder control valve **(10.16/Y344)** and the carrier functions pressurization control valve **(10.18/Y167)** [2].
2. Connect the electrical connector **Y167** to the solenoid of the brake circuit retarder control valve **(10.16)**, and leave the connector **Y344** unplugged [2].
3. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MCR** [2].
4. Loosen the locking nut of the valve **(10.15)** and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise fully open [2].
5. Start the diesel engine [2].
6. Run the boom zoom function backwards to activate electrical connector **Y167**. Run the function until the adjustment of the pressure relief valve **(10.15)** is locked [1, 2].
7. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm [1].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve **(10.15)** clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MCR** is **160 bars** [1].
9. Tighten the locking nut of the valve **(10.15)** [1].
10. Release the boom zoom function [1].
11. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle and shut down the engine after idling [1].
12. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **MCR** [3].
13. Unplug the electrical connector **Y167** from the valve **(10.16)** and return the electrical connectors back to their original positions (connector **Y344** to valve **10.16** and connector **Y167** to valve **10.18**) [3].

questions.question: According to the SM3 rotary actuator specifications, what is the maximum operating pressure in bar for the Ø215 series actuator compared to the Ø230 series?
questions.answer:
According to Chapter 1, "Technical Data," and Chapter 12, "Operating pressure," in the *User guide SM3 Boom* manuals, the maximum operating pressures for the two series of rotary actuators are as follows [1-4]:

*   **Ø215 series** (Specialtype-No. 21.910.16 and 21.910.20): The maximum operating pressure is **280 bar** (4,061 psi) [1-3]. 
*   **Ø230 series** (Specialtype-No. 21.281.09 and 21.281.10): The maximum operating pressure is **225 bar** (3,263 psi) [1, 2, 4].

questions.question: During the inward movement of the SB40 boom swing cylinder (4), which specific overcenter valve located in block (1) is opened by oil pressure to allow the return flow from the feed swing cylinder to join the boom swing cylinder's return line?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, there is a slight distinction to make regarding the boom models: for the **SB40 / SB40NV** booms, the specific overcenter valve opened by oil pressure is **(14.11)**, which is located in **block (14)**. *(Note: It is the SB20 / SB20NV booms that utilize overcenter valve **(1.09)** located in **block (1)** for this exact function).*

According to Section 4.2.6, "Boom swing function SB40, SB40NV -> Swing cylinder inward movement, automatic parallelism" (Page 32 in the *SB boom* manual), the step-by-step sequence for this hydraulic circuit is as follows [1-3]:

1. Oil flows from the carrier control valve port **(B5 / A8)** via the block **(1)** port **(A8)** to the pilot-controlled directional valve **(1.07)** [1].
2. From block **(1)** port **(L)**, the oil continues to the block **(14)** port **(L)** [1]. 
3. It flows onward through the directional valve **(.09)** and port **(L1)** located in the block **(14)**, and further on to the boom swing cylinder **(4)** port **(B)** and to its piston rod side [1]. 
4. Simultaneously, this oil pressure opens the overcenter valve **(.11)** located in the block **(14)** [1].
5. The capacity of the boom swing cylinder **(4)** third chamber decreases when the cylinder is run inward, causing oil to flow via the boom swing cylinder **(4)** port **(Y)** to the block **(14)** port **(B)** [2].
6. It continues through the block **(14)** port **(D1)** and onward from the feed swing cylinder **(5)** port **(B)** to the feed swing cylinder **(5)** rod side [2].
7. The return flow from the feed swing cylinder **(5)** piston side flows through the overcenter valve **(.02)** to the port **(A)** [3].
8. From there, it enters the boom block **(14)** port **(C1)**, continuing through the opened overcenter valve **(14.11)** to join the return line coming from the boom swing cylinder **(4)** piston side [3].
9. The combined return flow then continues through the boom block **(14)** port **(R)** to the block **(1)** port **(R)** [3].
10. Finally, it flows through the pilot-controlled directional valve **(1.05)** to the port **(B8)** and further on to the carrier control valve port **(A5 / B8)** and onward to the hydraulic oil tank [3].

questions.question: When adjusting the stabilizer maximum pressure switch (137), what specific pressure value must be read on the stabilizer pressure gauge (146) before opening the switch's adjusting screw until it disconnects?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the stabilizer maximum pressure switch (137), a specific pressure value of **130 bar** must be read on the stabilizer pressure gauge (146) before opening the switch's adjusting screw until it disconnects [1, 2]. 

According to Section 5.1.19, "Adjusting stabilizer max. pressure switch (137)" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Pages 108–109 of the standard manual and Pages 114–115 of the constant feed speed manual), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1-4]:

1. Turn the adjusting screw of the max. pressure switch **(137)** almost closed (clockwise) [1, 2].
2. Start the power pack [1, 2].
3. Run the feed cylinder against the front limit [1, 2].
4. Adjust the stabilizer pressure to **130 bar** with the pressure reducing/reliefing valve **(141)** [1, 2]. Read the pressure value in the stabilizer pressure gauge **(146)** [1, 2].
5. Open the adjusting screw of the max. pressure switch **(137)** until it is disconnected [1, 2].
6. Adjust the stabilizer max. pressure to the right value (**110 bar**), according to the chapter "Adjusting stabilizer max. pressure" [1, 5].

*(Note: The manuals specify that the adjusting value of the stabilizer max. pressure switch (137) must always be approximately 20 bar higher than the stabilizer max. operating pressure)* [5, 6].

questions.question: Which specific drilling module movement prevention valves are automatically activated whenever the diesel engine or powerpack is running to cut off feed pressure from the pilot-control valves and the boom pressure lines?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the specific drilling module movement prevention valves that are automatically activated whenever the diesel engine or powerpack is running are:

*   **Drilling module movement prevention valve (221)** for the pilot-control valve line, which cuts off the feed pressure from the pilot-control valves.
*   **Drilling module movement prevention valve (222)** for the boom line, which cuts off the boom pressure lines.

According to Section 4.2.11, "Operation of the drilling module movement prevention" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Pages 60–61/138 of the standard manual and Pages 62–63/144 of the constant feed speed manual), the operation is as follows [1, 2]:

1. Both valves **(221)** and **(222)** are activated whenever the diesel engine or powerpack is on, allowing oil to flow through them to the pilot control valves and the boom valves [1, 2]. 
2. When drilling module movement is prevented, the valves **(221)** and **(222)** change position, preventing the oil flow (feed and boom pressure) to the pilot control and boom valves [3, 4]. 
3. The oil from the pilot control and boom valves then flows back to the hydraulic oil tank **(110)** through the drilling module movement prevention valves **(221)** and **(222)**, and the collecting piece **(135)** [3, 4].

questions.question: When checking the settings of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) for an RD525 rock drill, what specific pressure value should the pressure controller (B) be adjusted to at measuring point MP2?
questions.answer:
When checking the settings of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** for an RD525 rock drill, the pressure controller **(B)** must be adjusted to **255 bar** at measuring point **MP2** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 5.1.1, "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" in the *Drilling hydraulics DD422i* manual (Pages 47–49), the step-by-step sequence to achieve this adjustment is as follows [1, 3-7]:

1. Remove the caps from the flow controller **(A)** and the pressure controller **(B)** and undo the locking nuts of their adjusting spindles [3].
2. Open the adjusting screws of the pressure controller **(B)** and the flow controller **(A)** almost fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
3. Connect the pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point **(MP2)** of the drilling control block [3].
4. Start the power pack [4].
5. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller **(A)** fully closed (clockwise) so the pump operates at constant pressure [4].
6. If the machine is equipped with a 140cc percussion/feed pump, run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the adjustment of the feed percussion pressure controller is locked. *(Note: With smaller feed/percussion pumps this action is not needed)* [4].
7. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller **(B)** clockwise until the pressure gauge shows 100 bar [4].
8. Let the load sensing line bleed into a separate container by running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and connecting a measuring hose to the measuring connector **(LS)**. Once all air has escaped, remove the measuring hose from the measuring connector **(LS)** or tighten the hose connection **(C)** of the flow controller **(A)** [5].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller **(B)** clockwise until the pressure gauge shows the correct pressure of **255 bar** for the RD525. Read the pressure value from the gauge connected to measuring point **MP2** [1, 5].
10. Lock the adjustment of the pressure controller **(B)** with the locking nut, and release the boom zoom function if you were using the 140cc pump [1].
11. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller **(A)** almost fully open (counterclockwise) [1].
12. Allow the pressure to stabilize in the pressure gauge connected to the measuring point **MP2** [1].
13. Adjust the stand-by pressure to **30 bar** from the flow controller **(A)** by turning the adjusting screw clockwise. *(Note: If there are oscillations in the hydraulic system, the adjustment value can be changed between 22-30 bar)* [6].
14. Lock the adjusting screw of the flow controller **(A)** with the locking nut [6].
15. Stop the power pack [6].
16. Allow the pressure to come down to zero in the pressure gauge connected to measuring point **MP2** [6].
17. Start the power pack [6].
18. Allow the pressure to stabilize in the pressure gauge connected to measuring point **MP2** [6].
19. If the stand-by pressure is in the recommended range, install the protective caps to the flow controller **(A)** and pressure controller **(B)** [7].
20. If the stand-by pressure is not in the right range, readjust the flow controller **(A)** by repeating steps 10-18 [7].
21. Stop the power pack [7].
22. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **MP2** [7].

questions.question: When bleeding the forward tilt cylinder to resolve parallelism issues with the boom in the down position (-30° or -24°), which specific one-way restrictor valve must be carefully opened 0 to 1 turns while the retracted cylinder is kept pressurized?
questions.answer:
When bleeding the feed forward tilt cylinder to resolve issues caused by air in the hydraulic circuit, the specific valve that must be carefully opened 0 to 1 turns is the **one-way restrictor valve (C)** (also referred to as the non-return valve in the text) [1, 2]. 

According to Section 4.3.2, "Lift circuit" (under the "Flushing and bleeding the boom hydraulic circuit" procedures) in the *SB20/SB20NV/SB40/SB40NV Booms* manual, the step-by-step sequence for bleeding with the boom in the normal position is as follows [2, 3]:

1. Turn the rotation mechanism approx. 90° so that the feed is set next to the boom [2]. 
2. Run the feed forward tilt cylinder from end to end two times [2].
3. Next, run the feed forward tilt cylinder fully out [2]. 
4. Lift the boom to its up position and keep the lift function on for another 10 seconds [2].
5. With the boom in this position, run the feed forward tilt cylinder fully in and then lower the boom to its down position (–30° or –24°) [2]. 
6. Keep the feed forward tilt cylinder (with the cylinder retracted) pressurized and very carefully open the non-return valve / one-way restrictor **(C)** for 0 to 1 turns [2]. *(Note: Before opening the one-way restrictor, you must cover it with an appropriate cloth to protect your eyes from the penetrative oil spray released when opening the restrictor)* [2, 3]. 
7. Close the one-way restrictor [2].
8. Repeat the procedure from step 5 (including opening and closing the restrictor) two more times [3].

questions.question: On rigs equipped with the optional TFX telescopic feed, which specific component controls the return oil flow to ensure that the TFX feed cylinder (27) returns to its home position before the primary feed cylinder (26) during a backward feed movement?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the specific component that controls this return oil flow is the **TFX one way restrictor valve (27.1)** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 4.4 "Feed" in the *Drilling hydraulics DD422i* manual (Page 35/76), this valve throttles the return flow from the main feed cylinder to ensure that the TFX feed cylinder **(27)** returns to its home position before the primary feed cylinder **(26)** [1, 2].

The step-by-step sequence for the backward feed movement on rigs equipped with the TFX feed is as follows:

1. Pulling the rock drill joystick backwards activates the **pilot control valve Y3B (20.21)** and initiates the feed backward movement [2].
2. Oil flows from the **drilling control valve block (20) port B2** to the **TFX control block (28)**, passing through the **TFX bottom cylinder chamber control valve (28.3)** to the **TFX feed cylinder (27)** [2].
3. Simultaneously, oil flows from **port B2** to the **feed cylinder (26)** via the **pressure relief valve (28.1)** [2].
4. Return oil from the **TFX feed cylinder (27)** flows to the **TFX collector piece (27.2)** [2].
5. Simultaneously, return oil from the **feed cylinder (26)** flows via the **TFX one way restrictor valve (27.1)** to the **TFX collector piece (27.2)**. *It is at this step that the restrictor valve performs its control function* [2].
6. From the collector piece, the combined oil flows back to the **drilling control valve block (20) port A2**, through the **main spool (20.16)** and **port T2** to the **collecting piece (7)** [2].
7. Finally, the oil flows via the **OW-cooler (5)** or the optional **OA-cooler (30)** to the **hydraulic oil receiver (4) port T1** [2].

questions.question: During water circuit operation, what specific pressure range must the pressure reducing valve (506) be adjusted to while monitoring the water pressure gauge (510.06), and what is the rating of the pressure relief valve (514) that protects against supply system peaks?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the specific pressure range and component ratings during water circuit operation are as follows:

*   **Pressure Reducing Valve (506):** Must be adjusted to a range of **1-7 bar** [1, 2]. 
*   **Pressure Relief Valve (514):** Has a rating of **15 bar** and is installed to protect the system in case of high-pressure peaks from the working site's water supply system [3].

According to Section 4.1, "Operation of the pressure reducing valve (506)" (Page 29), and Section 7.2.2, "Adjusting water pressure" (Page 47) in the *Water circuit NC7/DT821/DT1131* manual, the step-by-step sequence for adjusting this pressure is:

1. Adjust the pressure using the adjusting knob **(A/1)** on the pressure reducing valve **(506)** while the water pump **(501)** is running [1, 2].
2. Read the current pressure value on the water pressure gauge **(510.06)** [1]. 
3. Increase the pressure by turning the adjusting knob clockwise, and decrease the pressure by turning it counterclockwise [1, 2].
4. Strictly ensure that the value read on the gauge never exceeds the absolute maximum of **25 bar** [2].

questions.question: To get optimum damping performance and prevent cavitation, what mathematical relationship must the low-pressure (LP) accumulator's gas pre-charge pressure have to the return line pressure, and what is its normal pressurized bar range?
questions.answer:
To achieve optimum damping performance and prevent cavitation in the return lines and channels, the low-pressure (LP) accumulator's gas pre-charge pressure must be exactly **half of the return line pressure** [1-3]. Normally, the low-pressure accumulator is pressurized to a range of **2 - 4 bars** [1-3]. 

According to the "Filling pressures of accumulators -> Low pressure accumulator (LP)" section of the *maintenance instructions* (referenced on pages 22 and 25), adhering to these specifications is critical, as overfilling a low-pressure accumulator significantly increases the risk of cavitation, which can cause damage to the rock drill [4-6].

questions.question: When calibrating the activation pressure of the anti-jamming automatics, what specific feed pilot control pressure range must be verified at measuring point M3 after setting the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) to the 120 bar factory setting?
questions.answer:
When calibrating the activation pressure of the anti-jamming automatics, the specific feed pilot control pressure range that must be verified at measuring point **M3** is **19-21 bar** [1, 2].

According to Section 5.1.5, "Adjusting anti-jamming pressure" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Pages 93-95 of the standard manual and Pages 100-102 of the constant feed speed manual), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [3-6]:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the anti-jamming valve **(34)** adjusting screw [7, 8].
2. Turn the anti-jamming valve **(34)** adjusting screw first fully closed (clockwise), and then open it 2 turns (counterclockwise) [7, 8].
3. Start the powerpack [7, 8].
4. Run the rock drill against the rear stopper [7, 8].
5. Stop the powerpack [7, 8].
6. Loosen the locking nut of rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** of the rotation control block adjusting screw [7, 8].
7. Turn the LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** adjusting screw almost fully open (counterclockwise) [7, 8].
8. Turn the rotation speed regulating valve **(59)** closed (clockwise) [8, 9].
9. Plug the pressure side hose of the feed cylinder [8, 9].
10. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the hose support and plug the hose ends [9, 10].
11. Install a pressure gauge to the measuring point **M3** of the anti-jamming/return automatics block [9, 10].
12. Start the powerpack [9, 10].
13. Lock the control levers of the rotation and feed pilot control valves **(58)** and **(31)** to the back position [9, 10].
14. Adjust the desired anti-jamming activation pressure with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** by turning the adjusting screw clockwise to the factory setting of **120 bar** (RD314: 140 bar) [1, 2, 9, 10]. Read the pressure value in the rotation pressure gauge **(51)** [1, 2].
15. Adjust the anti-jamming valve **(34)** so that it directs feed pilot control pressure at the set pressure to the measuring point **M3** of the anti-jamming/return automatics block. Read the feed pilot control pressure (**approx. 19-21 bar**) in the pressure gauge installed in the measuring point **M3** [1, 2].
16. When the anti-jamming valve **(34)** is correctly adjusted, lock the adjusting screw of the valve **(34)** [1, 2].
17. Adjust the rotation pressure with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** to **180 bar** by turning the adjusting screw clockwise [11, 12]. Read the pressure in the rotation pressure gauge **(51)** [11, 12].
18. Lock the adjusting screw of the rotation LS-pressure relief valve **(65)** [11, 12].
19. Release the control levers of the rotation and feed pilot control valves **(58)** and **(31)** [11, 12].
20. Stop the powerpack [11, 12].
21. Remove the plugs from the disconnected rotation hoses and reconnect the hoses together [11, 12].
22. Remove the plugs from the feed cylinder pressure side feed line and reconnect the hose to the feed cylinder [11, 12].
23. Start the powerpack [6, 13].
24. Turn drilling rotation on again by locking the control lever of rotation pilot control valve **(58)** in the back position [6, 13].
25. Adjust the drill rod rotation speed to the desired value by turning the rotation speed regulating valve **(59)** counterclockwise [6, 13].
26. Release the control lever of the rotation pilot control valve **(58)** [6, 13].
27. Stop the powerpack [6, 13].
28. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **M3** for the anti-jamming/return automatics [6, 13].

questions.question: If an operator chooses the alternative collaring method of locking the rotation (58), percussion (14), and feed (31) pilot control levers into the back position, what specific physical adjustment must first be made to the feed speed regulating valve (150) to ensure drilling starts at half power?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, to ensure drilling starts at half power when using the alternative collaring method, you must first **turn the feed speed regulating valve (150) fully open (counterclockwise)** [1].

According to Section 4.2.7, "Operation of the collaring" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics, constant feed speed DD321* manual (Page 52/144), the step-by-step sequence is as follows [1, 2]:

1. Turn the **feed speed regulating valve (150)** fully open (counterclockwise) [1].
2. Lock all three control levers—the rotation, percussion, and feed pilot control valves—into the back position [1]. 
3. Drilling will now start at half power [1].
4. Drilling continues at half power until the drilling values are returned to correspond to full-power drilling by turning the **feed speed regulating valve (150)** [1].

questions.question: When lifting the SB20 boom, the boom control block (1) contains a pressure reducing valve (.02) (S7) that restricts the pressure entering the forward tilt cylinder (6) A-port to what specific value in order to prevent the 350 bar pressure reducing valve (6.02) from opening?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, when lifting the SB20 boom, the pressure reducing valve **(.02) (S7)** located in the boom control block **(1)** restricts the pressure entering the forward tilt cylinder **(6)** A-port to a specific value of **100 bars** [1, 2]. 

This 100-bar restriction ensures that the forward tilt cylinder's own pressure reducing valve **(6.02)**, which is rated at **350 bars**, is prevented from opening when certain auxiliary devices are used [1, 2].

questions.question: Whenever the diesel engine or powerpack is running, which specific drilling module movement prevention valves are automatically activated to cut off the oil flow from the pilot-control valves and the boom pressure lines?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the specific drilling module movement prevention valves that are automatically activated whenever the diesel engine or powerpack is running are:

*   **Drilling module movement prevention valve (221)** (pilot-control valve line): Cuts off the feed pressure from the pilot-control valves [1, 2].
*   **Drilling module movement prevention valve (222)** (boom line): Cuts off the boom pressure lines [2, 3].

According to Section 4.2.11, "Operation of the drilling module movement prevention" in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Pages 60–61/138 of the standard manual and Pages 62–63/144 of the constant feed speed manual) [4-7], the step-by-step sequence of operation is as follows:

1. The drilling module movement prevention valves **(221)** and **(222)** are activated always when the diesel engine or powerpack is on [4, 6]. In this situation, oil flows through these valves **(221)** and **(222)** to the pilot control valves and the boom valves [4, 6].
2. When the drilling module movement is prevented, valves **(221)** and **(222)** change position, which prevents the oil flow to the pilot control and boom valves [5, 7]. 
3. The oil from the pilot control and boom valves then flows back to the hydraulic oil tank **(110)** through the drilling module movement prevention valves **(221)** and **(222)**, and the collecting piece **(135)** [5, 7].

questions.question: If the drill rig is equipped with the TFX 500 telescopic feed, what specific pressure value in bar must the fast feed max pressure relief valve (30) be adjusted to while reading the feed pressure gauge (21)?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, if the drill rig is equipped with the TFX 500 telescopic feed, the fast feed max pressure relief valve **(30)** must be adjusted to **180 bar** [1, 2].

According to the "Adjusting fast feed max. pressure" section in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Page 103 for the standard system and Page 109 for the constant feed speed system), the step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the fast feed max. pressure relief valve **(30)** [3, 4].
2. Start the powerpack [3, 4].
3. Run the rock drill against the rear stopper by locking the control lever of the fast feed pilot control valve **(33)** into the front position, and at the same time adjust the fast feed max. pressure with the pressure relief valve **(30)**. Read the pressure value from the feed pressure gauge **(21)** to ensure it is set to **180 bar** for the TFX 500 feed [1-4]. 
4. Release the control lever of the fast feed pilot control valve **(33)** [1, 2].
5. Lock the adjusting screw of the fast feed max. pressure relief valve **(30)** [1, 2].
6. Stop the powerpack [1, 2].

questions.question: You are diagnosing a DD422i where the drilling feed is not working at all; you measure a normal pilot control pressure of 19-21 bar at measuring point M1, but the feed pressure gauge (21) shows no reading. Which specific component within the feed directional valve (23) assembly should you remove, inspect, and clean?
questions.answer:
If the pressure at measuring point **M1** is approximately **19-21 bar**, but the **feed pressure gauge (21)** does not show any reading, it is likely that the **spool** of the **feed directional valve (23)** is sticking [1, 2]. 

According to the "Feed not working at all (drilling)" troubleshooting procedures in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Section 6.9 / 6.10, Pages 124 / 130), the step-by-step sequence to remove, inspect, and clean the component is as follows [3, 4]:

1. Stop the powerpack.
2. Remove the front cover of the **feed directional valve (23)**. The spool comes out with the cover.
3. Clean the spool and the valve housing carefully.
4. Mount the spool back with care.

*(Note: While your scenario mentions the DD422i, the specific measuring points, pressure values, and component IDs provided in the source material specifically match the THC561 drilling hydraulic system utilized on rigs such as the DD321).*

questions.question: An operator reports that a specific boom movement on the SB40 boom is completely unresponsive; when you connect a pressure gauge to measuring point M7 of the feed and percussion control block and move the corresponding control lever, M7 receives no pressure. What specific component within the boom control valve assembly is most likely sticking?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, if a boom movement is not working and the measuring point **M7** does not receive pressure, the most likely cause is that the **load sensing line shuttle valve** of the corresponding control block is sticking [1, 2].

According to the "Boom movement not working" troubleshooting instructions in the boom manuals (Section 4.5.5, Page 45), you should inspect and resolve the issue using the following step-by-step sequence:

1. Stop the powerpack [2].
2. Remove the boom valve located at the top of the control panel [2].
3. Disassemble the boom valve and check the shuttle valves of all working blocks [2].
4. Reassemble the boom valve after cleaning and inspecting it, and mount it back [2]. 

*(Note: If the measuring point M7 had received pressure, it would instead indicate that the functional device of the boom is faulty [2].)*

questions.question: During drilling, the feed unexpectedly starts pulling backwards on its own due to the activation of the anti-jamming valve of the flushing control. If the rig is utilizing a water flushing circuit, what specific water flow switch ID must be checked to see if the flow has dropped below its set value?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, if the rig utilizes a water flushing circuit and the flow drops below its set value, you must check the **water flow switch (518)**. 

According to the "Flushing flow control" sections (Section 4.2.13 in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals, Page 65, and Section 3.2.8 in the *Water circuit NC7/DT821/DT1131* manual, Page 21), the step-by-step sequence for how this system automatically reverses the feed is as follows:

1. When the water flow in the flushing circuit drops below the set value of the **water flow switch (518)** (for example, due to a lack of water or a blocked drill bit), the **anti-jamming valve of flushing control (206)** is activated [1, 2]. 
2. Oil then flows through the **anti-jamming valve of flushing control (206)** and the **shuttle valve (207)** [1].
3. This provides pilot control pressure to the main **anti-jamming valve (34)**, causing it to change its position [1].
4. The feed pilot control pressure then reaches port **d** of the **feed directional valve (23)** by passing through the **shuttle valves (37)** and **(38)** [1].
5. This causes the **feed directional valve (23)** to change its position, directing feed pressure into **feed line B** [1].
6. Consequently, the feed starts pulling backwards and will continue to do so until the water flow returns to normal [1, 2].

questions.question: A rig's shank lubrication unit (SLU) triggers an alarm where the red indicator light is on, the green indicator light is off, and the drilling joystick centers itself, yet the oil amount appears normal. According to the SLU troubleshooting guide, if the air line pressure switch is adjusted correctly and the wiring is intact, what specific issue with the oil in the shank lubricator tank could be causing this electrical fault?
questions.answer:
According to the "SLU Troubleshooting" section (Section 8.1, Page 42 of the *Shank Lubrication Unit* manual) under the specific problem *"Normal amount of oil but alarm activated (red indicator light on, green indicator light off, drilling joystick is centered)"*, the specific issue with the oil could be that it is **dirty and conducting electricity** [1, 2]. 

To resolve this fault, the required remedy is to **change the oil in the shank lubricator tank** [2].

questions.question: The percussion half-power pressure is measuring significantly higher than the 100 bar factory setting. You have verified that both the percussion half-power pressure relief valve (6) and the monitoring valve (18) are functioning correctly. What specific orifice located at port 9 of the feed and percussion control block must be checked to see if it has loosened?
questions.answer:
If the percussion half-power pressure is measuring significantly higher than the 100 bar factory setting and you have already verified that the percussion half-power pressure relief valve (6) and monitoring valve (18) are functioning correctly, you must check the **orifice (9)** of the load-sensing line to see if it has loosened [1, 2].

According to the "Percussion half-power pressure too high" troubleshooting section in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (e.g., Page 123 of the standard manual, and Pages 128–129 of the constant feed speed DD321 manual), the step-by-step sequence to check and resolve the loosened orifice (9) at port 9 of the feed and percussion control block is as follows [2-4]:

1. Stop the powerpack [2, 4].
2. Remove the adapter from port 9 of the feed and percussion control block [2, 4].
3. Check if the orifice (9) is properly seated at the bottom of the drilling port 9 [2, 4].
4. If the orifice has loosened, retighten it carefully [2, 4].
5. Mount the adapter back on port 9 of the feed and percussion control block [2, 4].

questions.question: When adjusting the water hose reel brake valve (24) while reading the pressure at measuring point (23), what specific braking pressure range in bar should be set to ensure the water hose can be slowly reeled out by hand?
questions.answer:
To ensure the water hose can be slowly reeled out by hand, the braking pressure must be adjusted to a range of **20-30 bar** [1]. This pressure setting also ensures that the braking pressure will stop the water hose reel rotation when tramming stops [2].

According to Section 6.1, "Adjusting the water hose reel brake valve," the step-by-step sequence for this procedure is as follows:

1. Start the diesel engine [1].
2. Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point **(23)** of the water hose reel brake valve **(24)** [1].
3. Loosen the locking nut **(25)** of the water hose reel brake valve [1].
4. Activate the "reeling out the water hose" function and read the braking pressure from the pressure gauge [1].
5. Adjust the braking pressure to **20-30 bar** by turning the adjusting screw **(26)** clockwise or counterclockwise [1, 2]. 
6. Tighten the locking nut **(25)** [2].
7. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **(23)** [2].

questions.question: When calibrating the stabilizer reference pressure at measuring point R, what specific pressure value must the pressure reducing valve (145) be adjusted to?
questions.answer:
When calibrating the stabilizer reference pressure at measuring point **R**, the pressure reducing valve **(145)** must be adjusted to exactly **30 bar** [1, 2]. This reference pressure is used to compensate for the mass of the drilling equipment and the frictions of the feed beam [1, 2].

According to the "Adjusting stabilizer reference pressure" procedure (Section 5.1.23, Page 112 of the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manual, and Pages 117–118 of the *constant feed speed DD321* manual), the step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing valve **(145)** [1, 3].
2. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point **R** of the stabilizer control block [1, 3].
3. Start the powerpack [1, 3].
4. Run the rock drill against the rear limit [1, 3].
5. Adjust the stabilizer reference pressure to **30 bar** using the pressure reducing valve **(145)**. Read the pressure value from the gauge connected to measuring point **R** [1, 3].
6. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing valve **(145)** [3, 4].
7. Stop the powerpack [4, 5].

questions.question: While monitoring the pressure at measuring point M1, what exact pressure values should the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18) and the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) be adjusted to when running the feed against the front and rear end stoppers, respectively?
questions.answer:
While monitoring the pressure at measuring point **M1**, the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve **(20.18)** must be adjusted to exactly **200 bar** when running against the front end stopper, and the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve **(20.19)** must be adjusted to exactly **240 bar** when running against the rear end stopper [1, 2].

According to the troubleshooting sections 6.10 ("Feed / fast feed pressure is too low") and 6.11 ("Feed / fast feed pressure is too high") in the *Drilling hydraulics DD422i* manual (Pages 67-68), the complete step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows [1-5]:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point **(M1)** of the drilling control valve block **(20)** [3, 5].
2. Use the pressure controller **(B)** to adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** to **250 bar** [1, 5].
3. Run the feed against the front end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve **(20.18)** to **200 bar** [1, 2].
4. Run the feed against the rear end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve **(20.19)** to **240 bar** [1, 2].
5. Re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** as instructed in the section *Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)* [2, 4].

questions.question: When adjusting the cable reel control block for the "reeling out" function, what specific pressure value should the pressure relief valve (10) be set to while the reeling out button (D) is kept pushed down?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the cable reel control block for the "reeling out" function, the pressure relief valve **(10)** must be set to exactly **20 bars** while the reeling out button **(D)** is kept pushed down [1]. 

According to Section 5.1, "Adjusting control pressure relief valves (10 and 11)" in the *Basic adjustment of the cable reel and water hose reel* manuals (Pages 19–21), the specific step-by-step sequence for this portion of the adjustment is as follows:

1. Push the manual throttle button on the side of the steering stick such that the diesel engine rpm decreases to minimum [1]. Check the rpm from the tramming display [1].
2. Push the reeling out button **(D)** and keep it pushed down [1].
3. Turn the pressure relief valve **(10)** adjusting screw counterclockwise to adjust the pressure to **20 bars** [1].
4. Lock the adjustment of the pressure relief valve **(10)** with the locking nut (clockwise) [1].
5. Release the reeling out button **(D)** [2].
6. Shut down the diesel engine [2].
7. Remove the temporary hose from between the fittings and reinstall the pipes **(21)** and **(22)** [2].
8. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **M2 (18)** [2].

questions.question: When adjusting the mine's inlet pressure before the water booster pump using the pressure reducing valve (1), what specific pressure range must be set to ensure the pressure sensor (B230P) value stays under 25 bars?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the mine's inlet pressure before the water booster pump using the pressure reducing valve (1), the pressure must be adjusted to a range of **2-7 bars** [1, 2]. 

According to the "Adjusting the mine's inlet pressure" procedure (found in Section 7.2.7, Pages 44–45 of the *Flushing circuit* manuals and Section 5.11.7, Pages 238–239 of the *Operator's Manual DD422i StageV*), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Open the shut-off valve **(2)** [3, 4].
2. Turn the knob **(3)** fully open [3, 4].
3. Start the water booster pump [3, 4].
4. Turn the knob **(3)** to adjust the pressure to **2-7 bars** according to drilling conditions [1, 2]. Turning the knob clockwise increases the pressure and turning counterclockwise decreases the pressure [1, 2]. Check the pressure gauge **(4)** for the value [1, 2].
5. Select $\rightarrow$ Troubleshooting $\rightarrow$ Compressor and Water Pump and check that the pressure sensor **(B230P)** value is under **25 bars** [1, 2].

questions.question: What are the exact transport width, height, and length dimensions specified for the Sandvik DD422i development drill?
questions.answer:
According to the technical specifications for the Sandvik DD422i development drill, the exact transport dimensions are:

*   **Transport width:** 2 310 mm [1]
*   **Transport height:** 3 150 mm / 3 050 mm [1]
*   **Transport length:** 13 250 mm [1]

questions.question: When identifying the main components of the rock drill, what specific part does item number 8 correspond to, located alongside the flushing housing and stabilizer accumulator?
questions.answer:
Based on the main components of the hydraulic rock drill (RD520/525), item number **8** corresponds to the **pressure accumulator (high pressure)** [1-3]. 

In the component diagrams, it is listed alongside the flushing housing (6) and the pressure accumulator for the stabilizer (9) [1, 3].

questions.question: Based on the technical specifications, what is the net weight and the maximum parallel coverage area of the SB40 boom?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical specifications for the DD321 development drill, the specifications for the SB40 boom (type TS2-231) are as follows:

*   **Net weight:** 2 100 kg [1, 2]
*   **Maximum parallel coverage:** 44.5 m² [3, 4]

*(Note: While the specific parallel coverage for the boom is 44.5 m², the overall general coverage area for the rig equipped with two SB40 booms is listed as 49 m² [5, 6].)*

questions.question: When adjusting the minimum percussion pressure during full-power drilling using the monitoring valve (18), what specific pressure value should be read from the percussion pressure gauge (11) after the valve's adjusting screw is fully opened and then closed by exactly 3½ turns?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, when adjusting the minimum percussion pressure using the monitoring valve (18), the specific pressure value that should be read from the percussion pressure gauge (11) is **120 bar** [1]. 

According to Section 5.1.7 ("Adjusting min. percussion pressure") of the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Pages 96-97 of the standard manual, and Pages 103-104 of the constant feed speed DD321 manual), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1-5]:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the half-power pressure relief valve **(6)**.
2. Turn the adjusting screw of the half-power pressure relief valve **(6)** almost fully closed (clockwise).
3. Loosen the locking nuts of the monitoring valve **(18)**.
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the monitoring valve **(18)** fully open (counterclockwise) and then close it by 3½ turns.
5. Start the powerpack.
6. Turn percussion half-power on by locking the control lever of the percussion pilot control valve **(14)** to the back position.
7. Adjust the min. percussion pressure to **120 bar** with the monitoring valve **(18)**. Read the pressure value from the percussion pressure gauge **(11)**.
8. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw for the monitoring valve **(18)**.
9. Adjust the percussion half-power pressure relief valve **(6)** according to the chapter "Adjusting percussion half-power".
10. Release the control lever of the percussion pilot control valve **(14)**.
11. Stop the powerpack.

questions.question: When drilling a Ø64 mm hole with an RD525 rock drill, what specific drill rod rotation speed (± 10%) should be set using the rotation speed regulating valve (59)?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, when drilling a Ø64 mm hole with an RD525 rock drill, the specific drill rod rotation speed should be set to **180 rpm (± 10%)** [1-3]. 

According to the "Adjusting rotation speed" procedure (Section 5.1.13, Pages 104-105 of the standard *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manual, and Pages 110-111 of the constant feed speed manual), the speed is adjusted using the **rotation speed regulating valve (59)** with the following controls:
*   Turn the adjusting knob **counterclockwise to decrease** the speed [4, 5].
*   Turn the adjusting knob **clockwise to increase** the speed [4, 5].

To perform this adjustment while the system is running, the manuals outline the following sequence (found in the rotation circuit adjustment steps on Pages 92 and 99 of the respective *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals) [6, 7]:
1. Turn drilling rotation on by locking the control lever of the **rotation pilot control valve (58)** in the back position [6, 7].
2. Adjust the drill steel rotation speed to the desired value (180 rpm) using the **rotation speed regulating valve (59)** [6, 7]. 
3. Release the control lever of the **rotation pilot control valve (58)** to the middle position [6, 7].

questions.question: If the rock drill's water flushing circuit is in use, what specific component ID and valve setting limits the water feed pressure to 1-7 bars before reaching the WBP2 water booster pump?
questions.answer:
The water feed pressure before reaching the water booster pump (WBP2) is limited to 1-7 bars by the **pressure reducing valve**, which is identified as component **(506)** in the DD321/DT821/DT1131 manuals, and as component **(26)** or **(1)** in the DD422i/DD422iE manuals [1-3]. 

According to the *Water circuit* and *Flushing circuit* manuals (Section 4.1 "Operation of the pressure reducing valve", Section 5.1.3 "Checking the operation of the pressure reducing valve", and Section 7.2.7 "Adjusting the mine's inlet pressure"), the step-by-step sequence to adjust this valve is as follows [1, 3-6]:

1. Open the water circuit shut-off valve (507.02 or 2) so that water flows through the mud separator to the pressure reducing valve [1, 6].
2. Turn the adjusting knob (1 or 3) of the pressure reducing valve fully open [6].
3. Start the water booster pump [6].
4. Turn the adjusting knob to set the pressure to the 1-7 bar range (or 2-7 bar depending on drilling conditions) while the pump is running [1, 6]. Turning the knob clockwise increases the water pressure, and turning it counterclockwise decreases the pressure [1, 6].
5. Read the set pressure value from the mechanical water pressure gauge (510.06, 4, or 26.1) [1, 6, 7].
6. In the control system display, select *Troubleshooting* → *Compressor and Water Pump* and verify that the pressure sensor (B230P) value, which measures the flushing pressure after the water booster pump, remains under 25 bars [6].

questions.question: When adjusting the nominal level of feed pressure using the feed deviation valve (216), what is the maximum restricted deviation pressure range (± bar) that the operator can adjust from the basic level without altering the percussion pressure?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the nominal level of feed pressure using the feed deviation valve (216), the operator can adjust the feed pressure by a maximum restricted deviation range of **±45 bar** from the basic/nominal level without altering the percussion pressure [1-5]. 

According to the "Adjusting nominal level of feed pressure" procedure in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (e.g., Section 5.1.10, Pages 101–102 / 107-108), the step-by-step sequence to set this basic level is as follows:

1. Remove the hand wheel of the feed deviation valve (216) [6, 7].
2. Start the power pack [6, 7].
3. Turn the switches of the return automatics (S73 and S74) to the M position [6, 7].
4. Run the rock drill to the rear position [6, 8].
5. Pull the control lever of the percussion pilot control valve (14) to the back position and push the feed pilot control valve (31) to the front position [6, 8].
6. Adjust the percussion pressure to the correct level with the feed pressure regulating valve (20) [6, 8].
7. Adjust the feed pressure to the correct level with the feed deviation valve (216) [4, 8].
8. Release the control levers of the percussion pilot control valve (14) and the feed pilot control valve (31) [4, 8].
9. Stop the power pack [4, 5].
10. Attach the hand wheel of the feed deviation valve (216) into the initial position (pointer pin straight ahead) [4, 5]. 

Once this setup is complete, the feed deviation can be adjusted ±45 bar from this basic level using the knob [4, 5].

questions.question: During threading operations, what specific system pressure limit must the rotation pressure be kept strictly below to prevent the anti-jamming valve (34) from automatically activating and reversing the feed direction?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, during threading operations, the rotation pressure must be kept strictly below the **anti-jamming activation pressure** to prevent the feed direction from automatically reversing [1, 2].
