The specific pressure limit is determined by the adjustment of the **anti-jamming valve (34)**. The manufacturer's recommended range for this activation pressure is **110 to 140 bar**, with a factory setting of **120 bar** (or **140 bar** for the RD314 rock drill) [3, 4].

According to Section 4.3.1 ("Operation of the threading") in the *THC561 drilling hydraulics* manuals (Page 77/138 of the standard manual, and Page 82/144 of the constant feed speed manual), the step-by-step sequence for the threading operation is as follows:

1. Turn the rotation on by pulling back the control lever of the **rotation pilot control valve (58)** [5, 6]. *(If required, the speed of rotation can be adjusted with the **regulating valve (59)** for rotation speed)* [5, 6].
2. Pull the control lever of the **feed pilot control valve (31)** backwards to feed the rock drill forwards at a speed that corresponds to the thread pitch [5, 6].
3. Keep the feed speed constant throughout the threading operation [5, 6]. 
4. Adjust the feed pressure suitably using the **feed deviation valve (216)** (the normal feed pressure used for drilling can serve as the basic setting) [5, 6].
5. *(For constant feed speed DD321 systems)*: Adjust the feed speed suitably using the **feed speed regulating valve (150)** [2]. 

*Note: It is during this sequence that the operator must ensure the rotation pressure remains strictly below the set anti-jamming activation value to prevent the automatic reversal of the feed* [1, 2].

questions.question: According to the technical specifications, what is the exact extension length in millimeters for both the boom zoom and the feed, and what is the maximum roll-over angle?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical specifications in the source material, the exact measurements are as follows:

*   **Boom extension (boom zoom) length:** 1 050 mm [1-3]
*   **Feed extension length:** 1 350 mm [1-3]
*   **Maximum roll-over angle:** 358° [1, 4]

questions.question: During the automatic parallelism function of the boom lift, how does the third chamber (Y-port) of the boom lift cylinder (2) physically interact with the feed forward tilt cylinder (6) piston rod side via the pump cylinder line when the boom is being lowered?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Boom lower function" descriptions for the SB-series booms (Sections 4.2.1 and 4.2.2 in the *SB20/SB20NV/SB40/SB40NV Booms* manuals), the physical interaction during the automatic parallelism function works through the displacement of oil. 

When the boom is lowered, the capacity of the third chamber of the boom lift cylinder (2) physically decreases [1, 2]. This forces oil out of the third chamber and routes it to the feed forward tilt cylinder through the following sequence:

1. Oil flows out via the lift cylinder (2) port (Y) and travels along the pump cylinder line (PUMP LINE) [1, 2].
2. Depending on the specific boom model, the oil routes through a valve block:
   * **For SB20/SB20NV booms (Page 20):** The oil flows through block (1) via ports (Y-F1) [1].
   * **For SB40/SB40NV booms (Page 22):** The oil flows through block (14) via ports (H-F1) [2].
3. The oil then travels via the forward tilt cylinder (6) port (B) and enters the forward tilt cylinder (6) piston rod side [1, 2].
4. The oil entering the piston rod side causes the forward tilt cylinder to perform a retract stroke, pulling it inward [1, 2].

Because the cylinder volumes are mechanically matched, the distances traveled by the feed forward tilt cylinder (6) and the boom lift cylinder (2) are exactly equal, which automatically maintains the parallel alignment of the feed as the boom is lowered [1, 2].

questions.question: On the SB40 boom, in order for the extreme position control circuit to function properly, which three specific shuttle valves inside block (1) must supply hydraulic pressure to the P-line of the plunger valves (12) and (13)?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, in order for the extreme position control circuit to function properly on the SB40 boom, the three specific shuttle valves inside block (1) that must supply hydraulic pressure to the P-line of the plunger valves (12 and 13) are shuttle valves **(1.03)**, **(1.04)**, and **(1.06)** [1-3]. 

According to Section 4.4, "Extreme swing position control circuit SB40, SB40NV" in the *SB20/SB20NV/SB40/SB40NV Booms* manuals (Pages 38–40), these three shuttle valves allow hydraulic pressure to enter the plunger valve P-line whenever the boom is lifting, swinging, or performing both functions at the same time [1, 2, 4, 5]. 

If the boom's swing angle exceeds the allowed limit, the circuit operates using the following step-by-step sequence (using plunger valve 13 as the example):
1. The boom is swung to the side opposite the swing cylinder until the **plunger valve (13)** is mechanically activated [6-8].
2. Oil flows from the carrier control valve port **(A5 / B8)** to the block (1) port **(B8)**, and then through the shuttle valves **(.06)** and **(.04)** to the block (1) port **(P3)** [6-8].
3. The oil continues through the activated **plunger valve (13)** ports **(P-BR)** and diverges as a control pressure, which adjusts the spool position of the **pilot-controlled directional valve (1.05)** [6-8].
4. This allows the **swing cylinder (4)** piston side pressure to discharge freely into the hydraulic oil tank as long as the plunger valve remains activated [6-8].
5. Simultaneously, the oil that flowed through the plunger valve (13) travels to the **block (14)** connection **(I)**, changing the spool position of the **pressure-controlled directional valve (14.09)** [9-11].
6. The oil continues from the **block (14)** port **(L1)** to the **swing cylinder (4)** port **(B)** and into the piston rod side, which actively causes the boom to swing backward out of the extreme position [9-11].

questions.question: When calibrating the boom hydraulics, what specific pressure value in bar must the pressure reducing/relieving valve (210) be set to when running the boom zoom firmly against the stopper, as read from a gauge connected to measuring point M10?
questions.answer:
When running the boom zoom firmly against the stopper to raise maximum pressure, the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)** must be set to exactly **250 bar**, as read from the pressure gauge connected to measuring point **M10** [1]. After the calibration of the boom circuit's relief valves is complete, the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)** must be readjusted to its final operating pressure of **230 bar** [2].

According to Section 4.5.3, "Adjusting boom circuit max. pressure" (Pages 43-44 of the *SB20/SB20NV/SB40/SB40NV Booms* manual), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1-4]:

1. Install a pressure gauge to the measuring point **M10** of the drilling control block.
2. Loosen the adjusting screw locking nut of the boom valve max. pressure relief valve. 
3. Tighten the adjusting screw of the boom max. pressure relief valve almost to its end (over 250 bar).
4. Start the powerpack.
5. Loosen the adjusting screw locking nut of the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)** at the drilling control block.
6. Run the boom zoom inwards or outwards (whichever is safest) and hold against the stopper to raise maximum pressure.
7. Adjust the boom circuit max. pressure to **250 bar** with the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)**. Read the pressure value in the gauge connected to the measuring point **M10**.
8. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)**.
9. Loosen the adjusting screw locking nut of the boom valve max. pressure relief valve.
10. Run for instance, the zoom cylinder inwards.
11. Loosen the adjusting screw of the boom max. pressure relief valve until adjusting begins to effect. The valve begins to fizz when restricting pressure. The boom max. pressure relief valve begins to open exactly at 250 bar. Read the pressure in the pressure gauge at the measuring point **M10**.
12. Lock the adjusting screw of the boom circuit max. pressure relief valve.
13. Run the boom control operating valve for zoom or feed transfer. 
14. Adjust the boom circuit max. pressure to **230 bar** with the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)**. Read the pressure value in the gauge connected to the measuring point **M10**.
15. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)**.
16. Stop the powerpack.
17. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **M10**.

*(Note: A nearly identical sequence applies to adjusting the boom circuit max. LS pressure in Section 4.5.2, which also temporarily requires setting valve 210 to 250 bar while against the stopper before lowering it to 230 bar for final adjustment [5-8].)*

questions.question: During the outward movement of the boom swing cylinder (4) on an SB40 boom, which specific pilot-controlled directional valve in block (1) and 3/2 directional valve in block (14) route the oil flow to the boom swing cylinder's port A?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, during the outward movement of the boom swing cylinder (4) on an SB40 boom, the oil flow is routed to port A by the **pilot-controlled directional valve (.05)** in block (1) and the **3/2 directional valve (.10)** in block (14) [1-3].

According to Section 4.2.6, "Swing cylinder outward movement, automatic parallelism" in the *SB20/SB20NV/SB40/SB40NV Booms* manual (Page 32), the step-by-step sequence for this oil flow is as follows:

1. Oil flows from the carrier control valve port **(A5 / B8)** to the block (1) port **(B8)** [1-3].
2. The oil then flows to the **pilot-controlled directional valve (.05)** and out from the boom block (1) port **(R)** [1-3].
3. The flow continues to the block (14) port **(R)** [1-3].
4. From there, the oil flows through the **3/2 directional valve (.10)** and out from the block (14) port **(R1)** [1-3]. 
5. Finally, the oil moves onward to the boom swing cylinder (4) port **(A)** and further on to the boom swing cylinder (4) piston side [1, 2]

questions.question: What components are responsible for starting and protecting the water pump and compressor motors?
questions.answer: The water pump and compressor motors are started and controlled by contactors (**K4** and **K5**) [6]. They are protected from overloads by motor-protective circuit-breakers and trip blocks (**F4** and **F5**) [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific functions of circuit breakers F251, F252, F311, and F450?
questions.answer:
**F251**: A fault current circuit breaker for the sockets (and optionally the cabin heater) [10].
*   **F252**: A 1-phase circuit breaker specifically for sockets **X430** and **X431** (optional) [10].
*   **F311**: A fault current circuit breaker for the internal 220 V control voltage in the main switchgear [10].
*   **F450**: A circuit breaker for the internal 24 V control voltage in the main switchgear [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the main powerpack specifications and hydraulic tank capacities for the DD321?
questions.answer: The Sandvik DD321 is equipped with 2 x HPP555 (55 kW) powerpacks [1]. The drilling hydraulic system has an oil tank volume of 270 liters, which is replenished using an electric oil tank filling pump [1]. The system's hydraulic oil is cooled by an OW30 oil-to-water cooler (2 x 30 kW) [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose variable displacement pumps that do not rotate at all or have an abnormal speed?
questions.answer: First, measure the supply voltage to the power pack; if the voltage is correct, the fault is highly likely to be mechanical rather than electrical [15]. If the electric motor does not receive sufficient control voltage, you must refer to the electric system troubleshooting instructions [15]. Finally, visually inspect the pumps to check if any mechanical damage is physically preventing them from rotating [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes a boom to fail to hold its position and how is it diagnosed?
questions.answer: A boom failing to hold its position is typically caused by a leaking overcenter valve on the boom swing or lift cylinder, which happens due to a broken O-ring or worn seat surfaces [16-18]. It can also be diagnosed by checking for dirt in the hydraulic circuit, which requires flushing the circuit, or by diagnosing air trapped in the cylinders, which requires bleeding them [16-18]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the correct setpoint for the pilot control pressure and how is it calibrated?
questions.answer: The pilot control pressure is set to 30 bar [6]. To calibrate it, loosen the locking nut of the pilot control pressure regulating valve (43) and turn the adjusting screw almost fully open (counterclockwise) [7]. Connect a pressure gauge to measuring point M8 of the percussion and feed control block, start the powerpack, and push the feed pilot control lever forwards (to activate feed backwards) [6, 7]. Turn the adjusting screw of valve (43) clockwise until the gauge reads exactly 30 bar, then release the control lever and lock the adjusting screw [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is 24 VDC power supplied, converted, and managed within the main switchgear?
questions.answer: The 24 VDC power is primarily managed by the control system power supply units (**A3** and **A4**) [7]. A dedicated battery charger (**A1**) is used to charge the rig's batteries, and an optional specialized power supply unit (**A2**) can be installed specifically to power the SLU air cooler fan [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the boom circuit maximum load-sensing (LS) pressure adjusted and what are the target setpoints?
questions.answer: The target boom circuit max LS pressure is 230 bar [1]. To adjust this, first install a pressure gauge to measuring point M10 of the drilling control block, start the powerpack, and adjust the boom circuit max pressure to 250 bar using the pressure reducing/relieving valve (210) [2, 3]. Tighten the locking nut on valve (210), turn the max LS-pressure relief valve adjusting screw almost fully open, and start the diesel engine [4]. Run the zoom cylinder inwards at an engine speed of 1800 rpm and simultaneously adjust the LS pressure to 230 bar by turning the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure relief valve clockwise [1]. Stop the diesel engine, lock the adjusting screw, start the powerpack again, and re-adjust the boom circuit max pressure back to 230 bar with valve (210) [1, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used for the Boom Sensor converter (BS) and Feed Sensor converter (FS)?
questions.answer: The **RD (Resolver-to-Digital) module** serves as both the Boom Sensor converter (BS) and the Feed Sensor converter (FS) [9]. It is a general-purpose measurement unit designed for high-accuracy applications and built to meet SIL2 class safety requirements [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical checks should I perform if the diesel engine will not start?
questions.answer: First, ensure that the battery isolation switch is in the ON position and the main power is off (if the diesel interlocking option is used) [1]. Next, check that the **automatic fuse** on the main switchgear cabinet doors, the **battery circuit main fuse F11**, and the **battery circuit fuses F12 and F13** have not tripped [1]. You should also verify that the drive selector is in the middle position, all emergency stop devices have been reset, and the fire suppression system is not preventing the engine from starting [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I read and interpret CAN fault codes when they appear on the operator's LCD display?
questions.answer: When a new Diagnostic Trouble Code (**DTC**) is received, the LCD automatically shifts to the CAN fault code screen, indicated by an open book symbol [6]. The buffer will display the specific fault code components: the **Suspect Parameter Number (SPN)** (for example, SPN 111 indicates Coolant level), the **Failure Mode Identifier (FMI)** (such as 01 for faulty wiring), and the **Occurrence Count (OC)** [7-9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it indicate if the physical values screen on the display shows '------'?
questions.answer: The physical value display normally shows the current value and its measurement unit, but if the measurement falls outside the defined range, the display will show '------' [1, 2]. The most probable cause for a value exceeding these limits is a damaged sensor or cable [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical diagnostic checks should be performed if the power pack unexpectedly stops?
questions.answer: Begin by checking the indicator panel for any active alarms [4]. Verify that the water pump and compressor control switches are in position 1, or that inlet pressure is sufficient if external water or air is being used [4]. Additionally, check that none of the circuit breakers on the main switchgear cabinet door have tripped, ensure that all emergency stop devices are reset, and confirm that the pilot circuit is fully functional [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used for the Drilling GUI (DG) and what are its communication capabilities?
questions.answer: The Drilling GUI (DG) utilizes a **CCpilot XM2**, which is a PC-based onboard display computer featuring a 12" or 15" TFT touch screen with LED backlight [1]. It serves as the main user interface for drilling and is equipped with 4 x CAN connections, 2 x Ethernet, and 2 x USB 2.0 ports [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the water circuit pressure adjusted and what are the limitations?
questions.answer: The water pressure must never exceed 25 bar [21]. The mine's inlet pressure before the water booster pump is adjusted using a pressure reducing valve (506), which has an adjusting range of 1 to 7 bar [21, 22]. While the water pump is running, turn the adjusting knob clockwise to increase the pressure or counterclockwise to decrease it to the target of 2-7 bar, depending on drilling conditions [21, 23]. To ensure adequate flushing, the minimum inlet pressure to the drill rig must be 5 bar, and an optional 15 bar pressure relief valve can be installed before the flushing circuit to manage high-pressure peaks [24]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the proper pre-charge pressure setpoints for the rock drill accumulators?
questions.answer: The accumulators must be filled to their specified pressures to prevent cavitation or explosion risks [17, 18]. The correct gas pre-charge filling pressures are 50 bar for the high-pressure accumulator, 4 bar for the low-pressure accumulator, and 30 bar for the stabilizer accumulator [19]. This should be verified using a pressure gauge from the rock drill's special toolkit before the rock drill is installed [19, 20]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the diesel engine overspeed warning siren (H24) to activate and what is the operator response?
questions.answer: The indicator light flashes and a warning siren beeps if the diesel engine speed exceeds 2500 rpm [1-4]. The operator should immediately reduce the engine speed to prevent damage. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should I check if the diesel engine will not start?
questions.answer: Check that the battery isolation switch is in the ON position, the parking brake is engaged, the drive selector is in the middle position, and all emergency stop devices have been reset. You must also ensure that the battery circuit main fuse F11, fuses F12 and F13, and the automatic fuse on the main switchgear cabinet doors have not tripped, and verify that the fire suppression system is not preventing the engine from starting [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the troubleshooting procedure if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation pressure remains persistently low or insufficient during drilling, which can lead to underfeed and decreased penetration [10, 11].
*   **Cause:** The LS-pressure relief valve (65) of the rotation control block may be faulty, feed pressure might be too low, or the rock drill rotation motor may be leaking [10-12].
*   **Corrective Action:** Adjust the max pressure of the rotation circuit using the LS-pressure relief valve (65) to 180 bar; clean, repair, or replace it if it fails to adjust [10]. If the issue is underfeed, adjust the feed deviation valve (216) so rotation pressure sets between 80-100 bar (or 100-120 bar for the RD314) [11]. If the problem persists and feed pressure (19-21 bar) is normal, replace the leaking rock drill rotation motor [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I test the CAN bus termination resistors using a multimeter?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected and the **battery main switch S1** in position **0**, measure the total resistance between **CAN_HI** and **CAN_LO**. A normal reading is approximately **60 Ω ±5 Ω** (resulting from two **120 Ω** termination resistors at both ends of the bus) [1, 2]. If the measurement is **< 50 Ω**, there is a short-circuit; if it is **> 100 Ω**, one end of the bus is interrupted or a resistor is faulty; and if it reads **~40...50 kΩ**, the bus is interrupted at multiple points or both resistors are missing or faulty [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined circuit pressures for the percussion and rotation systems?
questions.answer: For the standard RD520 rock drill on the DD321, the maximum percussion pressure is 220 bar [1]. Based on factory settings, the full-power percussion pressure is generally set to 210 bar (when using a TF 500 feed), half-power percussion is set to 100 bar, and the minimum allowable percussion pressure is 120 bar [4, 5]. The maximum pressure of the rotation circuit is regulated at 180 bar [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the consequences and required actions if the hydraulic receiver or shank lubrication oil level is too low (H602)?
questions.answer: The indicator light will illuminate and the power pack, compressor, and water pumps will stop (the system uses a three-second delay to prevent false alarms caused by the drill rig rocking) [13-17]. If the indicator light blinks instead of staying solid, it specifically means the oil level in the shank lubrication is too low [13-17]. To resolve this, the operator must add a sufficient amount of oil to the respective tank and reset the control system by pushing the acknowledgement button (S505) [13-17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are CAN bus faults initially identified on the system?
questions.answer: Any fault on the CAN bus must first be identified using the instructions and notifications on the operator's display panel, which will indicate whether the bus nodes are in a fault mode or switched off [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I diagnose a power pack that will not start?
questions.answer: Check the indicator panel for any alarms, ensure the power supply is connected, and verify the main switch is on. Additionally, make sure all emergency stop devices are reset, the water pump or compressor is not running, and that none of the circuit breakers on the main switchgear cabinet door have tripped [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the SLU oil flow/air pressure error indicator light (H72) to activate, and how is it reset?
questions.answer: The Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) monitors oil flow and air pressure. If no oil flow is detected, or if the air pressure for the shank lubrication falls below 2.8 bar, the H72 indicator light comes on and automatic drilling is immediately stopped [24, 25]. The operator can reset this error by restarting the percussion or rotation and verifying whether the lubrication successfully starts again [24, 25]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What happens if the low water pressure indicator (H601) comes on, and how does the operator resolve it?
questions.answer: If the water pressure drops below 2.8 bar for more than four seconds, the pressure control system will stop the drilling operations [5-8]. The operator can turn off the indicator light and continue drilling normally by pressing the acknowledgement button (S505) [5-8]. However, if the water pressure remains below 2.8 bar for over a minute, the water pump stops; in this case, the operator must press the acknowledgement button (S505) and then restart the water pump using its switch (S501) [5-8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the battery main switch (S1) and the starter isolator switch (S2)?
questions.answer: The battery main switch (**S1**) disconnects the 24 VDC battery if both **S1** and the tramming panel battery ON/OFF switch are in the OFF position, though it does not disconnect the direct supply from the battery [4]. The starter isolator switch (**S2**) prevents the diesel engine and/or electric motors from starting when it is turned to the OFF position [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What triggers the low air pressure indicator (H609) and how is it addressed?
questions.answer: If the air pressure remains below 2.8 bar for more than 10 seconds, the pressure control system automatically stops the drilling [9-12]. The operator must press the acknowledgement button (S505) to turn off the indicator light and clear the warning [9-12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Why is the rotation speed regulation not working and how can it be fixed?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The rotation speed cannot be adjusted or remains uneven despite using the rotation speed regulating knob, leading to decreased penetration and higher stress on the mechanism [13, 14].
*   **Cause:** The rotation speed regulating valve (59) is faulty, the rotation directional valve (53) is sticking, or the rock drill rotation motor/mechanism is damaged [13, 15, 16].
*   **Corrective Action:** Clean, repair, or replace the rotation speed regulating valve (59) [13]. If this does not work, remove the rotation directional valve (53), clean the spool and housing carefully, and reinstall [15]. If the regulation still fails, refer to the rock drill maintenance manuals to inspect and repair or replace the rock drill rotation motor or mechanism [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the main switch (Q100) and what limitations does it have?
questions.answer: The main switch (**Q100**) cuts off the power supply to the drill rig and can be locked in the '0' position [1, 2]. It features thermal and magnetic tripping to protect the main panel's internal wiring and is equipped with an undervoltage relay that cuts off power if **K106** is activated [3]. However, the main switch does not turn off the voltage at the cable reel or the slip ring unit without a pilot system, nor does it disconnect the carrier's 24 VDC accumulator circuit [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the earth continuity protection relay (K9A)?
questions.answer: The **K9A** electrical protection relay provides earth continuity protection functions (such as pilot monitoring or ground checks) to ensure that the electrical distribution system in the mine operates safely [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot if the soft starter does not start the motor (380V - 575V systems) or the power pack main contactor only clicks (660V - 1000V systems)?
questions.answer: This typically indicates that the supplied power is too low [2]. You should **check the supply voltage from the voltmeter** located on the main switchgear cabinet door [2]. Verify that the voltage remains within the specified range across all operating conditions: during idling, when starting the power packs, and while drilling at full power [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot the system if the percussion is always on when the powerpack or diesel engine is running?
questions.answer: Stop the powerpack and install a pressure gauge to the tank line of the drilling pilot control valves (58), (14), and (31) [2]. Start the powerpack to check the tank line pressure [2]. If the pressure is over 1 bar, check if the tank line is correctly installed or if something is blocking the line [2]. If the pressure is below 1 bar, it is highly likely that the percussion main valve (3), the percussion selector valve (4), or the pilot control valve (14) is sticking [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific CAN bus faults cannot be detected when troubleshooting with a multimeter?
questions.answer: While a multimeter is effective for detecting cable faults, loose connections, and short-circuits, it cannot detect a faulty CAN sensor (sensor signal fault), missing CAN signals, or bit-level signal faults [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the target setpoints for minimum, half-power, and full-power percussion pressures, and how are they adjusted?
questions.answer: The minimum percussion pressure is set to 120 bar and is adjusted using the monitoring valve (18) [8]. The half-power percussion pressure is factory set to 100 bar (adjustable between 80-100 bar) and is calibrated via the percussion half-power pressure relief valve (6) [9, 10]. The full-power percussion pressure is factory set to 210 bar (but may vary between 150-230 bar depending on rock hardness and drill steels) and is adjusted using the percussion full-power pressure relief valve (7) [11, 12]. For all three settings, the adjustment involves loosening the valve's locking nut, turning the adjusting screw to achieve the target pressure on the percussion pressure gauge (11), and then re-tightening the locking nut [8, 10, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC) interface with the CAN bus and how are faults displayed?
questions.answer: The SLC controls the rig's shank lubrication unit and is connected directly to the CAN bus backbone [4, 5]. The physical unit features a diagnostic panel with dedicated LED indicators, including a **CAN-RUN** indicator light and a **CAN-ERR** indicator light, to visually display the communication status [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should I check if automatic drilling stops after 30 seconds?
questions.answer: Check the indicator panel for any active alarms and specifically verify that the shank lubrication fault indicator is not on [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specified hydraulic flow rates for the RD520 rock drill during operation?
questions.answer: When operating at the maximum percussion pressure level and at normal operating temperatures, the expected flow rate for the RD520 rock drill's percussion circuit is 105-115 l/min [6]. The required flow rate for the feed circuit is 4-8 l/min [6]. If the measured flow rates are higher than these specified values, the rock drill and the feed cylinder should be inspected immediately for internal wear or damage [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical components should be checked if the rock drill does not automatically return from the front end?
questions.answer: First, verify the position of **switches S73 and S74**, as the automatic return function will not operate in the manual position [7]. Check the operation of the **front limit pressure switch S80** [7]. Next, test the relays to see if **relays K70 and K71** pull at the front limit, and check if **relay K78** pulls at the front limit with a 6-second delay [7]. Finally, check the operation of the **Y47 return automatics selector valve** at the front limit via its LED indicator; if the LED illuminates correctly, you may need to check the hydraulic system instead [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which electrical components make up the power pack starter block and what are their functions?
questions.answer: The power pack starter block provides starter and overload control [5]. It includes the power pack circuit breakers (**F1** and **F2**), which provide motor protection with phase failure sensitivity and adjustable overload releases to handle current peaks [5]. It also contains the power pack motor contactors (**K1** and **K2**) [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I isolate a faulty termination resistor or locate a break in the bus if the total resistance is incorrect?
questions.answer: Disconnect both termination resistors from the bus and measure each one separately; an intact resistor will measure exactly **120 Ω** [5]. If both resistors are intact, the fault lies within the bus cable itself [5]. You can pinpoint the exact fault location by moving the termination resistor towards the next measuring point (any actuator/node on the bus), disconnecting the bus cable from the actuator, and connecting the termination resistor in its place to test individual segments [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component is responsible for filtering the oil coming directly from the variable displacement pump (1) and what are its specifications?
questions.answer: The pressure filter (8) or (112) filters the hydraulic oil immediately after the variable displacement pump (1) [3, 4]. It has a filtering level of 20 µm abs and is designed for a maximum operating pressure of 420 bar [3]. It is equipped with a clogging indicator (8.1) and a by-pass valve (8.3) [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot when the manually controlled fast feed is not working?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The fast feed movement does not start when turning the control lever of the fast feed pilot control valve (33) forwards or backwards [6, 7].
*   **Cause:** The spool of the feed directional valve (23) is sticking, or the fast feed pilot control valve (33) is faulty [8, 9].
*   **Corrective Action:** Check the pilot control pressure at measuring points M2 and M3; if an approx. 30 bar pressure is present but the feed doesn't work (and gauge 21 shows no reading), remove the front cover of the feed directional valve (23), carefully clean the spool and valve housing, and reinstall [7, 8]. If no pilot pressure is present at the measuring points, replace the faulty fast feed pilot control valve (33) [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the baseline pressure settings for the variable displacement pump, boom, and pilot circuits?
questions.answer: The main pressure relief valve is factory set to 250 bar, while the boom's maximum operating pressure is set to 230 bar [3]. The variable displacement pump's pressure controller is set to 230 bar, with its flow controller set between 22-30 bar [4]. The pilot control pressure for rotation, percussion, flushing, and fast feed is 30 bar, whereas the pilot control pressure specifically for the feed is 19-21 bar [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the Gatekeeper Controller (GSC) and what specific component is used?
questions.answer: The Gatekeeper Controller (GSC) utilizes an **IFM safety-PLC** equipped with a 55-pin connector [3]. It acts as a safety controller for the rig and features 2 x CAN interfaces and an RS232 port, operating within a voltage range of 10 to 32 VDC [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can I determine if a CAN bus short-circuit is connected to the ground or to the supply voltage?
questions.answer: In both scenarios, the resistance measured between **CAN_LO** and **CAN_HI** will still read approximately **60 Ω** [4]. To differentiate the fault, check the voltage levels: if the **CAN_LO** or **CAN_HI** voltage level remains continuously near **0 V**, it is a short-circuit to ground [4]. If the voltage level remains continuously near the **supply voltage (VS)**, it is a short-circuit to the supply voltage [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the rotation speed and direction controlled in the THC561 drilling hydraulics system?
questions.answer: The rotation direction is determined by the rotation pilot control valve (58), while the rotation speed regulating valve (59) sets the rotation speed to the desired value [7]. Based on these inputs, the rotation directional valve (53) controls the actual oil flow to the rotation mechanism/motor (54) [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps if the drilling feed pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Start by checking the operation of the feed pressure regulating valve (20) and/or the feed deviation valve (216) [3]. If these components do not adjust the pressure properly, stop the powerpack, and then clean, repair, or replace the faulty feed pressure regulating valve (20) and/or feed deviation valve (216) [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical components should be tested if drilling does not stop and the rock drill does not automatically return from the front end?
questions.answer: First, check the position of switches S73 and S74, as the automatic return function will not work if they are in the manual position [7]. Check the operation of the front limit pressure switch S80, verify if relays K70 and K71 pull at the front limit, and check if relay K78 pulls at the front limit with a 6-second delay [7]. Finally, check the Y47 operation at the front limit via its LED indicator; if the LED illuminates correctly, the fault is likely within the hydraulic system rather than the electrical system [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the feed directional valve (23) and how is it controlled?
questions.answer: The feed directional valve (23) directs the oil flow to the feed cylinder (28) and the feed mechanism [13]. Its operation and spool position are controlled by pilot pressure received from the feed pilot control valve (31) and the fast feed forwards pilot valve (33) [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the power pack unexpectedly stops while running?
questions.answer: Check the indicator panel for alarms and verify that the water pump and compressor control switches are in position 1 (or that the inlet pressure is sufficient if using external water/air). Also, confirm that the pilot circuit is functional, all emergency stops are reset, and no circuit breakers on the main switchgear cabinet door have tripped [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component functions as the Tramming GUI (VG) and what are its specifications?
questions.answer: The Tramming GUI (VG) uses an **EPEC 6107** PanelPC, which features a 7" LCD resistive color touch display [2]. It operates on a Linux system and includes 2 x CAN 2.0 B communication interfaces, along with Ethernet, RS232, and USB 2.0 ports [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the anti-jamming pressure calibrated and what is its default setpoint?
questions.answer: The factory setting for the anti-jamming pressure is 120 bar (or 140 bar for the RD314 rock drill), though it can be adjusted between 110 and 140 bar according to the rock type [14]. To calibrate, loosen the locking nut of the anti-jamming valve (34), turn the adjusting screw fully closed, and then open it exactly 2 turns [15]. Disconnect and plug the rotation hoses to prevent the drill rod from rotating, start the powerpack, and adjust the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) until the rotation pressure gauge reads the 120 bar target [15, 16]. Finally, adjust the anti-jamming valve (34) until it directs a feed pilot control pressure of approximately 19-21 bar to measuring point M3, and lock the adjusting screw [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose the hydraulic system when the percussion pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Begin by checking if the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve or the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve is stuck, and clean or replace them as necessary [6, 7]. You can also diagnose blocked LS-line orifices by starting the power pack, turning the percussion on, and moving the boom; if the boom functions are normal but the percussion pressure remains low, the orifices are likely partly blocked [7, 8]. Additionally, verify if any of the shuttle valves in the LS-line are leaking [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the correct procedure if the SB40 or SB40NV boom will not swing sideways?
questions.answer: This issue generally means the boom swing pillar plunger valve is stuck or the hose running from the plunger valves to the hydraulic oil tank is clogged [7]. Check the operation of the valves and verify the adjustment values of the one-way restrictor valves [7]. The one-way restrictor valves must be adjusted by first closing them fully, and then opening them a 1/4 to 3/4 turn [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What could cause all boom hydraulic functions to be slow or not work at all, and how is this diagnosed?
questions.answer: This issue can be caused by a low hydraulic oil level, incorrect oil viscosity, or leaks in the hydraulic circuit [1, 2]. To diagnose a pressure-relief valve malfunction, connect a pressure gauge (max. 250 bar) to the line between the control valve and the hydraulic pump using a T-fitting to see if the required 210 bar operating pressure is reached [1-3]. To diagnose a faulty oil pump, cross-connect the supply and LS lines of the pump to another boom to verify if the other boom also stops working properly [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are issues diagnosed when the pilot control valves for drilling (S70, S71, and S72) do not stay on?
questions.answer: Begin by checking the power supply fuse and the power supply feed cable. Next, check if the front limit pressure switch S80 is activated, and verify the operation of relays K77, K74, K129, and K70. If only S72 does not stay on while S70 and S71 operate normally, check that component V18 is fitted [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a short-circuit or an interrupted CAN bus using resistance measurements?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected, measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO [2, 3]. A measurement of < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [3]. A reading of > 100 Ω means one end of the bus is interrupted or the termination resistors are faulty, while a reading of ~40...50 kΩ means the bus is interrupted at multiple points or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which module acts as the Carrier Master (CM) and how is it connected to the CAN network?
questions.answer: The **SCU module** (machine control computer) is used as the Carrier Master (CM) in the control system [6]. It connects to the network using two CAN I/O connectors: connector **XJ1 (CAN1)** connects to the rear carrier bus, while connector **XJ2 (CAN2)** connects to the engine/driveline bus [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components handle the return oil filtering and cooling before it enters the hydraulic oil tank?
questions.answer: Return oil from various actuators is gathered in a collecting piece (7) or (115) [4, 9]. From there, it flows through the oil cooler (5) or (315) (such as the OW-cooler) to remove heat, and then passes through the return oil filter (4.3) or (113), which has a filtering level of 10 µm abs, before finally entering the hydraulic oil tank (110) [4, 9-12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should I do if the power pack unexpectedly stops working?
questions.answer: Begin by checking the indicator panel for any active alarms and verify that the water pump and compressor control switches are set to **position 1** (or that inlet pressure is sufficient if using external water/air) [3]. Ensure that **none of the circuit breakers** on the main switchgear cabinet door have tripped, that all emergency stop devices are reset, and that the pilot circuit is fully functional [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are CAN bus fault codes displayed and interpreted on the operator's LCD screen?
questions.answer: When a new diagnostic trouble code (DTC) is received, the LCD automatically shifts to the CAN fault code screen [1, 2]. It displays an open book symbol on the left side of the screen, the code name in the middle, and the code number from the buffer on the right-hand side [1, 2]. The buffer breaks down the fault into components such as the Suspect Parameter Number (SPN) (e.g., 111 for Coolant level), the Occurrence Count (OC), and the Failure Mode Identifier (FMI) (e.g., 01 indicating a specific fault like low coolant level or faulty wiring) [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the percussion to always be on when the powerpack or diesel engine is running?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The percussion mechanism operates continuously anytime the powerpack or engine is running, regardless of the control lever position [20, 21].
*   **Cause:** Tank line pressure might be blocked or incorrectly installed, the percussion main valve (3) or selector valve (4) is sticking, or the percussion pilot control valve (14) is leaking/sticking [22, 23].
*   **Corrective Action:** Verify that the tank line pressure of the pilot control valves (58, 14, 31) is below 1 bar [20, 22]. Test measuring point M9; if there is no pressure, clean, repair, or replace valves (3) or (4) [22, 23]. If M9 shows a pressure reading, replace the sticking percussion pilot control valve (14) [23]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How should I proceed if the percussion full-power maximum pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Check the operation of the percussion full-power pressure relief valve (7) and the monitoring valve (18) [5]. If the valves are faulty, stop the powerpack, and clean, repair, or replace valve (5) and/or (18) [6]. If boom functions are normal but percussion pressure remains low, the load-sensing line orifice (9) may be blocked [6]. To fix this, stop the powerpack, remove the adapter from port 9 of the feed and percussion control block, and verify that the orifice (9) is properly seated at the bottom of port 9, tightening it carefully if it has loosened [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system react if the engine coolant temperature gets too high?
questions.answer: The system will issue a warning if the coolant temperature exceeds 105 °C [26]. If the temperature rises further and exceeds 110 °C, the system issues a warning and will force an automatic engine shutdown in 30 seconds to protect the engine [26]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the variable displacement pump (1) in the drilling hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The variable displacement pump (1) delivers the required amount of hydraulic oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulic systems, as well as to the optional stabilizer and power extractor [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the correct procedure to measure the CAN bus normal operation voltage levels, and what values indicate a short-circuit?
questions.answer: The control system must be on to measure voltage. Turn the **battery main switch S1** to position **1** [3]. Measure the voltage between **CAN_HI and GND**, and then between **CAN_LO and GND** [3]. A fully intact CAN bus will return measurement results of **2.5 V ±0.2 V** [3]. If the measurement results are **< 1 V or > 4 V**, there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should I do if the drilling feed pressure is too low?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The rock drill jumps and shakes, penetration speed decreases, and the chuck or extension sleeve of the drill rod wears faster [1].
*   **Cause:** The feed pressure regulating valve (20) or feed deviation valve (216) may be faulty, the feed cylinder may be leaking, or the feed pilot control valve (31) may be defective [2-5].
*   **Corrective Action:** Check and adjust the feed pressure regulating valve (20) and feed deviation valve (216). If they do not adjust, plug the feed pressure line to test if the feed cylinder is faulty and replace the cylinder if necessary [2-4]. If the issue persists, clean, repair, or replace the faulty regulating/deviation valves, or check measuring point M1 and replace the feed pilot control valve (31) if the pressure is not approximately 19-21 bar [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose whether a CAN wire is short-circuited to ground or to the supply voltage?
questions.answer: In both situations, the resistance measured between CAN_LO and CAN_HI will remain approximately 60 Ω [4]. To determine the fault, check the voltage level: if the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level remains continuously near 0 V, it is a short-circuit to ground [4]. If the voltage level remains continuously near the supply voltage (VS), it is a short-circuit to the supply voltage [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the drilling feed pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Start the powerpack, lock the control lever of the feed pilot control valve to the front position, and check if the feed pressure regulating valve and/or the feed deviation valve correctly adjusts the pressure [10, 11]. If they do not adjust, stop the powerpack, plug the feed pressure line, and test again to determine if the feed cylinder itself is faulty [12, 13]. If the valve still does not adjust, the valve is faulty and must be cleaned, repaired, or replaced [13]. You should also verify the feed pilot control pressure, which needs to be approximately 19-21 bar [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I fix the percussion system if it is not working at all?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The percussion mechanism does not operate when the percussion control lever (14) is locked into the rear position [17, 18].
*   **Cause:** The rock drill may be faulty, the percussion main valve (3) or percussion selector valve (4) may be sticking, or the load-sensing line orifice (9) may be blocked [17-19].
*   **Corrective Action:** If the pressure gauge (11) shows a reading but percussion doesn't work, repair or replace the rock drill [17, 18]. If there is no pressure reading, clean, repair, or replace the percussion main valve (3) or selector valve (4) [18]. If percussion starts only partially and boom functions are normal, remove the adapter from port 9, check the orifice (9), clear the hole, and carefully remount it [18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system indicate clogged pressure or return oil filters (H611 and H607), and do they stop drilling operations?
questions.answer: The powerpack pressure filter clogged indicator (H611) or the return oil filter clogged indicator (H607) will light up if the respective filter has become dirty and needs to be replaced [9-12, 18-21]. These warnings serve as notices and do not stop drilling functions [9-12, 18-21]. To avoid false alarms caused by thick, cold oil, this monitoring system is temporarily bypassed when the oil temperature is below 30 °C [9-12, 18-21]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should I do if all hydraulic functions on the SB boom are slow or not working at all?
questions.answer: First, check the oil level and ensure the oil viscosity is correct [1]. If the hydraulic circuit is not leaking, the control valve pressure-relief valve may be functioning incorrectly, preventing the system from reaching the required 210 bar operating pressure [1]. Measure the pressure by connecting a pressure gauge (max. 250 bar) to the line between the control valve and the hydraulic pump using a T-fitting [1]. Malfunctions are usually caused by dirt blocking the cartridge valve; to repair this, remove the cartridge valve, replace its O-rings, and carefully clean it with compressed air before reinstalling [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the electrical system if the pilot control valves for drilling (S70, S71, and S72) do not stay on?
questions.answer: Check the power supply fuse and the power supply feed cable [6]. You should also check if the front limit pressure switch S80 is activated, and verify the correct operation of relays K77, K74, K129, and K70 [6, 7]. If only S72 does not stay on while S70 and S71 are functioning normally, verify that component V18 is fitted [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the most common causes of CAN bus cabling faults?
questions.answer: Common reasons for cabling faults include cable, wire, or connector interruptions, short-circuits, and installation errors, such as internal termination resistors that are loose or incorrectly connected [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the charging indicator light (H6) signify and what is the operator's required response?
questions.answer: The H6 indicator light comes on if the alternator is not working [27]. The operator must switch off the engine immediately and identify the cause of the charging failure [27]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the pilot control valves for drilling (S70, S71, and S72) do not stay on?
questions.answer: Start by checking the power supply fuse and the power supply feed cable [5, 6]. Next, verify if the **front limit pressure switch S80** is activated, and check the proper operation of **relays K77, K74, K129, and K70** [5, 6]. *Note:* If S72 specifically does not stay on even though S70 and S71 are functioning, check to ensure that component **V18** is fitted [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the hydraulic fluid filtration requirements and purity standards?
questions.answer: The hydraulic system utilizes a pressure filtration level of 20 µ and a return flow filtration level of 10 µ [1]. Additionally, the hydraulic oil tank is equipped with an air breather filter that has a filtering capacity of 5 µm [2]. To ensure optimal system health, the manufacturer recommends maintaining a hydraulic fluid purity class of 18/16/13 in accordance with the ISO 4406 (c) standard [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the VIU module within the CAN bus system?
questions.answer: The **VIU module** functions as a general-purpose input unit for the user interface and as a voltage input unit for applications (such as Main Switchgear Sensors and the Tramming controller) [8]. It operates as a **CANopen slave**, utilizing predefined configurable CANopen profiles to provide I/O reading and writing services to a CANopen client [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a rock drill that does not automatically return from the front end and drilling does not stop?
questions.answer: Check the position of switches S73 and S74, as the return function does not work in the manual position. Verify the operation of the front limit pressure switch S80, check if relays K70 and K71 pull at the front limit, and check if relay K78 pulls at the front limit with a 6-second delay. Finally, check the LED indicator for the Y47 return automatics selector valve operation at the front limit [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the diagnosis if the power pack main contactor only clicks (in 660V - 1000V systems) or the soft starter does not start the motor (in 380V - 575V systems)?
questions.answer: This fault indicates that the supplied power is too low. You can diagnose this by checking the supply voltage from the voltmeter located on the main switchgear cabinet door, ensuring the voltage remains within the specified range during idling, starting the power packs, and drilling at full power [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What conditions cause the transmission failure/malfunction warning light (H40) to illuminate?
questions.answer: This indicator light illuminates to warn the operator that the transmission oil pressure is too low, or that the transmission oil temperature is too high [22, 23]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What role does the breather (4.2) play in the hydraulic oil receiver?
questions.answer: The breather (4.2) filters air going to and from the hydraulic oil receiver (4) during oil level changes [5]. It features a 5 µm filter element and is equipped with two check valves that maintain a 0.3 bar overpressure in the tank while preventing oil from spilling out, even if the machine tips over [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD321 Technical Manual)

questions.question: You connect a pressure gauge to the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) and run the feed against the rear end stopper, but the pressure does not reach the expected 210 bar. After verifying that the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.15) is clean and functioning, what two shock/anti-cavitation valves and what specific compensator component must you check next in the drilling control valve block?
questions.answer:
If the pressure at the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) fails to reach approximately **210 bar** and the **electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.15)** is confirmed to be working, you must check the following components based on Section 6.9 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" of the "Drilling Hydraulics DD322i" manual (pages 65–66) [1-3]:

**1. Shock/Anti-cavitation valves**
You must check, clean, and (if necessary) replace the following two valves [4]:
*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.23)** [4]
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.22)** [4]

**2. Compensator Component**
If the shock/anti-cavitation valves are not the issue, you must check the **feed line pressure compensator (20.19)** using the following step-by-step sequence [4]:
1. Remove the pilot control block from the drilling control valve block [4].
2. Remove the compensator spool and spring from the drilling control valve block [4].
3. Clean and check the condition of the spool and the spring. Replace the spool and/or spring, if necessary [3].
4. Install the spool, the spring, and the pilot control block carefully back into the drilling control valve block [3]. 

*Note: The required tightening torque for the 4 pilot control block Allen screws is **10 Nm*** [3].

questions.question: When troubleshooting uneven rotation of the drill rod, you measure the pilot pressure at measuring connector YS while the power pack is running loaded. The pressure reads significantly lower than the required 35–50 bar range. Which three specific components (including a filter and two internal valves) must you check, clean, and potentially replace to restore proper internal pilot pressure?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.13 ("Rotation speed adjustment is not working") of the "Drilling Hydraulics DD322i" manual (pages 68–69), if the pilot pressure measured at connector **YS** is outside the required **35…50 bar** range while the power pack is running loaded, you must check the following three specific components [1, 2]:

1. **Pilot oil filter (20.24)**
2. **Pressure relief valve of the internal pilot pressure supply (20.26)**
3. **Pressure reducing valve of the internal pilot pressure supply (20.27)**

**Step-by-step diagnostic sequence:**
1. Connect a pressure gauge to measuring connector **YS** to check the pilot pressure [1]. 
2. Verify the pressure reading. The pilot pressure should be **35…50 bar** when the power pack is running loaded (note: the pressure might be slightly lower when the power pack is running unloaded) [1].
3. If the pressure differs from this value, check, clean and, if necessary, replace the **pilot oil filter (20.24)**, the **pressure relief valve of the internal pilot pressure supply (20.26)**, and the **pressure reducing valve of the internal pilot pressure supply (20.27)** [2].

questions.question: After replacing the minimum pressure valve on the compressor, you need to adjust it to the correct pressure setting of 5 bar +/- 0.2 bar. What is the exact distance, measured with a caliper gauge, that you must set from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body under the discharge valve cover?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the exact distance you must set from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body (or distance "A") using a caliper gauge is **9.5 mm** [1, 2].

According to the **CTN27D-H Screw Compressor manual** (Section 7.11, "Adjusting the minimum pressure valve"), the general procedure is [2]:
1. Stop the compressor and ensure the network is unpressurized.
2. Open the discharge valve cover and turn the adjustment screw located under it using a wrench.
3. Using a caliper gauge, set the distance from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body to **9.5 mm**.
4. Check the minimum pressure with a pressure gauge and adjust the preset value by turning the adjustment screw while the compressor is running or pressurized.

For the specific **DD322i Flushing Circuit / Maintenance** procedure (Section 8.2.17 / 5.13.17), the step-by-step sequence is [1, 3-5]:
1. Perform the required procedures prior to compressor maintenance. 
2. Disconnect the hose **(1)** from the T connection **(2)** and keep the hose disconnected during the adjustment.
3. Loosen the locking nut **(3)** of the adjusting screw **(4)**.
4. Set distance A to exactly **9.5 mm**.
5. Start the compressor.
6. From the drilling display, check that the **B611P** value is **5 bar ± 0.2 bar**, and ensure the **B605P** value is lower than the B611P value.
7. If necessary, continue turning the adjusting screw until the B611P value reaches exactly **5 bar ± 0.2 bar**.
8. Tighten the locking nut **(3)**.
9. Stop the compressor. 
10. Start the compressor again to re-check the B611P value and adjust further if necessary.

questions.question: You are diagnosing a CAN bus fault on a DD322i. The total resistance measured between CAN_HI and CAN_LO is normal (approx. 60 Ω), but the voltage measured between CAN_LO and GND is continuously reading near the supply voltage (VS). What specific fault condition does this indicate on the CAN network?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Control System DD322i" manual, Section 8.6.3 "CAN bus cabling faults" (page 101), this specific combination of measurements indicates a **short-circuit between the CAN wire and the supply voltage** [1, 2]. 

The manual specifies that during this specific fault condition:
*   The voltage level of CAN_LO or CAN_HI will read continuously near the supply voltage (VS) [1].
*   The resistance measured between CAN_LO and CAN_HI will still show a normal value of approximately 60 Ω [1].

To properly verify these voltage readings, the manual outlines the following step-by-step procedure in Section 8.6.2 "Measuring the CAN bus voltage level" (page 100):
1. Turn the battery main switch (S1) to position 1 [3]. *(Note: The control system must be ON during voltage measurement, whereas resistance measurements must be done with the power disconnected)* [3, 4].
2. Find the CAN bus connection diagrams from the electrical diagrams [3].
3. Measure the voltage between CAN_HI and GND, and between CAN_LO and GND, and write the results down [3]. 

Under normal conditions with no load on the bus, the expected voltage reading for both CAN_HI and CAN_LO to ground is 2.5 VDC ±0.2 V [3, 5]. Readings of < 1 V or > 4 V confirm the presence of a short-circuit on the CAN bus [3].

questions.question: While checking the steering pressure on the C300 carrier, you attach a pressure gauge to the steering and brake control manifold's pressure measuring connector (MPS) and turn the steering to the extreme position. At 1500 rpm engine speed, what is the exact expected pressure reading you should adjust the steering circuit main pressure relief valve to achieve?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, the exact expected pressure reading you should adjust the steering circuit main pressure relief valve to achieve is **220 bar** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 6.1.16 "Checking the steering pressure" in the Carrier manual and Section 5.7.16 in the Maintenance manual, this check should be performed when the oil is at operating temperature and the diesel engine is running at 1500 rpm (manual throttle - medium) [3, 4].

Here is the step-by-step sequence for checking and adjusting the steering pressure:

1. Attach a pressure gauge to the steering and brake control manifold's pressure measuring connector **(MPS)** [1, 2].
2. Start the engine [1, 2]. 
3. Push the steering stick forward or pull it backward until the articulation reaches the extreme position [1, 2].
4. The pressure level should be approximately **220 bar** [1, 2].
5. If needed, adjust the main pressure relief valve **(1)** to decrease or increase the pressure level as follows [1, 2]:
   * a) Loosen the locking nut **(2)** [1, 2].
   * b) Turn the adjusting screw **(3)** counterclockwise to decrease or clockwise to increase the pressure level [1, 2].
   * c) Tighten the locking nut **(2)** [1, 2].
6. Move the steering stick until the rig is straightened [1, 2].
7. Shut down the engine [1, 2].
8. Remove the pressure gauge [1, 2].

questions.question: When adjusting the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve, what is the required pressure setting at measuring point (1) for the standard DD322i versus the DU422i-W model?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 3.2 "Adjusting the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve" in the Hose Reel manual (page 14), the required pressure setting at measuring point (1) is **80 bar** for the standard model and **83 bar** for the DU422i-W model [1, 2].

The step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows:
1. Start the diesel engine and let it idle [3]. 
2. Connect the pressure gauge to the water hose reel measuring point (1) of the rear carrier control block [3].
3. Turn the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve locking nut (2) counterclockwise to loosen it [1].
4. Pressurize the system (e.g., by raising the jack carefully against the stopper) [1].
5. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (3) clockwise or counterclockwise to adjust the pressure to **80 bar** (or **83 bar** for the DU422i-W) [1].
6. Lock the adjusting screw (3) with the locking nut (2) by turning it clockwise [1].
7. Check the pressure value again and re-adjust, if necessary [1].
8. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point (1) [1].

questions.question: To properly adjust the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (1) using the pressure measuring connector (MP), what specific pressure value must the pressure controller (3) be set to before loosening the main valve's adjusting screw until the pressure drops to the final 270 bar target?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.3 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve" in the "Drilling Hydraulics DD322i" manual, the pressure controller (3) must be set to exactly **280 bar** before you loosen the main valve's adjusting screw to drop the pressure to the final 270 bar target [1, 2]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this procedure [1-3]:

1. Stop the power pack [3]. 
2. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (1) [3].
3. Tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (1) almost to its end (over 270 bar) [3].
4. Remove the caps from the flow controller (2) and the pressure controller (3) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump and loosen the locking nuts of their adjusting screws [3].
5. Open the adjusting screws of the pressure controller (3) and the flow controller (2) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [1].
6. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring connector (MP) [1].
7. Start the power pack [1].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (2) fully closed (clockwise). *Note: The pump is now operating at constant pressure* [1].
9. **Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (3) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows 280 bar** [1, 2].
10. Loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (1) until adjusting begins to take effect. The valve will begin to fizz when restricting the pressure, and the pressure value on the pressure gauge will drop to **270 bar** [2].
11. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (1) [2].
12. Adjust the values of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) as instructed in the "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" section [2].
13. Stop the power pack [2]. *(Note: Ensure the oil flow does not pass through the main pressure relief valve for a long time as this will cause the hydraulic system to heat up)* [4].

questions.question: After attaching a pressure gauge to port LS and adjusting the rotation main relief/bypass valve (1) to 200 bar, how much further must the adjusting screw be turned to achieve the final adjustment value of 230 bar?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.5 "Adjusting the rotation main relief / bypass valve" in the "Drilling Hydraulics DD322i" manual (page 53), after adjusting the pressure to 200 bar, you must turn the adjusting screw **clockwise half a turn** (which equals an additional 30 bar) to achieve the final adjustment value of 230 bar [1].

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this procedure as outlined in the manual:

1. Plug the rotation work line A from the rock drill or feed connection plate [2].
2. Attach a pressure gauge to port LS [2].
3. Remove the cover from the pilot valve of the rotation main relief/bypass valve (1) [1].
4. Loosen (counterclockwise) the adjusting screw of the valve (1) [1].
5. Start the power pack [1].
6. Start rotation in the counterclockwise direction [1].
7. Turn the adjusting screw clockwise to adjust the pressure to 200 bar [1].
8. Stop rotation and stop the power pack [1].
9. **Turn the adjusting screw clockwise half a turn (equals 30 bar) and thus the total adjustment value is 230 bar** [1].
10. Reinstall the cover and remove the pressure gauge [1].

questions.question: What specific values must the "noAirflowBlowdown" parameters be temporarily set to in order to prevent the blowdown valve (4) from opening while adjusting the modulation control valve to reach an 8 bar B611P reading?
questions.answer:
To prevent the blowdown valve (4) from opening while adjusting the modulation control valve (3), the "noAirflowBlowdown" parameters must be temporarily set to **0 bar** and **9.5 bar** [1-3]. 

According to Section 8.2.18 of the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (page 57) and Section 5.13.18 of the *Maintenance Manual DD322i* (pages 268–269), the exact step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows [1-5]:

1. Perform the necessary procedures prior to compressor maintenance [2, 5].
2. Loosen the locking nut (1) of the adjusting screw (2) [2, 5].
3. Loosen the adjustment screw (2) of the modulation control valve (3) [1, 2].
4. Temporarily set the `noAirflowBlowdown` parameter values to **0 bar** and **9.5 bar** to prevent the blowdown valve (4) from opening during the adjustment [1-3].
5. Start the compressor and water pump [1, 3].
6. Turn the adjusting screw (2) until the **B611P** pressure value on the drilling display reads exactly **8 bar** [1, 3].
7. Tighten the locking nut (1) [1, 3].
8. Stop the water pump and compressor [1, 3].
9. Set the `noAirflowBlowdown` parameters back to their original values [1, 3].

questions.question: While the engine is running at 1500 rpm, what target pressure should be achieved at measuring connector MPS when adjusting the steering circuit main pressure relief valve?
questions.answer:
The target pressure that should be achieved at measuring connector **MPS** is **220 bar** [1].

According to Section 4.6.3 ("Adjusting steering circuit main pressure relief valve") in the Carrier manual (pages 66–67), the step-by-step sequence for making this adjustment is as follows:

1. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **(MPS)** [2].
2. Loosen the locking nut **(1)** of the main pressure relief valve **(2)** and turn the adjusting screw **(3)** counterclockwise fully open [2].
3. Start the diesel engine [2].
4. Turn the pressurizing screw **(4)** clockwise to the down position to pressurize the carrier hydraulics [2].
5. Run the engine at **1500 rpm** [2].
6. Turn the adjusting screw **(3)** clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge is exactly **220 bar** [1, 2].
7. Tighten the locking nut **(1)** [1].
8. Run the engine at idle [1].
9. Turn the pressurizing screw **(4)** counterclockwise to the up position to de-pressurize the carrier hydraulics [1].
10. Shut down the engine [1].
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **(MPS)** [1].

Additionally, Section 5.7.16 ("Checking the steering pressure") in the Maintenance and Operator manuals (pages 229–230) notes that you can also check this pressure by pushing the steering stick forward or pulling it backward until the articulation reaches its extreme position while the engine is running at 1500 rpm [3, 4]. If the pressure needs adjustment from there, you loosen locking nut **(2)**, turn adjusting screw **(3)** to reach **220 bar**, and retighten the nut [4].

questions.question: What is the specified parallel coverage area for the SB55i boom, and what is the total expected transport weight of the DD322i drill rig depending on its options?
questions.answer: According to the equipment specifications, the parallel coverage area for the SB55i boom is **55.7 m²** [1]. The total expected transport weight of the DD322i drill rig is **21 500 kg**, which may vary depending on the specific options installed [2].

questions.question: What are the exact displacement capacities (in cc) for the percussion and feed pump compared to the air conditioning/combi-cooler pump within the standard HPP555 powerpack system?
questions.answer: Within the standard HPP555 powerpack system, the exact displacement capacity for the percussion and feed pump is **112 cc** [1]. In comparison, the displacement capacity for the air conditioning / combi-cooler pump is **41 cc / 33 cc** [1].

questions.question: In the rear carrier main components layout diagram, what specific assemblies or components are identified by numbers 2, 6, and 10?
questions.answer:
In the detailed layout for the rear section of the carrier (Section 3.2.1 of the Maintenance and Operator manuals, pages 94–95), the specific assemblies and components identified by numbers 2, 6, and 10 are:

*   **2:** Hydraulic oil receiver [1, 2]
*   **6:** MQ cabinet [1, 2]
*   **10:** Water regulation assembly [1, 2]

Additionally, if referring to the general "Main Components" layout diagram for the entire Drill Carrier C300 (Section 3.1 of the Carrier manual, page 15), those numbers identify the following assemblies:

*   **2:** Rear axle [3]
*   **6:** Brake assembly [3]
*   **10:** Gardan shafts [3]

questions.question: When configuring the system for either the RD520 or RDX5 rock drill, what is the specific difference in their maximum percussion rates in Hz, and what exact pressure value must the pressure controller (B) on the variable displacement pump (1) be set to for both models during normal full-power drilling?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, here is the information regarding the percussion rates and pressure settings for the RD520 and RDX5 rock drills:

**Difference in Percussion Rates**
According to the technical specifications, the exact difference in their maximum percussion rates is **7 Hz**. 
*   **RD520 (Standard):** Maximum percussion rate is 74 Hz [1].
*   **RDX5 (Optional):** Maximum percussion rate is 67 Hz [1].

**Pressure Controller Setting**
During normal operation, the pressure controller **(B)**—also referred to as component **(3)**—on the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** must be set to exactly **255 bar** for both the RD520 and RDX5 models [2-4].

If this pressure deviates from the set value (detailed in Section 6.3.2 "Pressure controller value deviates from the set value"), you must adjust it according to the step-by-step sequence found in Section 5.1.2 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" [3-5]. 

The exact adjustment sequence is as follows:
1. Remove the protecting cap from the pressure controller **(3)** and loosen the locking nut of its adjusting screw [6].
2. Open the adjusting screw of the pressure controller **(3)** fully open (counterclockwise) [6].
3. Run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and read the pressure from the pressure filter measuring point [3, 6].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller **(3)** very carefully clockwise while running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the pressure gauge shows the correct **255 bar** pressure value. Avoid a pressure raise above the correct pressure value. If the pressure rises too high, loosen the adjusting screw and wait for the reading to stabilize, as the pressure can drop very slowly [2, 4, 6].
5. Release the boom zoom function [7].
6. Tighten the locking nut of the pressure controller **(3)** adjusting screw [7].
7. After tightening, check the pressure setting again by running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and adjust the pressure again, if necessary [7].

questions.question: While adjusting the modulation control valve to achieve an 8 bar B611P reading on the drilling display, what specific parameter values must the "noAirflowBlowdown" be temporarily set to in order to prevent the blowdown valve (4) from opening during the adjustment?
questions.answer:
To prevent the blowdown valve (4) from opening while adjusting the modulation control valve (3), the "noAirflowBlowdown" parameters must be temporarily set to **0 bar** and **9.5 bar** [1-3]. 

According to Section 8.2.18 of the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (page 57) and Section 5.13.18 of the *Maintenance Manual DD322i* (pages 268–269), the complete step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows:
