1. Perform the procedures prior to compressor maintenance [2, 4].
2. Loosen the locking nut (1) of the adjusting screw (2) [2, 4].
3. Loosen the adjustment screw (2) of the modulation control valve (3) [1, 2].
4. Temporarily set the `noAirflowBlowdown` parameter values to **0 bar** and **9.5 bar** to prevent the blowdown valve (4) from opening during the adjustment [1-3].
5. Start the compressor and water pump [1, 3].
6. Turn the adjusting screw (2) until the **B611P** pressure value on the drilling display reads exactly **8 bar** [1, 3].
7. Tighten the locking nut (1) [1, 3].
8. Stop the water pump and compressor [1, 3].
9. Set the `noAirflowBlowdown` parameters back to their original values [1, 3].

questions.question: During water flushing setup, what exact pressure range must the pressure reducing valve (11) be adjusted to in order to control the feed pressure to the water pump (3), and what is the maximum pressure limit that sensor B230P must remain under?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, the pressure reducing valve **(11)** must be adjusted to lower the feed pressure to **1…7 bar** before the water pump **(3)** [1]. During the specific adjustment procedure, it is set between **2...7 bar** depending on drilling conditions, and the maximum pressure limit measured by sensor **B230P** after the water pump must remain **under 25 bar** [2, 3]. 

According to Section 7.2.6 (Flushing Circuit manual) and Section 5.15.6 (Operator's/Maintenance manuals) "Adjusting the mine's inlet pressure", here is the exact step-by-step sequence [2-4]:

1. Turn the knob **(1)** of the pressure reducing valve fully open.
2. Open the shut-off valve **(2)**.
3. Start the water pump **(3)**.
4. Turn the knob **(1)** to adjust the pressure to **2...7 bar** according to drilling conditions. Turning the knob clockwise increases the pressure and turning counterclockwise decreases the pressure. Check the pressure gauge **(3)** for the value.
5. On the drilling display, select **-> Troubleshooting -> Compressor and Water Pump -> B230P** and check that the pressure sensor value is under **25 bar**.

questions.question: A Deutz TCD 3.6 engine throws a DTC P100A 00 5571 0 code. What specific component does this Most Severe Level fault indicate has data above its normal operational range?
questions.answer: Based on the "Deutz engine DTC codes" manual, Section 2.1 "Diagnosis and error codes" (page 15), a DTC P100A 00 5571 0 code indicates that the **Pressure relief valve (PRV)** has data above its normal operational range (Most severe level) [1].

questions.question: According to the accumulator filling instructions, what is the required gas pre-charge filling pressure for the stabilizer accumulator on the RD520 and RD525 rock drill models?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided accumulator maintenance instructions and specifications, the required gas pre-charge filling pressure for the stabilizer accumulator on the RD520 and RD525 rock drill models is **30 bar** [1, 2].

According to Section 3.8.1 "Filling instruction" in the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions* manual (pages 23–25), the step-by-step sequence for filling the accumulator is as follows:

1. Check the condition of the filling valve (2). Replace it if there are any signs of damage [3].
2. Remove the cap **(4)** [3].
3. Screw the elbow adapter **(15)** to the filling valve **(2)** [3].
4. Push the quick coupling sleeve **(6)** onto the quick coupling stem **(5)** [3].
5. Undo the locking nut **(3)** [3].
6. Turn the pressure regulating valve **(11)** open [3].
7. Open the nitrogen bottle valve **(12)**. The gas bottle pressure gauge **(9)** will indicate the pressure in the bottle [3, 4].
8. Adjust the pressure of the stabilizer accumulator to the target 30 bar using the pressure regulating valve **(11)**. The accumulator pressure gauge **(8)** indicates the pressure inside the accumulator [2, 5].
9. Close the filling valve **(2)** by turning the locking nut **(3)** [5].
10. Close the nitrogen bottle valve **(12)** [5].
11. Turn the pressure regulating valve **(11)** open [5].
12. Disconnect the quick couplings **(5)** and **(6)** [5].
13. Release the elbow adapter **(15)** from the filling valve **(2)** [5].
14. Tighten the locking nut **(3)** to a torque of **15 Nm** [6].
15. Refit the cap **(4)** [6]. 

*Note: You must use only nitrogen (N2) to fill a pressure accumulator, and the accumulator must be installed on the rock drill before it is pressurized* [7].

questions.question: When configuring the RDX5 rock drill with the SCR option, what is the required shank length in millimeters, and what specific Sandvik part number (Shank ID) must be utilized for a T38 drill string?
questions.answer: When configuring the RDX5 rock drill with the SCR option, the required shank length is **720 mm** [1]. For a T38 drill string in this specific configuration, you must utilize Shank ID **Sandvik 7304-7668-01** [1]. This specification is detailed in the "Recommended shank lengths" table in Section 3.1.2 of the Cylinder feed TF5i / TFX5i manual [1].

questions.question: You are checking the flow controller (4) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1). When reading the pressure gauges connected to the pressure filter measuring point and the LS-line port PL, what exact pressure difference should you observe to confirm the flow controller is properly adjusted?
questions.answer:
When checking the flow controller **(4)** of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)**, the exact pressure difference you should observe is **30 bar**. This difference is calculated by subtracting the load sensing (LS) line pressure measured at port **PL** from the pump operating pressure measured at the **pressure filter measuring point** [1]. 

According to Sections 5.1.1 and 5.1.2 in the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual (pages 48–49), the step-by-step sequence to check and adjust this flow controller is as follows [1-3]:

**Checking the Flow Controller:**
1. Connect pressure gauges to the LS-line measuring port **(PL)** and to the pump **(1)** **pressure filter measuring point** [1].
2. Start the power pack and read the pressure gauges' values. Check that the pressure difference between the pressure filter and port PL is about **30 bar** [1]. 

**Adjusting the Flow Controller (If Necessary):**
1. Remove the protecting cap from the flow controller **(4)** and loosen the locking nut of its adjusting screw [2].
2. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller **(4)** almost fully open by turning it counterclockwise [3].
3. Read the pressure difference from the connected pressure gauges [3].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller **(4)** very carefully clockwise until the pressure difference is exactly **30 bar** [3]. 
   *(Note: Avoid a pressure difference greater than 30 bar. If the pressure rises too high, loosen the adjusting screw and wait for the reading on the pressure filter measuring point to stabilize, as the pressure can drop very slowly)* [3].
5. Tighten the locking nut of the flow controller **(4)** adjusting screw [4].
6. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure difference again and re-adjust if necessary [4].

questions.question: When operating a standard TF5i feed, what is the maximum specified feed force in kN, and what are the exact maximum working hydraulic pressure limits (in bar) for the forward feed movement compared to the return movement?
questions.answer:
For a standard TF5i feed, the maximum specified feed force is **25 kN** [1]. 

According to Section 3.1.1 "Feed cylinder" in the *Cylinder feed TF5i / TFX5i* manual, the exact maximum working hydraulic pressure limits for the TF5i feed cylinder are as follows:
*   **Forward feed movement:** 180 bar [2]
*   **Return movement:** 250 bar [2]

questions.question: When adjusting the minimum pressure valve on the compressor, what exact distance must be set from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body using a caliper gauge to achieve the target pressure of 5 bar ± 0.2 bar?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the minimum pressure valve on the compressor, the exact distance that must be set from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body using a caliper gauge is **9.5 mm** [1, 2].

According to Section 8.2.17 of the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (pages 56-57), Section 5.13.17 of the *Maintenance Manual DD322i* (pages 268-269), and Section 7.11 of the *CTN27D-H Operating Instructions* (pages 27-28), the complete step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows [1-6]:

1. Perform the procedures prior to compressor maintenance (ensure the compressor is stopped and the network is unpressurized) [2, 5]. 
2. Disconnect the hose **(1)** from the T connection **(2)** and keep the hose disconnected during the adjustment [1, 5].
3. Loosen the locking nut **(3)** of the adjusting screw **(4)** [1, 5].
4. Using a caliper gauge, set the distance (**A**) from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body to exactly **9.5 mm** [1, 2, 5].
5. Start the compressor [1, 5].
6. From the drilling display, check that the **B611P** pressure sensor value is **5 bar ± 0.2 bar** and that the **B605P** value is lower than the B611P value [1, 5].
7. If necessary, turn the adjusting screw while the compressor is running until the **B611P** value reaches the correct target of **5 bar ± 0.2 bar** [1, 4, 5].
8. Tighten the locking nut **(3)** [3, 6].
9. Stop the compressor [3, 6].
10. Start the compressor and check the **B611P** value again. Readjust if necessary [3, 6].

questions.question: In the automatic parallelism system, how does the internal Y-chamber of the specialized three-chamber cylinders interact with the feed tilt or feed swing cylinders during boom lift and swing movements?
questions.answer:
In the automatic parallelism system, the specialized three-chamber cylinders feature chambers A and B, plus a third chamber (Y-chamber) located inside the hollow piston rod [1]. 

According to Section 4.4 ("Three chamber cylinders") of the *Hydraulic cylinders* manual (page 25), when the boom lift or boom swing cylinder's length changes during movement, the volume of this internal Y-chamber also changes [1]. As a result of this volume change, the Y-chamber hydraulically interacts with the feed tilt or feed swing cylinders by either giving oil to or taking oil from them [1]. This direct exchange of oil is what enables the automatic parallelism system to function [1]. 

The manuals also note a critical operational safety detail regarding this interaction: the Y-chamber is completely separate and not connected with chambers A and B of the cylinder [2]. Therefore, the Y-port must never be plugged when the cylinder is in use or being disassembled, as plugging it will cause air pressurization inside the hollow rod chamber and lead to the unexpected ejection of cylinder parts [2, 3].

questions.question: While both the standard TF5i and telescopic TFX5i feed cylinders have a maximum forward feed working pressure of 180 bar, what are their respective maximum working pressure limits for the return movement?
questions.answer:
According to Section 3.1.1 ("Feed cylinder") of the *Cylinder feed TF5i / TFX5i* manual, the maximum working pressure limits for the return movement are as follows:

*   **Standard TF5i feed cylinder:** **250 bar** [1].
*   **Telescopic TFX5i feed cylinder:** **180 bar** [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the combi-cooler / air conditioning pump main relief valve, what specific pressure must be achieved using adjusting screw (3) while the pressure hose (4) is disconnected and plugged?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the combi-cooler / air conditioning pump main relief valve, the specific pressure that must be achieved using the adjusting screw **(3)** is **250 bar** [1].

According to Section 5.7 of the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual, the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows [1, 2]:

1. Attach a pressure gauge to the measuring connector **(1)** [1].
2. Open the locking nut **(2)** of the combi-cooler / air conditioning pump main relief valve [1].
3. Turn the adjusting screw **(3)** fully open (counterclockwise) [1].
4. Disconnect the pressure hose **(4)** and plug the hose [1].
5. Start the power pack 2 [1].
6. Turn the adjusting screw **(3)** clockwise to adjust the pressure to **250 bar** [1].
7. Close the locking nut **(2)** [1].
8. Stop the power pack 2 [1].
9. Re-connect the pressure hose [1].
10. Remove the pressure gauge [1].

questions.question: How do the operational roles of the counterbalance / articulation locking valves (8.1 and 8.2) in the steering and brake control manifold differ between active tramming and when the machine is stationary for drilling?
questions.answer:
Based on the CARRIER manual (Section 4.5.3 "Operation of steering circuit", pages 54–56, and Section 4.3.1 "Components (steering system)", page 31), the operational roles of the counterbalance / articulation locking valves (8.1 and 8.2) adapt depending on the machine's state:

*   **During Active Tramming (Steering Actuated):** 
    When the electro-proportional steering valve (8.6) is actively supplying oil to change the steering angle, the oil pressure from the active working line pilots the opposite counterbalance / articulation locking valve open [1, 2]. For example, when turning right, oil pressure in working line A pilots the B-line counterbalance valve (8.2) open to allow return oil from the steering cylinders (9 and 10) to flow back to the tank connection T [1, 3]. Conversely, when turning left, pressure in working line B pilots the A-line counterbalance valve (8.1) open [2, 4].
*   **During Active Tramming (Steering Not Actuated):** 
    While tramming, if the steering valve (8.6) is not actively being actuated by the joystick, the valves (8.1) and (8.2) act as pressure relief valves to protect the steering cylinders against external loads [5, 6].
*   **Stationary for Drilling (After Tramming):** 
    After the machine has been navigated to its position and is set up for drilling, valves (8.1) and (8.2)—working in conjunction with check valves (8.3 and 8.4)—act purely as articulation locking valves [5, 6]. The purpose of this function is to make the articulation joint stiffer during drilling operations [5, 6].

questions.question: During the adjustment of the SLU air line restrictor valve (2), what specific air pressure reading must be achieved on the control GUI before tightening the locking nut (1)?
questions.answer:
During the adjustment of the SLU air line restrictor valve **(2)**, the specific air pressure reading that must be achieved on the control GUI is **4 bars** [1, 2].

According to Section 9.4 of the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (pages 65-66), the complete step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows [1, 2]:

1. Loosen the locking nut **(1)** of the restrictor valve **(2)** [1].
2. Turn the adjusting screw **(3)** fully open [1].
3. On the GUI, select **-> Troubleshooting -> Shank Lubrication** [1].
4. Start both power packs and compressor [1].
5. Push the button **(4)** to select boom 1 [1].
6. Push the button **(5)** to activate air flushing for boom 1 [1].
7. Push the button **(6)** to select boom 2 [1].
8. Push the button **(5)** to activate air flushing for boom 2 [1].
9. Tighten the adjusting screw **(3)** until the Air pressure reading rises to exactly **4 bars** [1, 2].
10. Tighten the locking nut **(1)** of the restrictor valve [2].
11. Check the Air pressure reading from the GUI again [2]. If the reading has changed from the correct value of **4 bars**, readjust by:
    * a) Loosening the locking nut **(1)** [2].
    * b) Tightening or loosening the adjusting screw **(3)** until the value stabilizes at **4 bars** [2].
    * c) Tightening the locking nut **(1)** again [2].
12. Push the button **(4)** and then push the button **(5)** to deactivate boom 1 air flushing [2].
13. Push the button **(6)** and then push the button **(5)** to deactivate boom 2 air flushing [2].
14. Stop both power packs [2].

questions.question: When performing the boom lift (B26G) and boom swing (B20G) laser calibration, what specific tolerance range must the roll-over joint be positioned within before aligning the laser through the rear and front targets?
questions.answer:
When performing the boom lift (B26G) and boom swing (B20G) laser calibration, the roll-over joint must be positioned to 0° within a specific tolerance range of **-0.03°…+0.03°** [1].

According to Section 7.3 "Boom swing and lift sensor calibration with carrier laser" in the Boom manual, the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Select **-> Maintenance -> Calibration -> Boom Sensors -> Boom swing (laser) / Boom lift (laser)** [1].
2. Select **Go to Calibration** [1].
3. Attach the rear target **(1)** and front target **(2)** to boom 1 [1].
4. Select **Next** [1].
5. Run the roll-over joint to 0° (within the **-0.03°…+0.03°** tolerance) [1].
6. Run the boom extension to the back position (in) [1].
7. Run the feed rail extension to the back position (rear) [1].
8. Switch on the calibration laser [1].
9. Select **Next** [1].
10. Align the boom and feed such that the laser beam goes through the rear target **(1)** and hits the middle of the front target **(2)** [1, 2].
11. Select **Finish** [2].

questions.question: What are the specified measurement ranges for the pressure gauges used to check the charge gas pressure at filling valve (4) for the low-pressure versus high-pressure rock drill accumulators?
questions.answer:
The specified measurement ranges for the pressure gauges used to check the charge gas pressure are **0 to 10 bar for the low-pressure accumulators** and **0 to 100 bar for the high-pressure accumulators** [1].

According to Section 3.3 "Checking the charge gas pressure of a pressure accumulator" in the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions* manual (pages 12–13), the step-by-step sequence for checking the pressure is as follows:

1. Remove the rubber protection cap **(1)** (optional) or the metal cap **(2)** [1].
2. Screw the pressure gauge to the filling valve **(4)** [1].
3. Open the locking nut **(3)** [1].
4. Wait until the gauge pointer stops moving and then check the reading [1]. *(Note: If the reading is low, you must refer to the filling instructions to refill the accumulator [1])*
5. Close the locking nut **(3)** and, using a torque wrench, tighten the locking nut to exactly **15 Nm** [1].
6. Disconnect the gauge from the filling valve **(4)** [1].
7. Install the rubber protection cap **(1)** (optional) or the metal cap **(2)** back to its place [1].

questions.question: During a feed forward movement on a rig equipped with the optional TFX feed, which specific valve (component ID 25.3) in the TFX control block routes the return oil from the TFX cylinder back to the drilling control valve block port B3?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual, the specific valve identified as component ID 25.3 is the **TFX bottom cylinder chamber control valve** [1]. 

According to Section 4.4 "Feed forward" (page 35, under the "*TFX feed (optional)*" subsection), during a feed forward movement, return oil from the TFX feed cylinder (30) flows through the TFX bottom cylinder chamber control valve (25.3) within the TFX control block (25) directly to the drilling control valve block port B3 [2-4].

questions.question: According to the accumulator filling specifications, what is the required gas pre-charge pressure for the stabilizer accumulator on an HL1500 rock drill compared to an RD520 model?
questions.answer:
According to Section 3.8.2 "Filling pressures of accumulators" in the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions* manual (pages 26–27), the required gas pre-charge pressures for the stabilizer accumulators are:

*   **HL1500:** 50 bar [1]
*   **RD520:** 30 bar [1]

Based on Section 3.8.1 "Filling instruction" (pages 23–25), the step-by-step sequence to fill the stabilizer accumulator with nitrogen (N2) is as follows [2-6]:

1. Check the condition of the filling valve (2). The filling valve must be replaced if there are any signs of damage [3].
2. Remove the cap **(4)** [3].
3. Screw the elbow adapter **(15)** to the filling valve **(2)** [3].
4. Push the quick coupling sleeve **(6)** onto the quick coupling stem **(5)** [3].
5. Undo the locking nut **(3)** [3].
6. Turn the pressure regulating valve **(11)** open [3].
7. Open the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve **(12)**. The gas bottle pressure gauge **(9)** will indicate the pressure in the bottle [3, 4].
8. Adjust the pressure of the stabilizer accumulator to the target pressure (50 bar for HL1500, or 30 bar for RD520) using the pressure regulating/control valve **(11)**. The accumulator pressure gauge **(8)** indicates the pressure inside the accumulator [5].
9. Close the filling valve **(2)** by turning the locking nut **(3)** [5].
10. Close the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve **(12)** [5].
11. Turn the pressure regulating valve **(11)** open [5].
12. Disconnect the quick couplings **(5)** and **(6)** [5].
13. Release the elbow adapter **(15)** from the filling valve **(2)** [5].
14. Tighten the locking nut **(3)** to a torque of **15 Nm** [6].
15. Refit the cap **(4)** [6].

*Note: You must use only nitrogen (N2) to fill a pressure accumulator [2], and the accumulator must be installed on the rock drill before it is pressurized [7].*

questions.question: While checking the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1), you attach a pressure gauge to measuring connector M and read a pressure level significantly above the normal 3-5 bar tank pressure while the power pack is running unloaded. If the feed pressure gauge also shows a reading, which specific component in the feed directional valve block should you clean or replace to resolve this issue?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.3.1 "Flow controller value deviates from the set value" in the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual [1, 2], if you observe a pressure level above the normal tank pressure (approximately 3-5 bar or less) at the pressure filter measuring connector (M), and the feed pressure gauge also shows a reading while the power pack is running unloaded, you should clean the **feed valve main spool**. 

If cleaning the feed valve main spool does not resolve the issue, you must replace the entire **drilling control valve block** [2].

The step-by-step troubleshooting sequence for this specific issue is as follows:
1. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure filter measuring connector **(M)** [1].
2. Start the power pack and check the feed pressure gauge and the percussion pressure gauge from the main view of the control system [3].
3. If the feed pressure gauge shows a pressure reading while the power pack is running unloaded and simultaneously the measuring connector **(M)** indicates a pressure level above normal tank pressure, it is likely that the fault is in the feed directional valve block [2].
4. Stop the power pack and clean the **feed valve main spool** [2].
5. If cleaning does not help, replace the **drilling control valve block** [2].

questions.question: During compressor maintenance, you observe that the B611P pressure sensor value on the drilling display is fluctuating outside the required 5 bar ± 0.2 bar range. When adjusting the minimum pressure valve, what exact distance (in mm) must be set from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body using a caliper gauge before re-testing?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the minimum pressure valve, the exact distance that must be set from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body using a caliper gauge is **9.5 mm** [1-3].

According to Section 8.2.17 of the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (pages 56-57), Section 5.13.17 of the *Maintenance Manual DD322i - StageV* (pages 268-269), and Section 7.11 of the *Operating Instructions CTN27D-H* (pages 27-28), the step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Perform the procedures prior to compressor maintenance (ensure the compressor is stopped and the network is unpressurized) [2, 3].
2. Disconnect the hose **(1)** from the T connection **(2)** and keep the hose disconnected during the adjustment [1, 3].
3. Loosen the locking nut **(3)** of the adjusting screw **(4)** [1, 3].
4. Set the distance **A** (from the tip of the adjustment screw to the valve body) to exactly **9.5 mm** [1-3].
5. Start the compressor [1, 3].
6. From the drilling display, check that the **B611P** pressure sensor value is **5 bar ± 0.2 bar** and that the **B605P** pressure sensor value is lower than the B611P value [1, 3].
7. If necessary, turn the adjusting screw while the compressor is running or pressurized until the **B611P** value reaches the correct target of **5 bar ± 0.2 bar** [1, 3, 4].
8. Tighten the locking nut **(3)** [5, 6].
9. Stop the compressor [5, 6].
10. Start the compressor and check the **B611P** value again, readjusting if necessary [5, 6].

questions.question: You are troubleshooting a "Tramming forced stop" alarm and note that the front service brake accumulator charge pressure sensor (B962P) has dropped. According to the brake circuit specifications, at what exact pressure limit (in bar) will the system automatically activate the tramming forced stop and engage the spring-applied brakes?
questions.answer:
According to the brake circuit specifications (Section 5.7.3 "Service brake pressure monitoring" and Section 5.4 "Tramming forced stop"), the system will automatically activate the tramming forced stop when the service brake accumulator charge pressure drops to the exact limit of **75 bar** [1-3].

When the front service brake accumulator charge pressure sensor (**B962P**, also identified as component **23** in the braking system components list) detects that the pressure has dropped to this 75 bar limit, the control system executes the following sequence [1, 4, 5]:

1. A warning light turns on, an alarm message is shown on the drilling display, and "Tramming forced stop" is activated [1, 6].
2. The machine’s hydrostatic transmission is forced to neutral [1, 5].
3. An alert/alarm sound is given in the cabin and an interlock popup is displayed [1, 5].
4. The spring-applied brakes (parking brakes) are automatically engaged at zero speed, or at the latest after a maximum braking delay (which is factory set to 4 seconds) [1, 5].

*(Note: Prior to reaching this critical stop limit, the system will also display a preliminary notice if the pressure drops below the 110 bar notice limit)* [1, 6].

questions.question: The STATUS indicator on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) is emitting three consecutive flashes. What specific sensor malfunction and associated current signal value threshold (in mA) does this diagnostic blinking code indicate?
questions.answer:
When the yellow STATUS indicator on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) emits three consecutive flashes, it indicates a **malfunction of the air pressure sensor** (e.g., the sensor is broken, disconnected, or there is a problem with the air pressure) [1-3]. 

This diagnostic blinking code is triggered when the **current signal from the sensor drops below 2 mA** (the normal operating range is 4...20 mA) [1, 2]. 

Depending on the boom, this involves either the **Boom 1 air pressure sensor (1B127P)** or the **Boom 2 air pressure sensor (2B127P)** [4, 5]. 

According to Section 8.1.1 "CAN troubleshooting" in the *Shank lubrication unit DD322i* manual, the troubleshooting steps for this fault are as follows [3]:
1. Measure the sensor current signal to verify if it has dropped below 2 mA (the value should normally read between 4–20 mA).
2. Check the SLU air pressure.

questions.question: A Deutz TCD 3.6 engine on the C300 carrier triggers a DTC P106E 00 5100 4 fault. Based on the diagnostic code tables, what specific sensor or lamp circuit has a voltage below normal or is shorted to a low source?
questions.answer: Based on Section 2.1 "Diagnosis and error codes" of the *Deutz engine DTC codes* manual (page 19), a DTC P106E 00 5100 4 fault indicates that the **engine coolant temperature / level / charge air temperature lamp** has a voltage below normal or is shorted to a low source [1].

questions.question: While testing the C300 carrier's hydrostatic transmission charge pressure circuit, you push the parking brake release stud Y960. What exact release pressure (in bar) and engine rpm must be achieved, and which specific pressure relief valve (ID 1.5) limits this maximum charge circuit pressure?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, the exact release pressure that must be achieved is **28 bar** at an engine speed of **1800 rpm** [1, 2]. This maximum charge circuit pressure is limited by the **charge pressure relief valve (1.5)** [1, 3]. 

According to Section 6.1.14 ("Checking the brake pressures") of the *Drill carrier C300* manual (page 90) and Section 5.7.14 of the *Maintenance Manual DD322i - StageV* (page 228), the step-by-step sequence for checking the front axle's parking brake pressure is as follows [2, 4-6]:

1. Attach a pressure gauge to the front axle's parking brake pressure measuring point **(C)**.
2. Start the engine.
3. Allow the engine to idle.
4. Push the stud **Y960** to release the front axle and keep the stud pushed down.
5. Verify that the release pressure is **28 bar @ 1800 rpm**.
6. Release the stud **Y960** and check from the pressure gauge that the pressure decreases to **0 bar**.
7. Remove the pressure gauge.

questions.question: You are adjusting the water pump flow control valve (2) and checking the pressure from pressure gauge (3). To properly set the flow control valve, what exact pressure difference (in bar) must be adjusted using screw (4) relative to the B230P pressure value shown on the drilling display?
questions.answer:
To properly set the water pump flow control valve, the exact pressure difference between the **B230P** pressure value and the pressure gauge **(3)** must be adjusted to **13 bar** using the adjusting screw **(4)** [1]. 

According to Section 9.5 "Adjusting water pump flow control valve" in the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (page 67), the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Start the power pack and water pump [1].
2. Open the locking nut **(1)** of the water pump flow control valve **(2)** [1].
3. Check the pressure from the pressure gauge **(3)** [1].
4. From the drilling display, check the **B230P** pressure value [1].
5. Adjust the pressure difference (**B230P** value - pressure gauge value) to exactly **13 bar** using the adjusting screw **(4)** [1].
6. Close the locking nut **(1)** [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the rotation main relief/bypass valve (20.6), you plug the rotation work line A, attach a pressure gauge to port LS, and set the pressure to 200 bar while rotating counterclockwise. What specific final adjustment must be made to the adjusting screw after stopping rotation to achieve the correct total adjustment value of 230 bar?
questions.answer:
To achieve the correct total adjustment value of **230 bar**, the specific final adjustment required after stopping rotation is to **turn the adjusting screw clockwise half a turn** (which equals an additional 30 bar) [1].

According to Section 5.5 "Adjusting the rotation main relief / bypass valve" in the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual (page 53), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Plug the rotation work line **A** from the rock drill or feed connection plate [2].
2. Attach a pressure gauge to port **LS** [2].
3. Remove the cover from the pilot valve of the rotation main relief/bypass valve **(1)** (which controls the main valve **20.6**) [1].
4. Loosen (counterclockwise) the adjusting screw of the valve **(1)** [1].
5. Start the power pack [1].
6. Start rotation to the counterclockwise direction [1].
7. Turn the adjusting screw clockwise to adjust the pressure to **200 bar** [1].
8. Stop rotation and stop the power pack [1].
9. **Turn the adjusting screw clockwise half a turn (equals 30 bar) and thus the total adjustment value is 230 bar** [1].
10. Reinstall the cover and remove the pressure gauge [1].

questions.question: The steering circuit retarder function on the C300 carrier is failing to activate during downhill tramming. If the system uses the maximum rpm limit control principle, what specific combi-cooler hydraulic motor rpm threshold must be exceeded to immediately activate the retarder?
questions.answer:
According to Section 5.6 "Retarder control" in the tramming control system specifications (page 66), if the system uses the maximum rpm limit control principle, the retarder will activate immediately if the **combi-cooler hydraulic motor rpm exceeds the factory-set limit of 2600 rpm** [1, 2]. 

Based on Section 4.5.3 "Operation of steering circuit" (page 64), when this threshold is exceeded, the control system executes the following hydraulic sequence to apply the retarder:
1. The control system energizes the **carrier functions pressurization control valve (8.9)** [3].
2. This cuts off the direct flow path between ports **PS** and **T** within the **steering and brake control manifold (8)** [3].
3. The steering pump pressure is forced to rise as it works against the **steering circuit main pressure relief valve (8.7)**, which is set to **220 bar** [3].
4. This increased pressure level and torque load the hydrostatic transmission and the diesel engine, preventing them from overrunning during downhill tramming [3, 4]. 
5. Any excess oil flow passes through the pressure relief valve **(8.7)** to the tank connection **T** [3].

questions.question: During feed forward operation, the feed / fast feed speed is incorrect. You connect a pressure gauge to measuring connector YS to check the pilot pressure. If the power pack is running loaded, what exact pressure range (in bar) must you observe to rule out faults in the pilot oil filter (20.24) and internal pilot pressure supply valves?
questions.answer:
To rule out faults in the pilot oil filter **(20.24)** and the internal pilot pressure supply valves, you must observe an exact pressure range of **35…50 bar** at measuring connector **YS** while the power pack is running loaded [1]. 

According to Section 6.8 "Feed / fast feed speed is not correct" in the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual (pages 64–65), the step-by-step troubleshooting sequence for this pilot pressure check is as follows:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to measuring connector **YS** to check the pilot pressure [1]. 
2. Observe the reading. The pilot pressure should be **35…50 bar** when the power pack is running loaded *(Note: the pressure might be slightly lower when the power pack is running unloaded)* [1].
3. If the observed pressure differs from this 35…50 bar range, you must check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the following components [1]:
   * Pilot oil filter **(20.24)**
   * Pressure relief valve of the internal pilot pressure supply **(20.26)**
   * Pressure reducing valve of the internal pilot pressure supply **(20.27)**
4. If the pilot pressure is correct (within the 35...50 bar range), the internal supply components are ruled out, and the fault is likely located at the feed valve main spool or at the feed pilot control valves **(20.17 and/or 20.18)** [2].

questions.question: When adjusting the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve, what exact pressure (in bar) must be set using adjusting screw (3) for a standard machine, and what is the specific pressure requirement for the DU422i-W model?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve, the exact pressure that must be set using the adjusting screw **(3)** is **80 bar** for a standard machine, and **83 bar** for the **DU422i-W** model [1]. 

According to Section 3.2 "Adjusting the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve", the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows [1-3]:

1. Start the diesel engine and let it idle [3].
2. Connect the pressure gauge to the water hose reel measuring point **(1)** of the rear carrier control block [3].
3. Turn the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve locking nut **(2)** counterclockwise to loosen it [1].
4. Pressurize the system e.g. by raising the jack carefully against the stopper [1].
5. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve **(3)** clockwise/counterclockwise to adjust the pressure to **80 bar** (**83 bar** in DU422i-W) [1].
6. Lock the adjusting screw **(3)** with the locking nut **(2)** (clockwise) [1].
7. Check the pressure value again and re-adjust, if necessary [1].
8. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **(1)** [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the SLU air line restrictor valve (2), what specific air pressure reading must be achieved on the control GUI while both booms are activated for air flushing?
questions.answer:
To properly adjust the SLU air line restrictor valve (2), a specific air pressure reading of **4 bars** must be achieved on the control GUI (under Troubleshooting → Shank Lubrication) while both booms are activated for air flushing [1, 2]. 

According to Section 9.4 "Adjusting the restrictor valve" in the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (pages 66–67), the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Loosen the locking nut **(1)** of the restrictor valve **(2)** [1].
2. Turn the adjusting screw **(3)** fully open [1].
3. On the control GUI, select **→ Troubleshooting → Shank Lubrication** [1].
4. Start both power packs and the compressor [1].
5. Push the button **(4)** to select boom 1 [1].
6. Push the button **(5)** to activate air flushing for boom 1 [1].
7. Push the button **(6)** to select boom 2 [1].
8. Push the button **(5)** to activate air flushing for boom 2 [1].
9. Tighten the adjusting screw **(3)** until the Air pressure reading on the GUI rises to **4 bars** [1, 2].
10. Tighten the locking nut **(1)** of the restrictor valve [2].
11. Check the Air pressure reading again from the GUI. If the reading has changed from the correct value (4 bars):
    * a) Loosen the locking nut **(1)** [2].
    * b) Tighten/loosen the adjusting screw **(3)** until the value is exactly 4 bars [2].
    * c) Tighten the locking nut **(1)** [2].
12. Push the button **(4)** and then push the button **(5)** to deactivate boom 1 air flushing [2].
13. Push the button **(6)** and then push the button **(5)** to deactivate boom 2 air flushing [3].
14. Stop both power packs [3].

questions.question: When configuring the water pump flow control valve (2), what exact pressure difference (in bar) must be set using adjusting screw (4) between the B230P display value and the reading from pressure gauge (3)?
questions.answer:
According to Section 9.5 "Adjusting water pump flow control valve" in the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (page 67), the exact pressure difference that must be set between the **B230P** pressure value on the drilling display and the reading from the pressure gauge **(3)** is **13 bar** [1, 2].

The step-by-step sequence for this procedure is as follows:

1. Start the power pack and water pump [2].
2. Open the locking nut **(1)** of the water pump flow control valve **(2)** [2].
3. Check the pressure from the pressure gauge **(3)** [2].
4. From the drilling display, check the **B230P** pressure value [2].
5. Adjust the pressure difference (**B230P** value - pressure gauge value) to exactly **13 bar** with the adjusting screw **(4)** [2].
6. Close the locking nut **(1)** [2].

questions.question: According to the accumulator maintenance instructions, what specific maximum tightening torque (in Nm) must be applied to the accumulator bottom to ensure the mark (│) sits between marks (o) and (R)?
questions.answer:
According to Section 3.7.1 "Assembling an accumulator marked with an asterisk" in the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions* manual (pages 20–22), the specific maximum tightening torque that must be applied to the accumulator bottom is **300 Nm** [1, 2].

To correctly assemble the unit and ensure the bottom mark (│) ends up between the marks (o) and (R), you must follow this step-by-step sequence:

1. Check the numbers on the cover and the bottom to ensure they match [3].
2. Check the condition of the threads by installing the bottom to the cover *without* the diaphragm and tightening it to **150 Nm** [3]. *(Note: If the bottom rotates past the mark (R) at 150 Nm, the accumulator must be scrapped. If the threads are in good condition, remove the bottom)* [3].
3. Fit a new or inspected diaphragm to the cover, ensuring it sits in the groove with the correct side facing downwards (replace O-rings at the same time) [1].
4. Lubricate the surface of the diaphragm **(A)** and the bottom surface of the accumulator **(B)** with vaseline or lanolin [1].
5. Lubricate the thread of the bottom with vaseline or lanolin [1].
6. Use a torque wrench and the special tool to tighten the bottom to **300 Nm** [1, 2]. The bottom mark (│) must sit between the marks (o) and (R) when this torque is reached [2]. *(Note: If the bottom does not reach the mark (o) at the maximum torque of 300 Nm, the diaphragm must be replaced)* [2].
7. Place a straight edge tool **(1)** on the bottom face of the cover **(C)** to verify that the face of the bottom **(D)** sits below it [2].
8. Replace the filling valve and tighten it to a torque of **40 Nm** [4].

questions.question: When replacing and adjusting the compressor's minimum pressure valve, what exact distance (A) in millimeters must be set from the tip of the adjusting screw (4) to the valve body to ensure the B611P pressure stabilizes at 5 bar ± 0.2 bar?
questions.answer:
When replacing and adjusting the compressor's minimum pressure valve, the exact distance (A) that must be set from the tip of the adjusting screw (4) to the valve body is **9.5 mm** [1-3].

According to Section 8.2.17 of the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual, Section 5.13.17 of the *Maintenance Manual DD322i - StageV*, and Section 7.11 of the *Operating Instructions CTN27D-H*, the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Perform the necessary procedures prior to compressor maintenance (ensure the compressor is stopped and the network is completely unpressurized) [1-3].
2. Disconnect the hose **(1)** from the T connection **(2)** and leave the hose disconnected during the adjustment [1, 3].
3. Loosen the locking nut **(3)** of the adjusting screw **(4)** [1, 3]. 
4. Using a caliper gauge, set the distance **(A)** from the tip of the adjusting screw to the valve body to exactly **9.5 mm** [1-3].
5. Start the compressor [1, 3].
6. From the drilling display, verify that the **B611P** pressure sensor value is **5 bar ± 0.2 bar**, and ensure that the **B605P** pressure sensor value is lower than the B611P reading [1, 3].
7. If necessary, turn the adjusting screw while the compressor is running or pressurized until the **B611P** value reaches the required **5 bar ± 0.2 bar** [1, 3, 4].
8. Tighten the locking nut **(3)** [5, 6].
9. Stop the compressor [5, 6].
10. Start the compressor again and re-check the **B611P** value, readjusting if necessary [5, 6].

questions.question: According to the specifications, what is the exact parallel coverage area in square meters for the SB55i boom, and what is the boom's net weight in kilograms?
questions.answer:
According to the specifications, the exact parallel coverage area for the SB55i boom is **55.7 m²** [1]. The boom's net weight is specified as **2 500 kg** [1]. 

Additionally, the boom's lifting instructions note that the weight of the SB55i boom, including hoses but excluding the feed and rock drill, is **2005 kg** [2].

questions.question: When tramming a DD322i rig equipped with a standard TF5i-12' feed, what are the specified transport width, transport height options, and overall transport length in millimeters?
questions.answer:
When tramming a DD322i rig equipped with a standard TF5i-12' feed, the specified transport measurements are as follows:

*   **Transport width:** 2 025 mm [1].
*   **Transport height options:** 2 620 mm for the lower cabin option and 2 770 mm for the higher cabin option [1].
*   **Overall transport length:** 12 240 mm [1, 2]. *(Note: If equipped with the optional SCR rod retainer, the overall length increases to 12 385 mm [2]).*

questions.question: Based on the hydraulic system specifications, what is the total hydraulic oil tank volume in liters, and what is the maximum volume limit indicated by the sight glass?
questions.answer: According to the hydraulic system specifications, the total hydraulic oil tank volume is **173 liters** [1]. The maximum volume limit indicated by the sight glass is **145 liters** [1, 2].

questions.question: According to the hydraulic system specifications for the HPP555 powerpack, which specific drill rig functions are powered by the 112 cc pump compared to the 33 cc pump?
questions.answer:
Based on the hydraulic system specifications and component descriptions in the provided sources, the functions powered by the two pumps in the HPP555 powerpack are divided as follows:

*   **112 cc Pump (Variable Displacement Pump):** This pump (identified as component **3** in the power pack assembly or pump **1** in the drilling system diagram) delivers hydraulic oil to power the **percussion, feed, and boom** hydraulic systems [1-3]. Additionally, it supplies oil to the optional stabilizer and power extractor functions [1].
*   **33 cc Pump (Gear Pump):** This pump (identified as components **5** and **7** in the power pack assembly, or pumps **3** and **5** in the drilling system diagram) delivers hydraulic oil to power the **rotation** hydraulic system for the rock drills [1-3]. 

*(Note: References are found in the "HYDRAULIC SYSTEM" specifications table, Section 3.2.1 of the Maintenance Manual DD322i, and Section 3.1.1 of the Drilling Hydraulics DD322i manual)* [1-3].

questions.question: What is the exact fuel tank capacity in liters for a drill rig equipped with the Deutz TCD 3.6 diesel engine, and what is the maximum allowed fuel sulfur content in mg/kg for the Stage V version of this engine?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, here is the specific information regarding the fuel system for the Deutz TCD 3.6 diesel engine:

*   **Fuel Tank Capacity:** The exact fuel tank capacity for a drill rig equipped with the Deutz TCD 3.6 diesel engine is **150 liters** [1, 2].
*   **Maximum Fuel Sulfur Content:** For Stage V engines, you must use ultra-low sulfur diesel (ULSD) fuel with a maximum sulfur content of **15 mg/kg (0.0015%)** [3-7]. 

*(Note: References for these specifications can be found in Section 7.2 / 6.8 "Filling capacities" and Section 7.1.1 / 6.3 "Diesel engine" in the Carrier and Maintenance manuals [1-3, 5]. The manuals strongly warn that exceeding this sulfur limit can permanently damage the engine and exhaust after-treatment systems [4, 6, 7])*

questions.question: When adjusting the percussion pressure, you set the electro-proportional percussion pressure reducing/relief valve (20.11). What exact pressure (in bar) must the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.16) be adjusted to in order to properly limit the maximum pressure of the percussion/feed circuit?
questions.answer:
To properly limit the maximum pressure of the percussion/feed circuit, the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (**20.16**) must be adjusted to exactly **270 bar** [1]. 

According to Section 5.3 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve" in the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual (pages 51–52), the step-by-step sequence to achieve this adjustment is as follows:

1. Stop the power pack [2].
2. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (**1** / **20.16**) [2].
3. Tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (**1**) almost to its end (over 270 bar) [2].
4. Remove the caps from the flow controller (**2**) and the pressure controller (**3**) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump and loosen the locking nuts of their adjusting screws [2].
5. Open the adjusting screws of the pressure controller (**3**) and the flow controller (**2**) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
6. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring connector (**MP**) [3].
7. Start the power pack [3].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (**2**) fully closed (clockwise) so that the pump operates at constant pressure [3].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (**3**) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows **280 bar** [3, 4].
10. Loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (**1**) until the adjusting begins to take effect. The valve will begin to fizz when restricting the pressure, and the pressure value on the pressure gauge must drop to exactly **270 bar** [4].
11. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (**1**) [4].
12. Readjust the values of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump as instructed in its specific adjustment section [4].
13. Stop the power pack [4]. 

*(Note: The hydraulic system warms up while the main pressure relief valve restricts pressure, so ensure that the oil flow does not pass through the main pressure relief valve for an extended period [5].)*

questions.question: When setting up the water flushing circuit, what exact pressure range (in bar) must be adjusted using the pressure reducing valve (11) before the water pump, and what is the absolute maximum water circuit flushing pressure (in bar) allowed at pressure sensor B230P?
questions.answer:
When setting up the water flushing circuit, the pressure reducing valve (11) must be adjusted to lower the feed pressure before the water pump (3) to an exact range of **1...7 bar** (specifically adjusted to **2...7 bar** depending on drilling conditions) [1, 2]. The absolute maximum water circuit flushing pressure allowed at pressure sensor **B230P** (7) is **25 bar** [3, 4]. This system limit is maintained by the water circuit pressure relief valve (6) [5].

According to Section 7.2.6 "Adjusting the mine's inlet pressure" in the *Flushing Circuit DD322i* manual (pages 44–45) and Section 5.15.6 in the *Operator's Manual DD322i* (pages 262–263) [3, 4, 6, 7], the step-by-step sequence to configure this pressure is as follows:

1. Turn the adjusting knob **(1)** on the pressure reducing valve **(11)** fully open [3, 7].
2. Open the water shut-off valve **(2)** [3, 7]. 
3. Start the water pump **(3)** [3, 7].
4. Turn the knob **(1)** to adjust the feed pressure to **2...7 bar** according to your specific drilling conditions. Turning the knob clockwise increases the pressure and turning it counterclockwise decreases the pressure [2, 7]. Monitor this adjustment using the pressure gauge **(3 / 11.1)** [1, 2, 7].
5. On the drilling display, navigate to **→ Troubleshooting → Compressor and Water Pump → B230P** and verify that the water flushing pressure sensor value remains strictly under the **25 bar** limit [2, 4].

questions.question: In the drilling control system's Advanced Drilling Settings, which specific parameter defines the maximum allowable rotation pressure value before the system automatically activates the anti-jamming maneuvers?
questions.answer:
The specific parameter that defines the maximum allowable rotation pressure value before the system automatically activates the anti-jamming maneuvers is the **Anti-jamming monitoring limit** [1]. 

According to Section 6.2.6 "Editing/browsing rock types" in the *Operator's Manual DD322i - StageV* (pages 285–286), this parameter is configured as a specific Rock Type setting [1, 2]. 

To adjust this parameter, you must have supervisor, maintenance, or factory user level access and follow this step-by-step sequence:
1. Navigate to the rock types menu by selecting **→ Drilling Parameters → Edit Rock Types** [2].
2. Select the desired rock type category (e.g., Basic, Reaming, or LongHole) [2].
3. Select an existing rock type to edit, or select the add icon to create a new rock type [2, 3].
4. Select the **Anti-jamming monitoring limit** parameter from the list [1, 3].
5. Type the new maximum rotation pressure value into the field and select **OK** [3].

*(Note: The system also features a closely related parameter under Section 6.2.4 "Editing/browsing drilling monitorings" called the **Jammed bit rotation pressure monitoring limit**. When the rotation pressure rises above this specific limit, the system considers the bit to be jammed and activates the jammed bit monitoring [4, 5].)*

questions.question: During the collaring phase of drilling, what specific parameter's value acts as the threshold where the control system considers the "rock detect" to be found?
questions.answer:
During the collaring phase of drilling, the specific parameter that acts as the threshold for rock detection is the **Feed pressure rock detection limit** [1]. 

According to the *Operator's Manual DD322i - StageV* (Section 6.2.3 "Editing/browsing drilling settings", pages 279–280), the control system considers the "rock detect" to be found when the feed pressure reaches the following calculated value [1]:
**Collaring feed pressure - this parameter value = feed pressure**

Physically, the system monitors this contact using the **Rock detection pressure sensor (8.6 / B930P)** [2, 3].

If you need to adjust this parameter (requiring supervisor, maintenance, or factory user level access), you can follow this step-by-step sequence [4, 5]:
1. Navigate to the drilling settings by selecting **→ Drilling Parameters → General → Drilling Settings**.
2. From the "General Settings" list, select the **Feed pressure rock detection limit** parameter (the selected row will highlight in blue).
3. Select the current parameter value for **boom 1** or **boom 2**. 
4. Type the new numerical value into the field and select **OK** (alternatively, you can select **Edit All** to change the values for both booms simultaneously).

questions.question: When operating a TF5i feed with a maximum feed force of 25 kN, what exact maximum pressure limits (in bar) are established by the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.23) and feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.22) to protect the cylinder?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual (Section 3.1.2 on page 15 and Section 4.4 "Feed forward" on page 34), the maximum pressure limits established to protect the actuator ports (**A3** and **B3**) against pressure peaks and external forces are:

*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.23):** Limits the feed work port A3 maximum pressure to **210 bar** [1, 2].
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.22):** Limits the feed work port B3 maximum pressure to **230 bar** [1, 2].

*(Note: The maximum feed force of 25 kN for the TF5i feed is confirmed in the general specifications table [3]).*

While the manuals do not provide a specific step-by-step adjustment procedure for these pre-set shock/anti-cavitation valves, Section 6.9 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" (pages 64–66) outlines the following troubleshooting sequence to check them if your feed pressure drops [4-7]:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the load sensing line measuring connector (**LS**) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump [5].
2. Disconnect the electric connector from the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (**20.15**) and run the feed against the rear end stopper. The pressure at the **LS** measuring connector should be approximately **210 bar** [5].
3. If the pressure differs essentially, stop the power pack, then check, clean, and (if necessary) replace the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (**20.15**) [6].
4. Run the feed against the rear end stopper again and check the pressure. If the pressure is now approximately 210 bar, stop the power pack, reconnect the electric connector to valve (**20.15**), and remove the pressure gauge [6, 7].
5. If the previous steps did not remedy the low feed pressure situation, it indicates that either the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.23**) or the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.22**) is leaking or faulty. You must check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the valves (**20.23**) and (**20.22**) [7].

questions.question: According to the equipment specifications, what is the exact parallel coverage area for the SB55i boom, and what is the specified maximum extension length of the boom zoom cylinder in millimeters?
questions.answer: According to the BOOM specifications table in the equipment specifications document, the exact parallel coverage area for the SB55i boom is **55.7 m²** [1]. The specified maximum extension length of the boom zoom cylinder (listed as "Boom extension") is **1 400 mm** [1].

questions.question: When diagnosing the SB55i boom control valve block, what is the exact maximum pressure limit (in bar) set by the main pressure relief inlet element valve (1.1), and what specific pressure range must the pilot control pressure reduction/relief valve (9.1) maintain?
questions.answer:
When diagnosing the SB55i boom control valve block, the main pressure relief inlet element valve (**1.1**) sets an exact maximum pressure limit of **280 bar** for the boom/percussion circuit [1]. *(Note: The normal maximum operating pressure is actually determined by the pump pressure controller [1]).*

Furthermore, the pilot control pressure reduction/relief valve (**9.1**) must reduce and maintain the pilot oil pressure level to a specific range of **35…50 bar** [2]. 

These specifications are detailed in Section 3.1 "Hydraulics Boom control valve" of the *Boom SB55i* manual (pages 11–14) [1-3].

questions.question: When operating a rig equipped with the optional TFX5i telescopic feed, why must the feed pressure be adjusted approximately 15 bar higher than a standard TF5i feed, and which specific valve (ID 25.1) in the TFX control block causes this requirement?
questions.answer:
When operating a rig equipped with the optional TFX5i telescopic feed, the feed pressure must be adjusted approximately **15 bar higher** than a standard TF5i feed because of a **pressure relief valve mounted into the line of the upper feed cylinder B port** [1]. 

The specific component causing this requirement is the **pressure relief valve (25.1)** located within the TFX control block **(25)**. Its primary function is to **create back pressure for the piston rod side of the main feed cylinder (29)** [2]. During feed forward movement, return oil from the main feed cylinder **(29)** is forced to flow through this pressure relief valve **(25.1)** before returning to the drilling control valve block port **B3** [3]. 

According to Section 7.9 "Adjusting the length of the TFX feed" in the *Cylinder feed TF5i / TFX5i* manual (pages 41–42), the procedure for adjusting this pressure is as follows:

1. Using the feed pressure adjusting valve, set the feed pressure up by 15 bar compared to a standard TF feed. For example, if you normally use **100 bar** feed pressure with a TF feed, you must set the feed pressure to **115 bar** with the telescopic feed [4].
2. This feed pressure can also be adjusted during drilling. You can verify the adjustment is correct when the beam and the rock drill move simultaneously (though they will not move at the exact same speed) [4].
3. Note that the feed pressure is adjusted 0.5 times higher than the value of the adjusted valve compared to the standard TF feed [4].

questions.question: When setting the drill rig to the tramming position using the Boom Controls While Tramming (BCWT) option, which specific button must be pressed and held to automatically move the booms, and what specific position must the roll-over joints be in during this pre-set calibration?
questions.answer:
When setting the drill rig to the tramming position using the Boom Controls While Tramming (BCWT) option, you must press and hold the **"Moving booms to tramming position" button**, which is identified as **button (7)** on **Control panel CP3** [1, 2]. During the pre-set calibration for this position, the roll-over joints must **point upward** [3]. 

According to the *Control System DD322i* manual, Section "Tramming position pre-set (optional)" (pages 87–88) [3, 4], the complete step-by-step sequence to calibrate this pre-set position is as follows:

1. Tram the machine to a place where it is in a horizontal position [4].
2. Move the rock drills to the rear positions [4].
3. Push the tramming position button **(1)** and keep it pushed down. Release the button when the booms and feeds have moved to the current pre-set tramming position [4].
4. Move the feeds and booms manually to the desired tramming position. The rear ends of the feed beams have to rest lightly against the booms on the rubber supports, and the **roll-over joints have to point upward** [3].
5. On the control GUI, select **→ Maintenance → Calibration → Carrier → Boom Tramming Position** [3].
6. Select **Go to Calibration** [3].
7. Select **Save Position (2)** [3].
8. Push the button **(1)** again to test the new position [3].
9. Select **Accept Calibration (3)** to enable the new pre-set [3].

questions.question: While checking the feed forward and backward movements, you note that the standard TF5i feed cylinder has a maximum return movement pressure of 250 bar. What exact maximum pressure (in bar) does the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.22) limit the B3 work port to within the drilling control block?
questions.answer:
According to the *Drilling Hydraulics DD322i* manual (Section 3.1.2 "Drilling control valve block", page 15, and Section 4.4 "Feed forward", page 34), the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.22**) limits the maximum pressure at the **B3** work port to exactly **230 bar** [1, 2]. 

If a fault or leak is suspected with this pre-set shock/anti-cavitation valve (for example, if your feed/fast feed pressure drops too low), Section 6.9 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" (pages 64–66) outlines the following step-by-step troubleshooting sequence to test the feed circuit:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the load sensing line measuring connector (**LS**) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump [3].
2. Disconnect the electric connector from the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (**20.15**) and run the feed against the rear end stopper [3]. The pressure at the **LS** measuring connector should be approximately **210 bar** [3].
3. If the pressure differs essentially, stop the power pack, then check, clean, and (if necessary) replace the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (**20.15**) [4].
4. Run the feed against the rear end stopper and check the pressure at the **LS** connector again [4]. If the pressure is now approximately **210 bar**: stop the power pack, reconnect the electric connector to valve (**20.15**), and remove the pressure gauge [4, 5].
5. If the previous steps did not remedy the low feed pressure situation, it indicates that either the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.23**) or the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.22**) is leaking or faulty [5]. You must check, clean, and, if necessary, replace valves (**20.23**) and (**20.22**) [5].

questions.question: In the front carrier main components layout diagram, what specific assemblies or components are identified by numbers 1, 9, and 15?

When setting up the percussion system, what is the exact function of the electro-proportional percussion pressure reducing/relief valve (20.11) in relation to the load sensing line, and to what pressure limit must the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.16) be set?

If the rotation bushing and shank begin to overheat due to inadequate lubrication on an RDX5 rock drill, what specific oil consumption rate (in g/h) should be verified, and to what exact pressure must the SLU air line restrictor valve be adjusted when both boom air flushing valves are activated?

Within the drilling control system's anti-jamming parameters, how does the system utilize the "Jammed bit rotation pressure monitoring limit" versus the "Jammed bit feed speed monitoring limit" to determine if a drill bit is jammed during operation?

When operating the water flushing circuit, what exact pressure range must the water inlet pressure reducing valve (11) be set to before the water pump, and what is the maximum pressure limit maintained by the water circuit pressure relief valve (6)?

In the user interface's drilling settings, how does the "Collaring feed pressure" parameter function not only during the initial collaring phase but also as a baseline limit during full power drilling?

In the automatic parallelism system for boom lift and swing movements, how does the third chamber Y inside the hollow piston rod of the three-chamber cylinder hydraulically interact with chambers A and B during normal operation?
While both the TF5i and TFX5i feed cylinders share a maximum forward feed working pressure of 180 bar, what are their specific maximum working pressure limits for the return movement?

In the steering and brake control manifold, what is the exact function of the counterbalance / articulation locking valves (8.1 and 8.2) in relation to the articulation cylinders and external forces during drilling operations?
During the Boom Tramming Position Calibration procedure, what specific physical positions must the rear ends of the feed beams and the roll-over joints be set to before saving the new position?

In the drilling control valve block, what are the exact maximum pressure limits set by the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.23) compared to the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.22)?
How are issues diagnosed when the variable displacement or gear pumps do not rotate at all or have an abnormal speed?
questions.answer: You should first check the troubleshooting views from the control system to inspect the real-time electrical signaling, the control current of the modules, and the state of the programmable components [1, 2]. Next, inspect the machine for external leaks at hoses or connectors, mechanical binding, correct supply voltage to the devices, external cable damage, and appropriate pressure gauge readings [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the percussion to remain on continuously, and how is it corrected?
questions.answer:
Symptom:** Percussion is on all the time when the power pack or diesel engine is running [19].
**Cause:** The percussion selector valve or the percussion line main valve is stuck [19].
**Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and/or diesel engine immediately [20]. It is critical to repair this fault right away because running it this way can cause too low percussion pressure, which damages the seals of the accumulators in the rock drill [20]. Check, clean, and replace the percussion selector valve or percussion line main valve as necessary [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you fix an issue where the rotation speed adjustment is not working or the rotation is uneven?
questions.answer:
Symptom:** Rotation speed adjustment does not work as desired or the rounds of the drilling rod are not constant [12].
**Cause:** A stuck rotation valve main spool, faulty rotation pilot control valves, a faulty rotation line pressure compensator, or a damaged rock drill rotation mechanism [13].
**Corrective Action:** Connect a pressure gauge to measuring connector YS to check the pilot pressure (it should be 35…50 bar when loaded) [13]. If pressure is abnormal, check and replace the pilot oil filter and related supply valves [14]. If pilot pressure is correct, stop the power pack to check and replace the rotation pilot control valves [14, 15]. If the issue persists, extract and check the rotation valve main spool and then the rotation line pressure compensator spool and spring [15-17]. If the valves are in good condition, repair or replace the rock drill rotation motor [18].

**Percussion System. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose signal faults like short-circuits or open circuits on the control modules (e.g., FPVC or VCH)?
questions.answer: You can identify these faults by reading the 7-segment display on the module, which will cycle through a sequence showing the connector, the pin number, and a specific fault status letter (such as "s" for a short circuit to ground, "o" for an open circuit, or "b" for a short circuit to battery) [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Knowledge Box (KB) and what does it do?
questions.answer: The Knowledge Box (KB) allows for extended connectivity, data collection, and data transfer, ensuring smooth and safe communication through different equipment and networks [5]. Its primary function is to collect, process, and transfer monitoring data into "My Sandvik" to provide visualizations of fleet health, productivity, and utilization [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose faults using the LED indicators on the residual current protection relay (K9B) for the dewatering pump?
questions.answer: The K9B relay features a Green LED to indicate voltage presence and a Red LED to indicate an insulation fault [7, 8]. If both the Green and Red LEDs are continuously ON, a fault current has been detected [8]. If the Green LED is ON and the Red LED is flashing, it indicates a relay/sensor link fault [8]. If the Green LED is OFF while the Red LED is ON, a device malfunction has been detected [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the feed or fast feed pressure is too high?
questions.answer:
Symptom:** Feed / fast feed pressure is too high [6]. 
**Cause:** The electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve is stuck, or there is a fault in the feed line pressure compensator [6, 7]. 
**Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and replace or repair the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve [7]. If the pressure remains too high, remove the pilot control block from the drilling control valve block, clean and check the condition of the compensator spool and spring, and replace them if necessary [7, 8]. 

**Rotation System. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the expected hydraulic flow rates for the percussion and feed functions during drilling?
questions.answer: At the maximum percussion pressure level and at normal operating temperatures, the expected percussion flow rate is 105-115 L/min for the RD520 rock drill, and 100-115 L/min for the RDX5 rock drill [2]. For both rock drill models, the expected feed flow rate is 4-8 L/min [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component serves as the Drilling Master (DM1) and Carrier Master (CM) within the CAN bus control system?
questions.answer: The **XCU machine control computer** is used as both the Drilling Master (DM1) and Carrier Master (CM) [4, 5]. As the DM1, it connects to the CAN bus to act as a joint position controller that calculates forward and inverse boom kinematics, generates trajectories, and processes drilling control algorithms [6]. It features 4 x CAN I/O connections (supporting CAN-FD) [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the primary variable displacement pumps in the drilling hydraulic system?
questions.answer: Variable displacement pump (1)** delivers the required amount of oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulic systems, as well as the optional stabilizer and power extractor [1]. **Variable displacement pump (2)** delivers the required amount of oil to the compressor and water pump [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot when the percussion pressure is too low?
questions.answer:
Symptom:** Percussion pressure is too low [21].
**Cause:** The boom control main pressure relief valve is stuck, the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve is stuck, the percussion line main valve or selector valve is not opening properly, the electro-proportional percussion pressure reducing/relief valve is stuck, or the pump adjustment is incorrect [21, 22].
**Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack [22]. Check, clean, and replace the boom control main pressure relief valve, percussion line main valve, percussion selector valve, or percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve [22]. Adjust the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve if needed [22]. If this does not work, check and replace the electro-proportional percussion pressure reducing/relief valve [23]. Finally, install flow meters to check if the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump output is insufficient [23]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the primary method for diagnosing electrical system and CAN bus faults on the machine?
questions.answer: The primary troubleshooting method is using the self-diagnostics on the control system displays, such as the Drilling GUI or Tramming GUI [1, 2]. The troubleshooting diagram shows the real-time electrical signaling between control devices and components, the control current of the modules, and the state of programmable components [1, 2]. A red 'X' over a module on the display indicates that the module is offline, not working, or connected to an option not included on the machine [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What roles do the percussion line main valve and the main pressure relief valve serve?
questions.answer: The **percussion line main valve (20.8)** controls the oil flow of the percussion main line and directs it to the percussion mechanism [4]. The **percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.16)** limits the maximum pressure of the entire percussion and feed circuit to 270 bar [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure to fix an issue where the stabilizer pressure is either too low or too high?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack and check, clean, and (if necessary) replace the electro-proportional pressure reducing/relief valve (22.1) [6, 7]. Start the power pack and resume drilling; if the pressure is still incorrect, stop the power pack again to check, clean, and (if necessary) replace the stabilizer directional on/off valve (22.2) [7]. If these procedures do not remedy the situation, you must replace the entire stabilizer valve block [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the pressure reducing/relieving valves for the cable reel and water hose reel adjusted?
questions.answer: For the cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve, the pressure setpoint varies from 50 bar to 180 bar depending on the cross-sectional area of the installed cable; adjust the screw while the "reeling out the cable" function is active [11, 12]. The water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve is adjusted to 80 bar (or 83 bar for the DU422i-W model) by turning the adjusting screw while the system is pressurized (e.g., by raising the jack carefully against the stopper) [13]. The water hose reel brake valve should be adjusted during reel-out to 20-30 bar (35 bar for DU422i-W) so that the hose can be slowly pulled out by hand when the reeling out function is deactivated [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure and what are the expected values when measuring the CAN bus voltage levels?
questions.answer: With the control system on (battery main switch S1 in position 1), measure the voltage between CAN_HI and GND, and then between CAN_LO and GND [2]. The expected value for both with no load on the bus is 2.5 VDC ±0.2 V [2, 3]. When the bus is loaded, CAN_HI should measure above 2.5 VDC and CAN_LO should measure below 2.5 VDC [3]. If either measurement is < 1 V or > 4 V, it indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the setpoints and adjustment steps for the rotation main relief/bypass valve and the compressor/water pump main relief valve?
questions.answer: For the rotation main relief/bypass valve, loosen the adjusting screw, start counterclockwise rotation, and turn the screw clockwise until the pressure reaches 200 bar [8]. Stop rotation, then turn the adjusting screw clockwise another half turn (which equals 30 bar) for a total adjustment value of 230 bar [8]. For the compressor/water pump main relief valve, turn the pressure controller adjusting screw fully closed, force the pump's control current to 600 mA on the display, and turn the main relief valve adjusting screw until the gauge shows 260 bar [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What happens when an Emergency Stop pop-up dialog is displayed, and what must the operator do?
questions.answer: This pop-up indicates that one of the machine's emergency stops has been activated, which immediately stops all ongoing drill rig functions [3, 4]. The operator must resolve the reason why the emergency stop was triggered before they can resume using the drill rig [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a short-circuit or interruption using resistance measurements?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected, measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO; a normal reading is **~60 Ω ±5 Ω**, a reading **< 50 Ω** indicates a short-circuit, **> 100 Ω** indicates an interrupted bus end or faulty termination resistors, and **~40...50 kΩ** indicates multiple interruptions or missing resistors [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you distinguish between a CAN wire short-circuited to ground versus the supply voltage?
questions.answer: For both faults, the resistance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI will read normally at ~60 Ω; however, if a wire is shorted to ground, the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level will be **continuously near 0 V**, while a short to the supply voltage will show a voltage level **continuously near the supply voltage (VS)** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a fault diagnosed when the rotation pressure is too low during drilling?
questions.answer: First, check, clean, and if necessary replace the rotation main relief/by-pass valve (20.6) [15, 16]. If the pressure is still too low, sequentially check and potentially replace the pilot valve of the rotation main relief/by-pass valve (20.28), the shuttle valve (20.3), and the electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.7) [16]. If the issue persists, the rock drill rotation motor may be leaking and should be inspected [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the causes and corrective actions if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling?
questions.answer:
Symptom:** Rotation pressure is too low during drilling, despite correct pump adjustments [9].
