**Cause:** Incorrect adjustment of the rotation main relief/by-pass valve, a stuck pilot valve for the rotation main relief/by-pass valve, a leaking shuttle valve, a leaking electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve, or a leaking rock drill rotation motor [9, 10].
**Corrective Action:** Sequentially check, clean, and replace (if necessary) the rotation main relief/by-pass valve, its pilot valve, the shuttle valve, and the electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve [10]. If the pressure is still too low, check the rock drill rotation motor for leaks and repair or replace it [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the correct procedure to calibrate the joysticks and the carrier inclination sensor?
questions.answer: To calibrate a joystick, select Maintenance → Calibration → Carrier → Joysticks from the display, press 'Go to Calibration', push the top button of the specific joystick, follow the on-screen instructions, and finish [18]. To calibrate the carrier inclination sensor, tram the rig to a horizontal position, run the boom/feed extension in, run the roll-over joint to the top position, and place a precision spirit level on top of the boom 1 swing joint to ensure the front and side inclinations are exactly 0° before selecting 'Go to Calibration' in the Carrier Inclinometer menu [19]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What alarm is triggered when there is excessive water in the fuel system?
questions.answer: An alarm pop-up will appear on the drilling display when too much water has accumulated in the fuel pre-filter [16]. The required operator response is to drain the water from the fuel pre-filter [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the feed or fast feed speed is incorrect?
questions.answer:
Symptom:** Feed / fast feed speed is not correct despite proper pressures and functioning control systems [1].
**Cause:** The feed valve main spool is stuck, the pilot pressure from the feed pilot control valves is too low, or the feed line pressure compensator is faulty [1].
**Corrective Action:** First, verify the pilot pressure [2]. If correct, stop the power pack and remove the feed pilot control valves to check and replace them if necessary (using a 3 Nm tightening torque for the Allen screws) [2]. If this does not fix the issue, remove the pilot control block to clean and check the compensator spool and spring [3]. Finally, extract and inspect the feed valve main spool for faults, replacing the drilling control valve block if it is faulty [4]. If none of these steps work, check the feed cylinder for mechanical damage [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function and specific part number of the emergency stop relay?
questions.answer: The emergency stop relay is a Cat. 4 safety level device with 2-channel operation and short circuit protection, utilized for STOP category 0 applications [1]. Its specific part number is **NST-2004F** [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What machine control computer is used as the off-board controller (OC) in the Teleremote console?
questions.answer: The **SCU machine control computer** serves as the off-board controller (OC) [13]. It is equipped with 2 x CAN interfaces and a two-digit seven-segment display for application diagnostics, providing processing power for the off-board user interface [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be investigated if the STATUS (yellow) indicator on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) flashes three times?
questions.answer: Three flashes indicate that there is a problem with the air pressure or a malfunction in the air pressure sensor itself [9, 10]. You should measure the sensor current signal, which should normally read between 4 and 20 mA [10, 11]. If the current signal is lower than 2 mA, the air pressure sensor is either broken or disconnected [11]. Additionally, you should physically check the actual SLU air pressure [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose electrical connection issues such as open or short circuits directly from the control modules (like the FPVC or VCH)?
questions.answer: The modules feature a 7-segment display that cycles through an identification sequence and operational states [5, 6]. If there is a fault, the display will sequence through the node ID, the connector, the pin number, and a specific fault status letter: "o" indicates an open circuit, "s" indicates a short circuit to ground, and "b" indicates a short circuit to battery (for example, reading "24 - oP - J6 - 5s") [5, 7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific part numbers for the transformer protective circuit breakers, and what is their function?
questions.answer: The transformer protective circuit breaker for the 230/120Vac power supply system (F8) is part number **PKZM0-10-T** [4]. The protective circuit breaker for the 24Vdc power supply system (F10) is part number **PKZM0-4-T** [4]. Both function to provide adjustable overload releases to protect the transformer [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the B60G sensor on the HMI CAN bus?
questions.answer: The **B60G** is the Carrier Inclination Sensor [17]. It is a three-axis inclination sensor connected to the CAN bus used to measure the angles of the machine with respect to gravity [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do the functions of the MQ cabinet differ from the DQ cabinet?
questions.answer: The MQ cabinet is the Main Switchgear that manages the primary high-voltage systems (380-690 V), housing the main switch, power pack starter blocks, control transformers, and the 24 VDC control system power supply units (A3, A4) [9-11]. The DQ cabinet manages the low-voltage 24 VDC control system distribution, housing the battery main breaker, cabin master supply breaker, and various branch circuit breakers [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be investigated if the percussion is not working while the system is turned on?
questions.answer: If the percussion pressure gauge on the main view shows a reading but the percussion does not work, the rock drill itself is likely faulty and needs repair [3]. If the gauge shows 0 bar, the percussion selector valve (20.9) is likely stuck and needs to be cleaned or replaced [4]. If boom functions are normal but the pressure is simply too low or it doesn't start, the percussion line main valve (20.8) may be partly closed and must be checked [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the VIU module, and which specific control nodes utilize it?
questions.answer: The **VIU module** is a CANopen slave that serves as a general-purpose input unit for user interfaces and a voltage input unit for applications needing intensive local computing power [10]. It is utilized by the Teleremote Spotlight Controller (TSC) [10], the Main Switchgear Sensors (MS) [11], and the Tramming Controller (TCP) [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the primary method to initially identify a CAN bus system fault?
questions.answer: Any fault on the CAN bus must first be identified using the instructions and notifications on the **operator's display panel**, which will indicate whether the bus nodes are in a fault mode or switched off [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you test for a short-circuit or interruption on the CAN bus using resistance measurements?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected (battery main switch S1 in position 0), measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO using a multimeter [1]. A normal reading is approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω, which confirms the bus cables, connectors, and the two 120 Ω termination resistors are intact [1]. If the result is < 50 Ω, there is a short-circuit on the bus [1]. If the reading is > 100 Ω, one end of the bus is interrupted or a termination resistor is faulty, and a reading of 40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted at multiple points or both resistors are missing [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components should be investigated if the rotation pressure is too high during drilling?
questions.answer: First, check the drilling control settings and ensure the rotation speed of the drilling rod is adjusted to the proper level, as a rotation speed that is too low can increase pressure [3]. If the issue persists, the rotation line pressure compensator (20.2) may be faulty [4]. Remove the pilot control block, then remove the compensator spool and spring from the drilling control valve block to clean and check their condition [4]. Replace the spool and/or spring if necessary before reinstalling them [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a failure of the diesel engine to start?
questions.answer: Check the battery condition, verify that the battery isolation switch (S1) and the optional starter isolator switch (S2) are in the ON position, ensure no circuit breakers in the DQ cabinet have tripped, and check that the fire suppression system is not preventing the start [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific control module is used for the Boom and Drilling Controllers (BDC1, BDC2), Vehicle Controller (VC), End Carrier Controller (EC), and Switch Controller (SC), and what is its function?
questions.answer: These controllers utilize the **VCH (Valve Controller High Temp)** module [1-3]. It functions as a powerful I/O-module and CANopen slave that offers CANopen services for reading and writing the hardware's inputs and outputs [1]. It features separate output powering/cutoff circuitry designed to allow de-activating outputs safely in SIL2/PLd systems [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components control the pressure limits and safety of the boom and steering articulation systems?
questions.answer: In the boom circuit, the **main pressure relief valve (1.1)** limits the boom and percussion circuit's main pressure to 280 bar [6]. In the carrier steering system, the **counterbalance / articulation locking valves (8.1, 8.2)** act as articulation locks and protect the steering cylinders from overloading against external forces [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the visual and audible warnings of the fire suppression system, and how can the operator respond to an automatic engine shutdown?
questions.answer: If the fire suppression system activates, a loud siren will sound and the electronic alarm/timer box will display a red warning light to indicate a system fault or discharge [8-13]. The system initiates an automatic engine shutdown with a 6-second delay; however, the operator can press a delay extension button to get an additional 20 seconds before the engine shuts down [11-15]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes a yellow Notice pop-up to appear, and what is the required action?
questions.answer: A yellow Notice pop-up is displayed when the control system detects a medium-level problem [1, 2]. This does not require immediate action, but if the alert persists or is repeated frequently, the operator should investigate and correct the underlying reason for the alert [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary components and functions of the hydrostatic transmission (HST) pump assembly?
questions.answer: The **HST variable displacement pump (1.1)** delivers the required amount of oil flow to the hydrostatic transmission system [5]. The integrated **charge pump (1.2)** delivers charge oil to the high-pressure system and to the pressure controls of the HST pump (1.1) [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the maximum pressure settings for the primary drilling and carrier circuits?
questions.answer: The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve limits the maximum pressure to 270 bar [3, 4], while the maximum percussion pressure for both the RD520 and RDX5 rock drills is set to 255 bar [5]. On the carrier, the steering circuit main pressure relief valve is set to 220 bar, and the brakes/air conditioning/combi-cooler circuit main pressure relief valve is set to 250 bar [6-8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a potential CAN bus cabling fault using resistance measurements?
questions.answer: Ensure the power is completely disconnected and the battery isolation switch (S1) is in the 0 (OFF) position [1]. Measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO using a multimeter [2]. A normal reading is approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω, which indicates the bus cables, connectors, and two 120 Ω termination resistors are intact [1, 2]. If the result is < 50 Ω, there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [2]. If the reading is > 100 Ω, one end of the bus is interrupted or the termination resistors are faulty [2]. If the measurement is ~40...50 kΩ, the bus is interrupted at at least two points, or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which module functions as the Boom Sensors converter (BS1, BS2) on the boom bus?
questions.answer: The **RD (Resolver-to-Digital)** module is used as the Boom Sensors converter [8]. It acts as a CANopen slave for high-accuracy measurement applications, providing services for reading and writing resolver-to-digital conversions and analog sensor inputs [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning is given if the operator attempts to tram without the seat belt fastened or the cabin door closed?
questions.answer: The optional door latch and seat belt monitoring system will sound a warning buzzer and display a notice pop-up on the screen when the engine is started [5-7]. The operator must fasten their seat belt and securely close the cabin door before tramming [8-10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for replacing and adjusting the control system power supply units (A3, A4)?
questions.answer: Only qualified electricians should perform this task; start by isolating the electrical system, removing the broken unit, and replacing it while leaving both DC+ wires unconnected [3, 4]. Switch the power on and adjust the output voltage to 27.5 V ± 0.1 V in "Single use" mode with the same load conditions on both units [4]. Next, move the jumper from "Single use" to "Parallel use" mode to achieve load sharing [4]. Switch off the power, connect both DC+ terminals using a tightening torque of 0.8 Nm, and then switch the power back on [4]. Finally, verify that the DC-voltage display shows around 28.5 V without load and 27.5 V with full load [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the XCU module within the electrical control system?
questions.answer: The XCU module serves as the joint position controller [7]. It is responsible for calculating forward and inverse boom kinematics, trajectory generation, executing automatic positioning from one hole to another, and processing boom and drilling control algorithms [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you determine if a power factor correction capacitor is faulty?
questions.answer: Start one power pack at a time and let it idle, then check the power factor value on the electric quality measuring unit (P1); if the value drops under 0.5 and individual phase currents differ significantly, the capacitor is likely faulty and must be replaced [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning is given if the DEF/AdBlue fluid level gets too low?
questions.answer: An indicator will appear on the control system display if the DEF/AdBlue fluid decreases below the defined acceptable level [16, 17]. The operator must respond by refilling the DEF/AdBlue tank [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it indicate if the Ub and K1 LEDs are ON, but the K2 LED is OFF on the emergency stop relay (NST-2004F), and how do you resolve it?
questions.answer: This specific LED combination indicates that relay K1 is activated while K2 is deactivated [5, 6]. This means there is an error in the emergency stop circuit at terminals T14, T21, or T22, or the K1 relay itself may be welded or defective [6]. To resolve it, check the emergency stop inputs at those specific terminals and verify the integrity of the relay [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Why does a Blocked pop-up dialog occur, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: A Blocked pop-up appears when the control system prohibits the operator from performing a specific action that could cause personal injury or damage to the drill rig [3, 4]. The operator must identify and remove the cause of the error, after which the pop-up will disappear automatically [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose errors in the emergency stop electrical circuit using the emergency stop relay?
questions.answer: The emergency stop relay (NST-2004F) features three diagnostic LEDs: Ub, K1, and K2 [9]. If all three are ON, the circuit is functioning normally [9]. If Ub is ON but both K1 and K2 are OFF, there is an error between the two emergency stop inputs [9]. If Ub and K1 are ON but K2 is OFF, it indicates an error at terminals T14, T21, or T22, or that the K1 relay itself may be defective or welded [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the feed pressure is too low, assuming the pilot pressure has already been verified as correct?
questions.answer: The fault is likely located at the feed valve main spool or the feed pilot control valves [2]. Stop the power pack and remove the feed pilot control valves (20.17) and (20.18) [2]. Check and replace the valves if necessary, and then carefully reinstall them back into the drilling control valve block using a tightening torque of 3 Nm for the 2 Allen screws [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are specific errors within the emergency stop circuit diagnosed?
questions.answer: By checking the LEDs on the emergency stop relay (NST-2004F); for instance, if the Ub and K1 LEDs are ON but K2 is OFF, it indicates an error at terminals T14, T21, or T22, whereas if both K1 and K2 are OFF while Ub is ON, it indicates an error between the two emergency stop inputs [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the steering circuit and brakes/air conditioning main pressure relief valves, and what are their setpoints?
questions.answer: Both adjustments must be performed when the diesel engine is running at 1500 rpm with the manual throttle set to medium [1, 2]. For the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (220 bar), loosen the locking nut, turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise fully open, pressurize the carrier hydraulics with the manual screw, and then turn the adjusting screw clockwise until the gauge reads 220 bar [1, 2]. For the brakes/air conditioning/combi-cooler circuit (250 bar), plug the hose branching to the charging valve, open the adjusting screw fully, and then turn it clockwise until the pressure gauge reads 250 bar before tightening the locking nut [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are short-circuits diagnosed by measuring the CAN bus voltage levels?
questions.answer: With the control system turned on, measure the voltage between CAN_HI/CAN_LO and ground (GND); the expected value with no load is **2.5 VDC ±0.2 V**, but if the results are **< 1 V or > 4 V**, it indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the displacement capacities for the various hydraulic pumps on the powerpack?
questions.answer: The powerpack (HPP555) utilizes several pumps with specific displacements: the percussion and feed variable displacement pump is 112 cc, the compressor and water booster pump (WBP) is 45 cc, the rotation gear pump is 33 cc, and the air conditioning / combi-cooler gear pump is 41 cc / 33 cc [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the Deutz engine diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) starting with "U" indicate about the CAN bus system?
questions.answer: DTC codes starting with "U" generally point to CAN bus communication faults and timeouts [10, 11]. For example, U0010 and U0028 indicate special instructions for the Machine CAN [10]. U1715 indicates an abnormal update rate timeout for the CAN engine protection, and U1721 indicates an abnormal update rate timeout for the Machine CAN Engine start (GeraBox) [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific filtration requirements and micron ratings for the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: Sandvik recommends a hydraulic system purity class of 18/16/13 according to the ISO 4406 (c) standard [10]. The system uses a 20 µm absolute pressure filter (with a bypass that opens at 7 bar) and a 10 µm absolute return oil filter (with a bypass that opens at 2.5 bar) [1, 11, 12]. Other filtration ratings include a 5 µm hydraulic oil tank breather [13], an 8 µm HST charge pressure filter [14], an optional 2 µm absolute by-pass filter [15], and an optional 10 µm absolute stabilizer oil filter [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific contactors are used to control the power pack motor and the dewatering pump?
questions.answer: The power pack motor is controlled by contactors designated as **DILM170 (RDC24)** (component IDs K1 and K2) [2]. The dewatering pump utilizes a contactor designated as **DILM32** (component ID K9) [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system manage brake circuit pressures and operations?
questions.answer: The **dual circuit brake pedal (11)** provides precisely controlled output pressures to the service brake cylinders, which is proportional to the pedal stroke and the force applied by the operator [9]. The **brakes / air conditioning / combi-cooler circuit main pressure relief valve (8.11)** limits the maximum pressure in those respective circuits to 250 bar [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure and setpoint for adjusting the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve?
questions.answer: The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve must be set to 270 bar [5]. First, stop the power pack, loosen the locking nut, and tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (1) almost to its end (over 270 bar) [6]. Open the adjusting screws of the pump's pressure controller (3) and flow controller (2) almost fully open, connect a pressure gauge, and start the power pack [6, 7]. Turn the flow controller fully closed so the pump operates at constant pressure, turn the pressure controller clockwise until the gauge shows 280 bar, and finally loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve until it begins to fizz and the gauge drops to 270 bar [5, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do the rotation and feed compensator/relief valves function within the drilling control valve block?
questions.answer: The **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)** maintains a constant pressure difference over the rotation main spool (20.1) regardless of input and load pressure changes [2]. The **electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.15)** controls the feed load sensing (LS) pressure and limits its maximum value [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the restrictor valve to ensure correct shank lubrication air pressure?
questions.answer: Loosen the locking nut of the restrictor valve (2) and turn the adjusting screw (3) fully open [16]. Start both power packs and the compressor, then activate air flushing for both boom 1 and boom 2 using the control display [16]. Finally, tighten the adjusting screw until the air pressure reading on the display rises exactly to 4 bars, then tighten the locking nut [16, 17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the most common CAN bus cabling faults and how are they initially detected?
questions.answer: The most common cabling faults are **cable, wire, or connector interruptions and short-circuits**, which can easily be detected by performing troubleshooting with a multimeter [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the diagnosis procedure if the feed or fast feed pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to the load sensing line measuring connector (LS), disconnect the electric connector from the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.15), and run the feed against the rear end stopper [10]. If the pressure is not approximately 210 bar, the valve (20.15) is likely stuck [10, 11]. If the pressure is correct, proceed to inspect the feed port shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.22 and 20.23), the feed line pressure compensator (20.19), or plug the feed pressure lines to check if the feed cylinder itself is faulty [12-14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used for the Tramming GUI (VG) display?
questions.answer: The Tramming GUI (VG) utilizes a **CCPilot V700** component, which is a freely programmable display computer featuring a PCAP touch screen [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical checks should be performed if the power pack will not start or stops unexpectedly?
questions.answer: Check for alarm messages on the display, ensure the mains electric supply is connected with the main switch (Q1) in position 1 (ON), verify that no circuit breakers in the MQ cabinet have tripped, ensure the pilot circuit is functional, and confirm all emergency stop buttons are released [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the CAN-RUN and CAN-ERR LED indicators on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) signify during troubleshooting?
questions.answer: On the SLCU, if the green CAN-RUN LED is flashing, the unit is on standby awaiting a command; this indicates that the CAN bus connection is broken or the control unit is not sending a start command [6]. If the CAN-RUN LED gives a single flash, the SLCU has stopped due to an internal fault [6]. For the red CAN-ERR LED, a single flash means at least one CAN control error counter has reached the alarm limit, while a continuous ON state means the CAN control bus is off completely [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the possible causes and specific remedies if the boom does not hold its position?
questions.answer: The boom may drop if the overcenter valve of the boom swing or lift cylinder is leaking, the o-ring is broken, or the seat surfaces are worn; to fix this, replace the damaged or worn parts [5]. The issue could also be caused by dirt in the hydraulic circuit, which requires you to flush the hydraulic circuit, or because air is trapped in the cylinder, which requires bleeding the cylinders [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a red Alarm pop-up dialog indicate, and how should the operator respond?
questions.answer: A red Alarm pop-up indicates that the rig control system has detected a major problem [1, 2]. Because this could lead to component damage, the control system may halt some or all drill rig operations [1, 2]. The operator must give this immediate attention and must not use the drill rig until the cause of the alarm is resolved and corrected [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the maximum working pressures for the feed cylinders?
questions.answer: For the standard TF5i feed cylinder, the maximum working pressure is 180 bar for forward feed and 250 bar for return movement [9]. For the telescopic TFX5i feed cylinder, the maximum working pressure is 180 bar for both the forward feed and the return movement [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What type of keypads are used on the control panels (CP), and what are their specifications?
questions.answer: The control panel keypads utilize **Grayhill 3K keypads** [8]. They operate on a voltage range of 8 to 32 V, feature IP67 protection, and are vibration and impact resistant [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific CAN bus faults cannot be diagnosed using a multimeter?
questions.answer: A multimeter cannot be used to detect a **faulty CAN sensor (sensor signal fault)**, **missing CAN signals**, or **bit-level signal faults** [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you isolate a fault to a specific termination resistor or the bus cable itself?
questions.answer: Disconnect both 120 Ω termination resistors from the CAN bus and measure the resistance of each resistor separately [5]. If both resistors measure exactly 120 Ω, the resistors are intact and the fault is likely located within the bus cable itself [5]. To further pinpoint the fault location, move the termination resistor toward the next measuring point (which can be any actuator/node on the bus), disconnect the bus cable from that actuator, and connect the termination resistor in its place [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which fault codes indicate a communication timeout or failure between the Main and Secondary Engine CAN control units?
questions.answer: A large number of fault codes, including P1453, U173A, U173B, U173C, U1745, and U175C, indicate an "Abnormal update rate timeout" for the Engine CAN Main Secondary communication [13-16]. Additionally, codes like P1454, P1457, and P1458 indicate a CAN Main Secondary fault trigger specifically on the Secondary ECU [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the percussion pressure is too low, but the boom functions are normal and the percussion pressure gauge shows a reading?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack, then clean and check the percussion line main valve (20.8), the percussion selector valve (20.9), the pressure reducing valve of the percussion main valve (20.10), and the electro-proportional percussion pressure reducing/relief valve (20.11) [1]. Replace any of these components with new ones if necessary [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What CAN bus fault codes are specifically associated with electrical diagnostics for the exhaust aftertreatment system?
questions.answer: Fault code U1700 indicates an abnormal update rate timeout for the CAN communication to the NOx sensor before the catalytic converter [10]. Code U1718 means there is erratic or incorrect data regarding an exhaust aftertreatment CAN control message, while U1734 indicates an abnormal update rate timeout for that same control message [17, 18]. U1737 indicates a special instruction related to a shortcut in the exhaust aftertreatment CAN [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC/SLCU) on the CAN network?
questions.answer: The **SLC (or SLCU)** is a CANopen node that dispenses shank lubrication oil to the rock drills [15, 16]. It listens for the rock drill’s shank lubrication requests sent from the Drilling Master (DM1) node via the CAN backbone and controls the respective air and oil flows [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD322i Technical Manual)

questions.question: During a diagnostic check for excessively high drilling feed pressure, you install pressure gauges at measuring points M1 and M2 of the anti-jamming and return automatics block; if pressure reaches measuring point M2 only when the powerpack is started, which specific pilot control valve is most likely faulty?
questions.answer:
Based on the troubleshooting procedures for "Drilling feed pressure too high" in the hydraulics manual (Section 6.13, pages 131-132), if pressure reaches measuring point M2 only, the **fast feed pilot control valve (33)** is most likely faulty [1-3]. 

The manual details the following step-by-step sequence when investigating a pilot control pressure that is well over 21 bar:
1. Install pressure gauges to the measuring points M1 and M2 of the anti-jamming and return automatics block [1].
2. Start the powerpack [2].
3. Evaluate the pressure readings:
   * If pressure reaches the measuring point M2 only, it is likely that the **fast feed pilot control valve (33)** is faulty [2]. 
   * If both measuring points receive pressure simultaneously, it is likely that the **feed pilot control valve (31)** is faulty [2].
4. Stop the powerpack [2].
5. Replace the faulty valve [2].

*Note: Before performing this test, the manual specifies you should first verify the operation of the feed pressure regulating valve (20) and/or the feed deviation valve (216) [4].*

questions.question: When adjusting the minimum percussion pressure to 120 bar by turning the adjusting screw of the monitoring valve (18), you must first turn the adjusting screw of which specific pressure relief valve almost fully closed to ensure it does not interfere with the LS-circuit?
questions.answer:
Based on the "HYDRAULICS.pdf" manual, Section 5.1.8 "Adjusting min. percussion pressure" (Pages 104-105), you must first turn the adjusting screw of the **percussion half-power pressure relief valve (6)** almost fully closed [1, 2]. This is required because the monitoring valve (18) and the half-power pressure relief valve (6) are located in parallel in the percussion LS-circuit, and the lower adjusting value between the two will dictate the pressure [1].

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment procedure:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the **half-power pressure relief valve (6)** [2].
2. Turn the adjusting screw of the **half-power pressure relief valve (6)** almost fully closed (clockwise) [2].
3. Loosen the locking nuts of the **monitoring valve (18)** [2].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the **monitoring valve (18)** fully open (counterclockwise) and then close it by 3½ turns [2].
5. Start the powerpack [2].
6. Turn percussion half-power on by locking the control lever of the **percussion pilot control valve (14)** to the back position [2, 3].
7. Adjust min. percussion pressure to **120 bar** with the **monitoring valve (18)** [3]. Read the pressure value from the **percussion pressure gauge (11)** [3].
8. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw for the **monitoring valve (18)** [3].
9. Adjust the **percussion half-power pressure relief valve (6)** according to the chapter 'Adjusting percussion half-power' [3].
10. Release the control lever of the **percussion pilot control valve (14)** [3].
11. Stop the powerpack [3].

questions.question: When using nitrogen (N2) to fill the brake accumulators on a TC 9-12 carrier, what exact pressure should be set using the regulating valve (8) before closing the filling valve (1)?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, when filling the brake accumulators on a TC 9-12 carrier, the exact pressure should be set to **80 bar** using the regulating valve (8) [1, 2]. 

According to the "Filling the brake accumulators" procedure (found in the Carrier Manual, Section 6.1.7, page 50, and the Maintenance Manual, Section 5.8.7, pages 264-265), you must follow this exact step-by-step sequence before closing the filling valve (1):

1. Release the pressure from the brake accumulators according to the manual's instructions for releasing pressure [3, 4].
2. Remove the cap (3) [3, 4].
3. Screw the elbow adapter (10) to the filling valve (1) [3, 4].
4. Push the quick coupling sleeve (5) onto the stem (4) [3, 4].
5. Undo the locking nut (2) [3, 4].
6. Turn the pressure regulating valve (8) open [3, 4].
7. Open the nitrogen bottle valve (9). The gauge (7) will indicate the pressure in the bottle [3, 4].
8. Adjust the pressure slowly to **80 bar** (for TC 9-12 models) by turning the regulating valve (8). The gauge (6) will indicate the pressure in the accumulator [1, 2]. 
9. Once the correct pressure is reached, close the filling valve (1) by turning the locking nut (2) [1, 2].

questions.question: When calibrating the boom circuit maximum LS pressure on a THC system, after installing a pressure gauge at measuring point M10 and temporarily setting the pressure reducing/relieving valve (210) to 250 bar, what specific engine RPM must be maintained while running the zoom cylinder inwards to accurately set the LS-pressure relief valve to 230 bar?
questions.answer:
Based on the "BOOM.pdf" manual, Section 4.6.3 "Adjusting boom circuit max. LS pressure" (Pages 31-32), the specific engine speed that must be maintained while running the zoom cylinder inwards is **1800 rpm** [1, 2]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment procedure:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure relief valve for the max. LS-pressure [3].
2. Install a pressure gauge to the measuring point **M10** of the drilling control block [3].
3. Start the powerpack [3].
4. Run the boom zoom inwards or outwards (whichever is safest) and hold against the stopper to raise maximum pressure [3].
5. Adjust the boom circuit max. pressure to **250 bar** with the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)** at the drilling control block, reading the pressure value in the gauge connected to measuring point **M10** [4].
6. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)** [4].
7. Stop the powerpack [4].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the max. LS-pressure pressure relief valve almost fully open (counterclockwise) [4].
9. Start the carrier engine (diesel) [4]. 
10. Run the zoom cylinder inwards with the engine speed at **1800 rpm** and adjust at the same time the boom circuit max. LS pressure to **230 bar**, by turning the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure pressure relief valve clockwise. Read the pressure in the pressure gauge installed at measuring point **M10** [2].
11. Stop the diesel engine and lock the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure pressure relief valve [5].
12. Start the powerpack [5].
13. Run the boom control operating valve for zoom or feed transfer [5].
14. Adjust the boom circuit max. pressure back to **230 bar** with the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)**, reading the pressure value in the gauge connected to measuring point **M10** [5].
15. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)** [5].
16. Stop the powerpack [6].
17. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **M10** of the drilling control block [6]. 

*(Note: Prior to step 10, the manual also states to check if the carrier's hydraulic circuit has a pressure relief valve that restricts the adjustment; if so, it must be temporarily set approximately 10 bar higher than the target boom circuit max LS-pressure and returned to its original setting after the adjustment is complete)* [2, 6].

questions.question: If the water circuit pressure drops below 2.8 bar, the pressure switch (517) engages and illuminates the H601 warning indicator; exactly how long must the pressure remain below this threshold before the pressure control system automatically stops the drilling water pump?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, the water pressure must remain below the 2.8 bar threshold for **more than one minute** before the pressure control system automatically stops the drilling water pump. 

Here is the exact step-by-step sequence of how the system handles a low water pressure event (found in the *Operator's Manual*, Page 153, and the *Electric System Manual*, Section 4.3.3, Pages 28-29):

1. **Initial Drop & Drilling Stop (4 seconds):** If the water pressure drops below 2.8 bar, the pressure switch (517 / S422) engages. If the pressure remains below this limit for more than **four seconds** (the default threshold), the system automatically stops the drilling functions, and the red "water pressure low" indicator light (**H601**) on the QN panel is illuminated. At this stage, the water pump is still running.
2. **Water Pump Stop (1 minute):** If the fault duration continues and the water pressure remains below 2.8 bar for **more than one minute**, the pressure control system automatically stops the drilling water pump.
3. **Reset and Restart:** Once the pump has been stopped due to this one-minute delay, resetting the fault will not automatically restart the pump (even if the powerpacks are running and the water pump switch is in "automatic"). To resume operations, the operator must first press the pressure control reset button (**S505**) to clear the fault and turn off the H601 light, and then manually restart the water pump by turning the water pump operation switch (**S501**) to the "start" position.

questions.question: When adjusting the boom circuit maximum LS pressure on a THC system, what target pressure should be set using the LS-pressure relief valve after temporarily adjusting the pressure reducing/relieving valve (210) to 250 bar while reading the gauge at measuring point M10?
questions.answer:
Based on the "BOOM.pdf" manual, Section 4.6.3 "Adjusting boom circuit max. LS pressure" (Pages 31-32), the target pressure that should be set using the LS-pressure relief valve is **230 bar** [1]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment procedure [1-5]:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure relief valve for the max. LS-pressure.
2. Install a pressure gauge to the measuring point **M10** of the drilling control block.
3. Start the powerpack.
4. Run the boom zoom inwards or outwards (whichever is safest) and hold against the stopper to raise maximum pressure.
5. Adjust the boom circuit max. pressure to **250 bar** with the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)** at the drilling control block, reading the pressure value in the gauge connected to the measuring point **M10**.
6. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)**.
7. Stop the powerpack.
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the max. LS-pressure pressure relief valve almost fully open (counterclockwise).
9. Start the carrier engine (diesel). *(Note: Check if the carrier’s hydraulic circuit has a pressure relief valve that restricts the adjustment. If it does, temporarily adjust it to approximately 10 bar higher than the target boom circuit max. LS-pressure).*
10. Run the zoom cylinder inwards with the engine speed at **1800 rpm** and adjust at the same time the boom circuit max. LS pressure to **230 bar**, by turning the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure pressure relief valve clockwise. Read the pressure in the pressure gauge installed to the measuring point **M10**.
11. Stop the diesel engine and lock the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure pressure relief valve.
12. Start the powerpack.
13. Run the boom control operating valve for zoom or feed transfer.
14. Adjust the boom circuit max. pressure back to **230 bar** with the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)**, reading the pressure value in the gauge connected to the measuring point **M10**.
15. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(210)**.
16. Stop the powerpack.
17. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **M10** of the drilling control block.

questions.question: During the calibration of the rotation circuit, after setting the pressure controller (B) on the variable displacement pump (50) to 200 bar, what specific pressure value should the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) be adjusted to while reading the gauge at measuring point M?
questions.answer:
During the calibration of the rotation circuit, after setting the pressure controller (B) to 200 bar, the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) should be adjusted to **180 bar** [1]. 

According to the "HYDRAULICS.pdf" manual, section "Adjusting variable displacement pump (50)" (pages 93-94), the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the hose support and plug the hose ends [2].
2. Remove the protection caps of the flow controller (A) and the pressure controller (B) of the variable displacement pump (50) and undo the locking nuts of the adjusting screws [2].
3. Remove the protection cap of the LS-pressure relief valve (65) of the rotation directional valve (53) and undo the locking nut of the LS-pressure relief valve (65) [2].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure relief valve (65) fully close (clockwise) [3].
5. Connect the pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (M) of the rotation control valve (53) [3].
6. Turn the rotation speed regulating valve (59) fully closed (clockwise) [3].
7. Start the power pack [3].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) fully closed (clockwise). *(Note: The pump (50) is now operating at constant pressure)* [3].
9. Put the rock drill rotation on by pulling and locking the rotation control lever to the rear position (towards the operator) [3, 4].
10. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows 100 bar. Let the LS-line bleed into a separate container by loosening the hose connection of the flow controller (A) until all air has escaped, then tighten the connection [4].
11. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows **200 bar** at measuring point M [4].
12. Lock the adjustment of the pressure controller (B) with the locking nut [1].
13. **Turn the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure relief valve (65) counterclockwise until the pressure gauge shows 180 bar** [1].
14. Lock the adjustment of the LS-pressure relief valve (65) with the locking nut [1].
15. Put the rock drill rotation off by releasing the rotation control lever to the middle position [1].
16. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [1].
17. Allow the pressure to stabilize in the pressure gauge connected to the measuring point M [5].
18. Adjust the stand-by pressure to 20-23 bar from the flow controller (A) by turning the adjusting screw clockwise [5].
19. Lock the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) with the locking nut [5].
20. Stop the power pack and allow the pressure to come down to zero [5].
21. Start the power pack and allow the pressure to stabilize to confirm the stand-by pressure is in the recommended range, then install the protective caps [5]. 
22. Reconnect the rotation hose, adjust the rotation speed regulating valve (59) to the desired value, and remove the pressure gauge from measuring point M [6].

questions.question: To achieve the recommended factory setting for anti-jamming activation pressure on a standard rock drill, what specific feed pilot control pressure range should be read at measuring point M3 after adjusting the anti-jamming valve (34)?
questions.answer:
To achieve the recommended factory setting for the anti-jamming activation pressure on a standard rock drill, a feed pilot control pressure range of **approx. 19-21 bar** should be read at measuring point M3 after adjusting the anti-jamming valve (34) [1]. 

According to the *HYDRAULICS* manual, Section 5.1.6 "Adjusting anti-jamming pressure" (Pages 101-102), the complete step-by-step sequence for this calibration is as follows:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the anti-jamming valve (34) adjusting screw [2].
2. Turn the anti-jamming valve (34) adjusting screw first fully closed (clockwise), and open it then 2 turns (counterclockwise) [2].
3. Start the powerpack [2].
4. Run the rock drill against the rear stopper [2].
5. Stop the powerpack [2].
6. Loosen the locking nut of rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) of rotation control block adjusting screw [2].
7. Turn the LS-pressure relief valve (65) adjusting screw almost fully open (counterclockwise) [2].
8. Turn the rotation speed regulating valve (59) closed (clockwise) [2].
9. Plug the pressure side hose of the feed cylinder [2].
10. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the hose support and plug the hose ends [3].
11. Install a pressure gauge to the measuring point M3 of the anti-jamming/ return automatics block [3].
12. Start the powerpack [3].
13. Lock the control levers of rotation and feed pilot control valves (58) and (31) to the back position [3].
14. Adjust the desired anti-jamming activation pressure with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) by turning the adjusting screw clockwise, to the factory setting of 120 bar (RD314: 140 bar). Read the pressure value in the rotation pressure gauge (51) [1, 3].
15. Adjust the anti-jamming valve (34) so that it directs feed pilot control pressure at the set pressure to the measuring point M3 of the anti-jamming/return automatics block. Read the feed pilot control pressure (**approx. 19-21 bar**) in the pressure gauge installed in the measuring point M3 [1].
16. When the anti-jamming valve (34) is correctly adjusted, lock the adjusting screw of the valve (34) [1, 4].
17. Adjust rotation pressure with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) to 180 bar by turning the adjusting screw clockwise. Read the pressure in the rotation pressure gauge (51) [4].
18. Lock the adjusting screw of the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) [4].
19. Release the control levers of rotation and feed pilot control valves (58) and (31) [4].
20. Stop the powerpack [4].
21. Remove the plugs from the disconnected rotation hoses and reconnect the hoses together [4].
22. Remove the plugs from the feed cylinder pressure side feed line, and reconnect the hose to the feed cylinder [4, 5].
23. Start the powerpack [5].
24. Turn drilling rotation on again by locking the control lever of rotation pilot control valve (58) in the back position [5].
25. Adjust the drill rod rotation speed to the desired value by turning the rotation speed regulating valve (59) counterclockwise [5].
26. Release the control lever of the rotation pilot control valve (58) [6].
27. Stop the powerpack [6].
28. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point M3 for the anti-jamming/return automatics [6].

questions.question: When performing the basic adjustment for reeling the cable out with a 50 mm² (AWG 1/0) cable, what specific pressure value (P2) must be set using the pressure relief valve (6) while reading the pressure gauge at measuring point M2 or MB?
questions.answer:
Based on the "COMPONENTS.pdf" manual, Section 2.2 and 2.3 "Basic adjustment and max force control of reels" (pages 11-13 and 15-17), when reeling the cable out with a 50 mm² (AWG 1/0) cable, the specific pressure value (P2) must be set to **40 bar** [1, 2].

The adjustment sequence varies slightly depending on whether your reel control block is Version A (using measuring point M2) or Version B (using measuring point MB). 

**Step-by-Step Sequence for Version A (Measuring point M2):**
1. Remove the hoses (217) and (218) from the motor [3, 4].
2. Connect the hoses (217) and (218) by adding a fitting between the hoses [3, 4].
3. Loosen the pressure relief valve (5 and 6) locking nuts by turning them counterclockwise [4, 5]. Open the valve (6) adjusting screw fully open by turning counterclockwise and turn the valve (5) adjusting screw fully closed [4, 5].
4. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (M2) of the reel control block [5, 6].
5. Engage the parking brakes and start the diesel engine [5, 6].
6. Activate the "reeling the cable out" function (or "cable in" if without remote control) with full diesel revolutions, which activates the coil Y450 in the reel control block (1) and the coil Y248 in the carrier control block assembly [5, 6].
7. By turning the pressure relief valve (6) adjusting screw clockwise, adjust the pressure P2 to **40 bar** [1, 2, 6, 7].
8. Lock the adjustment of the pressure relief valve (6) with the locking nut by turning it clockwise [6, 7].
9. Lower the diesel revolutions to minimum [7, 8].
10. By turning the pressure relief valve (5) adjusting screw counterclockwise, adjust the pressure to 20 bar [7, 8].
11. Lock the adjustment of the pressure relief valve (5) with the locking nut by turning it clockwise [7, 8].
12. Stop the reeling function [7, 8].
13. Switch off the diesel engine [7, 8].
14. Remove the fitting between the hoses (217) and (218) and connect the hoses back to their original positions [7, 8]. 
15. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point (M2) [9, 10].

**Step-by-Step Sequence for Version B (Measuring point MB):**
1. Remove the hoses (217) and (218) from the motor [9, 10].
2. Connect the hoses (217) and (218) by adding a fitting between the hoses [9, 10].
3. Loosen the pressure relief valve (6) locking nut fully open by turning it counterclockwise [9, 10].
4. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (MB) [9, 10].
5. Engage the parking brakes and start the diesel engine [9, 10].
6. Activate the "reeling the cable out" function with full diesel revolutions, which activates the coil Y450 in the reel control block (1) and the coil Y248 in the carrier control block assembly [9, 11, 12].
7. By turning the pressure relief valve (6) adjusting screw clockwise or counterclockwise, adjust the pressure P2 to **40 bar** [1, 2, 11, 12].
8. Lock the adjustment of the pressure relief valve (6) with the locking nut by turning it clockwise [11, 12].
9. Lower the diesel revolutions to minimum [1, 2].
10. Stop the reeling function [1, 2].
11. Switch off the diesel engine [1, 2].
12. Remove the fitting between the hoses (217) and (218) and connect the hoses back to their original positions [1, 2].
13. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point (MB) [1, 2].

questions.question: What specific pressure range in bar should the pressure reducing valve (506) be adjusted to while the water pump (501) is running, as read on the water pressure gauge (510.06)?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Water circuit NC7/DT821/DT1131" manual, the pressure reducing valve **(506)** should be adjusted to a specific range of **1-7 bar** [1, 2]. 

According to Sections 4.1 "Operation of the pressure reducing valve (506)" and 7.2.2 "Adjusting water pressure", here is the exact step-by-step sequence for this adjustment:

1. Ensure the water pump **(501)** is running [1, 2].
2. Adjust the pressure using the adjusting knob **(A)** (or hand knob **(1)**). Turn the knob clockwise to increase the water pressure, or turn it counterclockwise to decrease the water pressure [1, 2].
3. Read the resulting pressure value on the water pressure gauge **(510.06)** [1].
4. Ensure the set value never exceeds **25 bar** [2].

questions.question: What is the parallel holding coverage area in square meters for the SB150 boom compared to the SB60 boom?
questions.answer: Based on the "BOOM.pdf" manual, Section 3.2 "Technical data" (Page 15), the parallel holding coverage area for the **SB150 boom is 159.0 m²**, compared to **56.5 m² for the SB60 boom** [1, 2].

questions.question: What is the kilowatt rating for the standard HPP575 hydraulic powerpacks, and what is the optional powerpack model and rating used with the RD520 rock drill?
questions.answer: The standard HPP575 hydraulic powerpacks have a rating of **75 kW** [1]. When the drill rig is equipped with the RD520 rock drill, the optional powerpack model used is the **HPP555**, which has a rating of **55 kW** [2].

questions.question: In the rear end module component identification diagram, which specific parts correspond to items 4, 8, and 10?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Rear end module" component identification diagram found in Section 3.1.3 of both the Maintenance and Operator's Manuals, the specific parts correspond to the following items:

*   **Item 4:** Cable reel [1, 2]
*   **Item 8:** Hydraulic oil receiver [1, 2]
*   **Item 10:** Water booster pump [1, 2]

questions.question: When adjusting the percussion full-power pressure relief valve (7) for an RD525 rock drill operating at a maximum piston impact frequency of 93 Hz, what is the optimum factory setting pressure that should be verified on the percussion pressure gauge (11)?
questions.answer:
Based on the "HYDRAULICS.pdf" manual, Section 5.1.10 "Adjusting percussion full-power" (Page 106), the optimum factory setting pressure for an RD525 rock drill is **210 bar** [1, 2]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for adjusting the percussion full-power pressure to this level:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the **percussion full-power pressure relief valve (7)** [3].
2. Turn the adjusting screw of the **percussion full-power pressure relief valve (7)** first fully closed (clockwise) and then open the adjusting screw 5 turns (counterclockwise) [3].
3. Start the powerpack [3].
4. Push the control lever of the **percussion pilot control valve (14)** to the front position [3].
5. Adjust the percussion full-power pressure to the desired level (210 bar) with the adjusting screw of the **percussion full-power pressure relief valve (7)**. Turn clockwise to increase the pressure and counterclockwise to decrease it. Read the pressure value from the **percussion pressure gauge (11)** [3].
6. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the **percussion full-power pressure relief valve (7)** [3].
7. Release the control lever of the **percussion pilot control valve (14)** [4].
8. Stop the powerpack [4].

questions.question: During the calibration of the anti-jamming valve (34) to the factory setting of 120 bar, what specific feed pilot control pressure range must be verified at measuring point M3 while the control levers for rotation (58) and feed (31) are locked in the back position?
questions.answer:
Based on the "HYDRAULICS.pdf" manual, Section 5.1.6 "Adjusting anti-jamming pressure" (Pages 101-102), the specific feed pilot control pressure range that must be verified at measuring point M3 is **approx. 19-21 bar** [1, 2].

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this calibration procedure:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the anti-jamming valve (34) adjusting screw [3].
2. Turn the anti-jamming valve (34) adjusting screw first fully closed (clockwise), and open it then 2 turns (counterclockwise) [3].
3. Start the powerpack [3].
4. Run the rock drill against the rear stopper [3].
5. Stop the powerpack [3].
6. Loosen the locking nut of rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) of rotation control block adjusting screw [3].
7. Turn the LS-pressure relief valve (65) adjusting screw almost fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
8. Turn the rotation speed regulating valve (59) closed (clockwise) [3].
9. Plug the pressure side hose of the feed cylinder [3].
10. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the hose support and plug the hose ends [4].
11. Install a pressure gauge to the measuring point M3 of the anti-jamming/return automatics block [4].
12. Start the powerpack [4].
13. Lock the control levers of rotation and feed pilot control valves (58) and (31) to the back position [4].
14. Adjust the desired anti-jamming activation pressure with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) by turning the adjusting screw clockwise, to the factory setting of 120 bar (RD314: 140 bar). Read the pressure value in the rotation pressure gauge (51) [2, 4].
15. Adjust the anti-jamming valve (34) so that it directs feed pilot control pressure at the set pressure to the measuring point M3 of the anti-jamming/return automatics block. Read the feed pilot control pressure (**approx. 19-21 bar**) in the pressure gauge installed in the measuring point M3 [2].
16. When the anti-jamming valve (34) is correctly adjusted, lock the adjusting screw of the valve (34) [2].
17. Adjust rotation pressure with the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) to 180 bar by turning the adjusting screw clockwise. Read the pressure in the rotation pressure gauge (51) [5].
18. Lock the adjusting screw of the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) [5].
19. Release the control levers of rotation and feed pilot control valves (58) and (31) [5].
20. Stop the powerpack [5].
21. Remove the plugs from the disconnected rotation hoses and reconnect the hoses together [5].
22. Remove the plugs from the feed cylinder pressure side feed line, and reconnect the hose to the feed cylinder [5, 6].
23. Start the powerpack [6].
24. Turn drilling rotation on again by locking the control lever of rotation pilot control valve (58) in the back position [6].
25. Adjust the drill rod rotation speed to the desired value by turning the rotation speed regulating valve (59) counterclockwise [6].
26. Release the control lever of the rotation pilot control valve (58) [6].
27. Stop the powerpack [6].
28. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point M3 for the anti-jamming/return automatics [6].

questions.question: When fine-tuning the feed force during full-power drilling to compensate for feed beam friction without altering the percussion pressure, what specific valve can be used to adjust the feed pressure by ±45 bar from the nominal level?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, the **feed deviation valve (216)** is used to adjust the feed pressure by approximately **±45 bar** from the nominal level [1-3]. 

Adjusting this specific valve affects *only* the feed pressure, regardless of the percussion pressure, making it the correct valve to compensate for feed beam friction, the mass of the drilling equipment, and varying rock conditions [2, 4].

To ensure the ±45 bar adjustment range is correctly centered, you must first set the basic nominal level. According to the *HYDRAULICS.pdf* manual, Section 5.1.11 "Adjusting nominal level of feed pressure" (Pages 108-109), here is the step-by-step sequence for this procedure [5-7]:

1. Remove the hand wheel of the **feed deviation valve (216)** [6].
2. Start the power pack [6].
3. Turn the switches of the return automatics (**S73** and **S74**) to the **M** position [6].
4. Run the rock drill to the rear position [6].
5. Pull the control lever of the **percussion pilot control valve (14)** to the back position and push the **feed pilot control valve (31)** to the front position [6].
6. Adjust the percussion pressure to the correct level using the **feed pressure regulating valve (20)** [6].
7. Adjust the feed pressure to the correct level using the **feed deviation valve (216)** [7].
8. Release the control levers of the **percussion pilot control valve (14)** and the **feed pilot control valve (31)** [7].
9. Stop the power pack [7].
10. Attach the hand wheel of the **feed deviation valve (216)** back into its initial position (with the pointer pin straight ahead) [7]. 

Once this basic adjustment is complete, the feed deviation can be fine-tuned ±45 bar from this basic level during drilling [7]. Turn the knob clockwise to increase the feed force (decrease the pressure difference between percussion and feed) and counterclockwise to decrease the feed force (increase the pressure difference) [1].

questions.question: To provide adequate flushing through the drill rod and bit to remove cuttings, what specific adjusting range (in bar) is available on the pressure reducing valve (506) before the water pump, as read on the water pressure gauge (510.06)?
questions.answer:
Based on the "PNEUMATICS.pdf" manual, the specific adjusting range available on the **pressure reducing valve (506)** is **1-7 bar** [1, 2]. 

According to Sections 4.1 "Operation of the pressure reducing valve (506)" (Page 29) and 7.2.2 "Adjusting water pressure" (Page 47), the step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Ensure the **water pump (501)** is running [1, 2].
2. Adjust the pressure using the **adjusting knob (A)** (also referred to as **hand knob (1)**) [1, 2]. Turn the knob clockwise to increase the water pressure, or turn it counterclockwise to decrease the water pressure [1, 2].
3. Read the resulting pressure value on the **water pressure gauge (510.06)** [1].
4. Ensure the set value never exceeds the maximum of **25 bar** [2].

questions.question: To properly dampen vibrations and prevent cavitation in a new RD525 rock drill, what specific pre-charge gas pressure must be filled into the high-pressure accumulator and the stabilizer accumulator before taking the drill into use?
questions.answer:
To properly dampen vibrations and prevent cavitation before taking a new RD525 rock drill into use, the high-pressure accumulator must be filled to **50 bar** and the stabilizer accumulator to **30 bar** [1, 2]. You must strictly use only nitrogen (N2) to fill these pressure accumulators [3]. 

According to Section 3.8.1 "Filling instruction" in the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill* maintenance manual (Pages 24-25), the exact step-by-step sequence for filling the accumulators is as follows [4-7]:

1. Check the condition of the filling valve, replacing it if there are any signs of damage [4].
2. Remove the cap (4) [4].
3. Screw the elbow adapter (15) to the filling valve (2) [4].
4. Push the quick coupling sleeve (6) onto the stem (5) [4].
5. Undo the locking nut (3) [4].
6. Turn the pressure regulating valve (11) open [4].
7. Open the nitrogen bottle valve (12) and verify the bottle pressure on the gas bottle pressure gauge (9) [4, 5].
8. Adjust the pressure in the low pressure accumulator to 5 - 10 bar by turning the regulating valve (11) [5]. *(Note: Although your question asks for the high-pressure and stabilizer accumulators, the low-pressure accumulator must ultimately be set to 4 bar for the RD525 during this sequence)* [1, 7].
9. Adjust the pressure in the high-pressure (H.P.) accumulator to 50 bar with the pressure control valve (11), checking the reading on the accumulator pressure gauge (8) [1, 6].
10. Adjust the pressure of the stabilizer accumulator to 30 bar with the pressure control valve, verifying the reading on the accumulator pressure gauge (8) [1, 6].
11. Close the filling valve (2) by turning the locking nut (3) [6].
12. Close the nitrogen bottle valve (12) [6].
13. Turn the pressure regulating valve (11) open [6].
14. Disconnect the quick couplings (5) and (6) [6].
15. Release the elbow adapter (15) from the filling valve (2) [6].
16. Mount the checking gauge (0-10 bar) into the low pressure accumulator filling valve (2) and by opening the locking nut (3) let the pressure flow out until the gauge shows 2 - 4 bar [6, 7].
17. Tighten the locking nut (3) to 15 Nm [7].
18. Refit the cap (4) [7].

questions.question: During the boom lift function, if the feed forward tilt cylinder (6) reaches its end position, from which specific valve within block (14) does the third chamber of the boom lift cylinder (2) receive replacement oil to maintain the automatic parallelism system?
questions.answer: Based on the "BOOM.pdf" manual, Section 4.2 "Boom lift and lower function" (Page 18), if the feed forward tilt cylinder (6) is in the end position during boom lifting, the third chamber of the boom lift cylinder (2) receives replacement oil from the hydraulic oil tank via the **intake valve (.07)** located within block (14) [1, 2].

questions.question: What is the exact difference in the maximum working pressure for the return movement between the standard TF 500 feed cylinder and the TFX 500 telescopic feed cylinder?
questions.answer:
The exact difference in the maximum working pressure for the return movement between the two feed cylinders is **70 bar**. 

According to Section 3.1.2 "Feed cylinders" in the feed manual:
*   The standard **TF 500** feed cylinder has a maximum working pressure of **250 bar** for the return movement [1].
*   The **TFX 500** telescopic feed cylinder has a maximum working pressure of **180 bar** for the return movement [2].

questions.question: In order to ensure that the hydraulic parallelism system functions correctly during boom positioning, what specific operational state must the extra swing cylinder of the feed (bolting) be in?
questions.answer: Based on the *Operator's Manual* (Section 4.4, Page 193), in order for the hydraulic parallelism system to function correctly, the extra swing cylinder of the feed (bolting) must be **completely drawn in** [1].

questions.question: If the powerpack is running but the boom fails to move on a THC rig, and the drilling module movement prevention switches (SH292/SH293) are confirmed to be off, which specific movement prevention valve (identified as Y456 or 222) in the boom line should be checked for a sticking spool?
questions.answer:
If the powerpack is running but the boom fails to move on a THC rig, and the drilling module movement prevention switches (**SH292/SH293**) are off, you should check the **drilling module movement prevention valve Y456 (222)** for a sticking spool or lack of a control signal [1]. 

According to the BOOM manual, Section 8.2.5 "Boom doesn't move" (Pages 77-78), you must follow this step-by-step sequence to check and troubleshoot this valve:

1. Check whether the valve **(222)** receives control by verifying if the LED on the valve socket is lit [2].
2. If the valve receives a control signal, check its operation as follows [2]:
   a) Stop the powerpack [2].
   b) Clean and repair, or replace the faulty valve [2].
3. If the valve does not receive control (the LED is not lit), check the electric connections referring to the separate electric system instructions [2].

questions.question: To obtain an accurate reading when checking the hydraulic oil tank level, what specific operational state must all cylinders be in, and in what exact position must the boom be placed?
questions.answer:
To obtain an accurate reading when checking the hydraulic oil tank level, all hydraulic cylinders must be **retracted** and the boom(s) must be placed in the **transportation position** (also referred to as the **tramming position**) [1-3].

According to the *Carrier Manual* (Section 5.1.3, Page 37), *Operator's Manual* (Section 5.14.1, Pages 269-270), and *Maintenance Manual* (Section 5.11.4, Page 310), you should follow this exact sequence to ensure an accurate check:

1. Position the rig on a **level surface** [2].
2. **Retract all hydraulic cylinders** [1-3].
3. Set the boom(s) to the **transportation/tramming position** [1-3].
4. Check the oil level by looking through the **level glass (sight glass)** on the side of the hydraulic oil tank/receiver [3-5]. 

Additionally, if the hydraulic oil level drops too low, the indicator light **(H602B)** on the tramming panel will automatically illuminate [3, 4].

questions.question: If the percussion full-power maximum pressure is exceeding the set value of 210 bar for an RD525 rock drill and the percussion max pressure relief valve (7) is functioning correctly, what component inside port 9 of the feed and percussion control block should be checked for loosening?

While diagnosing a Mercedes Benz engine on the carrier, you receive a fault code 01315 for the ambient pressure sensor; if fault codes 11415 and 11416 have already been removed, which two actual values should you read out and compare while the engine is stopped to check if they are within the +/- 10% tolerance band?

During drilling operations, the manually controlled fast feed fails to operate in either direction; if installing pressure gauges to measuring points M2 and M3 of the anti-jamming and return automatics block reveals a correct pilot control pressure of approximately 30 bar, which specific valve spool is most likely sticking?

When diagnosing insufficient rotation pressure during drilling despite the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) being correctly adjusted to 180 bar, what specific feed pilot control pressure should be verified at measuring point M1 while the feed deviation valve (216) is adjusted to set rotation pressure between 80 and 100 bar?

The powerpack fails to start and the fault relay is ON, as indicated by light H106; if the voltage meter shows no reading, which specific 110 V control circuit breaker and which protective switch of the 24 VDC feed transformer should be inspected?
What should be done if the engine control system reports a "CAN-High defective" fault (code 10100)?
questions.answer: Check the wiring for an open circuit fault and repair or replace it if necessary. Switch on the ignition, then delete the fault memory in both the ECU engine control (e.g., MR-PLD) and the SG FRE. Finally, perform a functional check [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the main switch (Q100) control, and what are its built-in safety features?
questions.answer: The main switch (Q100) turns the power supply to the drill rig on or off, though it does not cut off voltage at the cable reel or slip ring unit [6]. It is equipped with an undervoltage relay that cuts off power if K106 is activated, and for mechanical safety, the electrical cabinet door cannot be opened when the switch is in the ON (1) position [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a fault where the "CAN data is not plausible" (code 10102)?
questions.answer: Resolve the actual faults of the SG FRE, excluding CAN data bus fault codes 10201, 00202, and 10203, and then perform a functional check [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the Check Engine warning light indicate and how should the operator respond?
questions.answer: The Check Engine lamp comes on when critical parameters are out of bounds, such as coolant level/temperature, oil pressure, water-in-fuel, intake manifold temperature, crankcase pressure, DOC temperatures, DPF out over-temperature, or soot loading [1, 2]. The operator must have the engine serviced at the first available opportunity [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: Where is the CAN interface located within the TCAD/TDATA PC system?
questions.answer: The CAN interface is located on the VME card front plate, which houses both the CPU and the CAN components, along with USB and RJ45 bus connectors [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What happens if the compressor temperature becomes too high and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: If the compressor temperature reaches 100°C, the warning indicator light (H604) starts blinking [13, 14]. If it reaches 115°C, H604 goes on permanently, and the powerpack, compressor, and water pumps will automatically stop [13-15]. The operator must investigate the cause, wait for the temperature to drop below 112°C, and ensure the circuit breakers are on before restarting [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What configuration is required for the MR and +CPC4-eCAN2 components to function correctly on the CAN link?
questions.answer: To ensure proper communication and resolve potential CAN link faults (such as code 12202), the configuration for the MR parameter and the **+CPC4-eCAN2** parameter 1/01 must be checked and set to equal functionality to support one-wire capability [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the thermistor relays 1R112 and 2R112 monitor?
questions.answer: The thermistor relays 1R112 and 2R112 monitor the stator temperature of the powerpack motors for boom 1 and boom 2, respectively [8]. They are designed to trigger if the stator temperature reaches 155 °C [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the main switchgear (MP) in the electric system?
questions.answer: The main switchgear (MP) contains the main switch, the motor controls, and the power supply system for the electric devices on the rig [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if all boom hydraulic functions are operating slowly or not working at all on the THC system?
questions.answer: First, check if the hydraulic oil level is too low or the oil viscosity is too high, and inspect hoses and connections for leaks [1]. Next, verify if the required working pressure of 230 bar is being reached [1]. Install a pressure gauge (max. 250 bar) to the measuring point M10 of the drilling control block, run the rock drill backwards against the rear stopper, and measure the pressure to check if the pressure reducing/reliefing valve (210) is at the set value of 230 bar [2]. If the pressure is incorrect, clean, repair, or replace the valve (210) [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps are required if there is no communication with the MR over the CAN link (+CPC4-eCAN2 - MR, codes 12202 or 12214)?
questions.answer: Check the engine CAN wiring [9, 10]. You must also check the configuration to ensure the MR parameter and the +CPC4-eCAN2 parameter 1/01 are set to equal functionality (one-wire capability) [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a 110...120 V 1-phase socket outlet that is not working?
questions.answer: First, verify if the load is too great or if the **ground fault sensor has tripped** [5]. Check the **protective switch F310** of the transformer and the **circuit breaker F313** of the socket outlet terminal [5]. If the transformer is overloaded and overheated, the thermal protector will switch the socket load off; it will reset automatically once the transformer cools down [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you resolve a "no connection to CAN" (code 10104) error?
questions.answer: Check the CAN connection to the SG FRE by inspecting all cables, connectors, and electrical components for damage, loose contacts, and corrosion [8]. Repair as needed, then remove the engine CAN bus fault in the SG FRE [8]. Once communication with the ECU engine control is restored, check its calibration for one-wire capability [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system indicate a clogged hydraulic pressure or return oil filter, and what action is required?
questions.answer: A clogged pressure filter triggers indicator H611, while a clogged return filter triggers H607 [25-28]. These warnings do not automatically stop drilling functions, and they are bypassed when the oil is cold (below 30 °C) to prevent false alarms from thick oil [25-28]. The operator must replace the dirty filter [25-28]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the operating positions for the water booster pump switch (S501) and compressor 1 switch (S502)?
questions.answer: These switches have three operating positions on the switch panel: '0' for Stop, 'I' for Start (which will only activate the component if the powerpack is already running), and 'S' for a manual Start [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it mean if automatic drilling stops after 30 seconds?
