questions.answer: This can happen if there is an issue with the shank lubrication system [6]. Check the indicator panel for alarms and verify that the shank lubrication fault indicator is not on [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the water pressure low indicator (H601) signify and how should the operator react?
questions.answer: The H601 indicator lights up if the water pressure remains below 2.8 bar for more than four seconds, which automatically stops the drilling [16, 17]. The operator should press the acknowledgement button (S505) to turn it off and clear the fault [16, 17]. If the pressure remains low for over a minute, the water pump stops completely, and the operator must manually restart the pump using switch S501 after resolving the issue [16, 17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the Access Protector/Detector system warn the operator of a hazard zone intrusion?
questions.answer: If the detection scanner detects an object in the field, the red detection warning light starts blinking [29-31]. In protector mode, drilling and boom movements are immediately prevented [29, 30]. The operator must ensure no one is in the hazard zone and reactivate the system by pushing the acknowledgment button on the user interface before resuming normal drilling [32, 33]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the procedures and optimal setpoints for adjusting the percussion full-power pressure?
questions.answer: The optimal percussion full-power pressure depends on the rock drill model: 210 bar for RD525, RD520, and RDX5/HLX5 models, and 190 bar for the RD314 model [5]. To adjust it, loosen the locking nut of the percussion full-power pressure relief valve (7), turn the adjusting screw fully closed (clockwise), and then open it 5 turns counterclockwise [6]. Start the powerpack, push the percussion pilot control valve lever (14) to the front position, and adjust the valve (7) until the desired pressure is shown on the percussion pressure gauge (11) [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the steps to fix a system where the percussion is not working at all?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The percussion mechanism fails to strike when activated [10].
*   **Cause:** The fault could lie within the rock drill itself, a sticking percussion main valve (3) or percussion selector valve (4), or a blocked orifice (9) in the load-sensing line [10, 11]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** If the percussion pressure gauge (11) shows a reading but there is no percussion, the rock drill is likely faulty and must be repaired or replaced [10]. If the gauge shows no reading, clean, repair, or replace the percussion main valve (3) and selector valve (4) [10, 11]. If the percussion starts but only partially, remove the adapter from port 9 of the feed and percussion control block, and clear the blocked orifice (9) [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What role does the motor protector switch+contactor (1K100) play, and how is its triggering current configured?
questions.answer: The 1K100 acts as the starter for the powerpack of boom 1 and provides overload triggering [2]. Its triggering current is set to 1.2 times the nominal current specified on the motor's type plate, which is adjusted using the overload adjustment (FLA) dial wheel [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the boom circuit maximum LS-pressure adjusted and what is the target value?
questions.answer: The target value for the boom circuit maximum LS-pressure is 230 bar [1]. To adjust it, first install a pressure gauge to measuring point M10 of the drilling control block [2]. Temporarily adjust the boom circuit max pressure to 250 bar using the pressure reducing/relieving valve (210) [3]. Turn the adjusting screw of the max LS-pressure relief valve almost fully open, start the diesel engine, and run the zoom cylinder inwards at 1800 rpm [1, 3]. While doing this, turn the adjusting screw of the LS-pressure relief valve clockwise until the gauge reads 230 bar [1]. Finally, re-adjust the boom circuit max pressure back to 230 bar using the pressure reducing/relieving valve (210) [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a "CAN-High defective" (code 10100) or "CAN-Low defective" (code 10101) fault diagnosed?
questions.answer: Check the wiring for an open circuit fault and repair or replace it if necessary [7]. Then, switch on the ignition, delete the fault memory in both the ECU engine control (e.g., MR-PLD) and the SG FRE, and perform a functional check [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Multitimer unit (MTU) A100?
questions.answer: The Multitimer unit (A100) is used to adjust the delay times for both the water pressure monitoring and the air pressure monitoring systems [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the battery isolation switch (S1) and does it isolate all carrier devices when switched off?
questions.answer: The battery isolation switch (S1) turns the current from the carrier's battery to the drill rig's electric circuit on or off [4]. However, it does not isolate all devices; components like the alternator, signal horn, alarm beacon, and fire suppression system remain connected [4, 5]. Additionally, if the main switch (Q100) is ON, the main electric system continues to feed voltage to the carrier's systems even if S1 has been opened [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for filling the gas pre-charge pressure for the brake accumulators, and what are the setpoints?
questions.answer: You must only use nitrogen (N2) to fill the pressure accumulators [11]. First, shut down the engine and completely release the oil pressure from the brake accumulators by pressing the brake pedal several times until the gauges show 0 bar [12, 13]. Install the filling adapter to the filling valve (1) and open the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve [13]. Turn the pressure regulating valve (8) slowly to adjust the pressure to 65 bar for TC8 / NC7 models, or 80 bar for TC9-12 models, as indicated by the gauge (6) [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is insufficient rotation pressure diagnosed during drilling?
questions.answer: First, check if the **LS-pressure relief valve (65)** of the rotation control block adjusts to the recommended **180 bar**, replacing it if faulty [14, 15]. If the pressure is still low, it could be due to underfeed caused by low feed pressure; adjust the feed deviation valve (216) to set rotation pressure between 80 and 100 bar (100-120 bar for RD314) and verify the **feed pilot control pressure is 19-21 bar** [15-17]. If the issue persists, the rock drill rotation motor may be leaking and requires replacement [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the safety and operational tasks of the overcenter valves located in the boom circuit?
questions.answer:
The overcenter valves have several critical tasks [12]:
*   They act as safety valves to prevent the cylinder from moving if a hydraulic hose breaks.
*   They prevent oil flow from the cylinder to the tank during drilling, ensuring the boom accurately maintains its position.
*   They restrict oil flow from the return side until pressure on the pressurized side rises high enough, making boom movements smoother and preventing the boom's own weight from accelerating the movement.
*   They open to let oil out if an external force raises the cylinder pressure above the set value, allowing the boom to yield and avoiding mechanical damage. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the potential causes and diagnostic steps if all boom hydraulic functions operate slowly or not at all?
questions.answer: This can be caused by **low hydraulic oil levels**, high oil viscosity, or **leaking circuits** [1]. To diagnose, check oil levels and inspect hoses for leaks [1]. It may also be due to the pressure relief valve failing to reach the working pressure (**230 bar for THC, 210 bar for TPC**); check this by measuring pressure at point M10 or M2 depending on the system [2, 3]. Finally, verify if the oil pump is working or if its intake is blocked [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration requirements and purity class standards for the hydraulic fluid?
questions.answer: The hydraulic system requires **pressure filtering with a capacity of 20 µm absolute** and **return oil filtering with a capacity of 10 µm absolute** [1, 8, 9]. Additionally, the hydraulic oil tank is equipped with an **air filter with a capacity of 5 µm** [10]. The manufacturer recommends maintaining a hydraulic fluid purity class of **18/16/13 according to the ISO 4406 (c) standard** [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component functions as the engine control unit that communicates over the CAN link?
questions.answer: The **MR2** serves as the diesel engine control unit [4], which communicates with the rest of the rig's control system over the CAN link (such as the +CPC4-eCAN2 - MR connection) [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose an issue where **automatic drilling is stopped after 30 seconds**?
questions.answer: Check the indicator panel for any active alarms and specifically verify that the **shank lubrication fault indicator** is not on [8]. A lack of oil flow detected by the SLU unit or an air pressure drop below 2.8 bar in the shank lubrication system will trigger the **indicator light H72** and stop automatic drilling [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where the **powerpack starts, but stops after a while**?
questions.answer: This can occur if the **compressor temperature rises above 115 °C** or the **hydraulic oil temperature exceeds 75 °C (H610)** [2]. It may also be triggered by a **"shank lubrication oil level low" signal (H608)**, which stops all powerpacks with a 3-second delay until oil is added [2]. Additionally, check if the **hydraulic oil level drops below the minimum (H602)**; if so, add oil and press the **pressure switch reset button S505** [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where the drilling percussion is not working at all?
questions.answer: If the **percussion pressure gauge (11)** shows a reading but percussion fails, the rock drill itself is likely faulty and requires repair or replacement [5, 6]. If the gauge shows no reading, the **percussion main valve (3)** or **selector valve (4)** may be sticking and needs cleaning or replacement [6, 7]. If percussion only starts partially, check if the **orifice (9)** in the load-sensing line is blocked [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How should you troubleshoot a lack of communication with the MR over the CAN link (+CPC4-eCAN2 - MR, code 12202 or 12214)?
questions.answer: Check the engine CAN wiring [3, 4]. Additionally, check the configuration to ensure the MR parameter and the +CPC4-eCAN2 parameter 1/01 are set to equal functionality, specifically for one-wire capability [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the carrier's service brakes do not hold?
questions.answer: You should check for internal leaks within the brake cylinders and replace seals if necessary [20]. Also, check if the brake pressure is too low by inspecting the brake valve spring and hydraulic system pressure, bleed the brake system to remove trapped air, and inspect the **brake plates** for excessive wear [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you calibrate the maximum pressure for the rotation circuit?
questions.answer: The maximum rotation pressure is adjusted to 180 bar using the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) [8]. First, prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose and plugging the ends, then turn the rotation speed regulating valve (59) fully closed [8, 9]. Start the powerpack, lock the rotation pilot control valve lever (58) in the back position, and turn the pressure relief valve (65) adjusting screw until the rotation pressure gauge (51) reads 180 bar [8]. Note that the regulating valve (55) sets the maximum system pressure of the rotation to 25 bar above the adjusted rotation LS-pressure value [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: In the event of a jammed drill rod, which valve alters the feed direction?
questions.answer: The **anti-jamming valve (34)** controls the feed direction in an anti-jamming situation [5]. When rotation pressure exceeds the value set on this valve, it changes position to direct feed pilot control pressure to the feed directional valve (23), causing the feed to pull backwards [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the feed pressure regulated and modified during collaring and full-power drilling?
questions.answer: Feed pressure is primarily determined by the **feed pressure regulating valve (20)**, which affects both feed pressure and percussion pressure (for feed/percussion monitoring) during collaring and full-power drilling [3]. Additionally, the **feed deviation valve (216)** can be used to reduce or increase the feed force independently of the percussion pressure [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings are provided if the brake circuit pressure is insufficient?
questions.answer: The front (P3) or rear (P4) brake circuit pressure gauge indicator lights will come on if their respective pressures fall below 100 bar [8, 9]. Additionally, the parking brake engaged indicator (H15/H15B) will light up constantly if both circuits fall below set minimum limits, or it will blink if the brakes on one axle are left in a different state than the other (meaning the pressure difference between circuits is too high) [8-12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the **powerpack does not start or stops**?
questions.answer: First, verify that the **main switch is on**, the **fault relay is ON (H106 is indicating)**, and the water pump or compressor switches are in the running position [1]. If the voltage meter shows no reading, check the **circuit breaker F317** and the **fuses F310** for the 110 V control [1]. Finally, if the **indicator light H617** is not lit, check the **protective switch F310** of the 24 VDC feed transformer and the **circuit breaker F450** [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you resolve a "CAN-Low defective" fault (code 10101) in the CAN connection?
questions.answer: Check the wire for an open circuit fault and repair or replace it as needed. Turn on the ignition, delete the fault memory in the ECU engine control (e.g., MR-PLD) and the SG FRE, and then perform a functional check [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the powerpack does not start or stops?
questions.answer: Ensure the main switch is on, the fault relay is ON (indicator H106 is lit), and the water pump or compressor switches are in the running position [1, 2]. If the voltage meter shows no reading, check circuit breaker F317 and the F310 fuses for the 110 V control [2]. If indicator light H617 is not lit, check the protective switch F310 of the 24 VDC feed transformer and circuit breaker F450 [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the drilling feed pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Begin by testing the **feed pressure regulating valve (20)** and/or the **feed deviation valve (216)** to see if they adjust properly [9, 10]. If they do not, plug the feed pressure line and retest to determine if the feed cylinder is faulty or if the valves themselves need repair or replacement [11]. Additionally, verify if the **feed pilot control pressure** is at the correct **19-21 bar** range [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What role does the integrated brake valve (267) play in the braking system?
questions.answer: The **integrated brake valve (267)** directs hydraulic oil either to the parking and service brake circuits or to the secondary control circuit [9]. It utilizes pressure reducing/relieving valves (267.06 and 267.07) to adjust the service brake pressure to the rear and front axles according to the angle of the brake pedal [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The rotation pressure gauge shows insufficient pressure during drilling operations [6].
*   **Cause:** Low rotation pressure can be caused by a faulty rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65), severe underfeed due to low feed pressure (which causes the drill bit to lose contact with the rock), or an internal leak in the rock drill rotation motor [7-9]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Check the setting of the LS-pressure relief valve (65) and clean, repair, or replace it if it cannot reach the recommended 180 bar [7]. If underfeed is the issue, adjust the feed deviation valve (216) to set the rotation pressure between 80 and 100 bar (100-120 bar for RD314), and verify that the feed pilot pressure at M1 is approximately 19-21 bar [8]. If the pressure still remains persistently low, replace the leaking rock drill rotation motor [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the powerpack does not start or stops?
questions.answer: Make sure that the main switch is on** and verify that the water pump or compressor switches are in the running position [1]. Check the indicator lights ground; if the fault relay is ON, **H106 will be indicating** [1]. If the voltage meter shows no reading, check the **circuit breaker F317** and the **fuses F310** for the 110 V control [1]. Finally, if the **indicator light H617** is not lit, check the **protective switch F310** of the 24 VDC feed transformer and the **circuit breaker F450** [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the hydraulic filters monitored and what are their bypass pressure limits?
questions.answer: The **pressure filter** triggers an indicator light (H611) if the pressure difference across the filter exceeds **5 bar**, and its built-in bypass valve opens if the difference exceeds **7 bar** [8]. The **return filter** triggers an indicator light (H607) if the pressure difference rises above **2 bar**, and its bypass valve opens at **3 bar** [9]. To avoid false alarms caused by high oil viscosity, both monitoring indicators are bypassed when the hydraulic oil is cold (below 30 °C) [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if drilling does not stop due to no automatic return of the rock drill from the front end?
questions.answer: Check the positions of **switches S73 and S74**, as the automatic return does not work in the manual position [6]. Check the operation of the **front limit pressure switch S80** [6]. Verify if **relays K70 and K71** pull at the front limit, and if **relay K78** pulls at the front limit with a 6-second delay [6]. Finally, check the operation of **Y47** at the front limit via its LED indicator; if the LED illuminates, you must inspect the operation of the hydraulic system [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps for a "CAN-High defective" (code 10100) fault?
questions.answer: Check the wiring for an open circuit fault and repair or replace it if necessary [1]. Then, switch on the ignition, delete the fault memory in the ECU engine control (e.g., MR-PLD) and in the SG FRE, and perform a functional check [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the power pack main contactor is clapping when started?
questions.answer: This usually indicates that the power supply network is too weak [5]. Check the supply voltage and verify the dimensioning of the supply network, as well as the cross-sectional area and length of the supply cable [5]. You should also check the control voltage [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the repair procedure when the engine control system detects that the CAN data is not plausible (code 10102)?
questions.answer: You should resolve any actual faults present in the SG FRE, except for CAN data bus fault codes 10201, 00202, and 10203. Afterwards, perform a functional check [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps when there is "no connection to CAN" (code 10104)?
questions.answer: First, check the CAN connection to the SG FRE. Inspect all cables, connectors, plug connectors, and electrical components for damage, proper connection, loose contacts, and corrosion, and repair them if necessary [2]. Next, remove the engine CAN bus fault in the SG FRE. Once communication with the ECU engine control (e.g., MR-PLD) is restored, check the calibration of the ECU engine control for one-wire capability [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is indicated by the SLU oil flow / air pressure error / stabilizer pressure indicator light (H72)?
questions.answer: The H72 light is continuously on if a shank lubrication unit (SLU) oil flow or air pressure error occurs, which stops automatic drilling [19-23]. The operator must reset it by restarting the percussion or rotation [20]. If the H72 light flashes, it indicates the stabilizer pressure is too low or too high; drilling will continue once the pressure returns to the permissible range without needing a manual reset [19, 21-24]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the diesel engine failing to start?
questions.answer: Verify the battery isolation switch is ON, the parking brake is engaged, and the drive selector is in the middle position [3]. Additionally, ensure all emergency stop devices are reset, check the fuel level, and verify that the automatic fuse on the main switchgear cabinet and battery circuit fuses F11, F12, and F13 have not tripped [3]. Ensure the fire suppression system is not preventing the start [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps if the **working lights do not work**?
questions.answer: Inspect for a burnt working light bulb or a disconnected lighting plug [5]. For 110V lights, check the **lighting transformer’s protective fuse F310**, the **working lights circuit breaker F314**, and the **fault current protector switch F311** [5]. You should also check the **circuit breaker F317**, the **protective switch F318** (for the 24 VDC source), and the **circuit breaker F450** [5, 6]. If the external transformer is overloaded and hot, its thermal protector will switch the lights off until it cools down [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specifications for the hydraulic powerpacks and pump flow outputs?
questions.answer: The drill is equipped with two **HPP575 (75 kW) hydraulic powerpacks** [1]. The hydraulic system utilizes a variable displacement pump (1) for the percussion, feed, and boom circuits with a flow output of **30-45 l/min**, and a separate variable displacement pump (50) for the rotation circuit with an output of **15-20 l/min** [2]. The flow controllers for these pumps are set to **22-30 bar** for the percussion pump and **20-23 bar** for the rotation pump [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the manually controlled fast feed is not working?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Manually controlled fast feed fails to operate in either direction, though other drilling functions may still work [2].
*   **Cause:** This is usually caused by a sticking spool in the feed directional valve (23) or a completely faulty fast feed pilot control valve (33) [3, 4]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Install pressure gauges to measuring points M2 and M3 and run the fast feed back and forth. If the measuring points receive approximately 30 bar pressure but there is no feed movement, stop the powerpack, remove the front cover of the feed directional valve (23), and carefully clean the spool and valve housing [3, 5]. If measuring points M2 and M3 receive no pressure at all, replace the faulty fast feed pilot control valve (33) [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the stabilizer maximum and reference pressures adjusted?
questions.answer: The stabilizer maximum pressure is adjusted to a factory setting of 110 bar using the pressure reducing/relieving valve (141) [15]. This is done by running the feed cylinder against the front limit and turning the valve until 110 bar is shown on the stabilizer pressure gauge (146) [15, 16]. The stabilizer reference pressure (used to compensate for the mass of the drilling equipment) is adjusted to a factory setting of 30 bar using the pressure reducing valve (145) [17, 18]. This is calibrated while running the rock drill against the rear limit and reading the pressure from measuring point R [18]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the boom's automatic parallelism is not working properly, indicated by a loss of parallel holding?
questions.answer: The first indication of this failure is faulty seals in the third chamber of the boom swing or lift cylinder [3]. To pinpoint the faulty seals, you must test the seals according to the "Testing the lift/swing cylinder seals" procedure [3]. Another potential cause is a faulty O-ring or worn valve seat causing leakage in the pressure relief or overcenter valve; to locate the exact malfunction, disconnect the hoses one by one between the valve block and the control valve and replace any damaged or worn parts [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose very stiff steering on the drill carrier?
questions.answer: Stiff steering can be caused by a damaged **relief valve** or altered pressure adjustment, requiring a pressure check and potential valve replacement [18, 19]. Other causes include a damaged hydraulic pump, **leaking steering cylinder seals** (which can be identified if the cylinder heats up abnormally after several steering operations), or a damaged steering valve [19]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the issue of the feed moving backwards during drilling?
questions.answer: This issue is typically caused by a leaking non-return valve located between the feed transfer cylinder and the control valve, which requires cleaning the valve and replacing any damaged or worn parts [3]. Alternatively, it could be caused by leaking piston seals on the feed transfer cylinder or another external leak, in which case you must replace the piston seals [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined pressure levels for the pilot control, stabilizer, and anti-jamming systems?
questions.answer: The general **pilot control pressure is 30 bar**, while the specific feed pilot control pressure is maintained at **19-21 bar** [4]. The **stabilizer control pressures** are set to a minimum of 50 bar, a maximum of 110 bar, and a reference pressure of 30 bar [7]. The **anti-jamming sensitivity pressure is 120 bar** (or 140 bar for the RD314 rock drill) [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the **diesel engine will not start**?
questions.answer: Ensure that the **battery isolation switch is in the ON position**, the **parking brake is engaged**, the drive selector is in the middle position, and all **emergency stop devices** have been reset [3]. You should also verify the battery condition and fuel level, check if the fire suppression system is preventing the start, and inspect the **battery circuit fuses (F11, F12, F13)** and the automatic fuse on the main switchgear cabinet to see if they have tripped [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a "CAN-Low defective" (code 10101) fault diagnosed and resolved?
questions.answer: Check the wire for an open circuit fault and repair or replace it as needed [2]. Switch on the ignition, delete the fault memory in the ECU engine control (e.g., MR-PLD) and the SG FRE, and perform a functional check [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the procedures to follow when the drilling feed pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Start by checking the operation of the feed pressure regulating valve (20) and/or the feed deviation valve (216) [4]. Start the powerpack, lock the control lever of the feed pilot control valve (31) into the front position, and check if the valves (20) and (216) adjust the pressure correctly by reading the value on the feed pressure gauge (21) [4]. If the valves do not adjust properly, plug the feed pressure line and retest; if they still fail to adjust, clean, repair, or replace the faulty valve (20) and/or (216) [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specified maximum pressure settings for the percussion, rotation, and feed circuits?
questions.answer: The **full-power percussion pressure ranges from 190 to 240 bar**, depending on the specific rock drill model and feed combination [5]. The maximum pressure of the **rotation circuit is limited to 180 bar** [5]. The **maximum fast feed pressure is set to 210 bar** for TF/CF 500 feeds, and **180 bar** for TFX/CFX 500 feeds [5]. The system's overall **main pressure relief valve** is factory-set to **250 or 270 bar** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the hydraulic receiver oil level indicator (H602) to activate, and what is the correct response?
questions.answer: Indicator H602 turns on and stops the power pack, compressor, and water pumps if the hydraulic oil level drops below the allowed minimum for over 3 seconds [15, 16, 18]. The operator must add a sufficient amount of oil and push the reset button (S505) to clear the fault before restarting [15, 16, 18]. If the H602 light is blinking instead of solid, it indicates the shank lubrication oil level is too low [16, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a lack of communication with the MR over the CAN link (+CPC4-eCAN2 - MR) (codes 12202 or 12214)?
questions.answer: Check the engine CAN wiring and verify the configuration to ensure the MR parameter and the +CPC4-eCAN2 parameter 1/01 are set to equal functionality for one-wire capability [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary functions of the variable displacement pumps (1) and (50) in the drilling hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The variable displacement pump (1) provides the oil flow output for the percussion, feed, boom hydraulics, and pilot control (as well as the optional stabilizer) [1]. The variable displacement pump (50) is dedicated to providing oil flow output for the rotation circuit [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the setpoint for the anti-jamming activation pressure and how is it calibrated?
questions.answer: The recommended range for anti-jamming pressure is 110 to 140 bar, with a factory setting of 120 bar (or 140 bar for the RD314 rock drill) [19]. It is adjusted using the anti-jamming valve (34) [19]. Disconnect and plug the rotation hoses, turn the rotation speed regulating valve (59) closed, and install a pressure gauge at measuring point M3 [20, 21]. Lock the rotation and feed pilot control levers to the back position, temporarily adjust the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) to the desired anti-jamming pressure (e.g., 120 bar), and then adjust the anti-jamming valve (34) until the M3 gauge shows a feed pilot control pressure of approximately 19-21 bar [21, 22]. Afterward, remember to reset the rotation LS-pressure relief valve (65) back to 180 bar [23]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps if the working lights are not functioning?
questions.answer: First, check for a burnt working light bulb or a disconnected lighting plug [3]. Next, check the **lighting transformer’s protective fuse F310** [3]. For 110V lights, inspect the **working lights circuit breaker F314** and the **fault current protector switch F311** [3]. You should also check the **circuit breaker F317** for the 110...120 V control voltage, the **protective switch F318** of the 24 VDC source, and the **circuit breaker F450** [3, 4]. If the external transformer is overloaded and too hot, allow it to cool down so the thermal protector can automatically reset [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components are responsible for maintaining and controlling the percussion pressure?
questions.answer: The **percussion line pressure compensator (2)** keeps the percussion pressure constant regardless of variations in the input pressure [1]. The actual oil flow to the rock drill is controlled by the **percussion main valve (3)**, which is opened and closed by the **percussion selector valve (4)** according to the pilot control valve [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the standard CAN bus wiring connections identified in the electrical system?
questions.answer: An example of CAN bus wiring identifies the following pin connections: Pin 1 is Vcc, Pin 2 is Can low, Pin 3 is Ground, Pin 4 is Can high, and Pin 5 is the Shield (ground) [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What could cause the powerpack to start but stop after a while, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: The **compressor temperature may have risen above 115 °C**, which stops the power pack until it drops below 112 °C, or the **hydraulic oil temperature may have exceeded 75 °C** (indicated by light **H610**) [2]. A **"shank lubrication oil level low" signal (H608)** will also stop all powerpacks with a 3-second delay, requiring you to add SLCU oil to restart [2]. If the **hydraulic oil level drops below the minimum (H602 is lit)** for over 3 seconds, add oil and press the **pressure switch reset button S505** to restart [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning indicates a Fire System discharge or fault, and what happens to the machine?
questions.answer: The Fire System Status panel features lights for "Tank Pressure Low" or "System Fault or Discharge", and an alarm will sound with a loud siren if the fire suppression system activates [34-37]. If activated, the system triggers an automatic engine shutdown with a 6-second delay [35, 37]. The operator can press a delay extension button to gain an additional 20 seconds to move the machine to a safe location [35, 37]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the "Transmission failure/malfunction" indicator signify?
questions.answer: This indicator comes on to warn the operator that the transmission oil pressure is too low or the transmission oil temperature is too high [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the different signal types identified on a CAN module contact in the electrical drawings?
questions.answer: The CAN module signal types are identified by specific abbreviations: DI (digital input), DO (digital output), AI (analog input), PWM (pulse width modulated), FB (feedback), GND (ground), and REF (reference voltage) [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a malfunctioning **110...120 V 1-phase socket outlet** diagnosed?
questions.answer: The issue is typically caused by a load that is too great or a tripped **ground fault sensor** [7]. To diagnose, check the **protective switch F310** of the transformer and the **circuit breaker F313** of the socket outlet terminal [7]. Similar to the working lights, if the transformer is overloaded and overheats, the thermal protector will switch the socket load off and reset automatically once it cools down [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the diesel engine overspeed warning siren (H24) to activate?
questions.answer: The warning light flashes and the siren beeps if the diesel engine speed exceeds 2500 rpm [3, 4]. The operator must decrease the engine speed to prevent equipment damage [3-5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if there is "no connection to CAN" (code 10104)?
questions.answer: Check the CAN connection to the SG FRE by inspecting all cables, connectors, plug connectors, and electrical components for damage, correct connection, loose contacts, and corrosion [3]. Repair if necessary, then remove the engine CAN bus fault in the SG FRE [3]. Once communication with the ECU engine control is restored, check its calibration for one-wire capability [1, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the priority valve (262) in the carrier's steering system?
questions.answer: The **priority valve (262)** distributes the hydraulic oil delivered from the gear pump (251). It directs the oil primarily to the **steering valve (263)** for steering operations, and secondarily to the carrier's auxiliary functions [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the percussion full-power maximum pressure is too high?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The percussion pressure during full-power drilling exceeds the maximum recommended levels (e.g., above 210 bar) [13, 14].
*   **Cause:** This indicates an incorrectly adjusted or faulty percussion max. pressure relief valve (7), or a loosened load-sensing line orifice (9) inside the control block [14].
*   **Corrective Action:** First, try to correctly adjust the percussion max. pressure relief valve (7). If the valve does not respond to adjustments, clean, repair, or replace it [14]. If the valve is functioning properly but pressure remains too high, stop the powerpack, remove the adapter from port 9 of the feed and percussion control block, and carefully retighten the orifice (9) at the bottom of the port [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: How should you pinpoint the fault if the manually controlled fast feed is not working?
questions.answer: First, verify if other drilling functions work; if they do, check the fast feed pilot control pressure by installing pressure gauges to measuring points M2 and M3 of the anti-jamming and return automatics block [6]. Start the powerpack and run the fast feed back and forth using the fast feed pilot control valve (33) [6]. If the measuring points receive approximately 30 bar pressure but the feed pressure gauge (21) shows no reading, the spool of the feed directional valve (23) is likely sticking and its housing must be cleaned [7]. If no pressure is received at M2 and M3, replace the faulty fast feed pilot control valve (33) [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the causes and corrective actions if the feed moves backwards during drilling?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The feed creeps or moves backwards while actively drilling [1].
*   **Cause:** This is typically caused by a leaking non-return valve located between the feed transfer cylinder and the control valve, or by leaking piston seals on the feed transfer cylinder itself [1]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Clean the non-return valve and replace any damaged or worn parts. If the issue persists or an external leak is present, replace the piston seals on the feed transfer cylinder [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD421-60C Technical Manual)

questions.question: If the feed pressure is excessively low during operation and connecting a pressure gauge to the load sensing line connector (LS) of variable displacement pump (1) yields a value significantly different from 210 bar while the feed is run against the rear stopper, which specific electro-proportional valve should be investigated first?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, if the feed or fast feed pressure is excessively low, you should first investigate the **electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)** [1]. 

According to **Section 6.10: Feed / fast feed pressure is too low** (Page 65 of the Drilling Hydraulics manual), if the pressure reading differs essentially from 210 bar during this test, it is likely that this specific valve is stuck [1, 2]. 

You should follow this step-by-step sequence to investigate and resolve the issue:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) [1].
2. Disconnect the electric connector from the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) and run the feed against the rear end stopper [1]. 
3. Verify the pressure at the load sensing line measuring connector (LS), which should be approximately 210 bar [1]. 
4. If the pressure differs essentially from 210 bar, stop the power pack [1, 3].
5. Check, clean and, if necessary, replace the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) [3].
6. Run the feed against the rear end stopper again and check the pressure at the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) [3]. 
7. If the pressure is now approximately 210 bar, conclude the procedure by doing the following [3]:
   * a) Stop the power pack.
   * b) Connect the electric connector back to the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22).
   * c) Remove the pressure gauge from the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) of the pump (1).

questions.question: An operator reports that the yellow STATUS LED on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) is flashing three times; which specific sensor is likely broken or disconnected, and what exact current signal threshold (in mA) triggers this malfunction alert?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, if the yellow STATUS LED on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) flashes three times, it indicates a malfunction with the **air pressure sensor** (identified as component **10** in the SLU assembly or electrically as sensor **B127P** / **B127**) [1-3]. This means the sensor is likely broken or disconnected. 

**Current Signal Threshold:**
The malfunction alert is specifically triggered when the current signal from the air pressure sensor drops **lower than 2 mA** [2]. (The normal operating value for this sensor is between **4 and 20 mA** [2]).

**Troubleshooting Procedure:**
According to the *Shank Lubrication Unit* manual (*Section 8.1.1: CAN troubleshooting*, Page 39), you should perform the following steps to diagnose the issue:
1. Measure the sensor's current signal to verify if it is reading below 2 mA or within the normal 4–20 mA range [4]. 
2. Check the actual SLU air pressure in the system to determine if there is a genuine pressure problem or just a sensor fault [4].

*Reference details:*
*   **Section 3.3 (Page 13):** Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC) - LED Indicators [2, 5]
*   **Section 8.1.1 (Page 39):** CAN troubleshooting [4, 6]

questions.question: If the percussion function remains active continuously whenever the power pack or diesel engine is running—risking severe damage to the rock drill's accumulator seals due to low pressure—which two specific valves in the drilling control valve block (20) must be immediately inspected for being stuck or leaking?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, if the percussion function remains active continuously when the power pack or diesel engine is running, you must immediately inspect the following two valves located in the drilling control valve block (20):

*   **Percussion selector valve (20.9)** [1]
*   **Percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10)** [1]

If either of these valves is stuck and leaking, it allows pressure to constantly reach the rock drill's percussion mechanism [1]. It is critical to repair this fault immediately because operating with too low percussion pressure can cause severe damage to the seals of the accumulators inside the rock drill [2].

**Troubleshooting Procedure**
According to the *Drilling Hydraulics DD422i* manual, Section 6.6 (*Percussion is on all the time when power pack or diesel engine is running*, Page 62), you should perform the following steps:
1. Stop the power pack and/or diesel engine [2]. 
2. Check, clean and replace, if necessary, the valves (20.9) and (20.10) [2].

questions.question: During compressor testing with a heater, if the temperature sensor B240T detects rising heat, at what specific temperature must the control system display a notice pop-up, and at what higher temperature must it trigger an alarm and automatically shut down the compressor?
questions.answer:
During compressor testing with a heater, the control system must display a notice pop-up when the temperature sensor (**B240T**) reaches **105 °C**, and it must trigger an alarm pop-up and automatically shut down the compressor when the temperature reaches **115 °C** [1, 2]. *(Note: The component description in Section 4.1 "Air circuit operation" mentions the sensor sends a notice to the drilling display when the temperature rises to 100 °C [3]).*

According to the **"Checking the function of the thermometer safety limits"** procedure (Sections 5.13.14 and 8.3.14), the step-by-step testing sequence is as follows:
1. Remove the sensor from the compressor's body [1, 2]. 
2. Start the power packs, compressor, and water pump [1, 2]. 
3. Heat the sensor using a heater with an operation range of 0-120 °C and monitor the temperature gauge. **Do not use fire** [1, 2, 4].
4. When the temperature reaches **105 ºC**, check that the system gives a notice pop-up [1, 2]. 
5. When the temperature reaches **115 ºC**, check that the system gives an alarm pop-up and the compressor stops [1, 2].

questions.question: After replacing the feed port shock/anti-cavitation valves, you connect a gauge to measuring point M1 and set the variable displacement pump (1) to 250 bar; what are the precise pressure settings required for the feed port A valve (20.18) and feed port B valve (20.19) when running the feed against their respective stoppers?
questions.answer:
Based on the Drilling Hydraulics manual (Sections 6.10 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" and 6.11 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too high", pages 65–67), the required pressure settings are [1-4]:

*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18):** 200 bar
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19):** 240 bar

Here is the exact step-by-step sequence for adjusting the valves after they are replaced [2-6]:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point (**M1**) of the drilling control valve block (**20**) [2, 4].
2. Use the pressure controller (**B**) to adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) to **250 bar** [2, 4].
3. Run the feed against the front end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.18**) to **200 bar** [4, 5].
4. Run the feed against the rear end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.19**) to **240 bar** [4, 5].
5. Re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) to its standard operating setting as instructed in the section "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" [5, 6].

questions.question: When adjusting the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9), which measuring connector should the pressure gauge be attached to, and what is the exact target pressure reading when applying maximum diesel engine rpm?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, when adjusting the **steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9)**, the pressure gauge should be attached to the measuring connector **MPS** [1]. When applying the maximum diesel engine rpm, the exact target pressure reading is **220 bars** [2].

According to the *Drill carrier C400, C900* manual, **Section 4.7.4: Adjusting steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9)** (Pages 83–84), the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MPS** [1].
2. Loosen the locking nut from the steering circuit main pressure relief valve **(10.9)** and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise to fully open it [1].
3. Start the diesel engine [1].
4. Push the pressurizing stud **(10.23)** and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the "up" position, which will pressurize the carrier hydraulics [1, 2].
5. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm [2].
6. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve **(10.9)** clockwise until the reading on the pressure gauge is exactly **220 bars** [2].
7. Tighten the locking nut of the valve **(10.9)** [2].
8. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle [2].
9. Push the pressurizing stud **(10.23)** and turn it clockwise to lock the stud in the "down" position. Check the pressure gauge to ensure that the pressure level drops to the free circulation level (which is less than 30 bars) [2].
10. Shut down the engine [3].
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **MPS** [3].

questions.question: To correctly set the flow controller (A) on the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1), what specific pressure difference must be maintained between the pump operating pressure and the LS-line pressure?
questions.answer:
To correctly set the flow controller (A) on the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1), a pressure difference of **30 bar** must be maintained between the pump operating pressure and the LS-line pressure [1, 2]. 

According to Section 5.1.2 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" (Pages 46–47 of the Drilling Hydraulics manual), the step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. Remove the protecting cap from the flow controller (A) and loosen the locking nut on the flow controller (A) adjusting screw [2, 3].
2. Open the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) almost fully open by turning it counterclockwise [2].
3. Read the pressure difference (pump operating pressure minus LS-line pressure) from the pump's (1) two pressure gauges [2]. 
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) very carefully clockwise until the pressure difference is exactly 30 bar [2].
5. Tighten the locking nut of the flow controller (A) adjusting screw [4].
6. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure difference again to ensure the setting holds [4].

questions.question: After replacing the feed port shock/anti-cavitation valves, what are the exact pressure settings required for the feed port A valve (20.18) and the feed port B valve (20.19) when measured at point M1 with the pump set to 250 bar?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drilling Hydraulics DD422i* manual, Sections 6.10 ("Feed / fast feed pressure is too low") and 6.11 ("Feed / fast feed pressure is too high") on pages 65–67, the required pressure settings are [1-4]:

*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18):** 200 bar [2, 4]
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19):** 240 bar [2, 4]

Here is the exact step-by-step sequence required to adjust the valves after they are replaced [1-5]:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point (**M1**) of the drilling control valve block (**20**) [1, 4].
2. Use the pressure controller (**B**) to adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) to **250 bar** [1, 4].
3. Run the feed against the front end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.18**) to **200 bar** [2, 4].
4. Run the feed against the rear end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.19**) to **240 bar** [2, 4].
5. Re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) to its normal setting as instructed in the section "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" [2, 5].

questions.question: During the configuration of the optional air line flow meter (39), what specific numerical value must be assigned to the FCTR parameter, and what is the required Analogue End Point (AEP) value for DD/DT series rigs?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, during the configuration of the optional air line flow meter (39), the specific numerical value assigned to the **FCTR (Pipe diameter)** parameter must be **1.50** [1]. For DD/DT series rigs, the required **Analogue End Point (AEP)** value is **213** (which determines the measured value where the output signal is 20 mA) [2].

According to the *Flushing circuit (DD422i, DD422iE)* manual, Section 9.7 "Adjusting the air line flow meter (optional)" (Pages 69–72), the step-by-step sequence to set these parameters is as follows:

1. Open the cabin floor hatch to reach the flow meter controller (1) [3].
2. Push the **Mode/Enter** button (3) repeatedly until `FCTR` is displayed [3].
3. Push the **Set** button (4) and keep it pushed down until `FCTR` starts flashing. After five seconds, the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [3].
4. Push **Set**, keep it pushed down until the value **1.50** is displayed, and then release the button [3].
5. Push **Mode/Enter** briefly and `FCTR` is displayed again [3].
6. (Continue using the Mode/Enter and Set buttons to configure the `OU2` and `ASP` parameters as specified in the manual) [3].
7. Push **Mode/Enter** briefly until `AEP` is displayed [3, 4].
8. Push **Set** and keep it pushed down until `AEP` starts flashing. After five seconds, the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [4].
9. Push **Set**, keep it pushed down until the value **213** is displayed (for DD/DT series), and then release the button [4].
10. Push **Mode/Enter** briefly and `AEP` is displayed again [4].
11. Push **Mode/Enter** repeatedly until the current measured value is displayed, or wait for 15 seconds to allow the unit to return to operating mode [4, 5].

questions.question: To verify the front axle's parking brake release pressure, you must attach a gauge to measuring point C and push stud Y960; what specific pressure range indicates a successful release?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals (*Maintenance Manual* Section 5.6.16, Page 244, and *Drill carrier C400, C900* Section 6.1.15, Pages 117-118), a successful release of the front axle's parking brake is indicated by a pressure range of **26-28 bars** [1, 2]. 

Here is the exact step-by-step sequence to verify the front axle's parking brake release pressure:

1. Attach a pressure gauge to the front axle's parking brake pressure measuring point (**C**) [1, 2].
2. Start the engine [1, 2].
3. Allow the engine to idle [1, 2].
4. Remove the rubber cover (**1**) [1, 2].
5. Push the stud **Y960 (3)** to release the front axle and keep the stud pushed down [1, 2].
6. Verify that the release pressure is **26-28 bars** [1, 2].
7. Release the stud **Y960 (3)** and check from the pressure gauge that the pressure decreases to **0 bar** [1-3].
8. Remove the pressure gauge [2, 3].

questions.question: What are the specific displacements in cubic centimeters (cc) for the percussion and feed pump, the rotation pump, and the HVAC pump on the DD422i powerpack?
questions.answer:
Based on the Technical Specification and Main Components sections of the provided manuals, the specific displacements for the hydraulic pumps on the DD422i powerpack are defined as follows:

*   **Percussion and feed pump:** **110 cc** [1]. This is a variable displacement pump identified as component **4** on the power pack assembly, or pump **1** in the drilling hydraulics schematic [2, 3]. It delivers oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulic systems [3].
*   **Rotation pump:** **60 cc** [1]. This is a variable displacement pump identified as component **5** on the power pack assembly, or pump **2** in the drilling hydraulics schematic [2, 3]. It is dedicated to delivering oil to the rotation hydraulic system [3].
*   **HVAC pump (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning):** **26 cc** [1]. This is a fixed-displacement gear pump identified as component **6** on the left power pack assembly, or pump **3** in the drilling hydraulics schematic [2, 3]. It supplies oil for the HVAC circuit and/or the optional oil-air (OA) cooling system [2, 3].

questions.question: What is the overall length of the drill rig when equipped with a TFi500-14' feed, both with and without the TRR1 rod retainer?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided Technical Specification, the overall length of the Sandvik DD422i drill rig when equipped with the **TFi500-14'** feed is as follows:

*   **Without TRR1 rod retainer:** 13,450 mm [1].
*   **With TRR1 rod retainer:** 13,485 mm [1]. 

These dimensions can be found in the "Technical drawings" section of the Technical Specification under the "Type of feed" dimensions table [1].

questions.question: What is the total weight of the cabin assembly, and what specific size and part number of lifting eye bolts must be used to hoist it safely?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Weights and dimensions DD422i* manual (Section 5.1 "Cabin", Page 45), the specifications for lifting the cabin assembly are as follows:

*   **Total Weight:** The weight of the cabin assembly is **1790 kg** [1].
*   **Lifting Eye Bolts:** To hoist it safely, you must use **four (4) M20** size lifting eye bolts, specifically part number **AF04100021** [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25), what specific pressure value must the pressure controller (B) be set to while observing the gauge connected to measuring point MP2, before backing off valve (20.25) until the pressure drops to exactly 270 bar?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drilling Hydraulics DD422i* manual, Section 5.2 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve" (Pages 48–50), the pressure controller (**B**) must be set to exactly **280 bar** while observing the gauge connected to measuring point **MP2** before backing off the main pressure relief valve (**20.25**) [1, 2].

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment:

1. Stop the power pack [3]. 
2. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (**20.25**) [3]. 
3. Tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (**20.25**) almost to its end (over 270 bar) [1, 3]. 
4. Remove the caps from the flow controller (**A**) and the pressure controller (**B**) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) and undo the locking nuts of their adjusting spindles [1]. 
5. Open the adjusting screws of the pressure controller (**B**) and the flow controller (**A**) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [1]. 
6. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (**MP2**) of the drilling control valve block (**20**) [1]. 
7. Start the power pack [1]. 
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (**A**) fully closed (clockwise). Note that the pump is now operating at constant pressure [1, 2]. 
9. **Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows 280 bar** [2]. 
10. Loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (**20.25**) until adjusting begins to effect. The valve begins to fizz when restricting the pressure and the pressure value on the pressure gauge drops to exactly **270 bar** [2]. 
11. Adjust the values of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) as instructed in its specific adjustment section [2, 4]. 
12. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (**20.25**) [4]. 
13. Stop the power pack (taking care not to let oil flow pass through the main pressure relief valve for a long time as it heats the hydraulic system) [4].

questions.question: According to the shank lubrication adjustment specifications, what is the required lubrication amount (in g/h) for the RD520 and RD525 rock drills, and what specific pressure value should the restrictor valve be adjusted to using the air pressure reading on the GUI?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the specifications and adjustment procedures for the shank lubrication system are as follows:

**Required Lubrication Amount:**
For both the RD520 and RD525 rock drills, the required shank lubrication amount is **180–250 g/h** [1, 2]. 

**Restrictor Valve Pressure Setting and Procedure:**
When adjusting the restrictor valve (2), the specific target pressure value using the air pressure reading on the GUI is exactly **4 bars** [3, 4].

According to the *Flushing circuit* manual (*Section 9.4: Adjusting the restrictor valve*, Pages 65–66), the step-by-step sequence to achieve this setting is:

1. Loosen the locking nut **(1)** of the restrictor valve **(2)** [3]. 
2. Turn the adjusting screw **(3)** fully open [3].
3. On the GUI, select **→ Troubleshooting → Shank Lubrication** [3].
4. Start both power packs [3].
5. Push the button **(4)** to select boom 1 [3].
6. Push the button **(5)** to activate air flushing for boom 1 [3].
7. Push the button **(6)** to select boom 2 [3].
8. Push the button **(5)** to activate air flushing for boom 2 [3].
9. Tighten the adjusting screw **(3)** until the Air pressure reading on the GUI rises to **4 bars** [3].
10. Tighten the locking nut **(1)** of the restrictor valve [4].
11. Check the Air pressure reading again from the GUI. If the reading has changed from the correct value of 4 bars [4]:
    * a) Loosen the locking nut **(1)** [4].
    * b) Tighten/loosen the adjusting screw **(3)** until the value is exactly **4 bars** [4].
    * c) Tighten the locking nut **(1)** [4].
12. Push the button **(4)** and then push the button **(5)** to deactivate boom 1 air flushing [4].
13. Push the button **(6)** and then push the button **(5)** to deactivate boom 2 air flushing [4].

questions.question: Based on the recommended drill rod rotation speeds, what is the target rotation speed (± 10%) for a Ø45 mm drill bit using the RD525 rock drill, and how does this compare to the recommended rpm for the RDX5/RD520?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drilling Hydraulics DD422i* manual, Section 5.4 "Adjusting rotation speed" (Page 51), the recommended rotation speeds are as follows:

*   **RD525 rock drill:** The target rotation speed for a Ø45 mm drill bit is **240 rpm** (± 10%) [1]. 
*   **RDX5 / RD520 rock drills:** The target rotation speed for the same Ø45 mm drill bit is **200 rpm** (± 10%) [1].

This means the RD525 requires a faster rotation speed (by 40 rpm) compared to the RDX5/RD520 for that specific bit size [1]. 

**Adjustment Procedure:**
To set these target speeds, you must use the rotation speed encoder (note that this adjustment can only be made in feed-percussion follow-up and manual drilling modes) [2]. 
1. Turn the encoder **counterclockwise** to decrease the speed [2].
2. Turn the encoder **clockwise** to increase the speed [2].

questions.question: What is the specified maximum percussion rate (in Hz) for the RD525 hydraulic rock drill, and what specific shank adapter thread type is required when drilling 43–45 mm holes using an Alpha 340 tool?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Technical Specification* manual under the "Hydraulic rock drill" section, the specifications are as follows:

*   **Maximum Percussion Rate:** The specified percussion rate for the **RD525** hydraulic rock drill is **93 Hz** [1].
*   **Shank Adapter Thread Type:** When drilling **43–45 mm** holes using an **Alpha 340** tool, the required shank adapter thread type is **T38 (male)**. The exact recommended tool configuration for this hole size is **T38 – H35 – Alpha 340** [1].

questions.question: If the machine is equipped with the optional power extractor, what specific pressure value is the maximum percussion pressure limited to when the power extractor on/off valve (21.1) is activated by pressing button B on the rock drill joystick?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drilling Hydraulics DD422i* manual (Section 4.5 "Percussion", under the "Power extractor (optional)" heading, Page 38), when the optional power extractor is switched on by pressing **button B** on the rock drill movements joystick, it activates the coil **Y128** of the power extractor on/off valve (**21.1**) [1]. 

Simultaneously, the maximum percussion pressure is strictly limited to **150 bar** [1].

questions.question: According to the technical specifications, what is the exact parallel coverage area for the SB60 boom, and what are the total face drilling coverage area dimensions (height x width) for the DD422i rig?
questions.answer:
According to the *Technical Specification* manual, the exact parallel coverage area for the SB60 boom is **54 m²** [1]. 

For the DD422i rig, the total face drilling coverage area is 60 m², with specific dimensions of **6,590 mm (height) x 10,270 mm (width)** [2, 3].

questions.question: What are the precise inward turning angles required for both the inner boom and the outer boom when safely stowing the DD422i into its tramming position?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Operator's Manual DD422i* (Section 4.9.3 "Tramming position of the rig", Pages 188–189), when safely stowing the DD422i into its tramming position, the required inward turning angles are:

*   **Inner boom:** 6° inwards [1].
*   **Outer boom:** 11° inwards [1].

To correctly safely stow the machine into this tramming position, the manual outlines the following step-by-step sequence [1, 2]:

1. Turn the booms and feeds in the direction of the machine.
2. Retract the booms and feeds to the rear positions.
3. Lay down the rear ends of the feed beams lightly against the booms.
4. If on a level surface or when the drilling module is facing downhill, lift the rear jacks first, then the front jacks. If the drilling module is facing uphill, lift the front jacks first, then the rear jacks.
5. If the rig is equipped with a front jack beam, retract it.

questions.question: What are the exact maximum working pressures specified for the TF5 feed cylinder during forward feed and return movements, and which specific shock/anti-cavitation valves (by ID) protect actuator ports A2 and B2?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the exact maximum working pressures specified for the **TF5 feed cylinder** are:

*   **Forward feed:** 200 bar [1].
*   **Return movement:** 240 bar [1].

These values can be found in the *Cylinder feed TF5 / TFX5* manual (Section 3.4: Feed cylinder, Page 17) [1].

The specific shock/anti-cavitation valves in the drilling control valve block (20) that protect actuator ports A2 and B2 against pressure peaks and external forces are:

*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18):** Protects port A2 by limiting its maximum pressure to **200 bar** [2, 3].
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19):** Protects port B2 by limiting its maximum pressure to **240 bar** [2, 3].

These details are located in the *Drilling Hydraulics DD422i* manual (Section 3.1.1, Pages 13–14, and Section 4.5, Page 42) [2, 3].

questions.question: In the boom control valve block, which specific component (by ID number) provides pressure feedback to stabilize the boom's downward movement, and what is the maximum pressure limit set by the boom circuit's main pressure relief valve (10)?
questions.answer:
Based on the *SB Boom* manual, Section 3.2 "Boom control valve block", the components and their specifications are as follows:

*   **Pressure Feedback Component:** The specific component that provides pressure feedback to stabilize the boom's downward movement is the **pin spool (8)** [1]. This component is located specifically in the boom lift section and operates only during the boom lower-function [1].
*   **Maximum Pressure Limit:** The boom circuit's main pressure relief valve **(10)** limits the boom/percussion circuit's main pressure to a maximum of **270 bar** [1]. *(Note: The manual specifies that the normal maximum operating pressure is actually determined by the pump pressure controller [1]).*

questions.question: When parking the rig or tramming it onto a transport platform with the booms correctly stowed, what are the absolute maximum allowed front tilt and side tilt inclination angles before tipping hazards occur?
questions.answer:
When parking the rig or tramming it onto a transport platform, provided the booms are strictly secured in their tramming position, the absolute maximum allowed inclination angles are:

*   **Maximum front tilt angle: 15°** [1-3]
*   **Maximum side tilt angle: 5°** [1-3]

These limits are outlined in the "Maximum inclination angles" sections of the *Maintenance Manual DD422i* (Page 49), the *Operator's Manual DD422i* (Page 49), and the *Technical Manual - CS IV* (Pages 42–43) [1-7]. 

Operating, tramming, or parking the machine on a slope that exceeds these specified angles presents a severe **tipping hazard** that could result in death, severe injury, or property damage [4-6]. Furthermore, if the machine is on a slippery surface such as ice or smooth rock, the safe inclination angle is noticeably smaller than on non-slippery surfaces [4, 5, 7].

questions.question: What are the functions of key fuses and breakers such as F41, F58, and F60 located in the DQ cabinet?
questions.answer: The DQ cabinet houses primary 24 VDC circuit breakers and fuses [13, 14]. F41 is the 240 A battery main breaker [15, 16]. F58 is the 80 A master branch fuse for the 24 VDC control system, and F60 acts as the 125 A diesel alternator master fuse [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you fix the percussion system if it remains on continuously?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion is on all the time whenever the power pack or diesel engine is running [19].
*   **Cause:** The percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck and leaking, which continuously allows pressure to reach the rock drill's percussion mechanism [19].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and diesel engine immediately [20]. It is critical to repair this immediately because operating with too low percussion pressure can damage the seals of the accumulators inside the rock drill [20]. Inspect, clean, and replace valves (20.9) and (20.10) as needed [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct pressure controller and pilot pressure settings for the drilling hydraulics?
questions.answer: The pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve limits the pilot pressure to a level between 30 and 45 bar [6, 7]. The pressure controller for the percussion/feed pump must be set to 255 bar for the RD525 rock drill, and 230 bar for both the RD520 and RDX5 models [8]. The flow controller for the percussion/feed pump is adjusted to maintain a 30 bar pressure difference, while the rotation pump flow controller is set to maintain a 23 bar difference [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What alarms are triggered if the Sandvik fire suppression system detects a system fault or pressure drop?
questions.answer: If the double pressure switch detects that system pressure has fallen below its setting (due to a leak or system activation), it triggers an audiovisual alarm [9-11]. A red warning light for system fault or discharge will turn on, a loud siren/audible alarm will sound, and a 6-second engine shutdown delay timer will begin [6, 7, 9-11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where the power pack will not start?
questions.answer: Check the screen for alarm messages, ensure the starter isolator switch (S2) is in the ON position, check the mains electric supply connection, verify the main switch (Q1) is in position 1 (ON), and confirm all emergency stop buttons have been released [1, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the charge pump (1.2) located within the hydrostatic transmission (HST) pump (1) assembly?
questions.answer: The charge pump (1.2) is a fixed-displacement gear pump that delivers charge oil to the closed-loop high-pressure system to replace oil that flows to the receiver due to internal leaks [12-14]. It also generates pilot pressure for the servo cylinder (1.4), which adjusts the angle of the HST variable displacement pump (1.1), and serves as the pressure source to release the parking brakes [12, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the A1 and A2 circuit boards, and where are they located?
questions.answer: The A1 and A2 circuit boards are located inside the cabin and contain the circuit breakers/fuses for various specific rig functions [19, 20]. For example, on both boards, fuse F2 (10 A) supplies power to the Boom Controllers (BC), Drilling Controllers (DC), and Rod handler Controller (RC) [19-22]. They also house fuses for cabin lights, tramming panels, and modules like the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) and Central Greasing Unit (CGU) [19-24]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined pump displacements and required flow rates for the percussion and feed circuits on the DD422i?
questions.answer: The percussion and feed pump has a displacement of 110 cc [1]. The required flow rates at maximum percussion pressure and normal operating temperature depend on the rock drill model: 125-135 l/min for the RD525, 105-115 l/min for the RD520, and 100-115 l/min for the RDX5 [2]. The feed circuit flow rate is 4-8 l/min for all models [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you fix a percussion pressure that is too low despite functioning electric and control systems?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack [8]. Check, clean, and if necessary, replace the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) and re-adjust it [8]. If the problem persists, check, clean, and replace the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) [8]. Also, check if either of the LS-line orifices (20.12) or (20.13) is blocked, which can also cause the pressure to drop [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the proper procedure for handling a tripped circuit breaker or blown fuse, such as the 80 A master branch fuse (F58) or 125 A diesel alternator master fuse (F60)?
questions.answer: A tripped breaker or a burnt fuse is an indicator of an underlying failure, such as an overload or short circuit [6]. Before resetting the breaker to position I or replacing the fuse, you must locate and repair the root failure [6]. **Always use the original fuse size and type**, and never replace a fuse with one that has a higher ampere value than the original component [6]. Reset circuit breakers to position I only when the **main switch (Q1)** is in position 0 (OFF) if connected to the power supply network [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a CAN control bus that is completely off or experiencing excessive data transfer errors on the SLU?
questions.answer: Check the CAN-ERR (red) indicator light on the SLU. A single flash means the CAN control error counter has reached its alarm limit due to too many errors, which will reset automatically when data transfer is restored. If the light is lit continuously, the CAN control bus is completely off (Bus off) [3-5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it mean if the yellow STATUS LED on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) flashes three times?
questions.answer: Three flashes indicate a malfunction with the air pressure sensor, meaning the sensor is broken or disconnected [12]. To resolve this, maintenance or the operator should check the SLU air pressure and measure the sensor current signal, which should normally read between 4 and 20 mA (the error triggers if it is below 2 mA) [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does Cummins engine fault code 5939 indicate regarding the CAN bus, and what is the description of the failure?
questions.answer: Fault code **5939** (SPN 520968, FMI 9) indicates a **Machine Constrained Operation due to an Abnormal Update Rate** [1]. This means that no communication or an invalid data transfer rate has been detected on the J1939 data link (CAN bus) between the Engine Control Module (ECM) and the machine electronic control unit [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is an incorrect feed or fast feed speed diagnosed when pressures and control systems are otherwise normal?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block to check the pilot pressure, which should be between 30 and 45 bars when loaded [5]. If the pressure is correct, the fault is likely a stuck feed valve main spool (20.16) or an issue with the feed pilot control valves (20.20 and 20.21), which should be removed and inspected [5-7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a total loss of communication between the Engine Control Module (ECM) and the machine electronic control unit?
questions.answer: This is diagnosed by the presence of Cummins engine fault code 5939 (SPN 520968, FMI 9), which indicates a "Machine Constrained Operation - Abnormal Update Rate", meaning no communication or an invalid data transfer rate was detected on the J1939 CAN data link [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the air line and water inlet pressure reducing valves calibrated in the flushing circuit?
questions.answer: To adjust the air line pressure reducing valve, connect a pressure gauge to its measuring connector, turn the adjusting screw fully counterclockwise, start the compressor, and then turn the screw clockwise until the gauge reads approximately 6 bar (it can be adjusted up to 7 bar depending on the air network) [19, 20]. The mine's water inlet pressure before the water booster pump is adjusted using a pressure reducing valve; turning its knob clockwise increases pressure and counterclockwise decreases it, setting it to 2-7 bar according to drilling conditions to ensure the total flushing pressure after the booster pump remains under 25 bar [21]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does Cummins engine fault code 5939 indicate about the CAN bus network?
