questions.answer: Fault code 5939 (J1939 SPN 520968, FMI 9) indicates a "Machine Constrained Operation - Abnormal Update Rate" [6]. This means that either no communication or an invalid data transfer rate has been detected on the J1939 CAN data link between the Engine Control Module (ECM) and the machine electronic control unit [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the power pack stops unexpectedly during operation?
questions.answer: You should check the screen for any alarm messages, verify that none of the circuit breakers in the MQ cabinet have tripped, ensure all emergency stop buttons are released, and make sure that the pilot circuit is functional [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps are required if the percussion pressure is too high, even though sensors and control systems are working correctly?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack [7]. Check, clean, and if necessary, replace the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) [7]. If this does not remedy the situation, check that both of the LS-line orifices (20.12) and (20.13) are properly seated in their place in the drilling control valve block [7]. If either orifice is loosened, tighten it carefully [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is hydraulic oil filtered in the main drilling circuits, and what are the specific filter components involved?
questions.answer: Oil coming from the percussion/feed variable displacement pump (1) is filtered by the pressure filter (8), which utilizes a 20 µm filter element [4, 5]. Return oil from the steering, brake, hydrostatic transmission, drilling, and carrier functions is collected in the hydraulic oil receiver (4) and filtered by the return oil filter (4.3) using a 10 µm return filter element (4.3.2) [6, 7]. Additionally, an optional by-pass filter (10) can provide 2 µm fine filtering for oil taken from the rotation circuit [4, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Within the drilling control valve block (20), which specific valves control the primary rock drill functions (rotation, percussion, and feed)?
questions.answer: Inside the drilling control valve block (20), the rotation valve main spool (20.1) directs oil flow to the rotation mechanism [9]. The percussion selector valve (20.9) controls the opening and closing of the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10), which ultimately directs oil flow to the rock drill's percussion mechanism [10]. The feed valve main spool (20.16) directs oil flow to the feed cylinder to control forward and backward movements [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct settings for the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2) controllers and how are they adjusted?
questions.answer: The flow controller (A) should be adjusted to a pressure difference of 23 bar (pump operating pressure minus LS-line pressure) [10, 11]. To adjust the pressure controller (B), open its adjusting screw fully counterclockwise, run the rock drill rotation against a plug, and carefully turn the screw clockwise until the pressure gauge connected to the check valve block reads 200 bar [10, 12]. Always lock the adjustments with the locking nuts once the correct values are achieved [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What alarm occurs if the SLU control valve shut-off ball is left in the wrong position?
questions.answer: If the control valve shut-off ball is left open or closed for four operational cycles (deviating from normal operation), an alarm switches on, the user receives an error message, and drilling stops automatically [14]. The operator must correct the valve position, and the alarm will reset when pumping returns to normal [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What could be the problem if the CAN-RUN (green) LED indicator on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) is completely off?
questions.answer: If the **CAN-RUN indicator is completely off**, it means there is no supply voltage to the control unit, or the unit is currently resetting or down [5, 6]. You should wait a few seconds, and if the light still does not switch on, it indicates that the control unit is not functioning properly [7]. *(Note: If it is flashing, it means the unit is on standby, the CAN bus connection is broken, or it is awaiting a start command from the CAN bus control unit [8])*. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) if it loses power or communication?
questions.answer: Check the LED indicators on the SLU control unit; if the green CAN-RUN indicator is completely off, it means there is no supply voltage or the unit is malfunctioning [8, 9]. If the red CAN-ERR indicator is lit continuously, it indicates that the CAN control bus is completely off [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the role of the Engine Control Module (ECM) and how does it communicate with the machine?
questions.answer: The Engine Control Module (ECM) manages the diesel engine operations, controls the SCR aftertreatment system, and initiates automatic exhaust system cleaning when needed [5, 6]. It communicates with the machine's primary electronic control unit over the primary J1939 CAN data link network. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the SLU's yellow STATUS LED to flash four times, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: Four flashes indicate a malfunction with the lubrication oil level switch, meaning the oil level is below the minimum limit or the sensor is broken/disconnected [12, 13]. The operator should check the lubrication oil level in the tank and fill it if necessary; if the tank is full, check the sensor current signal (the error triggers if it drops below 1.7 mA) [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should you check if the power pack stops unexpectedly during operation?
questions.answer: First, check the display screen for any alarm messages [1]. Next, verify that none of the circuit breakers located in the **MQ cabinet** have tripped [1]. Finally, ensure that all emergency stop buttons have been released and confirm that the pilot circuit is fully functional [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the feed or fast feed pressure is too low during operation?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Feed or fast feed pressure is too low despite properly functioning electric and control systems [2].
*   **Cause:** The electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) is stuck, the feed port A or B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 or 20.19) are leaking, or the feed cylinder is faulty [2, 5, 6].
*   **Corrective Action:** Disconnect the electric connector from valve (20.22), run the feed against the rear stopper, and check the pressure at the load sensing (LS) measuring connector; it should be approximately 210 bar [7]. If the pressure differs significantly, clean or replace valve (20.22) [8]. If the problem persists, clean or replace the shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19), then carefully re-adjust valve (20.18) to 200 bar and valve (20.19) to 240 bar [5, 9]. To test the feed cylinder for leaks, plug pressure lines A2 and B2, start the power pack, and check feed operation; if pressure is normal, the cylinder is faulty and must be repaired [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are some of the main control system modules (controllers) used to manage the drill rig's operations?
questions.answer: The rig's control system utilizes a network of specific modules, including the Drilling master (DM1), Vehicle controller (VC), Engine control module (ECM), Boom controllers (BC), Drilling controllers (DC), End controller (EC), Shank lubrication controller (SLC), Hydrostatic transmission controller (AC), and the Tramming controller (TCP) [25, 26]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a broken CAN bus connection to the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) diagnosed?
questions.answer: Inspect the CAN-RUN (green) indicator light on the SLU control unit; if it is flashing, it indicates that the unit is on standby because the CAN bus connection is broken or it is awaiting a start command from the CAN bus control unit [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you test for a faulty power factor correction capacitor on the electric motor during diagnostics?
questions.answer: Start one power pack at a time, let it idle, and check the power factor value displayed on the electric quality measuring unit (P1) [4, 5]. If the power factor value is under 0.5 and the individual phase current differs significantly, the capacitor is likely faulty [5]. It cannot be repaired and must be replaced with a completely new unit [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can the operator use the control system's troubleshooting diagram to diagnose offline modules or inactive electrical signals?
questions.answer: Navigate to the Troubleshooting view on the display. If a red "X" appears on top of a module, it indicates that the module is offline, not working, or connected to an option not included on the rig [1]. A gray signaling arrow before a component means its electrical signaling connection is inactive, which can help pinpoint the specific control device causing the problem [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are electrical and operational faults indicated on the Lincoln lubricant feed pump's control circuit board?
questions.answer: Faults are displayed by a flashing red light on the central LED [11]. For example, 2 flashes indicate insufficient operating voltage, 4 flashes indicate a motor circuit breaker fault (overload or mechanical stalling), 6 flashes mean a low-level signal requiring a refill, and 8 flashes indicate a loose electrical contact at terminal 30 [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are managed by the Hydrostatic Transmission Controller (AC)?
questions.answer: The Hydrostatic transmission controller (AC) manages the carrier's drive train, specifically controlling the hydrostatic transmission (HST) pump and HST motor [5, 7]. This includes commanding the proportional solenoid valves (such as 1.11.1 for the A-side and 1.11.2 for the B-side) to adjust the pump angle [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specified gas pre-charge pressures for the brake and rock drill accumulators, and what gas must be used?
questions.answer: Accumulators must only be filled with nitrogen (N2) gas to prevent explosion hazards [14]. The brake accumulators should be filled to a gas pre-charge pressure of approximately 65 bar [15, 16]. For the rock drill accumulators, the standard filling pressures are 50 bar for the high-pressure accumulator, 4 bar for the low-pressure accumulator, and 30 bar for the stabilizer accumulator (for models like the RD520, RD525, and RDX5) [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose timeout or configuration errors on the primary vehicle CAN network (J1939 Network #1)?
questions.answer: These are diagnosed using Cummins engine fault codes: code 285 (SPN 639, FMI 9) indicates a SAE J1939 multiplexing PGN timeout error due to an abnormal update rate, while code 286 (SPN 639, FMI 13) indicates a SAE J1939 multiplexing configuration error or out-of-calibration issue [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where the power extractor has no pressure at all?
questions.answer: Connect a 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring point (M3) of the drilling control valve block (20) or power extractor valve block (21), or check the main view's percussion gauge [11]. If there is no pressure reading, stop the power pack and check if the power extractor on/off valve (21.1), percussion selector valve (20.9), or percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the CAN control bus if the CAN-ERR (red) indicator on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) is flashing or lit continuously?
questions.answer: If the **CAN-ERR indicator is flashing** (single flash), it means at least one CAN control error counter has reached or exceeded the alarm limit (too many errors). This fault condition will reset automatically when data transfer is OK [5, 6]. If the **indicator is lit continuously**, it indicates that the CAN control bus is completely off (Bus off) [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the percussion to remain on continuously when the power pack or diesel engine is running, and how is it diagnosed?
questions.answer: This occurs if the percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) gets stuck and leaks pressure to the percussion mechanism [3]. It is diagnosed by stopping the power pack and inspecting these valves; it must be fixed immediately as the low pressure can damage the rock drill's accumulator seals [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are tripped circuit breakers or blown fuses diagnosed and handled?
questions.answer: A breaker tripping or a fuse burning is a sign of an underlying failure, such as a short circuit or overload [2]. The root cause must be located and repaired before replacing the fuse with one of the exact original size and type, or resetting the breaker to position I while the main switch (Q1) is in position 0 (OFF) [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How should an operator respond to a yellow Notice pop-up dialog?
questions.answer: A yellow Notice indicates a medium-level problem that does not require immediate action [1, 2]. However, if the notice persists or repeats frequently, the operator should investigate the reason for the alert and correct the issue [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you interpret a red "X" and a gray signaling arrow on the control system's electrical Troubleshooting diagram?
questions.answer: A **red "X"** displayed on top of a module indicates that the module is either offline and not working, or it is connected to an option that is not included on the drill rig [3]. A **gray signaling arrow** before a component means the electrical signaling connection is inactive [4]. If a specific signal should be active but the arrow remains gray, the component controlling it is likely causing the problem [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose CAN bus communication issues using the LED indicators on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLC)?
questions.answer: Inspect the CAN-RUN (green) and CAN-ERR (red) LEDs on the control unit. If the CAN-RUN indicator flashes, the unit is on standby because the CAN bus connection is broken or it is awaiting a start command [9]. If the CAN-ERR indicator flashes once, a CAN control error counter has reached its alarm limit; if it is lit continuously, the CAN control bus is completely off (Bus off) [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which fuses and circuit breakers should be checked if there is a loss of power to the boom CAN bus systems or the front tramming CAN?
questions.answer:
You should check the following specific fuses depending on the affected system:
*   On the **A1 circuit board**, check fuse **F8 (2 A)**, which supplies the Boom 1 CAN BUS [2].
*   On the **A2 circuit board**, check fuse **F8 (2 A)** for the Boom 2 CAN BUS supply, and fuse **F9 (4 A)** for the Front tramming CAN and tramming display [3]. 
*   In **Junction box JB99**, check fuse **F3 (6 A)** for the Diesel CAN sensor supply [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the primary variable displacement pumps (1 and 2) in the drilling hydraulic system?
questions.answer: Variable displacement pump (1) delivers the required amount of oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulic systems, as well as the optional stabilizer and power extractor [1]. Variable displacement pump (2) is dedicated to delivering the required amount of oil to the rotation hydraulic system [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the specific function of the Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC) within the CAN network?
questions.answer: The purpose of the Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC) is to dispense shank lubrication oil to the rock drill(s). It receives the rock drill’s shank lubrication request from the Drilling Master (DM1) node via the CAN bus backbone [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the battery and mains isolation button (S9) on the tramming panel do?
questions.answer: The remote battery and mains isolation button (S9) controls the battery main breaker (F41) and the main switch (Q1) [6, 7]. Pressing it cuts off the power from the battery and trips the main switch (Q1) to switch off the main electric supply, although it does not turn off voltage to the cable reel, slip ring unit, or certain secondary systems like fire suppression [6-9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined pump displacements for the rotation and HVAC hydraulic circuits?
questions.answer: The rotation variable displacement pump has a displacement of 60 cc, and the HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) gear pump has a displacement of 26 cc [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the indicator lights (H1 and H9) and switches (S9 and S293) located on the MQ cabinet signify or control?
questions.answer: On the MQ cabinet, the H1 indicator light signals a wrong phase sequency, while the H9 indicator light shows a dewatering pump earth leakage (if lit continuously) or an earth circuit pilot fault (if blinking) [5, 10-12]. The S9 switch on this cabinet functions as the dewatering pump test/reset switch, and the S293 button is the dewatering pump EFLO reset button, which includes a blue LED to indicate EFL- and FC-faults [5, 10-12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) and what is the correct setpoint?
questions.answer: The adjustment must be done with the maximum diesel engine rpm [1]. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector MPS [1]. Loosen the locking nut and turn the adjusting screw of the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) counterclockwise to fully open it [1]. Start the diesel engine, push the pressurizing stud (10.23) and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position to pressurize the carrier hydraulics [1, 2]. Apply maximum diesel engine rpm, then turn the adjusting screw clockwise until the pressure gauge reads exactly 220 bars [2]. Finally, tighten the locking nut, return the engine to idle, and release the pressurizing stud [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked to diagnose a loss of power to the boom or front tramming CAN bus systems?
questions.answer: Check the specific CAN bus supply fuses located on the circuit boards. Inspect fuse F8 (2 A) on the A1 circuit board for the Boom 1 CAN bus, fuse F8 (2 A) on the A2 circuit board for the Boom 2 CAN bus, and fuse F9 (4 A) on the A2 circuit board for the front tramming CAN and display [6-8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do Cummins engine fault codes 285 and 286 signify regarding the primary vehicle CAN network (J1939 Network #1)?
questions.answer: Fault code **285** (SPN 639, FMI 9) indicates a **SAE J1939 Multiplexing PGN Timeout Error** due to an abnormal update rate [9, 10]. Fault code **286** (SPN 639, FMI 13) indicates a **SAE J1939 Multiplexing Configuration Error**, meaning the system is Out of Calibration [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the electrical testing procedure for the cable reel limit switches using the troubleshooting display?
questions.answer: Turn the **battery main switch (S1)** to position 1/ON and turn the control system ON/OFF switch to position 1 [5]. On the display screen, navigate to **Troubleshooting → Reel control** [5]. Reel the cable in for three rounds, then pull the cable off until **four rounds** are left on the reel and verify that **indicator light (7)** turns on [5]. Pull the cable off further until only **two rounds** remain, and verify that **indicator light (8)** turns off [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the percussion pressure is too low?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion pressure remains too low during drilling, even though electric systems and sensors operate correctly [15].
*   **Cause:** The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) or the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) is stuck, the LS-line orifices (20.12 or 20.13) are blocked, the pump output is insufficient, or the shuttle valves are leaking [15-17].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack to check, clean, or replace the main pressure relief valve (20.25) and the proportional relief valve (20.14) [16]. Remove the LS-line orifices (20.12 and 20.13) from the drilling control valve block to clean them [18]. Verify the flow rate of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) to ensure it meets the required specifications (e.g., 100-135 l/min depending on rock drill model) [17]. Finally, inspect shuttle valves (11), (13), and (20.15) for leaks and replace them if necessary [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for adjusting the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8) and the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15)?
questions.answer: First, unplug the electrical connectors of the brake circuit retarder control valve (10.16) and carrier functions pressurization control valve (10.18), then connect connector Y167 to the solenoid of valve (10.16) [3]. Attach 250 bar pressure gauges to measuring connectors MPB and MCR [3]. Loosen the locking nuts on both valves (10.8 and 10.15) [4]. Start the engine, activate the boom zoom backwards to lock the adjustments, and apply maximum engine rpm [4]. Turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.8) clockwise but ensure the MPB pressure gauge does not exceed 205 bars [4]. Next, turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.15) until the MCR gauge reads 210 bars, which is the maximum allowed pressure for brake accumulators and must never be exceeded [5]. After this, turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.8) counterclockwise until the MPB gauge drops to exactly 200 bars, and tighten its locking nut [5]. Finally, turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.15) until the MCR gauge reads 160 bars and tighten its locking nut [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you calibrate the pressure and flow controllers on the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)?
questions.answer: The flow controller (A) must be set to maintain a pressure difference of 30 bar between the pump operating pressure and the LS-line pressure [7, 8]. To adjust the flow controller, open its adjusting screw almost fully counterclockwise, read the pressure difference from the two gauges, and carefully turn the screw clockwise until the difference reaches 30 bar [8]. To adjust the pressure controller (B), open its adjusting screw fully counterclockwise, then turn it carefully clockwise while running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the correct pressure is reached [9]. The target pressure depends on the rock drill model: 255 bar for the RD525, and 230 bar for the RD520 and RDX5 [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the rotation pressure is too high during drilling?
questions.answer: First, verify the drilling control settings and ensure the rotation speed is not set too low, as a low speed can increase rotation pressure [8, 9]. If settings are correct, inspect the rotation line pressure compensator (20.2) for mechanical damage, and check the rock drill rotation motor or mechanism for faults [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the feed or fast feed pressure is too high, assuming the electric and control systems are operating properly?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack and check the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18) and the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) [1]. Clean the valves or replace them if damaged [1]. If the valves are replaced, connect a pressure gauge to measuring point M1, adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) to 250 bar, run the feed against the front end stopper to adjust valve (20.18) to 200 bar, and run the feed against the rear end stopper to adjust valve (20.19) to 240 bar [2]. If the issue persists, replace or repair the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) or check the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you test for a faulty power factor correction capacitor on the electric motor?
questions.answer: Start one power pack at a time and let the machine idle [2]. Check the power factor value displayed on the **electric quality measuring unit (P1)** [2]. If the **power factor value is under 0.5** and the individual phase current differs significantly, the capacitor is likely faulty [2]. The capacitor unit cannot be repaired and must be replaced entirely with a new unit [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a red Alarm pop-up indicate on the display, and what is the required operator response?
questions.answer: A red Alarm pop-up dialog is displayed when the rig control system detects a major problem [1, 2]. Because alarms indicate conditions that could cause damage to drill rig components, the control system may stop some or all operations [1, 2]. The operator must stop working immediately, give the alarm immediate attention, and resolve/correct the root cause of the error before using the drill rig again [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the required procedure and acceptable limit when performing an insulation resistance test on the low voltage circuit (380-1000 V)?
questions.answer: First, switch off the main power and unplug the rig from the tunnel supply center [3]. The insulation resistance measured at 500 VDC between the power circuit conductors and the protective bonding circuit must not be less than 1 MΩ [3]. The phases should be short-circuited during testing to ensure all circuits and wires, including motors and capacitors, are fully affected by the test voltage [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the primary isolation switches, specifically the battery main switch (S1), starter isolator switch (S2), and main switch (Q1)?
questions.answer: The battery main switch (S1) turns the current from the carrier's battery to the drill rig's electric circuit on or off [1, 2]. The optional starter isolator switch (S2) prevents the diesel engine from starting and opens the pilot circuit when turned to the OFF position [2, 3]. The main switch (Q1) controls the mains electric supply to the drill rig and cuts off the control conductor that monitors the supply cable and the protective conductor [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific circuit board fuses provide power to the boom and front tramming CAN bus networks?
questions.answer: On the A1 circuit board located in the cabin, fuse F8 (2 A) supplies power to the Boom 1 CAN BUS [9, 10]. On the A2 circuit board, fuse F8 (2 A) supplies power to the Boom 2 CAN BUS, and fuse F9 (4 A) supplies power to the front tramming CAN and tramming display [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the "Blocked" and "Emergency Stop" pop-up dialogs mean, and how should they be handled?
questions.answer: The "Blocked" pop-up appears when the control system prohibits an action that could cause personal injury or machine damage; it disappears automatically once the cause of the error is removed [3, 4]. The "Emergency Stop" pop-up is displayed when an emergency stop button is activated, which immediately stops all ongoing drill rig functions [3, 4]. The operator must resolve the reason the emergency stop was activated before continuing to use the drill rig [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you resolve a rotation pressure that is too low during drilling when the variable displacement pump is correctly adjusted?
questions.answer: Check, clean, and replace the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) and adjust it [9, 10]. If the situation continues, check, clean, and replace the shuttle valve (20.7) [10]. Inspect the optional electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) if your machine is equipped with it, as it may leak LS-pressure to the tank line and require replacement [10, 11]. If the pressure is still too low, check the rock drill rotation motor for leaks and repair or replace it if necessary [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings are generated if the hydraulic oil temperature becomes too high?
questions.answer: A temperature sensor in the hydraulic oil receiver continuously monitors the oil [5]. If the oil temperature exceeds +65 °C, the control system will display a notice [5]. If the temperature exceeds +75 °C, the control system gives a warning and automatically stops the power pack(s) to prevent damage [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the main control modules that make up the CAN bus control system network on the Sandvik DD422i?
questions.answer: The drill rig's CAN bus network consists of multiple specific controllers, including the Drilling master (DM1), Vehicle controller (VC), Engine control module (ECM), Front controller (FC), End controller (EC), Switch controller (SC), Tramming controller (TCP), Hydrostatic transmission controller (AC), Shank lubrication controller (SLC), Boom controllers (BC), Drilling controllers (DC), Resin pump controller (RPC), Resin hose controller (RHC), Mains controller (MC), and Mains sensor converter (MS) [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific filtration specifications for the breather, pilot oil, stabilizer, and optional by-pass circuits?
questions.answer: The hydraulic oil receiver breather filters air at 5 µm [13, 14]. The pilot oil filter cleans the oil supplied to the pilot control circuit at 160-200 µm [3]. The stabilizer oil line filter has a 10 µm absolute filtration level, with a clogging indicator at 5 bar and a bypass valve at 6 bar [15]. The optional by-pass filter for the rotation circuit provides very fine filtration at 2 µm absolute, featuring a clogging indicator set at 2 bar and a bypass valve that opens at 3.5 bar [16, 17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the general filtration size requirements and bypass settings for the primary pressure and return filters?
questions.answer: The standard filtration sizes are 20 µm for the pressure filter and 10 µm for the return filter [1]. The 20 µm absolute pressure filter operates at a maximum pressure of 420 bar, features a clogging indicator that trips at a 5 bar pressure difference, and has a bypass valve that opens at 7 bar [11]. The 10 µm absolute return oil filter has an electrical clogging indicator set at 2 bar and a bypass valve that opens at 3 bar [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the carrier double pump (7) in the carrier hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The carrier double pump (7) consists of two main sections: the steering pump (7.1), which delivers oil to the steering circuit, boom, and carrier functions, and the brake pump (7.2), which delivers oil to the brake circuit and the air conditioning system [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the priority valve (10.10) function within the steering and brake control manifold (10)?
questions.answer: The priority valve (10.10) ensures that the steering function is prioritized above all secondary circuits [15]. It uses the load sensing (LS) line pressure together with its internal 10 bar spring to continually prioritize steering [16]. Additionally, it acts as a steering circuit retarder valve; when the retarder is activated, it partially closes to raise the steering circuit main line pressure up to 200 bar, loading the transmission and diesel engine to prevent overrunning during downhill tramming [15, 17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are faulty electrical signaling connections or inactive modules diagnosed on the control system display?
questions.answer: Navigate to the Troubleshooting view, where a red "X" on top of a module indicates that the module is offline and not working [4, 5]. Additionally, a gray signaling arrow before a component indicates that its electrical signaling connection is inactive, helping pinpoint the control device causing the problem [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning is given if the operator attempts to tram without wearing a seat belt or closing the door?
questions.answer: The door latch and seat belt monitoring system will activate a warning buzzer and display a notice pop-up on the screen if the cabin door is not properly closed and/or the seat belt is not fastened before tramming [6-8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a fault where the percussion is not working even though the power pack is running?
questions.answer: Check the percussion pressure gauge on the main view. If it shows a reading but the percussion does not work, the rock drill is likely faulty [1, 2]. If the gauge does not show a reading, the percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is likely stuck and should be cleaned or replaced [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do Cummins engine fault codes 285 and 286 signify regarding the primary vehicle CAN network?
questions.answer: Fault code 285 (J1939 SPN 639, FMI 9) signifies a SAE J1939 Multiplexing PGN Timeout Error caused by an abnormal update rate [7, 8]. Fault code 286 (J1939 SPN 639, FMI 13) indicates a SAE J1939 Multiplexing Configuration Error, meaning the system is out of calibration [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: If the feed pressure measured at the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) is significantly below 210 bar when run against the rear end stopper, and the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) is functioning correctly, which specific shock/anti-cavitation valves on the drilling control valve block (20) must be checked, and what are their required pressure settings at ports A and B?
questions.answer:
If the feed pressure measured at the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) is significantly below 210 bar when run against the rear end stopper, and the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) has been ruled out, you must check the following valves on the drilling control valve block (20):

*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)**
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** [1, 2]

**Required Pressure Settings:**
*   **Port A (20.18):** 200 bar (when run against the front end stopper) [3]
*   **Port B (20.19):** 240 bar (when run against the rear end stopper) [4]

**Step-by-Step Adjustment Procedure:**
According to **Section 6.10 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" (Pages 57-58 in the Hydraulics manual)**, if these valves are replaced, you must follow this sequence to adjust them:

1. Check, clean and, if necessary, replace the valves (20.18) and (20.19) [2].
2. Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point (**M1**) of the drilling control valve block (**20**) [2].
3. Use the pressure controller (**B**) to adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) to **250 bar** [3].
4. Run the feed against the **front end stopper** and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.18**) to **200 bar** [3].
5. Run the feed against the **rear end stopper** and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.19**) to **240 bar** [4].
6. Re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) as instructed in the manual's section *Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)* [4].

questions.question: During a boom cylinder line B inspection where the piston rod is completely retracted and line B is pressurized, if oil leaks out specifically between the cylinder cover and the cylinder tube, which specific seal (by ID number) is indicated as faulty?
questions.answer:
Based on the **Hydraulic cylinders** manual, Section 4.5.2 "Line B, inspection" (Page 29), if oil leaks out specifically between the cylinder cover and the cylinder tube, the **cylinder cover seal (33)** is indicated as faulty [1].

Here is the step-by-step sequence for performing the Line B inspection as described in the source:
1. Run the piston rod completely in (fully retracted) [1].
2. Disconnect line A [1].
3. Pressurize line B [1].
4. Check for leaking [1]:
   * If oil leaks out of line A, one of the piston seals **(30, 31, or 32)** is faulty [1].
   * If oil comes out between the cylinder cover and the cylinder tube, the cylinder cover seal **(33)** is faulty [1].
   * If oil comes out between the cylinder cover and the piston rod, the rod seal **(34)** is faulty [1].

questions.question: When the percussion system is active and boom functions operate normally but percussion pressure is too low, and the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) has already been ruled out, which two specific LS-line orifices in the drilling control valve block must be removed and inspected for blockages?
questions.answer:
Based on the **Hydraulics manual**, Section 6.8 "Percussion pressure is too low" (Page 55), if the boom functions operate normally but percussion pressure remains low, the two specific LS-line orifices that must be removed and inspected for blockages are:

*   **Orifice (20.12)**
*   **Orifice (20.13)**

Here is the step-by-step sequence provided in the manual to check these orifices [1]:

1. Start the power pack [1].
2. Turn percussion on and move the boom. If the boom functions are normal, but the percussion pressure remains low, either of the orifices **(20.12)** or **(20.13)** may be at least partly blocked [1].
3. Stop the power pack [1].
4. Remove the plugs from the ports of the orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** [1].
5. Remove the orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** carefully [1].
6. Check, clean and, if necessary, replace the orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** [1].
7. Install the orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** and the plugs carefully back to the drilling control valve block [1].

questions.question: While adjusting the cable reel control block for reeling out a 70 mm² to 240 mm² cable, what must the brake pressure relief valve (11) be set to, and at which specific measuring point do you verify that the pressure relief valve (10) is set to exactly 20 bars?
questions.answer:
For reeling out a 70 mm² to 240 mm² cable, the brake pressure relief valve (11) must be set to **70 bar** [1]. You verify the **20 bar** setting for the pressure relief valve (10) using a pressure gauge connected to **measuring point M2 (18)** on the cable reel control block (7) [2].

According to Section 5.1 "Adjusting brake pressure relief valves (10 and 11)" in the Components manual (Pages 19-21), the step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Remove the pipes **(21)** and **(22)** from the cable reel control block and connect the fittings with a hose (NG6 - 3/8") [2].
2. Loosen the locking nuts for pressure relief valves **(10 and 11)** by turning them counterclockwise [2]. 
3. Turn the adjusting screw of valve **(11)** fully open, and turn the adjusting screw of valve **(10)** fully closed [2].
4. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point **M2 (18)** of the cable reel control block **(7)** [2].
5. Turn the tramming mode activation switch to the START position, then release it so it returns to position 1 [2].
6. Push the lower button on the side of the steering stick to increase the APU speed to its maximum of **2500 rpm** [3].
7. Turn the selection switch to position **C** [3].
8. Push the reeling out button **(D)** from the ERCP and keep it pushed down (this activates coils **Y450** and **Y173a**) [3].
9. Turn the pressure relief valve **(11)** adjusting screw clockwise until the pressure reaches **70 bar** (the correct setting for 70–240 mm² cables) [1].
10. Lock the adjustment of the pressure relief valve **(11)** with its locking nut [1].
11. Release the reeling out button **(D)** [1].
12. Push the lower button on the side of the steering stick to decrease the APU speed to its minimum of **1000 rpm** [1, 4].
13. Push the reeling out button **(D)** and keep it pushed down again [4].
14. Turn the pressure relief valve **(10)** adjusting screw counterclockwise to adjust the pressure to exactly **20 bars** [4].
15. Lock the adjustment of the pressure relief valve **(10)** with its locking nut [4].
16. Release the reeling out button **(D)** [4].
17. Turn the tramming mode activation switch to position 0 [4].
18. Remove the connecting hose, reinstall pipes **(21)** and **(22)**, and remove the pressure gauge from measuring point **M2 (18)** [5].

questions.question: After resealing the HLX5 rock drill, what exact charge gas pressures must be applied to the high-pressure accumulator, low-pressure accumulator, and stabilizer accumulator before the unit is put back into operation?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, the required charge gas pressures for the accumulators on the HLX5 rock drill (using only Nitrogen N2) are as follows:

*   **High-pressure (HP) accumulator:** 50 bar [1, 2]
*   **Low-pressure (LP) accumulator:** 4 bar (normally acceptable between 2 - 4 bars) [1, 3]
*   **Stabilizer accumulator (for HLX5 T):** 8 bar [4]

*(Note: While the general preparation instructions list a default stabilizer accumulator pressure of 30 bar, the specific pressure chart for stabilizer accumulators dictates 8 bar for the HLX5 T [1, 4].)*

### Step-by-Step Filling Sequence
To apply these charge gas pressures, follow the procedure described in Section 3.8.1 "Filling instruction" of the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions* [5-7]:

**Required Components & Tools:**
*   Filling valve (2)
*   Locking nut (3)
*   Cap (4)
*   Quick coupling stem (5) & sleeve (6)
*   Accumulator pressure gauge (8)
*   Gas bottle pressure gauge (9)
*   Pressure regulating valve (11)
*   Nitrogen bottle shut-off valve (12)
*   Elbow adapter (15)

**Procedure:**
1. Remove the cap (**4**) from the accumulator.
2. Screw the elbow adapter (**15**) to the filling valve (**2**).
3. Push the quick coupling sleeve (**6**) onto the quick coupling stem (**5**).
4. Undo the locking nut (**3**).
5. Turn the pressure regulating valve (**11**) open.
6. Open the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve (**12**). The gas bottle pressure gauge (**9**) will indicate the pressure in the bottle.
7. **For the LP accumulator:** Adjust the pressure to 5 - 10 bar by turning the regulating valve (**11**).
8. **For the HP accumulator:** Adjust the pressure to **50 bar** with the pressure regulating valve (**11**). The accumulator pressure gauge (**8**) will indicate the pressure in the accumulator.
9. **For the stabilizer accumulator:** Adjust the pressure to **8 bar** with the pressure regulating valve (**11**). The accumulator pressure gauge (**8**) will indicate the pressure.
10. Close the filling valve (**2**) by turning the locking nut (**3**).
11. Close the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve (**12**).
12. Turn the pressure regulating valve (**11**) open.
13. Disconnect the quick couplings (**5**) and (**6**).
14. Release the elbow adapter (**15**) from the filling valve (**2**).
15. **To finalize the LP accumulator:** Mount the checking gauge (0-10 bar) into the low-pressure accumulator filling valve (**2**) and, by opening the locking nut (**3**), let the pressure flow out until the gauge shows exactly **2 - 4 bar**.
16. Tighten the locking nut (**3**) to a torque of **15 Nm**.
17. Refit the cap (**4**).

questions.question: When adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) for an RD525 rock drill, what must the pressure controller (B) be set to when measured at point MP2, and what is the required stand-by pressure range for the flow controller (A)?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.1.1 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" in the *Drilling Hydraulics DD422iE* manual (Pages 40-42), here are the required settings and the step-by-step procedure [1-4]:

*   **Pressure controller (B) setting for the RD525:** 255 bar [5].
*   **Measuring point:** MP2 [2].
*   **Flow controller (A) stand-by pressure range:** The stand-by pressure should be adjusted to 30 bar. However, if there are oscillations in the hydraulic system, this adjustment value can be changed to a range between 22-30 bar [3].

**Step-by-Step Adjustment Sequence:**

1. Remove the caps from the **flow controller (A)** and the **pressure controller (B)** and undo the locking nuts of their adjusting spindles [2].
2. Open the adjusting screws of the **pressure controller (B)** and the **flow controller (A)** almost fully open (counterclockwise) [2].
3. Connect the pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (**MP2**) of the drilling control block [2].
4. Start the power pack [2].
5. Turn the adjusting screw of the **flow controller (A)** fully closed (clockwise). *Note: The pump is now operating at constant pressure* [6].
6. If the machine is equipped with a 140cc percussion/feed pump, run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the adjustment of the feed percussion pressure controller is locked. (With smaller pumps, this action is not needed) [6].
7. Turn the adjusting screw of the **pressure controller (B)** clockwise until the pressure gauge shows 100 bar [6].
8. Let the LS-line bleed into a separate container by running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and connecting a measuring hose to the measuring connector (**LS**). Once all air has escaped, remove the measuring hose from the measuring connector (**LS**) or tighten the hose/shuttle valve connection (**C**) of the **flow controller (A)** [5, 6].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the **pressure controller (B)** clockwise until the pressure gauge connected to the measuring point **MP2** shows exactly **255 bar** for the RD525 rock drill [5].
10. Lock the adjustment of the **pressure controller (B)** with the locking nut. *(Note: Release the boom zoom function only if you are using the 140cc pump)* [3].
11. Turn the adjusting screw of the **flow controller (A)** almost fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
12. Allow the pressure to stabilize in the pressure gauge connected to the measuring point **MP2** [3].
13. Adjust the stand-by pressure to **30 bar** (or between **22-30 bar** if there are oscillations) from the **flow controller (A)** by turning the adjusting screw clockwise [3].
14. Lock the adjusting screw of the **flow controller (A)** with the locking nut [3].
15. Stop the power pack [3].
16. Allow the pressure to come down to zero in the pressure gauge connected to **MP2** [3].
17. Start the power pack [3].
18. Allow the pressure to stabilize in the pressure gauge connected to **MP2** [7].
19. If the stand-by pressure is in the recommended range, install the protective caps to the **flow controller (A)** and **pressure controller (B)** [7].
20. If the stand-by pressure is not in the right range, readjust the **flow controller (A)** according to steps 10-18 [7].
21. Stop the power pack [4].
22. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **MP2** [4].

questions.question: When checking the service brake pressure, what specific pressure reading must be observed at measuring points A and B when the pedal is pressed down, and what is the correct parking brake release pressure range at measuring point D?
questions.answer:
When checking the service brake pressure, the pressure reading observed at **measuring points A and B** must be exactly **80 bars** [1]. For the rear axle's parking brake, the correct release pressure range at **measuring point D** is **26-28 bars** [2].

According to **Section 6.1.16 "Checking the brake and steering pressures"** in the Carrier/Maintenance manuals [1], here are the step-by-step procedures:

**Checking the service brake pressure (Measuring Points A and B):**
1. Attach a pressure gauge to the front brake circuit's pressure measuring point (**A**) [1].
2. Turn the tramming mode activation switch to position START, release the switch and it returns to position 1 [1].
3. Press the service brake pedal all the way down [1].
4. The pressure should be **80 bars** [1].
5. Turn the tramming mode activation switch to position 0 [1].
6. Remove the pressure gauge [1].
7. To check the rear circuit, attach a pressure gauge to the rear brake circuit's pressure measuring point (**B**) and repeat steps 2 through 6 [1, 3].

**Checking the rear axle's parking brake pressure (Measuring Point D):**
1. Attach a pressure gauge to the rear axle's parking brake pressure measuring point (**D**) [2].
2. Activate the tramming mode, if not already activated [2].
3. Push the stud **Y961 (2)** to release the rear axle and keep the stud pushed down [2].
4. The release pressure should be **26-28 bars** [2].
5. Release the stud **Y961 (2)** and check from the pressure gauge that the pressure decreases to 0 bar [2].
6. Remove the pressure gauge [2].
7. Reinstall the rubber cover [2].

questions.question: When configuring the parameters for the air line flow meter (B10F) on a DD/DT series rig, what specific numerical values must be assigned to the Analogue Start Point (ASP) and the Analogue End Point (AEP)?
questions.answer:
When configuring the parameters for the air line flow meter (**B10F**) on a DD/DT series rig, the specific numerical values that must be assigned are:

*   **Analogue Start Point (ASP):** **0** [1]. 
*   **Analogue End Point (AEP):** **213** [1].

According to **Section 9.7 "Adjusting the air line flow meter (optional)"** (Pages 68-69 in the Pneumatics manual), these values are programmed into the controller using the following step-by-step sequence:

1. Open the cabin floor hatch to reach the flow meter controller (**1**) [2].
2. *(After setting the FCTR and OU2 parameters...)* Push the **Mode/Enter** button briefly until **ASP** is displayed [3].
3. Push the **Set** button and keep it pushed down until **ASP** starts flashing [3]. After five seconds, the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [3].
4. Push **Set**, keep it pushed down until the value **0** is displayed, and then release the button [3].
5. Push **Mode/Enter** briefly and **ASP** is displayed again [3].
6. Push **Mode/Enter** briefly and **AEP** is displayed [3].
7. Push **Set** and keep it pushed down until **AEP** starts flashing [3]. 
8. Push **Set**, keep it pushed down until the value **213** is displayed (for DD/DT rigs), and then release the button [3].
9. Push **Mode/Enter** briefly and **AEP** is displayed again [3].
10. Push **Mode/Enter** multiple times until the current measured value is displayed, or wait for 15 seconds for the unit to return to operating mode [3].
11. If you wish to lock the unit, push **Mode/Enter** and **Set** simultaneously for ten seconds until "Loc" is displayed [3].

questions.question: When measuring the wear of the lower front slide piece on an SB 120i or SB 150i boom through inspection point C, what are the strict minimum and maximum allowed distance values between the outer and inner tube?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, when measuring the wear of the lower front slide piece on an SB 120i or SB 150i boom through inspection point **C**, the allowed distance values between the outer and inner tube are strictly:

*   **Maximum:** 19 mm
*   **Minimum:** 14 mm [1, 2].

**Step-by-step sequence:**
1. Locate the inspection point (**C**), which is provided for checking the wear of the lower front slide piece located between the outer and inner tube [1, 2]. 
2. Remove the screw plug from the inspection point (**C**) [1, 2].
3. Measure the distance between the outer and inner tube [1, 2].

**Section and Page References:** 
This information is located in **Section 5.1.5 "Checking the slide plates and pieces" (Page 31)** of the *SBi boom* manual, and **Section 5.4.5 "Checking the slide plates and pieces" (Page 210)** of the *Maintenance Manual DD422iE* [1-4].

questions.question: During the boom rotational joints sensor calibration procedure with a carrier laser, what is the required target angle and exact tolerance range (+/- degrees) for the roll-over joint before aiming the laser?
questions.answer:
During the boom rotational joints sensor calibration procedure with a carrier laser, the required target angle for the roll-over joint is **0°** with an exact tolerance range of **-0.03° to +0.03°** [1, 2].

According to **Section 7.3 "Boom rotational joints sensor calibration with carrier laser" (Page 52)** in the BOOM manual and **Section 7.1.3 (Page 94)** in the MEASURING manual, here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this procedure [1-6]:

1. Select **Maintenance → Calibration → Boom swing (laser) / Boom lift (laser) / Feed rail swing (laser) / Feed rail lift (laser)** from the display.
2. Select **Go to Calibration**.
3. Attach the targets.
4. Select **Next**.
5. Run the roll-over joint to **0° (within -0.03°…+0.03° tolerance)**.
6. Run the bolting cylinder in.
7. Run the boom extension to the back position (in).
8. Run the feed extension to the back position (rear).
9. Switch on the carrier laser.
10. Select **Next**.
11. Align the boom and feed such that the laser beam goes through the rear target (1) and hits the middle of the front target (2).
12. Select **Finish**.

questions.question: What is the stated maximum boom coverage area in square meters, and what are the specific width and height dimensions for this coverage on the DD422iE?
questions.answer: Based on the "KEY FEATURES" section of the technical specifications, the stated maximum boom coverage area for the Sandvik DD422iE is **60 m²** [1]. The specific dimensions for this coverage area are a width of **10,270 mm** and a height of **6,590 mm** [1, 2].

questions.question: For a rig equipped with the optional TFi500-16' feed, what is the specified net weight and the total hole length capability?
questions.answer:
Based on the Technical Specifications under the "DRILLING FEED" section, for a rig equipped with the optional **TFi500-16'** feed:

*   **Specified Net Weight:** 560 kg [1]
*   **Total Hole Length Capability:** 4,660 mm [1]

questions.question: What is the required minimum turning radius (R) and T-cross (C) transport measurement when tramming a DD422iE equipped with a TFi500-18' feed?
questions.answer:
For a DD422iE equipped with the TFi500-18' feed, the required transport measurements are as follows:

*   **Minimum turning radius (R):** 7,550 mm [1]
*   **T-cross (C) measurement:** 4,350 mm [1]

questions.question: When adjusting the percussion pressure for an RD525 rock drill, what specific maximum pressure value must the pressure controller (B) be set to at measuring point MP2, and which electro-proportional valve (by ID) actively controls the operational percussion pressure level during drilling?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the percussion pressure for an RD525 rock drill, the pressure controller (**B**) must be set to a maximum pressure of **255 bar** when measured at point **MP2** [1, 2]. During drilling, the operational percussion pressure level is actively controlled by the **electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14)** [3, 4].

According to **Section 5.1.1 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)"** in the Hydraulics manual (Pages 40-41), the step-by-step sequence to adjust this maximum pressure is as follows:

1. Remove the caps from the flow controller (**A**) and the pressure controller (**B**) and undo the locking nuts of their adjusting spindles [5].
2. Open the adjusting screws of both the pressure controller (**B**) and the flow controller (**A**) almost fully open by turning them counterclockwise [5].
3. Connect the pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (**MP2**) of the drilling control block [5].
4. Start the power pack [5].
5. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (**A**) fully closed (clockwise), putting the pump into constant pressure operation [6].
6. *(If the machine uses a 140cc pump, run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the adjustment is locked)* [6].
7. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (**B**) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows **100 bar** [6].
8. Let the LS-line bleed into a separate container (by running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and connecting a measuring hose to the measuring connector **LS**). Once all air escapes, remove the hose or tighten the connection [1, 6].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (**B**) clockwise until the pressure gauge connected to measuring point **MP2** shows the correct pressure for the RD525, which is **255 bar** [1, 2].
10. Lock the adjustment of the pressure controller (**B**) with the locking nut [2].

questions.question: During full-power drilling on an RD525 rock drill, if the stabilizer pressure is incorrect, which specific electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (by ID) should be checked, and what must the stabilizer accumulator's nitrogen pre-charge pressure be set to?
questions.answer:
During full-power drilling on an RD525 rock drill, if the stabilizer pressure is incorrect, you should check the **electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3)** [1, 2]. This valve acts as a pilot for the pressure reducing/relieving valve **(22.2)** to control the pressure level of the stabilizer [2, 3]. 

For the RD525 rock drill, the stabilizer accumulator's nitrogen (N2) pre-charge pressure must be set to exactly **30 bar** [4, 5]. 

If you need to pressurize the stabilizer accumulator, follow the step-by-step filling sequence from **Section 3.8.1 "Filling instruction"** of the *Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions*:

1. Remove the cap **(4)** [6].
2. Screw the elbow adapter **(15)** to the filling valve **(2)** [6]. 
3. Push the quick coupling sleeve **(6)** onto the stem **(5)** [6]. 
4. Undo the locking nut **(3)** [6]. 
5. Turn the pressure regulating valve **(11)** open [6]. 
6. Open the nitrogen bottle valve **(12)**. The gauge **(9)** will indicate the pressure in the bottle [6]. 
7. Adjust the pressure of the stabilizer accumulator to **30 bar** with the pressure control valve, using the accumulator gauge **(8)** to read the pressure [7]. 
8. Close the filling valve **(2)** by turning the locking nut **(3)** [7]. 
9. Close the nitrogen bottle valve **(12)** [7]. 
10. Turn the pressure regulating valve **(11)** open [7]. 
11. Disconnect the quick couplings **(5)** and **(6)** [7]. 
12. Release the elbow adapter **(15)** from the filling valve **(2)** [7]. 
13. Tighten the locking nut **(3)** to **15 Nm** [8]. 
14. Refit the cap **(4)** [8].

questions.question: In the drilling control system, what specifically happens when the rotation pressure exceeds the "Jammed bit rotation pressure monitoring limit," and how does the system use the "Jammed bit feed speed monitoring limit" to trigger anti-jamming actions?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, here is how the drilling control system handles jammed bit monitoring and anti-jamming actions:

**When rotation pressure exceeds the monitoring limit:**
*   According to the **Jammed bit monitoring** parameters (Page 314), when the rotation pressure rises above the **"Jammed bit rotation pressure monitoring limit"**, the system considers the bit to be jammed and activates monitoring [1].
*   Furthermore, if the pressure rises above the **"Rotation pressure for anti-jamming monitoring limit"**, the anti-jamming function is activated and actions are taken by the system to prevent the drill rod from getting stuck or damaged (Page 310) [2]. 

**How the system uses the feed speed monitoring limit:**
*   According to the **"Jammed bit feed speed monitoring limit"** parameter, if the feed speed drops below this specific limit *during* an active anti-jamming sequence, the system considers the bit to be jammed and activates monitoring [1].

**Additional System Conditions & Components:**
*   **Water Flow Sensor (34):** The control system also uses water flow rate information measured by the water flow sensor (**34**) after the water flushing valve (**29**) to help control the anti-jamming automatics (Page 30) [3].
*   **Sensor Bypasses:** The entire jammed bit monitoring function will be automatically disabled if the rotation pressure sensor or rock drill position sensor is bypassed, or if the rock drill position sensor is disabled [4].

questions.question: What is the stated maximum feed force in kN for the TFi500 feed, and what are the specific maximum working pressures allowed for the feed cylinder during forward feed and return movements?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, here are the specifications for the feed force and feed cylinder working pressures:

*   **Maximum Feed Force:** The stated maximum feed force for the TFi500 (TF5i) feed is **25 kN** [1, 2]. 
*   **Maximum Working Pressures:** According to **Section 3.4 "Feed cylinder"** (Page 16 of the Feed manual), the specific maximum working pressures allowed for the feed cylinder are **180 bar** for the forward feed movement and **250 bar** for the return movement [3].

questions.question: If the water flushing pressure spikes dangerously high from the mine's network, which specific pressure relief valve (by ID) protects the system by limiting the pressure before the mud separator to 15 bar, and what is the target flushing water pressure range during normal operation?
questions.answer:
If the water flushing pressure spikes dangerously high from the mine's network, the system is protected by the **pressure relief valve (24)** [1, 2]. This valve is permanently installed in the water inlet line specifically to safeguard the rig's water system against network pressure spikes, limiting the maximum water pressure before the mud separator assembly (25) to exactly 15 bar [1, 2]. 

According to the machine's technical specifications, the target flushing water pressure range during normal operation is **10 - 15 bar** [3].

questions.question: How does the hydraulic system utilize the third chamber (Y-chamber) inside the hollow piston rod of the three-chamber cylinders to maintain automatic parallelism during boom lift and feed tilt movements?
questions.answer:
Based on the **Hydraulic cylinders manual**, three-chamber cylinders are specifically used for the parallelism function on boom lift/swing movements together with feed tilt/swing movements, as well as for the feed extension cylinder [1, 2].

Here is how the hydraulic system utilizes the Y-chamber to maintain automatic parallelism:

*   **Internal Structure:** These special cylinders contain the standard hydraulic chambers (A and B), along with a **third chamber (Y-chamber)** that is located inside the hollow piston rod [2].
*   **Hydraulic Fluid Transfer:** When a boom movement is initiated—for example, when the boom lift cylinder's length changes—the internal volume of its Y-chamber changes simultaneously [2]. 
*   **Automatic Parallelism:** As this volume changes, the boom lift cylinder automatically gives or takes oil directly from the Y-chamber of the feed tilt cylinder [2]. This direct, proportional transfer of oil between the interconnected Y-chambers acts as the essential mechanism for keeping the feed perfectly parallel to its original angle during boom movements [2]. 

**Critical Safety and Operational Constraint:**
According to **Section 4.4.1 "Disassembling the three chamber cylinder" (Page 26)**, the Y-port of the hollow rod chamber must **never be plugged** when the cylinder is in use (or during disassembly/bleeding) [3, 4]. Because the Y-chamber is not connected to chambers A and B, plugging the Y-port will cause dangerous air pressurization inside the cylinder, which could lead to the unexpected ejection of cylinder parts, resulting in severe injury or death [3, 4].

questions.question: What are the specific dimensions (in mm) and total coverage area (in m²) for the maximum boom reach of the DD422iE equipped with SB60/SB60i booms?
questions.answer:
Based on the Technical Specifications for the Sandvik DD422iE, the dimensions and coverage area are defined as follows:

*   **Maximum Coverage Area:** According to the "KEY FEATURES" section, the maximum boom coverage is **60 m²**, with specific dimensions of **10,270 mm** in width and **6,590 mm** in height [1, 2].
*   **Parallel Coverage:** Specifically for a rig equipped with the **SB60 / SB60i** type of boom, the "BOOM" section lists the parallel coverage as **54 m²** [3].

questions.question: When preparing the machine for tramming or parking, what are the maximum allowed front tilt and side tilt inclination angles (in degrees), and what strict boom positioning rule must be followed to safely allow these angles?
questions.answer:
When preparing the machine for tramming or parking, the maximum allowed inclination angles are as follows:

*   **Maximum front tilt angle:** 15° [1, 2]
*   **Maximum side tilt angle:** 5° [1, 2]

**Strict Boom Positioning Rule:**
These maximum inclination angles are **only allowed when the booms are in the tramming position** [3, 4]. 

To safely achieve this, you must follow the step-by-step sequence for putting the rig into the tramming position, as detailed in **Section 4.9.4 "Tramming position of the rig" (Page 207 of the Operator's Manual)**:

1. Turn the booms and feeds in the direction of the machine [5].
2. Retract the booms and feeds to the rear positions [5].
3. Lay down the rear ends of the feed beams lightly against the booms [5].
4. If on a level surface or when the drilling module is facing downhill, lift the rear jacks first, then the front jacks. If the drilling module is facing uphill, lift the front jacks first, then the rear jacks [5, 6].
5. If the rig is equipped with a front jack beam, retract it [6].

*(Note: The rig must be in the tramming position whenever it is not supported by jacks [5].)*

questions.question: Within the boom control valve block, which specific component (by ID number) limits the boom and percussion circuit main pressure, and what is its exact pressure setting?
questions.answer:
Based on the BOOM manual, the specific component within the boom control valve block that limits the boom and percussion circuit main pressure is the **main pressure relief valve (10)** [1]. 

Its exact pressure setting is **270 bar** [1]. *(Note: The normal maximum operating pressure is determined by the pump pressure controller [1].)*

questions.question: During a return movement of the optional TFX feed system, through which specific valve (by ID) in the TFX control block (28) does the return oil from the TFX feed cylinder (27) flow before reaching port B2 of the drilling control valve block?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.4 "Feed" (under the "TFX feed (optional)" subsection) of the *Drilling Hydraulics DD422iE* manual (Page 33), the return oil from the TFX feed cylinder (27) flows through the **TFX bottom cylinder chamber control valve (28.3)** [1].

*Note: The manual specifies that this specific routing of return oil to port B2 occurs during the **feed forward movement**.* 

Here is the step-by-step sequence of this hydraulic flow [1, 2]:
1. When feed forward movement is activated (by the pilot control valve **Y3A (20.20)**), oil is directed from the drilling control valve block **(20)** port **A2** to the TFX feed cylinder **(27)**.
2. As the cylinder extends, the **return oil** from the TFX feed cylinder **(27)** flows through the **TFX bottom cylinder chamber control valve (28.3)** located in the TFX control block **(28)**.
3. From this valve, the return oil reaches port **B2** of the drilling control valve block **(20)**. 
4. *(Simultaneously, return oil from the primary feed cylinder **(26)** also flows to port **B2** via the pressure relief valve **(28.1)**)*.
5. From port **B2**, the oil flows through the main spool **(20.16)** and port **T2** to the collecting piece **(7)** before returning to the hydraulic oil receiver via the coolers. 

*(For clarity, if the feed is in a backward/reverse movement, the return oil from the TFX feed cylinder (27) flows to the TFX collector piece (27.2) and returns to port **A2** instead of B2 [3]).*

questions.question: How do you test for a side branch interruption on the CAN_LO or CAN_HI wires?
questions.answer: To test for a side branch interruption, measure the impedance between **CAN_LO** and **CAN_HI** on the suspected side branch [6, 7]. If the node is disconnected during the measurement, the bus impedance will read as **infinite** [6, 7]. If the node remains connected to the bus, the impedance will measure approximately **40 kΩ** [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which computer acts as the Carrier Master (CM1) and what are its core hardware specifications?
questions.answer: The Carrier Master (CM1) utilizes the **SCU machine control computer** [8]. It is powered by an 800 MHz Freescale ARM Cortex A8 processor and contains 512 MB RAM with 4GB eMMC memory [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the two primary variable displacement pumps in the drilling hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The **percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)** delivers the required amount of oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulic systems, as well as the optional stabilizer and power extractor [1]. The **rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2)** delivers the required amount of oil specifically to the rotation hydraulic system [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot incorrect feed or fast feed speeds in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block to verify that the pilot pressure is between 30-45 bars when the power pack is running loaded [7, 8]. If the pressure deviates from this, check the pilot oil filter (20.26) and pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27); if the pressure is normal, the fault likely lies with a stuck feed valve main spool (20.16) or the feed pilot control valves (20.20/20.21) [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) and the rotation pump (2)?
questions.answer: The rotation circuit variable displacement pump (**2**) is adjusted via its flow controller (**A**) to a stand-by pressure of **20-23 bar**, and its pressure controller (**B**) is set to a maximum drilling pressure of **200 bar** [7-10]. To adjust the **rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3)**, you must temporarily set the pump to operate at a constant pressure, turn the pressure controller (**B**) up to **260 bar**, and then loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (**20.3**) until the pressure drops and restricts at exactly **250 bar** [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptoms, causes, and corrective actions when feed or fast feed pressure is too high?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Feed or fast feed pressure is too high despite properly functioning electric and control systems [4].
*   **Cause:** The **electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)**, **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)**, or **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** is stuck [4]. The **feed line pressure compensator (20.17)** might also be faulty [5].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and check, clean, or replace valves **(20.18)** and **(20.19)** [6]. If these valves are replaced, you must re-adjust them using the **pressure controller (B)** and run the feed against the front and rear stoppers to set the correct pressures (200 bar and 240 bar, respectively) [6, 7]. If the issue persists, repair or replace valve **(20.22)**, or remove and inspect the **feed line pressure compensator (20.17)** [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning indicates that the fire suppression system has been activated, and what happens next?
questions.answer:
**Cause:** The fire suppression system is activated manually or automatically [13, 14].
*   **Warning & Response:** An alarm will sound and release a loud siren [4, 5]. If the rig is equipped with the shutdown kit, an electronic alarm/timer box will provide an audiovisual alarm. After a delay period, the driveline power will automatically shut down [14]. The operator must evacuate if there is a fire, or do not restart the machine until the cause is established, the fault is repaired, and used extinguishers are replaced [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used for the Front Controller (FC), and what is its specific design purpose?
questions.answer: The Front Controller (FC) is the **VCH (Valve Controller High Temp) module** [10]. It is a powerful I/O-module whose separate output powering/cutoff circuitry is specifically designed to allow de-activating outputs safely within SIL2/PLd systems [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do the primary pressure filter (8) and the optional by-pass filter (10) function within the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The **pressure filter (8)** filters the hydraulic oil immediately after the variable displacement pump (1) at a filtration level of 20 µm absolute and a maximum operating pressure of 420 bar [6]. The optional **by-pass filter (10)** provides finer filtration at 2 µm absolute, receiving oil from the rotation variable displacement pump (2) via a **shuttle valve (9)**, and strictly limits flow to 2.0 l/min using a **flow control valve (10.1)** [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What happens if the shank lubrication unit's control valve shut-off ball is left in the wrong position?
questions.answer:
**Cause:** The control valve shut-off ball is left open or closed for four operational cycles, deviating from normal operation.
*   **Warning & Response:** An alarm is switched on, the user receives an error message, and drilling is automatically stopped. The operator must correct the valve issue, as the alarm will only reset when pumping returns to normal [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component functions as the Drilling Master (DM) and what are its primary responsibilities?
questions.answer: The Drilling Master (DM) uses the **XCU machine control computer** [4]. One XCU module is responsible for controlling one boom, managing tasks such as joint position control, forward and inverse boom kinematics, trajectory generation, automatic hole-to-hole positioning, and executing drilling control algorithms [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component controls the emergency stop circuit, and what safety features does it provide?
questions.answer: The emergency stop circuit is controlled by **Duelco NST-2004** safety relays [9]. These relays provide a Category 4 safety level with 2-channel operation and short circuit protection [10, 11]. They monitor the dual-line emergency stop push buttons; if an emergency stop is activated, the relays will de-energize all valves by cutting power from the output units of the I/O control units [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning is given if the seat belt is unfastened or the cabin door is open before tramming?
questions.answer:
**Cause:** The seat belt is not fastened or the cabin door is not properly closed before initiating tramming.
*   **Warning & Response:** The door latch and seat belt monitoring system will activate a buzzer on the tramming panel and display a notice pop-up on the screen. The operator must properly close the door and fasten their lap belt to clear the warning and safely tram the rig [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical components and switches should be checked if the power pack fails to start?
questions.answer: If the power pack will not start, first check the screen for any alarm messages [3]. Ensure that the starter isolator switch (**S2**) is in the correct operating position [3, 4]. Check the connection of the mains electric supply and verify that the main switch (**Q1**) is in position **1 (ON)** [3]. Finally, ensure that all emergency stop buttons have been released [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific functions of the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) and the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.22)?
questions.answer: The **rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3)** limits the maximum pressure of the rotation circuit to 250 bars [4]. The **electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.22)** controls the feed load-sensing (LS) pressure and limits its maximum to 210 bars [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the green and red LED blink codes on the controller modules indicate about the system's operational or fault status?
questions.answer: A green LED blinking at 5 Hz means no operating system is loaded, at 2 Hz means it is running, and constantly ON means it is stopped [4]. A red LED blinking at 2 Hz indicates it is running with an error, while a solid red LED indicates a fatal error or that it has stopped with an error [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you interpret the diagnostic sequences on the FPVC (fast controller) module display during boot-up and operation?
questions.answer: During boot-up, the FPVC displays its controller type ID ("fc") followed by its major, minor, and build software versions (e.g., "fc – 01 – 00 – 00") [2, 3].
