During operation, it displays the node ID, network state ("Pr" for pre-operational, "oP" for operational, "st" for stopped), communication errors ("Co"), and any I/O fault statuses [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do abnormal resistance values between CAN_HI and CAN_LO indicate during troubleshooting?
questions.answer: When measuring resistance with the power off, a result of **< 50 Ω** indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [3]. If the measurement is **> 100 Ω**, it means one end of the CAN bus is interrupted or a termination resistor is faulty [3]. Furthermore, if the reading is approximately **40...50 kΩ**, the bus is interrupted at at least two points, or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are CAN bus cabling faults, such as short-circuits or interruptions, diagnosed?
questions.answer: These are diagnosed using a multimeter. With the power disconnected, measure the resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO (a healthy bus reads ~60 Ω; < 50 Ω indicates a short, > 100 Ω indicates an interruption) [5, 6]. Alternatively, with the power on, measure the voltage to ground (a healthy bus reads 2.5 V ±0.2 V; < 1 V or > 4 V indicates a short-circuit) [5, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the system warnings and responses if the hydraulic oil temperature becomes too high?
questions.answer:
**Cause:** The temperature of the hydraulic oil exceeds safe operating parameters.
*   **Warning & Response:** If the oil temperature exceeds **+65 °C**, the control system gives a yellow notice. If the temperature continues to rise and exceeds **+75 °C**, the control system gives a red warning (alarm) and will automatically stop the power pack(s) [6]. The operator must allow the oil to cool and investigate the cause of overheating before resuming operations. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose the cause of a power pack stopping unexpectedly during operation?
questions.answer: Check the screen for any active alarm messages, verify that the fluid inlet pressure is sufficient, inspect the MQ cabinet to see if any circuit breakers have tripped, ensure no emergency stop buttons have been activated, and make sure the pilot circuit is functional [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component acts as the Tramming GUI (VG), and what are its specifications?
questions.answer: The Tramming Graphical User Interface (VG) is the **EPEC 6107** [3]. It is a PanelPC featuring a 7-inch LCD resistive color touch display with an 800 x 480 WVGA resolution, operating on a Linux system [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the boom does not hold its position?
questions.answer: A boom failing to hold its position is often due to a leaking overcentre valve on the boom swing or lift cylinder, a broken O-ring, or worn seat surfaces, which require the damaged parts to be replaced [10, 11]. Alternatively, the issue could be caused by dirt in the hydraulic circuit (requiring the circuit to be flushed) or air trapped in the cylinder (requiring the cylinders to be bled) [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary system pressures set for the percussion and feed circuits?
questions.answer: The percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump is adjusted to a stand-by pressure of 22-30 bar [3]. The pump's maximum pressure controller is set based on the rock drill model: 255 bar for the RD525, or 230 bar for the RD520 and HLX5 [4, 5]. The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve is set to limit the maximum circuit pressure to 270 bars [6, 7]. Additionally, the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve is set to 200 bars, the feed port B valve is set to 240 bars, and the maximum feed load-sensing (LS) pressure is limited to 210 bars [7-9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration grades and bypass settings for the primary hydraulic filters?
questions.answer: The primary pressure filter has a filtration grade of 20 µm absolute and a maximum operating pressure of 420 bar; its clogging indicator triggers at a 5 bar pressure difference, and its bypass valve opens at 6 bar [17]. The return oil filter has a filtration grade of 10 µm absolute; its electrical clogging indicator activates at 2 bars, and the bypass valve opens at 3 bars [18]. Furthermore, the hydraulic oil receiver breather filter operates at a 5 µm filtration grade [19]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component delivers oil to the steering, brake, and carrier functions, and how is the steering oil flow directed?
questions.answer: The **Auxiliary power unit (APU) circuit gear pump (1.1)** delivers oil to the steering, brake, air conditioning (HVAC), and carrier functions [3]. The **steering valve main spool (2.1)** inside the steering and brake control manifold then directs the oil flow to valve port A or B and to the steering cylinders [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What alarm is triggered if there is an issue with the compressor temperature?
questions.answer:
**Cause:** The compressor oil temperature rises too high.
*   **Warning & Response:** An alarm is displayed on the control system display [21]. The operator must check the compressor cooling air fan and stop the compressor until the cooling issue is resolved [21]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specified pressure settings for the rotation circuit and steering/brake circuits?
questions.answer: The rotation circuit variable displacement pump is adjusted to a stand-by pressure of 20-23 bar [10, 11], with its pressure controller limiting maximum rotation pressure during drilling to 200 bar [10, 11]. The rotation circuit's main pressure relief valve is set to restrict pressure to 250 bars [12]. For the carrier's steering and brake system, the main pressure relief valve limits pressure to 207 bars [13, 14], the steering pilot pressure is limited to 30 bars [13], and the service brake accumulator charging valve maintains a pressure between 135-160 bars [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What function do the articulation locking valves (9 and 10) and the parking brake pressure reducing valve (28) serve on the carrier?
questions.answer: The left and right **articulation locking valves (9 and 10)** make the articulation joint stiffer during drilling by blocking the connection between the steering valve ports and the steering cylinders [8]. The **parking brake pressure reducing valve (28)** reduces the pressure for the parking brake hydraulic system to 30 bars to prevent over-pressurization on the parking brake [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the RD module in the control system?
questions.answer: The **RD (Resolver-to-Digital) module** serves as the **Boom Sensor converter (BS)** and **Feed Sensor converter (FS)** [6]. It is a general-purpose measurement unit designed for high-accuracy applications, processing resolver inputs, analog inputs (4 to 20 mA), and digital I/O signals from the boom and feed [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the grid monitoring relay (P2) diagnosed if there are issues with the battery charging system?
questions.answer: During main battery charging, open the lower hinged window in the MQ cabinet and push the ESC button on the relay for over three seconds to start the test function [10, 11]. Then, check the Battery System troubleshooting view; if charging is not on, the relay is working, but if charging remains on, the relay is faulty and must be replaced [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a "Blocked" pop-up dialog signify and how is it resolved?
questions.answer:
**Cause:** The control system prohibits the operator from performing an action that could cause personal injury or damage to the rig (e.g., attempting to tram while the parking brake is on).
*   **Warning & Response:** A "Blocked" pop-up dialog with a hand stop-sign icon is displayed on the screen. The operator must remove the cause of the error (e.g., disengage the parking brake), and the pop-up will disappear automatically [18-20]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the possible causes and procedural solutions if the boom will not swing sideways?
questions.answer: This issue could be caused by external leaks, a damaged swing cylinder seal, a damaged **control block valve Y1 or Y2**, or dirt and broken seals in the **overcentre valve** [7]. To fix this, visually check the hose connections for external leaks, install a new seal for the swing cylinder if it is damaged, check the operation of **valves Y1 or Y2** (and replace if necessary), and replace faulty parts while cleaning the **overcentre valves** [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: Why is the feed or fast feed pressure too low, and how can it be checked and resolved?
questions.answer: This is likely caused by a leak in the **electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)**, the **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)**, or the **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** [1]. To troubleshoot, connect a pressure gauge to the **load sensing line measuring connector (LS)** of the **percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)** [1]. Disconnect the electric connector from valve **(20.22)** and run the feed against the rear end stopper; the pressure at the **LS** connector should be approximately **210 bar** [1]. If the feed pressure is normal during testing but the issue persists in operation, the feed cylinder itself may be faulty, which can be tested by stopping the power pack, plugging the feed pressure lines **A2** and **B2**, and then starting the power pack to check the operation of the feed [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you test the operation of the grid monitoring relay (P2)?
questions.answer: To check the grid monitoring relay (**P2**), perform the test while the main batteries are charging [5]. Open the lower hinged window in the **MQ cabinet**, push the **ESC button** on the relay, and keep it pushed down for over three seconds to start the test function [5]. Then, select "Troubleshooting" -> "Battery System" on the GUI [6]. If charging is not on, the relay is working properly, but if charging remains on, the relay is faulty and must be replaced [6]. Press the **OK button** to complete the test [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose and part number of the grid monitoring relay (P2)?
questions.answer: The grid monitoring relay (**P2**), part number **CM-UFD.M33**, operates on a 24-240 V AC/DC control supply and monitors the electrical grid connections [13]. It is heavily involved in the charging system and can be tested during main battery charging by holding its ESC button for three seconds to verify it is correctly monitoring or interrupting the charging circuit [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure and what are the expected values when troubleshooting the CAN bus by measuring voltage levels?
questions.answer: First, turn the battery main switch (**S1**) to position **1** to ensure the control system is powered on during the measurement [7]. Measure the voltage between **CAN_HI** and **GND**, and then between **CAN_LO** and **GND** [7]. If the measurement results are **2.5 V ±0.2 V**, the CAN bus is intact [7]. If the measurement results are **< 1 V** or **> 4 V**, there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the procedures and required values when replacing the battery charger (A1)?
questions.answer: Turn the main switch (**Q1**) to position **0**, the battery pack isolator switch (**Q2**) to position **0**, the 24 VDC battery isolation switch (**S1**) to **OFF**, and turn off the main switch of the power supply center before replacing the unit [8]. After replacing the charger (**A1**), securely tighten the input and output terminals to a torque of **1.0 Nm** [8]. Switch the power back on, wait 30 minutes if the 24 VDC batteries are empty, and adjust the output voltage to **27.0 V ± 0.1 V** [9]. Finally, verify on the screen that the DC-voltage is around **27 V** without load [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the battery charger (A1) function, and what part number is associated with it?
questions.answer: The battery charger (**A1**), part number **CP10.241** (also available as CP10.242 or CP10.241-S1), is a DIN-rail mountable 24.0 VDC power supply capable of 10 A current [4, 5]. It is used to charge the two 12 V lead-acid batteries connected in series for the 24 VDC control system. Its output voltage is factory set to 24.1 V but can be adjusted using a built-in potentiometer [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the power pack will not start?
questions.answer: You should check the control screen for alarm messages, verify that the starter isolator switch (S2) is in the correct operating position, ensure the mains electric supply is connected with the main switch (Q1) in position 1 (ON), and confirm that all emergency stop buttons have been released [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a short-circuit between the two CAN wires (CAN_LO and CAN_HI) diagnosed?
questions.answer: When the two CAN wires short together, the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level will be continuously near 0 V [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined pump displacements and output flow rates for the percussion, feed, and rotation circuits?
questions.answer: The hydraulic system utilizes a 160 kW powerpack [1]. The primary percussion and feed pump has a displacement of 110 cc, while the rotation pump has a displacement of 60 cc [1]. Depending on the installed rock drill model, the pump output flow rates at maximum percussion pressure and normal operating temperature are 125-135 l/min for the RD525, and 105-115 l/min for both the RD520 and HLX5 [2]. The feed circuit flow rates are 4-8 l/min across all three rock drill models [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the main pressure relief valve (2.12) on the carrier hydraulic system, and what is the correct setpoint?
questions.answer: To perform this adjustment, activate the tramming mode and attach a **250 bar** pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MP** [1]. With the starter isolator switch (**S2**) allowing the APU circuit gear pump to operate, apply maximum revolutions to the pump [1, 2]. Turn the adjusting screw of the **main pressure relief valve (2.12)** clockwise until the reading on the pressure gauge reaches exactly **207 bars**, and then tighten the valve's locking nut [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the rotation pressure is too low despite the electric and control systems operating properly?
questions.answer: First, check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the **electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6)** [3]. If the rotation pressure remains too low after this procedure, it is highly possible that the **rock drill rotation motor** leaks [3]. In this case, you must check, repair, and if necessary, replace the **rock drill rotation motor** [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC / SLCU)?
questions.answer: The Shank Lubrication Control Unit (**SLCU**) controls and dispenses shank lubrication oil to the rig's rock drill(s) [12, 13]. It operates based on a shank lubrication request that comes from the Drilling Master (DM1) node via the CAN bus backbone [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are side branch interruptions on the CAN_LO or CAN_HI wires diagnosed?
questions.answer: Measure the bus impedance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI on the suspected side branch. If the node is disconnected during measurement, the impedance will be infinite [7, 8]. If the node remains connected to the bus, the impedance will measure approximately 40 kΩ [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary causes for percussion pressure being too high, and how is this diagnosed?
questions.answer: Assuming the electric and control systems are functioning properly, high percussion pressure is likely caused by a stuck electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14), which must be checked, cleaned, or replaced [5]. If this does not resolve the issue, check if the orifices (20.12) or (20.13) in the LS-line have loosened or disconnected, and tighten them if necessary [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure and what are the required setpoints for adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)?
questions.answer: Adjusting this pump involves setting both a flow controller (**A**) and a pressure controller (**B**) [3]. You must first adjust the flow controller (**A**) to achieve a stand-by pressure of **22-30 bar** (typically adjusted to **30 bar** depending on system oscillation) [4, 5]. Then, adjust the pressure controller (**B**) to set the maximum pressure according to the installed rock drill model: **255 bar** for the RD525, or **230 bar** for the RD520 and HLX5 [4-6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the main switch (Q1), and what is its specific part number?
questions.answer: The main switch (**Q1**) disconnects the mains electric supply, measures drill rig current, and acts as an overload device for the transformer [1, 2]. The circuit breaker type is an Eaton **NZMH3-ME350-S1** [1]. It can be locked in the 0 (OFF) position, but it is important to note that it does not switch off the voltage from the cable reel or slip rings unless a pilot system is used [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the most common physical causes of CAN bus faults?
questions.answer: The most common causes are cable, wire, or connector interruptions, short-circuits, installation errors, and incorrectly connected or loose internal termination resistors in some nodes [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptoms, causes, and corrective actions for percussion pressure that is too low?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion pressure is too low [10].
*   **Cause:** The **percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25)** or **electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14)** may be stuck [10]. Additionally, **LS-line orifices (20.12 or 20.13)** could be blocked, or **shuttle valves (11, 13, or 20.15)** in the LS-line could be leaking [1, 11, 12].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack to check, clean, or replace the main pressure relief valve **(20.25)** and valve **(20.14)** [11]. If the boom functions normally but percussion pressure remains low, remove the plugs and extract the LS-line orifices **(20.12 and 20.13)** to clean or replace them [12]. Finally, inspect and replace any leaking shuttle valves [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which controller module is used to operate the Tramming Controller (TCP), Gearbox Controller (GBC), and Main Switchgear Sensors (MS)?
questions.answer: The **VIU module** is the component used for the Tramming Controller (TCP), Gearbox Controller (GBC), and Main Switchgear Sensors (MS) [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What type of main batteries (BAT1 to BAT4) are used in the 650 VDC system, and what are their operational characteristics?
questions.answer: The main batteries are **Fiamm Z60-650** Sodium-Nickel-Chloride batteries [8]. Each battery module provides 24.7 kWh of energy at 650 VDC, weighs approximately 330 kg, and operates at a very high internal temperature range of 235 - 340 °C [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you determine if a CAN wire has short-circuited to ground or to the supply voltage?
questions.answer: If a CAN wire is short-circuited to ground, the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level will be continuously near 0 V [5]. If it is short-circuited to the supply voltage, the voltage level will be continuously near the supply voltage (VS) [5]. In both cases, the resistance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI typically remains around ~60 Ω [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the air line pressure reducing valve adjusted in the pneumatic flushing circuit?
questions.answer: Connect pressure gauges to the measuring connector (**MA**) on every boom circuit flushing valve and turn the adjusting screws (**1**) of the air line pressure reducing valves fully open (counterclockwise) [16]. Start the compressor, and then turn the adjusting screws (**1**) clockwise until the pressure gauges indicate approximately **6 bar** (this can be adjusted up to **7 bar** depending on the specific air network pressure) [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot joint or linear sensors that are not reading correctly?
questions.answer: Run the desired movement and observe the sensor's raw value on the control display. If the raw value is not visible at all, you must check the CAN system. If the raw value does not change during movement, check the sensor and its cabling. If the raw value changes irregularly, the sensor is likely faulty and must be checked [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptoms, causes, and corrective actions if the rotation speed adjustment is not working properly?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation speed adjustment does not work as desired, or the drill rod RPM is inconsistent [15].
*   **Cause:** There could be a fault in the rock drill, **rotation pilot control valves (20.4/20.5)**, **rotation valve main spool (20.1)**, or **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)** [15]. It could also be caused by incorrect pilot pressure due to a dirty **pilot oil filter (20.26)** or **pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27)** [16].
*   **Corrective Action:** Measure the pilot pressure at **line X**; it should be 30-45 bars under load. If incorrect, clean or replace the pilot oil filter **(20.26)** and valve **(20.27)** [16]. If the pilot pressure is correct, stop the power pack to check and replace the rotation pilot control valves **(20.4/20.5)** [17]. If still unresolved, extract and inspect the **rotation valve main spool (20.1)** and the **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)**, replacing the entire drilling control valve block if they are mechanically damaged [18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are CAN bus short-circuits and interruptions diagnosed using resistance measurements?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected, measure the resistance between the CAN_HI and CAN_LO wires. A healthy bus reads approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω, while a reading < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit, > 100 Ω indicates an interruption or faulty termination resistor, and 40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted at at least two points or both termination resistors are missing [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptoms, causes, and corrective actions if the percussion system operates continuously while the power pack is running?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion remains on at all times when the power pack is running [8].
*   **Cause:** Assuming the electric and control systems are operating properly, either the **percussion selector valve (20.9)** or the **percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10)** is stuck and leaking, which allows pressure to reach the rock drill's percussion mechanism [8].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack, then check, clean, and if necessary, replace valves **(20.9)** and **(20.10)** [8]. It is critical to repair this immediately, as low percussion pressure caused by this fault can damage the accumulator seals in the rock drill [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you prepare the machine to troubleshoot the CAN bus by measuring resistance, and what is the expected normal value?
questions.answer: To safely measure the CAN bus resistance, you must first ensure the power is disconnected from the control system by turning the battery main switch (**S1**) to position **0** [1, 2]. Using a multimeter, measure the total resistance between the **CAN_HI** and **CAN_LO** wires [3]. The expected normal value is approximately **60 Ω ±5 Ω**, which confirms that the bus cables, connectors, and both of the **120 Ω** termination resistors are intact [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What alarms occur if the service brake charge pressure drops during tramming?
questions.answer:
**Cause:** The front or rear service brake circuit charge pressure drops below factory-set limits or the pressure measurement fails.
*   **Warning & Response:** If the pressure drops below the **110 bar notice limit**, a notice is displayed on the screen and the warning light on Tramming panel A turns on. If the pressure drops further below the **stop limit**, an alarm message is displayed, the warning light turns on, and a tramming forced stop is automatically activated [7]. The operator must restore brake pressure to clear the forced stop. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for troubleshooting the CAN bus by measuring voltage levels, and what values indicate a healthy bus versus a short circuit?
questions.answer: For voltage measurements, the control system must be powered on; achieve this by turning the battery main switch (**S1**) to position **1** [4]. Measure the voltage between **CAN_HI** and **GND**, and then between **CAN_LO** and **GND** [4]. If the measurement results are **2.5 V ±0.2 V**, the CAN bus is intact [4]. However, if the results are **< 1 V** or **> 4 V**, there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you interpret the Ub, K1, and K2 LED indicators on the Duelco NST-2004 emergency stop relay to diagnose circuit faults?
questions.answer: The Ub LED indicates supply voltage [7, 8]. If both K1 and K2 are OFF while Ub is ON, there is an error between the two emergency stop inputs [8]. If K1 is ON and K2 is OFF, there is an error at inputs T14, T21, or T22, or K1 may be welded [8]. If K1 is OFF and K2 is ON, the error is at inputs T11 or T12, or K2 may be welded [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration requirements for the optional by-pass and stabilizer circuits, and the overall system oil cleanliness standards?
questions.answer: The optional by-pass filter provides very fine filtration at 2 µm absolute, with oil flow strictly limited to 2.0 l/min; its clogging indicator activates at 2 bars and the bypass valve opens at 3.5 bars [20, 21]. The rock drill stabilizer oil line filter has a filtration grade of 10 µm absolute, triggering a clogging indicator at 5 bars with a bypass opening at 6 bars [22]. Overall, the hydraulic fluid in the system must maintain a cleanliness class of 18/16/13 according to the ISO 4406 (c) standard [23, 24], and the recommended water content must remain strictly under 500 ppm for both mineral and biodegradable oils [24, 25]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is it diagnosed when the rotation pressure is too low during drilling operations?
questions.answer: If the rotation circuit variable displacement pump is correctly adjusted, low pressure is likely caused by leaks in the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3), the shuttle valve (20.7), or the optional electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) [12, 13]. You should check, clean, or replace these valves; if the issue persists, the rock drill rotation motor itself may be leaking and must be inspected and repaired [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are used for the control system power supply (A3, A4, A5), and what are their key specifications?
questions.answer: The control system power supply units (**A3, A4, A5**) use the part number **QT40.241** [6]. These are parallel-connected DIN-rail mountable 27.0 VDC power supplies capable of delivering 3x 40 A current with power reserves of 150% [7]. They support the starting of heavy loads like DC-motors and feature a "Parallel Use" jumper setting that regulates the output voltage to ensure the load current is shared evenly between the individual power supplies [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the access protector system warn the operator of an intrusion in the hazard zone, and what is the required response?
questions.answer:
**Cause:** A person enters the hazard zone, or an environmental change (e.g., water on the ground, jacks sinking) triggers the detection scanner [8-10].
*   **Warning & Response:** In *detector mode*, the red detection warning light starts to flash [9, 10]. In *protector mode*, drilling and boom movements are immediately prevented, the red detection warning light blinks, and a pop-up note/icon appears on the display. If the primary stopping function fails, the emergency stop will activate [11, 12]. The operator must ensure no one is in the hazard zone and push the acknowledgment button to reactivate the system [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the stabilizer pressure to be too low or too high, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: If the control systems are operating properly, incorrect stabilizer pressure is likely caused by either the stabilizer pressure reducing/relieving valve (22.2) or the electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3) leaking or being stuck [15]. Stop the power pack, check, clean, or replace valve (22.3) first, and if that fails, do the same for valve (22.2); if neither works, replace the entire stabilizer valve block (22) [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What types of CAN bus faults cannot be diagnosed using a multimeter?
questions.answer: A multimeter cannot be used to detect faulty CAN sensors (sensor signal faults), missing CAN signals, or bit-level signal faults [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the rotation pressure to be too high, and how is it troubleshot?
questions.answer: To troubleshoot high rotation pressure, connect a pressure gauge to **line X** of the **drilling control valve block** [4]. The pilot pressure should read between **30-45 bars** when the power pack is running loaded [4]. If the pressure differs from this value, the fault may lie with the pilot oil components; you should check, clean, and if necessary, replace the **pilot oil filter (20.26)** and the **pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27)** [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the variable displacement pumps do not rotate at all or their speed is abnormal?
questions.answer: First, check if the power pack soft start is functioning; if the power pack motor does not accelerate at all, check the control system alarms, as the fault is likely mechanical or related to the tramming battery [1]. If mechanical damage prevents the pumps from rotating, the damaged component must be repaired or replaced immediately [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you determine if a CAN wire has specifically short-circuited to ground or to the supply voltage?
questions.answer: If a CAN wire shorts to ground, the **CAN_LO** or **CAN_HI** voltage level will read continuously near **0 V**, even though the resistance between **CAN_LO** and **CAN_HI** remains at **~60 Ω** [5]. Conversely, if there is a short-circuit to the supply voltage, the **CAN_LO** or **CAN_HI** voltage level will be continuously near the supply voltage (**VS**), while the resistance will again still read **~60 Ω** [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a stabilizer pressure that is too low or too high during drilling?
questions.answer: If the electric and control systems are functioning correctly, either the **stabilizer pressure reducing/relieving valve (22.2)** or the **electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3)** likely leaks or is stuck [5]. First, stop the power pack, then check, clean, and if necessary, replace the **electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3)** [5, 6]. If the pressure is still incorrect after restarting and drilling, stop the power pack again and check, clean, or replace the **stabilizer pressure reducing/relieving valve (22.2)** [6]. If these steps fail to remedy the situation, replace the entire **stabilizer valve block (22)** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the brake pressure relief valves on the cable reel control block adjusted for reeling out?
questions.answer: With the reeling out button (**D**) pushed so the coils **Y450** and **Y173a** are activated, turn the **pressure relief valve (11)** adjusting screw clockwise to adjust the pressure based on the cable's cross-sectional area [13, 14]. For cables **25 mm² to 50 mm²** (AWG 1/0), set the maximum pressure to **40 bar** [14]. For cables **70 mm² to 240 mm²**, set it to **70 bar** [14]. After locking this adjustment, decrease the APU speed to **1000 rpm** (minimum), push the reeling out button again, and adjust the **pressure relief valve (10)** counterclockwise to exactly **20 bars** [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptoms, causes, and corrective actions if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation pressure is too low [13].
*   **Cause:** Assuming the rotation pump is correctly adjusted, leaks may be present in the **rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3)**, **shuttle valve (20.7)**, or the **electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6)** [13]. Alternatively, the rock drill rotation motor itself may be leaking [14].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and clean, check, or replace valves **(20.3)**, **(20.7)**, and **(20.6)** [13, 14]. If the pressure is still too low after addressing the valves, you must check, repair, or replace the rock drill rotation motor [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the steps for calibrating the bolting sensors?
questions.answer: First, tram the rig to a horizontal position, navigate to Maintenance → Calibration → Bolting joint on the display, and run the boom extension, feed extension, and bolting cylinder all the way in [17]. Next, run the boom lift to **0°**, feed lift to **0°**, and the roll-over joint to **-90° or +90°** (all must be within a **-0.03° to +0.03°** tolerance) [17]. Finally, place a precision spirit level on top of the boom 1 feed rail, level the carrier so the angle is roughly **0°**, input the measured reading, and select Calibrate [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can voltage measurements diagnose a short-circuit on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: With the control system powered on (battery main switch in position 1), measure the voltage between CAN_HI and GND, and then CAN_LO and GND. A healthy bus reads 2.5 V ±0.2 V, whereas a reading < 1 V or > 4 V indicates a short-circuit [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a hydraulic system where the percussion is not working despite being turned on?
questions.answer: Check the percussion pressure gauge on the control system's main view; if it shows a reading, the rock drill itself is likely faulty and requires repair or replacement [3]. If the electric and control systems are operating properly but there is no pressure, you should check and clean valves (20.14) and (20.11), and verify that the orifice (20.12) in the drilling control valve block is clean and undamaged [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are general control system and module communication faults diagnosed?
questions.answer: The primary troubleshooting method is the machine's self-diagnostics accessed via the GUI Troubleshooting view, which shows real-time electrical signaling [2, 3]. A red "X" over a module indicates it is offline or not working, while a gray signaling arrow before a component indicates an inactive signal, helping pinpoint the electrical fault [2, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can the CAN-RUN / ERR indicator LED on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) be used to diagnose CAN bus faults?
questions.answer: If the CAN-ERR indicator light flashes once, it means the CAN control error counter has reached or exceeded the alarm limit due to too many errors (this resets automatically when data transfer normalizes) [5, 6]. If the light stays on continuously, it indicates that the CAN control bus is completely off ("Bus off") [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component serves as the Drilling GUI (DG), and what is it used for?
questions.answer: The Drilling Graphical User Interface (DG) is the **CCpilot XM2**, which is a PC-based onboard display computer used to visualize real-time system information, such as drill/bolting plans, alerts, and productivity statistics [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the diagnostic fault codes on the VCH module display indicate about specific I/O signal faults?
questions.answer: On the VCH module display, an I/O fault status is indicated by the connector (e.g., J7), the pin number in hex, and a status letter. The status letters are "s" for a short circuit to ground, "o" for an open circuit, and "b" for a short circuit to the battery (for example, a display of "Ao" means output pin A has an open circuit) [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you troubleshoot a potential short or open circuit on the CAN bus by measuring resistance?
questions.answer: To troubleshoot by measuring resistance, first ensure the battery main switch (S1) is in position 0 to disconnect the power [1]. Measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO [2]. If the measurement result is approximately **60 Ω ±5 Ω**, the bus cables, connectors, and termination resistors are intact [2]. If the measurement result is **< 50 Ω**, there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [2]. If the measurement result is **> 100 Ω**, one end of the CAN bus is interrupted or the **120 Ω** termination resistors are faulty [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DD422iE Technical Manual)

questions.question: While adjusting the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8) at maximum diesel engine rpm, the pressure gauge connected to measuring point MPB tends to exceed 205 bars before the adjusting screw is fully closed; which specific valve must be adjusted to reduce this pressure, and what measuring point should be used to verify its temporary 210 bar setting?
questions.answer:
If the pressure tends to exceed 205 bars while adjusting the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8), you must adjust the **brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15)** to reduce the pressure [1]. To verify the temporary 210 bar setting for this valve, you must use the pressure gauge connected to **measuring connector MCR** [1].

According to Section 4.7.7 "Adjusting brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)" (Pages 83-85), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1-5]:

1. Unplug the electrical connectors of the brake circuit retarder control valve (10.16/Y344) and the carrier functions pressurization control valve (10.18/Y167) [2].
2. Connect the electrical connector Y167 to the solenoid of the valve (10.16), and leave the connector Y344 unplugged [2].
3. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector MPB and another 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector MCR [3].
4. Loosen the locking nuts from the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8) and the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) [3].
5. Start the diesel engine [3].
6. Run the boom zoom function backwards to activate the electrical connector Y167 [3]. Run the function until the adjustment of the pressure relief valves (10.8 and 10.15) is locked [3].
7. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm [3].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (10.8) fully clockwise, but simultaneously strictly observe that the reading in the pressure gauge connected to MPB does not exceed 205 bars [1, 3]. If the pressure tends to exceed 205 bars, use the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) to reduce the pressure to be able to turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.8) fully closed [1]. 
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (10.15) until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to MCR is **210 bars** [1]. *(Note: The maximum pressure level allowed to brake accumulators is 210 bars and must never be exceeded)* [4].
10. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (10.8) counterclockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to MPB drops to exactly 200 bars [4].
11. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (10.8) [4].
12. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (10.15) until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to MCR drops to 160 bars [4].
13. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (10.15) [4].
14. Release the boom zoom function [4].
15. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle and shut down the engine after idling [4, 5].
16. Remove the pressure gauges from the measuring connectors MPB and MCR [5].
17. Unplug the electrical connector Y167 from the valve (10.16) and return the electrical connectors back to their original positions (connector Y344 to valve 10.16, and connector Y167 to valve 10.18) [5].

questions.question: The rig is experiencing abnormally high feed pressure during operation, and you have already verified that the feed port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19) are correctly set to 200 bars and 240 bars respectively, and that the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) is intact; which three specific valves located within the feed load control block (27) must be inspected next for being stuck?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.11 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too high" of the Drilling Hydraulics manual (Pages 64-66), if the feed port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19) and the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) are intact, the three specific valves located within the feed load control block (27) that must be inspected for being stuck are [1]:

1. **Feed counterbalance valve (27.1)**
2. **Pilot controlled check valve (27.6)**
3. **Feed counter pressure electro proportional relief valve (27.5)**

The complete step-by-step diagnostic sequence for this fault is as follows [2-4]:

1. Stop the power pack.
2. Check the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18) and the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19). Clean the valves and replace if damaged.
3. If these valves (20.18 and 20.19) are replaced, they must be adjusted: 
   * Connect a pressure gauge to measuring point **M1**.
   * Use the pressure controller (B) to temporarily adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) to **250 bars**.
   * Run the feed against the front end stopper and adjust the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18) to **200 bars**.
   * Run the feed against the rear end stopper and adjust the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) to **240 bars**.
   * Re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) to its normal operating values.
4. If the steps above do not remedy the situation, repair or replace the electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22).
5. If the issue remains unresolved, check the operation of the feed load control block (27) to see if valves **27.1**, **27.5**, or **27.6** are stuck.
6. If the feed pressure is still too high, remove the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) from the drilling control valve block to check its condition. If it is mechanically damaged, the entire drilling control valve block must be replaced.

questions.question: An FPVC module's 7-segment display is flashing the diagnostic sequence "16 - oP – Co – J4 – 2o – J1 – 6b"; how do you decode this exact sequence to identify the operational state, the communication status, and the specific electrical faults occurring on the pins of connectors J4 and J1?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 8.8 "Diagnostics on the module display" (Page 115) of the control system manual, the diagnostic sequence "**16 - oP – Co – J4 – 2o – J1 – 6b**" flashed on an FPVC module's 7-segment display is decoded step-by-step as follows:

*   **16**: Indicates the **node ID** of the device is 16 [1].
*   **oP**: Indicates the network management operational state of the device is **operational** (other possible states are *Pr* = pre-operational, and *st* = stopped) [1].
*   **Co**: Indicates there is an active **communication error** [1].
*   **J4 – 2o**: Indicates a specific electrical fault on connector J4, pin 2. The "o" stands for an **open circuit**. In this exact example, it signifies that the current input at pin **XJ4.2 is open-circuited** [1, 2].
*   **J1 – 6b**: Indicates a specific electrical fault on connector J1, pin 6. The "b" stands for a **short circuit to the battery**. In this exact example, it signifies that pin **XJ1.6 is short-circuited to the battery** [1, 2]. 

*(Note: If an "s" were present in the pin status sequence, it would indicate a short circuit to ground [1]).*

questions.question: When assembling a high-pressure rock drill accumulator, you tighten the bottom to the cover with a new diaphragm installed; if the bottom mark (│) fails to reach the mark (o) when the maximum tightening torque of 300 Nm is applied, what specific component failure does this indicate and what corrective action is required?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 3.7.1 "Assembling an accumulator marked with an asterisk" (Pages 20–23 of the Pressure Accumulator Maintenance Instructions), if the bottom mark (│) fails to reach the mark (o) when the maximum tightening torque of 300 Nm is applied, it indicates a failure with the diaphragm, and the required corrective action is that **the diaphragm must be replaced** [1].

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for assembling this type of accumulator [1-4]:

1. Check the number on the cover and the bottom to ensure they are the same. High-pressure accumulators are marked with uneven numbers and low-pressure accumulators with even numbers [2].
2. Check the condition of the threads by installing the bottom to the cover without the diaphragm and tightening it to 150 Nm. If the bottom rotates past the mark (R) at 150 Nm, the accumulator must be scrapped. If the threads are good, remove the bottom [2].
3. Fit a new or inspected diaphragm to the cover, ensuring it is in the groove and the correct side is facing downwards. Replace the O-rings at the same time [3]. 
4. Lubricate the surface of the diaphragm (A) and the bottom surface of the accumulator (B) with vaseline or lanolin [3].
5. Lubricate the thread of the bottom with vaseline or lanolin [3].
6. Use a torque wrench and the special tool to tighten the bottom to **300 Nm**. The bottom mark (│) must end up between the marks (o) and (R). *(Note: The maximum tightening torque is 300 Nm. If the bottom does not reach the mark (o) with 300 Nm, the diaphragm must be replaced)* [1, 3].
7. Use a straight edge tool (1) to check that the face of the bottom (D) is below the bottom face of the cover (C). Ensure there is a gap between the tool and the face of the bottom [1].
8. Replace the filling valve and tighten it to a torque of 40 Nm [4].

questions.question: You are adjusting the deceleration of the cable reel rotation during tramming using pressure relief valve (11) on a rig equipped with a 70 mm² (AWG 2/0) cable; while pushing the reeling out button (D) on the ERCP, what exact pressure limit (P2) must be set while monitoring the gauge at measuring point M2?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the deceleration of the cable reel rotation using the pressure relief valve (11) on a rig equipped with a 70 mm² (AWG 2/0) cable, the exact maximum pressure limit (P2) must be set to **70 bars** while monitoring the gauge at measuring point M2 [1]. 

According to Section 5.1 "Adjusting control pressure relief valves (10 and 11)" (Pages 19-21 in the Basic Adjustment manual), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Remove the pipes (21) and (22) from the cable reel control block [2].
2. Connect the fittings with a hose (NG6 - 3/8") [2].
3. Turn the locking nuts of pressure relief valves (10) and (11) counterclockwise to loosen them. Turn the adjusting screw of valve (11) fully open and turn the adjusting screw of valve (10) fully closed [2].
4. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point M2 (18) of the cable reel control block (7) [2].
5. Start the diesel engine [2].
6. Push the manual throttle button on the side of the steering stick such that the diesel engine rpm increases to maximum. Check the rpm from the tramming display [2, 3]. 
7. Turn the selection switch on the External Reel Control Panel (ERCP) to position C [3].
8. Push the reeling out button (D) from the ERCP and keep it pushed down. This activates coils Y450 and Y173a [3].
9. Turn the pressure relief valve (11) adjusting screw clockwise to adjust the pressure limit (P2) to **70 bars** [1, 3].
10. Lock the adjustment of the pressure relief valve (11) with the locking nut by turning it clockwise [1].
11. Release the reeling out button (D) [1].
12. Push the manual throttle button on the side of the steering stick to decrease the diesel engine rpm to minimum [1].
13. Push the reeling out button (D) and keep it pushed down [1].
14. Turn the pressure relief valve (10) adjusting screw counterclockwise to adjust the pressure to 20 bars [1, 4].
15. Lock the adjustment of the pressure relief valve (10) with the locking nut by turning it clockwise [4].
16. Release the reeling out button (D) [4].
17. Shut down the diesel engine [4].
18. Remove the temporary hose from between the fittings and reinstall the pipes (21) and (22) [4].
19. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point M2 (18) [4].

questions.question: When adjusting the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) while the boom zoom function is run backwards to activate connector Y167, what specific pressure must be set on the gauge connected to measuring point MCR before returning it to the final 160 bar setting?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the specific pressure that must be set on the gauge connected to measuring point MCR before returning it to the final 160 bar setting is **210 bars** [1, 2]. 

This temporary setting occurs during the procedure for adjusting the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8), where the retarder valve (10.15) is also adjusted. The maximum pressure level allowed to brake accumulators is 210 bars, which must never be exceeded [2].

According to **Section 4.7.7 "Adjusting brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)"**, the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1-5]:

1. Unplug the electrical connectors of the brake circuit retarder control valve (**10.16/Y344**) and the carrier functions pressurization control valve (**10.18/Y167**) [3].
2. Connect the electrical connector **Y167** to the solenoid of the valve (**10.16**), and leave the connector **Y344** unplugged [3].
3. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MPB** and another 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring connector **MCR** [4].
4. Loosen the locking nuts from the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (**10.8**) and the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (**10.15**) [4].
5. Start the diesel engine [4].
6. Run the boom zoom function backwards to activate electrical connector **Y167**. Run the function until the adjustment of the pressure relief valves (**10.8** and **10.15**) are locked [4].
7. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm [4].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.8**) fully clockwise but simultaneously strictly observe that the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MPB** does not exceed **205 bars**. If the pressure tends to exceed 205 bars, use the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (**10.15**) to reduce the pressure to be able to turn the adjusting screw of valve (**10.8**) fully closed [1, 4].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.15**) until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MCR** is **210 bars** [1]. 
10. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.8**) counterclockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MPB** drops to **200 bars** [2].
11. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.8**) [2].
12. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.15**) until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MCR** is **160 bars** [2].
13. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.15**) [2].
14. Release the boom zoom function [2].
15. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle and shut down the engine after idling [2, 5].
16. Remove the pressure gauges from the measuring connectors **MPB** and **MCR** [5].
17. Unplug the electrical connector **Y167** from the valve (**10.16**) and return the electrical connectors back to their original positions (connector **Y344** to valve **10.16** and connector **Y167** to valve **10.18**) [5].

questions.question: To achieve the factory set fan rotation speed of approximately 2000 rpm for the compressor cooler, what exact pressure difference must be set using pressure relief valve (3) between measuring points MA (1) and MB (2)?
questions.answer:
To achieve the factory set fan rotation speed of approximately 2000 rpm for the compressor cooler, the exact pressure difference must be set to **60 bars** [1]. 

According to Section 8.4.14 "Adjusting the compressor cooler fan", the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1, 2]:

1. Attach pressure gauges to measuring points **MA (1)** and **MB (2)** [1].
2. Open the locking nut of the **pressure relief valve (3)** [1].
3. Loosen the adjusting screw of the pressure relief valve (3) [1].
4. Remove the electrical connector from the pressure relief valve (3) [1].
5. Tighten the adjusting screw until the pressure difference reaches exactly **60 bars** [1]. *(Note: The maximum allowed rotation speed of the hydraulic motor and fan is 2700 rpm and it must not be exceeded [2]).*
6. Close the locking nut of the pressure relief valve (3) [1].
7. Reinstall the cap to the pressure relief valve (3) [1].
8. Remove the pressure gauges from measuring points MA (1) and MB (2) [2].

questions.question: When setting the parameters for the optional air line flow meter, what specific Analogue End Point (AEP) value must be entered into the flow meter controller for a DL/DS series rig to ensure the 20 mA output signal is correctly scaled?
questions.answer:
When setting the parameters for the optional air line flow meter on a DL/DS series rig, the specific Analogue End Point (AEP) value that must be entered is **589** [1]. This determines the measured value at which the output signal reaches 20 mA [1, 2].

According to Section 9.5 "Adjusting the air line flow meter (optional)" (Pages 86-87 of the Flushing Circuit manual), the complete step-by-step sequence for setting the important parameters on the flow meter controller (1) is as follows:

1. Open the cabin floor hatch to reach the flow meter controller (1) [2].
2. Push Mode/Enter (3) so many times that **FCTR** is displayed [2].
3. Push Set (4) and keep it pushed down until FCTR starts flashing. After five seconds the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [2].
4. Push Set, keep it pushed down until value **1.50** is displayed and then release the button [2, 3].
5. Push Mode/Enter briefly and FCTR is displayed again [3].
6. Push Mode/Enter (3) so many times that **OU2** is displayed [3].
7. Push Set and keep it pushed down until OU2 starts flashing. After five seconds the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [3].
8. Push Set, keep it pushed down until **I** is displayed and then release the button [3].
9. Push Mode/Enter briefly and OU2 is displayed again [3].
10. Push Mode/Enter briefly and **ASP** is displayed [4].
11. Push Set and keep it pushed down until ASP starts flashing. After five seconds the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [4].
12. Push Set, keep it pushed down until value **0** is displayed and then release the button [4].
13. Push Mode/Enter briefly and ASP is displayed again [4].
14. Push Mode/Enter briefly and **AEP** is displayed [4].
15. Push Set and keep it pushed down until AEP starts flashing. After five seconds the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [4].
16. Push Set, keep it pushed down until value **589** (for DL/DS) is displayed and then release the button [1, 4, 5].
17. Push Mode/Enter briefly and AEP is displayed again [5].
18. Push Mode/Enter so many times that the current measured value is displayed or wait for 15 seconds. The unit is back in operating mode [5].
19. If you want to lock the unit, push Mode/Enter and Set simultaneously for ten seconds. **Loc** is displayed [5].
20. If you want to unlock the unit, push Mode/Enter and Set simultaneously for ten seconds. **uLoc** is displayed [5].

questions.question: When calibrating the compressor's capacity control valves in the field, at what specific pressure should the PS3 unloading pressure limit valve be adjusted to open, and what is the absolute maximum internal pressure it should allow?
questions.answer:
When calibrating the compressor's capacity control valves in the field, the PS3 unloading pressure limit valve should be adjusted to open at **8 bar(g)** [1]. If the adjustment is correct, the absolute maximum internal pressure it should allow is **10 bar(g)** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 6.2.1 "PS3 valve" (Pages 19-20 of the compressor operating instructions), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Before making any adjustments to the valves, connect a separate pressure gauge to the side of the Tempest unit [3].
2. Make sure the minimum pressure valve is adjusted to a minimum of **4 bar(g)** before making these adjustments [4].
3. Start the compressor with solenoid valve **Y363** de-energized and the network shut-off valve closed [4]. The compressor will now run off-loaded with the inlet valve closed [4].
4. Loosen the locking nut (**B**) using a 10 mm spanner [1].
5. Adjust the unloading pressure limit by turning the adjusting screw (**A**) on the PS3 control valve using a 3 mm hexagonal key [1]. Turning the screw (**A**) clockwise increases pressure and turning it counterclockwise lowers the pressure [1].
6. Adjust the PS3 valve to open at **8 bar(g)** [1]. By disconnecting tube **10**, it is possible to detect by hand that the line is not open below 8 bar(g) [1].
7. Verify that the internal pressure does not rise higher than **10 bar(g)**, which indicates the adjustment is correct [1].
8. If needed, the pressure can be lowered by opening the safety valve cap [5]. Caution must be taken as hot air will be discharged from the safety valve [5].

questions.question: When configuring the earth continuity monitoring system using the rotary switches on the front of the unit, what are the factory default settings for the series resistance trip level and the trip time delay?
questions.answer:
When configuring the earth continuity protection relay (**K9A**) using the rotary switches on the front of the unit, the factory default settings are as follows:

*   **Series resistance trip level (Trip level selection):** The factory setting is **45 Ω** [1]. The user can use the rotary switch to select between values of 10 Ω, 15 Ω, 20 Ω, 25 Ω, 35 Ω, and 45 Ω [1]. This setting represents the threshold for the series resistance, and if the resistance is measured to be greater than this threshold ±3 Ω, a trip will occur [1].
*   **Trip time delay (Trip time selection):** The factory setting is **500 ms** [2]. The user can use the rotary switch to select between settings of 50 ms, 100 ms, 200 ms, 300 ms, 400 ms, and 500 ms [2]. This represents the delay before the dewatering pump contactor (**K9**) will de-energize after a trip condition has occurred [2, 3]. 

These details are found in the "Electric System DL432i" manual, specifically in the configuration instructions for the Earth continuity protection relay (Pages 37-38) [1, 2].

questions.question: What are the exact transport measurements (height with cabin, width, and length) and the total transport weight of the DL432i drill rig?
questions.answer:
According to the Key Features section of the technical specifications, the exact transport measurements and total transport weight for the DL432i drill rig are as follows:

*   **Transport height (with cabin):** 3 050 mm [1]
*   **Transport width:** 2 500 mm [1]
*   **Transport length:** 11 850 mm [1]
*   **Transport weight:** 26 500 kg [1]

questions.question: According to the filling capacities specifications, what is the total volume of the C400/C900 carrier hydraulic oil tank and the diesel fuel tank?
questions.answer:
According to **Section 7.2 "Filling capacities"** in the Carrier and Maintenance manuals, the volumes are as follows:

**Hydraulic Oil Tank:**
*   The total volume of the **C400/C900** hydraulic oil tank is **270 liters** [1, 2]. 

**Diesel Fuel Tank:**
The capacity of the diesel fuel tank varies depending on the specific engine and carrier configuration [3-6]:
*   **150 liters:** For MB 904/906 LA, Cummins QSB 4.5/6.7, Cummins B4.5/B6.7, and Deutz TCD 3.6 engines [3-6]. *(Note: 150 liters is also listed as the standard fuel tank specification for the DL432i frame-steered C400D carrier [7]).*
*   **100 liters or 155 liters:** For Cummins QSB 4.5 (Tier3/Tier4F) engines [4, 6].
*   **410 liters:** For the Cummins QSB 6.7 (Tier4F) used specifically on the C900DH carrier [4, 6].
*   **55 liters:** For the Deutz D914L04 engine [3, 5].

questions.question: What are the four main components that make up the drilling module assembly, including the one listed as optional?
questions.answer:
According to Section 3.2.5 of the Maintenance and Operator's Manuals, the four main components that make up the drilling module assembly are [1, 2]:

1. **Hydraulic rock drill** 
2. **Feed unit** 
3. **Rod changer** 
4. **Bit changer** (optional) 

*(Note: These are found on page 118 of the Maintenance Manual and page 122 of the Operator's Manual [1, 2])*

questions.question: What is the specified maximum percussion pressure and the corresponding percussion rate in Hz for the RD927L hydraulic rock drill?
questions.answer: For the RD927L (TS2-356) hydraulic rock drill, the specified maximum percussion pressure is up to **210 bars**, and the corresponding percussion rate is **60 Hz** [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the mine's inlet water pressure using the pressure reducing valve (32), what specific pressure sensor ID measures the flushing pressure after the water booster pump, and what is the absolute maximum allowed reading in bars for this sensor?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the mine's inlet water pressure, the specific pressure sensor that measures the flushing pressure after the water booster pump is the **pressure transducer (B230P)** [1, 2]. The absolute maximum allowed reading for this sensor is **25 bars**, as the water circuit pressure relief valve (27) limits the maximum pressure of the system to this value [1, 3, 4].

According to Section 7.1.7 of the Flushing Circuit manual and Section 5.14.7 of the Operator's Manual ("Adjusting the mine's inlet pressure"), the complete step-by-step sequence for adjusting the mine's inlet pressure before the water booster pump using the pressure reducing valve (locally referred to as valve 1 in the procedure) is as follows [4, 5]:

1. Open the shut-off valve (2) [4, 5].
2. Turn the knob (3) fully open [4, 5].
3. Start the water booster pump [4, 5].
4. Turn the knob (3) to adjust the pressure to 2-7 bars according to drilling conditions [5, 6]. Turning the knob clockwise increases the pressure and turning counterclockwise decreases the pressure [5, 6]. Check the pressure gauge (4) for the value [5, 6].
5. Select -> Troubleshooting -> Compressor and Water Pump and check that the pressure sensor (B230P) value is under 25 bars [5, 6].

questions.question: During full-power drilling, the stabilizer pressure is actively controlled by the electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3); what is the strict minimum pressure difference that must be maintained between the percussion pressure and the stabilizer pressure?
questions.answer:
During drilling, the strict minimum pressure difference that must be maintained is **20 bars**; the percussion pressure must always be at least 20 bars higher than the stabilizer pressure [1]. 

According to Section 4.6 "Stabilizer" (Page 40 of the Drilling Hydraulics manual), the operation during full-power drilling follows this sequence:

1. When drilling is started, oil flows from the percussion and feed variable displacement pump (1) through the pressure filter (8) to connection port P2 of the drilling control valve block (20) [1]. 
2. From port P2, the oil flows internally to the stabilizer control block (22) [1]. 
3. Within the stabilizer control block, oil reaches the stabilizer on/off valve (22.1), the pressure reducing/relieving valve (22.2), and the electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3) [1]. 
4. The oil also reaches the stabilizer pressure sensor (18), which measures the pressure and sends this data to the control system [1]. 
5. Oil continues to flow to the rock drill's stabilizer via valves (22.1) and (22.2) [1]. 
6. The exact pressure level of the stabilizer is actively set by the reducing/relieving valve (22.2) and its electro-proportional pilot control valve (22.3), which is controlled based on feed pressure information provided by the control system to ensure the correct stabilizer pressure is maintained [1, 2].

questions.question: On the control system's rotation pressure gauge during torque control mode, what specific limit markers are visually indicated on the gauge to help the operator monitor the rotation pressure for power reduction and the anti-jamming monitoring limit?
questions.answer:
Based on the Operator's Manual DL432i (Section 4.5.6 "Information related to the drilling gauges", Page 176), the rotation pressure gauge visually indicates four specific limit markers to help the operator monitor the system during torque control mode [1]:

1. **Measured rotation pressure** (Marker 1)
2. **Rotation pressure for power reduction** (Marker 2)
3. **Anti-jamming monitoring limit** (Marker 3)
4. **Target rotation pressure** (in torque control mode) (Marker 4) [1] 

*(Note: The exact pressure values for these limits are not fixed; they are adjustable parameters configured through the gauge's settings menu based on the rock type and drilling conditions [2, 3]).*

questions.question: According to the control system's general settings, which specific collaring parameter dictates both the feed pressure applied during the collaring phase and the absolute minimum feed pressure allowed during full-power drilling?
questions.answer: According to the "General settings" under the "Collaring" parameters section (Page 289 of the Operator's Manual DL432i - StageV), the specific parameter that dictates both of these values is the **Collaring feed pressure** [1, 2]. This parameter explicitly defines the rock drill feed pressure used during the collaring phase, which also serves as the absolute minimum feed pressure allowed during full power drilling [2].

questions.question: Which specific hydraulic cylinders on the boom and feed utilize a three-chamber design featuring a third chamber (Y) inside the hollow piston rod to facilitate the automatic parallelism system?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Hydraulic cylinders" manual, the specific hydraulic cylinders that utilize a three-chamber design—featuring chambers A and B, plus a third chamber (Y) inside the hollow piston rod—are:

*   **Boom swing cylinders** [1, 2]
*   **Boom lift cylinders** [1, 2]
*   **Feed tilt/swing cylinders** [1, 2]
*   **Feed extension cylinder** [1, 2]

**Operation and Safety details:**
When a three-chamber cylinder's length changes (for example, the boom lift cylinder), the volume of the Y-chamber inside the hollow piston rod changes accordingly [2]. This allows the cylinder to give or take hydraulic oil from the feed tilt cylinder, facilitating the automatic parallelism system [2]. 

It is strictly noted that the Y-port must never be plugged when the cylinder is in use or being serviced [3]. The Y-chamber is not connected to chambers A and B, and plugging it will cause dangerous air pressurization inside the cylinder, leading to an unexpected ejection of parts or explosion of the cylinder and hoses [3-5]. 

*(Note: This information is found in the "Hydraulic cylinders" section, specifically under "Three chamber cylinders" on Page 25 [2]).*

questions.question: During boom lifting or lowering operations, which specific valve reduces and supplies the required 30 bar pilot pressure to the pilot valves (3 and 4) to shift the main spool (1)?
questions.answer:
During boom lifting or lowering operations, the specific valve that reduces and supplies the required maximum 30 bar pilot pressure to the pilot valves (3 and 4) is the **pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (9)** [1, 2]. 

According to Sections 4.1 "Lowering boom" and 4.2 "Lifting boom" (Pages 20 and 22 of the BOOM manual), this valve operates as part of the following step-by-step sequence:

1. The percussion pressure line delivers oil to port P of the boom control valve [1, 2].
2. The main pressure relief valve (10) limits the percussion circuit main pressure to 270 bars [1, 2].
3. The **pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (9)** reduces and supplies the maximum pressure of 30 bars to the pilot circuit pilot valves (3 and 4) [1, 2].
4. These pilot valves then supply the reduced pressure from the pilot line to the main spool (1) [1, 2].
5. The main spool (1) changes its position depending on which pilot valve is energized [1, 2]:
   * **For lowering the boom:** The pilot pressure is supplied from the energized pilot valve a (**3 / Y26A**). Oil flows through the main spool to port A2, onward to the lift cylinder (12) port B and to the cylinder's piston rod side, causing the cylinder to retract and lower the boom [1].
   * **For lifting the boom:** The pilot pressure is supplied from the energized pilot valve b (**4 / Y26B**). Oil flows through the main spool to port B2, onward to the lift cylinder (12) port A and to the cylinder's piston side, causing the cylinder to extend and lift the boom [2].

questions.question: What is the stated maximum operating pressure for the feed cylinder when feeding forward, and does this value differ during the return movement?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.4 "Feed cylinder" of the Cylinder Feed LF900 manual (Page 15), the stated maximum operating pressure for the feed cylinder when feeding forward is **200 bars** [1]. 

This value **does not differ** during the return movement; the maximum operating pressure remains exactly **200 bars** during the return movement as well [1]. 

For additional context on the feed cylinder's operation during these movements [1]:
* Oil is led into the cylinder through the piston rod to both sides of the piston. 
* When extending (feeding forward), oil flows through the **A-port oil connection (2)**.
* When retracting (return movement), oil flows through the **B-port oil connection (1)**.

questions.question: When extending the boom zoom cylinder (13), through which specific ports (C1/C2 and V1/V2) of the pilot-to-open check valve (14) must the hydraulic oil flow to extend the cylinder and subsequently return to the tank?
questions.answer:
When extending the boom zoom cylinder (13), the hydraulic oil must flow into the pilot-to-open check valve (14) through port **V1** and out through port **C1** to reach the cylinder and extend it [1]. Subsequently, the return oil flows from the cylinder into the pilot-to-open check valve through port **C2** and out through port **V2** to return to the tank [2].

According to Section 4.5 "Extending boom" (Pages 28-29 of the BOOM manual), the complete step-by-step hydraulic sequence is as follows [1, 2]:

1. The percussion pressure line delivers oil to port P of the boom control valve [1].
2. The main pressure relief valve (10) limits the percussion circuit main pressure to 270 bars [1].
3. The pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (9) reduces and supplies a maximum pressure of 30 bars to the pilot circuit pilot valves (3 and 4), which then supply the reduced pressure from the pilot line to the main spool (1) [1].
4. The main spool changes its position when the pilot pressure is supplied from the energized pilot valve a (**3 / Y101A**) [1].
5. Oil flows through the main spool to port A3, onward to the pilot-to-open check valve (14) port **V1** and through port **C1** to the zoom cylinder (13) port A [1]. From there, it flows to the cylinder piston side, causing the cylinder and the boom to extend [1].
6. Return flow from the zoom cylinder (13) piston rod side flows out of the cylinder port B, to the pilot-to-open check valve port **C2** and from port **V2** to the port B3 of the boom control valve [2].
7. Oil flows through the main spool (1) to port T and onward to the pressurized return collector, and from there back to the hydraulic oil tank [2].

questions.question: When the pilot valve (4 / Y103B) is energized to move the feed extension forward, through which specific main spool port does the hydraulic oil flow to reach port B of the feed extension cylinder (17)?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.11 "Feed extension forward" (Page 40 of the BOOM manual), when the pilot valve (**4 / Y103B**) is energized, the hydraulic oil flows through the main spool to **port B6** to reach port B of the feed extension cylinder (17) [1].

The complete step-by-step hydraulic sequence for moving the feed extension forward is as follows:

1. The percussion pressure line delivers oil to port P of the boom control valve [1].
2. The main pressure relief valve (**10**) limits the percussion circuit main pressure to **270 bars** [1].
3. The pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (**9**) reduces and supplies a maximum pressure of **30 bars** to the pilot circuit pilot valves (**3 and 4**), which then supply the reduced pressure from the pilot line to the main spool (**1**) [1].
4. The main spool changes its position when the pilot pressure is supplied from the energized pilot valve b (**4 / Y103B**) [1].
5. Oil flows through the main spool to **port B6**, onward to the feed extension cylinder (**17**) port B, and from there to the cylinder piston rod side, causing the cylinder to retract and the feed extension to move forward [1].
6. Return flow from the extension cylinder (**17**) piston rod side flows out of the cylinder port A and to **port A6** of the boom control valve [2].
7. Oil flows through the main spool (**1**) to port T and onward to the pressurized return collector and from there back to the hydraulic oil tank [2].

questions.question: How can an operator view the history of electrical alerts, such as pressure sensor or fuel level electrical failures?
questions.answer: The operator can access the Log view by selecting the menu icon and then "Log", or by selecting the alert symbol at the top of the display [8, 9]. The log shows current and historical data for alerts in chronological order, including problem duration, frequency, measurement values, and associated limit values, which helps assess the seriousness of the electrical error [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the setpoints for the main pressure relief valves and standby pressures in the drilling hydraulic circuits?
questions.answer: The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) limits the maximum pressure to 270 bars [12-14]. The rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) limits the rotation circuit's maximum pressure to 250 bars [15, 16]. The feed port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves are set to 200 bars and 240 bars, respectively, to protect the actuators against pressure peaks [17, 18]. The standby pressure (flow controller A) for the percussion/feed pump is adjusted to maintain a pressure difference of 22-30 bars (typically 30 bars) [19, 20], while the rotation pump flow controller is set to 20-23 bars [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose and fix a rotation system where the rotation pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Symptom:** Rotation pressure is abnormally low during drilling [10]. **Cause:** There is a leak in the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3), the shuttle valve (20.7), the electro proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6), or an internal leak within the rock drill rotation motor itself [10-12]. **Corrective Action:** Check, clean, and replace the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) and re-adjust it [11]. If unresolved, check and replace the shuttle valve (20.7), and inspect the electro proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) for leaks to the tank line [11]. Finally, if pressure remains low, check and repair the rock drill rotation motor [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the most common physical faults found in the CAN bus cabling?
questions.answer: Common cabling faults may include cable, wire, or connector interruptions, short-circuits, installation errors, and incorrectly connected or loose internal termination resistors [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components make up the dewatering pump starter block for short-circuit, overload, and earth continuity protection?
questions.answer: The dewatering pump starter block includes the **F9** motor-protective 1000 V circuit breaker (part number **NZMH2-A20-S1** for type C) and **F9A** overload protection relay for short-circuit and overload protection [11, 12]. It also includes the **K9** dewatering pump contactors, the **K9A** earth continuity protection relay, and the **K9B** residual current protection relay [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)
