questions.question: How can an operator identify problems with electrical signaling between control devices and system components using the control system display?
questions.answer: The operator can use the Troubleshooting diagram, which shows real-time electrical signaling [1-3]. A red X on a module indicates it is offline, not working, or connected to an option not included on the rig [3, 4]. A gray signaling arrow before a component shows that the connection is inactive, while a colored arrow indicates an active signal [5, 6]. Additionally, individual valve IDs display the exact control current being received and their ON/OFF state [5, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the rotation line pressure compensator (20.2) and the feed line pressure compensator (20.17)?
questions.answer: The rotation line pressure compensator (20.2) maintains a constant pressure difference over the rotation main spool (20.1) regardless of input and load pressure changes, which results in a constant rotation speed [3, 13]. Similarly, the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) maintains a constant pressure difference over the feed main spool (20.16), resulting in a constant flow rate and feed speed [4, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the main hydraulic pump specifications and output flow rates for the powerpack and water systems?
questions.answer: The DL432i is powered by a 90 kW HPP990 hydraulic powerpack [2]. The system utilizes a 140 cm³ variable displacement pump (1) for the percussion and feed circuits, and a 71 cm³ variable displacement pump (2) for the rotation circuit [9, 10]. During drilling at maximum percussion pressure, the flow rate for the RD921S rock drill is 120-135 L/min, and 135-150 L/min for the RD927L rock drill, while the feed circuit flow rate is 21 L/min [11]. The water booster pump (WBP3HP) is an 11 kW pump with an output capacity of 375 L/min at 15 bars (assuming a 5 bar inlet pressure) [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings occur if the access protector system detects an object in the hazard zone, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: In protector mode, if a person enters the hazard zone (or if triggered by water or sinking jacks), drilling and boom movements are prevented, the red detection warning light blinks, and a detection icon with a popup note appears on the display [13, 14]. The operator must make sure no one is in the hazard zone and then push the acknowledgment button to reactivate the system [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What symptoms indicate that the hydraulic rotation speed is adjusted incorrectly?
questions.answer: A rotation speed that is too high is diagnosed by fast wear on the drill bit's outer edge, fine drilling cuttings, and excessive wear on rock drill components [2]. Conversely, too low of a rotation speed causes uneven drill rod rotation, a decreased penetration speed, and increased strain on the rotation mechanism and drill rods [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the likely cause and procedure if the percussion remains on continuously when the power pack or diesel engine is running?
questions.answer: Assuming the electrical and control systems are operating properly, it is likely that either the percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck and leaking, which allows pressure to reach the rock drill's percussion mechanism [5]. You must stop the power pack and/or diesel engine immediately because too low percussion pressure can cause damage to the seals of the accumulators in the rock drill [6]. Then check, clean, and if necessary, replace the valves (20.9) and (20.10) [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning occurs if the cabin door is open or the seat belt is unfastened?
questions.answer: The door latch and seat belt monitoring system will trigger a buzzer warning sound and display a notice pop-up on the screen when the engine is started, warning the operator not to tram the rig [17-20]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you prepare the DL432i for CAN bus resistance measurements, and what are the expected normal values?
questions.answer: Disconnect the power from the control system by turning the battery main switch (S1) to position 0 [1, 2]. Measure the total resistance between the CAN_HI and CAN_LO wires [3]. A normal reading is approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω, which indicates that the cables, connectors, and both 120 Ω termination resistors at the ends of the bus are intact [1, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the steering and brake control manifold (10) and its priority valve (10.10)?
questions.answer: The steering and brake control manifold (10) directs and controls oil flow and pressure to the carrier's steering and brake circuits [15]. The priority valve (10.10) within it prioritizes the steering function above the secondary circuit and also acts as a steering circuit retarder valve [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can an operator diagnose why the power pack stops unexpectedly?
questions.answer: The operator should check for possible alarm messages on the display, verify that none of the circuit breakers in the MQ cabinet have tripped, make sure all emergency stop buttons have been released, and ensure that the pilot circuit is functional [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the expected resistance values when troubleshooting the CAN bus physical cables with a multimeter?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected, the normal total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO should measure approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω [13-15]. A reading of < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit, > 100 Ω indicates an interruption or faulty termination resistors, and ~40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted at at least two points with both termination resistors missing or faulty [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the procedures and values for adjusting the output voltage on the control system power supply units (A3, A4) after replacement?
questions.answer: Leave both DC+ wires unconnected and switch on the power [4]. Select "Single use" mode on both units and adjust the output voltage to exactly 27.5 V ± 0.1 V using the potentiometer [5]. Then, select "Parallel use" mode on both units to achieve load sharing, switch off the power, and connect the DC+ terminals [5], [6]. Finally, switch the power back on and verify the DC-voltage is around 28.5 V without load and 27.5 V with full load [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the feed system when the feed or fast feed speed is incorrect?
questions.answer: Symptom:** The feed or fast feed speed is not correct despite the pressures, electrical, and control systems operating properly [1]. **Cause:** The feed valve main spool (20.16) is stuck, or the pilot pressure from the feed pilot control valves (20.20 and/or 20.21) is too low [1]. **Corrective Action:** Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block to check the pilot pressure, which should be 30-45 bars when the power pack is loaded [2]. If incorrect, check, clean, and replace the pilot oil filter (20.26) and reducing valve (20.27) [2]. If the pressure is correct, remove, inspect, and potentially replace the feed pilot control valves (20.20, 20.21) and check the feed valve main spool (20.16) [2, 3]. If the main spool is faulty, replace the entire drilling control valve block [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do the percussion selector valve (20.9) and the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) operate together?
questions.answer: The percussion selector valve (20.9) is responsible for opening and closing the percussion main valve (20.10) [5]. When open, the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) directs the hydraulic oil flow directly to the rock drill's percussion mechanism (24) [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can an operator diagnose if the hydraulic feed pressure is set too high or too low?
questions.answer: Too high feed pressure is indicated by rotation jamming, increased rotation torque, and bending of the drilling rods [2]. Too low feed pressure results in loose drill rod connections, which causes percussion energy to reflect back to the rock drill and damage the equipment [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What CAN bus faults cannot be diagnosed using a multimeter?
questions.answer: A multimeter cannot detect faulty CAN sensors with sensor signal faults, missing CAN signals, or bit-level signal faults [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning conditions are indicated by the shank lubrication unit's status indicator flashing?
questions.answer: If the SLU status indicator flashes three times, there is a problem with the air pressure or the air pressure sensor is broken/disconnected [15]. If it flashes four times, the lubrication oil level in the tank is below the minimum limit or the level sensor is broken [16]. The operator should check the SLU air pressure or oil level, and verify that the sensor current signals are at normal values of 4–20 mA [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does an operator diagnose general hydraulic system health and potential filter issues?
questions.answer: The operator should visually check the hydraulic system for possible oil leaks, loose hoses, frayed wires, or other apparent service needs [4]. Additionally, they should check the oil level through the sight glass on the side of the receiver and monitor the drilling display for any warnings triggered by the pressure filter's clogging indicator [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you identify and reset an earth fault lockout (EFLO) or frozen contactor (FC) trip on the K293 protection relay?
questions.answer: EFLO and FC trips are visually indicated by the Blue LED on the S293 pushbutton, which is located on the door of the MQ main switchgear [8]. If an EFLO trip occurs, it is latched in the memory of the K293 relay and must be cleared externally by pressing the S293 reset pushbutton [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are CAN bus faults initially identified on the DL432i drill rig?
questions.answer: Any fault on the CAN bus must first be identified using the instructions and notifications on the operator's display panel, which notifies the operator if the bus nodes are in a fault mode or switched off [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a fault using the LED indicators on the residual current protection relay (K9B)?
questions.answer: On the K9B relay, if both the Green LED (5) and Red LED (6) are continuously ON, a fault current has been detected, which orders the associated contactor (K9) to open [2], [3]. If the Green LED is ON and the Red LED is flashing, it indicates a relay/sensor link fault, and if both are OFF, there is no voltage or the device is not in service [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose CAN bus short-circuits using voltage measurements?
questions.answer: With the control system turned on, measure the voltage between CAN_HI-GND and CAN_LO-GND [7]. The normal reading without load is 2.5 V ±0.2 V [7, 8]. If the measurement is < 1 V or > 4 V, there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [7]. A voltage continuously near 0 V indicates a short-circuit to ground or a short-circuit between the CAN wires, while a voltage continuously near the supply voltage (VS) indicates a short-circuit to the supply voltage [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How should you respond if the percussion system remains engaged unintentionally?
questions.answer: Symptom:** The percussion remains on all the time when the power pack or diesel engine is running [19]. **Cause:** The percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck and leaks, allowing pressure to reach the rock drill's percussion mechanism [19]. **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and/or diesel engine immediately, because running with continuous low percussion pressure can severely damage the seals of the accumulators in the rock drill [20]. Check, clean, and if necessary, replace the faulty valves (20.9 and 20.10) [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the thermostat valve (9) in the hydraulic return line?
questions.answer: The thermostat valve (9) monitors the returning oil temperature. If the oil temperature is below the thermostat valve's setting limit (45 °C), the return oil is guided straight to the hydraulic receiver [8, 12]. Once the temperature reaches the limit, the valve directs the oil to flow through the oil-water (OW) cooler (5) or the optional oil-air (OA) cooler (30) [8, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25)?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack, loosen the locking nut, and tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.25) almost to its end, over 270 bars [9, 10]. Open the flow and pressure controllers (A and B) of pump 1 almost fully [10]. Connect a gauge to MP2, start the power pack, turn flow controller A fully closed, and run the boom zoom against the rear stopper [10, 11]. Turn pressure controller B clockwise until the gauge shows 280 bars [11]. Then, loosen the main pressure relief valve (20.25) until it fizzes and the pressure drops to the setpoint of 270 bars [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which control system components utilize the VCH module, and what are its key features?
questions.answer: The Boom Controller (BC), Drilling Controller (DC), Rod handler Controller (RC), Vehicle Controller (VC), End Controller (EC), Switch Controller (SC), and Front Controller (FC) all use the **VCH (Valve Controller High Temp)** module [4-6]. It is a CANopen slave I/O-module featuring a Freescale Cortex-M4 100 MHz 32-bit processor and separate output powering/cutoff circuitry designed to safely deactivate outputs in SIL2/PLd systems [4, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are faults with the percussion pressure diagnosed during drilling?
questions.answer: Incorrect percussion pressure is diagnosed by observing specific drilling symptoms; too high pressure causes worn drill bits, shortened tool life, and an increased risk of drill rod jamming, while too low pressure results in a decreased penetration rate [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the master branch fuse (F58), glow plugs fuse (F59), and diesel alternator master fuse (F60) located in the DQ cabinet?
questions.answer: The **F58** (80 A) fuse serves as the master branch fuse for the 24 VDC control system [13, 15]. The **F59** (80 A) fuse protects the glow plugs [13, 15]. The **F60** (125 A) fuse acts as the diesel alternator master fuse [13, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the feed or fast feed pressure is too high?
questions.answer: Symptom:** Feed or fast feed pressure is too high, which can manifest as rotation jamming (varying rotation speed), increased rotation torque, or bending of the drilling rods [5, 6]. **Cause:** The electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22), feed port shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18, 20.19), feed counterbalance valve (27.1), pilot controlled check valve (27.6), or feed counter pressure electro proportional relief valve (27.5) is stuck, or the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) is mechanically damaged [5, 7]. **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and check, clean, or replace the feed port shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18, 20.19) and electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) [8, 9]. If replacing the feed port valves, adjust port A to 200 bars and port B to 240 bars [8, 9]. If the issue persists, check the feed load control block and inspect the feed line pressure compensator (20.17), replacing the drilling control valve block if it is damaged [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What alarms are triggered if the service brake accumulator pressure drops, and what happens to the rig?
questions.answer: If the pressure drops below 110 bars, a notice popup appears on the GUI [3]. If the pressure drops below the factory set limit of 75 bars, a warning light turns on, an alarm message is displayed, and a "tramming forced stop" is activated [3, 4]. During a forced stop, the hydrostatic transmission is forced to neutral, an alarm sounds in the cabin, and the spring-applied brakes engage [3, 5]. In emergency situations, the operator can use a maintenance-level bypass to move the rig, which limits the speed to a 4 km/h creep mode [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure and setpoint for adjusting the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)?
questions.answer: Unplug the electrical connectors for valves 10.16 and 10.18, and connect the Y167 connector to valve 10.16 [5]. Attach 250 bar pressure gauges to measuring connectors MPB and MCR [6]. Run the boom zoom backward to lock the adjustment [6]. At maximum diesel engine rpm, turn the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (10.8) fully clockwise, ensuring the MPB gauge does not exceed 205 bars [6, 7]. Adjust the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) until the MCR gauge reads 210 bars [7]. Finally, turn the 10.8 adjusting screw counterclockwise until the MPB gauge drops to exactly 200 bars, and tighten the locking nut [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings does the ANSUL fire suppression system provide, and how should the operator respond?
questions.answer: The system features a yellow warning light for low tank pressure and a red warning light for a system fault or discharge [1]. If the system activates or pressure drops, an audiovisual alarm triggers and a 6-second automatic engine shutdown timer begins [2]. The operator can press the delay extension button during the countdown to gain an additional 20 seconds, allowing them to have both hands free to safely drive the machine out of the way before the engine shuts down [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What module is used for the Mains Controller (MC) and Air Water Controller (AWC), and what is its design architecture?
questions.answer: The MC and AWC use the **FPVC (Fast Proportional Valve Controller)** module [12]. The FPVC is a CANopen slave I/O-module powered by a 72 MHz ARM7 32-bit processor and internal FPGA support [12, 13]. Its architecture is specifically designed to meet SIL2 class safety requirements [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the two primary variable displacement pumps (1 and 2) in the drilling system?
questions.answer: Variable displacement pump (1) delivers the required amount of oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulic systems, as well as the optional stabilizer and power extractor [1, 2]. Variable displacement pump (2) delivers the required amount of oil to the rotation hydraulic system [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a tripped circuit breaker or burned fuse indicate in the electrical system and how is it handled?
questions.answer: Breaker tripping or a fuse burn is a sign of a failure, such as an overload or short circuit, which must be repaired before resetting the breaker or replacing the fuse [3]. You must always use the original fuse size and type, and never replace it with a fuse having a higher ampere value than the original [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you identify the specific type of CAN bus short-circuit using voltage measurements?
questions.answer: If the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level remains continuously near 0 V, there is either a short-circuit between the CAN wire and ground, or a short-circuit directly between the CAN_LO and CAN_HI wires [7, 8]. If the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level remains continuously near the supply voltage (VS), there is a short-circuit between the CAN wire and the supply voltage [7]. Notably, in the cases of a short-circuit to ground or to the supply voltage, the resistance measured between CAN_LO and CAN_HI may still falsely display a normal value of ~60 Ω [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are faults in the electrical signaling between control devices and system components diagnosed?
questions.answer: They are diagnosed using the Troubleshooting diagram on the control system display, which shows real-time electrical signaling [4, 5]. A red X on a module indicates it is offline, not working, or connected to an option not included on the rig [4, 6]. A gray signaling arrow before a component shows that the signaling connection is inactive, while a colored arrow indicates an active signal [7, 8]. Individual valve IDs will also show the exact control current being received [7, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the troubleshooting procedure for low percussion pressure?
questions.answer: Symptom:** The percussion pressure gauge on the main view shows a low reading, or there is a noticeably decreased penetration rate (especially in softer rock) [21, 22]. **Cause:** The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25), electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14), or percussion pressure compensator (20.11) is stuck or dirty, or the LS-line orifices (20.12, 20.13) are blocked [21, 23, 24]. **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack [21, 25]. Clean, check, and replace valves 20.25, 20.14, and 20.11 as needed [21, 25]. If the pressure is still low, remove the plugs from the ports of the orifices (20.12, 20.13), carefully extract the orifices to check and clean them, and reinstall them securely into the drilling control valve block [19, 21, 24, 26]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Identify the functions of the control system modules EC, MC, BC, and DC.
questions.answer: The **EC** is the End controller, the **MC** is the Mains controller, the **BC** is the Boom controller, and the **DC** is the Drilling controller [16-19]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function and part number of the power pack circuit breaker (F1)?
questions.answer: The power pack circuit breaker (**F1**), part number **NZMN2ME140NA** (for a 55 kW motor), provides motor protection using an electronic release with phase failure sensitivity [10]. It includes an adjustable overload release (Ir = 70 - 140 A) with a long time pick-up delay to overcome current peaks, and an undelayed short-circuit release [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the power extractor pressure is abnormal or has no pressure at all?
questions.answer: Connect a 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring point (M3) of the drilling control valve block (20) or the power extractor valve block (21) [14]. If there is no pressure reading when the power extractor is run, check if the power extractor on/off valve (21.1), percussion selector valve (20.9), or percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck [14, 15]. If the pressure is too low or too high, the fault may be in the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) or the LS-line orifices (20.12) and (20.13), which should be removed, cleaned, and replaced if faulty [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a short-circuit or interruption on the CAN bus using resistance measurements?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected from the control system, measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO [3, 4]. A reading of approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω indicates the bus and its termination resistors are intact, while a reading of < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit [3, 5]. A reading of > 100 Ω indicates an interruption or faulty termination resistors, and a reading of ~40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted at at least two points with both termination resistors missing or faulty [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) and pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (10.11)?
questions.answer: To adjust the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9), attach a 250 bar gauge to measuring connector MPS, loosen the locking nut, and turn the screw counterclockwise to fully open [1]. With the engine at maximum rpm and the carrier hydraulics pressurized, turn the adjusting screw clockwise until the gauge reads 220 bars, then tighten the locking nut [1, 2]. For the pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (10.11), attach a 40 bar gauge to MX, fully open the screw, run the engine at maximum rpm with carrier hydraulics pressurized, and turn the screw clockwise until the gauge reads 35 bars [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure settings for the steering and braking circuits on the carrier?
questions.answer: The steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) limits the steering circuit's maximum pressure to 220 bars [21, 22]. The brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8) limits the service brake circuit's maximum pressure to 200 bars [21, 23]. The accumulator charging valve (21) maintains the charging oil pressure of the service brake accumulators between 135 and 160 bars [24]. Finally, the hydrostatic transmission (HST) charge pressure relief valve (1.5) limits the maximum pressure of the charge pressure circuit to 28 bars [25]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you isolate whether a resistance fault is in the bus cable or the termination resistors?
questions.answer: Disconnect both termination resistors from the bus and measure the resistance of each resistor separately [6]. If the resistance of both resistors is exactly 120 Ω, they are intact and the fault is likely located in the bus cable itself [3, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific steps and components to check if the diesel engine will not start?
questions.answer: Check for alarm messages on the display, ensure the battery isolation switch (S1) and starter isolator switch (S2) are in the ON position, and verify that no circuit breakers in the DQ cabinet have tripped [1]. Additionally, ensure all emergency stop buttons are released, the parking brake is engaged, neutral gear is selected, the fuel level is adequate, and the fire suppression system is not preventing the start [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the Carrier Master (CM) and the Off-board controller (OC), and what module do they share?
questions.answer: Both components use the **SCU** machine control computer, which runs on an 800 MHz Freescale ARM Cortex A8 processor [17, 18]. The Carrier Master (CM) operates on the rear carrier bus as the master for the carrier systems, while the Off-board controller (OC) acts as the main controller in the Teleremote console [17, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the drilling control valve block (20) and its main spools for rotation (20.1) and feed (20.16)?
questions.answer: The drilling control valve block (20) controls all primary drilling functions, including percussion, rotation, and feed [3]. Inside this block, the rotation valve main spool (20.1) directs oil flow to the work ports (A or B) of the rotation valve and to the rotation mechanism [3]. The feed valve main spool (20.16) directs oil flow to the work ports (A or B) of the feed valve and to the feed mechanism [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you read a communication error or pin short-circuit directly from an FPVC or VCH control module's 7-segment display?
questions.answer: The display flashes a sequence showing the node ID, operational state, error type, and exact pin fault, where "s" is a short circuit to ground, "o" is an open circuit, and "b" is a short circuit to the battery [10-12]. For example, the sequence "24 - oP – J6 – 5s" indicates Node ID 24, Operational state (oP), and output pin XJ6.5 is short-circuited to ground [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific filtration requirements and the recommended cleanliness class for the DL432i hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The standard hydraulic system requires a pressure filter with a filtration size of 20 µm absolute [1, 2], and a return oil filter rated at 10 µm absolute [2-4]. The hydraulic oil receiver is equipped with a breather that filters air to 5 µm [5]. If the machine is equipped with optional filters, the bypass filter provides 2 µm absolute filtration [6], and the stabilizer oil line filter is rated at 10 µm absolute [7]. The manufacturer's recommendation for the maximum permissible degree of contamination (cleanliness class) is 18/16/13 according to the ISO 4406 (c) standard [4, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose why the diesel engine will not start?
questions.answer: Check for possible alarm messages on the display, make sure the battery isolation switch (S1) and starter isolator switch (S2) are in the ON position, check that no circuit breakers in the DQ cabinet have tripped, and verify all emergency stop buttons are released [1]. Additionally, check that neutral gear is selected, the parking brake is engaged, check the fuel level and battery condition, make sure there is enough trailing cable on the reel so the alarm limit is not reached, and check that the fire suppression system is not preventing the engine from starting [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do Cummins engine fault codes 5939 and 5941 indicate regarding the primary J1939 CAN bus data link?
questions.answer: Code 5939 (SPN 520968 FMI 9) indicates an abnormal update rate, meaning no communication or an invalid data transfer rate was detected on the J1939 data link between the Engine Control Module (ECM) and the machine electronic control unit [16]. Code 5941 (SPN 520968 FMI 19) indicates that the received J1939 datalink message was not valid, triggering a "Received Network Data in Error" fault [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (3)?
questions.answer: Start the diesel engine and let it idle [17]. Connect a pressure gauge to the water hose reel measuring point (6) on the rear carrier control block [17]. Loosen the locking nut of the pressure reducing/relieving valve (3) and pressurize the system by raising a jack carefully against its stopper [17]. Turn the adjusting screw until the pressure reaches 80 bar (or 83 bar for the DU422i-W model), and then lock the adjustment screw [18]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be inspected if the feed or fast feed pressure is too high during operation despite mechanical, electrical, and control systems operating properly?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack and check if the electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22), the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18), the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19), feed counterbalance valve (27.1), pilot controlled check valve (27.6), or feed counter pressure electro proportional relief valve (27.5) is stuck [10]. If the port valves are replaced, the feed port A valve (20.18) should be adjusted to 200 bars, and the feed port B valve (20.19) to 240 bars [11, 12]. If the pressure is still too high, check the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) for mechanical damage and replace the whole drilling control valve block if necessary [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for measuring the CAN bus voltage level to check for short-circuits, and what are the correct values?
questions.answer: Ensure the control system is ON by turning the battery main switch (S1) to position 1 [5]. Measure the voltage between CAN_HI-GND and CAN_LO-GND [5]. With no load, both lines should measure 2.5 V ±0.2 V [5, 6]. When the bus is loaded, CAN_HI should be above 2.5 VDC and CAN_LO should be below 2.5 VDC [6]. A reading of < 1 V or > 4 V indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the adjustment procedure for the shank lubrication air pressure?
questions.answer: Loosen the locking nut of the restrictor valve and turn the adjusting screw fully open [16]. Start the power pack and activate air flushing [16]. Tighten the adjusting screw until the "Air pressure" reading on the control system display rises to exactly 4 bars, then tighten the locking nut [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific faults are indicated if the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO deviates from the normal 60 Ω?
questions.answer: A reading of < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [3]. A reading of > 100 Ω means one end of the bus is interrupted or the termination resistors are faulty [3]. A reading of ~40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted at at least two points and both termination resistors are missing or faulty [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are flushing pressure faults recognized during operation?
questions.answer: Low flushing pressure is identified by an increased risk of jamming, overheating drill bits, a decreased penetration rate, and overly fine cuttings [3]. Excessively high flushing pressure increases drill bit wearing and shortens the service life of the flushing housing seals [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you determine if a CAN side branch is interrupted using a multimeter?
questions.answer: Measure the bus impedance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI directly on the interrupted side branch [11, 12]. If the node is connected to the bus during the measurement, the impedance will be approximately 40 kΩ [11, 12]. If the node is disconnected during measurement, the bus impedance will be infinite [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What hydraulic components should be checked if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling, assuming the variable displacement pump (2) is adjusted correctly?
questions.answer: It is likely that a valve is leaking. First, check, clean, and if necessary, replace the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) [7, 8]. If this does not help, check and replace the shuttle valve (20.7) [8]. Next, inspect the electro proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6), which may be leaking LS-pressure to the tank line [8, 9]. Finally, if the pressure remains low, check the rock drill rotation motor for internal leaks [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What happens when the cable reel warning and stop limits are reached during tramming, and how must the operator respond?
questions.answer: When the first limit (warning) is reached (minimum 4 rounds of cable left), an alarm sounds, a pop-up appears, and the parking brake engages after a 4-second delay [6]. The operator can push and hold the bypass button and release the parking brake to carefully continue tramming [6-8]. If the second limit (alarm/stop) is reached (minimum 2 rounds left), the parking brake engages immediately [7]. The operator must then disconnect the cable from the power supply center and reel in the cable a half round using the External Reel Control Panel (ERCP) until the stop limit is released [7, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: If an abnormal resistance is measured, how do you isolate whether the fault is in the termination resistors or the CAN bus cable?
questions.answer: Disconnect both termination resistors from the bus and measure the resistance of each separately [4]. If both measure 120 Ω, they are intact and the fault is likely in the bus cable itself [4]. To isolate the exact fault location, move the termination resistor to the next measuring point (node/actuator), disconnect the bus cable from that actuator, connect the termination resistor in its place, and re-measure [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical fuses are located inside the JB99 junction box?
questions.answer: The **JB99** junction box contains three circuit breakers: **F1** (10 A) for the line heater relay and Engine Control Module (ECM), **F2** (10 A) for the DEF supply module, and **F3** (6 A) for the diesel CAN sensor supply [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Identify the function and component type of the Gatekeeper Controller (GSC).
questions.answer: The Gatekeeper Controller (GSC) utilizes an **IFM safety-PLC** equipped with a 16-bit C167CS processor [10]. It uses a 55-pin connector to interface with the system and operates on the front carrier bus [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are controlled by the BOU module, and what is its function?
questions.answer: The **BOU (Boom Control Unit)** module functions as the Boom Sensors converter (BS), Feed Sensors converter (FS), and the optional Bit Changer controller (BCS) [8]. It is a CANopen slave module with an internal 100 MHz Cortex-M4 ARM 32-bit processor and FPGA support, providing configurable function blocks such as pressure controllers, filters, and basic drilling control algorithms [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a blinking diesel engine shutdown light indicate, and how can the operator respond?
questions.answer: A blinking diesel engine shutdown light indicates a severe engine problem and that the automatic engine shutdown process has started [10, 11]. The operator can push the override button to keep the engine running for an additional 30 seconds; this allows the operator to safely move the machine if the stopped rig would block safety exits or cause an environmental hazard [10, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the compressor cooler fan pressure difference adjusted?
questions.answer: Attach pressure gauges to measuring points MA and MB, open the locking nut of the pressure relief valve (3), and remove its electrical connector [14]. Tighten the adjusting screw until the pressure difference between the two gauges reaches exactly 60 bars [14, 15]. This 60 bar pressure difference is the factory setting and corresponds to a fan rotation speed of approximately 2000 rpm [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component manages the oil distribution to the brake accumulators?
questions.answer: The accumulator charging valve (21) distributes oil from the brake pump (7.2) to the service brake circuit or to the secondary control circuit and air conditioning [17]. Its priority valve (21.1) and control valve (21.2) work together to ensure the system maintains a pressure of 135-160 bars in the service brake pressure accumulators (22 and 23) [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components utilize the VIU module, and what type of inputs is it designed to handle?
questions.answer: The **VIU** module is utilized by the Mains Sensor converter (MS), Tramming Controller (TCP), Teleremote Spotlight Controller (TSC), and Proximity Detection System Controller (PDSC) [14, 15]. It provides specific 5 V analog inputs for joysticks and potentiometers, digital inputs, and PT100/PT1000/PTC temperature sensor inputs [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the pressure filter (8) and the optional by-pass filter (10)?
questions.answer: The pressure filter (8) filters the hydraulic oil coming immediately from the variable displacement pump (1) at a filtration size of 20 µm absolute [8, 9]. The optional by-pass filter (10) provides secondary filtration by taking hydraulic oil from the rotation circuit and filtering it down to 2 µm absolute [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the main switch (Q1), battery isolation switch (S1), and starter isolator switch (S2)?
questions.answer: The main switch (**Q1**) cuts off the mains electric supply and can be locked in the 0 (OFF) position [1, 2]. The battery isolation switch (**S1**) disconnects the 24 VDC battery when in the OFF position, though it does not disconnect the direct supply from the battery [3, 4]. The starter isolator switch (**S2**) prevents the diesel engine from starting when in the OFF position; turning it OFF during operation shuts down the diesel engine [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the flow controller value of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) deviates from its set value and shows normal tank pressure?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring connector (LS) of the pump (1) [1]. If the pressure is normal tank pressure (approx. 3-5 bar or less), the flow controller (A) is likely incorrectly adjusted or stuck [2]. Adjust the stand-by pressure to the correct value (a pressure difference of 30 bar) with the flow controller (A) [2-4]. If adjusting does not help, stop the power pack and repair or replace the entire controller unit [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps for incorrect rotation speed or unresponsive rotation speed adjustment?
questions.answer: Symptom:** The rotation speed adjustment does not work as desired, the rounds of the drill rod are not constant, or you observe drilling defects like fast wear of the bit's outer edge (speed too high) or uneven rotation/decreased penetration (speed too low) [6, 13]. **Cause:** There is a fault in the rock drill, the rotation pilot control valves (20.4, 20.5), the rotation valve main spool (20.1), or the rotation line pressure compensator (20.2) [13]. **Corrective Action:** Adjust the rotation speed setting to the proper level for the rock [14]. If mechanical/hydraulic adjustment is failing, verify the pilot pressure is 30-45 bars [15]. Inspect, clean, or replace the rotation pilot control valves (20.4, 20.5), the rotation valve main spool (20.1), or the rotation line pressure compensator (20.2) [15-18]. Repair or replace damaged rock drill components [18]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the adjustment steps and setpoints for the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3)?
questions.answer: Tighten the main pressure relief valve (20.3) almost to its end, over 250 bar [12]. Connect a pressure gauge to measuring point MP1 [13]. Open flow controller A and pressure controller B on pump 2 almost fully [12, 13]. Start the power pack, turn flow controller A fully closed so the pump operates at constant pressure, and turn pressure controller B clockwise until the gauge shows 260 bar [13]. Finally, loosen the main pressure relief valve (20.3) until it fizzes and the pressure gauge drops to the setpoint of 250 bar [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical components and circuits should be checked if the power pack fails to start or stops unexpectedly?
questions.answer: If the power pack will not start, verify the mains electric supply connection, ensure the main switch (Q1) is in the 1 (ON) position, check for display alarm messages, and ensure all emergency stop buttons are released [7]. If it stops unexpectedly, check that none of the circuit breakers in the MQ cabinet have tripped and ensure that the pilot circuit remains functional [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the Drilling Master (DM1) and what type of module does it use?
questions.answer: The Drilling Master (DM1) utilizes an **XCU** machine control computer, which features a 4-core 1.2GHz ARM Cortex A53 processor [1, 2]. It is responsible for controlling one boom, handling joint position control, forward and inverse boom kinematics, trajectory generation, automatic hole-to-hole positioning, and basic drilling control algorithms [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the control system display differentiate between general alarms and notices, and what are the required operator responses?
questions.answer: The system displays Red Alarm pop-up dialogs for major problems, which require the operator's immediate attention to stop working and correct the error to prevent damage to the drill rig [21, 22]. Yellow Notice pop-up dialogs indicate medium problems that do not require immediate action, but the operator should investigate and correct the reason if the alert persists or is repeated often [21, 22]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the S9, H9, H1, and S293 components on the MQ cabinet?
questions.answer: The **S9** switch acts as a remote button that controls the battery main breaker (F41) and main switch (Q1) to cut off power, and also functions as a dewatering pump test/reset switch [5-7]. The **H9** indicator light shows a dewatering pump earth leakage fault (continuous light) or an earth circuit fault (blinking light) [2, 5]. The **H1** indicator light turns on to indicate a wrong phase sequence [2, 5]. The **S293** pushbutton features a blue LED that indicates EFL- and FC-faults, and is used to reset the dewatering pump EFLO [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL432i Technical Manual)

questions.question: If the feed pressure is too low during operation, and you've connected a gauge to the LS connector of pump (1) and disconnected the electrical connector from the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22), but the pressure fails to reach 210 bars against the rear end stopper, is valve 20.22 the culprit or should you move on to inspecting shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18) and (20.19)?
questions.answer:
Valve **20.22** is the likely culprit. According to the troubleshooting procedures for when the feed/fast feed pressure is too low, if the pressure at the measuring connector (LS) fails to reach approximately 210 bars during this test, you should address the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) first [1, 2]. You should only move on to inspecting the shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19) if resolving the issue with 20.22 does not fix the problem [3].

Here is the step-by-step diagnostic sequence defined in the manual (Section 6.10: Feed / fast feed pressure is too low, pages 68-69):

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring connector (LS) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) [1].
2. Disconnect the electric connector from the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) and run the feed against the rear end stopper [1]. The pressure at the measuring connector (LS) should be approximately **210 bars** [1].
3. **If the pressure differs essentially from that value**, it is likely that the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) is stuck [2].
4. Stop the power pack [2].
5. Check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) [2].
6. Run the feed against the rear end stopper again and check the pressure at the measuring connector (LS) [2]. 
7. If the pressure is now approx. 210 bars, stop the power pack, reconnect the electric connector to valve (20.22), and remove the pressure gauge [2, 3].
8. **Only if the steps above did not remedy the situation** should you consider that the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18) or the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) may be faulty [3]. 

If you do move on to step 8 and need to replace valves (20.18) and (20.19), they must be adjusted using the following sequence:
*   Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point (M1) of the drilling control valve [3].
*   Use the pressure controller (B) to adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) to **250 bars** [4].
*   Run the feed against the front end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18) to **200 bars** [4].
*   Run the feed against the rear end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) to **240 bars** [4].
*   Re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) back to its normal operating specifications [4].

questions.question: During an automatic isolation test, the display shows a red battery icon with a red "x" indicating a high-voltage insulation fault. Which specific battery module circuit breakers and signal connectors must be manually disconnected at the Battery Fuse Box (BFQ) to isolate the failed unit from the DC-link?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 2.8.1 "Insulation monitoring and isolation test" (found on pages 80-81 of the Maintenance Manual, pages 84-85 of the Operator's Manual, and pages 81-82 of the Safety and Environmental Instructions), here is the step-by-step procedure to manually isolate the failed unit from the DC-link [1-3]:

1. **Isolate the failed battery from the DC-link** by setting its specific battery module circuit breaker to the **OFF** position based on the battery number [1-3]:
   *   Battery module 1: Circuit breaker **Q4**
   *   Battery module 2: Circuit breaker **Q5**
   *   Battery module 3: Circuit breaker **Q6**
   *   Battery module 4: Circuit breaker **Q7**

2. **Disconnect the failed battery from the control system** by removing its specific signal connector from the Battery Fuse Box (BFQ) [1-3]. The potential signal connectors are:
   *   **X903P**
   *   **X904P**
   *   **X905P**
   *   **X906P**

3. **Protect the disconnected socket** by covering it with an item such as a plastic bag [1, 2, 4].

4. **Replace the failed battery** as soon as possible and contact a Sandvik representative for instructions on how to return the battery for investigation [1, 2, 4].

questions.question: The Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) is exhibiting a single flash on its green CAN-RUN indicator, while the yellow STATUS indicator flashes three times. Based on these specific LED codes, what two distinct internal unit or sensor failures are occurring simultaneously?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided technical manuals, the two distinct failures occurring simultaneously are:

**1. Internal Control Unit Fault (Green CAN-RUN Indicator - Single Flash)**
A single flash on the green CAN-RUN indicator means the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) has stopped completely due to an internal fault [1, 2]. 

**2. Air Pressure Sensor Malfunction (Yellow STATUS Indicator - Three Flashes)**
Three flashes on the yellow STATUS indicator mean there is a malfunction with the air pressure sensor, or the air pressure itself is problematic. Specifically, the air pressure sensor is either broken or disconnected, causing the current signal from the sensor to drop below 2 mA [3, 4]. 

**Diagnostic Procedure & Values:**
According to the troubleshooting guidelines (Section 8.1.1, Page 44) and the SLCU technical data (Section 3.3, Page 13):
*   Check the SLU air pressure [5, 6].
*   Measure the current signal from the air pressure sensor [5, 6]. A functioning sensor should output a normal value between **4 and 20 mA**; a signal lower than **2 mA** confirms the sensor is faulty or disconnected [3-6].

questions.question: When testing the compressor's thermometer safety limits with an external heater, at what specific temperature thresholds should the system trigger the initial notice pop-up, and subsequently the alarm pop-up that automatically stops the compressor?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.13.9, "Checking the function of the thermometer safety limits" (found in the *Maintenance Manual*, page 365, and *maintenance.pdf*, page 323), the specific temperature thresholds are:

*   **Notice pop-up:** Triggered at **105 °C** [1, 2].
*   **Alarm pop-up and compressor stop:** Triggered at **115 °C** [1, 2].

The step-by-step sequence for testing these limits with an external heater is as follows:

1. Remove the temperature sensor from the compressor's body [1, 2].
2. Start the power packs, compressor, and water pump [1, 2].
3. Heat the sensor using a heater with an operation range of 0-120 °C and monitor the temperature gauge. **Note:** Do not use fire [1-4].
4. When the temperature reaches **105 °C**, check that the system gives a notice pop-up [1, 2].
5. When the temperature reaches **115 °C**, check that the system gives an alarm pop-up and the compressor stops [1, 2].

questions.question: You are troubleshooting an issue where the optional power extractor has zero pressure. After connecting a 250-bar pressure gauge to measuring point M3, you confirm the reading is zero. Assuming the electrical systems are fully functional, which specific valve in block 21 and which two specific valves in block 20 are the primary suspects for being stuck?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.15, "Power extractor pressure is not normal or it has no pressure at all" (found on page 75 of the hydraulic troubleshooting instructions), the primary suspects for being stuck are:

*   **In block 21:** The power extractor on/off valve **(21.1)** [1].
*   **In block 20:** The percussion selector valve **(20.9)** and the percussion 2-way cartridge valve **(20.10)** [1].

The exact step-by-step diagnostic sequence defined in the manual is as follows:

1. Make sure that electrics and control system are operating properly [2].
2. Connect a 250-bar pressure gauge to the measuring point **(M3)** of the drilling control valve block **(20)** or to the measuring point **(M3)** of the power extractor valve block **(21)** [2]. (Alternatively, check the pressure from the percussion pressure gauge on the main view of the control system [2]).
3. Start the power pack [1].
4. Run the power extractor [1].
5. If the pressure gauge is not showing any pressure reading, it is likely that the power extractor on/off valve **(21.1)**, the percussion selector valve **(20.9)** or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve **(20.10)** is stuck [1].
   * a) Stop the power pack and check the valves [1].
   * b) Clean and, if necessary, replace the faulty valve(s) [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) on the DL422iE, what specific pressure value should be reached at measuring point MP2 using the pressure controller (B), and what is the target stand-by pressure for the flow controller (A)?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.1.1, "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" in the hydraulic troubleshooting instructions, the specific values for the Sandvik DL422iE are:

*   **Pressure controller (B):** Must be adjusted to reach **250 bars** at measuring point **MP2** [1].
*   **Flow controller (A):** The target stand-by pressure must be adjusted to **30 bars** [2].

Here is the step-by-step adjustment sequence as defined in the source material:

1. Remove the caps from the flow controller (A) and the pressure controller (B) and undo the locking nuts of their adjusting spindles [3].
2. Open the adjusting screws of the pressure controller (B) and the flow controller (A) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
3. Connect the pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (MP2) of the drilling control block [3].
4. Start the power pack [4].
5. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) fully closed (clockwise) [4].
6. Run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the adjustment of the feed percussion pressure controller is locked [4].
7. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows 100 bars [4].
8. Let the LS-line bleed into a separate container by connecting a measuring hose to the measuring connector (LS) or loosening the hose/shuttle valve connection (C) of the flow controller (A). Once all air has escaped, remove the measuring hose or tighten the connection [1, 4].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge connected to MP2 shows **250 bars** [1].
10. Lock the adjustment of the pressure controller (B) with the locking nut [1].
11. Release the boom zoom function [2].
12. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [2].
13. Allow the pressure to stabilize in the pressure gauge connected to MP2 [2].
14. Adjust the stand-by pressure to **30 bars** from the flow controller (A) by turning the adjusting screw clockwise [2].
15. Lock the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) with the locking nut [2].
16. Stop the power pack [2].
17. Allow the pressure to come down to zero on the MP2 gauge [5].
18. Start the power pack and allow the pressure to stabilize again at MP2 [5].
19. If the stand-by pressure is in the recommended range, install the protective caps to the flow controller (A) and pressure controller (B). If not, readjust the flow controller [5].
20. Stop the power pack and remove the pressure gauge from measuring point MP2 [6].

questions.question: When calibrating the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) at measuring point MP1, the pump's pressure controller must first be temporarily set to what pressure value before loosening the main relief valve until the pressure drops to exactly 250 bars?
questions.answer:
When calibrating the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) at measuring point MP1, the pump's pressure controller (B) must first be temporarily set to **260 bars** [1].

Based on Section 5.3, "Adjusting the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve" in the drilling hydraulics manual, the complete step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows:

1. Stop the power pack [2].
2. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) [2].
3. Tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.3) almost to its end (over 250 bar) [2, 3].
4. Remove the caps from the flow controller (A) and the pressure controller (B) of the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2) and undo the locking nuts of their adjusting spindles [3].
5. Open the adjusting screws of the pressure controller (B) and the flow controller (A) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
6. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (MP1) of the drilling control valve block (20) [3].
7. Start the power pack [3].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) fully closed (clockwise) so the pump operates at constant pressure [1, 3].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows **260 bar** [1].
10. Loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.3) until adjusting begins to effect; the valve begins to fizz when restricting the pressure and the pressure value on the pressure gauge drops to **250 bar** [1].
11. Adjust the values of the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2) back to normal operating specifications [4].
12. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.3) [4].
13. Stop the power pack [4]. 

Care should be taken during this process to ensure that the oil flow does not pass through the main pressure relief valve for a long time, as the hydraulic system will become warmer while the valve restricts pressure [4].

questions.question: To what specific pressure value should the gearbox actuators supply pressure reducing/relieving valve (2.13) be adjusted when checking the reading at measuring connector MTC?
questions.answer:
The gearbox actuators supply pressure reducing/relieving valve (2.13) should be adjusted to **7 bars** when checked at measuring connector MTC [1-3]. 

According to Section 4.5.6 of the Drill carrier C400E, C900E manual (pages 48-49), the adjustment procedure must be performed with the maximum APU circuit gear pump rpm [4]. The complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Activate the tramming mode [4].
2. Turn the starter isolator switch (S2) to the OFF position to prevent the APU circuit gear pump operation [5].
3. Attach a 40-bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector MTC [5].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure reducing/relieving valve (2.13) almost fully open [5].
5. Turn the starter isolator switch (S2) to the ON position to allow the APU circuit gear pump operation [5].
6. Push the pressurizing stud (2.16) and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position [5].
7. Apply the maximum revolutions of the APU circuit gear pump [5].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (2.13) clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge is exactly **7 bars** [3, 5].
9. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (2.13) [3].
10. Return the revolutions of the APU circuit gear pump to idle [3].
11. Push the pressurizing stud (2.16) and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the down position [3].
12. Turn the starter isolator switch (S2) back to the OFF position to prevent the APU circuit gear pump operation [3].
13. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector MTC [3].
14. Turn the starter isolator switch (S2) back to the ON position to allow the normal use of the machine [3].

questions.question: Which specific port must be plugged with a 250-bar pressure gauge, and to what pressure value should the feed extension work port pressure relief valve (21) be tightened when the feed extension is run forward against the front stopper?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.1, "Adjusting the feed extension work port pressure relief valve," you must attach the 250-bar pressure gauge directly to **port B5 (1)** [1, 2]. When running the feed extension forward against the front stopper, the adjusting screw (4) of the pressure relief valve (3) should be tightened until the pressure gauge shows exactly **200 bars** [1, 2]. 

*(Note: If a V30 and/or a larger 22-pipe carousel is used, this maximum pressure limit value may need to be readjusted to a higher setting [3, 4].)*

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this adjustment procedure as outlined in the manual [1, 2]:

1. Remove the hose from **port B5 (1)** and plug the hose.
2. Attach a 250-bar pressure gauge to **port B5 (1)**.
3. Open the locking screws **(2, 2 pcs)** of the pressure relief valve **(3)** and loosen the adjusting screw **(4)**.
4. Start the power pack.
5. Run the feed (unit) extension forward against the front stopper. During the forward movement, tighten the adjusting screw **(4)** until the pressure gauge shows **200 bars**.
6. Stop the feed extension forward movement.
7. Close the locking screws **(2, 2 pcs)**.
8. Remove the pressure gauge from **port B5 (1)**.
9. Unplug the hose and attach the hose back to **port B5 (1)**.

questions.question: When setting the mine's inlet water pressure via the pressure reducing valve to a range between 2 and 7 bars, what is the absolute maximum pressure value that pressure sensor B230P must not exceed?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Adjusting the mine's inlet pressure" section in the Operator's Manual (pages 254-255 and 277), the absolute maximum pressure value that pressure sensor **B230P** must not exceed is **25 bars** [1, 2]. 

The water circuit flushing pressure consists of the mine's inlet pressure combined with the water booster pump pressure [1, 2]. To set the mine's inlet pressure correctly, follow this step-by-step sequence:

1. Connect the machine to the mine's water network (if applicable) [3].
2. Open the shut-off valve **(1 or 2)** [3, 4].
3. Turn the pressure reducing valve knob **(2 or 3)** fully open [3, 4].
4. Start the water booster pump [3, 4].
5. Turn the knob **(2 or 3)** to adjust the pressure to **2-7 bars** according to the current drilling conditions [3, 4]. 
   * *Note: Turning the knob clockwise increases the pressure, while turning it counterclockwise decreases the pressure. Check the pressure gauge **(3 or 4)** to confirm the value* [3, 4].
6. In the control system display, navigate to **Troubleshooting → Compressor and Water Pump** and verify that the value measured by pressure transducer/sensor **(B230P)** is under **25 bars** [3, 5].

*(Note: Component ID numbers for the shut-off valve, knob, and gauge vary slightly between illustrations (1, 2, 3 vs. 2, 3, 4) in different versions of the manual's diagrams)* [3, 4].

questions.question: What are the specified left and right boom swing angles and the maximum boom extension length for the Telescopic boom ZR35?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical specifications for the Telescopic boom ZR35 (TS2-465), the specific measurements are:

*   **Boom swing angles:** Left 45° / Right 45° [1].
*   **Boom extension length:** 620 mm [1]. 

*(Note: Within the boom assembly, the boom swing is actuated by the boom swing cylinders, identified as components 5, 18, and 19, while the extension is actuated by the boom extension/zoom cylinder, identified as components 9 and 15 [2-5].)*

questions.question: What are the exact listed weights for the empty hydraulic oil receiver, the main electric motor (M1), and the complete ZR35 boom assembly?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Weights and Dimensions* section of the *Technical Manual DL422iE*, the exact listed weights for the components are as follows:

*   **Empty Hydraulic Oil Receiver:** The exact weight for the empty hydraulic oil receiver is **256 kg** (Section 2.1.1, Page 13) [1]. Note that the overall assembly containing the hydraulic oil receiver, oil-water cooler, and T2 transformer is listed as weighing 940 kg empty and without hoses (Section 2.1.1, Page 12) [2]. 
*   **Main Electric Motor (M1):** The main electric motor weighs **890 kg** (Section 2.1.2, Page 15) [3].
*   **ZR35 Boom:** The boom weighs **3500 kg** (Section 6.1, Page 51) [4].

questions.question: What are the designated power ratings for the hydraulic system's HPP1560 powerpack and the standard OW45 oil-to-water cooler?
questions.answer: The designated power rating for the hydraulic system's HPP1560 powerpack is 160 kW [1]. The standard OW45 oil-to-water cooler has a designated power rating of 45 kW [1].

questions.question: If the percussion pressure is too low despite normal control signals, which specific electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve and which percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve—normally set to limit maximum pressure to 270 bars—must be inspected in the drilling control valve block (20)?
questions.answer:
Based on the troubleshooting procedures for the drilling hydraulics, the two specific valves in the drilling control valve block **(20)** that must be inspected are:

1.  **Percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25)** – This valve normally limits the maximum pressure of the percussion/feed circuit to **270 bars** [1, 2]. 
2.  **Electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14)** – This valve controls the percussion pressure [3]. 

If the electric and control systems and sensors are operating properly but the percussion pressure remains too low, one of these valves may be stuck [4]. According to **Section 6.8: Percussion pressure is too low** (found in the *Drilling hydraulics DL422iE* manual, pages 65-66), you should follow this exact step-by-step diagnostic sequence:

1. Stop the power pack [4].
2. Check, clean and, if necessary, replace the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve **(20.25)** [4].
3. Adjust the valve as instructed in the section "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve" [5]. *(Note: The manual specifies tightening the adjusting screw of valve **20.25** almost to its end, over 270 bars, temporarily adjusting pump **(1)** pressure controller to 280 bars at measuring point **MP2**, and loosening the relief valve until the pressure drops exactly to 270 bars [6-8]).*
4. If the steps above did not remedy the situation, check, clean and, if necessary, replace the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve **(20.14)** [5].
5. The percussion pressure may also be too low if either of the LS-line orifices **(20.12)** or **(20.13)** is blocked. Follow these instructions to check the orifices:
   * a) Start the power pack [5].
   * b) Turn the percussion on and move the boom. If the boom functions are normal but the percussion pressure remains low, either of the orifices **(20.12)** or **(20.13)** may be at least partly blocked [5].
   * c) Stop the power pack [9].
   * d) Remove the plugs from the ports of the orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** [9].
   * e) Remove the orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** carefully [9].
   * f) Check, clean and, if necessary, replace the orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** [9].
   * g) Install the orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** and the plugs carefully back into the drilling control valve block [9].
6. The percussion pressure drops if the output of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** is insufficient. Install flow meters to the percussion and feed lines to check the pump's output [9]. *(For an HL1560/HF1560 rock drill, normal flow rates at maximum percussion pressure are 125–200 L/min for percussion and 21 L/min for feed [10]).*
7. If the flow rates are higher than those given, check the condition of the rock drill and the feed cylinder immediately [10].
8. Percussion pressure may also drop if any of the shuttle valves **(11)**, **(13)**, or **(20.15)** in the LS-line leak [11].
9. Check and, if necessary, replace the shuttle valves [11].

questions.question: For an HF1560ST rock drill, what is the correct nitrogen pre-charge pressure for the stabilizer accumulator, and which specific electro-proportional pressure relief valve (22.3) acting as a pilot must be adjusted if the stabilizer pressure runs too high during full-power drilling?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided technical manuals, here are the specifications and procedures you requested:

**Nitrogen Pre-charge Pressure**
For the HF1560ST rock drill, the correct nitrogen (N2) pre-charge pressure for the stabilizer accumulator is **40 bars** [1, 2]. 

**Valve Adjustment and Troubleshooting**
During full-power drilling, the pressure level of the stabilizer is set by the **stabilizer pressure reducing/relieving valve (22.2)**, which is piloted by the **electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3)** [3]. 

If the stabilizer pressure runs too high (or too low) during drilling despite the electric and control systems operating properly, it is likely that either valve **(22.3)** or **(22.2)** is leaking or stuck [4]. According to **Section 6.16: Stabilizer pressure is too low or too high** (Drilling Hydraulics DL422iE, pages 75–76), you must follow this step-by-step diagnostic sequence:

1. Stop the power pack [5].
2. Check, clean and, if necessary, replace the electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve **(22.3)** [5].
3. Start the power pack and drilling [5].
4. If the stabilizer pressure is still too high, stop the power pack [5].
5. Check, clean and, if necessary, replace the stabilizer pressure reducing/relieving valve **(22.2)** [5].
6. Start the power pack and drilling [5].
7. If these steps do not remedy the situation, replace the entire stabilizer valve block **(22)** [5].

questions.question: Based on the technical specifications for the HF1560ST hydraulic rock drill, what are the precise operating ranges for the piston's percussion rate in Hertz and the maximum rotation speed in rpm?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical specifications for the HF1560ST (TS2-419) hydraulic rock drill, the precise operating ranges are as follows:

*   **Percussion rate:** 35 – 45 Hz [1]. (This operates with a maximum percussion pressure of up to 200 bar [1]).
*   **Rotation speed:** 0 – 100 rpm [1]. (This is driven by the OMT500 rotation motor, which provides a rotation torque of 2 330 Nm [1]).

questions.question: The HF1560T rock drill requires a shank lubrication amount of 800-1200 g/h; if the oil flow ceases and the control valve (CT1) shut-off ball is left in an abnormal position for how many continuous operational cycles will the system trigger an alarm and stop drilling?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, if the oil flow ceases, the system will trigger an alarm and stop drilling if the control valve **(CT1)** shut-off ball is left open or closed for **four** continuous operational cycles [1]. 

Here is how the system monitors this process (found on page 18 of the *Shank lubrication unit* manual):

*   The shut-off ball of the lubrication pump output port check valve **(CT1)** operates as a control valve against the valve seat [2]. 
*   The oil flow through the check valve removes the ball from the seat surface, breaking the circuit [2]. 
*   The Shank Lubrication Control Unit **(SLCU, 3)** measures this electrical signal from the control valve **(CT1)** [2]. 
*   If the SLCU detects that the shut-off ball remains in an abnormal position (either open or closed) for **four operational cycles**, it sends a message to the control system [1, 2]. 
*   The control system then switches on an alarm, displays an error message to the operator, and stops the drilling after a delay [1, 2]. 

The alarm will be automatically reset once pumping returns to normal operation [1].

questions.question: With a maximum rated feed force of 31 kN, if the feed pressure runs dangerously high, which specific feed counterbalance valve (27.1) and pilot-controlled check valve (27.6) within the feed load control block (27) must be inspected for mechanical sticking?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.11, "Feed / fast feed pressure is too high" (found in the *Drilling hydraulics DL422iE* manual, pages 69-70), if the feed pressure is too high despite normal mechanical, electrical, and control system operation, the **feed counterbalance valve (27.1)** and the **pilot controlled check valve (27.6)** are indeed among the suspects [1]. However, the manual specifies that the **feed counter pressure electro proportional relief valve (27.5)** within the same feed load control block (27) could also be stuck [1]. 

Additionally, the primary culprits that must be inspected first are located in the drilling control valve block (20):
*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)** [1]
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** [1]
*   **Electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)** [1]

The manual outlines the following step-by-step diagnostic and adjustment sequence to address this issue:

1. Stop the power pack [2].
2. Check the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve **(20.18)** and the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve **(20.19)** [2].
3. Clean the valves and replace them if either is damaged [2].
4. If valves **(20.18)** and **(20.19)** are replaced, adjust them using the following steps:
   * a) Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point **(M1)** [2].
   * b) Use the pressure controller **(B)** to adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** to **250 bars** [2].
   * c) Run the feed against the front end stopper and simultaneously adjust the pressure of the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve **(20.18)** to **200 bars** [2].
   * d) Run the feed against the rear end stopper and simultaneously adjust the pressure of the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve **(20.19)** to **240 bars** [3].
   * e) Re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** back to its normal operating specifications [3].
5. If the steps above did not remedy the situation, replace or repair the electro proportional feed pressure relief valve **(20.22)** [3].
6. If the situation persists, check the operation of the feed load control block **(27)** (which houses valves **27.1**, **27.5**, and **27.6**) [1, 3].
7. If the feed / fast feed pressure is still too high, the fault may lie in the feed line pressure compensator **(20.17)** [4]. You must:
   * a) Remove the feed line pressure compensator **(20.17)** from the drilling control valve block [4].
   * b) Clean and check the condition of the compensator [4].
   * c) If the compensator is mechanically damaged, replace the entire drilling control valve block [4].

questions.question: What are the exact maximum limits for boom swing, standard horseshoe fan tilt, and drilling module roll-over for the Telescopic boom ZR35?
questions.answer:
Based on the Technical Specifications for the Telescopic boom ZR35 (TS2-465), the exact maximum limits are as follows:

*   **Boom swing:** Left 45° / Right 45° [1]. This movement is actuated by the left and right boom swing cylinders (18 and 19) [2].
*   **Standard horseshoe fan tilt:** Back 26° / Forward 45° [1]. This movement is actuated by the left and right boom tilt cylinders (16 and 17) [2]. *(Note: If the machine is equipped with the long horseshoe boom support, the fan tilt limits change to Back 40° / Forward 38°)* [1].
*   **Drilling module roll-over:** 360° [1].

questions.question: How do the overcenter (crossover) valves built into the boom hydraulic cylinders protect the mechanical structure if an external force raises the cylinder pressure beyond the valve's stamped set value?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 3.2 "Overcenter valves" (found on page 12 of the *Hydraulic cylinders* manual), if an external force raises the pressure in the cylinder higher than the set value stamped on the face of the overcenter (crossover) valve, the valve opens and lets oil out of the cylinder [1, 2]. 

This action enables the boom to yield under the external force, which successfully prevents mechanical damage to the boom structure [2]. 

*(Note: During removal and installation procedures, the overcenter valves are identified as component **(3)**, and their spare seal rings are identified as component **(1)** [1, 3].)*

questions.question: What is the maximum operating pressure for the LF1600 feed cylinder during both forward and return movements, and through what specific component is hydraulic oil routed to reach both sides of the cylinder's piston?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.4 "Feed cylinder" of the Cylinder feed LF1600 manual (pages 15-16), the specifications for the feed cylinder are as follows:

*   **Maximum operating pressure:** The maximum cylinder operating pressure is **200 bars** when feeding forward and **200 bars** during the return movement [1, 2].
*   **Oil routing component:** Hydraulic oil is routed into the cylinder to reach both sides of the piston specifically through the **piston rod (6)** [1, 2].
