5. In the control system display, select **→ Troubleshooting → Compressor and Water Pump** and verify that the pressure sensor **(B230P)** value remains under **25 bars** [3].

questions.question: During full-power drilling, what is the minimum required pressure difference in bars that must be maintained between the percussion pressure and the stabilizer pressure, and which specific electro-proportional valve controls this stabilizer pressure level?
questions.answer:
During full-power drilling, the percussion pressure must always be maintained at least **20 bars** higher than the stabilizer pressure [1]. 

The specific component that controls this stabilizer pressure level is the **electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3)**, which acts as a pilot control valve for the stabilizer pressure reducing/relieving valve (22.2) [1, 2]. During drilling, the control system uses feed pressure information to control this electro-proportional valve (22.3) to ensure the correct stabilizer pressure is always set [3].

This operation is detailed in Section 4.6 "Stabilizer" under the "Operation during full-power drilling" subsection of the Drilling Hydraulics manual [1, 4].

questions.question: Regarding the drill string components utilized with the module's 31 kN feed force, what is the specific structural difference between standard extension rods and MF rods in terms of their thread configurations?
questions.answer:
According to the "Drill steel" section in the Operators and Maintenance manuals, the specific structural difference between the two rod types used with the drilling module's 31 kN feed force [1] is based on their thread configurations:

*   **Standard Extension Rods:** Both ends of a standard extension rod have identical threads [2, 3].
*   **MF Rods:** MF rods are configured with a male thread on one end and a female thread on the other end [2, 3].

Both standard extension rods and MF rods share the same typical lengths, which are usually between 10 to 18 feet (300 to 540 cm) [2, 3].

questions.question: During the transition from collaring procedures to normal drilling, what specific control system parameter defines the time between the two separate steps of power increase during the ramp stage?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Operator's Manual DL422i StageV" (Section 6.2.4 "Editing drilling parameters", Page 279), the specific control system parameter that defines the time between the two separate steps of power increase during the ramp stage is the **Ramp flat time** [1]. 

This parameter is located under the "Ramp and full power" settings group [1, 2]. To access and adjust this parameter within the control system, follow this step-by-step sequence:

1. Navigate to the drilling settings by selecting: **→ Work Settings → Drilling** [3].
2. Locate and select **Ramp flat time** from the parameter list (the selected row will highlight in blue) [1, 3].
3. Select the current parameter value [3].
4. Enter the new time value into the input field and select **OK** [4].

questions.question: When adjusting the feed unit extension work port pressure relief valve (21), what exact pressure must be reached and locked on the gauge attached to port B5 while running the feed unit extension forward against the front stopper?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the **feed unit extension work port pressure relief valve (21)**, the exact pressure that must be reached on the pressure gauge attached to port B5 is **200 bars** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 5.1 "Adjusting the feed unit extension work port pressure relief valve" (Pages 27-28) of the Boom manual, the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [2-4]:

1. Remove the hose from port **B5 (1)** and plug the hose [2].
2. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to port **B5 (1)** [2].
3. Open the locking screws **(2, 2 pcs)** of the pressure relief valve **(3)** and loosen the adjusting screw **(4)** [2].
4. Start the power pack [2].
5. Run the feed unit extension forward against the front stopper [2]. During the forward movement, tighten the adjusting screw **(4)** until the pressure gauge shows **200 bars** [2].
6. Stop the feed unit extension forward movement [4].
7. Close the locking screws **(2, 2 pcs)** [4].
8. Remove the pressure gauge from port **B5 (1)** [4].
9. Unplug the hose and attach the hose back to port **B5 (1)** [4].

questions.question: Within the feed load control block (27), how does the feed counter pressure sequence valve (27.4) differ from the feed counterbalance valve (27.1) in terms of which side of the feed cylinder it maintains pressure against, and what triggers its relief pressure?
questions.answer:
Within the feed load control block (27), the two valves differ in the following ways based on Section 3.1.1 "Drilling system components" of the Drilling Hydraulics manual:

*   **Side of the feed cylinder maintained:** The feed counterbalance valve (27.1) maintains pressure against the **piston side** of the feed cylinder against external loads [1]. In contrast, the feed counter pressure sequence valve (27.4) maintains pressure against the **piston rod side** of the feed cylinder [2].
*   **Relief pressure trigger:** The feed counterbalance valve (27.1) relieves the piston side pressure simply when its specific valve pressure setting is reached [1]. The feed counter pressure sequence valve (27.4) relieves the piston rod side pressure when its valve pressure setting is reached, but its relief pressure is specifically **related to the piston side pressure** [2].

questions.question: When the operator initiates a right boom swing by energizing pilot valve "a" (3d / Y20A), how is the hydraulic oil flow specifically distributed between port A and port B of the right swing cylinder (18) and the left swing cylinder (19)?
questions.answer:
When the operator energizes **pilot valve a (3d / Y20A)**, it receives a maximum pilot pressure of **45 bar** from the pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (**8**) and shifts the main spool (**1d**) [1]. This action routes oil through the main spool to port **A4**, specifically distributing the hydraulic oil flow to extend the right cylinder and retract the left cylinder as follows [1, 2]:

**Supply Flow (from port A4):**
*   **Right swing cylinder (18):** Oil flows into **port A** and to the **cylinder piston side**, causing the cylinder to **extend** [2].
*   **Left swing cylinder (19):** Oil flows into **port B** and to the **cylinder piston rod side**, causing the cylinder to **retract** [2].

**Return Flow (to port B4):**
*   **Right swing cylinder (18):** Return oil flows from the **piston rod side** out through **port B** [2].
*   **Left swing cylinder (19):** Return oil flows from the **piston side** out through **port A** [2].

These combined movements cause the boom to swing to the right [2]. Both return flows merge and are directed to port **B4** of the boom control valve, passing through the main spool (**1d**) to port **T**, and then onward to the pressurized oil collector and hydraulic oil tank [3]. Throughout this operation, the main pressure relief valve (**9**) limits the circuit's main pressure to **250 bar** [1]. This process is outlined in Section 4.7 "Swinging boom to the right" (Pages 23-24) [1-3].

questions.question: How do the optional left and right articulation locking valves (13, 14) act as an interlock to stiffen the articulation joint and stabilize the carrier during drilling operations?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Drill carrier C400, C900" manual (Section 4.3.1 "Components (steering system)", Pages 31–32, and "Changing the steering angle", Pages 62–67), the optional left and right articulation locking valves (13, 14) act as an interlock to stiffen the articulation joint by blocking hydraulic oil flow between the steering manifold and the cylinders [1-3].

The specific mechanism is split between the two valves:
*   **Left articulation locking valve (13):** Makes the articulation joint stiffer by blocking the connection between the steering valve **port A** and the steering cylinders [1].
*   **Right articulation locking valve (14):** Makes the articulation joint stiffer by blocking the connection between the steering valve **port B** and the steering cylinders [2].

The step-by-step sequence for how these valves are utilized during operation is as follows:

1. **Tramming:** During normal tramming operations, the articulation locking valves (13 and 14) are kept in the neutral position. In this state, they remain open, and hydraulic oil flows freely between the steering and brake control manifold and the steering cylinders [3].
2. **Positioning:** The machine is navigated to the correct location and positioned for drilling [3].
3. **Locking Activation:** Once positioned, the operator presses the parking brake button. The control system responds by holding the main steering control valve in the middle position (even if the steering stick is turned) and steers the optional articulation locking valves to their locked position [4].
4. **Drilling Stabilization:** The activated valves block the connections at ports A and B, effectively locking the hydraulic oil within the steering cylinders. This makes the carrier's articulation joint rigid and stiffer [1, 2, 5]. The valves are kept actively locked throughout the duration of the drilling operation to maintain carrier stability [1, 2].

questions.question: According to the rig's technical specifications for boom coverage and reach, what is the maximum boom extension dimension, and what is the pivot point height range when the boom is positioned vertically?
questions.answer:
According to the "LONGHOLE BOOM" section in the rig's technical specifications, the dimensions for the telescopic boom (ZR35 / TS2-465) are as follows:

*   **Boom extension:** 620 mm [1, 2].
*   **Pivot point height (boom vertical):** 2 310 - 2 930 mm [2].

questions.question: How do you diagnose a fault with the multivoltage power factor correction capacitor?
questions.answer: Start one power pack at a time and let it idle, then check the power factor value displayed on the electric quality measuring unit (P1) [10]. If the power factor value reads under 0.5 and the individual phase currents differ significantly, the capacitor is likely faulty and must be entirely replaced [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the gear pump (3) and the vacuum pump (4.9) within the main hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The gear pump (3) delivers oil specifically to the air conditioning and the optional OA-cooler [1]. The vacuum pump (4.9) is used to form a vacuum inside the hydraulic oil receiver to minimize oil leakage during maintenance procedures [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where the percussion pressure is either too high or too low?
questions.answer: If the pressure is too high, check if the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) is stuck, or if the LS-line orifices (20.12 or 20.13) are loosened or disconnected from the drilling control valve block [5], [6]. If the pressure is too low, the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) or the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) may be stuck, or the LS-line orifices (20.12 or 20.13) may be blocked, and they should be checked, cleaned, or replaced [6], [7], [8], [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the Valve Controller High Temp (VCH) module used for the boom (BC1) and drilling controllers (DC1)?
questions.answer: The VCH module is a powerful I/O-module that serves as a CANopen slave, offering services for reading and writing inputs and outputs [16]. It features separate output powering/cutoff circuitry designed to allow de-activating outputs safely with SIL2/PLd systems [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are specific input/output signal faults diagnosed on control modules like the FPVC or VCH?
questions.answer: These modules feature a 7-segment display that shows a continuous diagnostic sequence consisting of the node ID, network management state, and specific pin errors [8, 9]. An I/O fault is indicated by the connector (e.g., J7), the pin number, and a letter status indicating the specific error type: "s" for a short circuit to ground, "o" for an open circuit, or "b" for a short circuit to the battery [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which modules function as the Drilling Master (DM1) and Carrier Master (CM) on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: The XCU machine control computer serves as the Drilling Master (DM1) [5]. It manages boom control, joint position control, forward and inverse boom kinematics, trajectory generation, automatic positioning, and drilling control algorithms [6]. The SCU machine control computer serves as the Carrier Master (CM) [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the pressure and flow controllers on the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)?
questions.answer: To adjust the **flow controller (A)**, carefully turn the adjusting screw clockwise until the pressure difference (pump operating pressure minus LS-line pressure) is **30 bars** [10], [11]. To adjust the **pressure controller (B)**, run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and tighten the screw until the pressure is **235 bars** (for the RD921S) or **250 bars** (for the RD927L or HL1560/HF1560) [12], [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: **How do you diagnose a short-circuit specifically between a CAN wire and ground?
questions.answer: This fault is diagnosed when the measured resistance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI remains at approximately **60 Ω**, but the **CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level is continuously near 0 V** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the diagnostic procedure if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling?
questions.answer: First, check, clean, and if necessary, replace the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) [14], [15]. If this does not resolve the issue, check the shuttle valve (20.7) [15]. Another possibility is that the electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) is leaking LS-pressure to the tank line and needs to be checked or replaced [15], [16]. Finally, if the pressure remains low, the rock drill rotation motor may be leaking and require repair or replacement [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure if the rotation pressure is too high during drilling?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation pressure is too high, which can cause excessive wear to the rock drill and rotation mechanism components, fine cuttings, or indicate bending of the drill rod [6, 11, 16].
*   **Cause:** Drilling control settings may be incorrect, the rotation speed may be set too low, the rotation line pressure compensator (20.2) might be faulty, or the rock drill rotation motor/mechanism could be damaged [10, 16, 17].
*   **Corrective Action:** First, adjust the rotation speed of the drilling rod to the proper level [17]. If unresolved, remove, clean, and check the condition of the rotation line pressure compensator (20.2), replacing the whole drilling control valve block if the compensator is damaged [17]. If the issue persists, stop the power pack and repair or replace the damaged component(s) in the rock drill [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: **How is a short-circuit between the two CAN wires (CAN_LO to CAN_HI) diagnosed?
questions.answer: A short-circuit between the CAN wires is indicated when the **CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level is continuously near 0 V** [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the primary method for diagnosing electrical system faults on the drill rig?
questions.answer: The primary troubleshooting method is using the self-diagnostics from the GUI by selecting "Troubleshooting," which displays a diagram showing real-time electrical signaling between control devices and system components [1]. Additionally, the operator can use the Log view, which displays current and historical data about alerts, including problem duration, frequency, and measurement values [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do the thermostat valve (9) and OW-cooler (5) work together to manage the hydraulic oil temperature?
questions.answer: If the oil temperature is below the thermostat valve (9) setting limit, the return oil is guided straight to the receiver [3]. Once the temperature limit is reached, the valve changes position to direct the oil through the OW-cooler (5), which removes heat from the drilling, boom, and carrier hydraulics return flows [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the part numbers for the battery charger (A1)?
questions.answer: The battery charger (A1) utilizes part numbers **CP10.241** or **CP10.242** (which feature screw terminals), or **CP10.241-S1** (which features spring-clamp terminals) [18]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you read an input/output (I/O) fault code directly from the 7-segment display on an FPVC or VCH module?
questions.answer: After the initial boot identification sequence, the module's display repeatedly shows the node ID, the network management state (Pr, oP, or st), any communication errors (Co), and specific I/O fault statuses [3, 4]. An I/O fault is displayed with the connector identifier (e.g., J7), the pin number in hex, and a status letter where "s" means short circuit to ground, "o" means open circuit, and "b" means short circuit to battery [3-5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you find a de-energized node or an interruption in the supply conductor (**VS**) on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: With the control system ON, measure the supply conductor voltage between the **VS** and **GND** terminals [7]. Normally, this voltage is approximately **24 VDC** [7]. While a lit power LED usually indicates correct supply voltage for most nodes, if a node has no LED lit, performing this measurement can confirm the issue [7]. A voltage drop continuously near **0 V** indicates a potential interruption point in the supply conductor [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used for the Tramming GUI (VG)?
questions.answer: The Tramming GUI uses an EPEC 6107 PanelPC equipped with a 7" LCD resistive color touch display and two CAN 2.0 B communication interfaces [3]. It provides the operator with real-time tramming data and alerts [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system warn the operator of a tramming overspeed condition?
questions.answer: If the tramming speed exceeds the factory set maximum value (12.5 km/h), the operator is notified with an **audible alert**, and the speed value color on the tramming display will **turn red** [23]. The operator must immediately reduce the tramming speed using the brake or accelerator pedal to prevent damage to the hydrostatic transmission (HST) motor [23]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the feed or fast feed pressure is too low?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Feed or fast feed pressure is too low, which can cause the rock drill to jump and shake, decreasing penetration speed and accelerating wear on the chuck and extension sleeve [1, 2].
*   **Cause:** The electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22), feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18), or feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) may be leaking [1]. Alternatively, the feed cylinder or feed load control block may have an internal leakage [3].
*   **Corrective Action:** Disconnect the electrical connector from valve (20.22) and run the feed against the rear stopper to check the pressure at the LS measuring connector [1]. Check, clean, or replace the feed pressure relief valve and shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18, 20.19) [1, 4]. If the valves are functioning, plug the feed load control block ports (C1 and C2) and test the feed to determine if the feed cylinder or load control block needs repair or replacement [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the operating pressure settings for the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump?
questions.answer: The pump's flow controller (stand-by pressure difference) is set to **22–30 bars** [2]. The pressure controller (maximum operating pressure) is set to **235 bars** for rigs equipped with the RD921S rock drill, and **250 bars** for rigs equipped with the RD927L or HL1560/HF1560 rock drills [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the maximum circuit pressure limits established by the system's relief valves for feed, rotation, and boom functions?
questions.answer:
**Feed Circuit:** The main pressure relief valve limits the maximum feed circuit pressure to **270 bars** [12]. Furthermore, the feed port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves are limited to **200 bars** and **240 bars**, respectively [12].
*   **Rotation Circuit:** The electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve limits the maximum rotation load-sensing pressure to **250 bars** [13].
*   **Boom Circuit:** The boom main pressure relief valve limits the boom circuit pressure to **250 bars**, while its pilot circuit operates between **30–45 bars** [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps are required if the percussion is not working at all?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion does not activate despite electric and control systems operating properly. The percussion pressure gauge on the main view shows no reading [21].
*   **Cause:** Either the percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck [21]. Alternatively, the rock drill itself may be damaged [21].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack [21]. Clean, check, and if necessary, replace the percussion selector valve (20.9) and the 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) [21]. If the gauge does show pressure but percussion still doesn't work, stop the power pack and repair or replace the rock drill [21]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the variable displacement pumps if they do not rotate at all or their speed is not normal?
questions.answer: First, check the troubleshooting views from the control system GUI to determine if the fault is in the hydraulic, electric, or control system [1]. Measure the supply voltage to the power pack; if the voltage is correct, the fault is likely mechanical [2]. Check if mechanical damage prevents the pumps from rotating, and repair or replace the damaged component [2]. A noisy power pack often predicts a mechanical fault, which requires immediate attention to avoid greater damage [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the pressure settings for the cable reel and water hose reel control valves?
questions.answer: The **cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (1)** is adjusted during the "reeling out" function based on the cable's cross-sectional area (e.g., **50 bars** for 25 mm² cables, **100 bars** for 50 mm² cables, and up to **180 bars** for 185-240 mm² cables) [22], [23]. The **water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (3)** is adjusted to **80 bars** (83 bars in the DU422i-W) while raising the jack carefully against the stopper [24], [25]. The **water hose reel brake valve (24)** is set to **20-30 bars** (35 bars in DU422i-W) while reeling out the hose [26], [27]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the earth fault lockout protection relay (K293) do?
questions.answer: The earth fault lockout protection relay (K293), an **EFL** unit, provides earth fault lockout (EFLO) and frozen contactor (FC) protection for the system [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the CAN-RUN and CAN-ERR LED indicator fault codes mean on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU)?
questions.answer: If the green CAN-RUN indicator flashes, the CAN bus connection is broken or awaiting a command (standby); a single flash means the SLCU stopped due to an internal fault [6]. For the red CAN-ERR indicator, a single flash means the CAN control error counter has reached its alarm limit (too many errors), while a solid red light means the CAN control bus is off [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is it diagnosed when the variable displacement pumps do not rotate at all, or their speed is not normal?
questions.answer: First, check the troubleshooting views from the control system to determine if the fault is in the hydraulic, electric, or control system [1], [2]. Measure the supply voltage to the power pack; if the voltage is correct, the fault is likely mechanical [3]. A noisy power pack often predicts a mechanical fault, which requires immediate repair or replacement of the component to avoid greater damage [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2) and its main pressure relief valve (20.3) adjusted?
questions.answer: The pump's **flow controller (A)** is adjusted to a pressure difference of **20-23 bars** [17]. The **pressure controller (B)** is adjusted by running the rock drill rotation against the plug to set it to **150 bars** (for the DL432i) or **180 bars** (for the DL422iE) [17]. The **main pressure relief valve (20.3)** is set by tightening its screw over **250 bars**, setting the pump's pressure controller to **260 bars**, and then loosening the relief valve until it fizzes and drops the pressure to exactly **250 bars** [18], [19], [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: **What types of CAN bus faults cannot be diagnosed using a standard multimeter?
questions.answer: While a multimeter is excellent for finding interruptions and short-circuits, it cannot be used to detect a **faulty CAN sensor** (sensor signal fault), **missing CAN signals**, or **bit-level signal faults** [4, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you locate a specific fault location or faulty termination resistor on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: First, disconnect both termination resistors from the bus and measure each separately; they should read exactly **120 Ω** [5]. If they are intact, the fault is likely in the bus cable [5]. To pinpoint the fault location, move a termination resistor towards the next measuring point (which can be any actuator or node on the bus), disconnect the bus cable from the actuator, and connect the termination resistor in its place to isolate sections of the bus [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the power pack stops or will not start due to an electrical issue?
questions.answer: Check for possible alarm messages on the screen, ensure the starter isolator switch (S2) is ON, verify the main switch (Q1) is in position 1, and ensure all emergency stop buttons are released [12]. Additionally, check that no circuit breakers in the MQ cabinet have tripped and make sure the pilot circuit is functional [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are faults in the emergency stop circuit diagnosed?
questions.answer: You can diagnose these faults by checking the LED indicators (Ub, K1, and K2) on the emergency stop relay [6]. If the Ub and K1 LEDs are ON but K2 is OFF, it points to an error in the emergency stop at terminals T14, T21, or T22, or suggests that the K1 contactor may be welded or defective [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the adjustment procedure for the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25)?
questions.answer: First, tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve over **270 bars** [14], [15]. Turn the pump's flow controller (A) fully closed, run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper, and turn the pressure controller (B) until the gauge shows **280 bars** [15], [16]. Then, loosen the main pressure relief valve (20.25) until it begins to fizz and restricts the pressure to exactly **270 bars** [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the rotation speed adjustment is not working properly?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation speed adjustment is not working, or the rotation of the drilling rod is uneven and not constant [10, 11]. 
*   **Cause:** The fault is likely in the rock drill itself, the rotation pilot control valves (20.4 or 20.5), the rotation valve main spool (20.1), or the rotation line pressure compensator (20.2) [10].
*   **Corrective Action:** Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control block to ensure pilot pressure is 30-45 bars [12]. If pressure is normal, stop the power pack, then remove, check, and replace the rotation pilot control valves (20.4, 20.5) [13]. If that fails, extract and check the condition of the main spool (20.1) and compensator (20.2), replacing the drilling control valve block if they are mechanically damaged [13-15]. Finally, check the rock drill rotation motor [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the power pack if it will not start?
questions.answer: First, check the display for any possible alarm messages [1]. Ensure that the starter isolator switch (S2) is in the ON position, the mains electric supply is connected, and the main switch (Q1) is turned to position 1 (ON) [1]. Finally, verify that all emergency stop buttons have been released [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the compressor's PS2 and PS3 capacity control valves adjusted?
questions.answer: The **PS3 unloading pressure limit valve** is adjusted using a 3 mm hexagonal key so that it opens at **8 bar(g)**, ensuring internal pressure will not rise above 10 bar(g) [28]. The **PS2 capacity control valve** is adjusted while the compressor is running on-load (with an internal pressure around 5 bar) so that the inlet valve starts to open at **7.5 bar(g)** [29], [30]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: **How can CAN bus health be diagnosed by measuring voltage levels?
questions.answer: With the control system live (ON), measure the voltage between **CAN_HI and GND**, and **CAN_LO and GND** [4, 5]. An intact bus will measure **2.5 V ±0.2 V** with no load [5]. If the measurements are **< 1 V or > 4 V**, there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the difference between an Alarm and a Notice on the control system display, and how should the operator respond to each?
questions.answer: An **Alarm (red pop-up)** is triggered when the control system detects a major problem [1, 2]. The operator must stop working immediately, check the Log or on-screen details, and correct the error situation to prevent damage before continuing to use the rig [1-4]. A **Notice (yellow pop-up)** indicates a medium problem [1, 2]. It does not require immediate action, but the operator should investigate and correct the underlying cause if the notice persists or is frequently repeated [1-4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What part numbers are associated with the Control Panels (LCP, RCP, MCP) and what is their function?
questions.answer: The control panels are identified by part numbers **BG00545381** and **BG00545382** [16]. They connect to the system via CANopen (PE535C) and are used to set and control the drilling functions of the rig by transmitting inputs from their joysticks, buttons, and rotary switches to the HMI unit [16, 17]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose CAN bus cabling faults such as short-circuits or interruptions?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected, measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO [4]. A normal, healthy bus will read ~60 Ω ±5 Ω [5]. A reading of < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit, > 100 Ω indicates an interruption at one end or a faulty termination resistor, and a reading of ~40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted in at least two places [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the steps for setting the feed unit extension work port pressure relief valve (21)?
questions.answer: Remove and plug the hose from port B5, and attach a 250 bar pressure gauge in its place [21]. Open the locking screws, start the power pack, and run the feed unit extension forward against the front stopper [21]. During this forward movement, tighten the adjusting screw until the pressure gauge shows exactly **200 bars** [21]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a tripped circuit breaker or blown fuse indicate and how is it handled?
questions.answer: Breaker tripping or a blown fuse is a sign of an electrical failure, such as an overload or short circuit, which protects wires and components from overheating and fire [3]. The specific failure must be investigated and repaired by a qualified electrician before resetting the breaker or replacing the fuse with one of the exact same size and type [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions and part numbers associated with the power pack circuit breaker (F1) and power pack motor contactors (K1, K2, K3)?
questions.answer: The power pack circuit breaker (F1), part number **NZMN2ME140NA** (for a 55 kW motor), features an electronic release for motor protection with phase failure sensitivity and adjustable overload releases [4]. The power pack motor contactors (K1, K2, K3), part number **DILM170(RDC24)**, are used to safely switch the power pack motors on and off [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What module acts as the Bit Changer Controller (BSC) and what does it do?
questions.answer: The BSC uses the RD (Resolver-to-Digital) module, which is a general-purpose CANopen slave measurement unit designed for high-accuracy applications [13]. It features four resolver-to-digital converters to accurately measure angles [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling and the rotation pump is adjusted correctly?
questions.answer: Check, clean, and if necessary, replace the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) [13, 14]. If that does not resolve the issue, inspect and clean the shuttle valve (20.7) [14]. Also, check if the electro proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) is leaking LS-pressure to the tank line and replace it if needed [14, 15]. Finally, if the pressure is still low, the rock drill rotation motor may be leaking and require repair or replacement [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the proper voltage levels for a healthy CAN bus, and how do you diagnose CAN wire short circuits?
questions.answer: With the control system turned ON, an intact CAN bus will measure 2.5 V ±0.2 V between CAN_HI and GND, and CAN_LO and GND under no load [12, 13]. If measurements are < 1 V or > 4 V, there is a short-circuit [12]. Specifically, if the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level is continuously near 0 V, there is a short-circuit between the CAN wire and ground (or between the two CAN wires) [14, 15]. If the voltage is continuously near the supply voltage (VS), there is a short-circuit to the supply voltage [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose and correct a feed pressure that is too high?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Feed pressure is too high, which can cause rotation jamming, bending of the drill rod, faster wear of the centralizers and chuck, and an increased risk of the piston striking the shank at an angle [2, 5, 6].
*   **Cause:** A valve is stuck—likely the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22), feed port shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 or 20.19), feed counterbalance valve (27.1), pilot-controlled check valve (27.6), feed counter pressure electro-proportional relief valve (27.5), or the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) [5, 7].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack [8]. Clean, check, and replace the shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19), then adjust them to 200 bars and 240 bars respectively [8, 9]. If this fails, repair or replace valve (20.22), check the operation of the feed load control block (27), and inspect the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) [7, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the battery and mains isolation button (S9)?
questions.answer: Located on the tramming panel, the battery and mains isolation switch (S9) turns off the current from the carrier's battery to the drill rig's electric circuit [2, 3]. It also trips the main switch (Q1), which cuts off the main electric supply to the rig [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are responsible for filtering and regulating the pilot oil in the drilling control block?
questions.answer: The pilot oil filter (20.26) filters the oil supplied to the pilot control circuit at a level of 160-200 µm [6]. The pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27) then reduces and limits this pilot oil pressure level to between 35 and 45 bars [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components are used for the compressor and water pump motor contactors (K4, K5, K9), and what are their part numbers?
questions.answer: The **DILM32-10(RDC4)** contactor is used for 5.5 - 11 kW motors, while the **DILM65-10(RDC4)** contactor is used for larger 18.5 kW motors, such as those on the CTN28 compressors [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the percussion is not working?
questions.answer: If the electric and control systems are operating properly, check the rock drill, as it may be faulty and need repair or replacement [4]. If the percussion is on but the percussion pressure gauge shows no reading, either the percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) may be stuck and needs to be cleaned, checked, or replaced [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the percussion pressure is too low despite the electric and control systems operating properly?
questions.answer: First, stop the power pack and check, clean, and adjust or replace the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) [8, 9]. If unsuccessful, check and clean the electro proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) [9]. Next, check if the LS-line orifices (20.12 or 20.13) are blocked by removing their plugs, cleaning them, and reinstalling them carefully into the drilling control valve block [10, 11]. Finally, install flow meters to check the output of the variable displacement pump (1); for example, the RD927L rock drill requires an output of 135-150 L/min at maximum percussion pressure [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you determine if there is an insulation fault or a relay/sensor link fault using the residual current protection relay (K9B)?
questions.answer: Check the LED indicators on the K9B relay [4, 5]. If both the green LED (voltage presence) and the red LED (insulation fault) are illuminated solidly, a fault current has been detected and the associated contactor (K9) will open [4, 5]. If the green LED is ON but the red LED is flashing, it indicates a relay/sensor link fault [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the alarm indications for the fire suppression system, and how can the operator respond during the shutdown delay?
questions.answer: If the system pressure drops below 900 kPa (due to activation or a leak), the electronic alarm/timer box triggers an audiovisual alarm, turning on the **yellow or red warning lights** and sounding a **loud siren** [5, 7, 15-18]. An automatic 6-second engine shutdown timer immediately begins [16, 18]. The operator can press the engine shutdown test/delay timer button to extend the delay by an additional **20 seconds**, which allows the operator to safely park the machine before the engine automatically shuts down [16, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the earth continuity protection relay (K9A) and the residual current protection relay (K9B)?
questions.answer: The earth continuity protection relay (K9A), part number **MEC-1**, is a remote start/stop relay that monitors the pilot-to-earth short-circuit resistance [8]. The residual current protection relay (K9B), part number **SE-105**, is a combination ground-fault and ground-check monitor for resistance-grounded systems [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used for the Drilling GUI (DG) and what is its function?
questions.answer: The Drilling GUI uses the CCpilot XM2, a PC-based onboard display computer with a 12" or 15" TFT touch screen [1]. It connects to the system via 4 CAN interfaces and provides the operator with real-time system information, drill and bolting plans, alerts, and productivity statistics [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: **How do you diagnose a short-circuit between a CAN wire and the supply voltage?
questions.answer: This fault is diagnosed when the measured resistance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI reads approximately **60 Ω**, but the **CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level is continuously near the supply voltage (VS)** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings are generated by the door latch and seat belt monitoring system?
questions.answer: If the seat belt is not fastened or if the cabin door is not properly closed before starting the engine or during tramming, a **buzzer on the tramming panel** will sound and a **notice pop-up** will be displayed on the screen [5-8]. The operator must ensure the door is securely closed and fasten their seat belt to clear the warning [5-8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: **How can you find a de-energized node or an interruption in the supply conductor (VS)?
questions.answer: Measure the supply conductor voltage between the **VS** and **GND** terminals with the control system ON, which should normally be about **24 VDC** [8]. A potential interruption point in the supply conductor is detected when the voltage drops to **0 V** [6, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose system errors using the Status LED on the Gatekeeper Controller (GSC)?
questions.answer: The GSC module is equipped with a built-in status LED to indicate operating states and faults [16]. If the LED is orange, there is an error in the start-up phase [16]. A green LED flashing at 5 Hz means no operating system is loaded [16]. A red LED flashing at 2 Hz indicates the system is running with an error, and a solid red LED indicates a fatal error or that the system has stopped with an error [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the steering and brake circuit main pressure relief valves adjusted?
questions.answer: The **steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9)** is adjusted to **220 bars** with the diesel engine at maximum rpm while pushing the pressurizing stud (10.23) [1], [2]. The **brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)** is set by turning its screw fully clockwise (ensuring the pressure does not exceed **205 bars** during the process), and then turning it counterclockwise until the pressure drops to exactly **200 bars** [3], [4], [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: **How should a CAN bus fault first be identified and what are the typical physical causes?
questions.answer: A fault should first be identified using the notifications on the operator's display panel, which indicate whether bus nodes are in a fault mode or switched off [1]. Typical physical causes for cabling faults include cable, wire, or connector interruptions, short-circuits, installation errors, and internal termination resistors that are loose or incorrectly connected [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are used for the Control Panel Keypads (CP)?
questions.answer: The control panel keypads are Grayhill 3K keypads used for controlling certain rig functions [21]. They are highly resistant to vibration and impacts, and they connect to the system using a 4-pin Deutsch DT connector [21]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do Cummins J1939 engine fault codes 291 and 5939 indicate regarding the CAN datalink?
questions.answer: Engine fault code 291 (J1939 SPN 625, FMI 9) indicates a Proprietary Datalink Error (OEM/Vehicle Datalink) with an abnormal update rate [8]. Fault code 5939 (J1939 SPN 520968, FMI 9) indicates that no communication or an invalid data transfer rate has been detected on the J1939 data link between the Engine Control Module (ECM) and the machine electronic control unit [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose and differentiate between a short-circuit to ground and a short-circuit to the supply voltage on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: Both faults will show a measured resistance between **CAN_LO** and **CAN_HI** of approximately **60 Ω** [8]. To differentiate them, measure the voltage: if there is a short-circuit between a CAN wire and ground, the **CAN_LO** or **CAN_HI** voltage level will be continuously near **0 V** [8]. If there is a short-circuit between a CAN wire and the supply voltage, the **CAN_LO** or **CAN_HI** voltage level will be continuously near the supply voltage (**VS**) [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you access the primary diagnostic tool for the electrical system, and what does the interface indicate?
questions.answer: The primary troubleshooting method is using the machine's self-diagnostics from the GUI by selecting "Troubleshooting" to view real-time electrical signaling between control devices and system components [1, 2]. In this view, a colored signaling arrow indicates that a signal is active, while a gray arrow shows an inactive connection [2]. If a red "X" appears over a module, it means the module is offline, not working, or connected to an option not included on the rig [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings and system actions occur if the Access Protector system detects an object in the hazard zone?
questions.answer: If an object or person is detected in the hazard zone, the **red detection warning light** starts to flash and a detection icon appears on the display [19, 20]. In "detector mode," this only serves as a warning [21]. In "protector mode," drilling, boom, and drill steel handling movements are **automatically prevented**, and a pop-up appears on the screen [20, 22]. The operator must ensure no one is in the hazard zone, then push the **acknowledgment button** to reactivate the system [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the role of the electric quality measuring unit (P1)?
questions.answer: The electric quality measuring unit (P1) is a multifunction energy meter with a graphic LCD display that visualizes and sets true RMS measurements, such as voltage, current, active energy, and phase sequence [11-15]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose an issue where the flow controller value for the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2) deviates from the set value?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring connector (LS) of pump (2) and start the power pack [16]. If the pressure is at normal tank pressure (approx. 3-5 bar or less), the flow controller (A) is likely incorrectly adjusted or stuck; adjust it to 20-23 bars or clean/replace the controller unit [17, 18]. If the LS pressure is above normal tank pressure, the rotation valve main spool (20.1) may be stuck and leaking; stop the power pack, clean the main spool (20.1), and if cleaning fails, replace the entire drilling control valve block (20) [19]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the setpoints and procedures for the steering circuit pilot and retarder pressures?
questions.answer: The **steering circuit pilot pressure reducing valve (10.11)** is set to **35 bars** at maximum diesel engine rpm while pushing the pressurizing stud to the up position [6], [7]. The **steering circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.14)** is adjusted to **200 bars** while running the boom zoom function backwards at maximum engine rpm [8], [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component manages the exhaust system on the carrier?
questions.answer: The Engine Control Module (ECM) manages the SCR aftertreatment system and initiates automatic exhaust system cleaning when needed [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the DEF/AdBlue indicator lights signify, and how should the operator respond?
questions.answer: If the DEF system indicator light is **continuously ON**, it means the DEF/AdBlue level is getting low [24]. If the light is **BLINKING**, the level is critically low [24]. In both cases, the operator must safely stop the machine and **refill the DEF/AdBlue tank** to ensure proper engine emission control [24]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specifications for the optional bypass filter and the stabilizer filter?
questions.answer:
**Bypass Filter:** This optional unit provides ultra-fine filtration at **2 µm absolute** [9]. A flow control valve strictly limits the oil flow through this filter to **2.0 L/min** [9, 10]. It gives a clogging warning at a 2-bar difference and bypasses at 3.5 bars [9, 10]. 
*   **Stabilizer Filter:** The oil coming from the rock drill stabilizer passes through a dedicated line filter with a filtering level of **10 µm absolute** [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose an earth fault lockout (EFLO) or frozen contactor (FC) trip on the dewatering pump circuit?
questions.answer: These faults are monitored by the earth fault lockout protection relay (K293) [2]. If an EFLO or FC trip occurs, the blue LED on the S293 reset button (located on the MQ main switchgear door) will illuminate [3]. Because an EFLO trip is latched in the K293 relay's memory, you must clear the fault and manually reset it using the S293 pushbutton [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the VCH module, and which controllers use it?
questions.answer: The VCH (Valve Controller High Temp) module is a CANopen slave I/O module featuring separate output powering and cutoff circuitry to safely deactivate outputs in SIL2/PLd systems [10]. It is used for the Boom Controller (BC1), Drilling Controller (DC1), Front Controller (FC), Vehicle Controller (VC), End Controller (EC), and Switch Controller (SC) [10-12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the CAN bus to determine if there is a short-circuit or interruption using resistance measurements?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected and the battery main switch (**S1**) in position 0, measure the total resistance between **CAN_HI** and **CAN_LO** [1]. An intact bus with both **120 Ω** termination resistors will read **~60 Ω ±5 Ω** [1, 2]. A reading of **< 50 Ω** indicates a short-circuit, a reading of **> 100 Ω** indicates one end of the CAN bus is interrupted or a termination resistor is faulty, and a reading of **~40...50 kΩ** indicates the bus is interrupted in at least two points or both termination resistors are missing/faulty [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration size specifications and purity requirements for the main hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The overall standard filtration sizes are **20 µm for the pressure circuit and 10 µm for the return circuit** [4]. The manufacturer's recommendation for the hydraulic oil purity class is **18/16/13** according to the ISO 4406 standard [5]. Additionally, the hydraulic tank breather filter has a filtering level of **5 µm** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system warn the operator about the cable reel reaching its limit during tramming, and what must the operator do?
questions.answer: When the first limit is reached (indicating there are only about four rounds of cable left on the reel), an **alarm sound** is given and a **pop-up** is shown on the display [13, 14]. The parking brake will engage after a four-second delay [13, 14]. If the operator needs to continue tramming temporarily, they must push and hold the **bypass button**; otherwise, they must stop and reverse direction to prevent pulling the cable out completely [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the CAN bus for short circuits and interruptions using a multimeter, and what are the expected resistance values?
questions.answer: With the power completely disconnected, measure the total resistance between the CAN_HI and CAN_LO terminals [10, 11]. An intact bus with its two 120 Ω termination resistors will read approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω [11]. A reading of < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit, > 100 Ω indicates an interruption at one end or a faulty termination resistor, and a reading of ~40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted in at least two places [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the optional bypass filter (10) operate, and what roles do its flow control valve (10.1) and bypass valve (10.2) play?
questions.answer: The bypass filter (10) provides ultra-fine filtration at a level of 2 µm [9]. The flow control valve (10.1) strictly restricts the oil flow through this filter to 2.0 L/min, and the bypass valve (10.2) opens to bypass the filter element if the pressure difference across the filter exceeds 3.5 bars [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component acts as the Gatekeeper Controller (GSC) on the front carrier bus?
questions.answer: The GSC uses an IFM safety-PLC equipped with a 16-bit C167CS processor and two CAN interfaces [20]. If replaced, it requires a pre-programmed spare part [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you use a multimeter to diagnose short-circuits or interruptions on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected and the battery main switch (S1) in position 0, measure the total resistance between the CAN_HI and CAN_LO terminals [8, 9]. An intact bus with two 120 Ω termination resistors will measure approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω [9]. A reading of < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit, a reading of > 100 Ω indicates an interruption at one end or a faulty termination resistor, and a reading of ~40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted in at least two places [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for diagnosing and fixing a feed or fast feed pressure that is too low?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring connector (LS) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) [4]. Disconnect the electric connector from the electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) and run the feed against the rear end stopper; the pressure should be approx. 210 bars [4, 5]. If it differs, check, clean, or replace valve (20.22) [5]. If that doesn't work, check the feed port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19) [6]. If replacing them, adjust port A to 200 bars and port B to 240 bars while the pump's pressure controller (B) is set to 250 bars [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for checking CAN bus health by measuring voltage levels, and what are the expected values?
questions.answer: Turn the battery main switch (**S1**) to position 1 so the control system is ON, then measure the voltage between **CAN_HI** and **GND**, and **CAN_LO** and **GND** [3]. An intact CAN bus will measure **2.5 V ±0.2 V** with no load [3, 4]. When loaded, **CAN_HI** should be above 2.5 VDC and **CAN_LO** should be below 2.5 VDC [4]. If measurements are **< 1 V or > 4 V**, there is a short-circuit on the bus [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are earth leakage or insulation faults diagnosed using the residual current protection relay (K9B)?
questions.answer: Check the LED statuses on the K9B relay to diagnose these faults [11]. If both the green LED (voltage presence) and the red LED (insulation fault) are ON solidly, a fault current has been detected [11]. If the green LED is ON and the red LED is flashing, it indicates a relay/sensor link fault [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you resolve an issue where the percussion pressure is too high?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion pressure is too high, leading to a shortened life of the rock drill, damaged drilling tools, and an increased risk of drill rod jamming [18, 19].
*   **Cause:** The electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) is stuck, or the LS-line orifices (20.12 or 20.13) have loosened or disconnected from the drilling control valve block [18, 20].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack [20]. Check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the proportional pressure relief valve (20.14) [20]. If this does not fix the issue, verify that both orifices (20.12 and 20.13) are properly in place in the valve block and carefully tighten them if they have loosened [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components control the main pressure limits for the rotation and percussion/feed circuits?
questions.answer: The rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) limits the maximum rotation pressure to 250 bars [4, 5]. The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) limits the maximum pressure of the percussion and feed circuits to its adjusted value (typically 270 bars) [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: **How do you diagnose a short-circuit or an interruption on the CAN bus by measuring resistance?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected, measure the total resistance between **CAN_HI** and **CAN_LO** [2, 3]. An intact bus with both 120 Ω termination resistors reads **~60 Ω ±5 Ω** [3, 4]. A reading of **< 50 Ω** indicates a short-circuit [3]. A reading of **> 100 Ω** indicates an interruption at one end of the bus or a faulty termination resistor [3]. A reading of **~40...50 kΩ** indicates the bus is interrupted in at least two places, or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used for the Rod Changer Controller (RC1) and Extended Rod Changer Controller (ERC1)?
questions.answer: These controllers use the FPVC (Fast Proportional Valve Controller) module [8]. The FPVC is a powerful CANopen slave I/O module with internal FPGA support designed to meet SIL2 class safety requirements, and it manages proportional valve outputs and other multifunction I/O [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Within the cable reel control block, what are the functions of the pressure reducing/relieving valve (1) and flow control valves (2.1 and 2.2)?
questions.answer: The cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (1) determines the force applied for cable reeling [7]. The flow control valve (2.1) determines the speed for reeling the cable in, while the flow control valve (2.2) determines the speed for reeling the cable out [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the main switch (Q1) and what hazard is associated with it?
questions.answer: The main switch (Q1) cuts off the mains electric supply and can be locked in the 0 (OFF) position [1]. The associated electrical hazard is that it does not switch off the voltage from the cable reel or from the slip rings without a pilot system, and the carrier's battery circuit remains on, posing an electric shock risk [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do the main pressure and return oil filters operate regarding clogging limits and bypass pressures?
questions.answer:
**Pressure Filter (20 µm):** The clogging indicator activates when the pressure difference reaches **5 bars**, and the bypass valve opens if the pressure difference exceeds **7 bars** [7, 8]. *(Note: If the oil is below +30 °C, the sensor is switched off to prevent false alarms due to high viscosity [8]).*
*   **Return Oil Filter (10 µm):** The electrical clogging indicator triggers a warning on the main screen when the pressure difference exceeds **2 bars**, and its bypass valve opens at **3 bars** [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What part number is associated with the inclination sensors used for the Boom and Drilling Module?
questions.answer: The system uses IKL inclinometers for the Boom Support Inclination (B182G), Boom Inclination (B20G), and Drilling Module Inclination (B18G) to measure angles with respect to gravity [22]. The part ID shown for the IKL module is **BG00423717** [23]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the general specifications for the hydraulic powerpack and oil tank capacity?
questions.answer: The system utilizes a **90 kW HPP1590 powerpack** [4]. The hydraulic oil tank has a volume of **270 liters** [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific flow rates for the percussion and feed circuits during drilling?
questions.answer:
The required flow rates at maximum percussion pressure vary based on the specific machine and rock drill model:
*   **DL432i with RD921S:** 120–135 L/min for percussion and 21 L/min for feed [1].
*   **DL432i or DL422iE with RD927L:** 135–150 L/min for percussion and 21 L/min for feed [1].
*   **DL422iE with HL1560 / HF1560:** 125–200 L/min for percussion and 21 L/min for feed [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the part number for the programming cable used during CAN bus module spare part installation?
questions.answer: The programming cable required for spare part installation mode is identified by part number/ID **BG01647579** [24]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the components and part numbers for the dewatering pump's circuit breaker (F9) and contactors (K9)?
questions.answer: For 1000 V (type C) systems, the dewatering pump uses the **NZMH2-A20-S1** motor-protective circuit breaker (F9) for short circuit protection [7] and the **LC1D80BW** contactor (K9) [8]. For type A and B systems, the **DILM32** contactor (K9) is used [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning conditions are triggered if the service brake charge pressure drops too low, and what is the required response?
questions.answer: If the charge pressure in either the front or rear brake accumulators drops below **110 bar**, a notice is displayed on the GUI and the warning light on Tramming panel A will turn on [9-11]. If the pressure drops further to **75 bar**, a red alarm is triggered, the warning light stays on, and a **tramming forced stop** is activated—the hydrostatic transmission forces into neutral, an alarm sounds, and the spring-applied brakes automatically engage [9, 10, 12]. The operator must stop and investigate the cause of the brake pressure loss [9, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you safely check for a faulty multivoltage power factor correction capacitor?
questions.answer: Start one power pack at a time and allow it to idle [6]. Observe the power factor value displayed on the electric quality measuring unit (P1) [6]. If the power factor value reads under 0.5 and the individual phase currents differ significantly, the capacitor is likely faulty [6]. A faulty capacitor unit cannot be repaired and must always be completely replaced [6]. Before touching any terminals, verify that there is no residual voltage, noting that residual voltage drops to 0 V immediately when the electric motor is stopped [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What module functions as the Main Switchgear Sensors (MS) and Tramming Controller (TCP)?
questions.answer: These systems use the VIU module [18]. The VIU is a general-purpose CANopen slave input unit designed for user interfaces and voltage inputs, providing 5 V analog inputs for joysticks and potentiometers while meeting SIL2 safety requirements [18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik DL422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: During operation, the feed pressure reads significantly lower than the expected 210 bars at the LS measuring connector when running against the rear end stopper; if the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) is functioning correctly, which two specific shock/anti-cavitation valves must be checked, and what are their respective target pressure settings when adjusted using the variable displacement pump (1) set to 250 bars?
questions.answer:
If the feed or fast feed pressure reads low and the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) is confirmed to be functioning correctly, you must check the **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)** and the **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** [1, 2]. 

If these valves need to be adjusted or replaced, the target pressure settings are **200 bars** for port A and **240 bars** for port B [3]. 

According to Section 6.10 ("Feed / fast feed pressure is too low") on pages 64-65 of the Drilling Hydraulics manual, you must use the following step-by-step sequence to adjust them [2-4]:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point (**M1**) of the drilling control valve [3].
2. Use the pressure controller (**B**) to temporarily adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) to **250 bars** [3].
3. Run the feed against the front end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.18**) to **200 bars** [3].
4. Run the feed against the rear end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.19**) to **240 bars** [3].
5. Once adjustments are complete, carefully re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) back to its normal operating pressure as instructed in the section *"Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)"* [3, 4].

questions.question: A machine exhibits excessively high rotation pressure during drilling, yet the rotation speed is set correctly and the rock drill rotation motor is undamaged; which specific pressure compensator on the drilling control valve block should be extracted and inspected for mechanical damage?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, if the rotation pressure is too high during drilling, the rotation speed is correctly adjusted, and the rock drill rotation motor is undamaged, you must extract and inspect the **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)** [1, 2].

According to Section 6.13 ("Rotation pressure is too high") on page 67 of the *Drilling Hydraulics* manual, you should follow this step-by-step procedure to inspect it:

1. Remove the rotation line pressure compensator (**20.2**) from the drilling control valve block [1].
2. Clean and check the condition of the compensator [1].
3. If the compensator is mechanically damaged, you must replace the whole drilling control valve block [1].

questions.question: You are troubleshooting the CAN bus with the battery main switch (S1) in the 0 (OFF) position and measure approximately 45 kΩ total resistance between the CAN_HI and CAN_LO lines; what two specific fault conditions could this high resistance reading indicate?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, measuring approximately 45 kΩ (~40...50 kΩ) total resistance between the CAN_HI and CAN_LO lines during CAN bus troubleshooting indicates the following fault conditions:

1. The bus is interrupted at at least two points.
2. Both 120 Ω termination resistors are missing or are faulty [1, 2]. 

According to Section 8.7.1 ("CAN bus troubleshooting by measuring resistance") on page 110 of the *Control system DL432i* manual, this diagnostic test follows a specific procedure:
1. Ensure the power is disconnected by turning the battery main switch (**S1**) to position **0** [3].
2. Ensure you have the CAN bus cable connection diagrams at hand [3].
3. Measure the total resistance between the **CAN_HI** and **CAN_LO** lines using a multimeter [2].

questions.question: You are diagnosing a shank lubrication issue and observe the yellow STATUS LED on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) repeatedly emitting a sequence of two flashes; what exact malfunction does this blink code indicate regarding the system's sensors?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, observing a sequence of **two flashes** on the yellow STATUS LED of the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) indicates a **malfunction in the lubrication oil flow**, specifically that the **signal from the flow sensor is not detected** [1, 2].

According to Section 8.1.1 ("CAN troubleshooting") in the *Shank lubrication unit* manual, when this specific error code occurs, you must consult the troubleshooting tables for causes of flow malfunction [3]. The "No oil flow" troubleshooting charts list the following potential causes and their corrective actions [4, 5]:

*   **Oil level too low / Air in the pump:** Check the oil tank level, add oil, and bleed the pump.
*   **Pump intake opening clogged:** Check and clean the tank.
*   **Inner tube clogged:** Remove the inner tube and clean or replace it.
*   **Oil viscosity too high:** Use the correct oil type.
*   **Pump control valve (CT5.1) broken or wire broken:** Check and replace the valve or wire.
*   **Pump timer faulty or timer frequency incorrectly adjusted:** Check the adjustment or replace the timer.
*   **Shank lubrication pressure hose damaged:** Replace or repair the hose.
*   **Foreign object in the suction side of the check valve (CT1):** Clean the check valve ball.
*   **Foreign object in the control plug non-return valve:** Clean the control plug / tank.
*   **Filler cap clogged (causing underpressure):** Clean the breather.
*   **Return hose to oil collecting tank clogged:** Remove the blockage.

questions.question: On the Fast Proportional Valve Controller (FPVC) 7-segment display, you observe a continuous diagnostic sequence reading "16 - oP – Co – J1 – 6b"; what exact electrical fault condition does the "6b" indicate for pin XJ1.6?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the "**6b**" in the diagnostic sequence indicates that pin **XJ1.6 is short-circuited to the battery** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 8.8 ("Diagnostics on the module display") on page 115 of the *Control system DL432i* manual, once the initial boot identification sequence is over, the FPVC's 7-segment display will repeatedly cycle through the following sequence of information [1]:

1. **The node id of the device** (e.g., "16").
2. **The network management state** of the device (e.g., "oP" for operational, "Pr" for pre-operational, or "st" for stopped).
3. **Communication error**, if there is any (indicated by "Co").
4. **I/O fault status** for each faulty signal, which consists of:
   * The connector of the faulty I/O (e.g., "J1").
   * The pin number (in hex) followed by a status letter [1]. 

The status letters are defined as [1]:
* **s** = short circuit to ground
* **o** = open circuit
* **b** = short circuit to battery

Therefore, in the specific sequence "16 - oP – Co – J1 – 6b", the system is indicating that node 16 is operational with a communication error, and specifically for connector J1, pin 6 has a short circuit to the battery [2].

questions.question: When adjusting the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) using a gauge connected to measuring point MPS, what is the correct target pressure setting?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.7.4 ("Adjusting steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9)") of the Drill carrier C400, C900 manual (page 81), the correct target pressure setting is **220 bars** [1-3].

The step-by-step procedure to achieve this setting is as follows:

1. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MPS** [2].
2. Loosen the locking nut from the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (**10.9**) and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise so it is fully open [2].
3. Start the diesel engine [2].
4. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position, which pressurizes the carrier hydraulics [2].
5. Shortly apply the maximum diesel engine rpm [2].
6. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.9**) clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge reaches the target of **220 bars** [2, 3].
7. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.9**) [3].
8. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle [3].
9. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it clockwise to lock the stud in the down position. Verify from the pressure gauge that the pressure level drops to the free circulation level (less than 30 bars) [3].
10. Shut down the engine [3].
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **MPS** [3].

questions.question: During the adjustment of the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8), what must the pressure reading at measuring connector MPB drop to after adjusting the retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) to 160 bars at connector MCR?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the pressure reading at the measuring connector **MPB** must drop to **200 bars** [1]. *(Note: According to the official procedure, the MPB gauge is adjusted to drop to 200 bars just prior to adjusting the retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) down to 160 bars).*

According to Section 4.7.7 ("Adjusting brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)") on pages 83–85 of the *Drill carrier C400, C900* manual, the exact step-by-step sequence is as follows [1-5]:

1. Unplug the electrical connectors of the brake circuit retarder control valve (**10.16/Y344**) and the carrier functions pressurization control valve (**10.18/Y167**) [2].
2. Connect the electrical connector **Y167** to the solenoid of the valve (**10.16**), leave the connector **Y344** unplugged [2].
3. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MPB** and another 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring connector **MCR** [3].
4. Loosen the locking nuts from brake circuit main pressure relief valve (**10.8**) and brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (**10.15**) [3].
5. Start the diesel engine [3].
6. Run the boom zoom function backwards to activate electrical connector **Y167**. Run the function until the adjustment of the pressure relief valves (**10.8** and **10.15**) are locked [3].
7. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm [3].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.8**) fully clockwise but simultaneously strictly observe that the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MPB** does not exceed 205 bars [3, 4]. *(If the pressure tends to exceed 205 bars, use the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) to reduce the pressure to be able to turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.8) fully closed)* [4].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.15**) until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MCR** is 210 bars [4]. *(Note: The maximum pressure level allowed to brake accumulators is 210 bars so it must never be exceeded)* [1].
10. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.8**) counterclockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MPB drops to 200 bars** [1].
11. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.8**) [1].
12. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.15**) until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MCR** is **160 bars** [1].
13. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.15**) [1].
14. Release the boom zoom function [1].
15. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle and shut down the engine after idling [1, 5].
16. Remove the pressure gauges from the measuring connectors **MPB** and **MCR** [5].
17. Unplug the electrical connector **Y167** from the valve (**10.16**) and return the electrical connectors back to their original positions - connector **Y344** to valve (**10.16**) and connector **Y167** to valve (**10.18**) [5].

questions.question: What is the target braking pressure range for the water hose reel brake valve (24) measured at point (23), and what is the specific required setting for the DU422i-W model?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the target braking pressure range for the water hose reel brake valve **(24)** is **20...30 bar** [1, 2]. For the specific **DU422i-W** model, the required setting is **35 bar** [2]. 

According to Section 6.1 ("Adjusting the water hose reel brake valve") on page 23 of the *Basic adjustment of the cable reel and water hose reel* manual, this is the step-by-step sequence for measuring and adjusting the pressure at measuring point **(23)**:

1. Start the diesel engine [1]. 
2. Connect the pressure gauge to the measuring point **(23)** of the water hose reel brake valve **(24)** [1]. 
3. Loosen the locking nut **(25)** of the water hose reel brake valve [1]. 
4. Activate the "reeling out the water hose" function and read the braking pressure from the pressure gauge [1]. 
5. Turn the adjusting screw **(26)** clockwise/counterclockwise to adjust the braking pressure to **20...30 bar** (or **35 bar** if using the DU422i-W model) [2]. *Note: When setting the appropriate braking pressure, ensure you are able to reel out the water hose slowly by hand, and that the braking pressure stops the water hose reel rotation when tramming stops* [2].
6. Tighten the locking nut **(25)** [2]. 
7. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point **(23)** [2].

questions.question: When adjusting the compressor unloading pressure limit valve (PS3) using a 3 mm hexagonal key, at what specific pressure should it be set to open to ensure internal pressure does not exceed 10 bar(g)?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the compressor unloading pressure limit valve (**PS3**) should be set to open at **8 bar(g)** [1]. If this adjustment is correct, the internal pressure will not rise higher than 10 bar(g) [1, 2].
