For a 37 kW dewatering pump, this specific F9 circuit breaker (Type A) utilizes an optional adjustable overload release setting of 25 - 32 A (Section "Dewatering pump short circuit protection with motor-protective 1000 V circuit breaker (F9), type A", Page 35-36) [4].

**Reset Procedure:**
Once the underlying issue with the K9 contactor is resolved, the trip will remain latched in the memory of the EFL relay. To clear it, an external reset must be manually performed by pressing the **S293 pushbutton** [1].

questions.question: On the Hammer Lubrication Controller (SLC), the yellow STATUS LED flashes three times while the green CAN-RUN LED remains solidly ON. Knowing the expected current signal from the sensor is 4-20 mA, what specific component failure does this indicate, and how does it impact the electrical control valve (CT5.1) regulating the oil flow?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided Technical Manual, here is the diagnostic breakdown for the Hammer Lubrication Controller (SLC) LED indications:

**1. LED Indications and Component Failure**
*   **Green CAN-RUN LED (Solidly ON):** This simply indicates that the SLC unit is currently powered ON (Technical Manual, Section 3.2 "Hammer Lubrication Controller (SLC)", Page 12) [1].
*   **Yellow STATUS LED (Three Flashes):** This specifically indicates a malfunction with the **air pressure sensor**. The control system registers this fault when the air pressure sensor is either broken or disconnected, causing the current signal from the sensor to drop **below 2 mA** (the normal expected value is 4...20 mA) (Technical Manual, Section 3.2 "Hammer Lubrication Controller (SLC)", Page 12) [2]. 

**2. Impact on the Electrical Control Valve (CT5.1)**
*   The **electrically controlled valve (CT5.1)** is directly controlled by the SLC to adjust the lubrication oil/semi-fluid dosage by changing the operation frequency of the hydraulically operated piston pumps based on drilling conditions (Technical Manual, Section 4.1 "Operation of the SLC", Page 16) [3, 4]. 
*   Because the SLC requires accurate air pressure data to determine the required amount of lubrication for current drilling conditions, the failure of the air pressure sensor disrupts the SLC's ability to properly control the frequency of **valve (CT5.1)**, compromising the correct dosage of lubrication oil to the ITH hammer [4].

questions.question: While attempting to adjust the steering circuit during power pack tramming, the pressure at measuring connector MPS only reaches 180 bars despite the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) being adjusted fully clockwise. If the pilot circuit pressure at measuring connector MX reads a steady 35 bars, which components—such as the load-hold check valve (10.22) or the shock/anti-cavitation valves (10.6, 10.7)—are most likely causing the pressure loss?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical documentation, the inability to reach the 220 bar setting at measuring connector **MPS** is primarily due to using the incorrect operating mode for adjusting the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (**10.9**), combined with the specific pressure limits enforced by the power pack tramming circuit and the shock/anti-cavitation valves. 

Here is the diagnostic breakdown of the components causing the pressure limitation and the correct procedures:

**1. Steering Circuit Pressure Reducing Valve (30.11)**
During power pack tramming, the steering circuit is not supplied by the main steering pump (**7.1**), but rather by the rotation variable displacement pump via the power pack tramming manifold (**30**) [1, 2]. The pressure supplied to the steering and brake control manifold (**10**) during this mode is strictly determined and reduced by the **steering circuit pressure reducing valve (30.11)** [3]. 
*   **The limit:** Valve **30.11** is calibrated to a maximum of **200 bars** [4]. Because this valve regulates the incoming pressure during power pack tramming, adjusting the main relief valve (**10.9**) fully clockwise will have no effect, as the supply pressure cannot exceed what **30.11** allows [3, 4].

**2. Shock/Anti-Cavitation Valves (10.6 and 10.7)**
If you are measuring the pressure while the steering joystick is pushed to the extreme position (which directs oil to the steering cylinders), the pressure is further limited by the shock/anti-cavitation valves on the working ports.
*   **The limit:** **Shock/anti-cavitation valve (10.6)** limits the working port A (steering right) pressure to **190 bars**, and **shock/anti-cavitation valve (10.7)** limits the working port B (steering left) pressure to **190 bars** [5-7]. If these valves are lifting early or leaking, they will cap the maximum system pressure at around 180–190 bars during steering movements. 

**3. Load-Hold Check Valve (10.22)**
While the **load-hold check valve (10.22)** is in the flow path to prevent backflow and load sinking [8], a severe internal leak here could theoretically contribute to pressure loss. However, it is not a pressure-regulating component, making the valves mentioned above (**30.11, 10.6, 10.7**) the more likely culprits for a hard pressure cap [5, 8].

### Correct Procedures for Resolution (Section 5.1.4 and 5.2.4)

**To properly adjust the Steering Circuit Main Pressure Relief Valve (10.9) to 220 bars:**
You cannot adjust this valve during power pack tramming. 
1. Start the **diesel engine** and attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring connector **MPS** [9].
2. Push the carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it counterclockwise to the UP position to pressurize the carrier hydraulics [10].
3. Apply **maximum diesel engine rpm** [10].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of valve **(10.9)** clockwise until the gauge reads exactly **220 bars** [10, 11].

**To diagnose and adjust the Steering Pressure during Power Pack Tramming (30.11):**
If you need to verify the power pack tramming steering pressure:
1. Start the power pack and attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring connector **MS** [12].
2. Lift the right rear jack to activate the carrier pressurization valve (**Y168**) [12].
3. Release the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) to the UP position to manually override solenoid **Y167** [12].
4. Force the steering circuit pressurization enabler valve (**30.9 / Y415**) from the GUI [12].
5. Adjust the steering circuit pressure reducing valve (**30.11**) until the gauge reads **200 bars** [4].

questions.question: The control system display shows an alarm for the 27.0 VDC power supply (A3/A4) after a 6-second delay, and the red Overload LED on the unit is flashing slowly. Since this indicates either an output voltage of U < 85% UN or a continuous short-circuit operation, how would you isolate the load circuits on the A2 circuit board without inadvertently triggering a fault in the NST-2004 emergency stop safety relay?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided technical manuals, here is the diagnostic and isolation procedure to address the power supply alarm without faulting the emergency stop relay:

**1. Alarm Confirmation**
On the 27.0 VDC control system power supply units (**A3, A4**), a slowly flashing red Overload LED confirms that the unit is experiencing either an output voltage of **U < 85% UN** or a **continuous short-circuit operation ("C")**. This state de-energizes the DC-OK contact, which opens and triggers an alarm on the drilling display after a **6-second delay** *(Electric System DU412i, Section 4.1, Page 29)*.

**2. Step-by-Step Electrical Isolation**
Because a short circuit is present, you must completely isolate the rig's electrical system before interacting with the circuit boards to prevent damage or injury *(Maintenance Manual, Section 2.6.1 / Electric System DU412i, Section 4.2.3, Page 152)*:
1. Turn off and lock the **main switch (Q1)** and remove the power plug from the electrical network.
2. Turn the **battery isolation switch (S1)** to the OFF (0) position and lock it.
3. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** to the OFF position and lock the DQ cabinet cover.
4. Because the S1 switch does not disconnect the direct supply from the battery, you must physically **disconnect the battery terminals** to ensure the complete isolation of the 24 VDC circuit.

**3. Isolating the A2 Circuit Board**
Once the 24 VDC circuit is completely dead, you can safely isolate the load circuits on the **A2 circuit board** (located in the cabin) by opening its specific circuit breakers. These breakers range from **F2 to F18** and protect localized circuits such as the Rod handler Controller (**F2**), Front tramming CAN (**F9**), cabin AC (**F12**), and Fire suppression (**F17**) *(Electric System DU412i, Section 3.8, Pages 51-52)*.

**4. Avoiding a Fault in the NST-2004 Emergency Stop Safety Relay**
The **NST-2004** relay is designed to deactivate and trigger a fault via its internal **PTC fuse F1** if it detects a **short circuit between the two emergency stop contacts** *(Electric System DU412i, Section 4.3, Page 59)*. 
* To avoid inadvertently triggering this fault while testing the A2 board, you must ensure no cross-wiring or testing shorts are introduced between the emergency stop input terminals (**T11, T12, T14, T21, T22, T34**). 
* Furthermore, you do not need to interact with the emergency stop power supply to isolate the A2 board; the supply to the emergency stop circuit is independently protected by circuit breaker **F12 (10 A)**, which is located separately in the **DQ cabinet**, not on the A2 circuit board *(Electric System DU412i, Section 3.3, Page 44)*.

questions.question: When adjusting the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (1), what must the stand-by pressure be set to using flow controller (A) after adjusting the pressure controller (B) to 230 bars at measuring point MP1?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.1.1 "Adjusting the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (1)" (Drilling Hydraulics DU412i, pages 35-36), the stand-by pressure must be set to **30 bars** [1]. 

Here is the step-by-step sequence following the adjustment of the pressure controller (B) to 230 bars:

1. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge connected to the measuring point **MP1** shows **230 bars** [2].
2. Lock the adjustment of the pressure controller (B) with the locking nut [1].
3. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [1].
4. Allow the pressure to stabilize in the pressure gauge connected to the measuring point **MP1** [1].
5. Adjust the stand-by pressure to **30 bars** from the flow controller (A) by turning the adjusting screw clockwise [1].
6. Lock the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) with the locking nut [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (12.3), what temporary pressure must the rotation pump's pressure controller (B) be set to before loosening the adjusting screw to achieve a 250 bar reading at MP1?
questions.answer:
Based on the Drilling Hydraulics DU412i manual (Section 5.2 "Adjusting the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve", pages 38-39), the rotation pump's pressure controller (B) must be temporarily set to **260 bars** before loosening the main pressure relief valve's adjusting screw [1]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for adjusting the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (12.3) to achieve the 250 bar reading:

1. Stop the power pack [2].
2. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (12.3) [2].
3. Tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (12.3) almost to its end (over 250 bars) [2].
4. Remove the caps from the flow controller (A) and the pressure controller (B) of the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (1) and undo the locking nuts of their adjusting spindles [3].
5. Open the adjusting screws of the pressure controller (B) and the flow controller (A) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
6. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (MP1) [1].
7. Start the power pack [1].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) fully closed (clockwise). *Note: The pump is now operating at constant pressure* [1].
9. **Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows 260 bars** [1].
10. Loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (12.3) until the adjusting begins to effect. The valve will begin to fizz when restricting the pressure, and the pressure value on the gauge will drop to **250 bars** [1].
11. Re-adjust the values of the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (1) as instructed in its specific adjustment section [4].
12. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (12.3) [4].
13. Stop the power pack. *Note: Take care that the oil flow does not pass through the main pressure relief valve for a long time, as the hydraulic system gets warmer while the valve restricts pressure* [4].

questions.question: When adjusting the feed counter balance valve on the feed load control block, what flow rate should be supplied to port C1 to calibrate the valve to 140 bars at gauge port MC1?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.6.1 "Adjusting feed counter balance valve" of the Drilling Hydraulics manual, a flow rate of **5 L/min** should be supplied to port C1 [1, 2]. It is recommended to perform this adjustment on a hydraulic bench by first removing the feed load control block from the machine [1].

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for adjusting the feed counter balance valve (16.1):

1. Connect the appropriate hydraulic power supply to port **C1** (with a capacity of e.g., 200 bar and 5 L/min) [1].
2. Connect port **V1** to the tank line [2].
3. Connect a pressure gauge to port **MC1** [2].
4. Loosen the locking nut and the setting of the valve [2].
5. Start the power supply [2].
6. Set the flow rate to **5 L/min** [2].
7. Increase the setting of the valve until the pressure gauge shows **140 bars** [2].
8. Lock the setting of the valve [2].
9. Remove the gauges and disconnect the hydraulic power supply [2].

questions.question: When measuring at connector MX with the diesel engine at maximum rpm, to what pressure must the steering circuit pilot pressure reducing valve (10.11) be adjusted?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided technical documentation (Section 5.1.5 "Adjusting steering circuit pilot pressure reducing valve (10.11)", pages 108-109), the steering circuit pilot pressure reducing valve (10.11) must be adjusted to **35 bars** [1].

Here is the step-by-step sequence for this adjustment procedure:

1. Replace the plug in measuring connection **MX** with the measuring connector G1/4 - M16x2 [2].
2. Attach a **40 bar pressure gauge** to the measuring connector **MX** [2].
3. Loosen the locking nut of the pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (**10.11**) and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise fully open [2].
4. Start the diesel engine [2].
5. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the UP position to pressurize the carrier hydraulics [2].
6. Apply shortly the **maximum diesel engine rpm** [2].
7. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.11**) clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge is **35 bars** [1].
8. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.11**) [1].
9. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle and shut down the engine after idling [1].
10. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the DOWN position [1].
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **MX** [1].

questions.question: To what pressure must the service brake circuit pressure reducing valve (30.10) be set at measuring connector MSB while forcing the service brake circuit pressurization enabler valve (30.8/Y417) from the GUI?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical documentation (Section 5.2.3 "Adjusting service brake circuit pressure reducing valve (30.10)", Page 115), the service brake circuit pressure reducing valve (**30.10**) must be set to **160 bars** at measuring connector **MSB** [1, 2].

Here is the step-by-step sequence for this adjustment procedure:

1. Open the locking nut of the service brake circuit pressure reducing valve (**30.10**) [1].
2. Loosen the adjusting screw of the valve (**30.10**) [1].
3. Attach a **250 bar pressure gauge** to the measuring connector **MSB** [1].
4. Start the power pack [1].
5. Push the button from CP2 to lift the right rear jack to the up position. Keep the button pushed down to activate the carrier pressurization valve (**Y168**) [1].
6. Force the service brake circuit pressurization enabler valve (**30.8/Y417**) from the GUI [1].
7. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**30.10**) until the reading in the pressure gauge is **160 bars** [2].
8. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**30.10**) [2].
9. Release the right rear jack button and stop forcing valve (**30.8/Y417**) from the GUI [2].
10. Stop the power pack [2].
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **MSB** [2].

questions.answer: Based on the Technical Specification document under the "HYDRAULIC SYSTEM" section, the specific model name of the main hydraulic powerpack used on the drill rig is the **HPP755**, and it has a power output rating of **55 kW** [1].
