For the D45 housing, this specifically involves checking the **shank lubrication return (SR) line** for water contamination [1, 2]. *(Note: You should also visually check if flushing water is escaping directly through the drain holes)* [1, 2].
3. Stop the flushing [3, 4].

questions.question: During the expansion of an inflatable rock bolt via water valve Y411, if the desired bolting pressure is not reached within 30 seconds as monitored by pressure switch S808, what specific visual indication occurs on the SH80 button to signal a bolting failure?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Operator's Manual DS411-C - StageV* (Section 4.5.19: "Bolting with Inflatable bolts", pages 270-272), if the desired bolting pressure is not reached within 30 seconds, the bolting process is automatically discontinued, and the indicator light on the **button (SH80) starts blinking rapidly** to indicate a bolting failure [1].

The complete step-by-step sequence for inflatable rock bolt installation and the associated pressure control logic is as follows:

1. Turn the switch **(S78)** to the position for the bolting head functions [2].
2. Turn the bolt feed to the hole centre by moving the control lever **(S85)** to the right (3 o'clock position) [2].
3. Push the bolt into the hole, up to the gripper jaws, by pushing the control lever **(S73)** forward (12 o'clock position) [2, 3]. 
4. Open the gripper jaws by pulling the control lever **(S77)** with the push-button pressed diagonally to the rear right (4.30 o'clock position) [3].
5. Swing the jaws out by releasing the push-button [3].
6. Push the bolt entirely into the hole [3].
7. If the stroke length of the feed is not sufficient, push the rest of the bolt using the feed extension cylinder by pushing the control lever **(S77)** forward (12 o'clock position) [3].
8. Stop the feed [3].
9. When the bolt is at the bottom of the hole, press the button **(SH80)** [3]. 
    *   The water valve **(Y411)** opens the high-water-pressure line to the bolt and closes the return line [4].
    *   Simultaneously, valves **(Y412)** and **(Y413)** start the pumping [4]. During pumping, the indicator light on the button **(SH80)** blinks slowly [1].
    *   *Normal Operation:* The pressure switch **(S808)** stops the pumping as soon as the desired bolting pressure is reached, at which point the indicator light becomes continuous [1, 4]. The water pressure remains on for 2 seconds before the water valve **(Y411)** releases the pressure through the return line, finishing the tightening, and the indicator light goes off [1, 4].
    *   *Failure Condition:* If the required bolting pressure is not reached within 30 seconds, pumping stops, and the indicator light on button **(SH80)** begins **blinking rapidly** [1].
10. Press the button **(SH80)** to switch off the indicator [1].
11. Return the bolt feed and drilling feed to the rear position [1].
12. Drive the anchor stud in, and move the bolting head with the boom to the next hole [5].

questions.question: While testing the front axle service brake on a TC10-TC12 carrier using switch S29, as the pressure on gauge P3 drops below 75 bar, what specific electrical state must be verified across contacts 13 and 14 of the front brake pressure switch S13B?
questions.answer:
When testing the front axle service brake, as the pressure drops below **75 bar**, you must verify that the electrical contact across **contacts 13 and 14** of the **front brake pressure switch S13B** is **open** [1]. 

According to the "Steering and braking system TC7-TC12, NC7" manual (Section 4.3.2: *Testing the ABA brake system - Checking the operation of brake system pressure alarms and clutch pressure switch*, pages 89–91), the step-by-step sequence to reach this state and verify the contact is as follows:

1. Start the diesel engine and let brake pressures (**P3** and **P4** gauges on the tramming panel) rise until they are fully charged on both lines [2, 3].
2. Stop the diesel engine by pressing the emergency stop button, and then return the emergency stop button to its normal position [3].
3. Reduce brake pressure on the front axle using the **service brake test switch S29** on the tramming panel [3]. Turn the switch repeatedly to the left and back to the center and watch the **P3 pressure gauge** until the pressure drops below **110 bar** and the **warning light H20** on the tramming panel lights up [3].
4. Continue reducing the pressure until the pressure drops below **100 bar** and the indicator light on the **pressure gauge P3** goes on [1].
5. Continue reducing the pressure until the pressure drops below **75 bar**. Measure from the **contacts 13 and 14** of the **front brake pressure switch S13B** that the contact is **open** [1].
6. Start the diesel engine and let the pressure accumulator pressures rise back to **135 bar** [1].

questions.question: To correctly calibrate the anti-jamming automatics pressure switch (14) using an ohm meter so that logic input ch 02.07 activates properly, where exactly must the rotation hoses be disconnected and plugged before temporarily adjusting the rotation pressure relief valve (30)?
questions.answer:
To correctly calibrate the anti-jamming automatics pressure switch **(14)**, the rotation hoses must be disconnected exactly from the **hose support** and the hose ends must be plugged [1].

According to the "DS411 Drilling and bolting hydraulics" manual (Section 5.1.5: *Anti-jamming automatics pressure control*, page 53), the complete step-by-step sequence to perform this calibration is as follows:

1. Turn the anti-jamming automatics off using the selector switch **(S79)** [1].
2. Start the power pack [1].
3. Move the rock drill against the rear stopper [1].
4. Stop the power pack [1].
5. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the **hose support** and plugging the hose ends [1].
6. Start the power pack [1].
7. Move the rotation lever **(S73)** to the right [1].
8. Adjust the rotation pressure relief valve **(30)** temporarily to the required anti-jamming automatics pressure [1].
9. Check the adjusted pressure from the pressure gauge **(41)** [2].
10. Use an ohm meter to adjust the anti-jamming automatics pressure switch **(14)** so that it functions with the required anti-jamming automatics pressure, or check when the logic input **ch 02.07** is activated [2]. *Note: When the adjustment is carried out correctly, the input LED will come on and off during a single revolution of the pressure switch adjusting screw* [2].
11. Adjust the rotation pressure relief valve **(30)** back to its original value [2].
12. Tighten the lock nut of the valve **(30)** and re-check the pressure [2].
13. Stop the power pack [3].
14. Remove the plugs from the disconnected rotation hoses and reconnect the hoses from the **hose support** [3].

questions.question: What is the specified boom extension length and the maximum operating height (C) for the TBR60 bolting boom according to the machine's technical specifications?

questions.question: When assembling an asterisk-marked RD314 pressure accumulator, if applying the maximum tightening torque of 300 Nm to the bottom fails to align the bottom mark (|) between the (o) and (R) marks on the cover, what specific internal component must be replaced?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Pressure accumulator for hydraulic rock drill, maintenance instructions" manual, if the bottom mark **(|)** fails to reach the mark **(o)** when the maximum tightening torque of **300 Nm** is applied, the **diaphragm** must be replaced [1]. 

According to Section 3.7.1 (*Assembling an accumulator marked with an asterisk*, pages 20–22), the complete step-by-step sequence for assembling this accumulator is as follows:

1. Check that the numbers on the cover and the bottom match (high-pressure accumulators use uneven numbers, and low-pressure accumulators use even numbers) [2].
2. Check the condition of the threads by installing the bottom to the cover *without* the diaphragm [3]. Tighten the bottom to **150 Nm** [3]. If the bottom rotates over the mark **(R)** at 150 Nm, the accumulator must be scrapped [3]. If the threads are in good condition, remove the bottom from the cover [3].
3. Fit a new or inspected **diaphragm** to the cover, ensuring it sits securely in the groove with the correct side facing downwards [3]. The **O-rings** should also be replaced at this time [3].
4. Lubricate the surface of the diaphragm **(A)** and the bottom surface of the accumulator **(B)** with vaseline or lanolin [1].
5. Lubricate the thread of the bottom with vaseline or lanolin [1].
6. Use a torque wrench and the special tool to tighten the bottom to a maximum of **300 Nm** [1]. The bottom mark **(|)** must end up between the marks **(o)** and **(R)** when 300 Nm is reached [1]. *(Note: If the bottom does not reach the mark (o) at 300 Nm, the diaphragm must be replaced)* [1].
7. Verify that the face of the bottom **(D)** sits below the bottom face of the cover **(C)** [4]. Place a straight edge tool **(1)** on the bottom face **(C)** of the cover to confirm there is a visible gap between the tool and the bottom face **(D)** [4].
8. Replace the **filling valve** and tighten it to the correct torque of **40 Nm** [4].

questions.question: When extending the front stinger using control lever S77 and directional valve coil Y152, to what specific pressure value does the pressure-reducing valve limit the circuit, and what is the required N2 gas pre-charge pressure in the stinger's stabilizing accumulator?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Hydraulic bolting head" manual (Section 4.2 / 4.3: *Stabilizer out/in*, page 16), the specific pressure values are:

*   **Pressure-reducing valve limit:** The circuit pressure is limited to **50 bar** [1].
*   **N2 gas pre-charge pressure:** The stabilizing pressure accumulator's pressure is required to be **35 bar** [1].

The step-by-step sequence for extending the front stinger is as follows:
1. Push the control lever **(S77)** forward while simultaneously pressing the push-button at the end of the control lever [1].
2. The directional valve coil **(Y152)** receives control voltage and moves the directional valve spool to position 2 [1].
3. Hydraulic oil flows from the variable displacement pump through port **(P)** and the pressure-reducing valve (which limits the pressure to 50 bar) to the directional valve [1].
4. The oil then flows through port **(A1)** to the pilot-controlled non-return valve on the piston side of the front stinger cylinder [1].
5. The return oil flow from the piston rod side flows to the pilot-controlled non-return valve (which is opened by the hydraulic pressure on the piston side), and then continues through the directional valve to the hydraulic oil tank [1].

questions.question: During a service brake test on a TC10-TC12 carrier, what specific pressure value should be observed at the front axle's pressure inspection point (A), and how does it differ from the target pressure for a TC8 or NC7 carrier?
questions.answer:
During a service brake test on a TC10-TC12 carrier, the specific pressure value that should be observed at the front axle's pressure inspection point **(A)** is **70 bar** [1]. This differs from the target pressure for a TC8 or NC7 carrier, which requires a higher pressure of **80 bar** [1].

According to the Maintenance Manual (Section *Checking the service brake pressure*, page 298), the step-by-step sequence for this test is as follows:

1. Attach a pressure gauge to the front brake circuit's pressure inspection point **(A)** [1].
2. Start the engine [1].
3. Press the service brake pedal to the end of its movement path [1].
4. The pressure should be **70 bar** (for TC9-12 carriers) or **80 bar** (for TC8 and NC7 carriers) [1].
5. Repeat the same measurement for the rear brake circuit by attaching a pressure gauge to the rear brake circuit's pressure inspection point **(B)** [1].

questions.question: When measuring the steering system at checking point (A) with the machine turned against the end stops, what is the maximum allowed pressure, and what specific adjustment screw ID must be turned to correct it?
questions.answer:
When measuring the steering system at checking point (A) with the machine turned against the end stops, the maximum allowed pressure is **140 bar** [1, 2]. If the pressure differs from this value, it must be corrected by turning the adjustment screw **(B, 263.01)** [1, 3].

According to the maintenance manuals (Section 5.7.20 / Section 6.1.20), the step-by-step sequence for this procedure is as follows:
1. Ensure the hydraulic oil is at operating temperature and the engine is running at full speed [1, 2].
2. Connect the manometer to the checking point **(A)** [1, 2]. 
3. Turn the machine to the full turning angle against the end stops [1, 2].
4. Verify that the pressure does not exceed the maximum allowed **140 bar** [1, 2].
5. If the desired pressure differs from the given value, adjust it by turning the adjustment screw **(B, 263.01)** to the desired direction [1, 3].

questions.question: To properly adjust the idle-running (standby) pressure of the variable displacement pump to its target of 30 bar, which specific flow controller ID must be adjusted after the pressure regulator B (48) is set?
questions.answer:
To properly adjust the idle-running (standby) pressure of the **variable displacement pump (1)** to its target of **30 bar**, you must adjust **flow controller A (47)** [1, 2]. 

According to the "DS411 Drilling and bolting hydraulics" manual (Section 5.1.2: *Pressure adjustments of variable displacement pump (1)*, pages 49–50), the step-by-step sequence to perform this adjustment is as follows:

1. Remove the **flow controller A (47)** and **pressure regulator B (48)** caps and loosen their locking nuts [3].
2. Loosen the **pressure regulator B (48)** adjusting screw almost entirely (counterclockwise) [3].
3. Tighten the **flow controller A (47)** adjusting screw (clockwise), which allows the pump to provide an even pressure [3].
4. Turn on the power pack [3].
5. Check the pressure on the **percussion-pressure gauge (39)** and begin increasing the pressure by turning the **pressure regulator B (48)** adjusting screw clockwise until the pressure gauge shows **220 bar** [3].
6. Tighten the **pressure regulator B (48)** locking nut [2].
7. Loosen the **flow controller A (47)** adjusting screw almost entirely (counterclockwise) [2].
8. Wait until the pressure reading on the gauge is even [2].
9. Adjust the idle-running pressure to **30 bar** by turning **flow controller A (47)** clockwise [2].
10. Tighten the **flow controller A (47)** locking nut [2].
11. Turn off the power pack [2].
12. Wait until the pressure gauge gives a zero reading [2].
13. Turn on the power pack [2].
14. Wait until the pressure in the pressure gauge is even [2].
15. If the idle-running pressure shown by the pressure gauge is within the recommended limits, install the **flow controller A (47)** and **pressure regulator B (48)** caps [2, 4].
16. If the idle-running pressure is not within the correct limits, re-adjust **flow controller A (47)** according to the instructions [4].
17. Turn off the power pack [4].

questions.question: If the boom movement control joysticks (S01 and S02) require calibration to ensure proper function during drilling, which specific digital interface system in the cabin is used to perform this task?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, the specific digital interface system used to calibrate the boom movement control joysticks (**S01** and **S02**) is the **BAD (Boom Adjustment Display)** [1]. 

According to the troubleshooting guidelines in Section 6.7 ("Boom control does not work"), if there are issues with the boom functions after the power pack is started, you must check the following sequence:
1. Check that the drilling joysticks for the boom in question are in their middle position [1].
2. Check that the selected boom FPVC module display shows S.E (selected) in the seven-segment display [1].
3. Make sure that the boom movement control joysticks (**S01** & **S02**) have been calibrated, which **can be done via the BAD (Boom Adjustment Display)** [1]. 

The BAD is located at the operator station and allows the operator to input various settings and values for boom adjustments [2, 3].

questions.question: What specific rotational direction and position must the bolting head and feed be placed in so that the feed properly rests against the boom's tramming support during the transport stowing procedure?
questions.answer:
Based on the Operator's Manual (Section 4.3.2: *Tramming position*, page 224), to ensure the feed properly rests against the boom's tramming support, the bolting head must be rotated **counterclockwise**. 

The complete procedure for placing the machine in the correct tramming/transport position is as follows:
1. Tram the boom and the feed as close to the centre line of the rig, and as low as possible [1].
2. Move the boom and feed transfers to their rear position [1].
3. Rotate the bolting head counterclockwise and turn it so that the feed rests against the tramming support of the boom [1].
4. Close and lock all doors and hatches so that they cannot be opened during tramming [1].
5. Ensure the cement platforms (if equipped) are raised to their upper position [1].

questions.question: What is the required procedure and target pressure for adjusting the main pressure relief valve (23) while monitoring pressure gauge (39) and operating the zoom cylinder inwards?
questions.answer:
Based on the "DS411 Drilling and bolting hydraulics" manual (Section 5.1.1: *Adjusting the main pressure relief valve (23)*, pages 47–49), the target pressure for the main pressure relief valve **(23)** is **245 bar** [1, 2]. 

The specific step-by-step sequence for adjusting this valve (which is performed after temporarily plugging the pump hoses and setting the carrier's main pressure relief valve to 250 bar) is as follows:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the main pressure relief valve **(23)** [3].
2. Rotate the main pressure relief valve **(23)** adjusting screw **(1)** almost fully open (counterclockwise) [2].
3. Start the diesel engine [2].
4. Select the boom movements with the selector switch **(S78)** and run the zoom inwards by pulling the joystick **(S77)** backward (6 o'clock position) and pushing the button simultaneously [2].
5. Rotate the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve **(23)** clockwise until the pressure gauge **(39)** shows **245 bar** [2].
6. Tighten the locking nut of the main pressure relief valve **(23)** [4].

*(Note: Following this sequence, you must readjust the carrier main pressure relief valve back to its standard 220 bar, stop the engine, and reconnect the previously plugged hoses [4].)*

questions.question: When assembling a rock drill pressure accumulator marked with an asterisk, what specific maximum tightening torque must be applied to the bottom, and between which two marks on the cover must the bottom's (|) mark align?
questions.answer:

1. Check that the numbers on the cover and the bottom match (high-pressure accumulators use uneven numbers, and low-pressure accumulators use even numbers) [2]. 
2. Check the condition of the threads by installing the bottom to the cover *without* the diaphragm and tightening the bottom to 150 Nm [2, 3]. If the bottom rotates over the mark (R) at 150 Nm, the accumulator must be scrapped [3]. If the threads are in good condition, remove the bottom from the cover [3].
3. Fit a new or inspected diaphragm to the cover, ensuring it sits securely in the groove with the correct side facing downwards [3]. The O-rings should also be replaced when the diaphragm is changed [3].
4. Lubricate the surface of the diaphragm (A) and the bottom surface of the accumulator (B) with vaseline or lanolin [1].
5. Lubricate the thread of the bottom with vaseline or lanolin [1].
6. Use a torque wrench and the special tool to tighten the bottom to a maximum of **300 Nm** [1]. The bottom mark **(|)** must end up between the marks **(o)** and **(R)** when 300 Nm is reached [1]. *(Note: If the bottom does not reach the mark (o) at 300 Nm, the diaphragm must be replaced [1]).*
7. Check that the face of the bottom (D) is below the bottom face of the cover (C) [4]. Place a straight edge tool (1) on the bottom face (C) of the cover to verify there is a visible gap between the tool and the bottom face (D) [4].
8. Replace the filling valve and tighten it to the correct torque of 40 Nm [4].

questions.question: When performing a test of the water pressure switch (S422), at what specific pressure threshold and after what exact time delay should the system automatically stop the water pump and drilling functions to activate the H601 indicator?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Water circuit - DS411/DS421" manual and the "Maintenance Manual DS411-C", the specific pressure threshold for the water pressure switch **(S422)** is **2.8 bar** [1, 2]. 

The system triggers automatic stops based on the following exact time delays [1, 2]:
*   **Drilling functions stop:** If the pressure remains below **2.8 bar** for more than **4 seconds** (default threshold). 
*   **Water pump stops:** If the pressure remains below **2.8 bar** for more than **1 minute**. 

When this pressure threshold is breached, the **H601** (water pressure low) warning indicator on the QN panel lights up [1-3]. 

According to the procedure "Checking the operation of the pressure switch (S422)" (Water circuit manual Section 4.6.1, pages 25–26; Maintenance Manual Section 5.12.1, page 338), the step-by-step sequence to test this function is as follows [2-4]:

1. Close the water circuit using the shut-off valve.
2. Observe the system as the water pressure drops below **2.8 bar**. The pressure switch should engage and light up the **H601** warning indicator on the QN panel.
3. Press the pressure switch reset button **(S505)**. The pressure switch is operating properly if the warning indicator does *not* go off.
4. Open the shut-off valve. The pressure switch is operating properly if the **H601** warning indicator goes off as the pressure exceeds **2.8 bar**.

*(Note: If the test runs long enough for the water pump to stop, the fault must be acknowledged with button **(S505)** and the pump must be restarted using the water booster pump start/stop switch **(S501)**) [1].*

questions.question: While the maximum forward drilling feed pressure is limited to 140 bar by proportional valve (55), what specific pressure target must the bolt feed pressure reducing and relieving valve (62) be set to when the bolting head is driven manually against the movement stop limit?
questions.answer:
Based on the "DS411 Drilling and bolting hydraulics" manual, when the bolting head is driven manually against the movement stop limit, the bolt feed pressure reducing and relieving valve **(62)** must be set to a specific pressure target of **160 bar** [1].

According to Section 5.1.14 (*Adjusting the bolt-feeding speed and bolt-feed pressure*, pages 58–59), the step-by-step sequence for this bolt-feed pressure adjustment is as follows:

1. Loosen the adjustment screw locking nut [2].
2. Loosen the adjustment screw almost entirely (counterclockwise) [2].
3. Turn on the power pack and move the bolting head manually forward against the movement stop limit [2]. If the movement does not start, begin increasing the pressure by turning the pressure reducing and relieving valve **(62)** adjusting screw clockwise until the movement starts [2].
4. Keep the feed forward movement manually controlled against the stop limit and begin increasing the pressure by turning the pressure reducing and relieving valve **(62)** adjusting screw clockwise until the pressure shows **160 bar** [1].
5. Lock the adjusting screw [3].

questions.question: During bolt cassette rotation driven by the Maltese cross mechanism, what specific directional valve coil is activated by control lever S77, and what type of valve regulates the flow to control the cassette's rotation speed?
questions.answer:
During bolt cassette rotation driven by the Maltese cross mechanism, turning the control lever **(S77)** left to the 9 o'clock position activates the directional valve **coil (Y67)** [1]. The cassette's rotation speed is regulated by a **flow-control valve** [1].

According to the "Hydraulic bolting head" manual (Section 4.9: *Cassette rotation*, page 20), the step-by-step hydraulic sequence for this operation is as follows:

1. Turn the control lever **(S77)** left to the 9 o'clock position, which causes the Maltese cross to rotate the cassette [1].
2. The directional valve **coil (Y67)** receives control voltage and moves the directional valve spool to position 1 [1].
3. Hydraulic oil flows from the variable displacement pump through port **(P)** to the directional valve [1].
4. The oil continues to the pilot-controlled non-return valve, and then through the **flow-control valve** (which regulates the cassette rotation speed) to the cassette rotation motor [1].
5. The return flow from the rotation motor passes back to the **flow-control valve**, continues through the pilot-controlled non-return valve to the directional valve, and finally flows through port **(T)** to the hydraulic oil tank [1].

questions.question: If the adjustable jaw on the gripping cylinder needs to handle 25-39 mm bolts, which specific bolts must be opened to move the jaw to position 'c', and which directional valve coil (Y68, Y70, or Y71) is used to swing the jaws back into the cassette?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Hydraulic bolting head" manual, the answers to your questions are as follows:

*   **Adjusting the gripping cylinder jaw:** To move the adjustable jaw **(1)** to position 'c' (for handling 25-39 mm bolts), you must open the **two M10 bolts (2)** [1]. This is referenced in Section 4.15: *Gripping cylinder*, page 25 [1].
*   **Swinging the jaws into the cassette:** The specific directional valve coil used to swing the gripper jaws back into the cassette is **coil (Y70)** [2]. This is referenced in Section 4.8: *Gripper jaws closed and jaws into cassette*, page 19 [2].

According to the manual, the step-by-step hydraulic sequence for swinging the jaws into the cassette is as follows:
1. Push the control lever **(S77)** to the left and into the 11 o'clock position [2]. 
2. The directional valve **coil (Y70)** receives control voltage, which moves the directional valve spool to position 1 [2].
3. Hydraulic oil flows from the variable displacement pump through port **(P)** to the directional valve [2].
4. The oil continues through the pilot-controlled non-return valve to the flow-control valve, and then through port **(B2)** to the piston rod side of the cylinder [2].
5. The return flow from the piston side of the cylinder travels through the flow-control valve and the pilot-controlled non-return valve, and ultimately passes through port **(T)** to the hydraulic oil tank [2].

questions.question: If drill-rod rotation pressure exceeds the anti-jamming sensitivity threshold of 80-120 bar as monitored by pressure switch (14), what specific coil activates on the feed directional control valve (7) to reverse the feed movement?
questions.answer:
Based on the "DS411 Drilling and bolting hydraulics" manual (Section 4.2.5: *Anti-jamming automatics*, pages 32-33, and Section 5.1.5: *Anti-jamming automatics pressure control*, page 52), if the drill-rod rotation pressure exceeds the anti-jamming sensitivity threshold of **80-120 bar**, **coil Y4** activates on the **feed directional control valve (7)** [1, 2]. 

The step-by-step sequence for this automated reverse movement is as follows:

1. The control system monitors the rotation-circuit pressure via the **rotation pressure switch (14)** (ensuring the anti-jamming selector switch **S79** is in the "on" position) [3].
2. If the drill bit hits a fissure and rotation becomes difficult, the pressure in the rotation circuit rises. If this pressure exceeds the adjusted anti-jamming threshold of **80-120 bar** and remains higher than this value for longer than the defined detection time (factory setting: **0.8 seconds**), the system initiates the anti-jamming automatics [1, 2].
3. **Coil Y4** of the **feed directional control valve (7)** receives the signal to activate, which moves the spool to **position 1** [1].
4. The feed direction immediately changes, and the rock drill moves backward to clear the jam [1].
5. Once the pressure drops back under the adjusted threshold, the feed will wait **0.5 seconds** before moving forward again, utilizing half percussion and half feed pressures for the next **4 seconds** before returning to full percussion and feed pressures [2].

questions.question: When moving the front stinger out via control lever S77 and directional valve coil Y152, what specific pressure limit is set by the pressure-reducing valve, and what is the N2 gas pre-charge pressure required for the stabilizing pressure accumulator?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Hydraulic bolting head" manual (Section 4.2 / 4.3: *Stabilizer out/in*, page 16), the specific pressure limit set by the pressure-reducing valve is **50 bar**, and the stabilizing pressure accumulator requires an N2 gas pre-charge pressure of **35 bar** [1].

The step-by-step sequence for moving the front stinger out is as follows:

1. Push the control lever **(S77)** forward and press the push-button at the end of the control lever at the same time [1]. 
2. The directional valve **coil (Y152)** receives control voltage and moves the directional valve spool to position 2 [1].

6. The return oil finally flows through the directional valve to the hydraulic oil tank [1]. 

During this operation, the pressure accumulator (pre-charged with **35 bar** of N2 gas) stabilizes the system's hydraulic pressure to ensure the front stinger remains in firm contact with the rock wall [1].

questions.question: When tramming the drill rig downhill, which specific gear must always be selected, and what is the strict maximum speed limit allowed (in km/h) if the rig must be moved with the booms separated?

questions.question: In the NC7 carrier steering and braking circuits, which specific components within the double pressure relief valve (261) limit the pressure of gear pump (251) to 220 bar and gear pump (252) to 200 bar?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Steering and braking system TC7-TC12, NC7" manual, the specific components within the **double pressure relief valve (261)** that limit the pressure of the gear pumps are as follows:

*   **Pressure relief valve (.01)** limits the pressure of **gear pump (251)** to **220 bar**. Gear pump 251 feeds oil to the steering circuit and carrier circuit [1].
*   **Pressure relief valve (.02)** limits the pressure of **gear pump (252)** to **200 bar**. Gear pump 252 feeds oil to the service and parking brake circuits [1].

These component specifications and limits are detailed in Section 2.1.1: *Double pressure relief valve (261)* (page 9) and Section 3.1.1: *Components for NC7* (page 22) of the manual [1, 2].

questions.question: In order to operate the utility boom from the operator station, what specific key switch ID on the tramming panel must be utilized, and what exact position must it be turned to?
questions.answer:
To operate the utility boom from the operator station, you must utilize the **key switch (S3)** located on the tramming panel [1-3]. This key switch must be turned to position **B ("Control from the operator station")** [1-3]. 

According to the Operator's Manual (Section 4.4.3: *Controlling the utility boom from the operator station*, pages 232–233), the step-by-step sequence to activate and use these controls is as follows:

1. Move the **key switch (S3)** on the tramming panel to the **"Control from the operator station"** position [3]. *(Note: The jacks operate only when the key switch is turned to this position [1, 2])*
2. Press the **utility boom selector button (SH703)** in the operator station until its indicator light lights up [4].
3. Operate the utility boom using the **joystick (S705)** [3, 4]. 

To deactivate the control when finished, press and hold the **utility boom selector button (SH703)** for approximately two seconds until its indicator light goes off [4].

questions.question: How can an operator visually identify the layout and status of backbone components like the DBI or B336G?
questions.answer: Operators can view the main backbone bus and its directly connected nodes, including the DBI (display module) and B336G (carrier inclination sensor), using the System Node Map screen [2]. The map displays green indicators when these components are functioning normally, and red or gray if there is a fault or connection issue [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components control the bolt feeding speed and maximum pressure during the bolting process?
questions.answer: The bolt feeding speed forward is adjusted by the flow control valve (21), and the bolt feeding speed backward is regulated by the flow control valve (22) [11-13]. The maximum bolt feeding pressure is adjusted by the pressure reducing and relieving valve (62) [6, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the proper procedure if an electrical fuse burns or a circuit breaker trips?
questions.answer: A breaker tripping or fuse burning indicates an underlying electrical failure that must be repaired before you attempt to reset the breaker or replace the fuse [4]. Always use the original equipment manufacturer's fuse size and type, and never replace a fuse with one that has a higher ampere value than the original [4]. When resetting protective switches to position I (ON), you must first turn the main switch to the 0 (OFF) position if the drill rig is connected to the power supply network [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What CAN bus module provides the data for diagnosing a "Major SW-version conflict" or checking hardware revisions?
questions.answer: Diagnostics for software and hardware revisions of modules like the FSC, BSC, and B336G (carrier inclination sensor) are tracked and displayed on the Error List and Service Log screens, which log the operational status and any conflicts between these intelligent network nodes [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where the hydraulic power pack will not start?
questions.answer: Start by checking the **indicator panel for any alarms** and verify the **connection of the power supply and main switch** [2]. You must also ensure **all emergency stop devices are reset**, check that neither the **water pump nor the compressor is currently running**, and ensure that **none of the circuit breakers on the main switchgear cabinet door have tripped** [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a network data error diagnosed on the engine's J1939 CAN bus?
questions.answer: A network data error is diagnosed by the presence of Cummins fault code 5941 (J1939 SPN 520968, FMI 19), which indicates a machine constrained operation due to network data received in error [10, 11]. This specifically means that the received J1939 data-link message was not valid [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the electrical troubleshooting steps if the diesel engine fails to start?
questions.answer: Ensure the battery isolation switch (S1) is turned to the ON position and check the condition of the 24 VDC batteries [2], [3]. Verify that the automatic fuse on the main switchgear cabinet doors and the fuses on the JB10 box have not tripped [2]. Additionally, ensure the parking brake is engaged, the drive selector is in the neutral (middle) position, and all emergency stop devices have been successfully reset [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the engine stop indicator light (H41) signify, and how should the operator react?
questions.answer: The H41 indicator lights up due to critical engine malfunctions, such as excessive engine speed, low oil pressure, low oil level, or excessively high coolant temperature [9]. The operator must observe the light's behavior to determine the required response: continuous red and yellow means stop the engine immediately, blinking yellow means stop within 30 seconds, and blinking yellow and red means stop within 10 seconds [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the key pressure settings for the variable displacement pump and the main system?
questions.answer: The system's **main pressure relief valve** must be adjusted to **245 bar** [3, 4]. The variable displacement pump is regulated by two controllers: the **pressure controller** is set to a maximum pressure of **220 bar**, while the **flow controller** (which dictates the standby or idle-running pressure) is set to **30 bar** [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical checks should be performed if the hydraulic power pack will not start?
questions.answer: First, check the indicator panel for any active alarms [1]. Check the connection of the power supply and ensure the main switch is turned on [1]. Ensure that all emergency stop devices have been reset, and verify that neither the water pump nor the compressor is currently running [1]. Finally, check that none of the circuit breakers on the main switchgear cabinet door have tripped [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for quickly calibrating the boom's linear sensors?
questions.answer: To perform a quick calibration of the boom's linear movements, open the Quick Calibration window on the boom adjustment display and run the desired linear movement to its mechanical rear position [9], [10]. Once in position, press the "Set" button for that movement, which will reset the sensor value to zero and display "Done" next to the button [9], [10]. Press the "Accept" button to finalize the calibration [9], [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure to get further troubleshooting details if a unit shows a red or gray indicator on the CAN bus map?
questions.answer: You should navigate to the **Error List screen**. If a unit has a red or gray indicator on the node map, its status is also logged in the error list, which provides the Time of the alarm, a non-language-specific Code, and an Error description that gives more detailed instructions on how the operator can rectify the problem or continue despite it [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the phase sequence fault (H603) warning, and what happens when it activates?
questions.answer: When the main switch is turned on, a relay (K120) checks the three-phase current to ensure the correct direction of rotation [14, 15]. If the direction of rotation (phase sequence) is incorrect, the H603 indicator light comes on and the system prevents the electric motors from starting [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a fault where all boom hydraulic functions are slow or not working at all?
questions.answer: Check if the hydraulic oil level is too low or the oil viscosity is too high. Inspect the hydraulic circuit, hoses, and connections for leaks. Check the main pressure relief valve at the pressure control block by observing the boom working pressure on the percussion pressure gauge to ensure the required 220 bar working pressure is reached [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the rotation pressure relief valve (30) adjusted, and what is its target value?
questions.answer: The rotation pressure relief valve (30) limits the maximum rotation pressure and should be adjusted to 150 bar [6], [7]. To adjust it, move the rock drill against the rear stopper, stop the power pack, close the rotation flow control valve (13), and disconnect/plug the rotation hoses at the hose support [8], [7]. Restart the power pack, move the rotation lever (S73) to the right, and adjust the pressure relief valve (30) until the pressure gauge (41) shows 150 bar [7]. Tighten the lock nut, stop the power pack, and reconnect the hoses [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the feed system does not work properly?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The hydraulic feed does not work [7].
*   **Cause 1:** The feed proportional pressure relief valve (55) or feed control valve (7) is clogged or failing to receive control voltage [7, 8].
*   **Corrective Action 1:** Check the control voltage to the valves [7, 8]. Feed the rock drill against the limits in the manual position and check for pressure on the feed pressure gauge (40) [7, 8]. Clean, repair, or change the clogged valve [7, 8].
*   **Cause 2:** The feed potentiometer (R70) is in the wrong position [8].
*   **Corrective Action 2:** Check and adjust the potentiometer position [8].
*   **Cause 3:** The feed flow control valves (8) or (9) have a leak or are clogged, or the feed pressure reducing/relieving valve (61) is leaking or incorrectly adjusted [9].
*   **Corrective Action 3:** Clean, repair, or change the flow control valves, and verify the correct adjustment of the pressure reducing/relieving valve (61) [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical issues should be investigated if the power pack stops unexpectedly during operation?
questions.answer: You should check the **indicator panel for alarms**, verify that **none of the circuit breakers on the main switchgear cabinet door have tripped**, ensure **all emergency stop devices have been reset**, and make sure that the **pilot circuit is fully functional** [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the main pressure relief valve (23) and the hydraulic filters (5 and 45)?
questions.answer: The main pressure relief valve (23) adjusts the maximum pressure for the variable displacement pump (1) [11, 15]. For filtration, the system utilizes a pressure filter (5) with a 20 µm absolute capacity to filter pressure in the variable displacement pump circuit, and a return filter (45) with a 10 µm absolute capacity to filter the return oil flow of both pumps before it enters the hydraulic oil tank (49) [1, 6, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot incorrect percussion pressure settings during operation?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rapid drill bit wear, shortened rock drill life, and an increased risk of drill rod sticking [4].
*   **Cause:** Too high percussion pressure setting for the given rock conditions [4].
*   **Corrective Action:** Decrease the percussion pressure [4, 5].
*   **Symptom:** Decreased penetration rate (especially in soft rock) [5].
*   **Cause:** Too low percussion pressure [5].
*   **Corrective Action:** Increase the percussion pressure to an optimal level using the percussion pressure adjustment potentiometer (R121) [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific sensors are connected to the CAN bus via the BSC module?
questions.answer: The BSC module serves as a connection node on the backbone bus for several boom-related sensors, specifically the B101G (Boom extension sensor), the B26G (Boom lift sensor), and the B20G (Boom swing sensor) [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the drill rod does not rotate freely or rotates unevenly?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The drill rod does not rotate freely or has uneven rotation [10, 15].
*   **Cause 1:** Poor alignment or incorrect clearances [15].
*   **Corrective Action 1:** Check the alignment of the drill rod and verify the centralizer wear piece clearances [15].
*   **Cause 2:** Too low rotation speed setting [10].
*   **Corrective Action 2:** Increase the rotation speed to prevent uneven rotation, decreased penetration rates, and higher stresses on the rotation mechanism [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Where can an operator find detailed diagnostic information for a CAN bus unit that displays a red or gray indicator?
questions.answer: The operator should check the Error List screen, which logs the status of these units and provides the time of the alarm, a non-language-specific code, and an error description with further instructions to rectify the problem [2-4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary functions of the variable displacement pump (1) and the gear pump (2) in the drilling hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The variable displacement pump (1) delivers oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulics circuits, and constantly adjusts itself to maintain an output-line pressure higher than the load-sensing line pressure [1, 2]. The gear pump (2) is a fixed displacement pump that delivers oil to the rotation circuit and functions as a feed pump for the system [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the rock drill percussion does not function or the percussion pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Install a pressure gauge in the LS port of the pressure relief block and feed the rock drill against the rear limit with maximum power [4]. If the pressure in the LS port does not rise to the defined value, the LS line orifice (24) is likely clogged or the proportional pressure relief valve (27) spool is jammed [4]. Remove the cap and clean the orifice (24) by drilling, or clean/repair the proportional pressure relief valve (27) [5]. Additionally, check if the system's main pressure relief valve (23) is leaking by installing a flow meter, or verify if the percussion main valve (6) is jammed despite receiving correct control voltage [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct pre-charge pressures for the brake accumulators and how are they filled?
questions.answer: The brake accumulators must be pre-charged with nitrogen gas (N2) to 65 bar for TC8/NC7 series carriers, 80 bar for TC9-12 series carriers, or 100 bar for NC4 carriers [11], [12]. To fill them, first completely release the hydraulic oil pressure from the brake accumulators [13], [14], [15]. Remove the accumulator cap, install the elbow adapter to the filling valve, and push the quick coupling sleeve onto the stem [14], [16]. Open the locking nut, the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve, and slowly adjust the pressure regulating valve until the gauge indicates the correct pressure [14], [16]. Close the locking nut, remove the adapters, and tighten the locking nut to 20 Nm [17], [18]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the diesel engine fails to start?
questions.answer: You should verify that the **battery isolation switch is in the ON position**, the **parking brake is engaged**, and the **drive selector is in the middle position** [1]. Additionally, check that the **automatic fuse on the main switchgear cabinet doors and fuses on the JB10 box have not tripped**, ensure the **batteries are in good condition**, and make sure all **emergency stop devices have been reset** [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot and resolve issues where the rotation does not function?
questions.answer: Check the rotation flow control valve (13) and rotation directional control valve (12) for clogs or electrical faults; clean, repair, or change them if necessary [10]. If the rotation pressure relief valve (30) is dirty, stuck, or incorrectly adjusted, it must be cleaned or changed [11]. To correctly adjust the rotation pressure relief valve (30), lock the drill rod or the shank, start the power pack, engage the drill rotation, and adjust the valve to 150 bar [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration size requirements for the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The hydraulic system utilizes both pressure and return flow filtering. The **pressure filter** has a filtering capacity of **20 µm absolute** [9]. The **return oil filter** has a capacity of **10 µm absolute** (or 12 µm as noted in general specs) [10, 11]. Additionally, the hydraulic oil tank is equipped with an **air filter** with a filtering capacity of **5 µm** to ensure the air entering the tank is clean [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you quickly check the overall status of the CAN bus and locate faulty objects?
questions.answer: You can check the CAN bus status by opening the **System Node Map screen**, which is accessed via the Diagnostics menu from the main menu [1, 2]. This screen displays the backbone bus nodes, and you can use the Tooltip function on the screen to get additional information regarding specific objects or components [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the rock drill percussion does not function or the percussion pressure is too low?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion does not function or the percussion pressure is too low [1].
*   **Cause 1:** The load-sensing (LS) line orifice (24) is clogged or the proportional pressure relief valve (27) spool is jammed [1].
*   **Corrective Action 1:** Install a pressure gauge in the LS port of the pressure relief block and feed the rock drill against the rear limit at maximum power [1]. If the pressure doesn't rise, remove the cap from the orifice (24) and clean it by drilling. If the orifice is clear, clean, repair, or change the proportional pressure relief valve (27) [2].
*   **Cause 2:** The system's main pressure relief valve (23) is leaking [2].
*   **Corrective Action 2:** Install a flow meter in the variable displacement pump's (1) pressure line and block the pressure line from the rock drill [2]. Turn the percussion on; if the flow meter indicates a flow of several liters, the valve (23) is leaking and must be cleaned, repaired, or changed [2, 3].
*   **Cause 3:** The main percussion valve (6) is jammed or has an electrical fault [3].
*   **Corrective Action 3:** Check for the correct control voltage. If the voltage and pressure (on gauge 39) are correct but it fails to operate, the valve (6) is jammed and must be cleaned, repaired, or changed [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the main switch (Q100) and the battery isolation switch (S1) in the electrical system?
questions.answer: The main switch (Q100) cuts off the power supply to the drill rig and can be locked in the '0' position [1-4]. However, it does not switch off the voltage from the cable reel or the slip rings without a pilot system, and the carrier's accumulator circuit remains on [1-4]. The battery isolation switch (S1) turns on and off the current from the carrier's battery to the drill rig's electric circuit [5, 6]. Even if S1 is opened, if the main switch (Q100) is ON, the main electric system will continue to feed voltage to the carrier's systems [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a malfunctioning hydraulic feed diagnosed?
questions.answer: Check the control voltage to the feed proportional pressure relief valve (55) and the feed control valve (7). Feed the rock drill against the limits in the manual position and check the feed pressure gauge (40) to see if these valves are clogged [8, 9]. Additionally, verify the position of the feed potentiometer (R70) and inspect the feed flow control valves (8) and (9) for clogs or leaks [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the component identified as B336G on the CAN bus network?
questions.answer: The B336G is the carrier inclination sensor, which monitors and provides data on the drill rig carrier's inclination in both the longitudinal and transverse directions [1-3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the proper diagnostic and repair procedure if an electrical fuse burns or a circuit breaker trips?
questions.answer: Fuses and circuit breakers protect wires and components against overheating and fire in case of overload and short circuits [4, 5]. A tripped breaker or blown fuse is a sign of an underlying failure that must be repaired before you attempt to reset the breaker or replace the fuse [4, 5]. Always use the original equipment manufacturer's fuse size and type, and never use a replacement with a higher ampere value [4, 5]. When resetting protective switches to position I (ON), you must first turn the main switch to the 0 (OFF) position if the drill rig is connected to the power supply network [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you test and troubleshoot the fault current protector switch (VYK device)?
questions.answer: Press the TEST button to check the operation of the fault current protector switch [6]. If the VYK device's fault current protection functions correctly, you can reset it by turning the main switch first to the OFF position and then back to the ON position [6]. If the earth leakage control does not switch the power off during the test, the control system is malfunctioning and must be repaired or replaced by a qualified electrician before any connected devices are started [7], [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps if the rock drill rotation does not function?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation does not function [14].
*   **Cause 1:** The rotation flow control valve (13) is faulty or clogged [14].
*   **Corrective Action 1:** Clean, repair, or change the valve [14].
*   **Cause 2:** The rotation directional control valve (12) has an electrical fault or is clogged [14].
*   **Corrective Action 2:** Check the control voltage input. If voltage is correct and pressure gauge (41) shows the correct pressure, clean, repair, or change the valve (12) [14].
*   **Cause 3:** The rotation pressure relief valve (30) is dirty, stuck, or incorrectly adjusted [15].
*   **Corrective Action 3:** Clean, repair, or change the valve [15]. To properly adjust it, lock the drill rod or shank, start the power pack, engage drill rotation, and adjust the valve to 150 bar [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the main pressure relief valve (23) and what is its correct setpoint?
questions.answer: The main pressure relief valve (23) must be adjusted to a target pressure of 245 bar [1]. To adjust it, first loosen the locking nut of the main pressure relief valve and rotate its adjusting screw (1) almost fully counterclockwise (open) [1]. Start the diesel engine, select boom movements with the selector switch (S78), and run the zoom inward by pulling the joystick (S77) backward while simultaneously pushing its button [1]. With the zoom held, rotate the adjusting screw clockwise until the pressure gauge (39) reads 245 bar, and then tighten the locking nut [1], [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components regulate the hydraulic feed speed and feed pressure during drilling?
questions.answer: The feed circuit pressure is adjusted by the proportional pressure relief valve (55) or the proportional pressure reducing and relieving valve (11) [5-7]. The maximum feed speed forward is adjusted by the flow control valve (8), while the return movement speed backward is adjusted by the flow control valve (9) [5, 7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the hydraulic power pack's main contactor clicks but the power pack fails to start?
questions.answer: A clicking main contactor indicates that the supplied electrical power is too low [1]. To diagnose this, check the supply voltage using the voltmeter located on the main switchgear cabinet door [1]. The voltage must remain within the specified acceptable range during engine idling, starting of the power packs, and while drilling at full power [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What CAN bus communication fault is diagnosed if the engine throws fault code 5939?
questions.answer: Fault code 5939 diagnoses an abnormal update rate on the J1939 data link, meaning that no communication or an invalid data transfer rate has been detected between the Engine Control Module (ECM) and the machine's electronic control unit [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the rock drill's percussion initiated, and which main component controls this action?
questions.answer: Percussion is controlled by the percussion main valve (6) [5]. When percussion is started, coil Y1 of the percussion main valve (6) activates and moves the spool, allowing oil from the variable displacement pump (1) to flow through the pressure compensator (59) to the main valve, and then into the percussion mechanism (32) [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which CAN bus fault code indicates a multiplexing timeout error on the primary vehicle network?
questions.answer: Cummins fault code 285 (J1939 SPN 639, FMI 9) is triggered for an SAE J1939 Multiplexing PGN Timeout Error [12, 13]. This indicates an abnormal update rate on the J1939 Network #1, which is the Primary Vehicle Network [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined circuit pressures for drilling and bolting functions?
questions.answer:
The drilling and bolting circuit pressures are adjusted to the following values:
*   **Percussion pressure:** Full percussion is set to **180 bar for the RD314 rock drill** (or 175 bar for the HL510), and half percussion is set to **120 bar** [4]. 
*   **Feed pressure:** The maximum forward drilling feed pressure is **140 bar** [5]. 
*   **Return movement pressure:** The maximum pressure for the return movement is **160 bar** [5].
*   **Rotation pressure:** The maximum pressure is limited by a relief valve to **150 bar** [6].
*   **Anti-jamming sensitivity pressure:** This is set between **80 and 120 bar** [5].
*   **Bolt rotation (tightening) pressure:** This is adjusted based on the bolt type; for example, it is **170 bar for M24 threads** (approx. 380 Nm) or 175 bar for approx. 420 Nm [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the "Hydraulic oil too hot" (H610) warning light to illuminate, and what is the required response?
questions.answer: The H610 indicator light comes on when the hydraulic oil temperature exceeds 75 °C, which automatically causes the power pack, compressor, and water pumps to stop [1, 2]. The operator should allow the oil to cool down, and the light will go off automatically once the temperature has dropped sufficiently [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where the variable displacement pump rotates normally, but the idle-run pressure is not at the required 30 bar?
questions.answer: Install a pressure gauge into the LS port of the drilling-control block and let the power pack idle. If the pressure is between 0 to 6 bar, check or adjust flow controller A (47). If there is over 6 bar of pressure in the LS port during free circulation, the directional valves (25) or (63) may be jammed or incorrectly receiving control voltage [2-4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What CAN bus communication fault is diagnosed if the engine throws Cummins fault code 5939?
questions.answer: Cummins fault code 5939 (J1939 SPN 520968, FMI 9) diagnoses an abnormal update rate on the machine's network [8, 9]. This means that no communication or an invalid data transfer rate has been detected on the J1939 data link between the Engine Control Module (ECM) and the machine's electronic control unit [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific sensors are connected to the CAN bus via the FSC module?
questions.answer: The FSC module links feed-related sensors to the main network, including the B18G (Roll-over sensor), the B130G (Feed swing sensor), and the B132G (Feed tilt sensor) [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the remote switch (S10) and the engine stop override button (S17)?
questions.answer: The remote switch (S10) is located on the tramming panel and is used to immediately cut off all power to the carrier and the pilot circuit, which causes the main power to turn off [7, 12-15]. The engine stop override button (S17) is used to bypass diesel engine stops caused by the engine's control units (such as for low oil pressure or low coolant level) or by the automatic fire extinguishing system [16, 17]. This button should only be used in emergency situations when the drill rig must be moved [16, 17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical faults should be checked if the water pump does not start?
questions.answer: You should check if there is **no current**, if the **water pump switch at the electric cabinet is in position 0**, or if the **control voltage circuit is faulty** [3]. Additionally, check if the **motor protector switch has triggered**, which can be caused by **faulty contact points, a loose or faulty cable connection, or a faulty motor winding** [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be suspected if an actuator displays a gray indicator on the System Node Map screen?
questions.answer: A gray indicator suggests that the actuator may be **de-energized** due to a power supply malfunction, or the physical CAN bus communication line to that component has become **interrupted** [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Why does the power pack's main contactor click when the power pack is started, and how can this be resolved?
questions.answer: The main contactor will click if the supplied electrical power is too low [1]. You should check the supply voltage using the voltmeter located on the main switchgear cabinet door [1]. Ensure that the voltage remains within the specified acceptable range during engine idling, starting of the power packs, and while drilling at full power [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose if the CAN bus traffic load is too high?
questions.answer: You can check the bus traffic load percentage on the System Node Map screen; if the load exceeds 35%, the value is displayed in red, indicating that the bus load is too high [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the potential causes and procedures to follow if the hydraulic feed does not work?
questions.answer: Check if the feed proportional pressure relief valve (55) or the feed control valve (7) is clogged by feeding the rock drill against the limits in the manual position and checking for pressure on the feed pressure gauge (40) [7, 8]. Clean, repair, or change these valves if they are clogged [7, 8]. Also, verify that the feed potentiometer (R70) is not in the wrong position, and inspect the feed flow control valves (8) and (9) or the feed pressure reducing/relieving valve (61) for leaks or clogs [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the half percussion pressure adjusted?
questions.answer: The half percussion pressure is adjusted via the NN-R121 resistor and should be set to 100 bar [22]. To perform this, turn the feed into the downward position and pull the joystick (S75) backward to the 6 o'clock (half percussion) position [22]. Use the adjusting screw on the NN-R121 resistor to set the pressure to 100 bar while monitoring the reading on the percussion pressure gauge (39) [22]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the feed backward pressure reducing/relieving valve (61)?
questions.answer: The feed backward pressure reducing/relieving valve (61) controls the maximum pressure of the return movement and is set to 160 bar [19], [20]. Loosen the locking nut and turn the adjustment screw almost entirely counterclockwise [20]. Turn on the power pack and use the manual controls to move the rock drill backward against the movement stop limit [20]. While holding the movement against the stop, turn the adjusting screw clockwise to begin the movement, and continue turning it clockwise until the pressure gauge reaches 160 bar before locking the adjusting screw [20], [21]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it mean if the power pack's main contactor clicks upon starting, and how is it diagnosed?
questions.answer: A clicking main contactor indicates that the **supplied electrical power is too low** [2]. You can diagnose this by checking the **supply voltage using the voltmeter located on the main switchgear cabinet door**; the voltage must remain within the specified acceptable range during engine idling, starting, and drilling [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical faults or warnings do the indicator lights H612, H610, and H624 on the indicator panel (QN) signify?
questions.answer:
**H612 (Powerpack motor overload):** Illuminates if the motor's circuit breaker (F100) or electronic motor protector relay (F101) triggers, or if the motor's thermal protection detects temperatures exceeding 110 °C [24, 25].
*   **H610 (Hydraulic oil too hot):** Illuminates when the hydraulic oil temperature exceeds 75 °C, which automatically forces the powerpack, compressor, and water pumps to stop [26, 27].
*   **H624 (External pump overflow):** Illuminates when the external pump's circuit breaker (F290) or electronic motor protector relay (F291) has triggered, which also stops the power pack, compressor, and water pumps [28, 29]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the electrical system track operating hours and supply voltage, and what are the specific gauge component IDs?
questions.answer: The system utilizes several specific gauges on the switchgear doors to track operating times and voltage. The supply voltage is monitored by the supply voltage meter (P410) [8-11]. Operating hours for the compressor are tracked by the compressor hour meter (P400) [8-11]. Powerpack operating times are tracked by hour meters 1P101, 2P101, and 3P101 (depending on the number of booms) [8-11]. Rock drill percussion times are tracked by hour meters 1P100, 2P100, and 3P100 [8-11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: During CAN bus troubleshooting, what does a red indicator for an actuator signify on the System Node Map?
questions.answer: A red indicator signifies that the actuator has been successfully detected on the CAN bus, but it currently has an **internal fault condition** or it has not been started by the control system [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the maximum pressure and speed of the drill rotation adjusted in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The maximum pressure of the rotation circuit is limited to 150 bar by the pressure relief valve (30) located in the pressure control block [11, 14]. The rotation speed is adjusted by the rotation flow control valve (13), which is pressure-compensated to ensure the rotation speed remains constant regardless of the load [5, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical faults should be investigated if the water pump does not start?
questions.answer: If the water pump fails to start, check if there is no electrical current, if the water pump switch at the electric cabinet is in the 0 position, or if the control voltage circuit is faulty [2]. Additionally, verify if the motor protector switch has triggered; this can be caused by faulty contact points, a loose or faulty cable connection, a faulty motor winding, or a mechanically blocked pump [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose stiff or sticking steering in the carrier's hydraulic system?
questions.answer: Check the relief valve and adjust or replace it if necessary. Test for steering cylinder seal leaks by operating the steering several times to see if the cylinder abnormally heats up [14]. If the steering is sticking or unsteady, bleed air from the system by driving the steering to extreme positions a few times, and check the steering valve and steering column bearing for wear [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Why does the variable displacement pump rotate normally, but the idle-run pressure differs from the normal value of 30 bar?
questions.answer: The flow controller A (47) may need adjustment. To adjust it, loosen the flow controller A (47) adjusting screw almost entirely (counterclockwise), wait for the pressure reading to even out, and then adjust the idle-running pressure to 30 bar by turning it clockwise [1, 2]. If adjusting this does not help, clean or change the flow controller unit [3]. If there is over 6 bar of pressure in the drilling-control block port LS during free circulation, the directional valves (25) or (63) may be jammed or receiving control voltage, and should be cleaned, repaired, or replaced [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the maximum permissible degree of contamination for the hydraulic fluid?
questions.answer: The system requires a highly clean fluid environment to prevent premature component failure. The maximum permissible degree of contamination is **cleanliness class 18/16/13** according to the **ISO 4406 (c)** standard [12, 13]. Furthermore, the recommended maximum water content for the hydraulic oils is **<500 ppm** [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be inspected if the drill rotation does not function?
questions.answer: Check the rotation flow control valve (13) for clogs. Verify the control voltage input and pressure gauge (41) reading for the rotation directional control valve (12) [11]. Also, check if the rotation pressure relief valve (30) is dirty, stuck, or incorrectly adjusted (it should be adjusted to 150 bar) [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What triggers the "Powerpack motor overload" (H612) alarm, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: The H612 light illuminates if the motor's circuit breaker (F100) or electronic motor protector relay (F101) triggers, or if the thermal protection system detects a motor temperature exceeding 110 °C [5, 6]. The operator must manually reset the circuit breaker by moving its control switch to 0 and then back to 1, or reset the electronic relay by pressing the "Reset" button (S300) located in the MP-switchgear door [5, 6]. The thermal protection resets automatically once the motor cools down [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the proper pressure settings and adjustment steps for the variable displacement pump?
questions.answer: The variable displacement pump (1) requires a maximum pressure setting of 220 bar and an idle-running pressure of 30 bar [3], [4]. To perform the adjustment, loosen the pressure regulator B (48) screw almost entirely counterclockwise, and tighten the flow controller A (47) screw clockwise [3]. Start the power pack, check the percussion-pressure gauge (39), and turn the pressure regulator B (48) adjusting screw clockwise until the gauge shows 220 bar [3]. Next, loosen the flow controller A (47) adjusting screw almost entirely counterclockwise, wait for the pressure to even out, and then turn it clockwise until the idle-running pressure reaches 30 bar [3], [5]. Lock both adjusting screws once the values are set [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the capacities and flow rates of the main hydraulic pumps?
questions.answer:
The hydraulic power pack features multiple pumps with the following capacities:
*   **Variable displacement pump** (for percussion, feed, boom, and bolting head movements): **140 l/min / 160 bar** [1].
*   **Gear pump** (for rotation): **65 l/min / 140 bar** [1].
*   **Gear pump** (optional, for air conditioning): **37 l/min / 150 bar** [1].
During normal drilling operation, the expected oil consumption is **105 to 115 l/min for percussion** and **4 to 8 l/min for the feed** [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the variable displacement pump does not operate or rotates slowly?
questions.answer: Check whether the pump or other power-pack components emit abnormal sounds. Measure the electric motor to ensure it has adequate input voltage; if it does, inspect the electric motor, clutch component, pump-drive shaft, and the pump itself for faults [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are faulty actuators or nodes visually diagnosed on the CAN bus network?
questions.answer: On the System Node Map, a red indicator signifies that an actuator has an internal fault or hasn't been started by the control system, while a gray indicator suggests the actuator is de-energized due to a power supply malfunction or the CAN bus communication line is interrupted [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the rock drill percussion does not function or the percussion pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Install a pressure gauge in the LS port of the pressure relief block and feed the rock drill against the rear limit at maximum power. If pressure does not rise, the LS line orifice (24) is likely clogged or the proportional pressure relief valve (27) is jammed [5]. You can also install a flow meter in the pressure line of the pump to check if the main pressure relief valve (23) is leaking, and verify that the percussion main valve (6) is receiving control voltage and is not jammed [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the "Water pressure low" (H601) indicator to activate, and what actions must the operator take?
questions.answer: The H601 light turns on if the water pressure remains below 2.8 bar for more than four seconds, which automatically stops the drilling functions [7, 8]. If the pressure remains below 2.8 bar for over a minute, the system will also stop the water pump [7, 8]. The operator should press the acknowledgment button (S505) to turn off the light and continue drilling, or if the pump has stopped, restart it manually using the S501 switch [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the H602 indicator light signify regarding oil levels, and how should the operator respond?
questions.answer: If the H602 light is steadily illuminated, the hydraulic receiver oil level has dropped below the allowed minimum, causing the power pack, compressor, and water pumps to stop [3, 4]. If the indicator light blinks, it means the shank lubrication unit (SLU) oil level is too low [3, 4]. To respond, the operator must add a sufficient amount of oil and reset the control system by pushing the S505 acknowledgment button [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components should be inspected if percussion and feed work normally, but the return movement does not function?
questions.answer: The fault is likely in valves (7), (8), (9), (11), or (61) [12]. Check the control-voltage input to the feed control valve (7); if the voltage is correct, one of these valves may be clogged and needs to be cleaned, repaired, or changed [12]. Also, ensure the maximum pressure of the return movement is properly adjusted with the pressure reducing/relieving valve (61) to the parameter of 160 bar [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What functions do the circuit breakers F450, F451.1-F451.6, and F452.1-F452.5 serve in the main switchgear?
questions.answer: The circuit breaker F450 protects the internal 24 V control voltage within the main switchgear [18-21]. The circuit breakers F451.1 through F451.6 are designated to protect the control system, instruments, and the carrier [19, 21-23]. The circuit breakers F452.1 through F452.5 protect the lighting circuits and the jacks control system [19, 21-23]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot issues related to abnormal feed force during drilling?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Sticking rotation (rotation pressure fluctuates), bending of the drill rod, increased wear on centralizers/chuck, or abnormal clinking sounds from the rock drill jumping [10, 11].
*   **Cause:** Incorrect feed force (either too high causing sticking/bending, or too low causing the drill to jump and lose contact) [10, 11].
*   **Corrective Action:** Adjust the feed force using the feed-power potentiometer (R70) to match the rock hardness and percussion pressure [10-13]. Ensure constant progressive movement without shaking and without dropping penetration rates [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it indicate if the bus traffic load value is displayed in red on the System Node Map screen?
questions.answer: If the bus traffic load percentage is displayed in red, it indicates that the CAN bus load is too high, specifically exceeding the parameter of **35%** [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings are provided for clogged hydraulic filters, and how do they affect operations?
questions.answer: The "Powerpack pressure filter clogged" (H611) and "Return oil filter clogged" (H607) indicator lights illuminate when the respective filters are so dirty they need to be replaced [10-13]. This warning does not stop drilling functions, allowing the operator to finish the task [10-13]. Note that when the oil is cold (below 30 °C), this monitoring system is bypassed to prevent false alarms caused by thick oil [10-13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS411 Technical Manual)

questions.question: If you measure a CAN bus impedance of ~40 kΩ between CAN_HI and CAN_LO on an interrupted side branch, what does this indicate about the state of the node connection during the measurement compared to an infinite impedance reading?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Control System DS412i" manual, measuring an impedance of ~40 kΩ versus an infinite reading on an interrupted CAN bus side branch indicates the following about the node's connection state:

*   **~40 kΩ Impedance:** Indicates that the node is **connected** to the bus during the measurement (referenced as **Node C** in the troubleshooting diagram) [1, 2]. 
*   **Infinite Impedance:** Indicates that the node is **disconnected** from the interrupted side branch during the measurement (referenced as **Node B** in the troubleshooting diagram) [1, 2].

**Measurement Procedure:**
According to Section 8.5.1 ("CAN bus troubleshooting by measuring resistance", Pages 103-105), this diagnostic logic applies to both **CAN_LO side branch interruptions** and **CAN_HI side branch interruptions** [1-3]. The step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. Ensure the measurement is carried out with the power disconnected [3].
2. Turn the battery main switch **S1** to position **0** [3].
3. Ensure the CAN bus cable connection diagrams are at hand [3].
4. Measure the bus impedance between the **CAN_HI** and **CAN_LO** lines on the interrupted side branch [1, 2].
5. Observe the reading:
