   * If the node is connected to the bus, it will read approximately **40 kΩ** [1, 2].
   * If the node is disconnected during measurement, it will yield an **infinite** impedance reading [1, 2].

questions.question: When adjusting the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8) at measuring connector MPB with the boom zoom run backwards, why must you use valve 10.15 to ensure the pressure never exceeds 205 bar during the adjustment, and what is the absolute maximum pressure allowed to the brake accumulators at measuring connector MCR?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.7.7 of the Carrier manual ("Adjusting brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)"), valve **10.15** (the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve) must be used during the adjustment of valve **10.8** because turning the adjusting screw of valve 10.8 fully clockwise can cause the pressure to spike [1, 2]. If the pressure at measuring connector **MPB** tends to exceed **205 bar**, valve 10.15 is used to reduce the pressure so that the adjusting screw of valve 10.8 can safely be turned fully closed without damaging the system [1, 2]. 

The absolute maximum pressure level allowed to the brake accumulators, which is measured at connector **MCR**, is **210 bar** and must never be exceeded [2, 3].

**Step-by-Step Adjustment Sequence:**
1. Unplug the electrical connectors of the brake circuit retarder control valve (**10.16/Y344**) and the carrier functions pressurization control valve (**10.18/Y167**) [4].
2. Connect the electrical connector **Y167** to the solenoid of the valve **10.16**, leaving the connector **Y344** unplugged [4].
3. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MPB** and another 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring connector **MCR** [1].
4. Loosen the locking nuts from both the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (**10.8**) and the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (**10.15**) [1].
5. Start the diesel engine [1].
6. Run the boom zoom function backwards to activate electrical connector **Y167** [1]. Run the function until the adjustment of the pressure relief valves (**10.8** and **10.15**) are locked [1].
7. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm [1].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.8**) fully clockwise but simultaneously strictly observe that the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MPB** does not exceed **205 bars** [1, 2]. If the pressure tends to exceed 205 bars, use the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (**10.15**) to reduce the pressure to be able to turn the adjusting screw of valve (**10.8**) fully closed [2].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.15**) until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MCR** is **210 bars** [2].
10. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.8**) counterclockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MPB** drops to **200 bars** [3].
11. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.8**) [3].
12. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.15**) until the reading in the pressure gauge connected to **MCR** is **160 bars** [3].
13. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.15**) [3].
14. Release the boom zoom function [3].
15. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle and shut down the engine after idling [3, 5].
16. Remove the pressure gauges from the measuring connectors **MPB** and **MCR** [5].
17. Unplug the electrical connector **Y167** from the valve (**10.16**) and return the electrical connectors back to their original positions - connector **Y344** to valve (**10.16**) and connector **Y167** to valve (**10.18**) [5].

questions.question: While diagnosing an incorrect feed speed, you connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block and read a normal pilot pressure of 35 bar. If the feed pilot control valves (20.20 and 20.21) test perfectly fine, what specific component inside the drilling control valve block must be extracted and checked next?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics" manual, Section 6.9 ("Feed / fast feed speed is not correct") on pages 66-67, if the pilot pressure at line X is normal (30-45 bar) and the feed pilot control valves (20.20 and 20.21) are functioning properly, the next specific component that must be extracted and checked is the **feed valve main spool (20.16)** [1-3].

Here is the step-by-step sequence to extract and check it:
1. Remove the pilot control block from the drilling control valve block (20) [3].
2. Extract the **feed valve main spool (20.16)** [3].
3. Check the condition and movements of the main spool [3]. If the main spool is found to be faulty, you must replace the entire drilling control valve block (20) [3]. 
4. Install the main spool and the pilot control block carefully back to the drilling control valve block [3]. 

*(Note: If these steps do not remedy the situation, the manual indicates that the feed cylinder may be damaged or some other mechanical fault on the feed may be preventing the movements [4])*

questions.question: You are calibrating the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2). After verifying the flow controller (A) maintains a 23 bar pressure difference, what specific adjustments must be made to pressure controller (B) while running the rock drill rotation against a plug to achieve the target pressure of 200 bar?
questions.answer:
To achieve the target pressure of **200 bar** for the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (**2**), you must adjust the pressure controller (**B**) by following the procedure outlined in Section 5.1.4 ("Adjusting the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2)", Pages 51-52) of the Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics manual [1, 2]. 

Here is the specific step-by-step sequence:
1. Remove the protecting cap from the **pressure controller (B)** and loosen the locking nut on its adjusting screw [1].
2. Open the adjusting screw of the **pressure controller (B)** fully open by turning it counterclockwise [1].
3. Run the rock drill rotation against the plug and read the **pump (2)** pressure from the pressure gauge connected to the **check valve block** [2].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the **pressure controller (B)** very carefully clockwise while running the rock drill rotation toward the plug until the pressure gauge shows the correct pressure value of **200 bar** [1, 2].
5. Release the rock drill rotation function [2].
6. Lock the adjustment of the **pressure controller (B)** with the locking nut [3].
7. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure setting again by running the rock drill rotation toward the plug to verify it holds the correct pressure [3].

questions.question: You are diagnosing an emergency stop circuit fault using the LEDs on the NST-2004 relay. If the Ub (supply) LED is ON, the K1 LED is ON, but the K2 LED is OFF, which specific terminals should you investigate for the error, and which relay contact is potentially welded?
questions.answer:
When diagnosing an emergency stop circuit fault on the **NST-2004** relay, if the **Ub** (supply) LED is ON, the **K1** LED is ON, and the **K2** LED is OFF, you should investigate terminals **T14**, **T21**, and **T22** for the error [1]. 

According to Section 4.3 ("Emergency stop relay", Pages 55-56) of the Electric System DS412i manual, this specific LED combination indicates that relay K1 is activated while relay K2 is deactivated [1, 2]. This means that the **K1** relay contact is potentially welded or defective [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) at measuring connector MPS, what specific diesel engine rpm must be applied to achieve the correct 220 bar setting?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.7.4 ("Adjusting steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9)") on page 81 of the Carrier manual, you must shortly apply the **maximum diesel engine rpm** to achieve the correct 220 bar setting [1-3]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for the adjustment procedure:

1. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MPS** [1].
2. Loosen the locking nut from the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (**10.9**) and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise until it is fully open [1].
3. Start the diesel engine [1].
4. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position to pressurize the carrier hydraulics [1].
5. Apply shortly the **maximum diesel engine rpm** [1].
6. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.9**) clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge is **220 bars** [1, 2].
7. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.9**) [2].
8. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle [2].
9. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the down position [2]. Check from the pressure gauge that the pressure level drops to the free circulation level (less than 30 bars) [2].
10. Shut down the engine [2].
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **MPS** [2].

questions.question: When adjusting the water hose reel brake valve (24) via measuring point (23), what is the target braking pressure range for a standard rig, and what is the specific pressure requirement for the DU422i-W model?
questions.answer:
Based on the component manuals, when adjusting the water hose reel brake valve (24) via measuring point (23), the target braking pressure range for a standard rig is **20 to 30 bar** [1]. For the DU422i-W model, the specific pressure requirement is **35 bar** [1]. 

According to Section 6.1 ("Adjusting the water hose reel brake valve"), you must follow this step-by-step sequence to perform the adjustment [1, 2]:

1. Start the diesel engine [2].
2. Connect the pressure gauge to the measuring point (**23**) of the water hose reel brake valve (**24**) [2].
3. Loosen the locking nut (**25**) of the water hose reel brake valve [2].
4. Activate the "reeling out the water hose" function and read the braking pressure from the pressure gauge [1, 2].
5. Turn the adjusting screw (**26**) clockwise/counterclockwise to adjust the braking pressure to the appropriate target (**20-30 bar**, or **35 bar** for the DU422i-W) [1]. 
*(Note: When the correct pressure is set, you should be able to reel out the water hose slowly by hand, and the braking pressure should stop the water hose reel rotation when tramming stops [1]).*
6. Tighten the locking nut (**25**) [1].
7. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring point (**23**) [1].

questions.question: What specific pressure difference must be maintained by the flow controller (A) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1), and what is the target value for the pressure controller (B) when operating an RD314 rock drill?
questions.answer:
The flow controller (**A**) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) must maintain a pressure difference of **30 bar** (pump operating pressure minus LS-line pressure) [1, 2]. When operating an RD314 rock drill, the target pressure value for the pressure controller (**B**) is **235 bar** [2, 3].

According to Section 5.1.2 ("Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)"), you must follow these specific step-by-step sequences if adjustments are required:

**Adjusting the pressure controller (B) [3-5]:**
1. Remove the protecting cap from the pressure controller (**B**) and loosen the locking nut on its adjusting screw.
2. Open the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (**B**) fully open by turning it counterclockwise.
3. Run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and read the pressure from the pressure gauge on the pressure filter measuring point.
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (**B**) very carefully clockwise while running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the pressure gauge shows the correct pressure value of **235 bar**. *(Note: Avoid raising the pressure above the correct value. If it rises too high, loosen the adjusting screw and wait for the reading on the pressure gauge to stabilize, as the pressure drop can be very slow)*.
5. Release the boom zoom function.
6. Tighten the locking nut of the pressure controller (**B**) adjusting screw.
7. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure setting again by running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper.

**Adjusting the flow controller (A) [5, 6]:**
1. Remove the protecting cap from the flow controller (**A**) and loosen the locking nut on its adjusting screw.
2. Open the adjusting screw of the flow controller (**A**) almost fully open by turning it counterclockwise.
3. Read the pressure difference (pump operating pressure minus LS-line pressure) from the pump (**1**) two pressure gauges.
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (**A**) very carefully clockwise until the pressure difference is **30 bar**. *(Note: Avoid a pressure difference of more than 30 bar. If the pressure rises too high, loosen the adjusting screw and wait for the reading on the pressure gauge on the pump (1) pressure filter to stabilize)*.
5. Tighten the locking nut of the flow controller (**A**) adjusting screw.
6. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure difference again.

questions.question: During the nitrogen filling procedure for the brake accumulators, what specific pressure must be set using the pressure regulating valve (11), and what is the required tightening torque for the filling valve locking nut (2)?
questions.answer:
During the nitrogen filling procedure for the brake accumulators, the pressure must be set to **65 bar**, and the required tightening torque for the filling valve locking nut (2) is **20 Nm** [1, 2]. 

*(Note: In the brake accumulator diagrams and instructions, the pressure regulating valve is designated as component **8**, not 11 [3, 4]. Component 11 refers to the pressure regulating valve in the separate rock drill accumulator instructions [5, 6]).*

According to Section 6.1.7 of the Carrier manual (Pages 104-105) and Section 5.7.7 of the Maintenance manual (Pages 236-238) regarding "Filling the gas pre-charge pressure for the brake accumulators", you must follow this complete step-by-step sequence:

1. Release the oil pressure from the brake accumulators according to the "Releasing the oil pressure from the brake accumulators" instructions [4, 7, 8].
2. Remove the cap (3) [7, 8].
3. Install the elbow adapter (10) to the filling valve (1) [7, 8].
4. Push the quick coupling sleeve (5) onto the stem (4) [7, 8].
5. Open the locking nut (2) [7, 8].
6. Turn the knob (8) to open the pressure regulating valve [7, 8].
7. Turn the knob (9) to open the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve [7, 8]. The gauge (7) indicates the pressure in the bottle [7, 8].
8. Turn the knob (8) to adjust the regulating valve pressure slowly to **65 bar** [1, 2, 8]. The gauge (6) indicates the pressure in the accumulator [1, 2].
9. Close the locking nut (2) [1, 2].
10. Turn the knob (9) to close the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve [1, 2].
11. Turn the knob (8) to open the pressure regulating valve [1, 2].
12. Disconnect the quick coupling stem (4) and sleeve (5) [1, 2].
13. Remove the elbow adapter (10) from the filling valve (1) [1, 2].
14. Tighten the locking nut (2) to a torque of **20 Nm** [1, 2].
15. Reinstall the cap (3) [1, 2].
16. After filling the pressure accumulators, check the brakes [1, 2]. Engage the parking brake, select neutral gear, start the diesel engine and let it run for at least three minutes [2, 9, 10]. Shut down the engine, then press the brake pedal all the way down at least five times and make sure the brake pressure stays over **65 bar** (check front/rear charge pressure values from tramming display) [9, 10].

questions.question: To achieve the correct air-mist flushing pressure during adjustment, what specific pressure reading must be achieved on the GUI before tightening the locking nut (1) of the restrictor valve adjusting screw (3)?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 9.4 ("Adjusting the restrictor valve") of the Flushing circuit DS412i manual, you must achieve a specific pressure reading of **4 bars** on the GUI before tightening the locking nut (**1**).

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for adjusting the restrictor valve (**2**):

1. Loosen the locking nut (**1**) of the restrictor valve (**2**).
2. Turn the adjusting screw (**3**) fully open.
3. On the GUI, navigate to **-> Troubleshooting -> Shank Lubrication**.
4. Start the power pack.
5. Push the button (**4**) to activate air flushing.
6. Tighten the adjusting screw (**3**) until the **Air pressure reading rises to 4 bars**.
7. Tighten the locking nut (**1**) of the restrictor valve.
8. Check the Air pressure reading again from the GUI. If the reading has changed from the correct value of **4 bars**:
   * a) Loosen the locking nut (**1**).
   * b) Tighten or loosen the adjusting screw (**3**) until the value is exactly **4 bars**.
   * c) Tighten the locking nut (**1**).
9. Push the button (**4**) to deactivate air flushing.
10. Stop the power pack [1, 2].

questions.question: What are the specific maximum boom lifting/lowering and swing angles (A and B) for the right-handed hydraulic SBR60i boom, and what is its total weight?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 3.2 ("Technical data") of the Hydraulic SBR60i boom manual, the specifications for the right-handed boom are as follows:

*   **Total weight:** 2920 kg [1].
*   **Boom lifting/lowering angles:** A: 55°, B: 25° [2].
*   **Boom swing angles:** A: 45°, B: 45° [2].

questions.question: What are the defined fuel tank capacities for the Cummins QSB 4.5 (Tier3/Tier4F) engine compared to the Cummins QSB 6.7 (Tier4F) on the C900DH carrier?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Filling capacities" tables provided in the Carrier, Maintenance, and Operator's manuals (Section 7.2 and Section 6.10), the defined fuel tank capacities for these specific engine configurations are as follows:

*   **Cummins QSB 4.5 (Tier3/Tier4F):** The defined capacity is **100 / 155 L** [1, 2]. 
*   **Cummins QSB 6.7 (Tier4F) on the C900DH carrier:** The defined capacity is **410 L** [1, 2].

For both of these engine configurations, the recommended fuel specification is **EN 590 Thermoshell Winter 1202** [1, 2].

questions.question: What is the specified hydraulic oil tank volume, and what are the required filtration sizes in microns for the pressure and return filters?
questions.answer:
The specified hydraulic oil tank volumes vary depending on the specific rig and carrier configuration. Based on the "Filling capacities" tables, the defined volumes are:

*   **Tramming (NC5):** 55 L [1, 2]
*   **Carrier (C300):** 145 L [3, 4]
*   **Drilling (NC5):** 200 L [5, 6]
*   **Drilling TC8 (DS rigs):** 210 L [7, 8]
*   **Carrier (C400, C900):** 270 L [9, 10]
*   **Drilling (TC8 and NC7-series):** 290 L [11, 12]
*   **Drilling (TC9):** 380 L [11, 12]
*   **Drilling (TC11–TC12):** 470 L [13, 14]
*   **Drilling (C1000):** 480 L [15, 16]

The required filtration sizes for the hydraulic system filters are as follows:
*   **Pressure filter (Component 8 / element 8.2):** The required filtration size is **20 µm abs** (microns) [17, 18]. 
*   **Return oil filter (Component 4.3 / element 4.3.2):** The required filtration size is **10 µm abs** (microns) [18-20].

**Procedure for Changing the Hydraulic Oil (and refilling the tank):**
When replacing the oil to meet these specified capacities, the following step-by-step sequence must be used to prevent contamination and component failure [21, 22]:
1. Position the rig on a level surface [21].
2. Retract all hydraulic cylinders and set the boom(s) to a tramming position [21].
3. Carefully clean the top of the hydraulic oil receiver so that any dirt does not get into the receiver [21].
4. Remove the receiver breather [21].
5. Empty the oil receiver into a receptacle using the drain valve [22].
6. Remove the service hatch at the top of the receiver to facilitate cleaning the receiver internally [22].
7. Clean, rinse, and dry the receiver thoroughly. Before filling the receiver, ensure that it is completely free of impurities [22].
8. Use fresh oil and a filter when filling the hydraulic oil receiver [22]. Fill to the specified capacity according to your rig's model and **DO NOT OVERFILL!** [22].

questions.question: When indexing the bolting head to the drilling center, what specific pressure do the relief valves (5.2, 5.3, 6.2, and 6.3) limit the upper and lower indexing circuits to, and which directional valves control the activation of the upper (6.4) and lower (5.4) indexing cylinders?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Hydraulic bolting head (BHi)" manual (Section 3.2.1 "Hydraulics", Page 18), the specifications for indexing the bolting head to the drilling center are as follows:

*   **Pressure Limits:** The relief valves for both the lower indexing circuit (**5.2** and **5.3**) and the upper indexing circuit (**6.2** and **6.3**) each limit the pressure in their respective circuits to **210 bars** [1, 2]. 
*   **Directional Valves:**
    *   The activation and direction of the **lower indexing cylinder (5.4)** are controlled by the **directional valve Y76 (5.1)** [1].
    *   The activation and direction of the **upper indexing cylinder (6.4)** are controlled by the **directional valve Y74 (6.1)** [2].

questions.question: According to the system parameters under Drill and Bolt Feed, what are the distinct default maximum movement pressures defined for "Bolt feed movement pressure" compared to "Drill feed movement pressure"?
questions.answer:
According to the "Drill and Bolt Feed" system parameters, which can be accessed via the Boom Work Settings menu, the distinct default maximum movement pressures are defined as follows:

*   **Bolt feed movement pressure:** 200.00 bar [1, 2]
*   **Drill feed movement pressure:** 180.00 bar [1, 2]

questions.question: When operating the Swellex bolting system, what specific grip pressure range is required to allow the bolt to be moved in and out of the hole, and what is the absolute maximum water pressure that can be obtained from the high-pressure water pump for expansion before the chuck gaskets leak?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, here are the specifics for operating the Swellex bolting system:

**Grip Pressure**
To allow the Swellex bolt to be moved in and out of the hole, the required grip pressure range is **50-100 bar** (Mechanised bolting with Swellex and Excalibur manual, Section 4.3 "Swellex/excalibur bolt feed", Page 14) [1]. 

**Maximum Expansion Water Pressure**
The absolute maximum water pressure obtainable for bolt expansion is **300 bar**. If any of the gaskets inside the swellex chuck (**2**) are faulty and leaking, this desired maximum pressure will not be obtainable. You can read the current pressure on the GUI (Mechanised bolting with Swellex and Excalibur manual, Section 4.1 "Checking the equipment", Page 13) [2].

**Step-by-Step Swellex Bolting Sequence**
According to the Operator's Manual (Section 4.14.11 "Swellex bolting (optional)", Pages 264-265), the complete operation procedure is as follows [3-5]:
1. Choose the bolting mode from the right control panel.
2. Move the bolting head with the swellex tool forward with the right drilling joystick so that it makes contact with the bolt.
3. Push the grip button on the joystick to attach the bolt to the Swellex tool. The bolt is filled with water, and the pressure is set to the grip pressure parameter.
4. Tilt the joystick forward to push the bolt up to the first bolt transfer jaw (the bolt transfer jaws support the bolt before it enters the hole).
5. Open the transfer jaws using the drill steel handling controls.
6. Move the jaws out all the way to the end towards the drill.
7. Push the bolt forward all the way into the hole. *(Note: If the stroke length of the feed is not sufficient, push the rest of the bolt into the hole using the feed extension cylinder).*
8. Push the bolting button on the joystick. The water pressure will increase to the designated expansion pressure parameter, and after that, the water is released from inside the bolt automatically.

questions.question: During bolt handling, which directional valve controls the front jaw actuator (2.4) swinging between the cassette and rotation mechanism, and what specific pressure do relief valves (2.2) and (2.3) limit this swinging circuit to?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Hydraulic bolting head (BHi)" manual (Pages 17-18), the front jaw actuator (**2.4**) swinging between the bolt cassette and the bolt rotation mechanism is controlled by **directional valve Y71 (2.1)** [1, 2].

The pressure for this swinging circuit is limited to **210 bar** by the respective pressure relief valves (**2.2** and **2.3**) [2].

questions.question: In the automated drilling and bolting control system, if the "Jammed bit monitoring" is enabled via the GUI, what specific bypassed sensors will cause this anti-jamming feature to be automatically disabled?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Operator's Manual DS412i - StageV" (Page 330), if the **Jammed bit monitoring** feature is enabled (slider position 1), it will be automatically disabled if either of the following specific sensors are bypassed [1]:

*   **Rotation pressure sensor** (Component 15 / B5P) [1, 2]
*   **Rock drill position sensor** (This anti-jamming monitoring will also be disabled if the rock drill position sensor itself is disabled via the settings) [1]

questions.question: In the steering and brake control manifold (10), what specific pressure are the working port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves (10.6 and 10.7) limited to, and how does the load sensing pressure interact with the priority valve's (10.10) 10-bar spring to ensure steering functions are prioritized?
questions.answer:
In the steering and brake control manifold (10), the working port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves (**10.6** and **10.7**) are both limited to a maximum pressure of **190 bar** [1]. Valve 10.6 limits the pressure for port A (steering to the right), while valve 10.7 limits the pressure for port B (steering to the left) [1].

During steering operations, the pressure in the load sensing (LS) line reaches the spring chamber of the steering circuit priority valve (**10.10**), causing it to close proportionally to the pressure level [2, 3]. The load sensing line pressure, working together with the priority valve's internal **10-bar spring**, ensures that the steering function is always prioritized above the other functions [2, 3]. 

These specifications are detailed in the Carrier manual in Section 4.3.1 ("Components (steering system)", Page 30) [1] and Section 4.6.3 ("Operation of steering circuit", Pages 62 and 66) [2, 3].

questions.question: If a control system malfunction prevents the use of control panel CP2 for operating the front and rear hydraulic jacks, what specific manual override procedure must be performed using the carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud (inside the left side box) and the valve Y168 stud before operating valves Y140, Y142, Y144, and Y146?
questions.answer:
If a control system malfunction prevents the use of control panel CP2, the following manual override sequence must be performed (detailed in the Maintenance Manual, Pages 386-389, and Operator's Manual, Pages 382-384) [1-6]. 

*(Note: Skip step 2 if the diesel engine is running, and skip steps 1 and 5 if the power pack is running) [1, 7].*

**Preparatory Override Sequence:**
1. **Pressurize the carrier hydraulics:** Push the carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud (located inside the left side box) and turn it **clockwise** to release the stud to the **UP** position [7, 8].
2. **Activate valve Y168:** Locate valve **Y168** in the rear carrier control block. Push the stud (**Y168**) with a pin or similar tool to activate the valve. **You must keep the stud pushed down during the entire override procedure** [7, 8].
3. **Lift the steps (required for front jacks only):** Before overriding the front jacks, you must remove the split pin (1) and the safety pin (2) to lift the steps (3) [2, 5]. When the steps (3) are in the upper position, put the safety pin (2) back and secure it with the split pin (1) [2, 5].

**Operating the Jack Valves:**
While keeping the **Y168** stud pushed down, refer to the following movement directions and press the specific directional valve studs with a pin or similar tool [2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10]:

*   **Front Left Jack:** Press **Y142A** to deliver oil to port B1 (lifts jack) or **Y142B** to deliver oil to port A1 (lowers jack) [2, 5].
*   **Front Right Jack:** Press **Y140A** to deliver oil to port B2 (lifts jack) or **Y140B** to deliver oil to port A2 (lowers jack) [9, 10].
*   **Rear Left Jack:** Press **Y146A** to deliver oil to port B3 (lifts jack) or **Y146B** to deliver oil to port A3 (lowers jack) [3, 6].
*   **Rear Right Jack:** Press **Y144A** to deliver oil to port B4 (lifts jack) or **Y144B** to deliver oil to port A4 (lowers jack) [3, 6].

**Completion:**
5. **De-pressurize the system:** Once the override procedure is finished, push the carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud and turn it **counterclockwise** to lock the stud securely to the **DOWN** position [3, 6].

questions.question: If the feed force drops unexpectedly, how do the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.22) and the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) interact to throttle the main feed line flow, and what are the respective setpoint pressures for the feed port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19) when calibrated properly?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics DS412i, DS512i" manual, the interaction between these components and the specific pressure requirements are as follows:

**Interaction to Throttle Feed Flow (Page 38):**
Oil flows to the load sensing (LS) line via the feed main spool (**20.16**) [1]. The pressure in this feed LS-line directly affects the feed line pressure compensator (**20.17**) [1]. The overall level of feed pressure is controlled and limited by the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (**20.22**), which limits the maximum feed LS pressure to 250 bar [1]. When valve **20.22** limits the LS pressure, this pressure drop is sensed by the feed line pressure compensator (**20.17**), which reacts by throttling the oil flow in the main feed line [1]. This throttling action causes the feed pressure, and as a result the feed force, to drop to the desired level [1].

**Setpoint Pressures (Page 39):**
When calibrated properly to protect the actuator ports (A2 and B2) against pressure peaks and external forces, the setpoint pressures are:
*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18):** Limited to a maximum pressure of **200 bar** [2].
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19):** Limited to a maximum pressure of **240 bar** [2].

**Calibration Sequence (Pages 67-68):**
According to Sections 6.10 and 6.11 ("Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" and "Feed / fast feed pressure is too high"), if the shock/anti-cavitation valves (**20.18** and **20.19**) need to be adjusted after replacement, you must follow this step-by-step sequence [3-6]:
1. Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring point **M1** [3, 5].
2. Use the pressure controller (**B**) to adjust the set pressure of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) to **235 bar** [3, 6].
3. Run the feed against the front end stopper and, at the same time, adjust the pressure of the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.18**) to **200 bar** [4, 6].
4. Run the feed against the rear end stopper and, at the same time, adjust the pressure of the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.19**) to **240 bar** [4, 6].
5. Re-adjust the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (**1**) as instructed in the "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" section [4, 6].

questions.question: In the closed-loop hydrostatic transmission system, what specific pressure does the charge pressure relief valve (1.5) maintain to feed oil to the low-pressure circuit, and how is this charge pressure utilized to release the front and rear parking brake cylinders (16.2 and 17.2)?
questions.answer:
Based on the sources provided, the charge pressure relief valve **(1.5)** limits and maintains a maximum pressure of **28 bar** (or 28-32 bar) in the charge pressure circuit [1-3]. While tramming, this charge pressure feeds oil to the closed-loop system's low-pressure circuit through the high-pressure relief valves **(1.8 or 1.9)** [4].

This same charge pressure is utilized to release the front and rear parking brake (spring-applied) cylinders **(16.2 and 17.2)**. According to the "Operation of spring applied brakes" section in the Carrier manual, the step-by-step sequence of this operation is as follows:

1. Oil from the charge pressure circuit, limited to **28 bar** by the charge pressure relief valve **(1.5)**, flows out of port **M3** of the transmission pump **(1)** [3, 5].
2. The oil travels to port **P** of the park brake manifold **(24)** [5].
3. The release of the brakes is controlled by two specific control valves on the manifold: **24.1** for the front axle and **24.2** for the rear axle. When uncontrolled, these valves block the connection to the cylinders, leaving them connected to the tank line and allowing the springs to keep the brakes applied [5].
4. When the control valves **(24.1 and 24.2)** are activated, the oil passes from port **P** through the control valves to ports **A** and **B** [5].
5. **Front Brakes:** From port **A**, oil flows to connections **P1** of the front axle. It enters the piston rod side chambers of the front parking brake cylinders **(16.2)**. The oil pressure pushes against the springs, releasing the front brakes [6].
6. **Rear Brakes:** From port **B**, oil flows to connections **P1** of the rear axle. It enters the piston rod side chambers of the rear parking brake cylinders **(17.2)**. The oil pressure pushes against the springs, releasing the rear brakes [6].

*Note: During this process, pressure sensors **(24.3 and 24.4)** monitor the spring-applied brakes to verify that the release pressure reaches the required **21-35 bar** range, and that the pressure difference between the front and rear axles remains under **5 bar** [6].*

questions.question: When adjusting the steering circuit pilot pressure reducing valve (10.11) at measuring connector MX, what specific pressure gauge capacity is required, what RPM state must the diesel engine be running at during adjustment, and what is the target pressure reading?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.7.5 ("Adjusting steering circuit pilot pressure reducing valve (10.11)") on pages 81-82 of the Carrier manual, the requirements for this adjustment are as follows:

*   **Pressure Gauge Capacity:** A **40 bar** pressure gauge must be attached to the measuring connector **MX** [1].
*   **Engine RPM State:** The adjustment procedure requires the **maximum diesel engine rpm** to be applied [2, 3].
*   **Target Pressure Reading:** The adjusting screw must be turned until the pressure gauge reads exactly **35 bars** [3].

**Step-by-Step Adjustment Sequence:**
According to the manual, the specific procedure is [1, 3]:
1. Replace the plug in measuring connection **MX** with the measuring connector G1/4 - M16x2.
2. Attach a 40 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MX**.
3. Loosen the locking nut of the pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (**10.11**) and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise until it is fully open.
4. Start the diesel engine.
5. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position to pressurize the carrier hydraulics.
6. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm.
7. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.11**) clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge is **35 bars**.
8. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.11**).
9. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle and shut down the engine after idling.
10. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the down position.
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **MX**.

questions.question: How is the steering circuit main pressure relief valve adjusted, and what is its setpoint?
questions.answer: The **steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9)** is set to **220 bar** [1]. To adjust it, connect a 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring connector **MPS** [2]. With the engine off, loosen the locking nut and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise fully open [2]. Start the engine, pressurize the carrier hydraulics using the pressurizing stud, and apply maximum engine rpm [2]. Turn the adjusting screw clockwise until the gauge reads **220 bar**, then tighten the locking nut, return the engine to idle, and de-pressurize the hydraulics [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are used for the main graphical user interfaces (GUIs) in the cabin?
questions.answer: The Drilling GUI (DG) utilizes a **CCpilot XM2**, which is a PC-based onboard display computer featuring an Intel Atom 1.6 GHz processor and a 12" or 15" TFT LED backlight touch screen. The Tramming GUI (VG) utilizes an **EPEC 6107**, which is a PanelPC equipped with a 7" LCD resistive color touch display. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps are required when the rotation speed adjustment is failing?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation speed adjustment does not work as desired, or the drill rod RPM fluctuates (is not constant) [16].
*   **Cause:** The pilot pressure is too low due to a blocked pilot oil filter (20.26) or a faulty reducing valve (20.27) [17]. Alternatively, there is a fault in the rotation pilot control valves (20.4, 20.5), a stuck rotation valve main spool (20.1), a mechanically damaged rotation line pressure compensator (20.2), or a damaged rock drill rotation mechanism [16, 18, 19].
*   **Corrective Action:** Connect a gauge to line X to verify pilot pressure is 30-45 bar; clean or replace the pilot filter and reducing valve if it is low [17]. If pilot pressure is correct, remove and inspect the rotation pilot control valves, the rotation valve main spool, and the pressure compensator [18, 19]. Replace faulty components (or the whole drilling control valve block if the main spool or compensator are mechanically damaged) [19, 20]. Finally, inspect the rock drill rotation motor itself [20, 21]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where all boom hydraulic functions are slow or not working at all?
questions.answer: You should first check if the hydraulic oil level is too low or if the oil viscosity is too high [1]. Next, inspect the hydraulic circuit hoses and connections for leaks [1]. Finally, check the boom working pressure from the percussion pressure gauge to ensure the main pressure relief valve at the pressure control block is functioning correctly and reaching the required 220 bar working pressure [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you locate a specific interruption point on the CAN bus using a termination resistor?
questions.answer: First, disconnect both termination resistors from the bus and measure each separately to ensure they read **120 Ω** [3]. If the resistors are intact, the fault is likely in the bus itself [3]. To locate the fault, move one termination resistor towards the next measuring point, which can be any node or actuator on the bus [3]. Disconnect the bus cable from the actuator and connect the termination resistor in its place [3]. By testing the resistance node by node, you can systematically isolate the exact location of the interruption [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the fault codes on the FPVC or VCH module's 7-segment display indicate during CAN bus troubleshooting?
questions.answer: After the initial boot sequence, the display repeatedly flashes a sequence of diagnostic information showing the **node ID**, the **network management state** (Pr = pre-operational, oP = operational, st = stopped), any **communication errors** (Co), and the **I/O fault status** for specific pins [3-5]. The pin fault status uses letter codes: **'s'** for short circuit to ground, **'o'** for open circuit, and **'b'** for short circuit to battery [4, 5]. For example, the sequence "24 - oP - J6 - 5s" indicates node 24 is operational, but connector J6, pin 5 is short-circuited to ground [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the yellow and red warning lights on the fire suppression system's electronic alarm/timer box indicate, and what happens when they activate?
questions.answer: The yellow warning light indicates low tank pressure, which occurs when the pressure falls below the 900 kPa factory setting of the double pressure switch [9-12]. The red warning light indicates a system fault or discharge [10, 12]. Activation of these switches triggers an audiovisual alarm, and as pressure drops, a 6-second engine shutdown delay timer begins [10, 12]. The operator can push the delay extension button using the key-operated override for an additional 20 seconds before the engine automatically shuts down [10, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What type of component is used for the physical control panel keypads (CP) that interface with the CAN system?
questions.answer: The system uses the **Grayhill 3K keypad** for the various control panels (such as CP1, CP2, CP3, and the Cement Mixer Panel) [17], [26]. These keypads operate on an 8...32 V voltage, are vibration and impact resistant, and connect to the system using a 4-pin Deutsch DT connector [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you resolve excessively high percussion pressure?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion pressure is too high despite normal operation of electrical systems and sensors [9].
*   **Cause:** The electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) is stuck, or the LS-line orifices (20.12 or 20.13) have loosened or disconnected [9, 10].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack [9]. Check, clean, and if necessary, replace the proportional pressure relief valve (20.14) [9]. If the issue persists, verify that both LS-line orifices (20.12 and 20.13) are properly seated in the drilling control valve block and carefully tighten them if they have loosened [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if a hydraulic boom is creeping?
questions.answer: Boom creeping is diagnosed by checking for a leaking overcenter valve on the boom swing or lift cylinder, which could be caused by a broken O-ring or worn seat surfaces [2]. If the valve is not damaged, check for dirt in the hydraulic circuit that requires flushing, or air trapped in the cylinder that requires bleeding [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What module functions as the Mains Controller (MC) and the Resin Controller (ARI)?
questions.answer: The **FPVC (Fast Proportional Valve Controller)** module is used for these functions. It is a powerful I/O-module with internal FPGA support for intensive local computing power, utilizing a 72 MHz ARM7 32-bit processor. Its architecture is designed to meet SIL2 class safety requirements for rough environments. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the optional articulation locking valve (13)?
questions.answer: The articulation locking valve (13) makes the articulation joint stiffer by blocking the connection between the steering valve port A and the steering cylinders [7]. The valve is activated and kept active during drilling after the machine has been navigated [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions and specific part numbers of the power pack starter block components F1 and K1?
questions.answer: Component **F1** is the power pack circuit breaker, which provides motor protection with phase failure sensitivity and adjustable overload releases. The part number is **NZMN2ME140NA** for 55 kW motors (DS412i and DS512i) and **NZMN2ME200NA** for 75 kW motors (DS422i). Component **K1** is the power pack motor contactor, which controls the power flow to the motor and uses part number **DILM170(RDC24)**. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component dictates whether the machine operates in drilling or bolting mode?
questions.answer: The drilling/bolting selection valve (21) selects if the drilling or bolting circuit is pressurized [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the central greasing alarm lamp to light up, and what should the operator do?
questions.answer: The central greasing alarm lamp lights up if a divider valve refuses to operate correctly [5, 6]. This can be caused by the reservoir running out of lubricant, a clogged lubricating point, a broken grease supplying pipe, stiff lubricant, or disturbances in the electric circuits [5, 6]. The operator must stop operating the machine and correct the failure immediately [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is an unexpectedly stopping power pack diagnosed?
questions.answer: Look for active alarm messages on the display [2]. Check the MQ cabinet to see if any circuit breakers have tripped [2]. Confirm that all emergency stop buttons are fully released and that the pilot circuit is functional [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the FPVC (Fast Proportional Valve Controller) module, and which specific controllers use it?
questions.answer: The **FPVC module** is a powerful I/O-module with internal FPGA support for intensive local computing power, designed to meet SIL2 class safety requirements for rough environments [9], [10]. It operates as a CANopen slave to read and write hardware I/Os, and is used specifically for the Resin Controller (ARI) and the Mains Controller (MC) [9], [10], [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the setpoints and procedures for adjusting the percussion/feed and rotation variable displacement pumps?
questions.answer: For the **percussion/feed pump (1)**, the flow controller (A) is set to a **30 bar** pressure difference, and the pressure controller (B) is set to **235 bar** (for RD314) [11-13]. To adjust the pressure controller, open the screw fully, run the boom zoom against the rear stopper, and turn the screw clockwise until the pressure filter gauge reads **235 bar**, then lock it [13, 14]. To adjust the flow controller, read the pressure difference between the pump operating pressure and the LS-line, and turn the screw clockwise until it reaches **30 bar** [15, 16]. For the **rotation pump (2)**, the flow controller is set to a **23 bar** difference, and the pressure controller is set to **200 bar**, adjusted while running the rock drill rotation against a plug [17-20]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration specifications for the main pressure and return oil filters?
questions.answer: The pressure filter (8) has a filtering level of 20 µm abs and a maximum operating pressure of 420 bar [4]. It features a clogging indicator that activates at a 5 bar pressure difference, and a by-pass valve that opens at 7 bar [5]. The return oil filter (4.3) has a filtering level of 10 µm abs [6]. Its electrical clogging indicator activates at a 2 bar pressure difference, and its bypass valve opens at 3 bar [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary methods for diagnosing CAN bus faults?
questions.answer: CAN bus faults are initially identified using the instructions and notifications on the operator's display panel, which notifies if nodes are in a fault mode or switched off [1]. Physical troubleshooting is then performed using a multimeter and the rig's electric circuit diagrams to measure the resistances of the termination resistors and the normal operation voltage levels [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning is given if the operator attempts to tram the rig without proper safety precautions inside the cabin?
questions.answer: A buzzer will sound on the tramming panel and a notice pop-up will be displayed on the screen if the seat belt is not fastened and/or the cabin door is not properly closed before tramming [15-17]. The operator must fasten the seat belt and close the door properly to proceed [15-17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the cable reel and water hose reel pressures adjusted for varying operational loads?
questions.answer: The **cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (1)** is adjusted based on the cable size: **50 bar** (25 mm²), **80 bar** (35 mm²), **100 bar** (50 mm²), **140-150 bar** (70-150 mm²), and **180 bar** (185-240 mm²) [28]. The **water hose reel pressure reducing valve (3)** is adjusted to **80 bar** (or 83 bar for DU422i-W) while the system is pressurized [29, 30]. The **cable reel control block** uses brake pressure valves to decelerate rotation: adjust valve (11) to **40 or 70 bar** (depending on cable size) while reeling out at maximum engine rpm, and adjust valve (10) to **20 bar** while reeling out at minimum engine rpm [31-34]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the roles of the percussion selector valve (20.9) and the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25)?
questions.answer: The percussion selector valve (20.9) opens and closes the percussion main valve (20.10) [3]. The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) limits the maximum pressure of the percussion/feed circuit to 270 bar [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning is triggered if there is an issue with the parking brake pressure?
questions.answer: If the pressure difference between the front (B960P) and rear (B961P) brake circuits rises above the factory set limit when the parking brake is released, a notice is displayed on the GUI [26]. The operator should investigate the notice using the system log to assess the seriousness of the error and determine required actions [27, 28]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the difference between a yellow "Notice" and a red "Alarm" pop-up on the control system display, and how should the operator respond to each?
questions.answer: A yellow "Notice" pop-up indicates a medium-level problem that does not require immediate action, but the operator should investigate and correct the reason if the alert persists or repeats [18-21]. A red "Alarm" pop-up indicates a major problem requiring immediate attention to prevent damage [19, 21]. The operator must stop working immediately and resolve the cause of the alarm, as the control system may halt some or all drill rig operations until the issue is corrected [18-21]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the STATUS LED blinking codes on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) indicate?
questions.answer:
The yellow STATUS LED communicates various states and faults: 
*   **Off:** Lubrication and Boost mode are off [12].
*   **Single flash:** Lubrication is allowed, and the user can start Boost [12].
*   **Continuously on:** Boost function is running [12].
*   **Two flashes:** Malfunction in lubrication oil flow (signal from flow sensor not detected) [13].
*   **Three flashes:** Air pressure sensor is broken, disconnected, or the signal is under 2 mA [14].
*   **Four flashes:** Lubrication oil level is low, or the level switch sensor is broken/disconnected (signal under 1.7 mA) [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component functions as the Main Switchgear Sensors (MS) and Tramming Controller (TCP)?
questions.answer: The **VIU (Voltage Input Unit) module** serves as the MS and TCP [14]. It is a general-purpose input unit for user interfaces and applications requiring intensive local computing power [14]. As a CANopen slave, it provides multiple 5 V analog inputs for joysticks and potentiometers, digital inputs/outputs, and CAN interfaces [15], [16], [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you calibrate the gas pre-charge pressure for the brake accumulators?
questions.answer: The brake accumulators require a nitrogen gas pre-charge pressure of **65 bar** [8]. First, completely release the oil pressure from the brake accumulators [8]. Remove the cap and attach a nitrogen bottle to the accumulator's filling valve using a quick coupling and elbow adapter [8]. Turn the pressure regulating valve knob slowly to adjust the pressure to **65 bar**, lock the filling valve nut, and disconnect the equipment [9]. Verify the calibration by running the engine, shutting it down, pressing the brake pedal five times, and ensuring the pressure stays over **65 bar** [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct pressure settings for the main relief valves in the drilling circuits?
questions.answer: The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) limits the maximum pressure of the percussion/feed circuit to 270 bar [9, 12]. The rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) limits the rotation circuit's maximum pressure to 250 bar [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the CAN bus supply conductor voltage to locate a de-energized node?
questions.answer: Keep the control system turned on during this measurement [5]. The voltage between the supply conductor (VS) and ground (GND) should normally be about 24 VDC [5]. If a node is missing power (which can be indicated by an unlit power LED), measure the voltage level between VS and GND one node at a time [5]. A potential interruption point in the supply conductor is detected when the measured voltage drops continuously near 0 V [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a missing or faulty node on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected, measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO, which should be approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω [4]. To check for a de-energized node, turn the system on and measure the voltage between the supply conductor (VS) and ground (GND) [5]. A normal reading is about 24 VDC; if the voltage drops continuously near 0 V at a node, there is a supply interruption [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific module is used for the Boom, Drilling, Rod Handler, Front, Vehicle, End, and Switch Controllers (BC, DC, RC, FC, VC, EC, SC), and what are its features?
questions.answer: These controllers use the **VCH (Valve Controller High Temp)** module. It is a CANopen slave I/O-module featuring separate output powering/cutoff circuitry designed for SIL2/PLd systems. It provides 12 analog inputs, 12 digital on/off I/Os, 27 multifunction I/Os (which can act as PWM outputs, digital inputs/outputs, or counters), and 2 CAN interfaces. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What triggers a shank lubrication control valve alarm during drilling, and what is the system's response?
questions.answer: If the control valve (CT1) shut-off ball is left open or closed for four operational cycles, deviating from normal operation, an alarm is switched on [13]. The operator receives an error message, and the control system automatically stops the drilling after a delay [13, 14]. The alarm resets when pumping returns to normal [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose CAN bus faults by measuring total resistance?
questions.answer: With the power disconnected (ensure the battery main switch S1 is in position 0), measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO [3, 4]. A reading of approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω indicates the bus cables, connectors, and termination resistors are intact [4]. A result of < 50 Ω indicates a short-circuit [4]. A reading > 100 Ω means one end of the bus is interrupted or a termination resistor is faulty [4]. A reading of ~40...50 kΩ means the bus is interrupted at at least two points, or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a side branch interruption?
questions.answer: For either a CAN_LO or CAN_HI side branch interruption, you must measure the bus impedance. The impedance will be infinite when measured between CAN_HI and CAN_LO with the node disconnected [10, 11]. If the node is connected to the bus during the measurement, the impedance will measure approximately 40 kΩ [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What procedures should be followed if the feed or fast feed speed is incorrect?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block to check the pilot pressure, which should be 30-45 bar [8]. If it deviates, check, clean, and potentially replace the pilot oil filter (20.26) and pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27) [9]. If the pilot pressure is correct, the fault may be the feed valve main spool (20.16) or the feed pilot control valves (20.20) and/or (20.21), which should be removed, checked, and replaced if necessary, making sure to apply a tightening torque of 10 Nm [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What alarms indicate that the compressor is overheating, and how does the system respond?
questions.answer: If the compressor oil temperature reaches 105 ºC, the system provides a notice pop-up [7]. If the temperature continues to rise and reaches 115 ºC, an alarm pop-up is displayed on the control system and the compressor automatically stops [7]. The operator should visually check the condition and fastening of the cooling air fan, and ensure it can rotate freely [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a problem where the variable displacement pumps do not rotate at all or their speed is abnormal?
questions.answer: Begin by checking the troubleshooting views from the control system and measuring the supply voltage to the power pack [3]. If the electric motor is receiving the correct voltage, the fault is likely mechanical, and you must inspect for mechanical damage preventing the pumps from rotating [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the NST-2004 component in the electrical system?
questions.answer: The **NST-2004** is the emergency stop relay. It operates as a Cat. 4 safety level device with 3 NO duplicated forced output contacts and 2-channel operation with short circuit protection. It monitors the dual emergency stop lines to safely disconnect power and stop all rig movements, hydraulic fluid, water, and pressurized air supply when an emergency stop button is pressed. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the compressor and water pump protected from overload, and what component models are used?
questions.answer: They are protected by motor-protective circuit breakers (**F4** and **F5**) featuring electronic wide-range overload protection that directly disconnects all poles in the event of an overload. An example combination for a 5.5 kW water pump is the **PKE 32** breaker with a **PKE-XTU-12** trip block. The associated contactors (**K4** and **K5**) use part number **DILM32-10(RDC4)** for 5.5 - 11 kW motors, and **DILM65-10(RDC4)** for 18.5 kW motors. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component serves as the Drilling Master (DM1) and Carrier Master (CM1), and what is its function?
questions.answer: The **SCU machine control computer** is used for both the Drilling Master (DM1) and the Carrier Master (CM1) [1], [2]. These act as master nodes in the drilling and carrier control systems, utilizing an 800 MHz Freescale ARM Cortex A8 processor, and feature multiple CAN and Ethernet interfaces to manage system operations and communications [3], [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are used for the main graphical user interfaces (GUIs) that connect to the system?
questions.answer: The Drilling GUI (DG) uses the **CCpilot XM2**, a PC-based onboard display computer with an Intel Atom 1.6 GHz processor and a 12" or 15" TFT touch screen [23]. The Tramming GUI (VG) uses the **EPEC 6107**, a PanelPC with a 7" LCD resistive color touch display and Cortex A9 32-bit processor [24], [25]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the Earth Fault Lockout (EFL) protection relay diagnosed using its LED indicators?
questions.answer: The EFL relay uses several LEDs for diagnostics: a flashing **Status** LED indicates the operating system is healthy, while an ON **Logical** or **Elec** LED means a frozen contactor trip is active [11]. An ON **Undervoltage** LED indicates an undervoltage trip [11]. Finally, if the **EFLO status** LED is ON, an earth fault lockout trip has occurred, and if it flashes, it means the relay is currently charging the phase cables during an EFLO test [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure when the percussion is stuck on continuously?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion remains on constantly whenever the power pack or diesel engine is running [11, 12].
*   **Cause:** The percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck and leaking, which continuously allows pressure to reach the rock drill's percussion mechanism [12]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and/or diesel engine immediately, as running with un-regulated low percussion pressure can severely damage the seals of the rock drill accumulators [12]. Check, clean, and replace the selector valve (20.9) and the 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) as necessary [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you identify the specific type of CAN bus short-circuit?
questions.answer: A short-circuit to ground is identified if CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage is continuously near 0 V while the resistance between them remains ~60 Ω [8]. A short-circuit to supply voltage is identified if CAN_LO or CAN_HI is continuously near the supply voltage (VS) while the resistance remains ~60 Ω [8]. A short-circuit between the CAN wires is identified if the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level is continuously near 0 V [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the optional hydraulic bypass filter (10) and its internal bypass valve (10.2)?
questions.answer: The optional bypass filter (10) filters the hydraulic oil taken from the rotation circuit down to 2µ [4]. Its internal bypass valve (10.2) bypasses the oil flow if the oil is too cold or when the oil filter element becomes blocked [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warning is triggered if the service brake charge pressure drops, and what is the required response?
questions.answer: If the pressure drops below 110 bar, a notice pop-up is shown on the GUI [1]. If the pressure drops further to 75 bar, a warning light turns on, a tramming forced stop is activated, an alarm message is displayed, and the spring-applied brakes engage at zero speed or within a four-second delay [1-4]. The operator must stop and correct the cause of the pressure drop, as the hydrostatic transmission is forced to neutral [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are CAN bus faults diagnosed by measuring voltage levels?
questions.answer: With the control system turned on (battery main switch S1 in position 1), measure the voltage between CAN_HI-GND and CAN_LO-GND [6]. An intact bus will read 2.5 VDC ±0.2 V with no load [6, 7]. When the bus is loaded, CAN_HI should rise above 2.5 VDC and CAN_LO should drop below 2.5 VDC [7]. If the measurement results are < 1 V or > 4 V, it indicates there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot low rotation pressure during drilling?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation pressure is too low during drilling operations, assuming the rotation pump is adjusted correctly and electrical systems are functional [13].
*   **Cause:** There is a leak in the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3), the shuttle valve (20.7), or the electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) [13, 14]. If all valves are intact, the rock drill rotation motor has internal leaks [15].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the system and inspect the main pressure relief valve (20.3), cleaning or replacing it and recalibrating its pressure if needed [13, 14]. Next, check and replace the shuttle valve (20.7) or the proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) [14, 15]. If the pressure remains low, check the rock drill rotation motor and repair or replace it according to the rock drill manuals [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the pilot oil conditioned for the pilot control circuit?
questions.answer: The pilot oil filter (20.26) filters the oil supplied to the pilot control circuit at 160-200 µm [2]. Additionally, the pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27) reduces and limits the pilot oil pressure level to 35-45 bar [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the CAN bus by measuring the total resistance, and what do the expected values indicate?
questions.answer: Ensure the battery main switch (S1) is in position 0 to disconnect power before measuring [1, 2]. Measure the total resistance between **CAN_HI** and **CAN_LO** [2]. If the result is approximately **60 Ω ±5 Ω**, the bus cables, connectors, and both **120 Ω termination resistors** are intact [1, 2]. If the result is **< 50 Ω**, there is a short-circuit on the bus [2]. If it is **> 100 Ω**, one end of the bus is interrupted or a termination resistor is faulty [2]. A reading of **~40...50 kΩ** means the bus is interrupted at at least two points, or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can specific CAN bus cabling short-circuits be identified through voltage and resistance measurements?
questions.answer:
You can identify the type of short-circuit by observing the voltage and resistance behaviors:
*   **Short to ground:** CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage is continuously near **0 V**, but the resistance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI remains **~60 Ω** [6].
*   **Short to supply voltage:** CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage is continuously near the supply voltage (**VS**), but the resistance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI remains **~60 Ω** [6].
*   **Short between CAN wires:** The voltage level for CAN_LO or CAN_HI drops continuously near **0 V** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can a faulty power factor correction capacitor be diagnosed in the electrical system?
questions.answer: Start one power pack at a time and let it idle [15, 16]. Check the power factor value from the electric quality measuring unit (P1) [15, 16]. If the power factor value is **under 0.5** and the individual phase currents differ significantly, the capacitor is likely faulty [15, 16]. A faulty capacitor cannot be repaired and must be replaced as a complete unit [15, 16]. Always ensure there is no residual voltage before touching the capacitor terminals [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the procedures and expected values when measuring the CAN bus voltage level during operation?
questions.answer: The control system must be kept on (turn the battery main switch S1 to position 1) during this measurement [4]. Measure the voltage between **CAN_HI-GND** and **CAN_LO-GND** [4]. With no load, both should read **2.5 VDC ±0.2 V** [4, 5]. When the bus is loaded, the voltage between CAN_HI and GND should rise **above 2.5 VDC**, and the voltage between CAN_LO and GND should drop **below 2.5 VDC** [5]. If your measurements are **< 1 V or > 4 V**, it indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a potential fault in the emergency stop relay (NST-2004) circuit?
questions.answer: Check the LED status of K1 and K2 on the relay [3]. If K1 is activated and K2 is deactivated, there is an error in the emergency stop at T14, T21, T22, or K1 may be welded [3]. If K1 is deactivated and K2 is activated, the error is at T11, T12, or K2 may be welded/defective [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a diesel engine that will not start?
questions.answer: Check the display for possible alarm messages [1]. Verify that the battery isolation switch (S1) and the optional starter isolator switch (S2) are in the ON position [1]. Check that no circuit breakers in the DQ cabinet have tripped and all emergency stop buttons are released [1]. Also, ensure neutral gear is selected, the parking brake is engaged, fuel and battery levels are adequate, there is enough trailing cable on the reel, and the fire suppression system is not inhibiting the start [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the system pressures for the air-mist flushing and mine water inlet calibrated?
questions.answer: To adjust the **air flushing restrictor valve**, loosen its locking nut and open the adjusting screw fully [38]. Start the power pack, activate air flushing from the GUI, and tighten the adjusting screw until the air pressure reading rises to exactly **4 bar**, then lock the nut [38, 39]. To adjust the **mine water inlet pressure**, open the shut-off valve, turn the pressure reducing valve knob fully open, and start the water booster pump [40, 41]. Adjust the knob until the pressure gauge reads between **2-7 bar** (based on conditions), and verify via the GUI that the pressure sensor (B230P) value after the booster pump remains **under 25 bar** [40, 41]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) sensor faults diagnosed?
questions.answer: Observe the STATUS indicator light blinking codes on the SLCU [6]. Three flashes indicate an air pressure sensor malfunction (the sensor is broken or disconnected with a signal < 2 mA) [6]. Four flashes indicate a lubrication oil level switch malfunction (the sensor is broken or disconnected with a signal < 1.7 mA) [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How should you troubleshoot a power pack that stops unexpectedly?
questions.answer: Check the control system display for any active alarm messages [2]. Inspect the MQ cabinet to verify that none of the circuit breakers have tripped [2]. Ensure that all emergency stop buttons have been fully released [2]. Additionally, make sure that the pilot circuit is functional [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the main pressure relief valves for the drilling hydraulics (percussion/feed and rotation) calibrated?
questions.answer: The **percussion/feed main pressure relief valve (20.25)** is set to **270 bar** and the **rotation main pressure relief valve (20.3)** is set to **250 bar** [21-24]. To adjust either, first tighten the relief valve's adjusting screw past its setpoint [21, 25]. Fully open the flow and pressure controllers of the corresponding pump (Pump 1 for percussion, Pump 2 for rotation) [21, 25, 26]. Start the power pack, close the pump's flow controller (putting it in constant pressure mode), and adjust the pump's pressure controller to 10 bar above the target (**280 bar** for percussion, **260 bar** for rotation) [24, 26]. Slowly loosen the main pressure relief valve screw until the valve fizzes and the pressure drops to the target (**270 bar** or **250 bar**), lock the nut, and then re-adjust the pump controllers to their normal operating settings [22, 24, 26, 27]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined pump outputs and flow rates for the hydraulic and water circuits?
questions.answer: For the RD314 rock drill, the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) must deliver a flow rate of 105-115 L/min for percussion and 4-8 L/min for feed at normal operating temperatures [1]. During a hydraulic test run, the percussion pump operates at 30-45 l/min and the rotation pump operates at 15-20 l/min [2]. The water booster pump (24) has a capacity of 100 l/min, requires a minimum inlet pressure of 2 bar, and provides a flushing water pressure of 10-15 bar [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of components F8 and F10 in the electrical system, and what are their part numbers?
questions.answer: Components **F8** and **F10** are transformer protective circuit breakers. **F8** provides protection for the 230/120 VAC power supply system and uses part number **PKZM0-10-T**. **F10** provides protection for the 24 VDC power supply system and uses part number **PKZM0-4-T**. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the alarm beacon under the operator station indicate?
questions.answer: With the tilting cabin option, a warning about the tilting of the operator station is issued via sound and light signals [15-17]. The alarm beacon under the operator station starts to blink and a warning signal sounds immediately after the tilting button is pushed, warning the operator and bystanders before the station begins to move after a delay [15-17]. Personnel must not enter the hazard zone under the tilted operator station [29-31]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration requirements for the HST, pilot, breather, and optional bypass filters?
questions.answer: The HST charge pressure filter (3) has an 8 µm filtering capability; its blocking indicator reacts at a 3.7 bar difference, and the by-pass valve opens at 5.6 bar [8]. The pilot oil filter (20.26) filters oil for the pilot control circuit at 160-200 µm [9]. The hydraulic oil receiver's breather (4.2) filters air at 5 µm and maintains a 0.3 bar overpressure in the tank [10]. The optional bypass filter (10) operates at 2 µm abs with a limited flow of 2.0 l/min; its clogging indicator activates at 2 bar, and the bypass valve opens at 3.5 bar [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pre-charge pressure settings for the rock drill's low and high pressure accumulators?
questions.answer: The **low pressure accumulator (LP)** should be pressurized to **2 - 4 bar**, which optimally represents half of the return line pressure. Overfilling the LP accumulator significantly increases the risk of cavitation [35, 36]. The **high pressure accumulator (HP)** gas pressure must be set relative to the maximum percussion pressure being used, which is determined using a specific calibration graph based on the diaphragm type (stem-type or normal) [36, 37]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps when the diesel engine will not start?
questions.answer: Check the display for possible alarm messages [1]. Make sure that the battery isolation switch (S1) and the optional starter isolator switch (S2) are in the ON position [1]. Check that none of the circuit breakers in the DQ cabinet have tripped, and ensure that all emergency stop buttons are released [1]. Verify that the neutral gear is selected, the parking brake is engaged, the fuel level is sufficient, and the battery condition is adequate [1]. Finally, ensure there is enough trailing cable on the reel before the alarm limit is reached, and verify that the fire suppression system is not preventing the engine from starting [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you read Cummins engine fault codes if the tramming display is unavailable?
questions.answer: You can read the codes via the ECM by entering Diagnostic Mode: turn the 'Diesel engine start/stop' switch (S2) to the ON position with the engine off, and turn the 'Diagnostic/manual regeneration switch' (S22) to position C [7, 8]. The system will automatically blink the active fault codes using the red **'Engine shutdown indicator light'** and the amber **'Check engine warning light'**, with a 2-second pause between each fault code [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the diagnosis if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling?
questions.answer: If the rotation pump is adjusted correctly and electrical systems are fine, check if the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3), the shuttle valve (20.7), or the electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) are leaking [8, 9]. If none of these valves are leaking, check the rock drill rotation motor itself for internal leaks [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the HST charge pressure filter (3)?
questions.answer: The HST charge pressure filter (3) filters the oil delivered by the charge pump (1.2) for the hydrostatic transmission system [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is an incorrect feed or fast feed speed diagnosed in the drilling hydraulic system?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block to verify that the pilot pressure is between 30-45 bar [6]. If the pressure is incorrect, check the pilot oil filter (20.26) and pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27) [6]. If the pilot pressure is correct, the fault is likely a stuck feed valve main spool (20.16) or an issue with the feed pilot control valves (20.20) and/or (20.21) [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are boom and feed sensor signals converted for the CAN bus, and what component handles this?
questions.answer: The **RD (Resolver-to-Digital) module** is used as the Boom Sensors converter (BS), Feed Sensors converter (FS), and for Boom Head Sensing (BHS) [12]. It is a general-purpose measurement unit and CANopen slave designed for high-accuracy applications, providing resolver-to-digital converters, analog inputs, and digital I/Os [12], [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot when the percussion pressure is too low but the electric and control systems are operating properly?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack and check, clean, or replace the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) or the electro proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) [3, 4]. Additionally, check if the LS-line orifices (20.12) or (20.13) are blocked by removing their plugs, extracting them, and cleaning or replacing them [4, 5]. Check the output of the variable displacement pump (1) and verify the flow rate is 105-115 L/min for the RD314 rock drill [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the power pack will not start?
