questions.answer: Check the control system display for possible alarm messages [2]. Verify the connection of the mains electric supply, ensure the main switch (Q1) is in position 1 (ON), and confirm that all emergency stop buttons have been released [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a feed system where the speed is incorrect?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Feed or fast feed speed is incorrect despite pressures, electrical, and control systems operating properly [1].
*   **Cause:** The feed valve main spool (20.16) may be stuck, or the pilot pressure from the feed pilot control valves (20.20 and/or 20.21) is too low [1]. A low pilot pressure could be caused by a dirty pilot oil filter (20.26) or a faulty pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27) [2]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block; it should read 30-45 bar [1]. If the pressure is incorrect, clean or replace the pilot oil filter and the pressure reducing and relief valve [2]. If the pressure is correct, remove and inspect the feed pilot control valves and the feed valve main spool, cleaning or replacing them as necessary (apply a 10 Nm tightening torque for pilot valves) [2, 3]. If the spool is mechanically damaged, replace the entire drilling control valve block [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary functions of the drilling system's variable displacement pumps (1) and (2)?
questions.answer: Variable displacement pump (1) delivers the required amount of oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulic systems [1]. Variable displacement pump (2) delivers the required amount of oil to the rotation hydraulic system [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the procedures and expected values when troubleshooting CAN bus cabling faults by measuring resistance?
questions.answer: First, ensure power is disconnected from the control system [3]. Measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO [4]. If the measurement result is approximately 60 Ω ±5 Ω, the bus cables, connectors, and both 120 Ω termination resistors are intact [3, 4]. If the result is < 50 Ω, there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [4]. If the result is > 100 Ω, one end of the CAN bus is interrupted or the termination resistors are faulty [4]. A reading of ~40...50 kΩ indicates the bus is interrupted at at least two points, or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the hydraulic SBR60i boom is creeping?
questions.answer: Check for a leaking overcenter valve on the boom swing or lift cylinder and replace the damaged or worn parts if there are broken O-rings or worn seat surfaces [2]. You should also flush the hydraulic circuit to remove any dirt, and bleed the cylinders if air is trapped inside [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the steering pump (7.1) do, and where is it located?
questions.answer: The steering pump (7.1) is part of the carrier double pump assembly (7) and delivers oil to the steering circuit, boom, and carrier functions [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the steps to troubleshoot when all hydraulic boom functions are slow or not working at all?
questions.answer: Check the hydraulic oil level and ensure the oil viscosity is correct [1]. Inspect hoses and connections for any leaks in the hydraulic circuit [1]. Check the main pressure relief valve at the pressure control block by observing the percussion pressure gauge; if the required 220 bar working pressure is not reached, clean, adjust, or replace the main pressure relief valve [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the setpoints and adjustment steps for the brake circuit main pressure and retarder pressure relief valves?
questions.answer: The **brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)** is set to **200 bar**, and the **brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15)** is set to **160 bar** [1, 4]. Unplug the electrical connectors for the retarder and pressurization control valves (Y344 and Y167), and connect Y167 to valve 10.16 [5]. Attach gauges to **MPB** and **MCR**, loosen the locking nuts, start the engine, and run the boom zoom backwards to lock the adjustment [6]. At maximum rpm, turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.8) fully clockwise, ensuring the MPB gauge **does not exceed 205 bar** [6, 7]. Turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.15) until MCR reads **210 bar** (the absolute maximum allowed for brake accumulators) [4, 7]. Adjust valve (10.8) counterclockwise until MPB drops to **200 bar** and lock it, then adjust valve (10.15) until MCR reads **160 bar** and lock it [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components determine the reeling force for the cable and water hoses?
questions.answer: The cable reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (1) determines the force for cable reeling [5]. The water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (3) determines the force for water hose reeling [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined pressure limits and relief valve settings for the carrier and tramming circuits?
questions.answer: In the steering circuit, the main pressure relief valve (10.9) is set to 220 bar [15], while the pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (10.11) supplies 35 bar to the pilot control valves [16]. In the brake circuit, the main pressure relief valve (10.8) limits maximum pressure to 200 bar [17, 18], and the absolute maximum pressure allowed to the brake accumulators is 210 bar [18]. The HST charge pressure relief valve (1.5) limits the maximum pressure of the charge pressure circuit to 28-32 bar [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the roles of the main battery and starter switches located in the DQ cabinet?
questions.answer: The battery isolation switch (**S1**) connects and disconnects the 24 VDC battery supply to the drill rig's electric circuits, though it does not disconnect the direct supply to critical safety and memory devices. The optional starter isolator switch (**S2**) is used to prevent the diesel engine from starting and opens the pilot circuit when turned to the OFF position, acting as a safeguard during maintenance. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the Automatic Resin Injection (ARI) system warn the operator of a blocked cartridge?
questions.answer: If the left or right tray's indexing system achieves one more revolution while the pneumatic linear drive (cylinder) is in the retracted position, a caution light will turn on to indicate a blocked cartridge in that specific tray [22, 23]. The operator must check that the loading trays are clean, remove any rocks, dirt, or resin obstructing the cartridges, and verify the pneumatic linear drive strokes and injection line [24, 25]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you pinpoint the location of an interrupted CAN bus cable?
questions.answer: First, disconnect both termination resistors from the bus and measure them separately to verify they each have a resistance of 120 Ω [5]. If they are intact, move a termination resistor towards the next measuring point (any actuator on the bus), disconnect the bus cable from the actuator, and connect the termination resistor in its place to systematically isolate the fault location [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the CAN bus supply conductor to locate a de-energized node?
questions.answer: Keep the control system turned on and measure the supply conductor voltage between **VS and GND**, which should normally be about **24 VDC** [7]. A correctly operating node is usually indicated by a lit power LED [7]. If one or more nodes are not live (unlit LED), locate the de-energized node by comparing the voltage level between VS and GND, measuring one node at a time [7]. A potential interruption point in the supply conductor is confirmed when the measured voltage drops to **0 V** [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which controllers utilize the VCH (Valve Controller High Temp) module, and what is its purpose on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: The **VCH module** is used for the Boom Controller (BC), Drilling Controller (DC), Rod Handler Controller (RC), Front Controller (FC), Screen Handler Controller (SHC), Vehicle Controller (VC), End Controller (EC), Switch Controller (SC), and Cement Mixer Controller (CMC) [5], [6], [7], [8]. It functions as a CANopen slave, offering CANopen services for reading and writing hardware inputs and outputs, and features separate output powering/cutoff circuitry designed to meet SIL2/PLd system safety requirements [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a flashing red CAN-ERR indicator on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) mean, and what procedures should be taken?
questions.answer: A single flash of the red CAN-ERR indicator means the alarm limit has been reached because at least one CAN control error counter has met or exceeded the error limit [6]. This fault condition resets automatically when data transfer is OK [6, 7]. If the power indicator is also off, you should check whether the control unit has supply voltage, check the condition of the automatic fuse, and verify the condition of the internal voltage regulator [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What module controls the rig's shank lubrication via the CAN bus, and how does it operate?
questions.answer: The **Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU)** controls the shank lubrication system [18]. It dispenses shank lubrication oil to the rock drill(s) based on requests received from the DM1 node via the CAN backbone [19]. It includes diagnostic LED indicators (POWER, CAN-RUN, CAN-ERR, and STATUS) to communicate system states and faults [18], [20], [21], [22]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose electrical faults using the NST-2004 emergency stop relay LEDs?
questions.answer: You can diagnose faults by observing the **Ub (supply)**, **K1**, and **K2** LEDs on the relay. If **Ub** is ON but **K1** and **K2** are OFF, the relay is deactivated due to an error between the two emergency stop inputs [1]. If **K1** is ON and **K2** is OFF, there is an error at T14, T21, T22, or the K1 contact may be welded or defective [2]. Conversely, if **K1** is OFF and **K2** is ON, the error is at T11, T12, or the K2 contact is welded or defective [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is likely at fault if the percussion pressure is too high, despite normal electrical and sensor operation, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: The electro proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) is likely stuck [7]. You must stop the power pack, then check, clean, and if necessary, replace valve (20.14) [7]. If the issue persists, check that the LS-line orifices (20.12) and (20.13) are properly in place in the drilling control valve block and carefully tighten them if they have loosened [3, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the percussion pressure is too low but the electrical and control systems are operating properly?
questions.answer: Stop the power pack and verify if the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) or the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) is stuck or dirty [4]. If these are functioning, remove and check the LS-line orifices (20.12) and (20.13) for blockages [4, 5]. Finally, check the output flow of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) to ensure it is sufficient [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: If the feed pressure is abnormally low during operation and running the feed against the rear end stopper yields a pressure reading significantly below 210 bar at the measuring connector (LS) of pump (1), which three specific feed circuit valves (by ID number) must be inspected for leaks before suspecting the feed cylinder?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics DS412iE" manual (Section 6.10: "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low," pages 55-56), if the feed pressure is abnormally low and fails to reach approximately 210 bar at the measuring connector (LS), you must inspect the following three specific feed circuit valves for leaks [1, 2]:

1. **Electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)**
2. **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)**
3. **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)**

Here is the step-by-step troubleshooting sequence before suspecting the feed cylinder [2-5]:

**Step 1: Test and inspect the electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)**
1. Connect a pressure gauge to the **measuring connector (LS)** of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) [2].
2. Disconnect the electric connector from the **electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)** and run the feed against the rear end stopper. The pressure should read approximately **210 bar** [2].
3. If the pressure is lower than this, stop the power pack [2]. 
4. Check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) [2, 3].
5. Reconnect the electric connector to valve (20.22), remove the gauge from the LS connector, and re-test [3].

**Step 2: Inspect and calibrate the shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19)**
If Step 1 does not remedy the situation, the fault likely lies with the shock/anti-cavitation valves. 
1. Check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)** and **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** [3, 4].
2. If these valves are replaced, calibrate them by connecting a pressure gauge to **measuring point (M1)** [4].
3. Temporarily use the **pressure controller (B)** to adjust the set pressure of the variable displacement pump (1) to **235 bar** [4].
4. Run the feed against the front end stopper and adjust the **port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)** to **200 bar** [5].
5. Run the feed against the rear end stopper and adjust the **port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** to **240 bar** [5].
6. Re-adjust the variable displacement pump (1) back to normal operating settings when finished [5].

**Step 3: Test the feed cylinder**
If the pressure remains too low after checking and resolving the three valves above, the feed cylinder itself may be faulty [5]. Verify this using the following steps:
1. Stop the power pack [5].
2. Plug the **feed pressure lines A2 and B2** [5].
3. Start the power pack and check the operation of the feed [5].
4. If the feed pressure normalizes, the feed cylinder is faulty and must be checked, repaired, or replaced [5].

questions.question: An operator reports that the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU) status LED is flashing three times; what specific component does this CAN diagnostic code point to, and what is the normal operating milliamp (mA) range expected when testing its current signal?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material provided, here is the diagnostic information for the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLU):

**Diagnostic Meaning**
When the yellow STATUS LED on the Shank Lubrication Controller (SLCU) flashes three times, it indicates a **malfunction in the air pressure sensor** (the sensor is either broken or disconnected), or there is a general problem with the air pressure [1-3]. 

**Component Identification**
This code points directly to the **SLU air line pressure sensor (B127 / B127P)** [4, 5]. Depending on the boom configuration of the rig, this will be specific to:
*   Boom 1: Sensor **1B127P** (connected to port 1XB127P) [4, 6]
*   Boom 2: Sensor **2B127P** (connected to port XB127 / 2XB127P) [7, 8]
*   Boom 3: Sensor **3B127P** (connected to port 3X127P) [7, 8]

**Normal Operating Range**
The normal operating current signal for the air pressure sensor is **4...20 mA** [1, 2]. The control system will trigger this 3-flash fault code if the current signal drops below **2 mA** [1, 2].

**Troubleshooting Steps**
According to the CAN troubleshooting procedures, you should perform the following steps to resolve this issue:
1. Measure the sensor's current signal to verify if it falls within the normal **4–20 mA** range [3]. 
2. Check the actual SLU air pressure in the system to ensure adequate pressure is being supplied [3].

**References**
*   *Electric system DS412iE*, Section 3.6.3 "Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC)", Page 39 [1]
*   *Shank Lubrication Unit (battery electric drill rig)*, Section 3.3 "Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC)", Pages 13-14 [2]
*   *Shank Lubrication Unit (battery electric drill rig)*, Section 8.1.1 "CAN troubleshooting", Page 42 [3]

questions.question: If the percussion pressure is verified to be too low, and both the main pressure relief valve (20.25) and electro-proportional relief valve (20.14) are functioning perfectly, which two specific orifices (by ID number) in the LS-line should be extracted from the drilling control valve block and checked for blockages?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.8 "Percussion pressure is too low" (Pages 53-54 of the *Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics DS412iE* manual), if the main pressure relief valve (20.25) and the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) are not the cause of the low percussion pressure, you must check the **LS-line orifices (20.12) and (20.13)** for blockages [1, 2].

Here is the step-by-step sequence provided in the manual to check and clean these orifices:

1. Start the power pack [2].
2. Turn the percussion on and move the boom. If the boom functions are normal, but the percussion pressure remains low, either of the orifices (20.12) or (20.13) may be at least partly blocked [2].
3. Stop the power pack [3].
4. Remove the plugs from the ports of the orifices (20.12) and (20.13) [3].
5. Remove the orifices (20.12) and (20.13) carefully from the drilling control valve block [3].
6. Check, clean and, if necessary, replace the orifices (20.12) and (20.13) [3].
7. Install the orifices (20.12) and (20.13) and the plugs carefully back into the drilling control valve block [3].

questions.question: A technician needs to adjust the steering pilot pressure on the carrier. To which specific measuring point must the 40 bar pressure gauge be connected, and what should the starter isolator switch (S2) be set to before making adjustments at maximum APU gear pump rpm?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drill carrier C400E, C900E* manual (Section 4.5.8 "Adjusting steering pilot pressure", pages 49-50), the pressure gauge must be connected to measuring connector **MX** [1, 2]. 

Before making adjustments at the maximum APU gear pump rpm, the **starter isolator switch (S2)** must initially be set to the **OFF** position (indicated by a crossed-out engine icon) to safely attach the gauge and open the valve, and then it must be set to the **ON** position (engine icon) to allow the pump to operate for the actual adjustment [1, 2].

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this procedure:

1. Activate the tramming mode [1].
2. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** to the **OFF** position to prevent the APU circuit gear pump operation [1].
3. Attach the pressure gauge to the **measuring connector MX** *(Note: The measuring point table on page 44 specifies a 40 bar gauge for MX [3], while the procedure step mentions attaching a 50 bar gauge [2])* [2, 3].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the **pressure reducing valve (2.10)** almost fully open [2].
5. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** to the **ON** position to allow the APU circuit gear pump operation [2].
6. Push the **pressurizing stud (2.16)** and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position [2].
7. Apply the maximum revolutions of the APU circuit gear pump [2].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the **pressure reducing valve (2.10)** clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge reaches the target of **30 bars** [2].
9. Tighten the locking nut of the **valve (2.10)** [2].
10. Return the revolutions of the APU circuit gear pump to idle [2].
11. Push the **pressurizing stud (2.16)** and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the down position [2].
12. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** back to the **OFF** position to prevent the APU circuit gear pump operation [4].
13. Remove the pressure gauge from the **measuring connector MX** [4].
14. Turn the **isolator switch (S2)** back to the **ON** position to allow the normal use of the machine [4].

questions.question: If the pilot pressure at line X of the drilling control valve block is confirmed to be within the normal 30-45 bar range but the fast feed speed remains incorrect, which specific feed pilot control valves and main spool (by ID numbers) must be removed, cleaned, and torqued to 10 Nm?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics DS412iE* manual (Section 6.9 "Feed / fast feed speed is not correct," Pages 54-55), if the pilot pressure at line X is correct (30-45 bars), the fault is likely located at the **feed pilot control valves (20.20) and/or (20.21)**, or the **feed valve main spool (20.16)** [1, 2]. 

Here is the step-by-step sequence required to remove, clean, and re-torque these specific components:

**Step 1: Check the Feed Pilot Control Valves (20.20 and 20.21)**
1. Stop the power pack [2].
2. Remove the feed pilot control valves **(20.20)** and **(20.21)** from the drilling control valve block [2].
3. Check and, if necessary, replace the valves [2].
4. Install the valves back to the drilling control valve block carefully. **Note:** The required tightening torque for these valves is **10 Nm** [3].

**Step 2: Check the Feed Valve Main Spool (20.16)**
If adjusting the pilot control valves did not remedy the situation, you must proceed to check the main spool [3]:
1. Remove the pilot control block from the drilling control valve block [3].
2. Extract the feed valve main spool **(20.16)** [3].
3. Check the condition and movements of the main spool. (If the feed valve main spool is faulty, the entire drilling control valve block **(20)** must be replaced) [3].
4. Install the main spool and the pilot control block carefully back to the drilling control valve block [3]. 

*(Note: If these steps do not resolve the incorrect feed speed, the manual advises that the feed cylinder may be damaged or another mechanical fault on the feed may be preventing movement, which would require further inspection and repair [4].)*

questions.question: When adjusting the main pressure relief valve (2.12) with the APU circuit gear pump at maximum revolutions, what specific pressure value should be reached at the measuring connector MP?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the main pressure relief valve (2.12) with the APU circuit gear pump at maximum revolutions, the pressure reading at the measuring connector MP should reach **207 bars** [1, 2]. 

Based on the *Drill carrier C400E, C900E* manual, Section 4.5.6 "Adjusting main pressure relief valve (2.12)" (Pages 47-48), here is the step-by-step sequence for this procedure [2-4]:

1. Activate the tramming mode [3].
2. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** to the OFF position to prevent the APU gear circuit gear pump operation [3].
3. Attach a **250 bar pressure gauge** to the **measuring connector MP** [3].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the **main pressure relief valve (2.12)** almost fully open [3].
5. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** to the ON position to allow the APU circuit gear pump operation [3].
6. Push the **pressurizing stud (2.16)** and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position [2].
7. Apply the maximum revolutions of the APU circuit gear pump [2].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the **main pressure relief valve (2.12)** clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge reaches **207 bars** [2].
9. Tighten the locking nut of the **main pressure relief valve (2.12)** [2].
10. Return the revolutions of the APU circuit gear pump to idle [2].
11. Push the **pressurizing stud (2.16)** and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the down position [2].
12. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** back to the OFF position to prevent the APU circuit gear pump operation [2].
13. Remove the pressure gauge from the **measuring connector MP** [4].
14. Turn the **isolator switch (S2)** back to the ON position to allow the normal use of the machine [4].

questions.question: What is the correct pressure setpoint for the steering pilot pressure reducing valve (2.10) when measured at test port MX?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drill carrier C400E, C900E* manual (Section 4.5.8 "Adjusting steering pilot pressure", pages 49-50), the correct pressure setpoint for the **steering pilot pressure reducing valve (2.10)** when measured at the **measuring connector (MX)** is **30 bars** [1].

Here is the step-by-step sequence for adjusting the steering pilot pressure:

1. Activate the tramming mode [2].
2. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** to the OFF position (preventing the APU gear circuit gear pump operation) [2].
3. Attach a **50 bar pressure gauge** to the **measuring connector MX** [1]. *(Note: The measuring points table in Section 4.5.2 lists a 40 bar gauge for MX [3], while the procedure specifies a 50 bar gauge [1])*
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the **pressure reducing valve (2.10)** almost fully open [1].
5. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** to the ON position to allow the APU circuit gear pump operation [1].
6. Push the **pressurizing stud (2.16)** and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position [1].
7. Apply the maximum revolutions of the APU circuit gear pump [1].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the **valve (2.10)** clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge reaches **30 bars** [1].
9. Tighten the locking nut of the **valve (2.10)** [1].
10. Return the revolutions of the APU circuit gear pump to idle [1].
11. Push the **pressurizing stud (2.16)** and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the down position [1].
12. Turn the **starter isolator switch (S2)** back to the OFF position to prevent the APU circuit gear pump operation [4].
13. Remove the pressure gauge from the **measuring connector MX** [4].
14. Turn the **isolator switch (S2)** back to the ON position to allow the normal use of the machine [4].

questions.question: What are the designated pressure setpoints for the flow controller (A) and pressure controller (B) on the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) when equipped with an RD314 rock drill?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics DS412iE" manual (Section 5.1.1 "Checking the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) pressures" and Section 6.3), the designated pressure setpoints for the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) when equipped with an RD314 rock drill are:

*   **Flow controller (A):** 30 bar (This is the pressure difference between the pump operating pressure and the LS-line pressure) [1-3].
*   **Pressure controller (B):** 235 bar [3, 4].

The manual (Section 5.1.2 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)") details the following step-by-step adjustment procedures:

**Checking and Adjusting Flow Controller (A)**
To check the pressure, connect pressure gauges to the LS-line (flow controller port X) and the pump (1) pressure filter measuring point [1]. If the flow controller (A) needs adjustment, follow these steps:
1. Remove the protecting cap from the flow controller (A) and loosen the locking nut on the flow controller (A) adjusting screw [5].
2. Open the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) almost fully open by turning it counterclockwise [5].
3. Read the pressure difference (pump operating pressure minus LS-line pressure) from the two pressure gauges on pump (1) [2].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) very carefully clockwise until the pressure difference reaches exactly 30 bar [2]. 
5. Tighten the locking nut of the flow controller (A) adjusting screw [2].
6. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure difference again to ensure it remains at 30 bar [2].

**Checking and Adjusting Pressure Controller (B)**
To check the pressure, run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and read the pressure gauge on the pressure filter measuring point [1]. If the pressure controller (B) needs adjustment, follow these steps:
1. Remove the protecting cap from the pressure controller (B) and loosen the locking nut on the pressure controller (B) adjusting screw [4].
2. Open the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) fully open by turning it counterclockwise [4].
3. Run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and read the pressure from the pressure gauge on the pressure filter measuring point [6].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) very carefully clockwise while running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the pressure gauge shows the correct pressure value of 235 bar [6].
5. Release the boom zoom function [5].
6. Tighten the locking nut of the pressure controller (B) adjusting screw [5].
7. After tightening the locking nut, verify the pressure setting again by running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper [5].

questions.question: What are the required pressure settings for the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18) and the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) when the feed is run against the front and rear end stoppers?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics DS412iE* manual (Sections 6.10 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" and 6.11 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too high", pages 55-56) [1-3], the required pressure settings are:

*   **Feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18):** 200 bar 
*   **Feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19):** 240 bar 

To calibrate these valves, the manual details the following step-by-step sequence [1-4]:

1. Connect a pressure gauge to the **measuring point (M1)** [1, 4].
2. Temporarily use the **pressure controller (B)** to adjust the set pressure of the **percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)** to **235 bar** [1, 3].
3. Run the feed against the front end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)** to **200 bar** [2, 3].
4. Run the feed against the rear end stopper and at the same time adjust the pressure of the **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** to **240 bar** [2, 3].
5. When finished, re-adjust the **percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)** back to its standard operating settings as instructed in the manual's section "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" [2, 3].

questions.question: When configuring the optional air line flow meter (46), what specific numeric values must be set for the FCTR, ASP, and AEP parameters on a DS series drill rig?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Flushing circuit DS412iE" manual, Section 9.5 "Adjusting the air line flow meter (optional)" (Pages 59-62), when configuring the optional air line flow meter (46) on a DS series drill rig, you must set the following specific numeric values [1, 2]:

*   **FCTR (Pipe diameter):** 1.50 [1]
*   **ASP (Analogue start point):** 0 [2]
*   **AEP (Analogue end point):** 589 (Note: 213 is used for DD/DT rigs, while 589 is specifically for DL/DS rigs) [2]

Here is the step-by-step sequence to configure these parameters using the flow meter controller (1), Mode/Enter button (3), and Set button (4) [2-5]:

**Setting the FCTR parameter:**
1. Open the cabin floor hatch to reach the flow meter controller (1) [2]. 
2. Push Mode/Enter (3) so many times that FCTR is displayed [2]. 
3. Push Set (4) and keep it pushed down until FCTR starts flashing. After five seconds the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [2]. 
4. Push Set, keep it pushed down until value **1.50** is displayed and then release the button [2]. 
5. Push Mode/Enter briefly and FCTR is displayed again [2]. 

**Setting the OU2 parameter (Scaling):**
6. Push Mode/Enter (3) so many times that OU2 is displayed [2]. 
7. Push Set and keep it pushed down until OU2 starts flashing. After five seconds the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [2]. 
8. Push Set, keep it pushed down until **I** is displayed and then release the button [2]. 
9. Push Mode/Enter briefly and OU2 is displayed again [3]. 

**Setting the ASP parameter:**
10. Push Mode/Enter briefly and ASP is displayed [4]. 
11. Push Set and keep it pushed down until ASP starts flashing. After five seconds the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [4]. 
12. Push Set, keep it pushed down until value **0** is displayed and then release the button [4]. 
13. Push Mode/Enter briefly and ASP is displayed again [4]. 

**Setting the AEP parameter:**
14. Push Mode/Enter briefly and AEP is displayed [4]. 
15. Push Set and keep it pushed down until AEP starts flashing. After five seconds the flashing stops and the parameter value can be changed [4]. 
16. Push Set, keep it pushed down until value **589** is displayed and then release the button [4, 5]. 
17. Push Mode/Enter briefly and AEP is displayed again [5]. 

**Finalizing the configuration:**
18. Push Mode/Enter so many times that the current measured value is displayed or wait for 15 seconds. The unit is back in operating mode [5]. 
19. If you want to lock the unit, push Mode/Enter and Set simultaneously for ten seconds. "Loc" is displayed [5]. 
20. If you want to unlock the unit, push Mode/Enter and Set simultaneously for ten seconds. "uLoc" is displayed [5].

questions.question: What is the fluid capacity and recommended oil classification for the hydraulic oil tank on the C400 and C900 carriers?
questions.answer:
The fluid capacity for the hydraulic oil tank on the C400 and C900 carriers is **270 liters** [1, 2]. 

The recommended oil classification for the hydraulic system is **DIN 51524 part 2 (HLP)** and **ISO 6743-4 (HM)** [1, 2]. The specific factory-recommended oils include:
*   **Sandvik OH46** (for cold ambient temperatures) [1, 2]
*   **Sandvik OH68** (for normal ambient temperatures) [1, 2]
*   **Sandvik OH100** (for high ambient temperatures) [1, 2]
*   **Plantohyd SE 46** or **Plantohyd SE 68** (if biodegradable synthetic ester fluids are required) [1, 2].

Based on the *Maintenance Manual DS412iE* (Section 5.10.4 "Changing the hydraulic oil", pages 280-281), the step-by-step sequence for changing the hydraulic oil is as follows:

1. Position the rig on a level surface [3].
2. Retract all hydraulic cylinders and set the boom(s) to a tramming position [3].
3. Carefully clean the top of the hydraulic oil receiver so that any dirt doesn’t get into the receiver [3, 4].
4. Remove the receiver breather [4].
5. Empty the oil receiver into a receptacle using the drain valve [4].
6. Remove the service hatch at the top of the receiver to facilitate cleaning the receiver internally [4].
7. Clean, rinse, and dry the receiver thoroughly, ensuring it is free of impurities before filling it back up [4].
8. Use fresh oil and a filter when filling the hydraulic oil receiver, making sure not to overfill [4]. If using the rig's electric filling pump, it will stop automatically when the correct level is reached; if filling manually, observe the correct oil level from the sight glass on the tank [5].
9. Install the service hatch and correctly tighten the hatch’s fastening nuts [5].
10. Start the power packs and check the correct oil level after the hydraulic pumps have been running for a few minutes [5]. Add oil if necessary [5]. If there is a need to bleed the hydraulic system, drive the relevant function a few times from one extreme position to another [5].

questions.question: What is the component designation for the 230 kVA multivoltage step-up/step-down autotransformer, and what are its rated input and output voltage ranges?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Electric system DS412iE* manual (Section 3.11 "Transformers (T1, T2)", pages 47-48), the component designation for the 230 kVA multivoltage step-up/step-down autotransformer is **T1** [1]. 

Its rated input and output voltage ranges are as follows:
*   **Primary (Input) Voltage:** 380 - 1000 V [2]
*   **Secondary (Output) Voltage:** 380 - 480 V, 690 V [2]

The manual provides the following specific rated input/output voltage and current mappings for its Yan0 connection [1, 3]:
*   **Input:** 1000 V (132 A) at terminals a1-a2-a3 $\rightarrow$ **Output:** 700 V (190 A) at terminals c1-c2-c3 [3]
*   **Input:** 575 V (231 A) at terminals b1-b2-b3 $\rightarrow$ **Output:** 480 V (277 A) at terminals c1-c2-c3 [3]
*   **Input:** 525 V (253 A) at terminals b1-b2-b3 $\rightarrow$ **Output:** 438 V (303 A) at terminals c1-c2-c3 [3]

questions.question: What is the combined weight of the Tramming Inverter Unit (TIU) and Compressor Inverter Unit (CIU) assembly located on the rear carrier?
questions.answer: Based on the *Weights and dimensions DS412iE* manual (Section 2.1.19 "TIU and CIU assembly", page 26), the combined weight of the Tramming Inverter Unit (TIU) and Compressor Inverter Unit (CIU) assembly located on the rear carrier is **87 kg** [1].

questions.question: When switching from drilling to bolting mode, directional valve Y82 (21.4) is actuated; which specific pilot operated directional valve reroutes oil from the rock drill's percussion mechanism (24) to the optional bolting head percussion mechanism (32), and what is the maximum percussion pressure allowed for the RD314 rock drill?
questions.answer:
When switching from drilling to bolting mode, the directional valve Y82 (21.4) activates and directs pilot pressure to actuate the pilot-controlled directional valves in the drilling/bolting selection valve (21) [1]. The specific valve that reroutes the oil flow from the rock drill's percussion mechanism (24) to the optional bolting head percussion mechanism (32) is the **pilot operated directional valve (21.3)** [2].

Based on the *Drilling and Bolting Hydraulics DS412iE* manual (Section 4.5 "Percussion", page 36), the step-by-step sequence for this rerouting is as follows:
1. When bolting mode and percussion are activated by the operator or control system, the directional valve Y82 (21.4) activates so that percussion affects the bolting head instead of the rock drill [3].
2. Oil flows from port PEP to the drilling/bolting selection valve (21) [3].
3. With the directional valve Y82 (21.4) activated, the oil flows through the pilot actuated directional valve (21.3) to selection valve port PE2 [3].
4. From port PE2, the oil continues to the bolting head percussion mechanism (32) [3].

According to the machine's *Technical Specification*, the maximum percussion pressure allowed for the RD314 rock drill is **160 bar** [4].

questions.question: In the Automatic Resin Injection (ARI) system, what specific valve controls the resin hose feed hydraulic motor (8.3), and what are the reduced operating air pressure and maximum air receiver pressure settings for shooting the resin into the hole?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, the specific components and pressure settings for the Automatic Resin Injection (ARI) system are as follows:

*   **Resin Hose Control Valve:** The direction of the resin hose feed hydraulic motor (8.3), which moves the resin hose in and out, is controlled by the **Directional valve Y55 (8.1)** within the resin hose feed control valve assembly (8) [1].
*   **Operating Air Pressure:** The reduced operating air pressure for shooting the resin into the hole is **4-5 bars**. This is managed by the pressure reducing valve (11.4), which lowers the incoming air pressure before it enters the optional ARI air receiver (11) [2, 3]. 
*   **Maximum Air Receiver Pressure:** The maximum pressure setting for the ARI air receiver is **8 bars**, which is strictly limited by the pressure relief valve (11.2) [2, 3].

These specifications can be found in the *Hydraulic bolting head (BHi)* manual (Page 18) [1] and the *Flushing circuit DS412iE* manual (Section ID 11 "ARI air receiver", Page 13 and the "Air circuit operation" section) [2, 3].

questions.question: The bolt cassette uses a Maltese Cross mechanism to manage its 8-bolt capacity; which specific directional valve controls the bolt cassette rotation, and by what exact fraction of a turn does the pin-driven turning piece rotate the cassette per cycle?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Hydraulic bolting head (BHi)* manual, here are the details regarding the bolt cassette's rotation mechanism:

**Controlling Valve:**
The bolt cassette rotation is controlled by the **Directional valve Y67 (3.1)** [1]. 

**Rotation Fraction:**
The hydraulic motor rotates a pin-driven turning piece, which turns the Maltese Cross by exactly **1/8 of a turn** per cycle [2]. 

**Maltese Cross Operating Sequence:**
The Maltese Cross mechanism utilizes eight turning slots and eight holding slots [2]. The operation follows this step-by-step sequence (found in Section 4.1 "Bolt cassette", pages 23-24):
1. **Phase 1:** The turning piece pin fits into the Maltese Cross turning slot, and the Maltese Cross begins to turn [3].
2. **Phase 2 & 3:** The Maltese Cross continues to turn until the turning piece pin comes out of the turning slot [3].
3. **Phase 4:** At this point, the sliding surface of the turning piece touches the Maltese Cross holding slot [3]. Due to the contact and shape of the parts, the Maltese Cross is prevented from turning any further [3]. The transfer plate and the Maltese Cross are in direct contact with each other, meaning the transfer plate turns with the Maltese Cross [3].

questions.question: What is the maximum rotation torque and rotation speed for the RD314 rock drill when equipped with an OMS100 motor, and which specific proportional valve controls the rotation LS pressure up to a maximum limit of 250 bar?
questions.answer:
Based on the machine specifications and hydraulic system documentation, here are the details for the RD314 rock drill:

*   **Maximum rotation speed:** 520 rpm (when equipped with the OMS100 motor) [1].
*   **Maximum rotation torque:** 340 Nm (when equipped with the OMS100 motor) [1].

The specific valve that controls the rotation LS pressure and limits it to a maximum of 250 bar is the **electro proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6)**, which is also identified electrically as valve **Y6** [2, 3]. This valve is integrated into the drilling control valve block (20) [2, 4].

questions.question: The control system uses anti-jamming automatics to prevent the drill string from getting stuck; which specific sensor measures the water flow rate after the water flushing valve (36) to provide critical data for this anti-jamming monitoring?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Flushing circuit DS412iE* manual (Section 5.1 "Water circuit operation" and the component list on page 17), the specific sensor that measures the water flow rate after the water flushing valve (36) is the **water flow sensor (41)**, which is electrically identified as **(B9F)** [1, 2]. 

After the water passes through the water flushing valve (36), it flows through this water flow sensor (41), which measures the flow rate and sends the data to the control system [2]. The control system then displays this information on the GUI and uses it to control the anti-jamming automatics [2].

questions.question: When preparing the carrier for towing, which two specific shock/anti-cavitation valves (by ID number) in the steering and brake control manifold (1) must be loosened by approximately 2.5 rounds counterclockwise to allow the steering cylinders to move freely, and what is their normal pressure limit setting?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, the two specific shock/anti-cavitation valves that must be loosened are identified in the system as **(2.6)** for port A (steering to right) and **(2.7)** for port B (steering to left) [1, 2]. In the specific towing bypass diagram, they are locally referenced as items **(2)** and **(3)** [3]. 

Their normal pressure limit setting is **190 bars** [1, 2].

According to the "By-passing the steering/articulation" procedure (found on page 378 of the *Operator's* and *Maintenance Manuals*), the step-by-step sequence to prepare the steering for towing is as follows:

1. From the steering and brake control manifold (1), **loosen the shock/anti-cavitation valves (2 and 3) approximately 2.5 rounds counterclockwise** to allow the steering cylinders (4) to move freely [3].
2. During towing, a small amount of oil may bypass and leak out from the opened valves, so you must **observe the amount of possible leakage constantly** [3].
3. Make sure that the loosened valves will not detach from the manifold during towing [3].
4. If the machine is equipped with optional articulation valves (5), **disconnect the electrical cables from the valves before towing** [3].
5. *Note:* Make sure that all leaked oil is collected and correctly disposed of [3].

questions.question: During tramming, a forced stop will be triggered if the service brake charge pressure in either the front or rear circuit drops below what specific factory-set pressure limit, and what is the notice limit pressure that activates a warning light on Tramming panel A?
questions.answer:
During tramming, a forced stop will be triggered if the service brake charge pressure in either the front or rear circuit drops below the factory-set stop limit of **75 bar** [1-3]. The pressure levels of the service brake accumulators are continuously monitored by the **rear service brake accumulator charge pressure sensor (26)** and the **front service brake accumulator charge pressure sensor (27)** [1, 4]. 

When the pressure drops below **75 bar** (or if the pressure measurement fails), the control system activates a tramming forced stop, an alarm message/interlock popup is displayed, the warning light on **Tramming panel A** turns on, an alarm sound is given in the cabin, the main electric motor is decelerated to zero velocity, and the spring-applied brakes are automatically engaged at zero speed or at the latest after a four-second delay [1, 3, 5].

The factory-set notice limit pressure is **110 bar** [1, 3]. If the pressure in either accumulator drops below this level, a notice popup is displayed on the drilling display and the warning light on **Tramming panel A** will turn on [1, 3].

*(References: Drill carrier C400E, C900E manual, Section 4.4.2 "Operation of brake circuit", Page 36; Control system DS412iE manual, Section 5.4 "Tramming forced stop", Page 66 and Section 5.5.3 "Service brake pressure monitoring", Page 69).*

questions.question: When bleeding the SBR60i boom rotary actuator equipped with valve plates, what specific low-pressure range must the respective cylinder chamber be under during the procedure, and what are the exact tightening torques required for the G1/8 (S1) and G1/4 (S2, S3) air bleeds?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Hydraulic SBR60i boom" manual (Section 6.13.6 "Bleeding the rotary actuator", pages 37-38), when bleeding the rotary actuator equipped with valve plates, the respective cylinder chamber must be under a low pressure of **about 20-50 bar** [1, 2].

The exact tightening torques required for the specific air bleeds are:
*   **G1/8 air bleed (S1):** 10 Nm [2]
*   **G1/4 air bleeds (S2 and S3):** 20 Nm [2]

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for the bleeding procedure:
1. Bleed the rotary actuator so that the air bleeds **S1, S2, and S3** are in the horizontal position [1].
2. Turn the rotary actuator to the end position before bleeding [1].
3. In the vent, the respective cylinder chamber (**pressure chamber 1 (DK1)** and **pressure chamber 2 (DK2)** respectively) must be under low pressure (about **20-50 bar**) [1, 2].
4. Open one of the air bleeds and close it when no air or oil with air bubbles comes out [2]. Once clear, close and tighten it using the proper torques: **G1/8 = 10Nm (S1)**, and **G1/4 = 20Nm (S2 and S3)** [2].
5. Repeat the procedure with the other air bleeds [2].
6. Idle the rotary actuator at low pressure slowly 3-5 times out and retract [2].

*(Note: Air bleeds **S1** and **S2** are specifically for **pressure chamber 1 (DK1)**, while air bleed **S3** is for **pressure chamber 2 (DK2)** [2].)*

questions.question: If the control system fails and prevents jack movements from control panel CP2, which specific carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud must be manually operated, and which exact directional valve stud (by ID) must be pushed with a pin to manually lower the rear left jack?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals (Section 7.12 "Manual override of the jacks' movements," *Maintenance Manual DS412iE* / *Operator's Manual DS412iE*, pages 382-384), if the control system fails and prevents jack movements from control panel CP2, you must manually operate the **carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud**. To manually lower the rear left jack, you must push the specific directional valve stud **Y146B**.

Here is the step-by-step sequence required to manually override the system and lower the rear left jack:

1. **Pressurize the system:** Push the **carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud** and turn it clockwise to release the stud to the up position. *(Note: Skip this step if the power pack is running)* [1, 2].
2. **Activate the override valve:** Push the stud **(Y168)** with a pin or similar tool to activate valve Y168. You must keep this stud pushed down during the entire override procedure. *(Note: Skip this step if the APU is running)* [1, 2].
3. **Lower the rear left jack:** While keeping Y168 pushed down, push the stud **Y146B** with a pin or similar tool. This delivers oil flow to port A3 and lowers the rear left jack [3-6].
4. **Lock the system:** When finished, push the **carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud** and turn it counterclockwise to lock the stud back into the down position [4, 6].

questions.question: In the carrier's service brake accumulator charging circuit, which specific gear pump (by ID) supplies oil via port CV to the accumulator charging valve (21), and what exact pressure range is valve (21) designed to maintain in the service brake accumulators (22 and 23)?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Drill carrier C400E, C900E* manual (Section 4.4.2 "Operation of brake circuit", page 36), the oil is supplied by the **auxiliary power unit circuit gear pump (1.1)** [1]. 

The accumulator charging valve (21) is designed to maintain an exact pressure range of **135-160 bar** in the service brake accumulators (22 and 23) [2]. 

The manual describes the following operational sequence for how the system charges the accumulators:
1. The **auxiliary power unit circuit gear pump (1.1)** supplies oil to the accumulator charging valve port P via port CV of the steering and brake control manifold (2) [1].
2. When the pressure level in the brake accumulators drops below **135 bars**, the **control valve (21.2)** changes its position and pilots the **priority valve (21.1)** [1].
3. The piloted **priority valve (21.1)** changes its position and directs the oil flow through the **check valve (21.5)** and **isolation valves (21.3 and 21.4)** to ports A1 and A2 of the accumulator charging valve [1].
4. From port A1, the oil flows to the **rear service brake circuit divider block (19)** and then to the **rear circuit service brake accumulator (22)** [3].
5. From port A2, the oil flows to the **front service brake circuit divider block (20)** and then to the **front circuit service brake accumulator (23)** [3].
6. The pressure accumulators will continue to be charged until the pressure reaches **160 bars** [3].
7. Once 160 bars is reached, the **valves (21.1 and 21.2)** return to their previous positions, and the system's operation returns to free circulation [3].

questions.question: What causes the rotation speed adjustment to stop working, and how is it corrected?
questions.answer: Symptom:** Rotation speed adjustment does not function properly or the rotations of the drilling rod are not constant [10]. **Cause:** The fault typically lies in the **rotation pilot control valves (20.4 or 20.5)**, the **rotation valve main spool (20.1)**, the **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)**, or the rock drill itself [10]. **Corrective action:** Verify the pilot pressure is **30-45 bars** [11]. If correct, remove, clean, and replace the **rotation pilot control valves (20.4, 20.5)** (tightening to 10 Nm) [12]. Next, extract and check the **rotation valve main spool (20.1)** and the **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)**, replacing the valve block if either is damaged [13, 14]. Finally, if all valves are functioning properly, repair or replace the rock drill rotation motor [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a tripped breaker or burned fuse indicate, and how is it diagnosed?
questions.answer: A tripped breaker or burned fuse indicates a failure such as an overload or short circuit, which protects wires and electrical components from overheating and fire [3, 4]. The underlying electrical fault (like damaged insulation, loose connections, or short circuits) must be investigated and repaired by a qualified electrician before resetting the breaker or replacing the fuse [3-6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the system if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling?
questions.answer: Check if the **rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3)**, the **shuttle valve (20.7)**, or the **electro proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6)** is leaking [10, 11]. Clean, check, and replace these valves if necessary, or check the rock drill rotation motor for internal leaks if the valves are functioning correctly [10-12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptoms, causes, and corrective actions if the feed or fast feed speed is incorrect?
questions.answer: Symptom:** The feed or fast feed speed is incorrect despite proper system pressures and functional electrical controls [1]. **Cause:** The **feed valve main spool (20.16)** is stuck, or the pilot pressure from the **feed pilot control valves (20.20 and/or 20.21)** is too low [1]. **Corrective action:** Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block to verify pilot pressure is **30-45 bars** [1]. If incorrect, check, clean, or replace the **pilot oil filter (20.26)** and **relief valve (20.27)** [2]. If the pilot pressure is normal, remove, inspect, and clean or replace the **feed pilot control valves (20.20, 20.21)** and the **feed valve main spool (20.16)** [2, 3]. If the spool is faulty, the entire drilling control valve block must be replaced [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot communication faults on the CAN bus system?
questions.answer: First, identify faults using the notifications and instructions on the operator's display panel [12]. If physical testing is required, ensure the power is off to measure the resistance between **CAN_HI and CAN_LO** (which should normally be **~60 Ω ±5 Ω**) [13, 14]. To check for short-circuits to ground or supply voltage, turn the system on and measure the voltage levels of the CAN wires [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What controllers utilize the VIU module, and what is its primary role in the control system?
questions.answer: The **VIU (Voltage Input Unit)** module acts as the **Tramming Controller (TCP)**, **Gearbox Controller (GBC)**, and **Main Switchgear Sensors (MS)** [8]. It functions as a general-purpose input unit for the user interface and serves as a voltage input unit for applications that require intensive local computing power [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a "Blocked" pop-up dialog mean during operation?
questions.answer: A "Blocked" pop-up dialog is displayed when the rig control system actively prohibits the operator from performing an action that could cause personal injury or damage to the rig [1, 2]. The operator must resolve the underlying cause of the error, after which the pop-up will disappear automatically [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the significance of the yellow "Notice" pop-up dialog, and what is the required response?
questions.answer: A yellow "Notice" pop-up is displayed when the control system detects a medium-level problem, such as low hydraulic oil [1-4]. It does not require immediate action to stop the machine; however, if the alert persists or is repeated often, the operator should investigate and correct the reason for the alert [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure and flow controller setpoints for the variable displacement pumps?
questions.answer: For the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump, the flow controller is set to 30 bar, and the pressure controller is set to 235 bar when using the RD314 rock drill [7]. For the rotation circuit variable displacement pump, the flow controller is set to 23 bar, and the pressure controller is set to 200 bar [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the feed or fast feed pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Symptom:** Feed or fast feed pressure is too low during operation [4]. **Cause:** There is a leak in the **electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)**, **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)**, **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)**, or the feed cylinder is faulty [4, 5]. **Corrective action:** Check, clean, or replace valves (20.18) and (20.19), then adjust their pressures to **200 bar** for port A and **240 bar** for port B [5, 6]. If the pressure remains low, plug the feed pressure lines A2 and B2 and start the power pack; if the feed pressure normalizes, the feed cylinder is faulty and must be repaired or replaced [5, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the system if the rotation pressure drops significantly when the rock drill rotation is loaded?
questions.answer: Check if the **rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3)** is leaking; if it is, replace it and adjust it according to the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve adjustment instructions [10]. If the problem remains, check, clean, and if necessary, replace the **shuttle valve (20.7)** [10]. Additionally, verify if the **electro proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6)** is leaking, as this would incorrectly allow the LS-pressure to vent to the tank line [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a situation where the feed or fast feed pressure is too high, assuming the electric and control systems are functioning properly?
questions.answer: A high feed pressure usually indicates that the **electro proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22)**, the **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)**, or the **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** is stuck [2]. Stop the power pack, then check, clean, or replace valves (20.18) and (20.19) [3]. If replacing them, connect a pressure gauge to **measuring point (M1)** and use the **pressure controller (B)** to adjust the set pressure of the **percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)** to **235 bar** [3]. If the issue persists, repair or replace valve (20.22) or inspect the **feed line pressure compensator (20.17)** for mechanical damage [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific adjustment procedures and voltage values required when replacing a control system power supply unit (A3, A4, or A5)?
questions.answer: After replacing the broken unit, switch on the power and adjust the output voltage to exactly **27.0 V ± 0.1 V** in **"Single Use"** mode, ensuring the same load conditions apply to both units [5]. Following this adjustment, move the jumper on the front of the unit from **"Single Use"** to **"Parallel Use"** mode to achieve proper load sharing [5]. Finally, check that the DC-voltage reading on the screen is around **28 V without load** and **27 V with full load** [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which CAN bus module acts as the Boom Controller (BC), Drilling Controller (DC), and Rod Handler Controller (RC), and what other controllers use this same hardware?
questions.answer: The **VCH (Valve Controller High Temp)** module serves as the **BC**, **DC**, and **RC** [3]. This exact same hardware module is also utilized for the **Vehicle Controller (VC)**, **End Controller (EC)**, **Switch Controller (SC)**, **Main Switchgear Controller (MC)**, and the **Screen Handler Controller (SHC)** [4], [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration requirements and specifications for the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The system requires a high level of cleanliness, with the manufacturer recommending a fluid purity class of 18/16/13 according to the ISO 4406 (c) standard [9]. The pressure filter operates at a filtration level of 20 µm absolute [10]. The return oil filter has a filtration level of 10 µm absolute [9]. The system also utilizes a 5 µm breather for the hydraulic oil receiver [11], a 160-200 µm pilot oil filter [4], and an optional 2 µm bypass filter [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the flow controller value of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump deviates from its set value?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to the **measuring connector (LS)** of the **percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)** [8]. If the pressure at this connector is above the normal tank pressure, it indicates a false control signal is reaching pump (1) [9]. This leakage can be caused by a stuck **percussion selector valve (20.9)**, **percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10)**, **feed valve main spool (20.16)**, or **feed line pressure compensator (20.17)** in the drilling control valve block [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings are triggered by the optional door latch and seat belt monitoring system?
questions.answer: If the operator's seat belt is not fastened or the cabin door is not properly closed before tramming, a buzzer will sound on the tramming panel [6, 7]. Additionally, a notice pop-up will be displayed on the screen alerting the operator to secure the cabin door and fasten the seat belt [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the maximum pressure limits and relief valve settings for the main drilling circuits?
questions.answer: The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve limits the maximum system pressure to 270 bar [4]. The rotation circuit main pressure relief valve limits the maximum rotation pressure to 250 bar [5]. For the feed circuit, the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve limits maximum pressure to 200 bar, and the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve is set to 240 bar [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a fault when the power pack will not start?
questions.answer: Check the screen for alarm messages, ensure the **starter isolator switch (S2)** is in the correct position, verify the mains electric supply is connected, make sure the **main switch (Q1)** is in position 1 (ON), and confirm that all emergency stop buttons have been released [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function and model of the brake resistors?
questions.answer: The brake resistors are **Danotherm PCG 10K0** units. They have a rated continuous power of 6 kW (capable of handling 70 kW overloads for 5 seconds) and are used to safely dissipate excess electrical energy generated by the electric motors during braking [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose interruptions or termination resistor faults on the CAN bus?
questions.answer: Ensure the power is disconnected by turning the battery main switch (S1) to position 0, then measure the total resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO [4]. If the measurement result is > 100 Ω, it indicates that one end of the CAN bus is interrupted or the termination resistors are faulty [5]. If the result is ~40...50 kΩ, the bus is interrupted at at least two points, or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can the control system's graphical user interface (GUI) be used to diagnose electrical signaling issues?
questions.answer: By navigating to the **-> Troubleshooting** menu on the display, you can view a diagram showing the real-time electrical signaling between control devices and system components [1, 2]. A **gray signaling arrow** before a component indicates the signaling connection is inactive, which can point to the component causing the problem [2-4]. Additionally, if a **red X** is shown on top of a module in the diagram, it means the module is offline, not working, or connected to an option not included in the machine [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system warn the operator if the service brake charge pressure drops too low?
questions.answer: If the front or rear brake circuit charge pressure drops below the 110 bar notice limit, a notice is displayed on the screen and a warning light on Tramming panel A turns on [5]. If the pressure drops further below the stop limit during tramming, a tramming forced stop is activated, an alarm message is displayed, and the warning light turns on [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you distinguish between a CAN wire shorted to ground versus a CAN wire shorted to the supply voltage?
questions.answer: In both scenarios, the resistance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI will still measure approximately 60 Ω [7]. To distinguish them, measure the voltage levels: if there is a short-circuit to ground, the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level will continuously be near 0 V [7]. If there is a short-circuit to the supply voltage, the CAN_LO or CAN_HI voltage level will continuously remain near the supply voltage (VS) [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific malfunctions are indicated by the flashing yellow STATUS LED on the Shank Lubrication Unit?
questions.answer: Two flashes indicate a malfunction in the lubrication oil flow because the flow sensor signal is not detected [14]. Three flashes signify an air pressure sensor malfunction, meaning the sensor is broken or disconnected [14]. Four flashes indicate a malfunction with the lubrication oil level switch [14]. The operator or maintenance personnel should check the respective sensors to resolve the fault. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you read the CAN diagnostic fault codes on an FPVC or VCH module's 7-segment display?
questions.answer: When powered up, the display runs a boot sequence and then cycles through the node ID, the operational state (**Pr** = pre-operational, **Op** = operational, or **St** = stopped), and any active faults [13, 14]. If there is a communication error, it displays **"Co"** [15]. For faulty I/O signals, it displays the connector ID (e.g., J7), followed by the pin number (in hex) and a letter indicating the specific status fault: **"s"** for a short circuit to ground, **"o"** for an open circuit, or **"b"** for a short circuit to battery [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure settings and procedures for the cable reel brake pressure relief valves (10 and 11)?
questions.answer: These valves control reel deceleration. Adjust the **reeling in valve (10)** to **20 bars** by turning its adjusting screw counterclockwise while holding the reeling out button (D) and running the APU at minimum speed (1000 rpm) [16]. The **reeling out valve (11)** setting depends on the cross-sectional area of the cable: set to **40 bars** for cables up to 50 mm², or **70 bars** for cables between 70 mm² and 240 mm² [17]. Adjust valve (11) clockwise while holding button (D) and running the APU at maximum speed (2500 rpm) [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you interpret the diagnostic fault codes shown by the status LED on the Gatekeeper Controller (GSC) module?
questions.answer:
The GSC features a single status LED that changes color and blink rate to indicate specific operating states or errors [11]. 
*   **Yellow (1 Hz):** Initialization or reset checks [12].
*   **Orange (ON):** Error in the start-up phase [12].
*   **Green (5 Hz):** No operating system loaded [12].
*   **Green (2 Hz):** Running normally [12].
*   **Green (ON):** Stopped [12].
*   **Red (2 Hz):** Running with an error [12].
*   **Red (ON):** Fatal error or stopped with an error [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: If the overall CAN bus resistance is incorrect, how can you isolate the fault to a specific termination resistor or bus section?
questions.answer: First, disconnect both termination resistors from the bus and measure them separately; each should measure exactly **120 Ω** [6]. If both resistors are intact, the fault is in the bus itself [6]. To isolate the location, move the termination resistor to the next measuring point (which can be any actuator/node on the bus), disconnect the bus cable from the actuator, and plug the termination resistor in its place to observe if the fault disappears [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the red "Alarm" pop-up dialog indicate on the main display, and how should the operator respond?
questions.answer: The red "Alarm" pop-up indicates that the rig control system has detected a major problem [1, 2]. This condition requires immediate attention and action to prevent damage to the rig components, and the control system may stop some or all operations [1, 2]. The operator must not use the rig until the cause of the alarm is resolved and corrected [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the troubleshooting process if the percussion pressure is too high?
questions.answer: Symptom:** Percussion pressure exceeds normal operating limits while electrical and control systems are functioning properly [17]. **Cause:** The **electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14)** is stuck, or either of the **orifices (20.12 or 20.13)** in the LS-line have become loosened or disconnected [17, 18]. **Corrective action:** Stop the power pack, then check, clean, and replace valve (20.14) if needed [18]. If the pressure is still too high, verify that both orifices (20.12) and (20.13) are properly seated in the drilling control valve block and tighten them carefully [18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose emergency stop circuit faults using the LEDs on the Duelco NST-2004 relays?
questions.answer: You can identify faults by checking the status of the **Ub (Supply)**, **K1**, and **K2** LEDs [5]. If **Ub is ON** but both **K1 and K2 are OFF**, there is an error between the two emergency stop inputs [6]. If **K1 is ON and K2 is OFF**, there is an error at T14, T21, or T22, or K1 may be welded or defective [6]. If **K1 is OFF and K2 is ON**, there is an error at T11 or T12, or K2 may be welded or defective [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific hardware components are used for the Drilling GUI (DG) and Tramming GUI (VG) control interfaces?
questions.answer: The **Drilling GUI (DG)** utilizes a **CCpilot XM2**, which is a PC-based onboard display computer [9]. The **Tramming GUI (VG)** utilizes an **EPEC 6107**, which is a PanelPC featuring a 7-inch LCD resistive color touch display running Linux and CODESYS 3.5 [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you test the CAN bus voltage levels, and what are the normal and abnormal operating values?
questions.answer: The control system must be ON for this test, so turn the **battery main switch (S1)** to position **1** [3]. Measure the voltage between **CAN_HI and GND**, and then **CAN_LO and GND** [3]. Both should normally read **2.5 V ±0.2 V** with no load on the bus [3, 4]. If the measurement is **< 1 V or > 4 V**, it indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the primary variable displacement pumps (1 and 2) in the drilling and bolting system?
questions.answer: The variable displacement pump (1) delivers the required amount of hydraulic oil to the percussion, feed, and boom hydraulic systems, as well as the optional stabilizer and power extractor [1]. The variable displacement pump (2) is dedicated to delivering the required amount of oil to the rotation hydraulic system [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific valves control the percussion function and regulate its pressure within the drilling control valve block?
questions.answer: The percussion selector valve (20.9) opens and closes the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10), which directs the main oil flow to the percussion mechanism [4]. The percussion pressure itself is adjusted and controlled by the electro proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you initially identify and diagnose faults on the CAN bus system?
questions.answer: Any fault on the CAN bus must first be identified using the instructions and notifications on the operator's display panel, which will notify the operator whether the bus nodes are in a fault mode or switched off [1]. For further physical troubleshooting, you can measure the resistances of the termination resistors (with power disconnected) and the voltage of the normal operation (with the system powered on) [1], [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the FPVC module, and which specific controllers on the DS412IE utilize it?
questions.answer: The **FPVC (Fast Proportional Valve Controller)** module is a powerful I/O-module equipped with internal FPGA support to provide intensive local computing power, designed to meet SIL2 class requirements [6]. On the CAN bus system, it operates as the **Resin Controller (ARI)** and the **DC Contactor Controller (DCC)** [6], [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the adjustment procedure and setpoint for the water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (3)?
questions.answer: Connect a gauge to the water hose reel measuring point (6) [19]. Loosen the locking nut on the **water hose reel pressure reducing/relieving valve (3)**, pressurize the system (for instance, by raising the jack carefully against the stopper), and adjust the screw until the pressure reaches exactly **80 bars** [19]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose a fault using the indicator LEDs on the Duelco NST-2004 emergency stop relays?
questions.answer: Check the **Ub, K1, and K2 LEDs** on the relay [2]. If **Ub is ON** but both **K1 and K2 are OFF**, there is an error between the two emergency stop inputs [2]. If **K1 is ON and K2 is OFF**, there is an error at **T14, T21, or T22**, or **K1** may be welded/defective [2]. If **K1 is OFF and K2 is ON**, there is an error at **T11 or T12**, or **K2** may be welded/defective [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What types of CAN bus faults can and cannot be diagnosed using a multimeter?
questions.answer: A multimeter can easily detect the most common bus faults, such as cable faults, loose connections, wire interruptions, and short-circuits [3]. However, a multimeter cannot detect faulty CAN sensors (sensor signal faults), missing CAN signals, or bit-level signal faults [3], [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are responsible for filtering the hydraulic oil in the main circuits, and what are their micron ratings?
questions.answer: The pressure filter (8) filters oil coming directly from the variable displacement pump (1) at a filtration level of 20 µm absolute [10, 11]. The return oil filter (4.3) filters return oil coming from the steering, brake, drilling, and carrier functions; its filter element (4.3.2) has a rating of 10 µm [12, 13]. Additionally, an optional bypass filter (10) can be used to filter oil taken from the rotation circuit at 2 µm [10, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose an unresponsive electrical component using the control system's GUI?
questions.answer: Navigate to **-> Troubleshooting** on the display to view a troubleshooting diagram showing real-time electrical signaling between control devices and system components [7, 8]. A **gray signaling arrow** before a component indicates that the signaling connection is inactive, which likely points to the component causing the problem [9-11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components provide earth continuity and residual current protection for the optional dewatering pump?
questions.answer: The **MEC-1** earth continuity protection relay (K9A) measures the resistance of the pilot-earth loop to ensure earth conductor integrity [17, 18]. The residual current protection relay (K9B) is either a **RH99M** or **SE-105** model, which measures earth leakage current and interrupts power via contactor K9 in the event of an insulation fault [19-21]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What alarms are triggered on the Fire Suppression System's electronic alarm box, and what is the operator's response?
questions.answer: If the system pressure drops (due to system discharge or a leak), a yellow "TANK PRESSURE LOW" or red "SYSTEM FAULT OR DISCHARGE" warning light will illuminate and an audible siren will sound [6, 7, 10-12]. This starts a 6-second automatic engine shutdown delay timer; the operator can press the delay extension button to gain an additional 20 seconds to safely stop the rig [10-12]. The system will remain in the alarm state until it is brought back to full pressure and reset [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you calibrate the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25)?
questions.answer: First, tighten the adjusting screw of the **percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25)** almost to its end (over **270 bar**) [7]. Next, force the variable displacement pump to operate at a constant pressure by fully closing its flow controller, and adjust its pressure controller to **280 bar** [8].
