Loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.25) until the valve begins to fizz and the pressure reading drops exactly to the target **270 bar** [8, 9]. After this is set, you must re-adjust the variable displacement pump to its standard settings and tighten the locking nut [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: When measuring resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO with the power off, what do abnormal readings of < 50 Ω, > 100 Ω, and ~40...50 kΩ indicate?
questions.answer: A measurement of **< 50 Ω** indicates a short-circuit on the CAN bus [2]. A reading of **> 100 Ω** means one end of the CAN bus is interrupted or one of the termination resistors is faulty [2]. A reading of **~40...50 kΩ** indicates the bus is interrupted in at least two places, or both termination resistors are missing or faulty [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a fault where percussion is not working or the percussion pressure is too low?
questions.answer: If the percussion pressure gauge shows no reading, the **percussion selector valve (20.9)** or **percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10)** may be stuck and needs to be cleaned or replaced [3]. If the pressure is too low or percussion does not start, check if the **electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14)** or **percussion pressure compensator (20.11)** is dirty, or if the **orifices (20.12) or (20.13)** in the LS-line are blocked [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the CAN-RUN and CAN-ERR LED flashing codes indicate on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU)?
questions.answer: The green **CAN-RUN** LED indicates the module's operating status: a **single flash** means it has stopped due to an internal fault, **flashing** means it is on standby awaiting a command (or the CAN connection is broken), **continuously ON** means it is operating normally, and **OFF** means it is resetting or powered down [7, 8]. The red **CAN-ERR** LED indicates CAN control errors: a **single flash** means the CAN control error counter has reached its alarm limit, **continuously ON** means the CAN bus is completely off, and **OFF** means there are no errors [7-10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components supply and direct hydraulic oil for the carrier's steering and braking systems?
questions.answer: The auxiliary power unit (APU) circuit gear pump (1.1) delivers oil to the steering, brake, HVAC, and carrier functions [15]. Within the steering and brake control manifold, the steering valve main spool (2.1) directs oil flow to the left and right steering cylinders [15]. The manifold also features a battery tramming retarder control valve (2.14) that, when energized, allows oil flow to the pressure compensator (2.15) to shift power consumption to the hydraulic system and prevent overheating of the battery system [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you differentiate between a CAN wire shorted to ground versus a CAN wire shorted to the supply voltage (VS)?
questions.answer: If there is a short-circuit to ground, the **CAN_LO** or **CAN_HI** voltage level will continuously be near **0 V**, but the resistance between CAN_LO and CAN_HI will still measure **~60 Ω** [5]. If there is a short-circuit to the supply voltage, the **CAN_LO** or **CAN_HI** voltage level will continuously remain near the supply voltage **(VS)**, also while the resistance remains **~60 Ω** [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of directional valves Y71, Y67, Y55, and Y68 on the hydraulic bolting head?
questions.answer:
**Directional valve Y71 (2.1):** Controls the front jaw movement, swinging it between the bolt cassette and the bolt rotation mechanism [6].
*   **Directional valve Y67 (3.1):** Controls the rotation of the bolt cassette [6].
*   **Directional valve Y55 (8.1):** Controls the direction of the resin hose feed hydraulic motor, which moves the resin/cement hose in and out [7].
*   **Directional valve Y68 (11.1):** Controls the direction of the rear bolt jaw cylinder (11.5) and the optional middle bolt jaw cylinder (11.4) [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the feed or fast feed speed is incorrect?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to **line X** of the drilling control valve block to check the pilot pressure, which should normally be **30-45 bars** [5]. If the pressure is incorrect, inspect the **pilot oil filter (20.26)** and **pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27)** [6]. If the pilot pressure is correct, the **feed valve main spool (20.16)** or **feed pilot control valves (20.20 or 20.21)** might be stuck and require cleaning or replacement [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component acts as the Drilling Master (DM1) and Carrier Master (CM1) in the control system?
questions.answer: Both the **Drilling Master (DM1)** and the **Carrier Master (CM1)** utilize the **SCU machine control computer** [11], [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the boom is creeping?
questions.answer: Boom creeping is typically caused by a leaking **overcenter valve** (due to a broken O-ring or worn seat surfaces), dirt in the hydraulic circuit, or air trapped in the cylinder [2]. Diagnosis and repair involve replacing the damaged valve parts, flushing the hydraulic circuit, or bleeding the cylinders [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure and expected values for troubleshooting the CAN bus by measuring resistance?
questions.answer: Ensure power is disconnected by turning the **24 VDC battery main switch (S1)** to position **0** [3]. Measure the total resistance between **CAN_HI and CAN_LO** [4]. If the result is approximately **60 Ω ±5 Ω**, the bus cables, connectors, and **120 Ω** termination resistors are intact [4]. If the measurement is **< 50 Ω**, there is a short-circuit [4]. If it is **> 100 Ω**, one end of the CAN bus is interrupted or the termination resistors are faulty [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) adjusted?
questions.answer: Tighten the adjusting screw of the **rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3)** over **250 bar** [10, 11]. Force the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2) to operate at a constant pressure by turning the flow controller adjusting screw fully closed, then set the pressure controller to **260 bar** [11, 12]. Loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.3) until the valve begins restricting pressure (indicated by a fizzing sound) and the pressure drops to the target **250 bar** [12]. Afterwards, restore the pump settings and tighten the locking nut [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component acts as the battery charger, and what is its part number?
questions.answer: The battery charger (A1) is a **CP10.241** (or CP10.241-S1/CP10.242) model. It is a 24.0 VDC power supply used to charge the carrier's 24 V lead-acid batteries when the main DC/DC converters are not being fed by the main high-voltage batteries [22-24]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which valves control the reeling in and out of the cable and water hoses on the rear carrier?
questions.answer: The 4/3-directional cable reel control valve (Y173) manages the cable reel, with solenoid Y173a reeling the cable out and Y173b reeling the cable in [17]. Similarly, the 4/3-directional water hose reel control valve (Y174) controls the optional water hose reel, with solenoid Y174a reeling the water hose out and Y174b reeling it in [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical system diagnostics should be checked if the power pack stops unexpectedly during operation?
questions.answer: If the power pack stops, you should first check the display screen for any active alarm messages [16]. Then, verify that the inlet pressure is sufficient, check that none of the circuit breakers inside the **MQ cabinet** have tripped, ensure all emergency stop buttons are fully released, and verify that the pilot circuit is functioning [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should you do if all hydraulic boom functions are slow or not working, and the required working pressure is not reached?
questions.answer: First, check the hydraulic oil level and ensure the **oil viscosity** is not too high [1]. Next, inspect the hoses and connections for any leaks in the hydraulic circuit [1]. Finally, check the percussion pressure gauge to verify if the required **220 bar working pressure** is reached; if the pressure is too low, check, clean, adjust, or replace the **main pressure relief valve** at the pressure control block [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the drilling/bolting selection valve (21) operate to switch between the rock drill and the bolting head?
questions.answer: The drilling/bolting selection valve (21) determines whether the rock drill or the bolting head is pressurized [2]. When its directional valve Y82 (21.4) is not actuated, the oil flow is directed from the drilling control block to the rock drill mechanism [3]. When directional valve Y82 (21.4) is actuated, it directs pilot pressure to a series of pilot-operated directional valves (21.1, 21.2, 21.3, 21.5, 21.6), which reroutes the oil flow to the bolting head mechanism instead [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure and expected value for checking the overall integrity of the CAN bus using resistance measurement?
questions.answer: Before measuring, you must disconnect the power by turning the **battery main switch (S1)** to position **0** [1]. Measure the total resistance between **CAN_HI and CAN_LO**; if the result is approximately **60 Ω ±5 Ω**, the bus cables, connectors, and both **120 Ω termination resistors** are intact [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the specific make, model, and function of the main high-voltage batteries on the drill rig?
questions.answer: The main batteries (BAT1, BAT2, BAT3, BAT4) are **Fiamm Z60-650** Sodium-Nickel-Chloride batteries. They provide a nominal 650 VDC and 24.7 kWh of energy to power the electric driveline system, allowing for zero-emission tramming [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the target pressures for the feed port shock/anti-cavitation valves, and how are they calibrated?
questions.answer: Temporarily use the pressure controller (B) to set the percussion/feed variable displacement pump (1) to **235 bar** [14, 15]. Run the feed against the front end stopper and adjust the **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)** to **200 bar** [15]. Next, run the feed against the rear end stopper and adjust the **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** to **240 bar** [15]. Re-adjust the pump back to normal operating settings when finished [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose and resolve an issue where the percussion is on all the time when the power pack is running?
questions.answer: Symptom:** The percussion remains continuously active whenever the power pack is running [16]. **Cause:** The **percussion selector valve (20.9)** or the **percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10)** is stuck and leaking, which allows pressure to constantly reach the rock drill's percussion mechanism [16]. **Corrective action:** Stop the power pack immediately, as running with too low percussion pressure can cause severe damage to the seals of the accumulators in the rock drill [16, 17]. Check, clean, and if necessary, replace valves (20.9) and (20.10) [17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary flow rates for the percussion, rotation, and feed pumps?
questions.answer: The percussion pump supplies a general flow of 30-45 l/min, and the rotation pump provides 15-20 l/min [1]. More specifically, at maximum percussion pressure using an RD314 rock drill, the flow rates are 105-115 L/min for percussion and 4-8 L/min for the feed [2]. Additionally, the water booster pump has a capacity of 50 l/min [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What type of relays are used in the emergency stop circuit, and what is their function?
questions.answer: The emergency stop circuit utilizes two **Duelco NST-2004** safety relays (K32A, K32B). Their primary function is to cut down power from the output units of the IO-controllers when an emergency stop button is pressed, ensuring that all hydraulic and rotating movements are safely de-energized [9-12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are variable displacement pumps diagnosed if they do not rotate or their speed is abnormal?
questions.answer: First, navigate to the GUI troubleshooting views (**-> Troubleshooting**) to check the electrical signaling between control devices and the drilling system components [7-9]. Next, measure the supply voltage to the power pack; if the voltage is correct, check for mechanical damage preventing rotation, which is often indicated by an unusually noisy power pack [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a flashing or continuously lit red CAN-ERR indicator on the Shank Lubrication Control Unit (SLCU) signify?
questions.answer: A **single flash** of the red **CAN-ERR indicator** means the CAN control error counter has reached or exceeded its alarm limit due to too many errors [6, 7]. This fault condition will reset automatically once data transfer is functioning correctly [6, 7]. If the indicator is **continuously on**, it signifies a "Bus off" state, meaning the CAN control bus is completely disconnected or turned off [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings occur if the trailing cable reel limits are reached during tramming, and how must the operator respond?
questions.answer: When the cable reel warning limit (low cable) is reached, the operator can temporarily bypass the warning to continue tramming by pushing and holding the bypass button while cycling the parking brake button [8]. If tramming continues until the cable reel stop limit is reached, an alarm will sound in the cabin, an interlock popup will appear, and the parking brakes will engage immediately [9]. This forced stop can then only be bypassed with user-level maintenance or factory access [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a short-circuit on the CAN bus using voltage and resistance measurements?
questions.answer: A short-circuit is indicated if the resistance between CAN_HI and CAN_LO measures < 50 Ω while the power is off [5]. Alternatively, you can measure the voltage levels with the system powered on; measure the voltage between CAN_HI and GND, and CAN_LO and GND [6]. If the results are < 1 V or > 4 V (deviating from the normal 2.5 V ±0.2 V), there is a short-circuit on the CAN bus [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the rotation pressure is too high during drilling?
questions.answer: Symptom:** Rotation pressure is excessively high while drilling [8]. **Cause:** This can be caused by incorrect drilling control settings, the rotation speed of the drilling rod being too low, a faulty **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)**, or a damaged rock drill rotation motor/mechanism [8-10]. **Corrective action:** First, adjust the rotation speed of the drilling rod to a proper level [9]. If the pressure remains high, remove, clean, and inspect the **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)**; if it is mechanically damaged, replace the entire drilling control valve block [9]. If the issue persists, stop the power pack and repair or replace the rock drill rotation motor [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function and specific part number of the main switch (Q1)?
questions.answer: The main switch (Q1) is a circuit breaker, specifically type **NZMH3-ME350-S1** (175-350 A), located in the MQ cabinet. It is used to disconnect the mains electric supply, measure the drill rig's current, and act as an overload protection device for the transformer [1-3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do the VCH, FPVC, RD, and VIU controller modules differ in function within the CAN bus system?
questions.answer:
**VCH (Valve Controller High Temp):** Used for the Boom Controller (BC), Drilling Controller (DC), and Rod Handler Controller (RC) [13].
*   **FPVC (Fast Proportional Valve Controller):** Used for the Resin controller (ARI) and DC Contactor Controller (DCC) [14].
*   **RD (Resolver-to-Digital):** Acts as the Boom Sensors converter (BS) and Feed Sensors converter (FS) for high-accuracy measurement [15].
*   **VIU (Voltage Input Unit):** Acts as the Tramming Controller (TCP), Gearbox Controller (GBC), and Mains Switchgear Sensors (MS) [16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure settings for the water flushing and brake accumulator circuits?
questions.answer: The standard flushing water pressure operates between 10-15 bar [3], with the water circuit's main pressure relief valve limiting the maximum water pressure to 25 bar [13]. For the carrier's braking system, the service brake accumulators are maintained at a pressure of 135-160 bar by the accumulator charging valve [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What module is used for the Boom Sensors converter (BS) and Feed Sensors converter (FS) on the CAN bus, and what is its main function?
questions.answer: The **RD (Resolver-to-Digital)** module is used for the **BS** and **FS** [1]. It is a general-purpose measurement unit designed for high-accuracy applications and built to meet SIL2 class safety requirements, processing resolver inputs, analog inputs, and digital I/O for the CAN interface [1], [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What type of component is used for the Control panel keypads (CP) that transmit operator commands to the system?
questions.answer: The control panel keypads (CP) are **Grayhill 3K keypads** [13]. They are vibration and impact-resistant units with an IP67 protection class, connecting to the system via a **4 pin Deutsch DT connector** [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you test the operation of the grid monitoring relay (P2) during maintenance?
questions.answer: Perform the test while charging the main batteries [1]. Open the lower hinged window in the **MQ cabinet**, push the **ESC button (1)**, and hold it down for over three seconds to start the test function [1]. Then, navigate to the display and select **-> Troubleshooting -> Battery System** [1]. If the charging is not on, the relay is working properly; if the charging remains on, the **grid monitoring relay (P2)** is faulty and must be replaced [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components serve as the primary control system power supply units, and what is their specific model?
questions.answer: The control system power supply units (A3, A4, and A5) are **QT40.241** models. They are DIN-rail mountable units that convert AC or DC input to a 27.0 VDC output. They are typically connected in parallel to provide power for the rig's 24 VDC control system [4-6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the main pressure relief valve (2.12) on the carrier, and what is its setpoint?
questions.answer: To adjust the **main pressure relief valve (2.12)**, first attach a **250 bar pressure gauge** to the measuring connector MP [1]. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve almost fully open, apply maximum revolutions to the APU circuit gear pump, and then turn the adjusting screw clockwise until the reading on the pressure gauge reaches **207 bars** [1, 2]. Finally, tighten the locking nut and return the APU circuit gear pump to idle [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components and procedures are involved if the boom functions normally, but the percussion pressure is too low or percussion does not start?
questions.answer: This issue is likely caused by the **electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14)** or the **percussion pressure compensator (20.11)** being stuck or dirty, or by blocked **orifices (20.12) or (20.13)** [5]. First, stop the power pack and check, clean, or replace valve (20.14) [6]. If this does not resolve the issue, verify that orifices (20.12) and (20.13) in the LS-line are properly in place, or remove their plugs to carefully extract, clean, and reinstall them if they are blocked [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the setpoints for the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1), and how are they adjusted?
questions.answer: The **flow controller (A)** should be set to a pressure difference of **30 bar**, and the **pressure controller (B)** should be set to **235 bar** (for the RD314 rock drill) [3-5]. To adjust the pressure controller, remove the protecting cap, loosen the locking nut, and open the adjusting screw fully [4]. Run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and turn the adjusting screw very carefully clockwise until the gauge on the pressure filter measuring point reaches **235 bar** [4, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS412 Technical Manual)

questions.question: If the variable displacement pump (1) rotates normally but the idle-run pressure differs from the standard 30 bar, and a pressure gauge installed in the LS port of the drilling-control block reads over 6 bar, which specific valves should be inspected for clogging?
questions.answer:
If a pressure gauge installed in the LS port of the drilling-control block reads over **6 bar** when the variable displacement pump (1) is in free circulation, you should inspect the **control valve for pump (25)** and the **boom-hydraulics proportional valve (31)** for clogging [1]. 

According to Section 6.2 of the Drilling Hydraulics manual (Pages 51–52), you should follow this step-by-step procedure to diagnose and resolve the issue:

1. Let the oil pressure even out before taking a reading from **pressure gauge (39)** [2].
2. Install a pressure gauge into the **LS port** of the drilling-control block [2].
3. Start the power pack and let it idle [2].
4. If the pressure in the LS port is over **6 bar**, verify if valves **(25)** or **(31)** are receiving control voltage [1].
5. **Note:** Before removing the electrical connection for the boom-hydraulics proportional valve (31), you must first open **fuse 321.8** [1].
6. Remove the electrical plugs from valves **(25)** and **(31)** [1]. 
7. If the fault persists after the plugs are removed, the cause is most likely that the valves are clogged. You must repair, clean, or change the faulty valve(s) [1].

questions.question: While diagnosing a failure in the boom's automatic parallelism, you replace the bleed nipple of chamber Y on the lift cylinder with a pressure gauge and pressurize chamber A; if the gauge rises significantly over 200 bar, what specific internal seal failure does this indicate?
questions.answer:
If the pressure gauge rises significantly over 200 bar, it indicates a **leakage through the seals of the triple chamber** in the boom swing or lift cylinder [1, 2]. 

According to Section 7.1.3 "Automatic parallelism not working properly" (Page 34 of the TBR60 Boom manual), the complete step-by-step procedure to pinpoint these faulty seals is as follows [1-3]:

1. Drive the boom to the vertical position and support it properly to work safely [3].
2. Detach the boom swing/lift cylinder piston rod head from the swing arm. Do not disconnect the hoses [3].
3. Drive the boom swing/lift cylinder to the maximum length. Observe that the feed swing/tilt cylinder will also move [3].
4. Drive the feed swing/tilt cylinder to its shortest length [3].
5. Remove the hose from the feed tilt/swing cylinder port A. Plug both the hose and the A-port (port names are marked on the cylinder next to the hose connection) [3].
6. Remove the bleed nipple of chamber Y on the lift cylinder and replace it with the pressure gauge [2].
7. Pressurize chamber A on the boom swing/lift cylinder by trying to drive it further out [2].
8. If the pressure on the gauge rises markably (over 200 bars), there is leakage through the seals of the triple chamber in the boom swing/lift cylinder, and the cylinder seals must be replaced with new ones [2].
9. Order the correct cylinder seal kit for the specified cylinder through Sandvik logistics [2].
10. After replacing the faulty seals, bleed the boom hydraulic system according to the bleeding instructions in the manual delivered with the unit [2].

questions.question: During the testing of the compressor's thermometer safety limits using a heater, which specific indicator light on the QN-panel should illuminate at 100 °C, and what component shutdowns must automatically occur when the temperature reaches 115 °C?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, during the testing of the compressor's thermometer safety limits, the red indicator light **H604** on the QN-panel must illuminate when the temperature reaches **100 °C** [1, 2]. When the temperature reaches **115 °C**, the **power pack, compressor, and water pumps** must automatically stop [2, 3].

According to Sections 5.15.15 (Compressor CTN) and 5.16.15 (Compressor CT) titled "Checking the function of the thermometer safety limits," this test should be conducted using the following step-by-step sequence [1, 4]:

1. Remove the temperature sensor from the compressor's body [1].
2. Start the power packs, compressor, and water pump [1].
3. Heat the sensor using a heater with an operation range of 0–120 °C (do not use fire) and monitor the temperature gauge [1].
4. When the temperature reaches **100 °C**, verify that the red indicator light **H604** on the QN-panel turns on [1]. 
5. When the temperature reaches **115 °C**, verify that the red indicator light **H604** remains on and that the **power pack, compressor, and water pumps** successfully stop [3, 5].

questions.question: If the drilling operations and water pump cease automatically, how can you verify whether the water pressure switch (S422) is correctly triggering the H601 indicator light by dropping the pressure below its 2.8 bar threshold for more than four seconds?
questions.answer:
To verify the operation of the water pressure switch (**S422**) and the **H601** warning indicator, follow this step-by-step procedure detailed in the manuals (referencing Sections 4.6.1, 6.1.1, and 5.13.1 for "Checking the operation of the pressure switch") [1-5]:

1. Close the water circuit using the **shut-off valve** [2, 3, 5]. 
2. When the water pressure drops below **2.8 bar**, the pressure switch should engage and illuminate the **H601** (water pressure low) warning indicator on the **QN panel** [2, 3, 5].
3. Press the pressure switch reset button (**S505**) [2, 3, 5].
4. The pressure switch is operating properly if the warning indicator **does not go off** at this point [2, 3, 5].
5. Open the **shut-off valve** [2, 3, 5].
6. The pressure switch is operating properly if the warning indicator **H601** goes off as the pressure exceeds **2.8 bar** [2, 3, 5].

questions.question: When performing the basic adjustment and max force control of the cable reel for a 70 mm² to 150 mm² cable, what must the maximum pressure (P1) be set to, and how many turns counterclockwise should the flow control valve (3.2) be opened after being fully closed?
questions.answer:
When performing the basic adjustment and max force control for a 70 mm² to 150 mm² (AWG 2/0) cable, the maximum reeling-in pressure (P1) must be set based on the specific reel type: **140 bar** for TCR 1 & TCR 2.0 E reels, and **150 bar** for TCR 2.5 E - TCR 5 and TCR 6 E reels [1, 2]. 

The adjusting screw of the cable reel flow control valve (3.2) must be opened by **4-5 turns counterclockwise** after being fully closed [3, 4].

According to Section 2, "Adjusting the reeling force according to cable size," the step-by-step sequence for adjusting the flow control valves is as follows:
1. Ensure the diesel engine and power packs are stopped before beginning the adjustment [5, 6].
2. Loosen the locking nuts of the cable reel flow control valve (3.1) and the water hose reel flow control valve (4.1) by turning them counterclockwise [5, 6].
3. Turn the adjusting screws of both flow control valves (3.1 and 4.1) fully open (counterclockwise) and lock their locking nuts [5, 6].
4. Loosen the locking nuts of the cable reel flow control valve (3.2) and the water hose reel flow control valve (4.2) by turning them counterclockwise [3, 4].
5. Turn the adjusting screw of the cable reel flow control valve (3.2) first fully closed (clockwise), then open it by 4-5 turns (counterclockwise) and lock the adjustment [3, 4].
6. Turn the adjusting screw of the water hose reel flow control valve (4.2) first fully closed (clockwise), then open it by 6-7 turns (counterclockwise) and lock the adjustment [4, 7].
7. Tighten the locking nuts of the flow control valves (3.2 and 4.2) [7, 8].

questions.question: When adjusting the main pressure relief valve (23) while running the zoom inwards, what specific pressure value should be reached on pressure gauge (39)?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the main pressure relief valve (23) while running the zoom inwards, the pressure gauge (39) should reach exactly **240 bar** [1]. 

According to Section 5.1.1 "Adjusting the main pressure relief valve (23)" (Pages 38-39 of the Drilling Hydraulics manual), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1-3]:

1. Loosen the locking nut of the main pressure relief valve (23) [2]. 
2. Rotate the main pressure relief valve (23) adjusting screw almost fully open (counterclockwise) [2]. 
3. Start the diesel engine [2]. 
4. Select the boom movements with the selector switch S78 and run the zoom inwards by pulling the joystick S77 backward (6 o'clock position) and pressing the button simultaneously [2]. 
5. Rotate the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (23) clockwise until the pressure gauge (39) shows **240 bar** [1]. 
6. Tighten the locking nut of the main pressure relief valve (23) [3].

questions.question: Which specific pressure relief valve is used to adjust the full power percussion pressure to the 150 bar target indicated on pressure gauge (39)?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the **pressure-relief valve (29)** is used to adjust the full power percussion pressure to the **150 bar** target [1].

According to Section 5.1.3 "Adjusting the percussion pressure" in the Drilling Hydraulics manual, the step-by-step procedure is as follows [2]:

**Note! Maintain shank lubrication while adjusting the percussion.** [2]

1. Turn on the percussion by turning the control lever **S75** into the forward position [2].
2. Adjust the percussion pressure to **150 bar** using the pressure-relief valve **(29)**. This pressure can be read on the pressure gauge **(39)** [2]. 
3. Lock the adjusting screw and check the adjusted pressure value [2].

questions.question: What is the correct Nitrogen (N2) gas pre-charge pressure required for the brake accumulators on TC 9-12 series drill carriers?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided Carrier manual (Sections 6.1.5, 6.1.7, and 6.1.23, pages 55-57 and 76-77), the correct Nitrogen (N2) gas pre-charge pressure for the brake accumulators on TC 9-12 series drill carriers is **80 bar** [1, 2]. The only allowable filling gas is nitrogen (N2) [3, 4]. 

If the pressure accumulators need to be filled or adjusted, the manual outlines the following step-by-step sequence:

1. Release the pressure from the brake accumulators according to the instructions for releasing accumulator pressure [3, 5]. 
2. Remove the cap **(3)** [5, 6].
3. Screw the elbow adapter **(10)** to the filling valve **(1)** [5, 6].
4. Push the quick coupling sleeve **(5)** onto the stem **(4)** [5, 6].
5. Undo/open the locking nut **(2)** [5, 6].
6. Turn the pressure regulating valve/knob **(8)** open [5, 6].
7. Open the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve/knob **(9)**. The gas bottle pressure gauge **(7)** will indicate the pressure in the bottle [5, 6].
8. Adjust the pressure slowly to **80 bar** (for TC 9-12 carriers) by turning the regulating valve **(8)**. The accumulator pressure gauge **(6)** indicates the pressure inside the accumulator [6, 7].
9. Close the filling valve **(1)** by turning/closing the locking nut **(2)** [6, 7].
10. Close the nitrogen bottle shut-off valve/knob **(9)** [6, 7].
11. Turn the pressure regulating valve/knob **(8)** open [6, 7].
12. Disconnect the quick coupling stem **(4)** and sleeve **(5)** [6, 7].
13. Release/remove the elbow adapter **(10)** from the filling valve **(1)** [7, 8].
14. Tighten the locking nut **(2)** to a torque of **20 Nm** [7, 8].
15. Refit/reinstall the cap **(3)** [7, 8].
16. After filling the pressure accumulators, you must check the brakes by performing the following test [7, 8]:
    *   Engage the parking brake [8, 9].
    *   Select the neutral gear (drive selector in middle position) [8, 9].
    *   Start the diesel engine and let it run for at least three minutes (ensure warning lights turn off) [8, 9].
    *   Shut down the diesel engine [8, 9].
    *   Switch the power on by turning the ignition switch to the middle position [8].
    *   Pump/press the brake pedal all the way down at least five times and make sure the brake pressure stays over **80 bar** (monitored on gauges **P3** and **P4**) [9, 10].

questions.question: Which potentiometer on the proportional amplifier A81 inside the logic box must be adjusted to set the LF 600 maximum feed pressure to 120 bar on gauge (40)?
questions.answer:
To set the LF 600 maximum feed pressure to **120 bar**, you must adjust the **I(max)** potentiometer on the proportional amplifier **A81** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 5.1.10 "Feed minimum/maximum pressure control, anti-jamming automatics/threading pressure control" of the Drilling Hydraulics manual (Pages 46-47), the step-by-step sequence is as follows [3-5]:

1. Turn the feed into the horizontal position [4].
2. Turn the control panel feed potentiometer **R70** into position **10** [2].
3. Push the joystick **S85** forward (12 o'clock position) to the drilling position [2].
4. Move the rock drill against the front stop by pushing joystick **S73** forward (12 o'clock position) [2, 4].
5. Keep the joystick in this position and adjust the feed maximum pressure from potentiometer **I(max)** of proportional amplifier **A81** [2]. 
6. Read the pressure on the feed pressure gauge **(40)** and adjust until it reaches the target of **120 bar** for the LF 600 feed [2]. *(Note: Rotating the potentiometer counterclockwise increases the pressure and rotating it clockwise lowers the pressure [2].)*

questions.question: When calibrating the anti-jamming automatics pressure switch (14) to 100 bar, which specific logic input channel should be monitored to verify its activation?
questions.answer:
When calibrating the anti-jamming automatics pressure switch (14) to its factory setting of **100 bar**, you should monitor logic input **ch 02.07** to verify its activation [1, 2]. 

According to Section 5.1.6 "Anti-jamming automatics pressure control" in the Drilling Hydraulics manual, the complete step-by-step sequence for this calibration is as follows:

1. Turn the anti-jamming automatics off using the selector switch **(S79)** [3].
2. Start the power pack [3].
3. Move the rock drill against the rear stopper [3].
4. Stop the power pack [3].
5. Prevent the drill rod from rotating by disconnecting the rotation hose from the hose support and plugging the hose ends [3].
6. Start the power pack [3].
7. Move the rotation lever **(S73)** to the right [3].
8. Adjust the rotation pressure-relief valve **(30)** temporarily to the required anti-jamming automatics pressure (100 bar) [3].
9. Check the adjusted pressure from the pressure gauge **(41)** [2].
10. Use an ohmmeter to adjust the anti-jamming automatics pressure switch **(14)** so that it functions with the required pressure, or check when the logic input **ch 02.07** is activated. When the adjustment is carried out correctly, the input LED will turn on and off during a single revolution of the pressure switch adjusting screw [2].
11. Adjust the rotation pressure-relief valve **(30)** back to its original value [2].
12. Tighten the lock nut of the valve **(30)** and re-check the pressure [2].
13. Stop the power pack [2].

questions.question: What is the total weight of the Sandvik DS421, and what are its exact transport and bolting lengths as defined in the technical specifications?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical specifications provided, the machine's dimensions and weight are defined as follows:

*   **Total weight:** **25,000 kg** (depending on the selected options) [1].
*   **Transport length:** **11,955 mm** [1].
*   **Bolting length:** **12,415 mm** [1].

questions.question: What is the rated power output of the HPP555 hydraulic powerpack, and what are the respective capacities of its variable displacement percussion pump and rotation gear pump?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical specifications and the hydraulic powerpack data provided in the manuals, the ratings and capacities are as follows:

*   **Rated Power Output:** The HPP555 hydraulic powerpack features a rated power output of **55 kW** [1, 2].
*   **Variable Displacement Percussion Pump (Component 3 / Component 1):** This pump, which provides oil for the percussion, feed, boom, and bolting head movements, has a displacement capacity of **100 cc** [2]. Its operational flow/pressure capacity is rated at **140 l/min at 160 bar** [1]. 
*   **Rotation Gear Pump (Component 4 / Component 2):** This constant-output pump, dedicated exclusively to the rock drill's rotation mechanism, has a displacement capacity of **33 cc** [2]. Its operational flow/pressure capacity is rated at **65 l/min at 140 bar** [1].

*(Note: The component IDs **3** and **4** reference the Powerpack Main Components list in Section 3.1 [3], while IDs **1** and **2** reference the main hydraulic circuit components [4].)*

questions.question: Which six specific pressures can be monitored using the six carrier measuring adapters located on the machine's frame?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 3.1.3 "Carrier frame parts" (Page 108 of the Carrier and Maintenance Manuals), the six specific pressures that can be monitored using the carrier measuring adapters on the frame are [1, 2]:

1. **Service brake pressure (front):** 70 bar (for TC9-12) or 80 bar (for TC7-8, NC7) [3, 4]
2. **Service brake pressure (rear):** 70 bar (for TC9-12) or 80 bar (for TC7-8, NC7) [3, 4]
3. **Parking brake pressure (front):** 30 bar (for TC7-9, NC7) or 100 bar (for TC10-12) [5, 6]
4. **Parking brake pressure (rear):** 30 bar [7, 8]
5. **Accumulators charging pressure:** 135–160 bar [9, 10]
6. **Transmission clutch pressure:** 17–19 bar [3, 8]

According to Section 6.1.22 / 5.7.22 "Maintenance procedures done as required", the step-by-step sequences to check these pressures using the measuring point assembly (284) are as follows [3, 4]:

**Checking the service brake pressure:**
1. Attach a pressure gauge to the front brake circuit's pressure inspection point **(A)** [3, 4].
2. Start the engine [3, 4].
3. Press the service brake pedal to the end of its movement path [3, 4].
4. The pressure should be **70 bar** (TC9-12) or **80 bar** (TC7–8, NC7) [3, 4].
5. Repeat the same measurement for the rear brake circuit by attaching a pressure gauge to the rear brake circuit's pressure inspection point **(B)** [3, 4].

**Checking the front axle's parking brake pressure:**
1. Attach a pressure gauge to the front axle's parking brake pressure inspection point **(C)** [5, 6].
2. Start the engine [5, 6].
3. Release the parking brake [5, 6].
4. The release pressure should be **100 bar** (TC10-12) or **30 bar** (TC7–9, NC7) [5, 6].

**Checking the rear axle's parking brake pressure:**
1. Attach a pressure gauge to the rear axle's parking brake pressure inspection point **(D)** [5, 6].
2. Start the engine [9, 10].
3. Release the parking brake [9, 10].
4. The release pressure should be **30 bar** [9, 10].

**Checking the charging oil pressure of the service brake accumulators:**
1. Attach a pressure gauge to the pressure accumulator's pressure inspection point **(E)** [9, 10].
2. Start the engine [9, 10].
3. The pressure should rise quickly to **135-160 bar** [9, 10].

*(Note: The provided source material lists the transmission clutch pressure as 17-19 bar in the functional diagrams, but does not detail a specific step-by-step text procedure for testing it at its specific adapter point [3, 8].)*

questions.question: When adjusting the rock drill percussion settings, which specific pressure relief valves must be calibrated to set the half power percussion to 100 bar and the full power percussion to 150 bar, as read on pressure gauge (39)?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided drilling hydraulics manuals, two different pressure relief valves are used to calibrate the percussion settings, which are monitored on **pressure gauge (39)**.

**Full Power Percussion (150 bar)**
The full power percussion pressure is adjusted using **pressure-relief valve (29)** [1]. 
According to Section 5.1.3 "Adjusting the percussion pressure," the step-by-step sequence is as follows:
*Note! Maintain shank lubrication while adjusting the percussion.* [1]
1. Turn on the percussion by turning the control lever **S75** into the forward position [1].
2. Adjust the percussion pressure to **150 bar** with the **pressure-relief valve (29)** [1]. This pressure can be read on the **pressure gauge (39)** [1].
3. Lock the adjusting screw and check the adjusted pressure value [2].

**Half Power (½) Percussion (100 bar)**
The half power percussion pressure is adjusted using **pressure-relief valve (28)** [2].
According to Section 5.1.4 "Adjusting the ½ percussion pressure," the step-by-step sequence is as follows:
1. Turn the ½ percussion on by pulling back the control lever **S75** [2].
2. Adjust the ½ percussion pressure to **100 bar** with the **pressure-relief valve (28)** [2]. The pressure can be read on the **pressure gauge (39)** [2].
3. Lock the adjusting screw and check the adjusted pressure value [2].

questions.question: While the maximum feed pressure during drilling is set to 120 bar via the I(max) potentiometer on proportional amplifier A81, what must the anti-jamming and thread closing pressure be set to using potentiometer R81?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided drilling hydraulics manuals, the anti-jamming automatics and threading pressure (thread closing) must be set to **70 bar** using the connection strip potentiometer **R81** [1, 2].

According to Section 5.1.10 "Feed minimum/maximum pressure control, anti-jamming automatics/threading pressure control" (Page 47), this adjustment is performed using the following step-by-step sequence [1, 3]:

1. Push the joystick **S85** forward (12 o'clock position) to the drilling position [3].
2. Move the rock drill against the front stop by pushing joystick **S73** forward (12 o'clock position) [1, 3].
3. Turn the joystick **S73** to the upper right (01.30 o'clock position) and hold the joystick in this position [1].
4. Adjust the anti-jamming automatics/threading pressure to **70 bar** (depending on the rock quality) with the adjusting screw of the connection strip potentiometer **R81**, which is located in the logic cabinet. The pressure can be read on the input pressure gauge **(40)** [1].
5. *Note: Rotating the potentiometer clockwise increases the pressure and rotating it counterclockwise lowers the pressure* [1].

questions.question: Instead of split set installation, this rig feeds steel strand for reinforcement; what must the pressure reducing valve for the steel strand feeding mechanism's tightening cylinder be adjusted to, and what is the required Nitrogen pre-charge for its accumulator?
questions.answer:
To adjust the steel strand feeding mechanism's tightening cylinder, the pressure reducing valve (**A**) must be adjusted to **100-140 bar** [1]. The required Nitrogen (N2) pre-charge for its pressure accumulator is **50 bar** [1].

According to Section 3.3.1 "Steel strand feeding unit adjustments" in the Steel strand feeding system manual, the procedure is as follows:

1.  Adjust the pressure reducing valve to **100-140 bar**. This adjustment must be made while feeding the steel strand into the hole (with joystick **S73** pushed to the 12 o’clock position) to activate the steel strand feeder tightening (**Y198**) [1].
2.  Pre-fill the pressure accumulator with Nitrogen (N2) to exactly **50 bar** [1].

questions.question: When indexing the bolting turret/head from the drilling and boom control panel, which specific PLC output coils control the bolting head rotation counterclockwise and clockwise, and which outputs control its tilt backward and forward?
questions.answer:
Based on the DS421 Drilling Controller and Operator manuals, the specific PLC output coils that control the bolting head rotation and tilt are as follows:

*   **Bolting head rotation counterclockwise (CCW):** PLC Output **OUT 05** (Pin 4), coil **Y18** [1].
*   **Bolting head rotation clockwise (CW):** PLC Output **OUT 05** (Pin 5), coil **Y19** [1].
*   **Bolting head tilting backward:** PLC Output **OUT 06** (Pin 4), coil **Y132** [2].
*   **Bolting head tilting forward:** PLC Output **OUT 06** (Pin 5), coil **Y133** [2].

According to the operation instructions, the step-by-step sequence to operate these functions from the drilling and boom control panel is:

1. Turn the Function mode selector switch (**S78**) to position **B** (or position 2) to select **Bolting head functions** [3, 4].
2. Use the Joystick for boom and bolting head controls (**S77**) to perform the desired movements [5]:
   *   **Bolting head tilt forwards:** Push the joystick (**S77**) forwards (12 o'clock position).
   *   **Bolting head tilt backwards:** Pull the joystick (**S77**) backwards (6 o'clock position).
   *   **Bolting head rotation CCW:** Move the joystick (**S77**) to the left (9 o'clock position) while simultaneously keeping the push-button (**PB**) depressed.
   *   **Bolting head rotation CW:** Move the joystick (**S77**) to the right (3 o'clock position) while simultaneously keeping the push-button (**PB**) depressed.

questions.question: When retracting the cement hose from the drilled hole (Y54 slow feed) during the grouting operation, what pressure range must the cement hose reel's pressure reducing valve be set to so that the hose winds as fast as the feed mechanism pulls it?
questions.answer:
To ensure the cement hose winds properly when being retracted from the hole, the cement hose reel's pressure reducing valve must be set to a range of **50 - 70 bar** [1]. 

According to Section 3.4 "Hydraulic circuit adjustments" (Page 20 of the Cement feeding system manual), the step-by-step sequence for this adjustment is as follows:

1. First, adjust the pumping speed of the cement pump (**Y57**) before attempting to adjust the cement hose feeding from the hole slow feed (**Y54**) [1]. 
2. Adjust the cement hose reel pressure reducing valve to the **50 - 70 bar** target [1].
3. Finally, adjust the cement hose winding in (**Y53**) using its one-way restrictor so that the hose winds at the exact same speed as the cement hose feeding mechanism feeds the hose backward [1].

questions.question: According to the bolting coverage specifications, what is the maximum operating height (H2) and width (W2) for a drill rig equipped with the CBH-6 bolting head, and what is the exact boom extension length of the TBR60 boom?
questions.answer:
Based on the technical specifications provided in the source material, the required dimensions are as follows:

*   **Bolting Coverage (CBH-6):** According to the "BOLTING COVERAGE" table, a drill rig equipped with the **CBH-6** bolting head has a maximum operating height (**H2**) of **8,400 mm** and a maximum operating width (**W2**) of **10,730 mm** [1]. 
*   **TBR60 Boom Extension:** According to the "BOLTING BOOM" specifications, the exact boom extension length of the TBR60 boom is **1,200 mm** [2].

questions.question: When checking the steering system pressure by turning the machine to the full turning angle against the end stops, what is the maximum allowed pressure that should be verified at checking point (A), and which specific adjustment screw (B, 263.01) must be turned to correct it?
questions.answer:
When checking the steering system pressure, the maximum allowed pressure that should be verified at checking point **(A)** is **140 bar** [1]. If the pressure requires correction, it must be adjusted by turning the adjustment screw **(B, 263.01)** [1, 2].

According to the "Checking the steering pressure" procedure detailed in the Carrier manual (Pages 74-75), this check must be performed when the oil is at operating temperature and the engine is running at full speed [1]. 

The complete step-by-step sequence is as follows:
1. Connect the manometer to the checking point **(A)** [1].
2. Turn the machine to the full turning angle against the end stops [1].
3. Verify that the maximum allowed pressure is **140 bar** [1].
4. If the desired pressure differs from the given value, adjust it by turning the adjustment screw **(B, 263.01)** to the desired direction [1, 2].

questions.question: When operating the hand throttle switch (SH56) on the tramming panel with the parking brake engaged and the gear in neutral, what three specific engine speed levels are sequentially activated each time the switch is temporarily turned to position (C)?
questions.answer:
When operating the hand throttle switch (**SH56**) on the right side of the tramming panel, the three specific engine speed levels that are sequentially activated are **1200 rpm**, **1400 rpm**, and **1600 rpm** [1, 2]. 

According to Section 3.3.2 "Tramming panel (DP)" in both the Maintenance Manual (Page 151) and Operator's Manual (Page 148), the hand throttle is a 3-level system. The step-by-step sequence to operate it is as follows:

1. Ensure the gear is in the **neutral position** and the **parking brake is on** [1, 2]. (The hand throttle cannot be used while driving).
2. Turn the switch to position **(B)** [1, 2]. *(Note: If the switch is in position (B) when the drill rig is started, the hand throttle will not start, but the indicator light will be on.)*
3. Turn the switch to position **(C)** for a moment. The engine speed will raise to the first level of **1200 rpm** [1, 2].
4. Turn the switch to position **(C)** a second time. The engine speed will raise to the second level of **1400 rpm** [1, 2].
5. Turn the switch to position **(C)** a third time. The engine speed will raise to the third level of **1600 rpm** [1, 2].
6. If the switch is turned to position **(C)** a fourth time, the engine speed will return to the first level of **1200 rpm** [1, 2].
7. To turn the hand throttle off, turn the switch to position **(A)** [1, 2]. Keep the switch in position (A) whenever it is not in use [1, 2].

questions.question: When preparing the machine for tramming, what exact positions must the boom and feed transfers, the steel strand reel, and the cement platforms be placed in before the jacks are raised?
questions.answer:
When preparing the machine for tramming, the components must be placed in the following exact positions according to Section 4.3.2 "Tramming position" (Operator's Manual DS421, Page 191):

*   **Boom and feed transfers:** Must be in their **rear position**. The boom and the feed must also be trammed as close to the center line of the rig, and as low as possible [1].
*   **Steel strand reel:** Must be turned to the **tramming position** [1].
*   **Cement platforms:** Must be lifted to their **upper position** [1]. 

*(Additionally, all doors and hatches must be closed and locked so they cannot open during tramming)* [1].

According to Section 4.3.6 "Setting the rig in motion" (Operator's Manual DS421, Page 196), the step-by-step sequence to prepare and raise the jacks is as follows:

1. Make sure that the rig is in the tramming position (as described above) [2].
2. Switch on the tramming lights (**S4/S5**) [2].
3. Raise the jacks. First raise the rear jacks (**SH43-SH44**), then the front jacks (**SH41-SH42**) [2].
4. Retract the front jacks (**SH40**) [2].

questions.question: If the carrier experiences a breakdown and requires towing, what mandatory mechanical connection must be used, and what are the strict maximum limits for towing speed and distance?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals (Section 7.1 of the Maintenance Manual and Section 6.1 of the Operator's Manual), the requirements for towing the carrier are as follows:

*   **Mandatory Mechanical Connection:** You must use a **fixed towing bar** [1, 2]. It is explicitly forbidden to use a rope or cable for towing the drill rig [1, 2].
*   **Maximum Towing Speed:** **3 km/h** [1, 2].
*   **Maximum Towing Distance:** **3 km** [1, 2].

According to Sections 7.1.1 and 6.1.1, "Preparing for towing," the step-by-step sequence to prepare the machine for towing is:
1. Stop the engine and disconnect the machine from the power supply [3, 4].
2. Put the wheel chocks in place [3, 4].
3. Ensure that brakes are engaged in the towing vehicle [3, 4].
4. Fasten a towing bar between the drill rig to be towed and the towing vehicle [3, 4].
5. Release the brakes of the drill rig to be towed [3, 4].

questions.question: What are the indications of a fire suppression system activation, and how can the operator respond if the machine needs to be safely moved?
questions.answer: If the fire suppression system activates (which occurs automatically at 150 °C or via manual actuation), an audiovisual alarm sounds and an electronic timer begins a 6-second delay before automatically shutting down the engine [13-15]. If the operator must move the machine in an emergency, they can press and hold the delay extension/override button on the alarm/timer box to gain an additional 20 seconds of operation, though the machine will shut down as soon as this spring-return button is released [14-16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the steps for calibrating the sensors on the TMS Data Displaying Unit?
questions.answer: To calibrate the **rotation and tilt angles**, manually point the boom to the desired **0-degree angle** and press OK on the display [21, 22]. To calibrate the **drilling depth transducer**, move the rock drill to its extreme rear position and press OK, then move it to the front limit, enter the exact distance moved in centimeters, and press OK [22]. Finally, to calibrate the **cement hose or steel cable depth**, move the hose or cable forward by at least **31 pulses**, measure the distance, input the distance in centimeters on the screen, and press OK [23, 24]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system respond to a shank lubrication failure, and what must the operator do?
questions.answer: If there is a drop in air pressure, decreased oil flow, or a low oil level (indicated by H608), the system triggers an alarm, turns on a red indicator light, automatically centers the drilling joystick, and stops drilling after a 30-second delay [9-11]. The operator will see a "Shank lubrication failure" message on the display and must center all control desk controls, investigate and resolve the root cause (such as adding oil to the SLU tank), and reset the system by restarting the drill [10-12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific valves are responsible for controlling the rock drill's feed movements?
questions.answer: The **feed control valve (7)** directs the oil flow into the feeding mechanism, while the overall feed circuit pressure is adjusted by a **proportional pressure relieving and reducing valve (11)** [3]. For high-speed movements, the **rapid feed directional valve (20)** is used, which works in conjunction with **flow control valve (21)** to adjust rapid forward speed and **flow control valve (22)** to adjust rapid backward speed [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the repair procedure for a defective CAN-High (fault code 10100) or CAN-Low (fault code 10101) connection?
questions.answer: Check the respective wire for an open circuit fault and repair or replace it if necessary [5, 6]. After repairing the wire, switch on the ignition, delete the fault memory in the ECU engine control (e.g., MR-PLD), delete the fault memory in the SG FRE, and perform a functional check [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the repair instructions if the system logs a defective CAN-High connection (SPN 625 / FMI 14, fault code 10100)?
questions.answer: For a defective CAN-High connection (**fault code 10100**), check the wire for an open circuit fault and repair or replace it if necessary [5]. After repairing the wire, switch on the ignition, delete the fault memory in the ECU engine control (e.g., **MR-PLD**), delete the fault memory in the **SG FRE**, and perform a functional check to verify the repair [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the TMS system's RD-module connect to the inclination CAN-sensor and the display unit?
questions.answer: The TMS system's **RD-module** uses the **RD-XJ6** terminal block for its CAN communications. It connects to the inclination CAN-sensor using pins **RD-XJ6:2 (CAN L)** and **RD-XJ6:4 (CAN H)**, and it communicates with the **RD-OP3** display unit using pins **RD-XJ6:3 (CAN L)** and **RD-XJ6:5 (CAN H)** [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a diesel engine that refuses to start?
questions.answer: Ensure the battery isolation switch is in the ON position, the parking brake is engaged, and the drive selector is in the middle/neutral position. Next, check the fuel level, battery condition, battery circuit main fuse F11, battery circuit fuses F12 and F13, and ensure that all emergency stop devices have been reset and that the fire suppression system is not inhibiting the start [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the feed pressures and the anti-jamming settings during drilling?
questions.answer: For the LF 600 feed, the **maximum feed pressure is set to 120 bar** using the I(max) potentiometer on the proportional amplifier A81 inside the logic box [8]. The **anti-jamming/threading pressure is adjusted to 70 bar** via the R81 potentiometer [9]. Furthermore, the **anti-jamming automatics pressure switch (14)** is factory-set to **100 bar**; if the rotation pressure exceeds this threshold for more than 0.8 seconds due to a rock fissure, the system automatically reverses the rock drill feed [7, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Why might the boom's automatic parallelism not work properly, and how is the hydraulic cylinder tested for this fault?
questions.answer: A failure in automatic parallelism is often caused by faulty seals in the triple chamber of the boom swing cylinder or lift cylinder, which can unexpectedly lower the boom [9]. To pinpoint the faulty seals, remove the bleed nipple of chamber Y on the lift cylinder and replace it with a pressure gauge [10]. Pressurize chamber A on the boom swing or lift cylinder by trying to drive it further out [10]. If the pressure gauge rises markably **over 200 bars**, there is a leakage through the triple chamber seals, and the cylinder seals must be replaced with a new kit [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the powerpack does not start or stops during operation?
questions.answer: Make sure that the main switch is on and the water pump or compressor switches are in the running position [1]. If the voltage meter does not show any reading, check the circuit breaker F317 [1, 2]. If the indicator light H617 is not lit, check the protective switch F310 of the 24 VDC feed transformer, and the circuit breaker F450 [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary hydraulic pressure settings and how are they adjusted?
questions.answer: The **idle-run pressure** is adjusted to **30 bar** by turning the variable displacement pump's flow controller A (47) [1]. The **system main pressure relief valve (23)** is set to **240 bar**; this is adjusted by turning its screw while running the boom zoom cylinder inwards and reading the pressure gauge (39) [2, 3]. **Full power percussion** is adjusted to **150 bar** using the pressure relief valve (29), while **half power percussion** is set to **100 bar** using the pressure relief valve (28) [4, 5]. The **rotation pressure** is limited to a maximum of **150 bar**, which is set by adjusting the relief valve (30) while the drill rod is physically locked from rotating [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the two standard hydraulic pumps on the Sandvik DS421 and what functions do they power?
questions.answer: The system is powered by two main pumps: a **variable displacement pump (1)** that delivers oil to the percussion, feed, boom, and bolting hydraulics circuits, and a **constant-output rotation pump (2)** that provides output exclusively for the rock drill's rotation mechanism [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose and repair an ADM2 to MR CAN link fault (SPN 625 / FMI 2, fault code 12202)?
questions.answer: This fault code indicates no communication with the MR [9, 10]. To fix it, check the engine CAN wiring and verify the software configuration to ensure that the MR parameter and the ADM2 parameter 1/01 are set to equal functionality (one wire capability) [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a J1939 CAN-interface fault (SPN 639 / FMI 2, fault code 14902) diagnosed?
questions.answer: This fault indicates that the CAN identifiers ETC#1 or ACC#1 are missing [13]. This occurs when the PGN ETC1 was received only once and did not disappear [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure setpoints for the steel strand feeding unit and the water circuit?
questions.answer: On the steel strand feeding mechanism, the **tightening cylinder pressure reducing valve is adjusted to 100-140 bar**, and its associated **pressure accumulator must be pre-filled with Nitrogen to 50 bar** [17]. In the water circuit, the **water pressure reducing valve is adjusted to 1-7 bar** (and must never exceed 25 bar) by turning its adjustment screw while the water pump is running [18, 19]. The system also utilizes a **water pressure switch (S422) set to 2.8 bar**, which will stop drilling operations if the pressure remains below this limit for more than 4 seconds [20]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the powerpack does not start and the indicator light H617 is not lit?
questions.answer: You should check the protective switch F310 of the 24 VDC feed transformer and the circuit breaker F450 [1]. If the voltage meter also fails to show any reading, you must check the circuit breaker F317 [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the oil filling pump if it fails to operate?
questions.answer: First, verify that the oil tank is not already full [3]. If the tank is not full, check if the circuit breaker F452.4 has tripped, and inspect the control circuits and wiring for any faults [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the engine malfunction indicator light (H42) to turn on regarding the CAN system?
questions.answer: The engine malfunction indicator light (H42) will come on if there is no CAN connection to the engine control unit (MR2), if the CAN data is unreasonable, or if there are active faults of medium or high priority in the carrier adaptation unit's (ADM2) fault memory [5-8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component in the OptiMine Onboard kit connects to the existing machine CAN bus to collect measurement data, and what are its specific CAN connectors?
questions.answer: The **Data management unit (Cross Core XA AI)** interfaces with the machine's CAN bus to structure and collect equipment data [7, 8]. It utilizes four specific connectors for CAN communication: **X8 (CAN 1 in)**, **X9 (CAN 1 out)**, **X10 (CAN 2 in)**, and **X11 (CAN 2 out)** [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the required pre-charge pressures for the brake accumulators and what are the steps to fill them?
questions.answer: Brake accumulators must exclusively be filled with **Nitrogen gas (N2)** [11, 12]. The correct pre-charge pressure is **65 bar for TC 7-8 / NC 7 carriers** and **80 bar for TC 9-12 carriers** [13-15]. To fill them, release all existing brake pressure, connect a nitrogen bottle to the accumulator's filling valve via an elbow adapter and quick coupling, and use the pressure regulating valve to slowly bring the accumulator gauge to the target pressure [14-16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the variable displacement pump rotates normally, but the idle-run pressure differs from the normal value of 30 bar?
questions.answer: Install a pressure gauge into the LS port of the drilling-control block and let the power pack idle [1]. If the pressure reads between 0 and 6 bar (tank pressure), the fault is likely in the adjustment of the pump's flow controller A (47) or the pump is clogged, meaning you should adjust the free-circulation pressure to the correct value using regulator A (47) [1]. If the pressure in the LS port exceeds 6 bar, the pump control valve (25) or the boom proportional flow control valve (31) might be clogged and should be cleaned or replaced [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the symptom, cause, and corrective action if the rock drill rotation fails due to the relief valve?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rock drill rotation does not function [7]. 
*   **Cause:** The rotation pressure-relief valve (30) is dirty, stuck, or incorrectly adjusted [8]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Clean, repair, or replace the valve (30). To properly adjust it, lock the drill rod or shank, start the power pack, engage the drill rotation, and adjust the valve to exactly 150 bar [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the proper procedure for testing the logic inputs and outputs if a PLC-controlled movement fails?
questions.answer: If a function is engaged but the corresponding logic LED is not lit, switch off the voltage and use an ohmmeter to measure the resistance between the logic cabinet terminal X10.5 and the logic input terminal [5]. If testing the output and the solenoid valve LED is not lit, check if 24 V is supplied to the output terminal [6]. If the 24 V voltage is present, switch off the power and measure the wiring between terminal X10.4 and the logic output terminal with an ohmmeter [6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What happens when the hydraulic oil temperature gets too hot (H610) and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: If the hydraulic oil temperature exceeds 75 °C, the H610 indicator light turns on and automatically stops the powerpack, compressor, and water pumps [1, 4, 5]. The fault clears and the indicator light turns off automatically once the oil temperature has dropped sufficiently below 75 °C, allowing the operator to safely restart the systems [1, 4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Why would the powerpack start but then stop after a while with the H610 indicator light turning on?
questions.answer: This indicates that the hydraulic oil tank temperature has risen above 75 °C [1]. The powerpacks will stop automatically to protect the system, and the fault will only clear allowing a restart when the temperature drops back down below 75 °C [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are boom control failures diagnosed?
questions.answer: First, ensure the drilling joysticks for the boom in question are in their middle position [10]. Check the control voltage to the boom proportional valve (31) [10]. If the voltage is correct, check the control pressure input on pressure gauge (39) by driving the zoom cylinder in; if pressure is present but the boom fails to move, the proportional valve (31) may be clogged [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps for CAN-High or CAN-Low connection defects (SPN 625 / FMI 14, fault codes 10100 and 10101)?
questions.answer: Fault code 10100 indicates a defective CAN-High connection, while 10101 indicates a defective CAN-Low connection [11, 12]. Check the respective wire for an open circuit fault and repair or replace it if necessary [11, 12]. After repairing, switch on the ignition, delete the fault memory in the ECU engine control (MR-PLD) and in the SG FRE, and perform a functional check [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a malfunction in the percussion system diagnosed when percussion pressure is too low?
questions.answer: Install a pressure gauge in the LS port of the pressure-relief block and feed the rock drill against the rear limit at maximum power [4]. If the pressure does not reach the defined 150 bar, the LS line orifice (24) is likely clogged or the valve (29) spool is jammed [4]. You can also check for a leaking main pressure-relief valve (23) by installing a flow meter in the variable displacement pump's pressure line while the pressure line from the rock drill is blocked [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are operating hours and supply voltages monitored on the main switchgear?
questions.answer: The system tracks usage with several specific gauges: **1P100 and 2P100** log the rock drill percussion hours for booms 1 and 2, **1P101 and 2P101** track the running hours for powerpacks 1 and 2, and **P400** monitors the compressor hours [2, 15]. The rig's incoming electrical supply is monitored using the **Supply digital voltage meter + supply A-meter (P410)** [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the CAN-unit in the PLC drilling controller, and how is it mechanically installed?
questions.answer: The **CAN-unit** (e.g., **DRM21**) integrates CAN communication capabilities into the PLC drilling controller [12]. For **CS-series** PLCs, it is mounted directly to the backplane by hooking the claw on the bottom and tightening the securing screw [13]. For **CJ-series** PLCs, which do not use a backplane, the unit is carefully aligned and connected directly to adjacent units, then locked into place using yellow sliders on the top and bottom [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you test for a faulty inclination CAN-sensor using the TMS data displaying unit?
questions.answer: Navigate to the "Troubleshoot" display (Menu → Diagnostics) and test the sensor by physically moving the boom rotation or boom tilt [7, 8]. The sensor's raw value on the display should actively change between 0 and 65535 [8]. If the values do not change, the sensor or its electrical connections (such as CAN L on Pin 2 and CAN H on Pin 4) should be inspected [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptom, cause, and corrective action if the rotation directional control valve is at fault?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rock drill rotation does not function [7]. 
*   **Cause:** The rotation directional control valve (12) is clogged or missing control voltage [8]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Check the control voltage input to the valve (12). If the voltage is correct and the rotation pressure gauge (41) shows the correct pressure, clean, repair, or change valve (12). If voltage is missing, refer to electrical troubleshooting [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a clapping powerpack main contactor diagnosed?
questions.answer: A clapping main contactor is typically caused by a power supply network that is too weak. To diagnose this, you must check the control voltage, the overall supply voltage, and ensure proper dimensioning, cross-sectional area, and length of the supply cable [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the maximum feed pressures and anti-jamming settings?
questions.answer: The feed mechanism's **maximum pressure is adjusted to 120 bar** [8]. To prevent the drill string from getting stuck, the **anti-jamming and thread closing pressure is set to 70 bar**, and the **anti-jamming pressure switch (14) activates at 100 bar** if rotation becomes difficult [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Identify the key components involved in regulating the rock drill's percussion mechanism.
questions.answer: The **percussion main valve (6)** acts as the precontrolled cartridge valve that initiates percussion, routing oil through the **pressure compensator (10)** to the **percussion mechanism (32)** [3]. The operating pressure is monitored using **pressure gauge (39)** and is set by the **pressure relief valve (28)** for half power percussion and the **pressure relief valve (29)** for full power percussion [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a feed that does not function?
questions.answer: Verify the control voltage to the feed pressure reducing proportional valve (10) [6]. If the voltage is correct, manually feed the rock drill against the front limit and check the feed pressure gauge (40) [6, 7]. If pressure is indicated, the proportional valve (10) may be clogged [7]. You should also check the control voltage to the feed directional control valve (7) and observe pressure gauge (39) when feeding against the rear limit [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is responsible for cutting off the main power supply, and what component provides external single-phase power?
questions.answer: The **Main switch (Q100)** cuts off the power supply to the rig and features thermal and magnetic tripping to protect the main panel's internal wiring [1]. The **1-phase socket outlet (X300)** provides external power and is equipped with a 5 mA ground fault sensing unit [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined operating pressures for the drilling and rotation circuits?
questions.answer: Full power percussion is set to 150 bar** using the pressure relief valve (29), while **half power percussion operates at 100 bar** via the pressure relief valve (28) [8, 9]. The **rotation pressure is limited to a maximum of 150 bar** by its designated pressure relief valve (30) [8, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the powerpack starts normally but stops after a while?
questions.answer: This usually indicates a thermal or fluid level protective shutdown. Check if the compressor air temperature has exceeded 115 °C (illuminating H604), the hydraulic oil tank temperature has risen above 75 °C (illuminating H610), or if the hydraulic or shank lubrication oil levels have dropped below their minimums (illuminating H602 or H608). Also, verify that the compressor or water pump motors are not overloaded [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: When inspecting a physical CAN bus connection for wiring faults, what standard pinout configuration should be verified?
questions.answer: When checking the CAN bus wiring, verify the connections against this standard layout: Pin 1 is Vcc, Pin 2 is CAN Low, Pin 3 is Ground, Pin 4 is CAN High, and Pin 5 is the Shield (ground) [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the low hydraulic oil level alarm (H602) and how should the operator respond?
questions.answer: The H602 indicator light turns on and stops the powerpack, compressor, and water pumps if the hydraulic fluid drops below the minimum level for more than three seconds [1-3]. The operator must add a sufficient amount of hydraulic oil and press the pressure switch reset button (S505) to turn off the indicator light and allow the system to be restarted [1-3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the rock drill feed when it fails to function?
questions.answer: First, check the control voltage to the feed pressure reducing proportional valve (10) [3]. If the voltage is correct, manually feed the rock drill against the front limit and check if pressure is indicated on the feed pressure gauge (40) [3, 4]. If pressure is shown on the gauge (40), the feed pressure reducing proportional valve (10) is likely clogged and must be cleaned, repaired, or changed [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the low water pressure warning (H601) indicate, and what actions are required?
questions.answer: The H601 warning light illuminates and the pressure control system stops the drilling if the flushing water pressure remains below 2.8 bar for more than four seconds [6-8]. The operator should press the acknowledgement button (S505) to turn off the light [7, 8]. If the pressure remains low for over a minute, the water pump will also automatically stop, requiring the operator to press S505 and then manually restart the water pump using switch S501 [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a powerpack that does not start or fails to indicate voltage?
questions.answer: First check that the main switch is on and the water pump/compressor switches are in the running position. If the voltage meter shows no reading, check the circuit breaker F317. If the indicator light H617 is not lit, check the protective switch F310 of the 24 VDC feed transformer and the circuit breaker F450 [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration requirements and purity standards for the hydraulic oil?
questions.answer: The system requires **20 µm absolute filtration for the pressure line** from the variable displacement pump, and **10 µm absolute filtration for the common return line** [3, 11, 12]. To maintain trouble-free operation, the recommended oil purity classification follows the **17/13 ISO standard** [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the hydraulic oil tank capacity and how is the fluid cooled?
