questions.answer: The hydraulic oil tank has a volume of **270 liters** [3]. To prevent the oil from overheating, the return flow passes through an **OW30 (30 kW) water-actuated oil cooler** before re-entering the tank [3, 13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary control units that communicate over the SAE J1939 CAN link to manage engine and vehicle functions?
questions.answer: The primary units are the engine control unit, referred to as the **MR2** or **PLD-MR**, and the vehicle control unit, known as the **ADM2** [1-4]. They communicate over the engine CAN link to monitor and control various operational parameters, and a loss of this communication triggers specific J1939 CAN interface faults, such as fault code 12202 [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the relays 1K101, 1K112, K77, and K320 in the electrical system?
questions.answer: 1K101** serves as the auxiliary starter relay for the boom 1 powerpack [9]. **1K112** is the thermistor relay for temperature control of the boom 1 powerpack electric motor [9]. **K77** acts as the emergency stop relay [10], and **K320** is the phase sequence control relay that prevents the motors from starting if the three-phase current has an incorrect direction of rotation [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the logic inputs and outputs if a rig movement fails?
questions.answer: Turn the corresponding control panel switch or joystick to the operating position and check if the logic LED is lit [3]. If not, switch off the voltage and use an ohmmeter to measure the resistance between logic cabinet terminal X10.5 and the logic input terminal being checked [3]. If you are testing the output and the solenoid valve LED is not lit, verify that 24 V is supplied to the output terminal; if voltage is present, switch off the power and measure the wiring between terminal X10.4 and the logic output terminal [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the powerpack main contactor to clap, and what should be inspected?
questions.answer: Main contactor clapping is typically caused by a power supply network that is too weak [4]. You must check the control voltage, the overall supply voltage, the dimensioning of the supply network, and the cross-sectional area and length of the supply cable [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components protect the main hydraulic circuit from overpressure and control the boom's movement speed?
questions.answer: The overall hydraulic circuit is protected by the **main pressure relief valve (23)** [4]. Meanwhile, the movement speed of the boom is specifically regulated by the **boom proportional flow control valve (31)** [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you determine if a leaking system main pressure-relief valve is the cause of insufficient pump output?
questions.answer: Install a flow meter in the pressure line of the variable displacement pump (1) and block the pressure line leading to the rock drill [7]. Start the power pack and turn the percussion on [7]. If the flow meter indicates a flow of several liters, the fault is most likely a leak in the system's main pressure-relief valve (23) [7]. To fix the issue, you must clean, repair, or replace the main pressure-relief valve (23) [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot an ADM2 to MR CAN link fault (SPN 625 / FMI 2, fault code 12202) indicating no communication?
questions.answer: To resolve a "no communication with MR" fault (**12202**), you must first check the engine CAN wiring for any physical issues [4]. Next, check the software configuration: ensure that the MR parameter and the ADM2 parameter **1/01** are set to equal functionality, specifically configuring them for "one wire capability" [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components make up the rotation control and monitoring system?
questions.answer: The **rotation control valve (12)** manages the oil flow directed into the **rotation mechanism (34)** [3, 4]. The rotation pressure is limited by the **pressure relief valve (30)** and is visually monitored on **pressure gauge (41)** [4, 5]. Additionally, the **anti-jamming automatics pressure switch (14)** constantly monitors this rotation circuit pressure to reverse the feed if the drill rod begins to get stuck [4, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components provide short circuit protection and overload triggering for the boom powerpacks?
questions.answer: The **Motor protector switches (1F100 and 2F100)** provide short circuit protection for boom 1 and boom 2 [3]. The **Motor protector switch+contactors/starters (1FK100 and 2FK100)** handle the starting of the powerpacks and include overload triggering, with the thermal switch's triggering current set to 1.2 times the nominal current found on the motor's type plate [4]. Alternatively, optional soft starters can be used for smooth starting and electronic overload protection [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the working lights fail to illuminate?
questions.answer: Check if the working light bulb is burnt or if the lighting plug is disconnected [14]. You should also inspect the lighting transformer’s protective fuse F310, the working lights circuit breaker F314, and the fault current protector switch F311 [14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the engine malfunction indicator light (H42) comes on due to a CAN communication issue?
questions.answer: The engine malfunction indicator light (**H42**) will illuminate if there is no CAN connection to the engine control unit (**MR2**) or if the CAN data is unreasonable [1]. To troubleshoot, observe the main instrument's LCD matrix display; if a new diagnostic trouble code (DTC) is received, the display will automatically shift to the CAN fault code screen [2]. You can then read the specific **Suspect Parameter Number (SPN)** and **Failure Mode Identifier (FMI)** from the buffer to identify the exact cause [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptom, cause, and corrective action if the main percussion valve fails?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion does not function [3]. 
*   **Cause:** The main percussion valve (6) is clogged or is not receiving control voltage [3]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** First, check if the valve receives control voltage. If the voltage is correct, start the power pack and engage the percussion. If the pressure on gauge (39) is correct, the valve (6) is likely clogged and must be cleaned, repaired, or changed. If there is no control voltage, perform electrical troubleshooting [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the hydraulic pump does not operate or fails to reach the required idle-run pressure?
questions.answer: Check if the electric motor has adequate input voltage and if the pump rotates [1]. If the pump rotates normally but the idle-run pressure differs from 30 bar, install a pressure gauge in the LS port of the drilling-control block [2]. An LS port pressure between 0 to 6 bar indicates a fault in the adjustment of the pump regulator A (47) or a clogged pump, while a pressure over 6 bar indicates clogged valves (25 or 31) [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the standby and main system pressure settings for the variable displacement pump?
questions.answer: When idling, the variable displacement pump's **stand-by pressure is set to 30 bar** [7, 8]. During operation, the pump's **pressure control valve limits pressure to 220 bar**, while the **system main pressure-relief valve (23) is set to 240 bar** to protect the overall circuit [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the terminator resistor in the OptiMine CAN bus installation, and where is it connected?
questions.answer: The terminator resistor ensures the proper electrical resistance on the CAN bus, which should measure exactly **60 ohms** across the CAN H and CAN L connections when power is isolated [14, 15]. During the OptiMine kit installation, a terminator resistor is added to the **"CAN 2 out" (X11)** connector on the Data management unit, and the original terminal resistor must be removed from the driving panel connector (**DP-2X54**) so that there are only two terminating resistances on the entire machine CAN bus [14-17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the symptom, cause, and corrective action if the percussion pressure is too low or fails to function due to the pressure-relief valve?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion does not function or percussion pressure is too low [1]. 
*   **Cause:** The percussion pressure-relief valve (29) does not adjust, spool is jammed, or the load-sensing (LS) line orifice (24) is clogged [1, 2]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Install a pressure gauge in the LS port of the pressure-relief block and feed the rock drill against the rear limit at maximum power. If the pressure does not rise to the factory setting of 150 bar, clean the orifice (24) by drilling it out, or clean, repair, or replace the valve (29) [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the working lights fail to turn on?
questions.answer: Check for burnt bulbs or disconnected lighting plugs, then inspect the lighting transformer's protective fuse F310, the working lights circuit breaker F314, and the fault current protector switch F311. Additionally, verify circuit breaker F317 for the 110...120 V control voltage, and check the 24 VDC power source protective switch F318 and circuit breaker F450 [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a CAN communication failure with the engine control unit (MR2) diagnosed?
questions.answer: A loss of CAN connection to the engine control unit (MR2), or unreasonable CAN data, will illuminate the engine malfunction indicator light (H42) [1]. To diagnose the exact cause, observe the main instrument's LCD matrix display; if a new diagnostic trouble code (DTC) is received, the display will automatically shift to the CAN fault code screen to show the specific Suspect Parameter Number (SPN) and Failure Mode Identifier (FMI) [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the symptom, cause, and corrective action if the feed system fails due to the proportional valve?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The rock drill feed does not function [5]. 
*   **Cause:** The feed pressure reducing proportional valve (10) is clogged or lacks control voltage [5, 6]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Verify the control voltage amount from the drilling control. If it is correct, manually feed the rock drill against the front limit. If pressure appears on the feed pressure gauge (40), the valve (10) is likely clogged and must be cleaned, repaired, or replaced. If the voltage is incorrect, refer to electrical troubleshooting [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptom, cause, and corrective action when the feed directional control valve malfunctions?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** The feed does not function [5, 6]. 
*   **Cause:** The feed directional control valve (7) is clogged or lacks control voltage [6, 7]. 
*   **Corrective Action:** Check the control voltage input. Manually feed the rock drill against the rear limit. If pressure is indicated on gauge (39), the valve (7) is likely clogged and should be cleaned, repaired, or changed. If there is no control voltage, inspect the electrical system [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Identify the sensors used to monitor hydraulic oil level, oil temperature, and compressor air temperature.
questions.answer: The **Oil level switch (S420)** monitors the hydraulic fluid, providing switching points for a low-level alarm and the oil filling pump [7]. The **Oil temperature switch and gauge (S424)** monitors the hydraulic oil, triggering an alarm and stopping the rig at 75 °C, while also bypassing oil filter monitoring when the oil is cold (below 30 °C) [7]. The **Temperature switch (S441)** monitors the compressor's output air [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the rock drill rotation fails to function?
questions.answer: Check the control voltage to the rotation directional control valve (12) and the pressure reading on gauge (41) [8]. If the voltage is correct, the rotation pressure-relief valve (30) might be dirty, stuck, or incorrectly adjusted [9]. This can be diagnosed by locking the drill rod, engaging rotation, and attempting to adjust the relief valve (30) to exactly 150 bar [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific components on the drilling control panel and inside the PLC box are used to adjust the feed force and rotation speeds?
questions.answer: On the control panel, the **Feed force adjustment knob (R70)** is used to manually adjust the feed force during drilling [12, 13]. Inside the logic box, proportional amplifiers process these signals: **A81** is the proportional amplifier for the feed pressure (working with potentiometer **R81** for anti-jamming), and **A82** is the proportional amplifier for rotation speed, which uses potentiometers **R82.1** to set the drilling rotation limit and **R82.2** for the threading rotation limit [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: When inspecting a physical CAN bus connection for wiring faults, what is the standard pinout configuration to verify?
questions.answer: When checking the CAN bus wiring for correct pin assignments or shorts, verify the connections against the standard layout: **Pin 1** is Vcc, **Pin 2** is CAN Low, **Pin 3** is Ground, **Pin 4** is CAN High, and **Pin 5** is the Shield (ground) [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the hydraulic pump capacities and flow rates for the main systems?
questions.answer: The system utilizes a **100 cc variable displacement pump** to power the percussion, feed, boom, and bolting head movements, delivering **140 l/min at 160 bar** [1-3]. A separate **33 cc constant-output gear pump** drives the rotation circuit, providing **65 l/min at 140 bar** [2-4]. During active drilling at 150 bar, the normal oil consumption is **85 to 95 l/min for the percussion mechanism** and **2 to 6 l/min for the feed** [5, 6]. If equipped with an optional hydraulic air conditioning pump, it provides an additional **37 l/min at 150 bar** [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot an ADM2 to MR CAN link fault indicating no communication (fault code 12202)?
questions.answer: First, check the engine CAN wiring for physical faults [3]. Next, check the software configuration to ensure that the MR parameter and the ADM2 parameter 1/01 are both set to equal functionality, specifically configured for "one wire capability" [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a suspected failure of the inclination CAN-sensor on the TMS data displaying unit?
questions.answer: Navigate to the "Troubleshoot" display via the Menu (Menu → Diagnostics) [7]. Test the sensor by physically moving the boom rotation and boom tilt; the raw value on the display should change between **0 and 65535** [8]. If the values do not change, check the electrical connections at the RD-module terminal block, specifically verifying **RD-XJ6:2 (CAN L)**, **RD-XJ6:4 (CAN H)**, and **RD-XJ6:1 (VS)** for the inclination CAN-sensor [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the steps to diagnose and repair rotation failure caused by the rotation pressure-relief valve?
questions.answer: If rotation does not function, the rotation pressure-relief valve (30) may be dirty, stuck, or incorrectly adjusted [5]. To resolve this, lock the drill rod or shank, start the power pack, and engage the drill rotation [6]. Adjust the rotation pressure-relief valve (30) until the rotation pressure gauge (41) reads exactly **150 bar** [5, 6]. If the valve does not respond or the issue persists, clean, repair, or replace the pressure-relief valve (30) [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS421 Technical Manual)

questions.question: When troubleshooting excessively low feed pressure where the load sensing line at pump 1 fails to reach 210 bar, how do you determine whether the fault lies with the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.22) or the feed port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19) before performing their respective 200 bar and 240 bar calibrations?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.10 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" (Page 57 of the Drilling hydraulics DS422i manual), you can determine the source of the fault by following this step-by-step diagnostic procedure:

1. **Connect a pressure gauge** to the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) [1].
2. **Disconnect the electric connector** from the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) [1]. 
3. **Run the feed** against the rear end stopper [1].
4. **Check the pressure** at the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) [1]. The pressure should reach approximately 210 bar [1]. 

**Determining the Fault:**
* **If the pressure differs essentially from 210 bar:** It is likely that the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) is stuck [1]. You must stop the power pack to check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the valve (20.22) [2]. 
* **If the pressure reaches approximately 210 bar** (either initially or after cleaning/replacing valve 20.22) but the feed pressure issue persists: The manual states that either the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18) or the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) may be faulty [2, 3]. Only then do you proceed to check, clean, replace, and perform the 200 bar and 240 bar calibrations for those specific valves [3].

questions.question: A Cummins engine enters Machine Constrained Operation and logs fault code 5939; what specific datalink and component communication pathway must be diagnosed for an abnormal update rate or invalid data transfer rate?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Cummins engine fault codes" section (Page 50 of 62) in the engine manual, when fault code 5939 (J1939 SPN 520968, FMI 9, Amber Lamp) is logged, you must diagnose the **J1939 data link between the ECM (Engine Control Module) and the machine electronic control unit** [1]. 

This code triggers a "Machine Constrained Operation" due to an abnormal update rate, signifying that no communication or an invalid data transfer rate has been detected on this specific communication pathway [1].

questions.question: If the RD414 rock drill experiences vibrating percussion pressure hoses—indicating a potential accumulator failure—what are the correct gas pre-charge pressures for the high-pressure, low-pressure, and stabilizer accumulators that must be verified, and what is the torque spec for their filling valves?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, here are the required pressures, torque specifications, and step-by-step procedures for the rock drill accumulators.

**Accumulator Gas Pre-Charge Pressures**
According to Section 5.2.17 "Pressure accumulator filling pressures" (Maintenance Manual, page 208), the correct nitrogen (N2) gas pre-charge pressures for the RD414 accumulators are [1, 2]:
*   **High-pressure accumulator:** 40 bar
*   **Low-pressure accumulator:** 4 bar
*   **Stabilizer accumulator:** 30 bar

*Note: Vibrating percussion pressure hoses are specifically noted as a symptom of empty high-pressure accumulator(s), which causes cavitation and damages the rock drill (Section 5.2.13, page 203) [3].*

**Filling Valve Torque Specifications & Verification Procedure**
According to Section 5.2.12 "Checking the accumulator filling valve and cover plug condition" (Maintenance Manual, page 202), the condition and torque of the filling valves must be checked using the following steps [3-5]:
1. Check that the **filling valve (4)** is tightened to the accumulator body. The correct tightening torque is **40 Nm** [4]. 
2. Verify that there is a **rubber protection cap (1)** (optional) or **metal cap (2)** protecting the filling valve thread. Replace the cap if it is damaged or missing [5].
3. Remove the rubber protection cap (1) or metal cap (2) [5]. 
4. Visually inspect the filling valve and its parts for any damage. *(Note: Do not remove the filling valve from a pressurized accumulator!)* [5].
5. Check that the **locking nut (3)** is tightened to exactly **15 Nm** [3].
6. Reinstall the rubber protection cap (1) or metal cap (2) [3]. 

Furthermore, checking the accumulator charge gas pressure requires a special toolkit gauge (0-100 bar for high-pressure, 0-10 bar for low-pressure) [6]. The locking nut (3) is loosened to check the pressure reading and re-tightened to **15 Nm** using a torque wrench once the check or refilling is complete [6, 7].

questions.question: When the percussion is engaged but the percussion pressure gauge shows no reading, and you rule out the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) and LS-line orifices (20.12 and 20.13), what is the diagnostic procedure to check if the percussion selector valve (20.9) or percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.5 "Percussion is not working" (Page 53 of the Drilling hydraulics DS422i manual), if the percussion is turned on and the electric and control systems are operating properly, but the percussion pressure gauge on the main view does not show any reading, it is likely that either the percussion selector valve (20.9) or the percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck [1]. 

To diagnose and resolve this issue, follow this step-by-step procedure:
1. Stop the power pack [2].
2. Clean, check and, if necessary, replace the faulty valve(s) (20.9 and/or 20.10) [2].

questions.question: When adjusting the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) to its 220 bar specification, what specific engine speed and measuring connector (MPS) conditions are required during the calibration?
questions.answer:
The calibration of the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) requires the use of maximum diesel engine rpm and the attachment of a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector MPS [1]. 

According to Section 4.7.4 (pages 83–84), the step-by-step adjustment sequence is as follows:
1. Attach a 250 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector MPS [1].
2. Loosen the locking nut from the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9) and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise fully open [1].
3. Start the diesel engine [1].
4. Push the pressurizing stud (10.23) and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the up position to pressurize the carrier hydraulics [1, 2].
5. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm [2].
6. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (10.9) clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge is 220 bars [2].
7. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (10.9) [2].
8. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle [2].
9. Push the pressurizing stud (10.23) and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the down position, then check from the pressure gauge that the pressure level drops to the free circulation level (less than 30 bars) [2].
10. Shut down the engine [3].
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector MPS [3].

questions.question: During the calibration of the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8), why must the pressure at measuring point MPB temporarily be monitored not to exceed 205 bar before dropping it to exactly 200 bar?
questions.answer:
During the calibration of the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8), you must temporarily monitor the pressure at measuring point MPB so it does not exceed **205 bar** while turning the adjusting screw fully clockwise [1]. **If the pressure tends to exceed 205 bar, you must use the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) to reduce the pressure, which allows you to safely turn the adjusting screw of valve (10.8) fully closed** [1]. This safety measure ensures that the system pressure does not spike uncontrollably before establishing the maximum system limit at measuring point MCR, because the absolute **maximum pressure level allowed to the brake accumulators is 210 bar** [2]. Once this 210 bar limit is set at MCR, you can safely loosen valve (10.8) until the MPB pressure drops to the final **200 bar** specification [2].

According to Section 4.7.7 "Adjusting brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)" (Drill carrier C400, C900, pages 86–87), the complete step-by-step sequence is:

1. Unplug the electrical connectors from the brake circuit retarder control valve (**10.16/Y344**) and the carrier functions pressurization control valve (**10.18/Y167**) [3].
2. Connect the electrical connector **Y167** to the solenoid of valve (**10.16**), leaving **Y344** unplugged [3].
3. Attach 250 bar pressure gauges to measuring connectors **MPB** and **MCR** [3].
4. Loosen the locking nuts on the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (**10.8**) and the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (**10.15**) [1].
5. Start the diesel engine [1].
6. Run the boom zoom function backwards to activate **Y167** until the adjustments for valves (**10.8** and **10.15**) are locked [1].
7. Apply shortly the maximum diesel engine rpm [1].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of valve (**10.8**) fully clockwise, but **strictly observe that the reading at MPB does not exceed 205 bar**. If it tends to exceed 205 bar, use valve (**10.15**) to reduce the pressure so you can turn valve (**10.8**) fully closed [1].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of valve (**10.15**) until the reading at **MCR is 210 bar** (the maximum allowed to brake accumulators) [2].
10. Turn the adjusting screw of valve (**10.8**) counterclockwise until the reading at **MPB drops to 200 bar** [2]. 
11. Tighten the locking nut of valve (**10.8**) [2].
12. Turn the adjusting screw of valve (**10.15**) until the reading at **MCR is 160 bar** [2].
13. Tighten the locking nut of valve (**10.15**) [4].
14. Release the boom zoom function, return the diesel engine rpm to idle, and shut down the engine [4].
15. Remove the pressure gauges and return the electrical connectors to their original valves [4].

questions.question: For the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1), how do you correctly calibrate the flow controller (A) to a 30 bar pressure difference and the pressure controller (B) to a 250 bar setpoint for the RD414 rock drill?
questions.answer:
Before beginning the adjustments, ensure the hydraulic oil temperature is between 40-50 °C and that the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) is turned almost fully open (counterclockwise) [1]. 

According to Section 5.1.2 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)" (Pages 40-41), the correct step-by-step calibration procedures are as follows:

**Adjusting the pressure controller (B) to 250 bar for the RD414:**
1. Remove the protecting cap from the pressure controller (B) and loosen the locking nut on the pressure controller (B) adjusting screw [2, 3].
2. Open the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
3. Run the boom zoom function against the rear stopper and read the pressure from the pressure gauge connected to the pressure filter measuring point [3].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) very carefully clockwise while running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper until the pressure gauge shows the correct pressure value of 250 bar for the RD414 [2, 3]. Avoid raising the pressure above 250 bar. If the pressure rises too high, loosen the adjusting screw and wait for the reading to stabilize, as the pressure drop can be very slow [4].
5. Release the boom zoom function [4].
6. Tighten the locking nut of the pressure controller (B) adjusting screw [4].
7. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure setting again by running the boom zoom function against the rear stopper [4].

**Adjusting the flow controller (A) to a 30 bar pressure difference:**
1. Ensure you have pressure gauges connected to the LS-line (flow controller port X) and the pump (1) pressure filter measuring point [5].
2. Remove the protecting cap from the flow controller (A) and loosen the locking nut on the flow controller (A) adjusting screw [6].
3. Open the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [6].
4. Read the pressure difference (pump operating pressure minus LS-line pressure) from the two pressure gauges [6].
5. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) very carefully clockwise until the pressure difference is exactly 30 bar [6]. Avoid a pressure difference of more than 30 bar. If it rises too high, loosen the adjusting screw and wait for the reading on the pressure filter gauge to stabilize [7].
6. Tighten the locking nut of the flow controller (A) adjusting screw [7].
7. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure difference again to verify the 30 bar setpoint [7].

questions.question: What is the procedure to adjust the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2) so its flow controller (A) achieves a 20-23 bar pressure difference and its pressure controller (B) reaches the 200 bar setpoint?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the procedure to check and adjust the rotation circuit variable displacement pump (2) is detailed in Sections 5.1.3 and 5.1.4 of the "Drilling hydraulics DS422i" manual (Pages 41–42). 

Here is the step-by-step sequence for preparation and calibration:

**Preparation (Section 5.1.3)**
1. Plug the hoses going to the rock drill rotation between the drilling block and the rock drill [1].
2. Connect pressure gauges to the LS-line (flow controller port X) and the pump (2) check valve block measuring point [1].

**Adjusting the Pressure Controller (B) to 200 bar (Section 5.1.4)**
1. Remove the protecting cap from the pressure controller (B) and loosen the locking nut on its adjusting screw [2].
2. Open the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) fully open by turning it counterclockwise [2].
3. Run the rock drill rotation against the plug and read the pump (2) pressure from the pressure gauge connected to the check valve block [3].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) very carefully clockwise while running the rock drill rotation toward the plug until the pressure gauge shows the correct 200 bar pressure value [2, 3].
5. Release the rock drill rotation function [3].
6. Lock the adjustment of the pressure controller (B) with the locking nut [3].
7. After tightening the locking nut, verify the pressure setting again by running the rock drill rotation toward the plug [3].

**Adjusting the Flow Controller (A)**
*(Note: Section 6.4 and the checking procedure in 5.1.3 state the correct target pressure difference for flow controller A is 20-23 bar [1, 4]. However, step 4 in the manual's adjustment sequence explicitly writes "30 bar", which may be a typo in the original text. The steps below reflect the manual's exact written sequence.)*
1. Remove the protecting cap from the flow controller (A) and loosen the locking nut on its adjusting screw [3].
2. Open the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) almost fully open by turning it counterclockwise [3].
3. Read the pressure difference (pump operating pressure minus LS-line pressure) from the pump's (2) two pressure gauges [5].
4. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) very carefully clockwise to achieve the required pressure difference (the manual states to turn it until the difference is 30 bar, though the specified operating target is 20-23 bar) [1, 4, 5].
5. Lock the adjustment of the flow controller (A) with the locking nut [6].
6. After tightening the locking nut, check the pressure difference again to confirm the setting [6].

questions.question: How do you properly adjust the mine's inlet water pressure using the pressure reducing valve (1) to reach the 2-7 bar setpoint, ensuring the B230P pressure sensor reads under the 25 bar limit?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.17.7 "Adjusting the mine's inlet pressure" in the Operator's Manual DS422i - StageV (Page 302), you can adjust the mine's inlet pressure before the water booster pump by following this step-by-step procedure [1]:

1. Open the shut-off valve (**2**) [1].
2. Turn the knob (**3**) on the pressure reducing valve (**1**) fully open [1].
3. Start the water booster pump [1].
4. Turn the knob (**3**) to adjust the pressure to the **2-7 bar** setpoint according to drilling conditions [1]. Turning the knob clockwise increases the pressure, while turning it counterclockwise decreases the pressure [1]. Verify the value on the pressure gauge (**4**) [1].
5. On the display, select **Menu -> Troubleshooting -> Compressor and Water Pump** and check that the pressure sensor (**B230P**) value reads under **25 bars** [1]. 

*Note: The total water circuit flushing pressure consists of the mine's inlet pressure and the water booster pump pressure combined, which is why the sensor (B230P) located after the water booster pump must not exceed the 25 bar limit [1].*

questions.question: What are the specific transport and bolting dimensions (width, height, and length) as well as the total weight of the Sandvik DS422i drill rig?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Technical Specification" document for the Sandvik DS422i, the specific transport and bolting dimensions, as well as the total weight, are defined as follows:

*   **Transport / Bolting Width:** 2,730 mm / 3,290 mm [1]
*   **Transport Height:** 3,050 mm [1]
*   **Transport / Bolting Length:** 13,800 mm / 14,000 mm [1]
*   **Turning width (T-section):** 4,100 mm [1]
*   **Total Weight:** 29,000 kg (depending on the options equipped) [1]

questions.question: What is the rated capacity of the C400/C900 hydraulic oil tank, and which specific Sandvik oil is recommended for first filling in cold ambient temperatures?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Filling capacities" sections of the manuals, the rated capacity of the C400/C900 hydraulic oil tank is **270 liters** [1, 2]. 

For the first filling in cold ambient temperatures, the specific recommended oil is **Sandvik OH46** [1, 2].

questions.question: Which specific valve ID within the steering and brake control manifold functions as the steering circuit free circulation cut-off, retarder, and fan valve?
questions.answer:
Within the steering and brake control manifold (10), the specific valve that functions as the steering circuit free circulation cut-off, retarder, and fan valve is **valve 10.12** [1, 2]. 

According to the "Components (steering system)" table on Page 30 of the Drill carrier C400, C900 manual, its primary function is to direct the oil to the hydraulic oil receiver or to the secondary circuit by closing the tank connection [1, 3].

questions.question: When calibrating the percussion/feed circuit, why must the pressure controller (B) of variable displacement pump 1 temporarily be adjusted to 280 bar before loosening the main pressure relief valve (20.25) to establish its final 270 bar maximum setpoint?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.2 "Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve" (Pages 43–44 of the Drilling hydraulics DS422i manual), the pressure controller (B) of the variable displacement pump (1) must temporarily be set to **280 bar** to raise the system's constant pressure above the target relief setting [1]. By doing this, when you subsequently loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.25), it will actively begin to restrict the pressure (indicated by a "fizzing" sound) and bring the pressure reading on the gauge down to exactly the **270 bar** maximum limit [1]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for this calibration:

1. Stop the power pack [2].
2. Loosen the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25) [2].
3. Tighten the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.25) almost to its end (over 270 bar) [2].
4. Remove the caps from the flow controller (A) and the pressure controller (B) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) and undo the locking nuts of their adjusting spindles [3].
5. Open the adjusting screws of the pressure controller (B) and the flow controller (A) almost fully open (counterclockwise) [3].
6. Connect a pressure gauge to the pressure measuring point (MP2) of the drilling control valve block (20) [3].
7. Start the power pack [1].
8. Turn the adjusting screw of the flow controller (A) fully closed (clockwise) so that the pump operates at constant pressure [1].
9. Turn the adjusting screw of the pressure controller (B) clockwise until the pressure gauge shows **280 bar** [1].
10. Loosen the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.25) until the adjusting begins to effect. The valve will begin to fizz when restricting the pressure and the pressure value on the gauge will drop to **270 bar** [1].
11. Re-adjust the values of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) to their normal operating settings (as instructed in section *Adjusting the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1)*) [1].
12. Tighten the locking nut of the adjusting screw of the main pressure relief valve (20.25) [4].
13. Stop the power pack [4].

*Note: The hydraulic system gets warmer while the main pressure relief valve restricts pressure, so you must take care that the oil flow does not pass through the main pressure relief valve for a long time during this procedure [4].*

questions.question: During drilling or rod handling, if the feed pressure is incorrectly limited, how do you diagnose whether the fault lies with the 250 bar electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.22) or the mechanical feed port A and B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 set to 200 bar and 20.19 set to 240 bar)?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 6.10 "Feed / fast feed pressure is too low" in the Drilling hydraulics DS422i manual (Pages 57–58), you can diagnose whether the fault lies with the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) or the mechanical shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 and 20.19) by following this step-by-step procedure [1-5]:

**Diagnostic Sequence:**
1. Connect a pressure gauge to the load sensing line measuring connector (**LS**) of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) [2].
2. Disconnect the electric connector from the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (**20.22**) [2].
3. Run the feed against the rear end stopper [2].
4. Check the pressure reading at the load sensing line measuring connector (LS) [2]. The pressure should reach approximately **210 bar** [2]. 

**Determining the Fault:**

*   **If the fault lies with the electro-proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.22):** The pressure will differ essentially from the expected 210 bar, indicating that valve (20.22) is stuck [2]. You must stop the power pack, then check, clean, and, if necessary, replace the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) [2, 3]. Run the feed against the rear stopper again to verify the pressure reaches approximately 210 bar before reconnecting the electric connector [3].
*   **If the fault lies with the feed port A or B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 or 20.19):** The LS line pressure will successfully reach approximately 210 bar during the test [3]. If this is the case, stop the power pack, reconnect the electric connector to valve (20.22), and remove the pressure gauge [3]. Because valve (20.22) is functioning normally, the manual states that either the feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.18**) or the feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (**20.19**) may be faulty [4]. You must then check, clean, and, if necessary, replace valves (20.18) and (20.19) [4].

**Follow-Up Calibration:**
If either of the mechanical shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18 or 20.19) are replaced, you must use measuring point (**M1**) and the pump's pressure controller (B) set to 250 bar to adjust the feed port A valve (20.18) to **200 bar** against the front end stopper, and the feed port B valve (20.19) to **240 bar** against the rear end stopper [4, 5].

questions.question: When operating the RC600 rod changer, what specific sequence of rock drill rotation (counterclockwise), feed movements, and jaw operations must be executed to successfully uncouple a rod string and release the joint between the drill rod and the rock drill?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 3.2.3 "Procedure when uncoupling a rod string" (Page 14 of the Rod changer RC600S -series manual), the specific step-by-step sequence to uncouple a rod string and release the joint between the drill rod and rock drill is as follows [1, 2]:

1. Rotate a suitable slot to the location of the cassette’s filling opening during the drilling [1].
2. Rattle the threads open when the hole has been drilled to the intended depth [1].
3. Tighten the threads of the shank with the retaining centralizer [3].
4. Using the drifter (rock drill), pull the rod string out of the hole so that the extension sleeve comes to the location of the retaining centralizer [3].
5. Close the retaining centralizer’s jaws [3].
6. Move the long arms into the drilling center, but don’t close the cassette jaws [3].
7. Release the joint between the drill rods by means of the rock drill rotation mechanism (counterclockwise) [3].
8. Close the fixed jaw [3].
9. Release the joint between the drill rod and rock drill by means of the rock drill rotation mechanism (counterclockwise) [2, 3].
10. Move the drill rod into the cassette [2].
11. Open the cassette jaws [2].
12. Rotate the cassette anti-clockwise so that a vacant slot comes to the location of the cassette’s filling opening [2].
13. Drive the drifter to the extension sleeve and carry on the uncoupling as instructed above [2].

questions.question: In the feed-percussion follow-up mode, how does the drilling power encoder knob—which scales from 0% (minimum feed pressure) to 100% (maximum feed pressure)—interact with the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) to maintain optimal RD414 rock drill percussion?
questions.answer:
In the **feed-percussion follow-up mode**, the percussion pressure is dynamically controlled based on the feed pressure to ensure optimal operation of the rock drill percussion [1]. 

When the operator uses the drilling power encoder knob to adjust the drilling power from 0% (hole/rock type specific minimum feed pressure) to 100% (hole/rock type specific maximum feed pressure), it has a direct effect on the feed pressure, with each click corresponding to a 1% change [2]. This feed pressure adjustment indirectly affects the target percussion pressure because of the system's follow-up logic (Operator's Manual DS422i, Page 331) [2].

Hydraulically, this relationship is maintained through the interaction between the system's compensators and the **electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14)** (Drilling hydraulics DS422i, Page 34) [3]:
*   The electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve **(20.14)** is responsible for setting the actual target percussion pressure level for the system [4]. 
*   During drilling, oil flows from the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump **(1)** through the normally open percussion pressure compensator **(20.11)** to the rock drill [4]. 
*   If the pump's pressure level rises above the selected percussion pressure due to the feed functions, the percussion pressure compensator **(20.11)** actively lowers the percussion pressure to match the level set by the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve **(20.14)** [4]. 
*   The oil flow reaching the electro-proportional valve **(20.14)** in the load sensing (LS) line is restricted by orifices **(20.12)** and **(20.13)** [4]. 
*   Ultimately, the flow regulator of the variable displacement pump **(1)** is actuated by this load pressure and continuously tries to maintain the specific pressure level set by the electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve **(20.14)** [5].

questions.question: If the RD414 rock drill (which requires 14 kW of percussion power at 78 Hz) experiences vibrating percussion pressure hoses, what specific gas pre-charge pressures must be verified for the high-pressure (40 bar), low-pressure (4 bar), and stabilizer (30 bar) accumulators to prevent cavitation damage?
questions.answer:
To prevent cavitation damage and resolve the issue of vibrating percussion pressure hoses, you must verify the following specific nitrogen (N2) gas pre-charge pressures for the RD414 rock drill accumulators:

*   **High-pressure accumulator:** 40 bar [1, 2]
*   **Low-pressure accumulator:** 4 bar [1, 2]
*   **Stabilizer accumulator:** 30 bar [1, 2]

**Diagnostic Context:**
Vibrating percussion pressure hoses are specifically noted as a symptom of an empty high-pressure accumulator [3]. If an accumulator is empty or filled with too high a pressure, it causes cavitation that will damage the rock drill [3]. Specifically, overfilling the low-pressure accumulator significantly increases the risk of cavitation in the return lines [4].

**Step-by-Step Pressure Verification Procedure:**
According to Section 3.3 "Checking the charge gas pressure of a pressure accumulator" (Pressure accumulator maintenance instructions, Page 13), the verification requires the special toolkit pressure gauges (0–100 bar for high-pressure, 0–10 bar for low-pressure) [5]. 

1. Remove the rubber protection cap (**1**) (optional) or the metal cap (**2**) from the accumulator [5].
2. Screw the correct pressure gauge to the filling valve (**4**) [5].
3. Open the locking nut (**3**) [5].
4. Wait until the gauge pointer stops moving, and then check the pressure reading [5]. 
5. Close the locking nut (**3**) and use a torque wrench to tighten it to exactly **15 Nm** [6].
6. Disconnect the pressure gauge from the filling valve (**4**) [6].
7. Install the rubber protection cap (**1**) or the metal cap (**2**) back into its place [6].

*Note: During routine maintenance (Section 5.2.12 of the Maintenance Manual, Page 202), you should also verify that the filling valve (**4**) is properly tightened to the accumulator body at a torque of **40 Nm** [7]. Never remove the filling valve from a pressurized accumulator [7, 8].*

questions.question: When adjusting the steering circuit pilot pressure reducing valve (10.11) to achieve exactly 35 bar at measuring connector MX, what specific engine speed must be applied and how must the carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud (10.23) be positioned?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 4.7.5 "Adjusting steering circuit pilot pressure reducing valve (10.11)" (Drill carrier C400, C900 manual, pages 84–85), the calibration requires **maximum diesel engine rpm** and the carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud (10.23) must be pushed and turned counterclockwise to release it to the **up position** to pressurize the system [1, 2]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for the adjustment:

1. Replace the plug in measuring connection **MX** with the measuring connector G1/4 - M16x2 [1].
2. Attach a 40 bar pressure gauge to the measuring connector **MX** [1].
3. Loosen the locking nut of the pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (**10.11**) and turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise fully open [1, 2].
4. Start the diesel engine [2].
5. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it counterclockwise to release the stud to the **up position** to pressurize the carrier hydraulics [2].
6. Apply shortly the **maximum diesel engine rpm** [2].
7. Turn the adjusting screw of the valve (**10.11**) clockwise until the reading in the pressure gauge is exactly **35 bars** [2].
8. Tighten the locking nut of the valve (**10.11**) [2].
9. Return the diesel engine rpm to idle and shut down the engine after idling [2, 3].
10. Push the pressurizing stud (**10.23**) and turn it clockwise to lock the stud to the **down position** [3].
11. Remove the pressure gauge from the measuring connector **MX** [3].

questions.question: When the steering joystick is pushed forward and main spool (10.1) directs oil to working port A, which specific shock/anti-cavitation valve limits the pressure to 190 bar, and what spring pressure is utilized by the priority valve (10.10) to prioritize steering over secondary circuits?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Changing the steering angle to right" section in the Drill carrier C400, C900 manual (Pages 62–63), here are the specific details regarding the steering circuit:

*   **Shock/anti-cavitation valve:** When the main spool (10.1) directs oil to working port A, the pressure is limited to exactly 190 bar by the **shock/anti-cavitation valve (10.6)** [1].
*   **Priority valve spring pressure:** To prioritize steering over secondary circuits, the load sensing (LS) line pressure acts on the spring chamber of the **steering circuit priority valve (10.10)** together with its internal **10 bar spring** [2].

questions.question: In the event of a control system failure requiring a manual override of the front jacks, which specific pilot valves must be physically actuated with a pin to lower the front left jack (Y142B) and extend the front jack beam (Y169B)?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 7.18 "Manual override of the jacks' movements" (Maintenance Manual, pages 394–395 and Operator's Manual, pages 386–387), to lower the front left jack and extend the front jack beam during a control system failure, you must physically actuate the studs for pilot valves **Y142B** and **Y169B** respectively [1, 2]. Additionally, if the diesel engine is running instead of the power pack, you must simultaneously actuate and hold down the stud for valve **Y168** [3, 4].

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence:
1. **Pressurize the carrier hydraulics** (Skip this step if the power pack is running): Push the carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud and turn it clockwise to release the stud to the **up position** [5, 6].
2. **Activate valve Y168** (Skip this step if the power pack is running): Push the stud with a pin or similar tool to activate valve **Y168** (located in the rear carrier control block). **You must keep this stud pushed down during the entire override procedure** [3, 4]. 
3. **Access the front valves:** Remove the split pin (**1**) and the safety pin (**2**) so that you are able to lift the steps (**3**) [3, 4].
4. **Secure the steps:** When the steps (**3**) are in the upper position, put the safety pin (**2**) back and secure it with the split pin (**1**) [3, 4].
5. **Actuate the specific jack valves:** Using a pin or similar tool, press the corresponding studs for the desired movements:
   *   **To lower the front left jack:** Press the stud for valve **Y142B**, which delivers oil flow to port A1 [1, 2].
   *   **To extend the front jack beam:** Press the stud for valve **Y169B**, which delivers oil flow to port A3 [1, 2].
6. **Lock the system** (Skip this step if the power pack is running): When finished, push the carrier hydraulics pressurizing stud and turn it counterclockwise to lock the stud to the **down position** [7, 8].

questions.question: During automated drilling, how does the control system use feed pressure information to dynamically adjust the electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3), and what is the required gas pre-charge pressure for the stabilizer accumulator?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, here is how the control system dynamically adjusts the stabilizer pressure and the required gas pre-charge pressure for the accumulator.

**Dynamic Adjustment of the Stabilizer Pressure**
According to Section 4.6 "Stabilizer" (Drilling hydraulics DS422i, Pages 36–37), the function of the stabilizer control block (**22**) is to adjust the stabilizer pressure as a function of the effective feed pressure to a specific maximum limit during drilling [1]. The system executes this adjustment through the following mechanism:
1. The control system continuously receives feed pressure information during drilling [2].
2. Based on this information, the control system electrically adjusts the **electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3 / Y125)** [2]. 
3. Valve (**22.3**) operates as a pilot valve for the **stabilizer pressure reducing/relieving valve (22.2)**, causing valve (**22.2**) to set and maintain the correct physical pressure level directed to the rock drill's stabilizer [3, 4].
4. During this dynamic adjustment, the system ensures that the percussion pressure always remains at least **20 bar** higher than the stabilizer pressure [1].

*(Note: During threading and rattling, the stabilizer on/off valve (**22.1**) connects the stabilizer line to the tank, meaning there is no pressure in the stabilizer [1, 2].)*

**Required Gas Pre-Charge Pressure**
According to Section 5.2.17 "Pressure accumulator filling pressures" (Maintenance Manual DS422i, Page 208) and Section 3.8.2 "Filling pressures of accumulators" (Pressure accumulator maintenance instructions, Pages 26-27), the required nitrogen (N2) gas pre-charge pressure for the RD414 **stabilizer accumulator is 30 bar** [5, 6]

questions.question: When preparing the drill rig for transport on a platform to prevent a tipping hazard, what specific orientation and extension positions are required for the boom and feed to ensure the rig's center of gravity is safely maintained?
questions.answer:
To prevent a tipping hazard when preparing the drill rig for transport on a platform, the rig must be placed in its **tramming position**, because turning the boom alters the rig's center of gravity and can cause it to roll over [1]. When the rig is in this position, the maximum allowed front tilt angle is 15° and the maximum side tilt angle is 5° [2].

According to Section 4.11.3 "Tramming position of the rig" (Operator's Manual DS422i, Page 219), the specific orientation and extension positions must be set using the following step-by-step sequence:

1. Move the **boom and feed extensions** into their **rear positions** [1].
2. Move the **boom and feed** as close to the **center line of the rig**, and **as low as possible** [1, 3].
3. Rotate the **drilling module** so that it is on the **right side of the boom** [3].
4. Move the steel strand reel to the tramming position [3].
5. Lift the optional cement container filling screw to the up position [3].
6. Close the covers, hatches, and doors so they cannot open during tramming [3].
7. Lift the cement platform to the up position [3].

You must verify that this tramming position is fully established before driving the rig onto the transport platform or whenever the rig is not supported by its jacks [1, 4, 5].

questions.question: During a thermometer safety limit test on the compressor, if you heat the temperature sensor (B240T) and successfully receive a notice pop-up at 105 °C, but the compressor fails to shut down and trigger an alarm pop-up at 115 °C, what specific control logic or wiring fault should be investigated?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the notebook details the procedure for "Checking the function of the thermometer safety limits" (Maintenance Manual DS422i - StageV, Sections 5.15.14 / 8.3.14, pages 42/305) and identifies the function of the temperature sensor **B240T**, which monitors the compressor temperature, sends a notice to the GUI, and is designed to shut down the compressor when the temperature reaches 115 °C [1, 2].

**However, the sources do not contain any specific troubleshooting steps, control logic diagrams, or wiring faults to investigate if the compressor successfully issues the notice but fails to trigger the 115 °C alarm and shutdown.** 

For reference, the provided sequence for checking the thermometer safety limits is:
1. Remove the sensor from the compressor's body.
2. Start the power packs, compressor, and water pump.
3. Heat the sensor using a heater (operation range 0-120 °C; do not use fire) and monitor the temperature gauge. 
4. When the temperature reaches 105 ºC, check that the system gives a notice pop-up. 
5. When the temperature reaches 115 ºC, check that the system gives an alarm pop-up and the compressor stops [1].

questions.question: What are the pressure settings for the feed port shock/anti-cavitation valves, and how are they adjusted?
questions.answer: Feed port A (20.18) is set to 200 bar, and feed port B (20.19) is set to 240 bar. To adjust them, temporarily set the percussion/feed pump (1) pressure controller to 250 bar. Run the feed against the front end stopper to adjust port A to 200 bar, and run it against the rear end stopper to adjust port B to 240 bar. Once completed, re-adjust the pump back to its correct operating pressure [25, 26]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose electrical faults using the LED indicators on the Lincoln lubricant feed pump?
questions.answer: If the left and right green LEDs are off, there is no operating voltage at terminal 30, which could mean a blown fuse, cable break, or defective board [11]. For the central red LED, flashing every 2 seconds means insufficient voltage, flashing every 4 seconds indicates the motor circuit breaker tripped due to overload or mechanical stalling, and flashing every 8 seconds points to a loose contact at terminal 30 [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What maintenance step must be performed on CAN connectors to prevent future communication faults after an electrical repair?
questions.answer: If you replace components in the 24 V electrical system or remove any protective agents during repairs, you must reapply a protective agent to the mating surfaces. Specifically for CAN-connectors, you must apply the protective agent CRC 2-26 (part ID 81762209) [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if all boom hydraulic functions are slow or not working at all?
questions.answer: Check if the hydraulic oil level is too low or the oil viscosity is too high, and inspect hoses and connections for leaks [1]. Additionally, check if the main pressure relief valve at the pressure control block is functioning incorrectly; the boom working pressure should reach 220 bar, which can be verified using the percussion pressure gauge [1]. If the pressure is too low, clean, adjust, or replace the main pressure relief valve [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot inconsistent or unresponsive rotation speed adjustments?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation speed adjustment is not working as desired or drilling rod rotation is not constant [16].
*   **Cause:** A fault in the rotation pilot control valves (20.4, 20.5), rotation valve main spool (20.1), rotation line pressure compensator (20.2), or a damaged rock drill rotation mechanism [16].
*   **Corrective Action:** First, verify the pilot pressure at line X is between 30-45 bar [17]. If low, service the pilot oil filter (20.26) and reducing/relief valve (20.27) [17]. If pilot pressure is normal, remove, clean, and replace the rotation pilot control valves (20.4, 20.5) [17, 18]. Next, check the rotation valve main spool (20.1) and the pressure compensator (20.2); if either is mechanically damaged, replace the entire drilling control valve block [18-20]. Lastly, repair the rock drill rotation motor if all valves are functioning properly [20].

**Percussion System Troubleshooting. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does a Notice pop-up dialog (yellow) differ from an Alarm, and how should the operator respond?
questions.answer: A yellow Notice pop-up indicates a medium problem that does not necessarily require immediate action from the operator [1, 2]. However, the operator should investigate the cause, especially if the notice persists or is repeated often, and take steps to correct the error situation [1-4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes low rotation pressure during drilling and how is it corrected?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Rotation pressure is too low during drilling [13].
*   **Cause:** Leaks in the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3), the shuttle valve (20.7), the optional electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6), or an internal leak in the rock drill rotation motor [13-15].
*   **Corrective Action:** Check, clean, and replace the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3) and calibrate it [13, 14]. If the pressure remains low, inspect and replace the shuttle valve (20.7) and the optional electro-proportional LS pressure relief valve (20.6) [14]. If the issue still persists, check the rock drill rotation motor for leaks and repair or replace it according to the rock drill manuals [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the primary circuit breakers F41, F42, and F58 located in the DQ cabinet?
questions.answer: In the DQ cabinet, the **F41 (240 A)** acts as the battery main breaker, the **F42 (63 A)** serves as the cabin master supply breaker, and the **F58 (80 A)** is the master branch fuse for the 24 VDC control system [14-17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the procedures and setpoints for adjusting the steering circuit main pressure relief valve and the pilot pressure reducing valve?
questions.answer: To adjust the steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9), connect a 250 bar pressure gauge to measuring connector MPS. Pressurize the carrier hydraulics, apply maximum diesel engine rpm, and adjust the valve until the gauge reads exactly 220 bar [1-3]. To adjust the pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (10.11), connect a 40 bar gauge to connector MX. Under maximum diesel engine rpm, adjust the valve's screw until the pressure reads 35 bar [1, 4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components on the Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC) are used to identify the status of its CAN bus communication?
questions.answer: The SLC features specific LED indicators on the unit to diagnose communication status. It includes a green CAN-RUN indicator light (which indicates if the unit is receiving a start command) and a red CAN-ERR indicator light (which flashes or stays on if error counters exceed limits or the bus is off) [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which circuit breakers should be checked if there is a power loss or communication failure on the front or rear tramming CAN networks?
questions.answer: You should check the F9 circuit breakers in the cabin [5, 6]. On the A1 circuit board, check the F9 (2 A) breaker for the rear tramming CAN [5, 6]. On the A2 circuit board, check the F9 (4 A) breaker for the front tramming CAN and tramming display [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a CAN bus error using the red CAN-ERR indicator light on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLCU)?
questions.answer: Observe the flashing pattern of the red CAN-ERR light. If it is continuously on, the CAN control bus is off [3, 4]. If it flashes once, at least one CAN control error counter has reached or exceeded the alarm limit (too many errors); this fault condition resets automatically when data transfer is OK [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a creeping boom?
questions.answer: A creeping boom is diagnosed by checking for a leaking overcenter valve on the boom swing or lift cylinder, which is often caused by a broken O-ring or worn seat surfaces [4, 5]. If the valves are intact, the creeping may be caused by dirt in the hydraulic circuit (which requires flushing) or air trapped in the cylinder (which requires bleeding) [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a feed system that operates at the wrong speed?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Feed or fast feed speed is not correct despite normal system pressures [1].
*   **Cause:** The feed valve main spool (20.16) is stuck, or the pilot pressure from the feed pilot control valves (20.20 and/or 20.21) is too low [1].
*   **Corrective Action:** Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block; the pilot pressure should read 30-45 bars under load [1]. If it is low, check, clean, and replace the pilot oil filter (20.26) and the pilot oil pressure reducing/relief valve (20.27) [2]. If pilot pressure is correct, stop the power pack and inspect the feed pilot control valves (20.20, 20.21), replacing them if necessary (torque to 10 Nm) [2, 3]. If the issue persists, extract and inspect the feed valve main spool (20.16), and replace the entire drilling control valve block if the spool is faulty [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a power pack that will not start?
questions.answer: Check for possible alarm messages on the display, verify that the mains electric supply is connected, ensure the main switch (Q1) is in position 1 (ON), and confirm that all emergency stop buttons are released [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the brake circuit main pressure relief valve and brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve?
questions.answer: Connect gauges to MPB (brake supply) and MCR (brake line). Run the boom zoom backwards at maximum engine rpm to lock the adjustments. First, ensure MPB does not exceed 205 bar. Turn the brake circuit retarder pressure relief valve (10.15) until MCR reaches 210 bar (the absolute maximum allowed for brake accumulators). Next, adjust the brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8) until MPB drops to exactly 200 bar. Finally, readjust the retarder valve (10.15) until the MCR reading lowers to 160 bar [6-9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the pressures for the water booster pump and air-mist flushing?
questions.answer: The mine's inlet water pressure before the booster pump should be adjusted using the pressure reducing valve to 2-7 bar, ensuring the pressure measured after the water booster pump remains under 25 bar [30, 31]. To adjust the air-mist flushing restrictor valve, activate air flushing, loosen the locking nut, and turn the adjusting screw until the air pressure reading on the GUI reaches exactly 4 bar [32, 33]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components control the rotation pressure and flow in the drilling control valve block (20)?
questions.answer: The **rotation valve main spool (20.1)** directs oil flow to the rotation mechanism, while the **rotation line pressure compensator (20.2)** maintains a constant pressure difference over the spool to ensure constant rotation speed regardless of input and load changes [3]. The **rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3)** limits the maximum rotation pressure to **250 bar** [3]. The optional **electro proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6)** limits the maximum rotation LS pressure to 250 bar [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary components and their functions for controlling percussion within the drilling control valve block (20)?
questions.answer: The **percussion selector valve (20.9)** opens and closes the **percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10)**, which directs oil flow to the rock drill's percussion mechanism [5]. The **percussion pressure compensator (20.11)** keeps percussion pressure constant, while the **electro proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14)** controls the overall percussion pressure [5, 6]. The **percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve (20.25)** limits the circuit's maximum pressure to **270 bar** [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are some of the primary electronic control modules that communicate on the Sandvik DS422i CAN bus network?
questions.answer: The CAN bus system consists of numerous interconnected control modules. Key components include the Vehicle Controller (VC), End Controller (EC), Front Controller (FC), Drilling Master (DM1), Drilling Controller (DC), Boom Controller (BC), Rod Controller (RC), Strand Steel Controller (SSC), Cement Mixer Controller (CMC), and the Engine Control Module (ECM) [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the diesel engine will not start?
questions.answer: Check for alarm messages on the display, ensure the battery isolation switch (S1) and starter isolator switch (S2) are in the ON position, check that no circuit breakers in the DQ cabinet have tripped, and verify that all emergency stop buttons are released [1]. You should also verify the fuel level, battery condition, neutral gear, parking brake, and check if the fire suppression system or trailing cable alarm limit is preventing the start [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific maintenance procedure must be followed after repairing 24 V electrical components to prevent future CAN bus faults?
questions.answer: If you replace components or remove any protective agents during repairs, you must reapply a protective agent to the mating surfaces to ensure conductivity [14, 15]. Specifically for CAN-connectors, you must apply the protective agent CRC 2-26 (part ID 81762209) [15]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct pressure settings for the percussion/feed circuit and rotation circuit variable displacement pumps?
questions.answer: For the percussion/feed pump, the flow controller should maintain a 30 bar pressure difference, and the pressure controller should be set to 250 bar for an RD414 rock drill [2, 3]. For the rotation pump, the flow controller should maintain a 20-23 bar pressure difference, and the pressure controller should be set to 200 bar [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the rotation pressure is too low during drilling, assuming the variable displacement pump is adjusted correctly?
questions.answer: The issue is likely a leak in the rotation circuit main pressure relief valve (20.3), the shuttle valve (20.7), or the optional electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6) [7]. Check, clean, and replace the main pressure relief valve (20.3) if necessary [7]. If that fails to resolve the issue, check and replace the shuttle valve (20.7) [8]. If the machine is equipped with an electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve (20.6), check and replace it as well [8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose stabilizer pressure that is too low or too high during drilling?
questions.answer: First, verify the operation of the stabilizer controls using the control system's troubleshooting view [8]. If the electrical systems are working, the fault is likely a leaking or stuck stabilizer pressure reducing/relieving valve (22.2) or electro-proportional stabilizer pressure relief valve (22.3) [9]. Stop the power pack, then check, clean, or replace the valve (22.3); if the issue persists, clean or replace the valve (22.2), and finally replace the entire stabilizer valve block (22) if necessary [9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose CAN bus communication errors using the LED indicators on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLCU)?
questions.answer: Check the red CAN-ERR indicator light. If it flashes once, it means at least one CAN control error counter has reached or exceeded the alarm limit, which resets automatically when data transfer normalizes [2, 3]. If the indicator is continuously on, the CAN control bus is off [2, 3]. Additionally, a flashing green CAN-RUN light means the CAN bus connection is broken and the unit is not receiving a start command from the control unit [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you fix excessively high feed pressure?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Feed or fast feed pressure is too high [9].
*   **Cause:** The electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22), feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18), or feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19) is stuck [9]. Alternatively, the feed line pressure compensator (20.17) could be mechanically damaged [10].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack and clean valves 20.18 and 20.19, replacing and recalibrating them if damaged [11, 12]. If that does not resolve the issue, repair or replace the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) [12]. Finally, remove the feed line pressure compensator (20.17); if it is mechanically damaged, you must replace the entire drilling control valve block [10].

**Rotation System Troubleshooting. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is pressure regulated in the steering and brake control manifold (10)?
questions.answer: The **steering circuit main pressure relief valve (10.9)** limits the maximum steering circuit pressure to **220 bar** [9]. The **brake circuit main pressure relief valve (10.8)** limits the maximum brake circuit pressure to **200 bar** [9]. Additionally, the **pilot circuit pressure reducing valve (10.11)** feeds a reduced **35 bar** pressure to the pilot control valves [10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you calibrate the main pressure relief valves for the percussion/feed and rotation circuits?
questions.answer:
Because these valves work in tandem with the variable displacement pumps, they must be set slightly higher than the pump pressure controllers:
*   **Percussion/feed circuit (20.25):** Tighten the relief valve to over 270 bar. Temporarily adjust the pump (1) pressure controller to 280 bar. Loosen the main relief valve until the pressure drops to 270 bar (when it begins to "fizz"). Afterwards, readjust the pump back to its normal setting [19-21].
*   **Rotation circuit (20.3):** Tighten the relief valve to over 250 bar. Temporarily set the pump (2) pressure controller to 260 bar. Loosen the main relief valve until the pressure drops to 250 bar. Readjust the pump back to normal [22-24]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components control the feed cylinder pressures and speeds in the drilling control valve block (20)?
questions.answer: The **feed line pressure compensator (20.17)** maintains a constant pressure difference over the **feed valve main spool (20.16)** to ensure constant feed speed [6]. The **feed port A shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.18)** limits the feed port A maximum pressure to **200 bar**, while the **feed port B shock/anti-cavitation valve (20.19)** limits the feed port B maximum pressure to **240 bar** [8]. The **electro proportional feed LS pressure relief valve (20.22)** limits the maximum feed LS pressure to **250 bar** [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct gas pre-charge and filling pressures for the machine's accumulators?
questions.answer: The brake accumulators must have a gas pre-charge pressure of 65 bar [27]. For the rock drill accumulators, fill the high-pressure accumulator to 40 bar, the low-pressure accumulator to 4 bar, and the stabilizer accumulator to 30 bar [28, 29]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot an incorrect feed or fast feed speed assuming pressures and control systems are otherwise normal?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to line X of the drilling control valve block to check the pilot pressure, which should be 30-45 bars when the power pack is running loaded [4]. If the pressure differs, check, clean, and replace the pilot oil filter (20.26) and the pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve (20.27) [5]. If the pilot pressure is correct, stop the power pack and inspect the feed pilot control valves (20.20) and (20.21) (reinstall with a tightening torque of 10 Nm) or check the feed valve main spool (20.16) for damage [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the cause if the percussion remains on all the time while the power pack or diesel engine is running?
questions.answer: Assuming the electrical and control systems are functioning normally, this fault is caused by a stuck or leaking percussion selector valve (20.9) or percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) [6, 7]. The power pack should be stopped, and these valves must be cleaned or replaced immediately to prevent damage to the rock drill's accumulator seals [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the green CAN-RUN LED on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLCU) is flashing?
questions.answer: A flashing green CAN-RUN LED indicates that the SLCU is on standby and is awaiting a command from the CAN bus control unit [1]. This can also mean that the CAN bus connection is broken and the control unit (CAC) is not sending a start command [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for diagnosing abnormally low percussion pressure?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion pressure is too low [24].
*   **Cause:** The main pressure relief valve (20.25) or electro-proportional relief valve (20.14) is stuck, LS-line orifices (20.12, 20.13) are blocked, shuttle valves (11, 13, 20.15) are leaking, or the pump output is insufficient [24-27].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack. Clean, check, replace, and recalibrate the main pressure relief valve (20.25) and electro-proportional valve (20.14) [24, 25]. If unresolved, remove and clean the LS-line orifices (20.12 and 20.13) [25, 26]. Next, use flow meters to check pump output; flow rates should be 70-80 L/min for the RD414 percussion [26, 27]. If flow rates are higher, check the rock drill and feed cylinder for internal leaks [27]. Finally, check and replace leaking shuttle valves (11, 13, 20.15) [27]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary electrical power generation, transformation, and storage components on the rig?
questions.answer: The primary components include the **Battery (6)** for 24 VDC storage, the **Alternator (15)** for generating DC power, and the **Starting motor (14)** for the diesel engine [21, 22]. The system also features an optional **Multivoltage transformer (1)** for handling various mine site voltages and a **Compensation capacitor (13)** [21, 22]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can Cummins engine electrical faults be diagnosed using the ECM diagnostic mode?
