questions.answer: Turn the 'Diagnostic/manual regeneration switch' (S22) to position C while the 'Diesel engine start/stop' switch (S2) is in the ON position without the engine running [5]. The ECM will automatically blink the active fault codes using the 'Engine shutdown indicator light' and 'Check engine warning light', with each active fault blinking twice before moving to the next [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components and indicators are located on the MQ cabinet door?
questions.answer: The MQ cabinet door features the **Main switch (Q1)** and the **Multifunction energy meter (P1)** [1, 2, 12]. It also contains several indicator lights and buttons, including the **Wrong phase sequence indicator light (H1)**, the optional **Dewatering pump EFLO reset button (S293)**, and the optional **Earth leakage fault indicator light / reset button (S391)** [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you diagnose electrical faults using the LED indicators on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLCU)?
questions.answer: If the yellow STATUS indicator flashes three times, the air pressure sensor is broken or disconnected, indicated by a current signal lower than 2 mA (the normal value is 4...20 mA) [4, 5]. If it flashes four times, the oil level is below the minimum limit or the level switch sensor is broken, which is indicated by a current signal lower than 1.7 mA [4, 5]. If the red CAN-ERR indicator flashes once, an error counter has reached the alarm limit; if it is continuously on, the CAN control bus is off [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components are responsible for charging and storing oil for the service brakes?
questions.answer: The **accumulator charging valve (21)**, using its **control valve (21.2)** and **priority valve (21.1)**, directs oil from the brake circuit pump to maintain a **135-160 bar** pressure [11, 12]. This oil is stored in the **rear service brake pressure accumulator (22)** and **front service brake pressure accumulator (23)**, which serve as oil reserves for the brake cylinders [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which DQ cabinet circuit breakers provide power supply to the various rig control modules?
questions.answer: The **F43 (4 A)** breaker supplies the Mains sensor (MS) and Mains contactor (MC) controllers inside the MQ cabinet, as well as the filling pump control [14, 16]. The **F44 (6 A)** supplies the Vehicle controller (VC) [14, 16]. The **F45 (10 A)** supplies the End controller (EC), the optional Air water controller (AWC), the optional Cement mixer controller (CMC), the optional Steel strand controller (SSC), and the optional Resin pump controller (RPC) [14, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary switches used to isolate power in the electrical system and what are their specific functions?
questions.answer: The **Main switch (Q1)** cuts off the mains electric supply and can be locked in the OFF position [1, 2]. The **Battery isolation switch (S1)** disconnects the 24 VDC battery; however, it does not disconnect direct supply to certain components like the fire suppression system or alarm beacon [3-5]. The optional **Starter isolator switch (S2)** prevents the diesel engine from starting and opens the pilot circuit [4, 6-8]. Additionally, the **Battery and mains isolation button (S9)** located on the tramming panel remotely controls the battery main breaker (F41) and main switch (Q1) to cut off both battery power and the main electric supply [9-11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific circuit breakers are responsible for protecting the components on the front and rear tramming CAN networks?
questions.answer: The tramming CAN networks are protected by the F9 circuit breakers located in the cabin. The F9 (4 A) breaker on the A2 circuit board supplies the front tramming CAN and tramming display, while the F9 (2 A) breaker on the A1 circuit board protects the rear tramming CAN [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the cause of a Blocked pop-up dialog and what is the required response?
questions.answer: A Blocked pop-up dialog is displayed when the rig control system actively prohibits the operator from performing an action that could cause personal injury or damage to the rig [5, 6]. The operator must resolve the underlying error causing the block; the pop-up will disappear automatically once the cause is removed [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the troubleshooting procedure if the percussion pressure is too high while the electric and control systems are operating properly?
questions.answer: The electro-proportional percussion pressure relief valve (20.14) is likely stuck [2]. Stop the power pack, then check, clean, and replace the valve (20.14) if necessary [2]. If this does not resolve the issue, check that both orifices (20.12) and (20.13) in the LS-line are properly in place; if either orifice has loosened, tighten it carefully [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the circuit breakers found on the A1 circuit board within the cabin?
questions.answer: The A1 circuit board contains several breakers protecting specific circuits: **F2 (10 A)** protects the Boom 1 BC (Boom Controller) and DC (Drilling Controller); **F3 (10 A)** protects the FC (Front Controller); **F6 (10 A)** protects the front tramming lights and optional cabin heater motor; **F9 (2 A)** protects the rear tramming CAN; and **F10 (4 A)** protects the TCP (Tramming Control Panel) [18-20]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific part number is required for protecting CAN bus connectors during component maintenance or replacement?
questions.answer: If you replace components in the electrical system or remove protective agents during a repair, you must reapply a protective agent to the mating surfaces. For CAN-connectors, you must specifically use the protective agent CRC 2-26 (part ID 81762209) [5]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do Cummins engine fault codes 285 and 286 indicate regarding the CAN bus system?
questions.answer: Both codes point to issues on J1939 Network #1, which is the Primary Vehicle Network [9-12]. Code 285 indicates a SAE J1939 Multiplexing PGN Timeout Error caused by an abnormal update rate [9-12]. Code 286 indicates a SAE J1939 Multiplexing Configuration Error, meaning the system is out of calibration [10, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should you do if the flow controller value of the percussion/feed circuit variable displacement pump (1) deviates from the set value?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to the measuring connector (LS) of the variable displacement pump (1) and start the power pack [9]. If the pressure is normal tank pressure (approx. 3-5 bar or less), the flow controller (A) is likely incorrectly adjusted or stuck; adjust the stand-by pressure to a 30 bar difference [9-11]. If the pressure is above normal tank pressure, check for a leaking percussion selector valve (20.9), percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10), feed valve main spool (20.16), or feed line pressure compensator (20.17) [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you handle a situation where percussion will not turn off?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion remains on constantly while the power pack or diesel engine is running [23].
*   **Cause:** The percussion selector valve (20.9) or percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) is stuck and leaking, allowing constant pressure to reach the rock drill's percussion mechanism [23].
*   **Corrective Action:** Stop the power pack or diesel engine immediately to prevent damage to the rock drill's accumulator seals [23]. Check, clean, and replace the faulty valves (20.9 and 20.10) [23]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it signify if the diesel engine indicator Light 1 begins blinking, and what is the operator response?
questions.answer: A blinking Light 1 indicates that the engine shutdown process has started [13]. The engine will shut down automatically unless the operator intervenes by pushing the shutdown override button (if safe and authorized to do so) [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What procedure and specific product must be used to protect CAN connectors after electrical system repairs?
questions.answer: If you replace components in the 24 V electrical system or remove any protective agents during repairs, you must reapply a protective agent to the mating surfaces [4]. For CAN-connectors, you must specifically apply the protective agent CRC 2-26 (part ID 81762209) [4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions of the variable displacement pumps (1) and (2) in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The **variable displacement pump (1)** delivers the required oil to the **percussion, feed, boom hydraulic systems, and the optional stabilizer** [1]. The **variable displacement pump (2)** delivers oil to the **rotation hydraulic system** [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the different states of the DEF/AdBlue® level indicator light signify, and what action is required?
questions.answer: If the DEF indicator (Light 3) is solid, the DEF level is getting low [12]. If it is blinking, the level is too low [12]. If the DEF indicator is blinking while the main engine warning light (Light 1) is solid, the level is critically low and engine power will be reduced [12]. In all these scenarios, the operator must refill the DEF/AdBlue® tank to clear the warning and restore normal engine power [12]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the feed pressure is abnormally low?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Feed or fast feed pressure is too low [4].
*   **Cause:** The electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) is stuck, the feed port A or B shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18, 20.19) are leaking, or the feed cylinder is faulty [4, 5].
*   **Corrective Action:** Disconnect the electrical connector from valve (20.22), run the feed against the rear stopper, and check if the pump LS line pressure reaches approximately 210 bar [6]. If it does not, clean or replace the electro-proportional feed pressure relief valve (20.22) [6, 7]. If it does reach 210 bar, check and replace the shock/anti-cavitation valves (20.18, 20.19), then re-calibrate them [5, 7, 8]. If valves are fine, plug the feed pressure lines A2 and B2; if feed pressure returns to normal, the feed cylinder is faulty and must be repaired [5, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should the operator do if an Alarm pop-up dialog (red) appears on the display?
questions.answer: A red Alarm pop-up indicates the control system has detected a major problem that requires immediate attention and action to prevent damage to the drill rig components [1, 2]. The control system may stop some or all operations [1, 2]. The operator must stop working immediately, follow any on-screen instructions or check the Log for troubleshooting details, and refrain from using the drill rig until the cause is resolved and corrected [1-4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components should be inspected if the power pack will not start or stops unexpectedly?
questions.answer: Check the connection of the mains electric supply and ensure the main switch (Q1) is in position 1 (ON) [2]. Verify that none of the circuit breakers in the MQ cabinet have tripped and ensure that the pilot circuit is functional [2]. Also, look for possible alarm messages on the display and ensure all emergency stop buttons are released [2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the percussion/feed and rotation circuit variable displacement pumps calibrated?
questions.answer:
**Percussion/feed pump (1):** Connect gauges to the LS-line (port X) and the pressure filter. Adjust the flow controller (A) to achieve a 30 bar pressure difference. For the pressure controller (B), run the boom zoom against the rear stopper and adjust the valve to 250 bar for an RD414 rock drill [10-14]. 
*   **Rotation pump (2):** Plug the rotation hoses and connect gauges to the LS-line and check valve block. The flow controller (A) should be checked at about 23 bar, but if adjustment is needed, turn the flow controller screw to achieve a 30 bar pressure difference. The pressure controller (B) should be adjusted to 200 bar while running rotation against the plug [15-18]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific circuit breakers should be checked if the front or rear tramming CAN networks lose power?
questions.answer: You should check circuit breaker F9 in the cabin [8-11]. For the rear tramming CAN, ensure the F9 circuit breaker (2 A) has not tripped [8, 10]. If the issue is with the front tramming CAN and tramming display, check the F9 circuit breaker (4 A) [9, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical checks should be performed if the diesel engine will not start?
questions.answer: Check that the battery isolation switch (S1) and the optional starter isolator switch (S2) are in the ON position [1]. Ensure that none of the circuit breakers in the DQ cabinet have tripped, verify the battery condition, and check that all emergency stop buttons are released [1]. Additionally, confirm there is enough trailing cable on the reel so the alarm limit has not been reached, and check that the optional fire suppression system is not preventing the start [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings are triggered when operating the steel strand reel or optional cement container filling screw?
questions.answer: Whenever the steel strand reel swing or cement container filling screw up/down movements are operated, a visual warning light and an audible alarm sound are automatically activated and will remain active throughout the duration of the movement [14, 15]. The operator should ensure the hazard zone is clear of personnel [16, 17]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC) interact with the CAN bus network to perform its function?
questions.answer: The Shank Lubrication Controller (SLC) is connected directly to the CAN bus backbone. Its primary function is to dispense shank lubrication oil to the rock drill(s), and it knows when to do this by receiving a shank lubrication request from the Drilling Master (DM1) node via the backbone [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the percussion completely fails to operate?
questions.answer:
**Symptom:** Percussion is not working when activated [21].
*   **Cause:** Mechanical failure within the rock drill itself, or a stuck percussion selector valve (20.9) or percussion 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) [21].
*   **Corrective Action:** Observe the percussion pressure gauge on the main view. If it shows a pressure reading but percussion does not start, the rock drill is faulty and must be repaired or replaced [21]. If the gauge shows no reading at all, stop the power pack and clean, check, or replace the percussion selector valve (20.9) and the 2-way cartridge valve (20.10) [21, 22]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure settings for the pilot oil circuit and the main pressure relief valves?
questions.answer: The pilot oil pressure reducing and relief valve reduces and limits the pilot pressure to 35-45 bar [5, 6]. The percussion/feed circuit main pressure relief valve is set to limit the maximum pressure to 270 bar, while the electro-proportional rotation LS pressure relief valve limits the maximum rotation LS pressure to 250 bar [5, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the primary cause of hydraulic system failures on the Sandvik DS422i and how is it diagnosed?
questions.answer: Oil contamination is the primary cause, accounting for 70-80% of all hydraulic system failures [1]. Contaminants such as dirt, water, rubber particles from worn seals, and metallic debris can be diagnosed through regular fluid analysis, which provides early warning signs of component wear and unexpected failures [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the expected hydraulic flow rates for the percussion and feed circuits during maximum operation?
questions.answer: At the maximum percussion pressure level and normal operating temperature, the flow rate for the RD414 rock drill percussion should be 70-80 L/min, and the feed flow rate should be 4-8 L/min [1]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it mean if the green CAN-RUN indicator light on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLCU) is flashing or off?
questions.answer: If the light is flashing, the SLCU is on standby and waiting for a command from the CAN bus control unit, which typically means the CAN bus connection is broken and the control unit (CAC) is not sending a start command [1, 2]. If the light is off, it indicates there is no supply voltage to the control unit or the unit is resetting [2-4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a loss of communication between the engine control module (ECM) and the machine's electronic control unit diagnosed?
questions.answer: This is diagnosed by Cummins engine fault code 5939, which signifies "Machine Constrained Operation" due to an abnormal update rate [13, 14]. This code triggers when no communication or an invalid data transfer rate has been detected on the J1939 data link between the ECM and the machine electronic control unit [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What Cummins engine fault codes indicate erratic data or invalid datalink messages on the machine's CAN networks?
questions.answer: Cummins fault code 4437 signifies that data on J1939 Network #4 is erratic, intermittent, or incorrect [7, 8]. Fault code 5941 indicates "Machine Constrained Operation" because a received J1939 datalink message was not valid [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the electrical diagnostic steps if a pump does not work because the motor does not turn?
questions.answer: Check the terminal board and electrical panel for incorrect connections, reset any triggered automatic switches or replace blown fuses, verify the power supply connection, and if the built-in thermal overload protection device tripped, wait for it to reset [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific alarms and notices generated by the automatic greasing system?
questions.answer: The automatic greasing system will generate a yellow notice if the grease level is low or if the pause time parameter is set too short [11]. It will generate a red alarm for high pressure (requiring the operator to locate a blocked greasing point), too low pressure (indicating a potential hose breakage), or low pressure caused by an air bubble [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What other hydraulic filters are used in the system, and what is the overall fluid cleanliness requirement?
questions.answer: The system uses a breather filter on the oil receiver with a 5 µm rating, an optional bypass filter rated at 2 µm absolute (with a clogging indicator at 2 bar and bypass at 3.5 bar), a stabilizer oil line filter rated at 10 µm absolute, and a pilot oil filter rated at 160-200 µm [5, 10-12]. The manufacturer's overall recommendation for the hydraulic fluid cleanliness class is 18/16/13 according to the ISO 4406 (c) standard [13]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the troubleshooting procedure if the Lincoln lubricant feed pump motor does not run, based on its control circuit board LEDs?
questions.answer: Check the operational status LEDs on the control circuit board [8]. If the left and right green LEDs are off, there is no operating voltage at terminal 30; check the supply line, correct the back-up fuse, or look for an internal cable break [9]. If the central red LED flashes in intervals of 4 seconds, the motor circuit breaker has tripped due to an overload, short circuit, or mechanical stalling, requiring an electrical and mechanical check of the motor [10]. If the red LED flashes in intervals of 8 seconds, check the electrical connections for a loose contact at terminal 30 [11]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the common causes and diagnostic steps if the diesel engine will not start?
questions.answer: Diagnose by checking for alarm messages on the display, ensuring the battery isolation switch (S1) and optional starter isolator switch (S2) are in the ON position, checking that no circuit breakers in the DQ cabinet have tripped, and verifying all emergency stop buttons are released [1]. Additionally, check the fuel level, battery condition, neutral gear, parking brake engagement, trailing cable length, and ensure the fire suppression system isn't preventing the start [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which Cummins engine fault codes indicate multiplexing errors on the Primary Vehicle Network (J1939 Network #1)?
questions.answer: Cummins fault code 285 indicates a SAE J1939 Multiplexing PGN Timeout Error caused by an abnormal update rate [5, 6]. Fault code 286 indicates a SAE J1939 Multiplexing Configuration Error, meaning the system is out of calibration [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What warnings will occur if the operator attempts to tram without wearing a seat belt or with the cabin door open?
questions.answer: The machine is equipped with a door latch and seat belt monitoring system [7, 8]. If the engine is started while the seat belt is unfastened or the door is improperly closed, a buzzer on the tramming panel will sound and a notice pop-up will be displayed [7-10]. The operator must close the door and fasten the seat belt before tramming [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot CAN bus errors using the red CAN-ERR LED on the Shank Lubrication Unit (SLCU)?
questions.answer: Observe the flashing pattern of the red CAN-ERR LED on the SLCU [2, 3]. If the LED flashes once, it means at least one CAN control error counter has reached or exceeded the alarm limit, which will reset automatically when data transfer is OK [2]. If the LED is continuously on, it indicates that the CAN control bus is off [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a potentially faulty power factor correction capacitor?
questions.answer: Start one power pack at a time and let it idle [3]. Check the power factor value from the electric quality measuring unit (P1) [3]. If the power factor value is under 0.5 and the individual phase current differs significantly, the capacitor is likely faulty [3]. Because the unit cannot be repaired, the entire multivoltage capacitor unit must be replaced [3]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which Cummins engine fault codes indicate a communication issue on the J1939 CAN network, and what do they signify?
questions.answer: Cummins fault codes 285 and 286 indicate issues on J1939 Network #1 (the Primary Vehicle Network) [5, 6]. Code 285 signifies a SAE J1939 Multiplexing PGN Timeout Error due to an abnormal update rate [5, 6]. Code 286 indicates a SAE J1939 Multiplexing Configuration Error meaning it is out of calibration [6]. Additionally, fault code 4437 indicates that data on J1939 Network #4 is erratic, intermittent, or incorrect [7]. (Ref: Sandvik DS422i Technical Manual)

questions.question: When testing the brake pump maximum pressure, what is the correct diagnostic procedure involving sequence valve V3503, adjustment screw 513, and measurement point MP501, and what should the target pressure gauge reading be?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 13.12.3 "Brake pump pressure check / adjustment" (page 828) in the Service and Repair Manual, and Section 5.6.13 "Check brake pump pressure" (page 323) in the Maintenance Manual, the target gauge reading for the brake pump maximum pressure is **280 bar (± 8 bar)** [1, 2]. 

The step-by-step diagnostic procedure is as follows:

1. Ensure the machine is on an even surface, the parking brake is applied, and movement is prevented by wheel chocks [3, 4].
2. Install the frame articulation locking device [3, 4].
3. Screw the sequence valve **V3503** adjustment screw **513** to the closed position (all the way in) [1, 4].
4. Connect a **400-bar pressure gauge** to the sequence valve **V3503** measuring point **MP501** [1, 4].
5. Start the engine [1, 4].
6. Record the pressure gauge reading to verify it meets the **280 bar (± 8 bar)** target [1, 2, 4].
7. If the maximum pressure needs adjustment, use adjustment screw **501** [2].
8. Stop the engine [1, 2].
9. Screw the sequence valve **V3503** adjustment screw **513** back to the fully open position, and then turn it **¼ turn back in** [2].

questions.question: When diagnosing low transmission clutch pressure with normal clutch leakage, how do you verify if the clutch pressure regulator valve is correctly maintaining the required 16.55 to 19.33 bar range using pressure transducer B3005?
questions.answer:
Based on the Service and Repair Manual LH410 (Section 9.2 "Transmission hydraulics", pages 315-316), the clutch pressure regulator valve (**Component 7**) is responsible for maintaining the clutch pressure between 16.55 and 19.33 bar [1, 2]. This pressure is monitored using pressure transducer **B3005** located at the clutch pressure measurement point (**Component 13**) [3, 4]. 

When diagnosing "low clutch pressure with normal clutch leakage" (Section 9.3.7 "General troubleshooting", page 332), the potential causes and corrective actions are [5]:
*   **Low oil level:** Fill to the proper level.
*   **Broken spring in the transmission regulator valve:** Replace the spring.
*   **Clutch pressure regulator valve spool stuck in open position:** Clean the valve spool and sleeve.
*   **Faulty charging pump:** Refer to the Dana manual's paragraph on charging pump output.

To verify the transmission pressure readings from transducer B3005, you can monitor the real-time 4-20 mA signal sent to the **Middle module (pin XM3.7)** via **Gauge window 1** ("Transmission oil pressure") on the VCM display [6, 7]. 

You can also perform the formal **"Transmission pressure sensor test"** (Maintenance Manual LH410, Section 5.1.11, pages 208-209) using the following step-by-step sequence [8, 9]:
1. Open the transmission pressure sensor test window from the functions test window by pressing the **Brake** button [8].
2. Select **Low transmission oil pressure activates brakes** [9].
3. Ensure the machine is on level ground and shut down the engine. Check the gauge in the window to ensure the transmission oil pressure decreases to **0 bar** [9].
4. Start the engine and check the gauge in the window to ensure that the transmission oil pressure increases to the normal operating level [9].
5. Press **OK** to continue the test [9].

questions.question: To diagnose missing CAN 2 bus signals resulting in a "Pressure Sensor 1: Error on CAN bus" (Front 145) alarm, how do you perform a resistance measurement inside the electric box utilizing the AMP8 connector pins XF4-7 and XF4-8 and M12 connector X223?
questions.answer:
Based on the Service and Repair Manual LH410 (Section 12.10.4 "System notifications and troubleshooting", pages 668–670), the "Front 145" alarm indicates that Pressure Sensor 1 has failed or has an error on the CAN bus [1]. 

To diagnose missing signals on the CAN 2 bus by checking the wiring *inside* the electric box (Action 3), follow this step-by-step sequence:

1. Disconnect the AMP8 connector **XF4** [2].
2. Disconnect the M12 connector **X223** [2].
3. Measure the resistance between the following specific connector pins using a multimeter [2]:
   *   **XF4-7** and **X223-4** [2].
   *   **XF4-8** and **X223-2** [2].
   *   **X223-2** and **GRN.X2** [2].
4. Verify the readings. The target resistance should be about **0 Ω (Ohms)** in all of these wires [2].

questions.question: What is the exact sequence of steps, including the use of the frame articulation locking device and manifold block hose disconnections, to test if the steering cylinder piston seals are internally bypassing from the rod side to the piston side?
questions.answer:
Based on the Service and Repair Manual LH410, Section 11.10.2 "Steering cylinder bypass test" (specifically the "Cylinder piston side leakage test" on pages 599–602), here is the exact step-by-step sequence to test if the piston seals are internally bypassing from the rod side to the piston side [1-5]:

**Preliminary and Safety Steps:**
1. Ensure the machine is on an even surface, the parking brake is applied, and movement in the driving direction is prevented with wheel chocks [2].
2. Ensure that the bucket is lowered and the boom is resting on its stops [2].
3. Install the **frame articulation locking device** [2].
4. Before performing any maintenance on the hydraulic system, depressurize the hydraulic oil tank. Pressure is released by using the directional valve on top of the hydraulic oil tank. Ensure the valve closes fully once all pressure is relieved [2, 3].
5. Release hydraulic pressure from both the left and right steering hydraulic circuits. This is safely done by using a capillary test hose into the steer test points. Gradually screw the quick connects on to release the pressure in a controlled manner, and collect any oil in an oil drain container [3].

**Testing Procedure:**
6. Disconnect the **piston side hydraulic line** from the manifold block of the cylinder you are testing. **Cap the manifold** to eliminate any high-pressure oil injection hazard during the test [4].
7. Allow the cylinder piston side oil to drain completely into an oil drain container via the disconnected hose until all oil flow has stopped [4].
8. With a second person observing the container and piston side hose end from a safe position, start the engine and move the steering joystick to **pressurize the rod side hydraulic circuit** of the cylinder being tested [4].

**Diagnostic Conclusion & Reassembly:**
9. If oil is observed coming from the cylinder, the piston seals are bypassing in this direction (rod to piston side) [5]. *Note: Because cylinder piston seals are directional, it is possible for a cylinder to bypass in one direction only. If it is bypassing, the cylinder needs replacement or overhaul [5].*
10. Shut down the engine [5].
11. Remove the cap from the manifold block and reconnect the piston side cylinder hose to the block. You must use a **new O-ring** [5].
12. Check the hydraulic oil level [5].
13. Start the engine and check for oil leaks, repairing as needed [5].
14. Stop the engine [6].

questions.question: While physically inspecting the Turbocharger Boost Control (VGT) actuator on a TAD87x series engine due to a P256214 fault code, what are the specific acceptable stroke length measurements in millimeters required when checking both the rotational play and the up/down rod movement?
questions.answer:
When investigating a **P256214** fault code (Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor "A" internal error), the specific acceptable stroke length measurements for the VGT actuator on TAD87x series engines are as follows:

*   **Rotational play (turning stroke):** You must be able to turn the actuator, with the rod, by hand. The length of the stroke between the actuator end positions must be approximately **25 mm** [1].
*   **Up/down stroke length:** You must be able to move the actuator, with the rod, up and down by hand. The length of the stroke between the actuator end positions must be approximately **13 mm** [1].

If the actuator cannot be turned or moved in these directions, or if the stroke lengths fall short of these measurements, you must examine the cause of the restriction [1]. If the VGT unit is determined to be faulty and is causing the P256214 internal sensor error, the complete VGT unit must be changed [2].

questions.question: When checking the pilot control pressure at measurement point MP405 with the engine idling, what is the specified target pressure and what is the transition point pressure when the ignition current is switched off and on repeatedly?
questions.answer:
Based on Section 5.6.10 "Test the pilot system hydraulic pressure" in the Maintenance Manual (pages 318–319) and Section 10.12.2 "Pilot pressure test" in the Service and Repair Manual (pages 546–547) [1-6], the specified target pressure at engine idle is **35 bar (±10 bar)** [2, 3, 5]. The transition point pressure is **15 bar (± 2 bar)** [3, 6]. 

The complete step-by-step diagnostic procedure is as follows:

1. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the pilot control pressure line at measurement point **MP405** [2, 5].
2. Start the engine and let it idle [2, 5].
3. Record the gauge reading to verify the pressure is **35 bar (±10 bar)** [2, 3, 5].
4. Shut down the engine and switch the ignition current back on immediately. *(Note: Do not start the engine)* [3, 5].
5. Switch the ignition current "off" and "on" repeatedly and follow the pressure decrease by reading the gauge [3, 6]. 
    * Each time the ignition current is switched "off", the pressure should start to decrease [3, 6]. 
    * When the ignition current is switched "on", the pressure should stop decreasing [3, 6].
    * When the transition point of **15 bar (± 2 bar)** is reached, the pressure will drop to **0 bar** [3, 6].
6. Add or remove pressure from the accumulator if necessary using a separate gas filling device [6, 7].
7. Remove the measuring hose from measurement point **MP405** [7].

questions.question: When checking the engine cooler fan pump maximum pressure for a Volvo engine at measurement point MP301, what is the target pressure value and which adjustment screw is used?
questions.answer:
Based on the Maintenance Manual (Section 5.6.12, pages 320-321) and the Service and Repair Manual (Section 8.9.2, pages 293-295), the target maximum pressure for the engine cooler fan pump on a machine equipped with a Volvo engine is **190 bar (±5 bar)** [1, 2]. If adjustments are necessary, **adjustment screw 301** is used [2]. 

The step-by-step diagnostic sequence is as follows:

1. Ensure the hydraulic oil temperature is between 60-80°C and check that the engine temperature is less than 80°C [3]. 
2. Connect a **400-bar pressure gauge** to the measurement point **MP301** [4].
3. The test can be set up using either the VCM display (adjusting the pump controller minimum current to 40 mA and maximum current to 50 mA) or by physically detaching connector **341(2)** from the pump regulator [4].
4. Start the engine and accelerate it to maximum rpm [2].
5. Check the pressure from the gauge. For a Volvo engine, the value must be **190 bar (±5 bar)** [2]. 
6. Adjust the pressure when necessary by turning **adjustment screw 301** [2].
7. Stop the engine [2].

*Note: If the machine is equipped with a Volvo engine and connector 341(2) was detached for the procedure, the main switch must be turned off and on after plugging the electrical connector back in* [2].

questions.question: During the brake pump pressure check, what position must the sequence valve V3503 adjustment screw 513 be set to before verifying the maximum pressure of 280 bar (± 8 bar) at measurement point MP501?
questions.answer:
Based on the Maintenance Manual LH410 (Section 5.6.13 "Check brake pump pressure", pages 322-323) and the Service and Repair Manual LH410 (Section 13.12.3 "Brake pump pressure check / adjustment", pages 828-829), the sequence valve V3503 adjustment screw 513 must be set to the **closed position (all the way in)** before verifying the maximum pressure [1, 2].

The step-by-step diagnostic procedure is as follows:

1. Ensure the machine is on an even surface, the parking brake is applied, and movement is prevented by wheel chocks [2, 3].
2. Install the frame articulation locking device [2, 3].
3. Screw the sequence valve **V3503** adjustment screw **513** to the **closed position** [1, 2].
4. Connect a **400-bar pressure gauge** to the sequence valve **V3503** measuring point **MP501** [1, 2].
5. Start the engine [1, 2].
6. Record the pressure gauge reading. The correct maximum pressure is **280 bar (± 8 bar)** [1, 2, 4].
7. Adjust the maximum pressure if necessary using adjustment screw **501** [4].
8. Stop the engine [1, 4].
9. Screw the sequence valve **V3503** adjustment screw **513** to the fully open position and then **¼ turn back in** [1, 4].

questions.question: When calibrating the bucket pump dp-pressure by connecting gauges to measurement points MP201 and MP202, what is the required pressure difference and which adjustment screw (202) must be adjusted?
questions.answer:
The required pressure difference for the bucket pump dp-pressure is **30 bar (±2 bar)** [1, 2]. If the pressure difference needs to be corrected, you must use **adjustment screw 202** [1, 2].

According to the Maintenance Manual LH410 (Section 5.6.14 "Check bucket pump pressure", pages 325-327) [1, 3, 4] and the Service and Repair Manual LH410 (Section 12.14.3 "Checking and adjusting the bucket pump pressures", pages 741-742) [2, 5], the step-by-step procedure is as follows:

1. Ensure the hydraulic oil temperature is between 60...80ºC [3, 6].
2. Connect 400-bar pressure gauges to the measurement points **MP201** and **MP202** (located at the bucket pump) [2, 4].
3. Start the engine [1, 2].
4. Check the pressure difference from the gauges. The pressure difference must be **30 bar (±2 bar)** [1, 2].
5. Adjust the dp-pressure if necessary by turning **adjustment screw 202** [1, 2].

questions.question: When setting the valve clearance on a cold Volvo engine using a feeler gauge, what are the specific clearance settings in millimeters for both the intake and exhaust valves?
questions.answer:
Based on the Volvo Workshop Manual, the specific valve clearance settings for a cold engine (oil temperature < 80 °C / 176 °F) are:

*   **Intake valves (Inl.):** **0.4 mm** (±0.05 mm) [1-3].
*   **Exhaust valves (Ex.):** **0.5 mm** (±0.05 mm) [1, 4].

To adjust the clearance, the sources outline the following step-by-step procedure:

1. Check the valve clearance between the rocker arm and the valve yoke using a feeler gauge set [3-5]. 
2. If the value is incorrect, loosen the adjuster screw locking nut on the rocker arm [4, 5].
3. Turn the adjuster screw until the correct clearance is achieved [4, 5].
4. **For the intake valves:** Use a 0.40 mm and a 0.45 mm feeler gauge. Set the clearance so that the 0.40 mm gauge can be inserted without great resistance (only slight resistance should be felt when pulling it back and forth). It should *not* be possible to insert the 0.45 mm feeler gauge without resistance [5, 6].
5. **For the exhaust valves:** Use a 0.50 mm and a 0.55 mm feeler gauge. Set the clearance so that the 0.50 mm gauge can be inserted without great resistance. It should *not* be possible to insert the 0.55 mm feeler gauge without resistance [4, 7].
6. Once the correct clearance is set, counterhold the adjuster screw while tightening the locking nut to a torque of **33 Nm (24.3 lbf. ft.)** [4-7].

questions.question: What are the exact filling capacities in liters for the fuel tank, hydraulic oil tank, and brake oil tank on the Sandvik LH410?
questions.answer:
According to Section 4.4 "Filling capacities" in the Maintenance Manual (page 186) and Section 10.1 "Hydraulic oil" in the Service and Repair Manual (page 457), the filling capacities for the Sandvik LH410 are as follows:

*   **Fuel tank:** 310 liters [1].
*   **Hydraulic oil tank:** 240 liters [1, 2].
*   **Brake hydraulic oil tank:** 57 liters [1, 2].

Please note that the manufacturer specifies these capacities as approximate values. When changing or adding fluids, you should always verify the exact filling capacity by checking the sight glasses or dipsticks for each specific tank [1].

questions.question: What are the specified output power, maximum torque, and engine displacement values for the standard Volvo TAD1140VE diesel engine powerpack?
questions.answer:
According to the Operator's Manual specifications (page 297), the Volvo TAD1140VE diesel engine powerpack has the following values:

*   **Output power:** 235 kW at 2100 rpm [1].
*   **Maximum torque:** 1568 Nm at 1300 rpm [1].
*   **Engine displacement:** 10.84 liters [1].

questions.question: What are the overall length (L1), overall width (W1), and maximum raised bucket height (H11) dimensions for a Sandvik LH410 equipped with a standard 4.0 m³ bare lip bucket?
questions.answer:
According to the "DIMENSIONS" tables in the Operator's Manual LH410 (pages 302-303), the specifications for a machine equipped with a standard **4.0 m³ bare lip bucket** are:

*   **Overall length (L1):** 10073 mm [1]
*   **Overall width (W1):** 2544 mm [2]
*   **Maximum raised bucket height (H11):** 5134 mm [2]

questions.question: When checking the brake pump maximum pressure for pump block P3511, what specific adjustment must be made to sequence valve V3503's screw 513 before measuring at MP501, and what is the target 280 bar (±8 bar) diagnostic procedure?
questions.answer:
Based on the Maintenance Manual LH410 (Section 5.6.13 "Check brake pump pressure", pages 322-323) [1-3] and the Service and Repair Manual LH410 (Section 13.12.3 "Brake pump pressure check / adjustment", pages 828-829) [4-6], before measuring the brake pump maximum pressure, you must screw the **sequence valve V3503 adjustment screw 513** to the **closed position (all the way in)** [3, 5].

The complete step-by-step diagnostic procedure to verify the target 280 bar (± 8 bar) maximum pressure for pump block P3511 is as follows:

1. Ensure that the machine is on an even surface, the parking brake is applied, and movement is prevented by wheel chocks [2, 5].
2. Install the frame articulation locking device [2, 5].
3. Screw the sequence valve **V3503** adjustment screw **513** to the closed position [3, 5].
4. Connect a **400 bar pressure gauge** to the sequence valve **V3503** measuring point **MP501** [3, 5].
5. Start the engine [3, 5].
6. Record the pressure gauge reading to verify it meets the correct maximum pressure of **280 bar (± 8 bar)** [3, 6].
7. Adjust the maximum pressure if necessary using **adjustment screw 501** [3, 6].
8. Stop the engine [3, 6].
9. Screw the sequence valve **V3503** adjustment screw **513** back to the fully open position, and then **¼ turn back in** [3, 6].

questions.question: What is the specified operating pressure range maintained by the transmission clutch pressure regulator valve, and which specific pressure transducer (B-number) is utilized to monitor this parameter?
questions.answer:
The transmission clutch pressure regulator valve (Component 7) maintains the clutch pressure within a specified operating range of **16.55 to 19.33 bar** [1, 2]. 

This parameter is monitored by the transmission oil pressure transducer **B3005** (or B305), which is located at the clutch pressure measurement point (Component 13) [3-5]. This information can be found in the Service and Repair Manual LH410, Section 9.2 "Transmission hydraulics" on pages 315–316 [1, 2, 4].

questions.question: When adjusting the boom and bucket double pump block P3211, what specific pressure difference should be observed between measurement points MP201 and MP202 to confirm the load-sensing dp-pressure is correctly calibrated?
questions.answer:
According to the Service and Repair Manual LH410 (Section 12.14.3 "Checking and adjusting the bucket pump pressures", pages 741-742) and the Maintenance Manual LH410 (Section 5.6.14 "Check bucket pump pressure", pages 326-327), when checking the load-sensing dp-pressure for the boom and bucket pump block **P3211**, the correct pressure difference should be **30 bar (±2 bar)** [1-4].

The step-by-step procedure to confirm and calibrate this is as follows:
1. Connect 400-bar pressure gauges to the measurement points **MP201** and **MP202**, located at the bucket pump [3, 5].
2. Start the engine [1, 3].
3. Check the pressure difference from the gauges; the reading must be **30 bar (±2 bar)** [1, 3].
4. If the pressure difference is incorrect, adjust it by turning **adjustment screw 202** [3].

questions.question: When calibrating the brake charging valve V3502 using a gauge at measurement point MP503, what are the specific upper and lower pressure limits that dictate when the charging valve spool shifts to redirect flow from pump block P3511?
questions.answer:
Based on the Service and Repair Manual LH410, the specific pressure limits that dictate when the brake charging valve (V3502) spool shifts to redirect flow from the pump block (P3511) are:

*   **Lower Limit:** **150 bar (± 5 bar)** [1, 2]. As soon as the oil pressure in the accumulators drops below 150 bar, the charging valve spool shifts back to its initial position, and the charging cycle starts from the beginning [1].
*   **Upper Limit:** **190 bar (± 5 bar)** [2, 3]. When the pressure in the pump line increases up to 190 bar, the charging valve spool shifts to the third position. This drops the control pressure to 0 bar, which opens the external sequence valve (V3503) and redirects pump flow away from the accumulators [3, 4].

According to Section 13.12.4 "Brake charging valve pressure check" (pages 830-833), the complete step-by-step procedure to check and calibrate these limits using a gauge at measurement point MP503 is as follows [2, 5-8]:

1. Make sure that the machine is on an even surface, the parking brake is applied, and movement is prevented with wheel chocks [5].
2. Install the frame articulation locking device [6].
3. Turn off the engine [6].
4. Check from the VCM System display that the brake charging pressure is 0 bar [6].
5. Connect a capillary test hose to the measurement connection (A) to make sure that the brake charging circuit is non-pressurized [6].
6. Check the pre-charge pressure of the brake system pressure accumulator (B), which should be 90 bar (± 3 bar). Recharge/discharge if needed [6].
7. Remove the capillary test hose from the measurement connection (A) [7].
8. Connect a **400-bar pressure gauge** to measurement point **MP503** of brake charging valve M2 (A) [7].
9. Screw the brake charging cartridge's adjusting screw (D) lightly to the closed position. *(Note: Do not overtighten as it can damage the charging valve)* [7].
10. Turn the charging valve's pressure reducing valve (C) open [7].
11. Turn the pressure relief valve (F) open [7].
12. Start the engine [7].
13. Wait until the pressure accumulators are fully charged. Check from the gauge display that the pressure reading will not rise [7].
14. Adjust the pressure with the pressure reducing valve's adjusting screw (C). The correct pressure is **205 bar (+2 / -5 bar)** [2].
15. Unscrew the brake charging cartridge adjusting screw (D) to decrease the pressure until the correct lower limit pressure is reached. The correct setting is **150 bar (± 5 bar)** [2].
16. Turn the adjustment screw of the pressure relief valve (F) so that the pressure rises to set the upper limit. The correct setting is **190 bar (± 5 bar)** [2].
17. Test the functioning by detaching the valve's coil or electric connector (E) [8]. Wait until the pressure falls under 150 bar, reconnect the coil/connector, and check that it charges to the correct **190 bar (± 5 bar)** upper limit. Adjust if necessary [8].

questions.question: What is the normal operating pressure range (in bar) regulated by the transmission torque converter pressure regulator, and at what specific pressure limit does the converter safety valve intervene if the regulator fails?
questions.answer:
According to the Service and Repair Manual LH410 (Section 9.2 "Transmission hydraulics", pages 315–316), the converter pressure regulator (**Component 9**) regulates the normal operating pressure in the torque converter and is set to maintain it between **3.79 and 4.83 bar** [1, 2]. 

If the converter pressure regulator fails to operate properly, the converter pressure safety valve (**Component 8**) intervenes to ensure the pressure is kept below a maximum limit of **8.96 bar** [2].

questions.question: What is the function of the brake release pump unit A3542 and its associated components?
questions.answer: The brake release pump unit **A3542** is an electrically driven pump (powered by electric motor **M320**) used to generate pressure to release the parking/emergency brakes if the machine breaks down or the engine shuts off unexpectedly [19]. It includes a pressure relief valve **V3582** that limits the maximum pressure to 210 bar, a limit switch **S3048** that permits the pump to operate only when the accumulator pressure is below 140 bar, and a non-return valve to prevent the accumulator's capacity from flowing back into the pump [19, 20]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the InfraFREE CAN bus cable color-coded and pinned for navigation module connections?
questions.answer: The InfraFREE CAN bus cable is a 5 x 0.5 mm² cable equipped with a 5-pin MIL male connector [8, 9]. Inside the cable, the green wire is used for CAN High (CAN H) on Pin **C**, the brown wire is used for CAN Low (CAN L) on Pin **D**, and the yellow wire serves as the ground (GND) on Pin **B** [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the steps to calibrate the brake charging valve pressures (reducing, lower limit, and upper limit)?
questions.answer: Connect a gauge to MP503 on the brake charging valve M2 [11]. Lightly screw the charging cartridge's adjusting screw (D) to the closed position, then fully open the pressure reducing valve (C) and the pressure relief valve (F) [11]. Start the engine, let the accumulators charge, and adjust the pressure reducing valve (C) to 205 bar (+2/-5 bar) [11, 12]. Next, unscrew the charging cartridge adjusting screw (D) until the pressure drops to the lower limit setpoint of 150 bar (±5 bar) [12]. Finally, turn the pressure relief valve adjusting screw (F) to set the upper limit to 190 bar (±5 bar) [12]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the ejector pressure (optional feature) checked and adjusted?
questions.answer: Connect gauges to MP213 and MP214 on the ejector cylinder pressure lines [17, 18]. Extend the ejector plate completely against the limiter; the pressure at MP213 should read 210 bar (±5 bar), which can be adjusted via screw 213 after removing its cover plug [18]. Then retract the plate completely against the limiter; the pressure at MP214 should read 160 bar (±5 bar), which can be adjusted via screw 214 [18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the "ERROR! BUCKET IS NOT EMPTY!" message during the weighing process?
questions.answer: This error happens when the operator lowers the boom without dumping the bucket first, so the system recognizes the bucket still has material [12, 13]. The operator should perform a new weighing and properly dump the bucket, ensuring they remember to empty the bucket before lowering the boom next time [13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you verify the CAN bus status and connection parameters via the Remote Monitoring System (RMT)?
questions.answer: Log into the RMT, open the Signals page, type "CAN error state" into the search field, and verify the value is **0** (which indicates the CAN bus state is OK) [10]. If the state is not 0, verify the Data management unit's status LED is GREEN and check that the CAN bus connection is securely fitted to the **CAN 1** connector [10]. Ensure that the CAN bus has a **120 Ohm** resistance connected to the output of the **CAN 1** connection, and verify with the power isolated that only two terminating resistors are on the machine, yielding a **60 Ohm** reading across the CAN H and CAN L wires [10, 11]. Finally, ensure the CAN bus configurations are set to **CAN 1** and the communication speed is exactly **250 kbit/s** [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the overall health and physical configuration of the CAN bus network verified?
questions.answer: You can verify CAN bus health through the Remote Monitoring Tool (RMT) by checking that the **"CAN error state" is 0** [14]. If errors are present, verify that the module's status LED is green, the bus speed is set to **250 kb/s**, and the connection is securely on CAN 1 [14, 15]. With the power isolated, measure the resistance across the CAN H and CAN L wires; it must read exactly **60 Ohms**, which confirms that only two 120-Ohm terminating resistors are properly installed on the network [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How should an operator respond to an "Engine over-rev warning" or "Engine Overspeed"?
questions.answer: This warning appears when the engine speed is too high and exceeds the set parameter limits [7, 8]. The operator must decrease the engine revolutions below the warning limit [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the role of the steering main valve, and what is its component ID?
questions.answer: The steering main valve, identified as **V3102**, is a hydraulically controlled, pressure-compensated mobile valve that directs oil flow to the steering cylinders [4, 5]. It features an integrated priority block that limits pressure to the steering valve to 130 bar, safety relief valves limiting steering cylinder pressure to 160 bar, and a main pressure relief valve limiting the maximum valve inlet pressure to 290 bar [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you test if the steering cylinder piston seals are bypassing from the piston side to the rod side?
questions.answer: Turn the machine fully to the right (to test the left cylinder) or fully to the left (to test the right cylinder) and install the frame articulation locking device. Depressurize the hydraulic tank and release the hydraulic pressure from the steering circuits by connecting a capillary test hose to the steering test points. Disconnect the rod side hydraulic line at the manifold block and allow it to drain into a container. Start the engine and turn the steering joystick in the same direction the machine is already articulated. If oil flows from the disconnected cylinder line, the piston seals are bypassing and the cylinder requires replacement or overhaul [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical transducers monitor the pressures in the brake system?
questions.answer: The brake system pressures are monitored by four primary 4-20 mA analog transducers [14]. Pressure transducer **B3056** measures the front brake circuit pressure, **B3057** measures the rear brake circuit pressure, **B3034** measures the brake charging/accumulator pressure, and **B3058** measures the brake pedal output pressure [15, 16]. These sensors feed data to the Middle and Rear control modules [14, 17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you verify the brake pump maximum pressure?
questions.answer: Ensure the machine is on a level surface, the parking brake is applied, wheel chocks are in place, and the frame articulation locking device is installed. Screw the sequence valve **V3503** adjustment screw **513** all the way in to the closed position. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the sequence valve **V3503** measuring point **MP501**. Start the engine and check the reading; the correct maximum pressure is **280 bar (±8 bar)**. After the test is complete, stop the engine and make sure to unscrew the adjustment screw **513** back to the fully open position [8-10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specifications and outputs for the boom, bucket, and engine cooler pump (double pump P3221)?
questions.answer: The double pump P3221 also features two blocks. Block **P3211** is responsible for the boom and bucket hydraulics, delivering a flow of 143 l/min at 2200 pump rpm with a maximum pressure of 265 bar (±8 bar) [2-4]. Block **P3311** handles the engine cooler, delivering 56 l/min at 2200 pump rpm with a maximum pressure of 190 bar (±5 bar) for Volvo engines or 150 bar (±5 bar) for Mercedes-Benz engines [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the system displays "Chair 64 No data received in SAE J 1939 from ECM"?
questions.answer: This alarm indicates a **contact failure between the J1939 and the CAN bus** [9]. To diagnose, turn the ignition key to position 1 and measure the voltage of connectors XC4.7 and XC4.8 against the earth, which should be **2-3 V** [9]. Then, turn the power off and measure the resistance between the two pins; it should read **55-65 Ohms** [10]. If the resistance differs, inspect the terminal resistor and wire harness [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component transforms the voltage for the radio/CD player, and what are the functions of relays K0011 and K0023?
questions.answer: The voltage transformer **G0003** transforms the machine's +24V voltage to +12V to power the radio/CD player [1]. Relay **K0011** is the engine running relay; when the engine is running, the interface grounds this coil, which then controls the current supply for the optional beacon **E1043** and the air conditioning unit [1]. Relay **K0023** is the horn signal relay; it becomes energized to sound the signal horn **H3001** for three seconds when the engine starts, or when the operator presses the horn button on the joystick [1-3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the steering main valve relief and external load relief pressures?
questions.answer: To adjust the steering main valve relief, first screw the steering pump maximum pressure screw (101) and stand-by pressure screw (102) lightly in [5, 6]. Connect a gauge to MP101 and check that the pressure is 290 bar (±8 bar); adjust it using screw 106 if necessary [6]. For the external load reliefs, install the frame articulation lock and connect gauges to MP103 and MP104 [7]. Turn the machine against the locking device in each direction; the pressure for both the left (MP103) and right (MP104) should be 160 bar (±5 bar), adjusted via screws 103 and 104 [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the steering or bucket control does not work?
questions.answer: If the steering or bucket control fails, first ensure the engine is running and check all emergency stops (one in the cabin and one on both sides of the machine) to ensure they are not activated. Verify the cabin door is closed, as the system includes an interlock for the steering and bucket hydraulics. Check if the frame articulation locking device is installed. Additionally, look for any active alarms on the control system display, verify that the hydraulic oil level is not low, and confirm that the pilot pressure is correct [1]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the general rule for operators when any warning or alarm appears on the display?
questions.answer: If any warning (indicated by a blinking yellow triangle and yellow light) or alarm (indicated by a blinking red triangle and red light) appears, the operator must not operate the loader until the cause has been determined and the possible fault has been repaired [1-6]. The operator should call a service person to address the underlying issue [1, 3, 4, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot STE_COMM, BO_COMM, or BU_COMM errors indicating no angle measurement is received from the CAN bus?
questions.answer: These errors mean the steering, boom, or bucket angle measurements are missing because the **CAN sensor, the sensor cable, or the CAN bus interface card is broken** [11-13]. Diagnosis involves conducting a visual inspection and running a hardware test (`hwtest`) on the specific sensor to pinpoint the failure, followed by replacing the faulty cable, sensor, or interface board [11-13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you perform quick diagnostics on the digital outputs of the control modules to test wire harnesses or actuators?
questions.answer: You can use the "I/O Force" window on the display to manually force the digital outputs of a module's connector on or off [12]. Select the desired module and connector, switch the output to "1" (on) or "0" (off), and press and hold the SEND button to activate the forcing [12, 13]. If an alarm stops when an output is forced, it usually indicates a short circuit in the wire harness [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component regulates the brake charging pressure, and what sub-components does it contain?
questions.answer: The brake charging valve **V3502** regulates the brake accumulator oil pressure to the proper working range of 150-190 bar [6, 7]. It contains a main pressure relief valve set to 300 bar to protect against pressure peaks, a pressure reducing valve set to 205 bar, a charging valve, and a pressure relief valve [8, 9]. It also includes solenoid valves such as **Y3052** (for discharging accumulators when the machine shuts down) and **Y3001** / **Y3048** (for activating the parking and emergency brakes) [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the machine's main ignition current does not go on?
questions.answer: First, check that the main switch is in the ON position [1]. Next, inspect the main circuit breakers **F3035** and **F3064** located in the fuse box **X3056** to ensure they are not tripped [1]. Finally, check the system voltage on the VCM display; the normal operating voltage should be approximately **24-27 Volts** [2]. If the voltage is below normal, inspect the battery connections [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What troubleshooting steps should be taken if there is absolutely no pressure in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: A complete loss of pressure is often due to a **clogged intake, low oil level, an air leak in the intake, excessively high oil viscosity, or a faulty pump** [3]. To diagnose this, **check the entire system from the reservoir to the pump**, ensuring filters and strainers are not plugged, verify the oil level, and inspect the intake side for any air leaks [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a "Control system module missing" (e.g., Chair 26) alarm that activates the emergency stop?
questions.answer: Check the alarm log to identify the missing module and turn off the main power [1]. Inspect the AMP8 connector (e.g., pins XM4.4 and XM4.5) to ensure it carries the machine's operating voltage of 24-27 V [1]. Verify there is zero resistance to the machine's ground on the ground pins, and measure the CAN-bus resistance between pins XM4.2 and XM4.6, which must be 55-65 Ohms [2]. If all wiring and resistance values are correct but the alarm persists, change the missing module [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot missing PDO messages from CAN sensors, such as "Pressure sensor message is missing" (Front 138, 139) or "Inclination sensor message is missing" (Front 140)?
questions.answer: First, reboot the machine [6]. If the error persists, disconnect the AMP8 connector XF4 from the Front module and measure the resistance between CAN High and CAN Low (pins 7 and 8), which should be about 60 Ohms [7]. Verify the voltage at the end of the CAN 2 bus is approximately 24 V [8]. To identify a sensor that may have disrupted the bus, disconnect all sensors and reconnect them one by one with a terminator, rebooting each time until the faulty unit is found [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are boom or bucket controller errors (such as the bucket not dumping within 20 seconds or sensor readings not responding) diagnosed?
questions.answer: These operational errors can stem from **hydraulic leakages, broken sensor fastenings, actuator problems, or physical obstructions** like the bucket pushing against an object [5, 6]. Diagnosis involves **conducting a visual inspection** for objects under the bucket or broken sensor mounts, **testing the steering and actuator response in remote mode**, and taking logs for system support to pinpoint hydraulic leakages [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the ride control and boom floating functions electrically activated, and what sensors do they rely on?
questions.answer: Ride control is activated by the operator using button **S0038**, and boom floating is activated using button **S0074** [19]. Both functions require the boom to be lowered to operate safely, which is monitored by the boom lower limit inductive switch **S2036** and the ride control limit switch **S2034** [20-22]. Once the sensors confirm the boom is in the correct position, the system energizes the corresponding solenoid valves [20, 23, 24]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the Data Management Unit in the AutoMine Remote Monitoring system, and which connectors are assigned to the CAN bus?
questions.answer: The Data Management Unit collects and structures measurement data from the machine's existing CAN bus and transmits it to the AutoMine Remote Monitoring server [10]. It uses specific ports to interface with the network: connector **X8** is for CAN 1 in, **X9** is for CAN 1 out, **X10** is for CAN 2 in, and **X11** is for CAN 2 out [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a noisy hydraulic pump and what are its usual causes?
questions.answer: A noisy pump is typically caused by **air in the system, cavitation (a vacuum on the intake), or a worn pump** [3]. Diagnosis involves **checking the complete system for air leaks**, checking for restrictions on the intake line, ensuring the pump and reservoir air vents are not clogged, and verifying that the oil viscosity is not too high [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes the "The engine will be shut down!" pop-up and what should be done?
questions.answer: This alarm occurs when a low engine oil pressure is detected; a counter will appear on the screen showing the remaining time until the engine automatically shuts down [9]. The operator or service personnel should immediately check the engine oil level, ensure the oil filters are not blocked, and verify the oil pressure sensor function [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What troubleshooting steps should be taken if the system displays a "Chair 64 No data received in SAE J 1939 from ECM" alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm indicates a contact failure between the J1939 and the CAN bus [3]. First, turn the ignition key to position I (power on) and disconnect the Chair module connectors **XC4.7** and **XC4.8** [3]. Measure the voltage of both connectors against the earth; it should read approximately **2-3 V** [3]. If there is no voltage, the cable must be repaired [3]. Next, turn the ignition key to position 0 (power off) and measure the resistance between **XC4.7** and **XC4.8** [4]. The resistance should be **55 - 65 Ohms** [4]. If it differs from this range, inspect the terminal resistor and the wire harness [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions and part numbers of the ignition switch and the door switch?
questions.answer: The ignition switch **S0004** controls the engine states, including parking (P), electric power on (I), and starting the engine (III) [4, 5]. The door switch **S1147** monitors whether the cabin door is open or closed, acting as a safety interlock that prevents functions like steering, boom, and bucket control if the door is open [6-8]. The switch also directly routes battery voltage to illuminate the cabin lights when the door is opened [6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a "CANopen transmit buffer full (bus overloaded)" alarm indicate and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: Alarms such as Chair 4, Dash 4, Front 4, Middle 4, or Rear 4 indicate that the CANopen transmit buffer is full due to bus overloading [4, 5]. If these alarms are active and the machine is not working, the CAN bus coupling needs to be systematically checked and repaired [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical components control the automatic fire suppression system?
questions.answer: The fire suppression system (such as the Sandvik FS1000 or Ansul Checkfire) utilizes a fire sensor connected to the Dashboard module [27]. If a fire is detected, the Dashboard module triggers the activation relay/output **K0255** to release the extinguisher [27]. The system operates on its own 3.6 VDC internal battery located in its control module, and relies on twin pressure switches (900 kPa and 1200 kPa) to monitor the activation circuit pressure and shut down the engine upon discharge [28, 29]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a "Chair 33 / 34" alarm indicating a short circuit in the voltage supply of the left-hand side steering joystick push buttons?
questions.answer: Detach the Chair module connector pin **XC1.1** [3, 4]. Turn off the system’s operating voltage and then turn it back on [3, 4]. If the alarm does not reappear, the fault is a short circuit to the earth or supply voltage within the wire harness, which must be repaired [3, 4]. If detaching the pin does not stop the alarm, the Chair module itself is broken and needs to be replaced [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the sequence valve V3503 in the hydraulic circuit?
questions.answer: The sequence valve **V3503** directs hydraulic flow to the brake charging valve, using its spring force to define the brake charging volume flow [12]. When brake charging is not active, the sequence valve directs the excessive oil flow to the hydraulic motors in the side coolers (**A3561** and **A3562**) to rotate the cooling fans, and then routes the flow to the wheel end brakes for cooling and flushing [7, 13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for setting the steering pump dp-pressure and maximum pressure?
questions.answer: First, connect 400-bar gauges to pressure measurement points MP101 and MP102 and start the engine [3, 4]. The dp-pressure difference must be 30 bar (±2 bar), and it is adjusted via screw 102 [4]. To set the maximum pressure, connect a gauge to MP101, lower the boom against the limiter, and hold the joystick in the extreme position [4]. The maximum steering pump pressure must be 250 bar (±8 bar), which is adjusted using screw 101 [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the bucket pump pressures (dp-pressure and maximum pressure) checked and adjusted?
questions.answer: To check the dp-pressure, connect 400-bar pressure gauges to measurement points MP201 and MP202 [1]. With the engine running, the pressure difference must be 30 bar (±2 bar), which can be adjusted using adjustment screw 202 [1]. To check the maximum pressure, connect a gauge to MP201, lower the boom against the limiter, and hold the joystick in the extreme position [1]. The maximum pressure must be 265 bar (±8 bar), and it is adjusted using screw 201 [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are faults related to a missing control system module diagnosed when the emergency stop is activated?
questions.answer: Check the alarm log to identify the missing module, then turn off the main power and inspect the AMP8 connector [5]. Measure the connector pins (e.g., XM4.4 and XM4.5) to ensure they carry the machine's operating voltage of 24-27 Volts [5]. Also, verify there is zero resistance to the machine's ground on the ground pins, and check that the CAN-bus resistance across the connector (e.g., XM4.2 and XM4.6) is between 55 and 65 Ohms [6]. If the wiring and resistance values are correct, the missing module must be replaced [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system indicate an "OVERLOAD!" during weighing, and what is the required action?
questions.answer: If the weighing result exceeds the maximum load limit, a pop-up is shown to the operator and the event is entered into the error log [12, 13]. Because overloads damage the machine and decrease its lifetime, the operator must reduce the load in the bucket on the next lift [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specified pressure settings for the steering hydraulic circuit?
questions.answer: The steering hydraulic circuit has several precise pressure setpoints: the steering pump maximum pressure is **250 bar (±8 bar)**, the dp-pressure is **30 bar (±2 bar)**, and the pilot pressure is **35 bar (±10 bar)** [3, 5]. Furthermore, the steering valve main relief is set at **290 bar (±8 bar)**, the priority valve pressure is **130 bar (±5 bar)**, and the external load pressure relief is set at **160 bar (±5 bar)** [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific angle and pressure sensors operate on the CAN bus, and what are their component IDs?
questions.answer: The middle joint (articulation) angle sensor (**B330**) and the boom position sensor (**B232**) are connected to the CAN bus and communicate using the CANopen protocol [4-6]. Additionally, the system utilizes CAN-based sensors for boom pressure 1 (**B2031**, piston side), boom pressure 2 (**B2032**, rod side), and inclination/tilt (**B2041**) [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure if the system displays a "Chair 43 Module ref 5 V out of limits" alarm related to the throttle pedal coupling?
questions.answer: Check the **+5 V REF** voltage on the **XC3** connector’s measurement window [5, 6]. If the voltage is low, disconnect the Chair module connector pin **XC3.2** [6]. If the voltage settles back to **5 V**, the fault lies in the joystick cables or the potentiometer [6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the setpoints and adjustment procedures for the engine cooler fan pump?
questions.answer: Connect a gauge to MP301 to check the stand-by pressure, which must be 25 bar (±5 bar) [13-15]. This is adjustable via screw 302 or through the VCM display by modifying the minimum current [14, 15]. To check the maximum pressure, connect a gauge to MP301 and accelerate the engine to maximum rpm [15, 16]. The maximum pressure value must be 190 bar (±5 bar) for Volvo engines or 150 bar (±5 bar) for Mercedes-Benz engines, and it can be adjusted via screw 301 [16]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the main circuit breakers for the battery and machine electrics, and where are they located?
questions.answer: The main circuit breaker for the battery and starter motor is **F3035**, rated at 400 Amps [25, 26]. The main circuit breaker for the general machine electrics (and the optional emergency steering pump supply) is **F3064**, rated at 150 Amps [25, 26]. Both of these critical breakers are located in the rear frame circuit breaker box designated as **X3056** [25, 26]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure to check and adjust the bucket pump maximum pressure?
questions.answer: Ensure the hydraulic oil temperature is at normal operating levels (60-80ºC). Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the bucket pump measurement point **MP201**. Start the engine, lower the boom against the limiter, and hold the joystick in the extreme position. The maximum pressure value on the gauge must be **265 bar (±8 bar)**. If the pressure needs adjustment, turn adjustment screw **201** until the correct value is reached [2-5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary root causes of hydraulic system failures on the loaders?
questions.answer: The four most common basic causes of hydraulic system failures are **dirt, heat, water, and cavitation** [1]. **Dirt is considered the worst** of the four because it acts as an abrasive, causing rapid wear to the hydraulic components [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the part numbers and functions of the terminating resistors used in the CAN bus system?
questions.answer: Terminating resistors are required at each end of the CAN bus to prevent signal reflection, ensuring stable communication across the network [1, 2]. Each terminating resistor provides 120 Ohms of resistance, which equates to a 60 Ohm reading when measured across the CAN High and CAN Low wires in the middle of the bus [1, 2]. If a CAN joint point (e.g., connector **X3153**) is not connected to a module, a 120-Ohm end resistor (part number **55032288**, part 2) must be installed [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary filters in the main hydraulic and brake systems, and what are their part numbers?
questions.answer: The main hydraulic oil tank is equipped with a return filter **Z3421** to clean returning oil and features magnetic filtration [21, 22]. The brake hydraulic oil tank uses the return filter **Z3521** for the brake flushing return flow [21, 23]. Additionally, the high-pressure brake circuit features a pressure filter, **Z3511**, which separates particles from the oil before it reaches the brake valves, and is equipped with a bypass valve and an electrical clogging indicator (**S3078**) [6, 24]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you perform a leakage test on the lift cylinders?
questions.answer: Make sure the bucket is empty, raise the boom, and install the boom locking pins. Stop the engine, install the frame articulation locking device, and depressurize the hydraulic oil tank. Bleed the hydraulic pressure from the lift cylinders using a test hose on the junction block test points. Disconnect the piston side hydraulic line of the left side lift cylinder at the junction block and let it drain into a container. Start the engine and slowly push the boom control joystick forward into the "boom down" position. If oil flows from the disconnected line, the **left side** cylinder piston seal is leaking. If oil flows from the junction block itself, the **right side** cylinder piston seal is leaking [5, 11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions and part numbers of the main piston-type double pumps in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The system utilizes two piston-type double pumps.
