The **P3122** pump has two blocks: block **P3111** produces the pressure and flow required for steering and pilot control, and block **P3511** supplies the brake hydraulics, oil coolers, and air conditioning [1, 2]. The second double pump, **P3221**, also features two blocks: block **P3211** powers the boom and bucket hydraulics, while block **P3311** is an electrically adjusted pump that supplies the engine cooling system [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a "No data received in SAE J 1939 from ECM" (Chair 64) alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm points to a contact failure between the J1939 and the CAN bus [10]. Turn the ignition key to position 1 (power on) and measure the voltage of connectors XC4.7 and XC4.8 against the earth, which should be 2-3 V [10]. Next, turn the power off and measure the resistance between the two pins, which must be 55-65 Ohms [11]. If the resistance is out of range, inspect the terminal resistor and the wire harness [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a "Tilt angle lengthways high alarm" handled?
questions.answer: This alarm (e.g., Front 75, 87, 95, 98) indicates the machine's tilt angle is dangerously high [17, 18]. The operator should immediately try to reduce the tilt angle of the machine to ensure safe working conditions [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should an operator do if they receive a "Low accuracy!" or "Weighing error" pop-up during a lift?
questions.answer: These warnings indicate that weighing was performed under improper conditions, such as varying the lifting speed, varying the engine RPM, or starting the lift without the bucket in the fully back position [14-16]. The operator does not need to repeat the weigh, as the result is still logged, but next time they must avoid varying the lifting and engine speed, and maintain full, constant RPM and joystick control during the weighing lift [14-16]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Where do the CAN 2 bus pressure sensors and inclinometer connect to the VCM system, and how is that specific bus terminated?
questions.answer: The CAN 2 bus sensors communicate with the machine's **Front module** through the AMP8 connector **XF4**, utilizing pin **7** for CAN High and pin **8** for CAN Low [12]. The CAN 2 bus is terminated at the far end of the line (near the pressure sensors) by a CAN terminator featuring an M12 connector, identified as **XJ216B** [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a sluggish or slow-moving hydraulic system diagnosed?
questions.answer: If a hydraulic system slows down, becomes sluggish, or loses pressure, it usually indicates a faulty component or an internal/external leak [4]. To locate the fault, you should **measure the time it takes the hydraulic system to complete a cycle** and **check to see if the pressure output is normal** [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration requirements and specifications for the main hydraulic and brake systems?
questions.answer: The main hydraulic oil tank utilizes the return filter **Z3421**, which has a filtering capacity of **β10=75** and includes magnetic filtration [7]. It has a spring-loaded non-return bypass valve that opens if the pressure difference exceeds **1.6 bar** [7]. The brake hydraulic circuit utilizes a high-pressure filter **Z3511** with a finer filtration capacity of **β10=200** [8]. This brake pressure filter features an electric indicator (S3078) that triggers an alarm if the pressure difference exceeds **5 bar**, and a bypass valve that opens at a **7 bar** difference [8]. The brake system also uses its own return filter **Z3521** with a bypass valve that opens at a **0.4 bar** difference [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does the "Hammer kept on too long time" alarm mean when using the optional hydraulic breaker?
questions.answer: This alarm (Front 24) means the hydraulic hammer has been used continuously for too long and the system has automatically shut it down [19]. The operator must stop hammering for a moment to allow the rammer temperature to reduce [19]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if there is a "Front 65 Drive shaft speed sensor A failure" alarm?
questions.answer: First, verify the wire harness by measuring the resistance of the cable between the Front module connector pin **XF3.16** and the sensor **S3038** connector pin **4** [7, 8]. If the cable is intact, check the sensor current supply by measuring the voltage from connector **S3038** pin **1**, which must read exactly **12 V** [8]. If the voltage is correct and the harness is not broken, the sensor itself is faulty and must be replaced [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot missing CAN sensor readings from the navigation module for the boom/box or middle joint sensors?
questions.answer: Establish a telnet connection to the navigation module and run the hardware test tool [5, 6]. Use the command **`hwtest -c MJ`** to test the middle joint sensor, or **`hwtest -c BO`** for the boom/box sensor [7]. If the printed reading is zero, it indicates a fault in the Navigation module CAN cable, the Sensor cable, the Navigation module CAN interface, or the sensor itself [7]. If no CAN data is received from *any* devices, replace the CAN cable first, then the navigation module [8]. If only the specific sensor fails but other CAN devices work, the sensor cable or sensor is broken; test the cable with a multimeter, or swap the sensor with a spare unit and run the `hwtest` again [8, 9]. Note that replaced sensors must be recalibrated via the VCM System interface [9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the brake pump maximum pressure checked and adjusted?
questions.answer: Ensure the machine is safely parked and the frame articulation lock is installed [9]. Screw the sequence valve V3503 adjustment screw 513 all the way in to the closed position and connect a gauge to MP501 [9]. Start the engine and verify the maximum pressure is 280 bar (±8 bar); adjust using screw 501 if required [9, 10]. After checking, ensure you screw the sequence valve adjustment screw 513 back to the fully open position and then turn it ¼ turn back in [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be done if the system shows a "Module ref 5 V out of limits" alarm (e.g., Chair 43)?
questions.answer: This means the operating voltage for components like the steering joystick or throttle pedal is too low [9]. Check the +5 V REF voltage on the corresponding connector's measurement window (e.g., XC3) [9]. If the voltage is low, remove the relevant connector pins (e.g., XC3.2 and XC3.10) [9]. If the voltage settles back at 5V, the fault lies in the steering joystick, throttle pedal, boom/bucket joystick, or their wire harnesses, which should be disconnected one by one to isolate the short [9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a "CANopen transmit buffer full (bus overloaded)" alarm mean, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: Alarms such as "Chair 4", "Dash 4", "Front 4", "Middle 4", or "Rear 4" indicate that the CANopen transmit buffer is full, meaning the CAN bus is overloaded [12, 13]. If these alarms appear in the alarm log and the machine is not working, the CAN bus coupling must be checked and repaired [13]. Similarly, if the system throws alarms for "CANopen error frames detected" (e.g., Chair 5, Front 5, Rear 5), the CAN bus coupling also needs to be systematically checked and fixed to clear the communication errors [14]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which sensors are used to measure the temperature of the machine's oils, and where do they connect?
questions.answer: The hydraulic oil temperature is measured by sensor **B3001**, the transmission oil temperature by sensor **B3002**, and the brake hydraulic oil temperature by sensor **B3068** [12, 13]. These are PT1000 analog temperature sensors that send their signals directly to the Middle module [13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the cause of a "Tire over temperature" alarm and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: This alarm (e.g., Chair 60-63) indicates that the tire temperature is too high [10]. The required operator response is to decrease the tramming speed of the machine [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component controls the movement of the boom and bucket, and how does it function?
questions.answer: The boom and bucket main valve, **V2201**, is a proportional directional two-section monoblock valve controlled by electrohydraulic pilot valves [15-17]. It uses internal spools to control the flow to the tilt cylinder and lift cylinders [16, 18]. The valve block includes a main pressure relief valve (**V2281**) set to 300 bar, pressure relief valves limiting the cylinders to 280 bar, and anti-cavitation valves to prevent cavitation in the cylinders [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the flow rates and maximum pressures for the double pump P3122?
questions.answer: The piston-type double pump P3122 consists of two blocks. Block **P3111** produces the hydraulic flow for steering and pilot control with a maximum pressure of 250 bar and a flow rate of 143 l/min at 2200 pump rpm [1]. Block **P3511** provides flow for the brake hydraulics, oil coolers, and air conditioning with a maximum pressure of 280 bar and a flow rate of 56 l/min [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot an emergency stop activation caused by a "Control system module missing" (Alarm Chair 26)?
questions.answer: Check the alarm log to identify which module is missing, then turn off the main power [9]. Check the AMP8-connector for current flow (e.g., pins **XM4.4** and **XM4.5**); these pins must carry the machine's operating voltage of approx. **24-27 V** [9]. Check the ground connection (e.g., pins **XM4.1** and **XM4.3**) for zero resistance to the machine's ground using a multimeter [10]. Finally, measure the CAN-bus resistance between pins **XM4.2** and **XM4.6** with the power off; it should be **55 - 65 Ohms** [10]. If all wiring, ground, and CAN-bus resistance values are correct, replace the missing module [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system indicate a blown circuit breaker and how is it addressed?
questions.answer: If any circuit breaker blows, with the exception of the main circuit breakers F3035 and F3064, a specific alarm will appear on the control system display [11, 12]. To diagnose, check the state of the automatic fuses; if the problem continues after resetting, the wiring harness must be inspected for faults [13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose "Pressure sensor message is missing" or "Inclination sensor message is missing" errors on the CAN 2 bus?
questions.answer: These errors (e.g., Front 138, 139, 140) mean PDO messages are missing. First, reboot the machine; if that fails, **measure the CAN 2 bus resistance between CAN High and CAN Low, which should be about 60 Ohms** [4-6]. Also verify the power supply is approx. 24 V [7]. To identify a sensor that may have "killed" the bus, **disconnect all sensors and reconnect them one by one** with a terminator, rebooting each time until the faulty unit is found [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which electrical components handle the operator's steering and boom/bucket inputs?
questions.answer: Steering is controlled by the left-hand joystick **S1149**, which connects to the Chair module and sends Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) signals to the Middle module to operate the steering proportional valves [9]. The boom and bucket are controlled by the right-hand joystick **S1148**, which is connected to the Dashboard module and sends PWM signals to the Front module to control the boom up/down and bucket functions [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does it mean when the system logs alarms like "Chair 4" or "Front 4 CANopen transmit buffer full (bus overloaded)", and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: These alarms indicate that the CANopen transmit buffer is full, meaning the **CAN bus is overloaded** [1]. If these alarms—or similar "CANopen error frames detected" alarms (e.g., Chair 5, Middle 5)—are active and the machine is not working, the **CAN bus coupling must be systematically checked and repaired** [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should the operator do if a "Tire under pressure" alarm appears?
questions.answer: This alarm (e.g., Chair 128-135) means the tire pressure is too low [11]. The operator must check that the tire or its valve is not damaged and add more air if necessary [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a "short to ground" or "short to external voltage" alarm on a module supply pin?
questions.answer: Detach the specific connector pin indicated by the alarm (for example, pin XF2.1 on the Front module or XM2.23 on the Middle module) and turn the system's operating voltage off and back on [3, 4]. If the alarm stops, the fault is a short circuit within the wire harness, which must be repaired [3, 4]. If the alarm persists, the module itself is broken and must be replaced [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary pressure limits and settings for the brake hydraulic circuit?
questions.answer: The brake pump's maximum pressure is set to **280 bar (±8 bar)** [6]. The brake charging valve regulates the system to maintain an upper charging limit of **190 bar (±5 bar)** and a lower limit of **150 bar (±5 bar)** [6]. Additionally, the brake system pressure accumulator pre-charge pressure is set to **90 bar (±3 bar)** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a system voltage that is unstable or an alternator failure alarm?
questions.answer: Check the alternator charging voltage on the display, which should be approximately 26-28 Volts when the engine is running [8]. Inspect both the negative and positive cables and connectors between the batteries, the Engine Management System (EMS), and the alternator for poor contact or unwanted voltage drops [9, 10]. If the cables and batteries are in good condition, the alternator may be faulty or overcharging and requires replacement [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you verify the overall integrity of the CAN bus network using resistance measurements?
questions.answer: With the power from the CAN bus turned off, use a multimeter to measure the resistance between the CAN high and CAN low wires [1]. You should get a reading of **60 Ohms** (because there are **120 Ohm** terminating resistors at each end of the bus, equating to 60 Ohms in parallel anywhere in the middle) [1]. For example, when troubleshooting a missing module, measure the resistance between pins **XM4.2** and **XM4.6** on the AMP8 connector; the acceptable range is **55 - 65 Ohms** [2]. When the power is on, the voltages in both CAN high and CAN low will constantly fluctuate according to the CAN state [1]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the machine's main ignition current does not turn on?
questions.answer: First, verify that the main switch is in the ON position [1]. Next, inspect the main circuit breakers F3035 and F3064 in the fuse box X3056 to ensure they have not tripped [1]. Finally, check the system voltage on the display; the normal operating voltage should be approximately 24-27 Volts, and if it is lower, the battery connections should be checked [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH410 Technical Manual)

questions.question: When troubleshooting the retrieval hook circuit, if residual pressure from the brake pistons fails to drain through the relay valves after cylinder pressure drops below 10 bar, which specific selector valves must be inspected and which of their ports connect directly to the brake relay A-ports?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, here is the information regarding the retrieval hook circuit's selector valves and port connections:

**Selector Valves to Inspect**
If residual pressure fails to drain from the brake pistons when the retrieval hook cylinder (A3521) pressure drops below 10 bar, you must inspect the two selector valves located inside the brake relay manifolds (*Section 13.12.1 Retrieval hook system description, Page 723-724*):
*   **Front axle selector valve (V2504)** [1]
*   **Rear axle selector valve (V3505)** [1]

**Port Connections**
On these selector valves, **port 4** is the specific port that connects directly to the brake relays' A-port (*Section 13.12.6 Selector valve, Page 727*) [2]. 

**System Operation Context**
According to *Section 13.12.6 Selector valve (Page 727)*, these valves select the correct pressure supply for the brakes:
*   When the retrieval hook is pulled and pressure rises above 10 bar, the selector valves switch positions. Port 4 is blocked, and port 2 is connected to port 3 (the axle brake pressure port), allowing oil from the hook cylinder to flow to the brake pistons to release the brakes [1, 2].
*   When the pressure from the hook cylinder decreases below 10 bar, the valves switch back to their normal position. Port 4 opens to port 3, which allows the residual pressure from the brake pistons to drain safely through the relay valves [2, 3]. 

**Retrieval Hook Function & Pressure Drop Test Procedure**
While the sources do not detail a sequence for disassembling a stuck selector valve, they provide a specific step-by-step procedure to test the retrieval hook's pressure holding and draining capabilities (*Retrieval hook visual check, Pages 221-222*):
1. Install the retrieval hook test device to the hook and secure it [4].
2. Connect a hydraulic pump (minimum capacity 400 cc) to the test device connector [4, 5].
3. Use the hydraulic pump until the hook is fully extracted (approx. 100 mm) and brakes are released [5, 6].
4. Have a second person verify from the cabin control system display that the front and rear brake circuit pressures (**MP518** and **MP519**) read **107 ± 10 bar** [6].
5. Press the brake pedal and check that the brake circuit pressures properly drop to **0 bar (+5 bar)** [6].
6. Use the hydraulic pump again until the hook is fully extracted and brakes are released [7].
7. Measure the time it takes for the pressure to drop 10 bar from the maximum. The minimum allowed time is **60 seconds**, and the maximum time should be **170 seconds** [7]. 
8. Release the pressure from the pump, ensure the hook fully retracts, and make sure the brakes successfully re-engage [7].

questions.question: A technician forces the cooler pump (P3311) to minimum displacement (100% pump control) via the Cooling System Test window with the engine under 80 °C. If the pressure at MP301 is significantly off from the target 17 ± 2 bar, which specific electric proportional valve controlling the pump displacement needs to be investigated?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Service and Repair Manual*, if the cooler pump (**P3311**) stand-by pressure is significantly off from the target **17 ± 2 bar** at measuring point **MP301**, you should investigate the **electric proportional valve V2317** [1]. This valve controls the pump's displacement based on the control current it receives [1]. You may also need to check the associated pump controller/solenoid designated as **Y3089** (also referred to as Y301 in the electrical outputs), which receives the physical control signal wiring [2, 3]. 

The specific step-by-step sequence for this diagnostic test is detailed in the **Cooler pump pressure check procedure** (*Section 8.7.2, Pages 351-353*):

1. Park the machine on a level surface, lower the bucket to the ground, ensure the boom rests on the stops, prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, and install the frame articulation locking device [4].
2. Shut down the engine and let it cool down. The engine temperature must be under **80 °C** when checking or adjusting the pump stand-by pressure [4].
3. Connect a **400 bar pressure gauge** to the cooler pump pressure measuring point **MP301** [3].
4. Turn the main switch and starter isolation switches to the "ON" position and start the engine [3].
5. Operate the engine at low idle [3].
6. Force the pump to minimum displacement by setting the pump control to **100%** in the control system's Cooling System Test window [3].
   * *Alternative method:* Disconnect the control signal wiring from the pump controller **Y3089** and use an external power source to feed **600 mA** current directly to the controller [3].
7. Check the gauge to verify if the stand-by pressure value at **MP301** falls within the required range of **17 ± 2 bar** [3, 5].

questions.question: If the steering pump (P3111) differential pressure measured between MP101 and MP102 at engine idle remains stuck at 20 bar despite turning adjustment screw (1), which specific valve inside the priority block responsible for directing the higher LS-pressure to the pump should be inspected?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material provided, if the differential pressure (dp-pressure) for the steering pump (**P3111**) cannot be adjusted to the required **30 ± 2 bar** and remains stuck, you should inspect the **LS-shuttle valve** [1, 2]. 

**Component Details and Function**
Located in the steering valve's priority block, the **LS-shuttle valve** (identified as component 8) controls the source of the load-sensing (LS) signal that dictates the steering pump's output [3, 4]. The LS-signals from both the steering valve and the boom and bucket valve are connected to this shuttle valve, which is specifically responsible for directing the higher of the two LS-pressures to the steering pump [4]. Because the dp-pressure limits how much greater the pump's pressure is compared to the LS-pressure, a malfunctioning LS-shuttle valve failing to deliver the correct LS-signal will prevent proper dp-pressure adjustments [2]. 

*(Reference: Section 11.5.1 Priority block, Pages 529-530)*

**Diagnostic Procedure Context**
The steps you took to find this fault are detailed in the **Steering pump pressure check and adjusting procedure** (*Section 11.4.1, Pages 522-523*):
1. Park the machine on a level surface, lower the bucket to the ground, ensure the boom rests on the stops, prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, and install the frame articulation locking device [5].
2. Connect **400 bar pressure gauges** to measurement points **MP101** and **MP102** (place the gauges so they can be read from the cabin) [6]. 
3. Start the engine and operate it at idle [6].
4. Check the dp-pressure, which is the calculated difference between the values at **MP101** and **MP102**. The required range is **30 ± 2 bar** [6]. 
5. If the value is outside of the required range, stop the engine, adjust the setting using **pump adjustment screw (1)**, and start the engine to repeat the check [6].

questions.question: A machine logs a P009400 (Fuel System Leak Detected - Small Leak) code due to an unexpected fuel pressure drop during engine shutdown. In addition to the high pressure system and rail pressure sensor, which specific valve requires an oscilloscope signal check and fuel return inspection?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the specific valve that requires an oscilloscope signal check and fuel return inspection when a **P009400 (Fuel System Leak Detected - Small Leak)** code is logged is the **ePRV** (electronic Pressure Relief Valve) [1]. 

According to the "Fault Codes" section in the engine electrical service manual, this fault occurs when the Engine Management System (EMS) monitors an unexpected fuel pressure drop in the rail during the engine shutdown sequence [1]. 

The step-by-step corrective action sequence for this diagnostic code is:
1. **Check the high pressure system** for leakage [1].
2. **Inspect the ePRV:** Check all wiring and the connectors between the **ePRV** and the EMS. Check the **ePRV signal using an oscilloscope**, and visually check the fuel return from the **ePRV** to ensure it is not stuck open or partially open [1].
3. **Inspect the rail pressure sensor:** Check all cables and connectors between the rail pressure sensor and the EMS. Log the rail pressure by using the Vodia diagnostic tool or by performing a voltage measurement [2].

questions.question: An operator complains that bucket movements are not being properly blocked when the boom joystick control signal exceeds 90%. Which specific valve located in the inlet block is failing to apply pressure to the bucket B1-line load hold valve to prevent this movement?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided Service and Repair Manual, the specific valve failing to block bucket movements is the **prioritization valve Y201** located in the inlet block [1]. 

**System Operation Context:**
According to the manual, the prioritization valve **Y201** uses pressure from the pressure line to prevent bucket movements when the boom is in heavy use [1]. When the boom and bucket joystick's boom control signal exceeds 90% (which is adjustable from the control system), valve **Y201** is activated [1]. 

Once activated, pressure from the pressure line goes directly to the pilot side of the **main valve bucket B1-line load hold valve** [1]. This applied pressure keeps the load hold valve closed, preventing oil flow between the bucket spool and the valve **B1-port**, thereby preventing bucket movement even if the bucket spool itself is being controlled by the operator [1]. If the boom control signal drops below 90%, valve **Y201** deactivates and the bucket is allowed to move normally [1].

*(Reference: Service and Repair Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 12.5 Boom and bucket main valve, Page 608)* [1].

questions.question: When adjusting the steering pump (P3111), what is the correct differential pressure (dp-pressure) value that must be calculated between measurement points MP101 and MP102 while the engine is running at idle?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided Service and Repair Manual, when adjusting the steering pump (**P3111**), the correct differential pressure (dp-pressure) calculated between measurement points **MP101** and **MP102** while the engine is running at idle must be **30 ± 2 bar** [1, 2].

Here is the step-by-step sequence for checking and adjusting this pressure (*Section 11.4.1 Steering pump pressure check and adjusting procedure, Pages 522-523*):

1. Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine [3].
2. Prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the bucket to the ground, and ensure the boom rests on the stops [3].
3. Connect **400 bar pressure gauges** to the measurement points **MP101** and **MP102** [3]. Place the gauges so they can be read from the operator seat in the cabin. 
4. Start the engine and operate it at idle [4].
5. Check the dp-pressure by calculating the difference between the pressure values at **MP101** and **MP102** [4]. 
6. If the value is outside the required range of **30 ± 2 bar**, stop the engine and adjust the setting using **pump adjustment screw (1)** [4]. 
7. Start the engine and repeat the check until the pressure is within the correct range [4].

questions.question: If the general pilot pressure measured at MP405 requires adjustment to reach the target 35 ± 5 bar, what is the absolute maximum pressure limit provided by the pilot pressure relief valve to protect the system?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided Service and Repair Manual, if the general pilot pressure requires adjustment, the absolute maximum pressure limit provided by the **pilot pressure relief valve** (Component 4 in the priority block) is **50 bar**. 

The function of this pilot pressure relief valve is to physically protect the system from overpressure by limiting it to 50 bar in situations where the standard reducing valve (which maintains the normal **35 ± 5 bar**) malfunctions or experiences an unexpected fault *(Section 11.5.1 Priority block, Page 529)*.

If the pilot pressure falls outside the required range and must be adjusted, the manual details the following step-by-step sequence *(Section 11.5.2 Pilot pressure block, Pilot pressure check and adjusting procedure, Pages 532-534)*:

1. Park the machine on a level surface, shut down the engine, lower the bucket to the ground, ensure the boom rests on the stops, prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, and install the frame articulation locking device [1].
2. Connect a **400 bar pressure gauge** to the pilot pressure measurement point **MP405**. Place the gauge so it can be read while sitting in the operator seat in the cabin [2].
3. Start the engine and operate it at idle [2].
4. Check the pilot pressure while the pump is at maximum pressure. To achieve this, move the bucket against the stoppers and check the pressure at the same time [2].
5. If the pressure value is outside the required **35 ± 5 bar** range, adjust the pressure using **adjustment screw (3)** [3]. 
6. **Important Safety Step:** Start the adjustment from the minimum setting and make only small adjustments at a time, checking the result with the pump at maximum pressure after each adjustment. An over-pressurized pilot circuit could cause damage to the system [3].
7. Turn off the engine and wait until the pressure in the gauge reaches **0 bar** before disconnecting [3].

questions.question: What specific parameter must be adjusted in the Parameter Management menu to achieve the correct brake pedal released pressure of 115 ± 2 bar measured at MP504 for the electronic service brake pedal valve (V3511)?
questions.answer:
The specific parameter that must be adjusted is the **"No control current"** parameter [1]. This parameter defines the service brake control current for the electronic service brake pedal valve (V3511) when the brakes are fully released [1, 2]. 

To achieve the correct released pressure of **115 ± 2 bar** measured at **MP504**, follow this step-by-step adjustment sequence [1, 3, 4]:

1. Open the brake valve current limits window by navigating to **Maintenance > Parameter Management > Brake valve > Current Limits** on the control system display [1].
2. Release the parking brake [1].
3. Adjust the **"No control current"** parameter value until the pedal pressure reaches the required target of 115 ± 2 bar [1, 3].
4. Shut down the engine [4].
5. Disconnect the 400 bar pressure gauge from measuring point **MP504** [4].

questions.question: When performing a standard valve adjustment on the Volvo engine, what are the exact required clearance dimensions in millimeters for both the intake valves and the exhaust valves?
questions.answer:
Based on the Volvo Workshop Manual (Group 21 - Engine, Valve Adjustment, Standard, page 110) [1], the exact required clearance dimensions for a standard valve mechanism adjustment are:

*   **Intake valves:** 0.2 mm [2]
*   **Exhaust valves:** 0.8 mm [3]

*(Note: If the engine is equipped with the VCB valve mechanism, the exhaust valve clearance requirement changes to 1.6 mm [4], but it remains 0.8 mm for the standard and iEGR mechanisms [3, 5]).*

**Step-by-Step Sequence for Standard Valve Adjustment:**

**Prerequisites:** The valve cover must be removed, and the specific valve mechanism must be identified [2]. 
**Required Tools:** Rotation tool (Part No. **88840317**) [2].

1. **Rotate Engine:** Crank the engine in the direction of rotation to the next camshaft marking using the rotation tool [2]. For example, if it lands on "5", this indicates the adjustment of the inlet, outlet, and injector rocker arm for cylinder 5 [2]. 
   * *Important Note:* You must ensure that the line marked on the camshaft is perfectly centered between the marks on the bearing cap when the adjustment is carried out [2].
2. **Adjust Intake:** Adjust the clearance of the intake valve to **0.2 mm** [2].
3. **Tighten Intake Locknut:** Tighten the valve adjuster screw locking nut according to the specification in Group 21 - Engine, page 11, which requires a tightening torque of **38 Nm** [2, 6].
4. **Verify Intake:** Check the valve play with a feeler gauge to ensure it is correct [2].
5. **Adjust Exhaust:** Adjust the clearance of the exhaust valve to **0.8 mm** [3].
6. **Tighten Exhaust Locknut:** Tighten the locknut to the **38 Nm** specification [3, 6].
7. **Verify Exhaust:** Check the valve play [7]. 

*(Note: After completing the intake and exhaust valves, the sequence proceeds to adjusting the injector pre-load to 240° past zero-clearance before cranking the engine to the next camshaft marking [7]).*

questions.question: During the HVAC cabin pressure sensor calibration process, what specific physical action must the technician take and how long must they wait to ensure the pressure difference reads 0 Pa before initiating the calibration?
questions.answer:
To calibrate the HVAC cabin pressure sensor, the technician must **open the cabin door fully** and **wait at least 30 seconds** to allow the inside and outside pressures to equalize until the difference reads **0 Pa** [1]. 

According to the *Service and Repair Manual LH515i - StageV (Page 253)*, this calibration is required when the HVAC system is initially installed or if the sensor modules have been replaced [1]. 

Here is the complete step-by-step sequence for the calibration procedure:
1. Navigate to the **Cabin Pressure Sensor Calibration** window on the display [1].
2. **Open the cabin door fully** [1].
3. **Wait at least 30 seconds** for the outside and inside pressure to equalize (Difference = **0 Pa**) [1].
4. Press the **Calibrate** button [1].
5. Press the **Accept Calibration** button to complete the process [1].

questions.question: What are the machine's overall dimensions, specifically the total length with a 6.3 m³ bucket at ground level, maximum width, and height?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, the overall dimensions for the Sandvik LH515i loader are as follows:

*   **Total length (bucket at ground, 6.3 m³ bucket):** 11,220 mm
*   **Maximum width:** 2,930 mm
*   **Height (bucket at ground):** 2,535 mm

*(References: Maintenance Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 6.1 Machine specification, Page 360 [1]; Operator's Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 8.1 Machine specification, Pages 275-276 [2, 3]; Service and Repair Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 17.1 Machine specification, Page 995 [4]).*

questions.question: When calculating transport measurements, what are the specific Δx, Δy, and Δz values for the machine's center of gravity relative to the center hinge?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, when calculating transport measurements, the coordinate system is located at the center hinge with the joint shaft height in the middle of the unit [1, 2]. 

The specific values for the machine's center of gravity relative to this center hinge are:
*   **Δx:** -173 mm [1, 2]
*   **Δy:** 70 mm [1, 2]
*   **Δz:** 234 mm [1, 2]

*(References: Maintenance Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 2.3.3 Center of gravity, Page 49; Operator's Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 2.3.3 Center of gravity, Pages 47-48).*

questions.question: What are the exact fluid filling capacities for the fuel tank, main hydraulic oil system, engine coolant, and AdBlue/DEF tank?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, the exact fluid filling capacities for the Sandvik LH515i loader are as follows:

*   **Fuel tank:** 572 liters [1-3]
*   **Main hydraulic oil system:** 405 liters [1]
*   **Engine coolant:** 60 liters [1-3]
*   **AdBlue/DEF tank:** 50 liters [1-3]

*(References: Maintenance Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 4.5 Filling capacities, Pages 191-192; Operator's Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 6.3/8.3 Engine, Pages 277, 361).*

questions.question: When adjusting the steering pump (P3111), what specific differential pressure (dp-pressure) must be calculated between measuring points MP101 and MP102 while the engine is running at idle?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided service and maintenance manuals, the correct differential pressure (dp-pressure) calculated between measurement points **MP101** and **MP102** while the engine is running at idle must be **30 ± 2 bar** [1, 2].

Here is the step-by-step sequence for checking and adjusting this pressure, according to the *Steering pump pressure check and adjusting procedure* (Service and Repair Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 11.4.1, Pages 522-524):

1. Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine [3]. 
2. Prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the bucket to the ground, and make sure the boom rests on the stops [3].
3. Connect **400 bar pressure gauges** to the measurement points **MP101** and **MP102** [3, 4]. Place the pressure gauges so they can be read while sitting in the operator seat in the cabin [4].
4. Start the engine and operate it at idle [4].
5. Check the dp-pressure, which is the calculated difference between the pressure values at **MP101** and **MP102** [4].
6. If the value is outside of the required **30 ± 2 bar** range, stop the engine and adjust the setting using **pump adjustment screw (1)** [4].
7. Start the engine and repeat the check until the pressure falls within the correct range [4].
8. Shut down the engine and disconnect the 400 bar pressure gauges from **MP101** and **MP102** [5].

questions.question: When checking the boom and bucket pump (P3211), what is the required maximum pressure reading at measurement point MP201 when driving the bucket up against the stoppers?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, when checking the boom and bucket pump (**P3211**), the required maximum pressure reading at measurement point **MP201** when driving the bucket up against the stoppers is **295 ± 8 bar** [1, 2].

Here is the step-by-step sequence for checking and adjusting this maximum pressure (*Service and Repair Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 12.4.1, Pages 602-603* and *Maintenance Manual LH515i - StageV, Section 5.8.9, Pages 332-333*):

1. Park the machine on a level surface, lower the bucket to the ground, ensure the boom rests on the stops, prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, and install the frame articulation locking device [3].
2. Make sure the steering pump dp-pressure is within the required range (30 ± 2 bar) [4]. 
3. Connect a **400 bar pressure gauge** to the bucket pump pressure line measuring point **MP201** [5]. Place the pressure gauge so you can read the value while sitting in the operator seat in the cabin [5].
4. Start the engine [5].
5. Move the bucket control joystick to drive the bucket up against the stoppers (roll bucket back position) and keep the joystick at the fully moved position [5, 6]. *Note: In case the engine stalls, raise the engine rpm* [5].
6. Record the gauge reading to check the boom and bucket pump maximum pressure [6]. 
7. Check that the pressure value is within the required range of **295 ± 8 bar** [1, 6].
8. If the value is outside of the required range:
   * Stop the engine [6].
   * Adjust the setting using **pump adjustment screw (2)** [6]. 
   * Start the engine and repeat the check [6].
9. Once correct, shut down the engine and disconnect the 400 bar pressure gauge from MP201 [7].

questions.question: In the load-sensing (LS) system, what specific size orifice located in the LS-line between pilot valve Y206 and the limitation manifold port X is responsible for successfully limiting the LS-pressure to 100 bar when the boom is pressed down?
questions.answer:
The specific size of the orifice responsible for successfully limiting the LS-pressure is **1.2 mm** [1]. 

When the boom is pressed down, pressure from the boom and bucket pilot valve **Y206** is directed to port **X** on the limitation manifold [1]. Once the pressure at port X reaches 5 bar, the pressure from the LS-line connects to a 100 bar pressure relief valve [1]. The flow coming from the boom and bucket valve LS-line is restricted by this **1.2 mm orifice** [1]. If this orifice is missing or too large, the pressure relief valve will not be able to successfully limit the pressure in the LS-line to 100 bar [1]. 

*(Reference: Service and Repair Manual LH515i - StageV, Page 609-610)*

questions.question: During an emergency steering test, what is the expected pressure at measurement point MP109 when the electric motor (M3020) in the hydraulic power pack (A3141) is activated, and which specific pressure relief valve limits this maximum pressure?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, during an emergency steering test, the expected pressure at measurement point **MP109** is **100 ± 5 bar** [1]. 

When the electric motor (**M3020**) in the hydraulic power pack (**A3141**) is activated, the maximum pressure is specifically limited to **100 bar** by the **pressure relief valve V3181** to prevent overloading the electric motor [2, 3]. 

The step-by-step sequence for the **Emergency steering system function (option) check** (*Section 5.1.9, Pages 203-204*) is as follows [4-6]:
1. Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine.
2. Check that the emergency stops are not activated.
3. Turn the ignition key to position 1 (power on).
4. Push the emergency steering button on the instrument panel and keep it pressed.
   * The pump should start and stay on until you release the button or the maximum time (default 10 seconds) is reached. The emergency steering symbol will appear in the main window of the VCM system display.
5. Go to the Troubleshooting menu and select Steering.
6. Check that the emergency steering button indicator and the Aux Steering Pump ON indicator activate.
7. Check that the steering pressure increases to **100 bar** (keep the button pressed when checking the pressure).

questions.question: What specific type of differential is equipped on both the front and rear Kessler D106 axles of the loader's drivetrain?
questions.answer: Based on the *Service and Repair Manual LH515i - StageV* (*Section 9.7 Axles, Page 407*), both the front and rear Kessler D106 axles (specifically model Kessler D106 PL341/528-NLB-FS) are equipped with a **limited slip differential** [1].

questions.question: What is the procedure and correct value for checking the maximum pressure of the brake charging pump (**P3513**)?
questions.answer: First, connect a **400 bar pressure gauge** to the brake valve block at measuring point **MP501** [5, 6]. Start the engine and wait for the brake system pressure accumulators to fully charge [5, 6]. The pressure gauge reading should be **170 ± 10 bar** [7, 8]. If the reading is outside this range, stop the engine, adjust the setting using the pump adjustment screw on the brake charging pump (**P3513**), and repeat the procedure [6, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the maximum and differential (dp) pressures for the steering pump (**P3111**)?
questions.answer: To check the dp-pressure, connect **400 bar pressure gauges** to the measuring points **MP101** and **MP102** [1, 2]. Start the engine and operate it at idle; the dp-pressure (the difference between MP101 and MP102) should be **30 ± 2 bar** [3, 4]. If it needs adjustment, use **pump adjustment screw (1)** [4]. To check the maximum pressure, move the bucket joystick to the roll back position and keep it there [5, 6]. The pressure reading at **MP101** should be **280 ± 8 bar** [3, 6]. If out of range, adjust using **pump adjustment screw (2)** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What conditions trigger Tire Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS) alarms, and how should they be addressed?
questions.answer: TPMS alarms are triggered by tire leaks, extreme over/under pressure, low pressure, tire overheating (temperatures over 93 °C), or a low sensor battery [11]. The operator should stop the machine, check the tire pressure, inspect the tire and valve for damage, and add air if necessary [12]. If a low battery alarm is active, the entire tire pressure sensor must be replaced, as the battery cannot be changed [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the brake charging pump (**P3513**) and brake accumulator pressures checked and adjusted?
questions.answer: Connect a **400 bar gauge** to **MP501** [12, 13]. Start the engine, let the accumulators fully charge, and verify that the brake charging pump's maximum pressure is **170 ± 10 bar** [12, 14, 15]. If it is outside this range, adjust it using the pump adjustment screw [15]. Additionally, you should check the brake accumulator pre-charge pressure at **MP521** with the engine off and the hydraulics fully de-pressurized; the correct value is **90 ± 3 bar** [16-18]. If the pre-charge pressure is too low, the accumulator must be recharged with nitrogen [18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the diagnostic procedure for an "Output short circuit to ground" alarm?
questions.answer: Check if the alarm stops by manually forcing the output ON using the **I/O Forcing window** in the troubleshooting menu [7, 8]. If the alarm stops, the fault is in the wire harness and it needs to be repaired [8]. If the issue is not in the harness, the controller is broken and must be changed [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the control system visually indicate warnings versus alarms, and what is the required operator response for each?
questions.answer: Warnings (notices) are indicated by a yellow bell symbol on the display and a yellow indicator light; they may not require immediate action, but the operator should investigate the reason, especially for repeated notices [1-3]. Alarms are indicated by a red bell symbol and a red indicator light; they require immediate attention, and the operator must stop working immediately and correct the error situation [1, 2, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you locate a faulty component if the overall hydraulic system is sluggish or losing pressure?
questions.answer: If the system slows down, becomes sluggish, or loses pressure, you can begin locating the faulty component by checking the time it takes for the hydraulic system to complete a cycle and verifying if the pressure output is normal [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined flow rates, displacements, and maximum pressures for the main hydraulic pumps?
questions.answer: The **steering pump (P3111)** has a displacement of 75 cm³/rev, generating a max flow of **162 L/min at 2325 rpm** with a maximum system pressure of **280 bar** [1]. The **boom and bucket pump (P3211)** also has a 75 cm³/rev displacement, providing **162 L/min at 2325 rpm** with a maximum system pressure of **300 bar** [1]. The electronically controlled **cooler pump (P3311)** has a 60 cm³/rev displacement, producing **130 L/min at 2325 rpm** with a maximum pressure of **250 bar** [2]. The **brake charging pump (P3513)** has an 18 cm³/rev displacement, providing **39 L/min at 2325 rpm** with a maximum pressure of **170 bar** [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a short circuit to supply alarm on an analog input, such as the steering valve supply pressure sensor (**B101**), troubleshot?
questions.answer: An analog input short circuit to supply alarm indicates that the input current is too high, often caused by a short circuit to the voltage supply or a sensor failure [4]. First, check the signal status from the diagnostics window and inspect the wire harness between the module (e.g., Tank Controller 2, pin **TC2 X1:6**) and the sensor (**B101**) [4, 5]. If the wiring is intact, check the sensor's functionality and replace it if faulty [5]. If the issue persists after these steps, the controller itself is likely broken and must be replaced [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if the main current of the machine does not turn on?
questions.answer: First, verify that the battery main switch is in the ON position [1]. Next, check that the main circuit breakers **F001** and **F003**, located in the rear frame fuse box **+U2**, have not tripped [1]. Finally, check the battery voltage on the control system display (it should be **26-28 V**); if the voltage is below normal, inspect the battery connections [1], [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used as an emergency backup to release the brakes if the engine or main brake pump fails?
questions.answer: The **electronic brake release pump (A3542)**, which is driven by electric motor **M501**, serves as an alternative oil supply [4, 22, 23]. It temporarily charges the brake system pressure accumulators to allow the operator to release the parking/emergency brakes [23]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct voltage values and procedures when troubleshooting the battery charging system?
questions.answer: With the engine off, use the **88890074 Multimeter** to measure the voltage across the battery; a fully loaded battery should have a nominal voltage of approximately **25.4 V** [2]. Next, start the engine and run it at **1500 rpm** [3]. Measure the voltage over the battery and the alternator again; the nominal charging voltage should be approximately **27.8-28.6 V** [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the main hydraulic pumps on the machine and what are their functions?
questions.answer:
The machine features four main hydraulic pumps connected to the upbox [1, 2]:
*   **Steering pump (P3111):** Provides the necessary oil flow and pressure for the machine's steering hydraulics [2].
*   **Boom and bucket pump (P3211):** A variable displacement pump that provides oil flow and pressure to operate the boom and bucket hydraulics [2, 3].
*   **Brake charging pump (P3513):** A constant pressure axial piston variable pump that supplies oil flow and pressure for the brake hydraulics [2, 4, 5].
*   **Cooler pump (P3311):** An electronically controlled variable displacement axial piston pump that provides hydraulic flow and pressure to rotate the cooler fan motors [2, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes a Vehicle Communication Engine Subnet Bus Off fault (DTC U008088) and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: This fault causes an engine derate and prevents urea injection due to missing CAN communication on the engine subnet [5, 8]. It is diagnosed by checking the engine subnet wiring and connectors (specifically B:5 and B:1) for open or short circuits, and by inspecting the ACM CAN sensor power supply wiring [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the correct procedure and associated electrical pin for testing the fire suppression system without causing an unwanted discharge?
questions.answer: Before starting the test, you must **detach the system cable going to the fire suppression cartridges** to prevent an unwanted actuation [8]. Once disconnected, navigate to the Troubleshooting menu and select **Fire Suppression Test** [8]. The system utilizes Cabin controller 2, connector **X2.5**, to send a **24 V / 0 V** signal to activate the fire suppression system during the test [9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are utilized to operate the optional ride control and boom float systems?
questions.answer: These systems utilize the **ride control block (V2214)**, which is located in the front frame next to the boom and bucket main valve (**V2201**) [20]. The system operates in conjunction with two 6.0-liter piston-type pressure accumulators to suspend the boom during driving: the right accumulator (**Z2231**) is pre-charged to 20 bar, and the left accumulator (**Z2232**) is pre-charged to 50 bar [20, 21]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes a **U300001** (Control Module General Electrical Failure) fault, and how is it resolved?
questions.answer: This fault indicates that the internal voltage supply in the Engine Management System (EMS) has failed, which will prevent the engine from starting [10]. The corrective action is to replace the EMS, after which a service regeneration will be necessary to reset the soot load in the new EMS [10], [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the machine's main current does not go on?
questions.answer: First, ensure the battery main switch is in the ON position [1]. Next, verify that the main circuit breakers **F001** and **F003**, located in the rear frame fuse box **+U2**, are not tripped [1]. Finally, check the battery voltage on the control system display by tapping the plus sign on the main screen; the expected voltage is **26-28 V** [1]. If the operating voltage is below this normal range, inspect the battery connections [1]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the designated circuit pressure setpoints for the steering and boom/bucket hydraulics?
questions.answer: For the steering circuit, the maximum pressure measured at MP101 is **280 ± 8 bar**, while the dp-pressure (differential between MP101 and MP102) is **30 ± 2 bar** [4]. The left and right steering pressures (MP103 and MP104) are both set at **210 ± 8 bar** [5]. For the boom and bucket circuit, the maximum pump pressure (MP201) is **295 ± 8 bar** with a stand-by pressure of **35 ± 2 bar** [5, 6]. The system's general pilot pressure must be maintained at **35 ± 5 bar** [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes an air quality system alarm, and what is the required corrective action?
questions.answer: An air quality system alarm is triggered if the CO2 level inside the cabin exceeds 2,500 ppm [5, 6]. The operator should increase the cabin airflow or drive the machine to an area with better air quality. If the CO2 level does not decrease, the air filters and pressurizer fan must be checked [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Generate troubleshooting Q&A pairs about the feed system, rotation system, and percussion system on the Sandvik LH515i - Loaders. Include symptom, cause, and corrective action.
questions.answer:
Based on the provided sources, the Sandvik LH515i is an underground loader designed exclusively to load, haul, and dump rock material [1]. Because it is a loader and not a drill rig, it does not feature a feed system, rotation system, or percussion system. 

Therefore, the sources do not contain any troubleshooting information for these systems.

I would be happy to generate troubleshooting Q&A pairs for the systems that *are* equipped on the LH515i and covered in the sources. Some of the main systems include:
*   **Boom and bucket hydraulics** (e.g., joystick control failures, bucket positioning errors)
*   **Steering system** (e.g., steering valve faults, center articulation issues)
*   **Powertrain and transmission** (e.g., gear selection failures, oil temperature warnings)
*   **Braking system** (e.g., brakes failing to release, low accumulator pressure)
*   **Integrated Weighing System (IWS)** (e.g., low accuracy warnings, failed weighing lifts)

Please let me know if you would like troubleshooting guides for any of these loader-specific systems!. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you calibrate the electronic service brake pedal valve and set its released pressure?
questions.answer: The service brake valve calibration is initiated via the **Calibration window** on the control system display while the engine is running and the parking brake is released [24]. The automatic calibration process identifies the proportional valve control current for the brake piston contact pressure/activation threshold (default **85...87 bar**) and maximum braking (**5 bar**) [25]. To set the correct released pressure, check **MP504** with the brake pedal fully released; it should read **115 ± 2 bar** [14, 26]. If adjustment is needed, alter the **"No control current" parameter** in the Parameter Management menu until the pedal pressure falls within this required range [26]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical and system checks should be made if the engine does not start?
questions.answer: You should verify that all emergency stop buttons are pulled up (deactivated), confirm there are no active alarms displayed on the control system, and check the fuel level [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should you investigate if the hydraulic system has no pressure?
questions.answer: If the system has no pressure, you should check the intake line from the reservoir to the pump to ensure filters and strainers are not clogged, verify the oil level is not too low, inspect for air leaks on the intake side, and determine if the oil viscosity is too high or if the pump is faulty [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specifications and by-pass limits for the main and brake hydraulic return filters?
questions.answer: The main return filter (**Z3421**) and the brake return filter (**Z3521**) both feature an integrated magnet pack to collect metal particles before the oil passes through the replaceable filter element [9]. The main hydraulic filter's clogging indicator activates at a pressure difference of **1.2 bar**, and its internal by-pass valve opens to allow oil through if the pressure difference reaches **1.7 bar** [9, 10]. The brake return filter's clogging indicator activates at **0.3 bar**, with its by-pass valve opening at **0.4 bar** [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What electrical system conditions and interlocks should be checked if a gear cannot be selected?
questions.answer: If a gear cannot be selected, verify that no emergency stop buttons are activated (pull them up if they are pushed down), ensure the engine is running, confirm the cabin door is fully closed, and verify the parking brake is not engaged [3]. Additionally, check the circuit breakers in fuse box **+U2** to ensure none are tripped [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific hydraulic system conditions will prevent the machine brakes from releasing?
questions.answer: The machine brakes may fail to release due to several hydraulic conditions and system interlocks, specifically: **low hydraulic oil level**, **low brake oil level**, **low transmission oil pressure**, **low brake pressure accumulator pressure**, or a **brake valve malfunction** [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptoms and diagnostic steps for a **U001088** (CAN Communication Backbone 1 Net Bus Off) fault?
questions.answer: A **U001088** fault prevents the engine from starting, or if the engine is already running, it can only be stopped by pushing the aux-stop button [7], [8]. It is caused by missing communication on CAN backbone 1 [8]. Diagnostics involve checking all wiring and connectors (specifically pins **B51** and **B55**) connected to CAN backbone 1 for open or short circuits [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a fault where a gear cannot be selected?
questions.answer: Ensure that no emergency stop buttons are activated, verify the cabin door is fully closed, confirm the parking brake is not engaged, and inspect the circuit breakers in fuse box **+U2** to ensure none are tripped [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a bus communication failure alarm, such as a "FrontBus bus communication failure" from the Master Control Unit (MCU)?
questions.answer: This alarm indicates the **MCU** is failing to communicate or detecting errors on the specific bus [1, 2]. To troubleshoot, check the cabling and bus connectors, and **measure the bus resistance and voltage levels** [2]. If the resistance or voltage levels differ from normal, repair the wire harness [2]. Additionally, you can monitor the **CAN Bus Status** window in the Troubleshooting menu to view the live bus load, RX/TX errors, and the status of I/O modules [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the cooler pump (**P3311**) stand-by and maximum pressures?
questions.answer: With the engine temperature under 80 °C, connect a **400 bar gauge** to **MP301** [27, 28]. In the control system's Cooling System Test window, force the pump to minimum displacement (100% pump control) to check the stand-by pressure, which should be **17 ± 2 bar** [9, 28]. To check the maximum pressure, force the pump to maximum displacement (0% pump control) and run the engine at full rpm [29]. The maximum pressure should be **250 ± 10 bar**, and the cooler fan should rotate at **2100 ± 100 rpm** [9, 14, 29]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the component designations for the physical diagnostic connection ports used to monitor the separate CAN bus subnets?
questions.answer: The machine features several dedicated connectors for diagnosing specific CAN bus networks. These include **XU123** for the FrontBus [13], **XU124** for the CabinBus [14], **XU125** for the RearBus [15], and **XU126** / **XU127** for the J1939 Engine bus (Volvo Vodia diagnostic connection) [16]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary main circuit breakers and their capacities, and how are they released in an emergency?
questions.answer: The primary main fuses are located in switchgear cabinet **+U2** and include **F001** (400 A) and **F003** (200 A) [4]. In case of an emergency, pressing the main circuit breaker release button (**S064**) connects the coil of **F001** to ground, which opens the primary contacts and cuts the power supply to the starter (**M4006**) and circuit breaker **F003** [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct pressure settings for the brake and cooling circuits?
questions.answer: The brake charging pump pressure (MP501) must be set to **170 ± 10 bar** [7]. The front and rear brake pressures (MP518 and MP519) should read **107 -0/+10 bar** when the brakes are fully released [8]. The service brake valve pressure (MP504) should be **115 ± 2 bar**, and the brake flushing pressure (MP507) should measure between **1.0 - 2.5 bar** [7]. The cooling circuit operates with a stand-by pressure of **17 ± 2 bar** and a maximum pressure of **250 ± 10 bar** measured at MP301 [6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which component collects data from the CAN bus system to transmit telemetry to external servers?
questions.answer: The Data collection unit (**DCU**), also known as the Knowledge box, is connected to the CAN networks (such as CAN 1) to collect process data, active alarms, and usage counters from the machine. It then transmits this information to a local OptiMine server or the My Sandvik IOT cloud [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the setpoints for the steering line pressures and how are they adjusted?
questions.answer: Connect **400 bar gauges** to **MP103** (steering right) and **MP104** (steering left) [30]. Start the engine and steer the machine against the frame articulation locking device [30]. The pressure for both right and left steering should be **210 ± 8 bar** [11, 30]. If the values are out of range, adjust them using the designated adjustment screws (**1** and **2**) on the steering valve block [31]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What specific fluid levels and system pressures will trigger a critical alarm resulting in an automatic engine shutdown or emergency brake application?
questions.answer: The control system will trigger an emergency brake application and automatically shut down the engine if it detects a low hydraulic oil level, low brake oil level, low transmission oil pressure, low brake accumulator pressure, or low engine oil pressure [7-9]. The operator will see a pop-up warning with a countdown timer before the engine stops [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the CAN bus fault code **U000188** (CAN Communication Backbone 2 Net Bus Off) diagnosed?
questions.answer: This fault code indicates missing CAN communication on Backbone 2 (BB2), which prevents the AM-Tool from reading fault codes [7]. To troubleshoot this, check the wiring harness and connectors (specifically pins **B22** and **B21**) for open or short circuits, and verify that the bus has the correct termination resistance [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a **U008088** (Vehicle communication engine subnet Bus Off) fault that results in engine derate or no urea injection?
questions.answer: This fault is caused by missing CAN communication on the engine subnet, typically due to an open or shorted high/low circuit in the engine subnet wiring [7, 8]. You should check the harness and connectors, specifically inspecting connectors **B:5 and B:1** [8]. Furthermore, check all wiring connected to the Engine subnet and inspect the Aftertreatment Control Module (ACM) CAN sensor power supply wiring [7, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary electronic control modules that communicate over the CAN bus, and what are their specific hardware types and designations?
questions.answer: The machine's control system relies on modules communicating via CANopen and SAE J1939 protocols [1, 2]. These include the Display Control Unit (**DCU**, an EPEC 6112 display), Master Control Unit (**MCU**, an XS6C module), two Safety Controllers (**SC1**, **SC2**, SC52 modules), and eight GL84 slave I/O modules operating as two Cabin Controllers (**CC1**, **CC2**), two Front Controllers (**FC1**, **FC2**), two Tank Controllers (**TC1**, **TC2**), and two Rear Controllers (**RC1**, **RC2**) [2-4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is returning hydraulic oil filtered, and what are the specific filter part numbers?
questions.answer:
Returning hydraulic oil is filtered by two separate return filters located in the hydraulic tank, which both feature an integrated magnet pack, a clogging indicator, and a by-pass valve [13-15]:
*   **Z3421:** The return filter for the main steering and boom/bucket hydraulics [13, 14].
*   **Z3521:** The return filter for the brake hydraulics [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps should be taken if the AM-Tool cannot read fault codes and DTC **U000188** (CAN Communication Backbone 2 Net Bus Off) is active?
questions.answer: This fault indicates missing CAN communication on Backbone 2 (BB2) [4]. The possible root causes are an open circuit (OC) or short circuit (SC) on pins **B22 or B21** [4]. To correct this, check the wiring harness and connectors, and specifically **verify the correct termination resistance** on the bus [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a situation where the machine's main current does not go on?
questions.answer: First, check that the battery main switch is in the ON position [1]. Next, verify that the main circuit breakers **F001** and **F003** in the rear frame fuse box **+U2** are not tripped [1]. Finally, check the battery voltage on the control system display to ensure it is within the normal operating range of **26-28 V** [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the main power distribution boxes in the electrical system and what are their component designations?
questions.answer: The main power distribution boxes are the Instrument panel (**+U1**), the Fuse box or Switchgear cabinet (**+U2**), and the Transmission controller box (**+U3**) [1]. Additionally, machines equipped with the optional Arctic package utilize a separate electric box (**+U7**) to house electrical components like fuses for the heating system [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific electrical solenoid valves are responsible for controlling the automatic central lubrication system and the service brakes?
questions.answer: The automatic central lubrication system is controlled by solenoid valve **Y402**, which dictates the servo oil flow to the double-acting grease pump [12, 13]. The service brakes are controlled by the electronically controlled proportional valve **Y508** (the electric service brake pedal valve), which regulates brake relay pilot pressure based on the operator's pedal input [14, 15]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the operator input switch commands (like lights, wipers, and ride control) into the CAN bus system?
questions.answer: Operator inputs are handled by two dedicated CAN keypads located in the cabin, designated as Cabin panel 1 (**CP1**) and Cabin panel 2 (**CP2**) [10, 11]. These CAN-connected panels read button presses for functions like driving lights, wipers, bucket floating, and gear selection, and transmit them over the CabinBus [10, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for diagnosing an "Output short circuit to ground" control system alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm is triggered when a control system module's output electric current is too high [5]. To diagnose it, manually force the specific output ON using the I/O Forcing window in the troubleshooting menu [5], [6]. If the alarm stops, the fault is a short circuit to the voltage supply within the wire harness, which must be repaired [6]. If the alarm persists, the controller is broken and must be replaced [6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the procedures and setpoints for the boom and bucket pump (**P3211**) pressures?
questions.answer: Connect **400 bar gauges** to **MP201** and **MP202** [7, 8]. At idle, the stand-by pressure (the difference between MP201 and MP202) should be **35 ± 2 bar** [8, 9]. Adjust this setting using **pump adjustment screw (1)** [10]. To check the maximum pressure, drive the bucket up against the stoppers; the pressure at **MP201** should be **295 ± 8 bar** [10, 11]. Adjust this maximum pressure using **pump adjustment screw (2)** [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you perform a pilot pressure check, and what is the expected pressure value?
questions.answer: Connect a **400 bar pressure gauge** to the pilot pressure measurement point **MP405** [11]. Start the engine and operate it at idle [11]. Check the pilot pressure while moving the bucket against the stoppers to place the pump at maximum pressure [11]. The expected pilot pressure is **35 ± 5 bar** [7, 8]. If adjustments are necessary, use the adjustment screw starting from the minimum setting and make small adjustments at a time, as an over-pressurized pilot circuit can cause damage to the system [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Where can you connect diagnostic tools to test specific CAN buses like the CabinBus, RearBus, and J1939 Engine bus?
questions.answer: The machine is equipped with dedicated diagnostic connectors for troubleshooting specific CAN buses. For example, the CabinBus diagnostic connector is **XU124** [10], the RearBus diagnostic connector is **XU125** [11], and the J1939 Volvo Vodia diagnostic connection is **XU127** [12], which is physically located near the Ethernet and USB ports [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can you tell if there is excessive air in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: Excessive air in the system can usually be recognized by the erratic and uneven operation of the hydraulic system, and it is also a leading cause of oil cavitation [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a **U008088** (Vehicle communication engine subnet Bus Off) fault code?
questions.answer: This fault causes an engine derate and prevents urea injection due to missing CAN communication on the engine subnet [8]. To diagnose it, check the engine subnet wiring and connectors (specifically **B:5** and **B:1**) for open or short circuits [8], [9]. You should also check the ACM CAN sensor power supply wiring [9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What can happen if a new CAN bus component is connected to the system without being initialized first, and what is the proper installation procedure?
questions.answer: Uninitialized components can cause faults in the bus operation or make the bus completely inoperative [5, 6]. While modules like the **GL84 slave I/O module** and **XS6C Main Controller Unit** configure automatically, other spare parts must be initialized [5, 6]. To do this, go to the Maintenance menu, select **Install Spare Part**, restart the display into the installation view, and connect the component to the spare part programming socket [6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a "High brake pressure difference" alarm indicate and what action must be taken?
questions.answer: This alarm indicates a pressure difference between the service brake valve and the front circuit, which creates a significant risk that the brakes may drag and overheat [16]. The operator or service personnel must stop the machine and check the actual pressures at the designated measurement points using the diagnostic window [16]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a CAN Communication Backbone 2 Net Bus Off fault (DTC U000188)?
questions.answer: This fault is characterized by the AM-Tool or Vodia being unable to communicate or read fault codes [4, 6]. To diagnose and correct this issue, check the wiring harness and connectors (such as pins B22 and B21) for open or short circuits, and verify that the bus has the correct termination resistance [4, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which sensors monitor the physical positioning of the boom and bucket, and where are they located?
questions.answer: The boom position is monitored by the Boom position sensor (**B282**), which is a CAN sensor located on the right-side upper lift arm pin [7]. The bucket position is monitored by a linear sensor, the Bucket position sensor (**B281**), which is mounted at the bottom of the bucket cylinder tube [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose internal and external hydraulic leaks?
questions.answer: External leaks on the pressure side are easy to locate by visually checking for the presence of hydraulic fluid, while intake side leaks are much harder to detect [4]. Internal leaks within components often cause overheating and can usually be diagnosed by performing either by-pass or draw tests [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration requirements for the high-pressure brake circuit and pilot pressure lines?
questions.answer: The high-pressure brake filter (**Z3511**) provides **10 µm** filtration for the brake circuit to ensure particles are separated from the hydraulic oil [11]. The pilot pressure filter also provides **10 µm** filtration to guarantee clean oil for the steering, boom, and bucket pilot controls [12]. To protect the system from losing pilot control if the filter clogs, the pilot filter features a blockage sensor that triggers an alarm at **3.5 bar**, and a by-pass valve that opens at **5 bar** [12]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the component IDs and functions for the electrical motors driving the brake release, hydraulic filling, and auxiliary steering pumps?
questions.answer: Electric motor **M501** drives the emergency brake release pump (**A3542**) to temporarily charge the brake accumulators if the main pump fails [8]. Electric motor **M002** operates the hydraulic oil filling pump [9]. Electric motor **M101** drives the auxiliary steering pump to provide hydraulic flow for emergency steering [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose and repair a noisy hydraulic pump?
questions.answer: A noisy pump is typically caused by air in the system, cavitation, or a worn pump [2]. To diagnose and correct it, you should check the complete system for air leaks, look for restrictions on the intake side, inspect for a clogged pump or plugged air vent in the reservoir, ensure the oil viscosity is not too high, and repair or replace the pump if worn [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific control modules make up the machine's control system architecture?
questions.answer: The control system includes the Display Control Unit (**DCU**), Master Control Unit (**MCU**), two Safety Controllers (**SC1**, **SC2**), two Cabin Controllers (**CC1**, **CC2**), two Front Controllers (**FC1**, **FC2**), two Tank Controllers (**TC1**, **TC2**), and two Rear Controllers (**RC1**, **RC2**) [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the correct setpoint for the pilot pressure, and how is it adjusted?
questions.answer: The pilot pressure should be **35 ± 5 bar**, measured at **MP405** while the engine is at idle and the pump is at maximum pressure (achieved by moving the bucket against the stoppers) [11, 20, 21]. To adjust, use the adjustment screw starting from the minimum setting and make small adjustments at a time, as an over-pressurized pilot circuit can cause damage [20, 22]. Note that the pilot pressure relief valve limits the absolute maximum pressure to **50 bar** to protect the system [23]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the symptoms and diagnostic steps for a CAN Communication Backbone 1 Net Bus Off fault (DTC U001088)?
questions.answer: This fault prevents the engine from starting, or if the engine is already running, it can only be stopped by pushing the aux-stop [4]. It is caused by missing CAN communication on Backbone 1 [5]. To diagnose it, check all wiring and connectors (specifically pins B51 and B55) connected to CAN backbone 1 for open or short circuits [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a general bus communication failure alarm (e.g., "FrontBus bus communication failure")?
questions.answer: This alarm indicates the Master Control Unit (MCU) is failing to communicate or detecting errors on a specific bus [1]. To diagnose, check the CAN Bus Status window in the troubleshooting menu to monitor the bus load and any RX/TX errors, visually inspect the cabling and bus connectors, and measure the bus resistance and voltage levels [1-3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be investigated if a hydraulic pump is excessively noisy or experiencing cavitation?
