questions.answer: A noisy pump is typically caused by air in the system or a worn pump [1]. To troubleshoot cavitation (a vacuum on the intake due to insufficient oil), you should **check for restrictions on the intake side**, inspect for a **clogged pump**, ensure the **air vent in the reservoir is not plugged**, and verify that the **oil viscosity is not too high** [1]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you check and adjust the differential pressure (dp-pressure) for the steering pump (**P3111**)?
questions.answer: To check the dp-pressure, carefully connect **400 bar pressure gauges** to the measuring points **MP101** and **MP102** [2, 3]. Start the engine and operate it at idle [3]. The dp-pressure is the calculated difference between the readings at MP101 and MP102 [3]. If the value is out of the required range, stop the engine, adjust the setting using the **pump adjustment screw (1)** on the steering pump (**P3111**), and restart the engine to re-check [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is an "Analog input has no current" alarm (e.g., parking valve supply pressure electrical failure) diagnosed?
questions.answer: This alarm is typically caused by a broken wire or sensor failure [5]. Diagnose it by checking the sensor status in the diagnostics window and inspecting the wire harness between the module and the actuator [6]. If the harness is intact, the sensor may have failed and should be replaced; if the problem persists, the controller must be replaced [6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What CAN bus faults occur when a new component is connected without initialization, and how is it fixed?
questions.answer: Connecting uninitialized components can cause bus operation faults or make the CAN bus completely inoperative [11]. To fix this, connect the component to the dedicated spare part programming socket and use the "Install Spare Part" function in the Maintenance menu to properly configure it before use [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the steering valve block (**V3102**) and what are its main sections?
questions.answer:
The steering valve block (**V3102**) provides hydraulic flow and pressure for the machine's steering system and consists of three main sections [7, 8]: 
1.  **Pilot block:** Provides pilot pressure for the steering valve, boom and bucket valve, and optional hydraulics [9].
2.  **Priority block:** Directs the steering pump output either to the steering valve or to the boom and bucket valve (prioritizing steering when in use) and provides the load-sensing (LS) signal to the steering pump [10, 11].
3.  **Steering valve:** Controls the directional movement of the machine by directing oil flow to the steering cylinders [12]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific CAN sensors are used to monitor the machine's articulation and boom movements?
questions.answer: Machine steering is measured by the Steering angle sensor (**B181**), which is a CAN encoder located on the upper middle hinge joint [4-6]. Boom positioning is monitored by the Boom position sensor (**B282**), which is a CAN encoder communicating on the Boom Bus [4, 7]. Additionally, the system utilizes CAN-based Boom pressure sensors (**B202** and **B203**) and an Inclinometer (**B481**) [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you safely test the electrical output to the central lubrication valve (**Y402**) using the control system?
questions.answer: Navigate to the Troubleshooting menu, select Modules, and then **Tank controller 1** [6, 7]. Locate pin **X1.41**, which provides the **24 V / 0 V** signal to the automatic central lubrication valve (**Y402**) [6]. You can use the **Force Value** button in the test window to manually set the output voltage of the valve ON or OFF to confirm the electrical circuit is functioning [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which machine filters trigger system alarms when they require maintenance?
questions.answer: The control system monitors filter health and will display a warning or alarm pop-up if a blockage is detected in the main hydraulic return filter, brake return/flushing filter, brake pressure filter, engine air filter, or pilot oil pressure filter [15]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which alarm conditions force the machine into "Power unit de-rate mode" to limit engine torque?
questions.answer: The machine will limit engine torque (de-rating in 20% steps) to protect the power unit if it detects a high hydraulic oil temperature alarm, a high brake hydraulic oil temperature alarm, or a Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) alarm [13, 14]. The operator is informed via a pop-up display and the torque is limited until the cause of the alarm is resolved [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components make up the primary pressure control and storage for the brake circuit?
questions.answer: The brake charging pump delivers oil through the **brake pressure filter (Z3511)**, which removes particles using a 10 µm element [16, 17]. The filtered oil enters the **parking brake block (V3515)** and charges the **brake accumulator (Z3531)**, which stores hydraulic oil to act as an alternative supply if the main pump cannot be used or if demand exceeds pump capacity [4, 16]. Pilot pressure for the brake relays is controlled by the **electronic service brake pedal valve (V3511)** [4, 18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik LH515i Technical Manual)

questions.question: If the stand-by pressure for the boom and bucket pump (P3211) measured at MP201 is reading below the specified 35 ± 2 bar at engine idle, which specific adjustment screw must be turned to restore the correct system pressure?
questions.answer:
To restore the correct stand-by pressure for the boom and bucket pump (P3211), you must turn **pump adjustment screw (2)** [1]. 

According to the *Service and Repair Manual* (Chapter 12: Boom and Bucket Hydraulics, Section 12.4.1 "Boom and bucket pump pressure check and adjusting procedure", pages 730–732), the step-by-step sequence to safely check and adjust this pressure is as follows:

1. **Prepare the machine:** Park the machine on a level surface, shut down the engine, prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the bucket to the ground, and make sure the boom rests on the stops [2].
2. **Connect the gauge:** Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the measurement point **MP201** [2]. Place the gauge so it can be read from the operator seat [3].
3. **Verify steering pressure:** Make sure the steering pump differential pressure is at least 25 bar [3].
4. **Test the pressure:** Start the engine and operate it at idle [3]. Check the stand-by pressure from the gauge to see if it meets the required **35 ± 2 bar** [3, 4].
5. **Adjust the pressure:** Because the reading is below the target value, you must:
   * Shut down the engine [1].
   * Adjust the setting using **pump adjustment screw (2)** [1].
   * Start the engine and repeat the check to verify the new pressure [1].
6. **Complete the procedure:** Once the correct pressure is achieved, shut down the engine and disconnect the 400-bar pressure gauge from **MP201** [5].

questions.question: When diagnosing a Volvo engine derate triggered by DTC P009B73 (Fuel Pressure Relief Control Actuator Stuck Closed), which specific EMS electrical connector pins must be checked with an oscilloscope to verify the ePRV signal?
questions.answer:
To verify the ePRV (Electronic Pressure Relief Valve) signal when diagnosing DTC P009B73, you must check EMS connector pins **A28** and **A62** using an oscilloscope [1, 2]. 

According to the fault tracing procedures for DTC P009B73 (which triggers an engine derate because no rail pressure drop is detected during ePRV activation), the diagnostic sequence is as follows:
1. Check all wiring and the connectors between the ePRV and the EMS [2].
2. Check the ePRV signal using an oscilloscope across the specific pins [2].

The EMS connector pins dedicated to the ePRV signal, as detailed in the Measurements table and related ePRV fault codes (such as P009B11 and P009B13), are:
*   **Pin A28:** PWM output (Low side switch) [1, 3].
*   **Pin A62:** PWM output (High side switch) [1, 3].

**Safety Warning:** Because this fault indicates the ePRV actuator is stuck closed, there is a risk of high fuel pressure remaining in the fuel rail after engine shutdown. You must refer to workshop manual Group 21–26 for related safety and pressure procedures [4].

questions.question: If the Volvo engine logs DTC P023A07 (Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump “A” Control - Mechanical Failures) resulting in excessively high intake manifold temperatures, what specific VODIA test routine must be executed to observe temperature changes while varying the pump speeds?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, to diagnose DTC P023A07 (Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump “A” Control - Mechanical Failures), you must execute the VODIA test routine named the **"Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump Test"** [1]. 

This fault code indicates that the pump motor is overloaded—likely due to a blocked charge air cooling circuit or a stuck pump rotor—which results in no cooling of the charge air, excessively high air inlet manifold temperatures, and a possible engine derate [1, 2].

According to the corrective action guidelines, the step-by-step diagnostic sequence is as follows:
1. Run the VODIA routine **"Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump Test"** [1].
2. While varying the pump speeds during the test, observe the system to check if there are any air inlet manifold temperature changes [1].
3. If no temperature changes are observed, inspect the charge air cooling circuit for blocked pipes or hoses [1].
4. If clearing the circuit does not resolve the issue, replace the charge air cooler coolant pump [1].

questions.question: To verify the pilot pressure accumulator (Z3131) pre-charge is within the 12 ± 2 bar specification, which specific measuring point must you connect your 400-bar gauge to while ensuring the pilot system is fully depressurized at MP405?
questions.answer:
To verify the pilot pressure accumulator (Z3131) pre-charge, you must connect the 400-bar pressure gauge to the pre-charge pressure measurement point **MP425** [1, 2]. 

According to the "Pilot pressure check and adjusting procedure" found in the *Service and Repair Manual* (pages 638–640) and *Maintenance Manual* (pages 321–322), the step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. **Prepare the machine**: Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine. Prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the boom to rest on the bottom limits, and turn the bucket lip to rest on the ground [3, 4].
2. **Depressurize the pilot system**: Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to pilot pressure measurement point **MP405** to make sure that the system is fully de-pressurized [1, 2]. 
3. **Measure the pre-charge pressure**: Connect a second 400-bar pressure gauge to the pre-charge measurement point **MP425** of the pressure accumulator [1, 2].
4. **Verify the pressure value**: Check that the pressure value is within the required range, which is specified as **12 ± 2 bar** (with the engine not running and hydraulics non-pressurized from MP405) [5].
5. **Adjust if necessary**: If the measured value is not within the required range, you must increase or decrease the pre-charge pressure of the pressure accumulator from measuring point **MP425** using an accumulator precharge filling device [1, 2, 6].
6. **Complete the check**: Disconnect the pressure gauge from **MP425** [6, 7]. *(Note: If you need to proceed to check the operating pilot pressure, you would leave the gauge connected to MP405 and start the engine)* [6, 7].

questions.question: When investigating a "Clutch pressure switch error" (Middle 65) that prevents gear engagement, which specific Middle module connector pin must you check for operating voltage while a gear is engaged and the engine is running?
questions.answer:
When investigating a "Clutch pressure switch error" (Middle 65), you must check Middle module connector pin **XM2.20** for operating voltage while a gear is engaged and the engine is running [1]. 

According to the VCM system troubleshooting guide (Service and Repair Manual, page 847), the specific diagnostic sequence is as follows:
1. **Pressure switch:** Check the clutch pressure switch functionality and replace the pressure switch if it is broken [1].
2. **Wiring harness:** Check the wiring harness to ensure there is voltage present at pin **XM2.20** when the engine is running and a gear is engaged [1]. 

Additionally, the system component specifications note that the 24 V operating voltage supply for the clutch pressure switch is output from Middle module connector pin **XM2.1** [2].

questions.question: When adjusting the steering pump (P3111) differential pressure, what pressure difference should be measured between MP101 and MP102 at engine idle, and which adjustment screw must be turned if the reading is out of the 25 ± 2 bar specification?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, when adjusting the steering pump (**P3111**) differential (dp) pressure, the pressure difference measured between measuring points **MP101** and **MP102** at engine idle should be **25 ± 2 bar** [1, 2]. 

If the reading is out of this specification, you must turn **pump adjustment screw (2)** [2].

According to the *Service and Repair Manual* (Section 11.4.1 "Steering pump pressure check and adjusting procedure", pages 630–632), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [2-4]:

1. **Prepare the machine:** Park the machine on a level surface, shut down the engine, prevent movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, and lower the bucket to the ground so the boom rests on the stops.
2. **Connect gauges:** Connect 400-bar pressure gauges to measurement points **MP101** and **MP102**. (Place the gauges so they can be read from the cabin).
3. **Run engine:** Start the engine and operate it at idle.
4. **Check pressure:** Check the dp-pressure by calculating the difference between the values at **MP101** and **MP102**. Verify that it is within the default setting of **25 ± 2 bar**.
5. **Adjust if necessary:** If the value is not within the correct range:
   * Shut down the engine. 
   * Adjust the setting by turning **pump adjustment screw (2)**. 
   * Restart the engine and repeat the check.
6. **Finalize:** Once the correct pressure is achieved and any other maximum pressure checks are completed, shut down the engine and disconnect the 400-bar pressure gauges from **MP101** and **MP102**.

questions.question: During the optional ejector bucket pressure adjustment, what is the required pressure at measuring point MP214 when the ejector plate is completely retracted against the limiter, and which specific adjustment screw must be turned to correct it?
questions.answer:
Based on the *Service and Repair Manual* (Section "Ejector pressures (option) check and adjustment", pages 802–804), when the ejector plate is completely retracted against the limiter, the required pressure at measuring point **MP214** is **160 bar (±5 bar)** [1]. If the pressure needs to be corrected, you must remove the cover plug and turn **adjustment screw 214** [1].

The step-by-step sequence for checking and adjusting this pressure is as follows:
1. Park the machine on a level surface, shut down the engine, prevent movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the bucket to the ground so the boom rests on the stops, and isolate the machine to level 3 by turning the main switch and starter isolation switch to the OFF position [2, 3].
2. Ensure that the main pump pressures are properly adjusted before adjusting the ejector pressure [3].
3. Connect 400-bar pressure gauges to pressure measurement points **MP213** and **MP214** on the pressure lines of the ejector cylinders [3, 4].
4. Start the engine [4].
5. Retract the ejector plate completely in and keep the movement on against the limiter [1]. *(Note: The manual also describes extending the plate completely to check MP213 at 280 ±5 bar prior to this step [4]).*
6. Check the pressure reading from the gauge attached to **MP214** to ensure it is **160 bar (±5 bar)** [1].
7. Verify from the VCM display that the bucket pump is operating at max pressure [1].
8. Adjust the pressure if necessary by turning **adjustment screw 214** (remember to remove the cover plug before adjusting) [1].

questions.question: If the brake accumulator pre-charge pressure is suspected to be low, what specific pressure value should be verified at measuring points MP521 and MP522 when the engine is not running and the hydraulics are fully depressurized?
questions.answer:
If the brake accumulator pre-charge pressure is suspected to be low, the specific pressure value that must be verified at measuring points **MP521** (Brake accumulator 1) and **MP522** (Brake accumulator 2) is **90 ± 3 bar** [1, 2].

According to the "Brake system pressure accumulator check" / "Brake accumulator pre-charge check" procedures detailed in the *Maintenance Manual* (Section 5.8.13, pages 330–331) and the *Service and Repair Manual* (Section 13.7.1, pages 874–875), the step-by-step sequence is as follows [3-6]:

1. **Prepare the machine:** Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine. Prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, and lower the bucket to the ground so that the boom rests on the stops [3, 6, 7]. 
2. **Verify zero pressure on VCM:** Check the VCM display to make sure that the brake charging pressure reads 0 bar [4, 6].
3. **Isolate power:** Isolate the machine to level 3 by turning the main switch and starter isolation switch to the OFF position [6].
4. **Depressurize the circuit physically:** Connect a capillary test hose to measurement point **MP501** to confirm that the brake hydraulics are fully de-pressurized [4, 6, 8].
5. **Measure the accumulators:** Detach the cover cap from the pressure accumulator and connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the gas valve on the gas side of the brake accumulator. Measure the pre-charge pressure from both **MP521** and **MP522** of the accumulator assembly [4, 8].
6. **Verify the reading:** Check that the measured pressure is **90 ± 3 bar**, as defined in the Pressure Settings specifications [1, 2].
7. **Recharge if necessary:** If the pre-charge pressure is too low, the accumulator must be recharged with nitrogen [8, 9].

questions.question: What are the specific pre-charge pressure requirements for the right (Z2231) and left (Z2232) ride control accumulators when checking them from the accumulator measuring points with the hydraulics non-pressurized?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, the specific pre-charge pressure requirements for the 6-liter piston-type ride control accumulators, when measured with the engine off and hydraulics non-pressurized, are:

*   **Right ride control accumulator (Z2231):** 20 bar [1, 2].
*   **Left ride control accumulator (Z2232):** 70 bar [1-3].

According to the "Boom suspension accumulators check (option)" procedure in the *Maintenance Manual* (Section 5.8.18, pages 340–341), the step-by-step sequence to verify these pressures is as follows:

1. **Prepare the machine:** Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine. Prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the bucket to the ground, and make sure the boom rests on the stops. Isolate the machine to level 3 by turning the main switch and starter isolation switch to the OFF position [4, 5]. 
2. **Depressurize the circuit:** Make sure the accumulators are non-pressurized by connecting a capillary test hose to the accumulator measuring point [5].
3. **Clean the fittings:** Clean the area around the connect fittings in the accumulators thoroughly [5].
4. **Access the valves:** Remove the gas charging valve protecting plugs [5].
5. **Measure the pressure:** Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the gas charging valves and record the gauge readings [6]. Verify that the pressures match the 20 bar (Z2231) and 70 bar (Z2232) specifications [1, 3, 6].
6. **Finalize:** Refit the cover plugs [6]. If the pre-charge pressure is too low, the accumulator must be recharged with nitrogen [6].

questions.question: During the Volvo engine VCB valve adjustment procedure, after loosening the unit injector adjusting screw until zero clearance is obtained (by feel until the roller can no longer be turned), how many degrees must the adjusting screw be tightened further before locking the nut?
questions.answer:
During the Volvo engine VCB (Volvo Compression Brake) valve adjustment procedure, the unit injector adjusting screw must be tightened a further **240°** after achieving zero clearance [1]. 

According to the "Valve Adjustment, VCB" procedure in Section 21-4 of the workshop manual, the step-by-step sequence for adjusting the injector is as follows:
1. Remove all VCB rocker arm springs [2].
2. Crank the engine using the **9993590 Rotation tool** to the next camshaft marking [2, 3].
3. Adjust the clearance of the intake valve to 0.2 mm and tighten the locknut according to the Special Tightening Torques specification [3].
4. Adjust the injector rocker arm pre-load by loosening the adjuster screw until a clearance is obtained on the injector [3].
5. Adjust the screw until the clearance disappears, confirming by feel until the roller can no longer be turned [1].
6. Tighten the adjusting screw a further **240°** [1].
7. Tighten the locknut according to the specification [1], which is **52 Nm** (listed under "Valve mechanism IEGR without shims, VCB mechanism" in the Special Tightening Torques section) [4].

questions.question: What are the exact maximum width and overall height dimensions of the Sandvik LH517i when it is equipped with a low profile cabin instead of the standard profile cabin?
questions.answer:
When the Sandvik LH517i is equipped with a low profile cabin, its exact dimensions are as follows:

*   **Maximum width (low profile cabin):** 3 340 mm [1-3]
*   **Height (low profile cabin):** 2 410 mm [1, 3, 4]

*(For comparison, the standard profile cabin has a maximum width of 3 200 mm and a height of 2 800 mm [1-3]).*

These measurements are documented in the "Machine specification" sections of the provided manuals:
*   *Maintenance Manual*, Section 6.1 (Page 361) [1]
*   *Operator's Manual*, Section 8.1 (Pages 271–272) [2, 4]
*   *Service and Repair Manual*, Section 17.1 (Pages 1218–1219) [3]

questions.question: According to the filling capacities table, what is the exact fluid capacity in liters for the machine's main hydraulic oil tank compared to the Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) tank?
questions.answer: The exact fluid capacity for the machine's main hydraulic oil is **320 liters**, whereas the capacity for the Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) is **75 liters** [1]. This information is detailed in the "Filling capacities" table found in Section 4.5 of the Maintenance Manual [1, 2].

questions.question: Based on the main systems overview for component identification, which specific machine frame section houses the boom and bucket mechanics as opposed to the ROPS/FOPS certified cabin?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Main systems overview" (Section 3.3 in both the Maintenance and Operator's Manuals), the **front frame** contains mainly the boom and bucket mechanics [1, 2]. 

In contrast, the ROPS/FOPS certified cabin, along with the main machine components, is located on the **rear frame** [1, 2].

questions.question: When adjusting the load-sensing steering pump (P3111), what specific pressure value must be achieved at measuring point MP101 when the bucket is pulled backwards against the end stops, and what should the differential pressure read between MP101 and MP102 at engine idle?
questions.answer:
When adjusting the load-sensing steering pump (**P3111**), the required pressure values are as follows:
*   **Maximum Pressure:** When the bucket is pulled backwards against the end stops, the pressure measured at **MP101** must be **280 ± 8 bar** [1].
*   **Differential (dp) Pressure:** When the engine is running at idle, the pressure difference between **MP101** and **MP102** must read **25 ± 2 bar** [1].

According to the *Service and Repair Manual* (Section 11.4.1 "Steering pump pressure check and adjusting procedure") and the *Maintenance Manual* (Section 5.8.20), the step-by-step sequence to verify and adjust these pressures is:

1. **Prepare the machine:** Park the machine on a level surface, shut down the engine, prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, and lower the bucket to the ground so the boom rests on the stops [2, 3].
2. **Connect gauges:** Connect 400-bar pressure gauges to measurement points **MP101** and **MP102**, placing them so they can be read from the operator seat in the cabin [4, 5].
3. **Run engine:** Start the engine and operate it at idle [5].
4. **Check and adjust differential pressure:** Calculate the difference between the values at **MP101** and **MP102** and verify it is **25 ± 2 bar** [4, 5]. If the value is outside of this range, shut down the engine, turn **pump adjustment screw (2)**, restart the engine, and repeat the check [5].
5. **Load the system:** Move the bucket control joystick to the roll bucket back position and keep it there (if the engine stalls, raise the engine rpm) [4-7].
6. **Check and adjust maximum pressure:** Record the gauge reading at **MP101** to verify the steering pump maximum pressure is **280 ± 8 bar** [6, 7]. If the value is outside of this range, shut down the engine, turn **pump adjustment screw (1)**, restart the engine, and repeat the check [7].
7. **Complete procedure:** Shut down the engine and disconnect the 400-bar pressure gauges from **MP101** and **MP102** [7, 8].

questions.question: During a check of the brake accumulator charging system, what target pre-charge pressure should be verified at measuring points MP521 and MP522 with the engine off, and what should the brake charging pump (P3513) pressure read at MP501 with the engine running at idle?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, here are the target pressures and the step-by-step sequences for verifying the brake accumulator charging system. 

**Target Pressures:**
*   **Brake Accumulators Pre-Charge Pressure:** Measured at measuring points **MP521** (Brake accumulator 1) and **MP522** (Brake accumulator 2) with the engine off and hydraulics non-pressurized from MP501, the target pressure is **90 ± 3 bar** [1, 2].
*   **Brake Charging Pump (P3513) Pressure:** Measured at measuring point **MP501** with the engine running at idle, the target pressure is **170 ± 10 bar** [3].

**Step-by-Step Procedures:**

**1. Brake system pressure accumulator check (Maintenance Manual, Section 5.8.13, pages 330–331)** [4-6]
1. **Prepare the machine:** Park on a level surface, shut down the engine, prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the bucket to the ground, and make sure the boom rests on the stops [5].
2. **Charge the accumulators:** Start the engine and let it run at idle for a few minutes to fill the accumulator with fluid [5, 6].
3. **Discharge the pressure:** Shut down the engine and wait for five minutes to let the pressure accumulator discharge to the tank [6].
4. **Verify zero pressure via VCM:** Check the VCM display to make sure that the charging pressure reads 0 bar [6].
5. **Verify zero pressure physically:** Connect a capillary test hose to measuring point **MP501** to confirm the pressure is fully discharged [6].
6. **Measure pre-charge pressure:** Detach the cover cap from the pressure accumulator and connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the gas valve on the gas side of the brake accumulator. Measure the pre-charge pressure from both **MP521** and **MP522** [6].
7. **Evaluate:** Check that the pressure value matches the table value of **90 ± 3 bar**. If the pressure is too low, it must be recharged with nitrogen [1, 2, 6].

**2. Brake pump pressure check (Maintenance Manual, Section 5.8.11, page 328)** [7, 8]
1. **Prepare the machine:** Follow the same safe parking and machine isolation preparations as described above (wheel chocks, articulation lock, bucket lowered, engine off) [7].
2. **Connect the gauge:** Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the brake valve block measuring point **MP501**. Place the gauge so it can be read from the operator's seat in the cabin [8].
3. **Check the maximum pressure:** Start the engine. Wait until the brake system pressure accumulators are fully charged before checking the value [8].
4. **Evaluate:** Read the gauge value to verify it meets the specification of **170 ± 10 bar** [3, 8]. Adjust the maximum pressure if necessary [8].

questions.question: When testing the boom and bucket pump (P3211) stand-by pressure at measuring point MP201, what specific pressure reading indicates correct adjustment (35 ± 2 bar), and what must the steering pump differential pressure be verified as prior to this test?
questions.answer:
When testing the stand-by pressure for the boom and bucket pump (**P3211**) at measuring point **MP201**, the specific gauge reading that indicates correct adjustment is **35 ± 2 bar** [1, 2]. Prior to performing this test, you must verify that the steering pump differential (dp) pressure is **at least 25 bar** [1, 2].

According to the *Service and Repair Manual* (Section 12.4.1 "Boom and bucket pump pressure check and adjusting procedure", pages 730–732) and the *Maintenance Manual* (Section 5.8.19, pages 342–343), the step-by-step sequence is as follows:

1. **Prepare the machine:** Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine [3]. Prevent machine movement with wheel chocks, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the bucket to the ground, and make sure the boom rests on the stops [3]. 
2. **Connect the gauge:** Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the measurement point **MP201** [3]. Place the pressure gauge so that it can be read while sitting at the operator seat in the cabin [2].
3. **Verify steering pressure:** Make sure the steering pump differential pressure is at least **25 bar** [2].
4. **Test the pressure:** Start the engine and operate it at idle [2].
5. **Evaluate:** Check the boom and bucket pump stand-by pressure from the gauge [2]. 
6. **Adjust (if necessary):** If the value is outside of the default setting (**35 ± 2 bar**), shut down the engine, adjust the setting using **pump adjustment screw (2)**, start the engine, and repeat the check [4].
7. **Complete the procedure:** Shut down the engine and disconnect the 400-bar pressure gauge from **MP201** [5].

questions.question: The front and rear axles of the LH517i drive train utilize Kessler D106 axles; what specific type of differential do these axles incorporate to manage traction?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, both the front and rear **Kessler D106 PL441/528S-NLB-FS** axles incorporate a **limited slip differential** to manage traction [1, 2]. 

This specification is detailed in the "Axles" section of the *Service and Repair Manual* (pages 471–472) [1, 2]. Additionally, the *Maintenance Manual* (page 179) notes that a specific axle oil additive (Lubrizol 6178LZ, Sandvik p/n 04696527) must be used to make this limited slip differential function smoother [3].

questions.question: During an emergency steering test, what specific pressure value should be observed at measuring point MP109 to confirm that the pressure relief valve (V3181) is correctly limiting the system to protect the electric motor (M3020)?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, during an emergency steering test, the specific pressure value that should be observed at measuring point **MP109** is **100 ± 5 bar** [1]. 

This pressure level confirms that the pressure relief valve (**V3181**) is correctly limiting the system to 100 bar, which prevents the electric motor (**M3020**) in the hydraulic power pack (**A3141**) from overloading [2, 3]. 

According to the "Emergency steering system function (option) check" found in the *Maintenance Manual* (Section 5.1.13, pages 201–202) [4-6], the step-by-step sequence to perform this test is as follows:

1. **Prepare the machine:** Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine [5]. 
2. **Verify emergency stops:** Check that the emergency stops are not activated [5]. 
3. **Turn on power:** Turn the ignition key to position 1 (power on) [5].
4. **Activate the system:** Push the emergency steering button on the instrument panel and keep it pressed. The pump should start and stay on until the button is released or the maximum time (default 10 seconds) is reached. The emergency steering symbol will also appear in the VCM system display's main window [5].
5. **Observe the pressure:** While keeping the button pressed, check that the steering pressure increases to **100 bar** [6] (specifically **100 ± 5 bar** when measuring at **MP109**) [1].

questions.question: What are the specifications for the pilot pressure filter and the brake pressure filter?
questions.answer: Both the pilot pressure filter and the brake pressure filter (Z3511) have a filtration rating of 10 µm [14, 15]. The pilot pressure filter includes a blockage sensor that triggers at 3.5 bar and a by-pass valve that opens at 5 bar to ensure the main hydraulics always have working pilot pressure even if the filter becomes completely blocked [14]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure setpoints and adjustment steps for the optional ejector bucket?
questions.answer: Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring points MP213 and MP214 on the pressure lines of the ejector cylinders [14, 15]. Start the engine, extend the ejector plate completely, and hold it extended against the limiter [15]. The pressure at MP213 must be 280 ± 5 bar [15]. If the pressure requires adjustment, remove the cover plug and turn adjustment screw 213 [15]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the pilot pressure checked and what is its expected range?
questions.answer: Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point MP405 [1, 2]. Because pilot pressure is reduced from the steering pump pressure, which is only about 25 bar at idle, the pilot pressure cannot be accurately measured without placing a load on the system [1, 3]. To test it, move the boom downwards against the bottom limits (stoppers) or pull the bucket upwards against the stoppers while checking the pressure [1, 3]. The normal pilot pressure range is 35-50 bar, and it is limited by the pilot pressure relief valve to a maximum of 50 bar [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for checking and adjusting the engine blower pump stand-by pressure?
questions.answer: Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point MP301, start the engine, and operate at low idle [7, 8]. Force the pump to its minimum displacement by setting the pump control to 100% in the VCM Pump Test window, or alternatively, by feeding a 600 mA current to the pump controller Y3089 from an external power source [9, 10]. If the pressure is outside the correct limits, shut down the engine, adjust the stand-by pressure using adjustment screw 302, and repeat the test [10]. The blower pump circuit's maximum pressure is protected by pressure relief valve V3381, which limits the pressure to 230 bar [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the system gives a "CAN Communication Backbone 1 Net" (U001088) Bus Off alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm is caused by missing CAN communication on the BB1 network, which will prevent the engine from starting or mean it can only be stopped using the aux-stop [5, 8]. The potential root causes are an open or short circuit at pins B51 or B55, or an internal electronic failure in the ECU(s) [7-9]. To troubleshoot, check all wiring connected to CAN backbone 1 and inspect connectors B:14 and B:10 [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps for a "No data received in SAE J 1939 from ECM" (Chair 64) alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm indicates a contact failure between the J1939 and the CAN bus [1]. First, with the machine's power on and the ignition key turned to position 1, disconnect connectors XC4.7 and XC4.8 and measure their voltages against earth; the voltage should be approximately 2-3 V [1, 2]. If there is no voltage, repair the cable [2]. Next, turn the ignition key to position 0 and measure the resistance between connector pins XC4.7 and XC4.8 [2]. The resistance should be around 55-65 Ohm [2]. If it differs, check the terminal resistor and wire harness [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a "CAN Communication Backbone 2 Net" (U000188) Bus Off alarm diagnosed?
questions.answer: This alarm indicates missing CAN communication on the BB2 network, which prevents the AM-Tool from reading fault codes [7]. The possible root causes are an open circuit or short circuit at pins B21 or B22 [7]. To troubleshoot, check the wiring harness and connectors, and verify that the CAN bus has the correct termination resistance [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the Vehicle Control and Management (VCM) system distributed, and where are its main connection boxes located?
questions.answer: The VCM system relies on five main control modules connected via a CAN bus: the Chair module (XC), Dashboard module (XD), Front module (XF), Middle module (XM), and Rear module (XR) [1, 5]. These modules and their corresponding fuses are housed across different electrical junction boxes, including the Front Frame Box (**X2021**), the Middle Box (**X3003**), and the Rear Box (**X3056**) [1, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the main switch is turned on but the machine has no power?
questions.answer: Verify that the main switch is fully in the ON position, ensure the main circuit breakers (F3035 and F3064) located in the rear frame box (X3056) are not tripped, and check the VCM display to ensure the control system operating voltage is at the normal 24–27 V [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which specific connector pins on the main control modules are dedicated to the CAN bus networks?
questions.answer: The CAN bus connections are routed through the fourth connector on each of the main modules (XC4, XD4, XF4, XM4, and XR4) [1-5]. For the CAN 1 network, pin 7 is used for CAN 1 HIGH and pin 8 is used for CAN 1 LOW [2-5, 11]. For the CAN 2 network, pin 5 is used for CAN 2 HIGH and pin 6 is used for CAN 2 LOW [2-5, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps for a "Hydraulic oil level warning" (Middle 106) or "Hydraulic oil level alarm" (Middle 107)?
questions.answer: First, check the oil level in the hydraulic oil tank and add more oil if necessary [1]. If the warning is activated, detach connector XM1.19 and measure the voltage; if the alarm is activated, detach connector XM3.23 and measure the voltage [1]. If the voltage matches the machine's operating voltage, the Middle module is faulty and must be replaced [1]. Otherwise, measure the resistance of the cable for limit switch S3012 (warning) from connector pin C to connector XM1.19, or for limit switch S3056 (alarm) from connector pin C to XM3.23 [1, 2]. If there is no connection, repair the cabling [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you resolve a "CAN Communication Backbone 2 Net" (U000188) Bus Off alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm indicates missing CAN communication on the BB2 network, which prevents the AM-Tool from reading fault codes [5]. The possible root cause is an open circuit or short circuit at pins B21 or B22 [5]. To fix this, check the wiring harness and connectors (specifically checking connectors B:6 and B:2) [5-7]. Additionally, verify that the CAN bus has the correct termination resistance [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is an emergency stop circuit supply voltage short diagnosed?
questions.answer: Detach the Chair module connector pin XC2.2, then force the output in the I/O Forcing window; if the alarm stops, the fault is a short circuit to earth or operating voltage in the wire harness, which must be repaired [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the troubleshooting steps for a "Module supply pin XC1/1 short to ground" (Chair 33) or "short to external voltage" (Chair 34) alarm?
questions.answer: These alarms indicate a short circuit in the voltage supply of the left-hand side steering joystick push buttons [2]. Detach the Chair module connector pin XC1.1, turn off the system's operating voltage, and then turn it back on [2]. If the alarm is not repeated, the fault is a short circuit to earth in the wire harness [2, 3]. If checking for external voltage and the alarm stops upon detachment, the fault is a short circuit to the supply voltage in the wire harness [3]. If these steps do not fix the issue, the Chair module is broken and must be replaced [3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure specifications for the pilot circuit and auxiliary functions like the optional ejector bucket?
questions.answer: The normal pilot pressure is 35 ± 5 bar, and it is limited by a pilot pressure relief valve to a maximum of 50 bar [7, 8]. If the loader is equipped with an ejector bucket, its pressure is set to 280 ± 5 bar [7, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration requirements and bypass specifications for the main and brake hydraulic return filters?
questions.answer: The main hydraulic return filter (Z3421) features 10 µm filtration; its blockage indicator activates at a 1.2 bar pressure difference, and its by-pass valve opens at 1.7 bar to allow oil flow if saturated [11, 12]. The brake hydraulic return filter (Z3521) uses 20 µm filtration; its blockage indicator activates at a 0.3 bar pressure difference, and its by-pass valve opens at 0.4 bar [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a "Boom valve signal wire broken (no feedback)" (Front 35) alarm?
questions.answer: Check the measurement window for the Front module to see if the values for connector pins XF1.3 and XF1.4 change when the joystick is moved back and forth [8]. If the PWM signal values change normally, inspect the wire harness [8]. If the values do not change, detach the Front module connector pin XF1.3, measure the current (mA) between the cable and earth with a multimeter, and move the joystick back and forth [8]. If there is still no current, measure the wire harness from Front module connector pins XF1.3 and XF1.4 [8]. Furthermore, measure the coil's impedance, which should be approximately 12 ohms [8]. If none of these steps resolve the issue, replace the Front module [9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the part numbers and functions of the primary electric motors used in the loader?
questions.answer:
The main electric motors in the system include:
*   **M4006**: The engine starter motor [1].
*   **M3020**: The emergency steering pump motor, which provides alternative oil flow for steering if the main hydraulic steering fails [1, 7].
*   **M3018**: The brake release pump motor, which charges the brake system pressure accumulators to release the park/emergency brakes during a main pump or engine failure [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps for a "Control system module missing" (Chair 26) or "I/O module missing from the CAN bus" alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm occurs when a module stops communicating with the CAN bus [4, 5]. First, turn off the main power and check the AMP8-connector for current flow to the module; pins such as XM4.4 and XM4.5 must carry the machine's operating voltage of approximately 24-27 V [4]. Check the ground connection of the missing module from the AMP8-connector (e.g., XM4.1 and XM4.3) to ensure there is no resistance between the pins and the machine's ground [6]. Next, measure the CAN bus resistance from the AMP8 connector between pins XM4.2 and XM4.6, which should be 55 - 65 Ohms [6]. Finally, measure the CAN bus from the AMP8 connector to the display module's X1 connector (e.g., XM4.2 to X1.2, and XM4.6 to X1.6) to ensure no resistance is detected [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the system triggers a "CAN Communication Backbone 1 Net" (U001088) Bus Off alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm is caused by missing CAN communication on the BB1 network, which will prevent the engine from starting or restrict it to only being stopped using the aux-stop [7]. Diagnosis involves checking all wiring connected to CAN backbone 1 for open or short circuits, specifically inspecting pins B51 and B55 [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes a "Hydraulic oil level" or "Brake oil level" warning/alarm, and what should be done?
questions.answer: These pop-ups indicate that the **hydraulic or brake oil level has dropped below its specific warning or alarm limit** [8, 9]. The required operator response is to immediately **check the respective oil tank and add more oil** [8, 9]. If the physical fluid levels are normal, service personnel must check the wiring, sensors, or the Middle control module for faults [8, 9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the main switch is on but the machine has no power?
questions.answer: First, check that the main switch is fully in the ON position [1]. Next, inspect the main circuit breakers F3035 and F3064 located in the rear frame box X3056 to ensure they are not tripped [1]. Finally, verify the control system voltage on the VCM display, which should normally be approximately 24–27 V; if the operating voltage is below normal, check the battery connections [1]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a "Steering valve signal wire broken (no feedback)" (Middle 51) alarm?
questions.answer: Check the diagnostics window to see if the coil's current value changes when steering is controlled [3]. If it does not change, detach the Middle module connector pin XM1.5, use a multimeter to measure the current (mA) between the cable and earth, and turn the steering joystick back and forth [3]. If there is no current, measure the wire harness between Middle module connector pins XM1.3 and XM1.5, and XM1.2 and XM1.5 [3]. Additionally, verify the coil’s impedance; the resistance between connector pins 2-5 should be approximately 22 ohms [3]. If these steps do not fix the issue, the Middle module is broken and must be replaced [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the target pre-charge pressures for the hydraulic accumulators?
questions.answer:
The pre-charge pressures (measured with the engine off and the hydraulics fully depressurized) are as follows [16]:
*   **Brake accumulator 2:** 90 ± 3 bar (measured at MP522) [16].
*   **Ride control accumulator Z2231 (right side):** 20 bar [16, 17].
*   **Ride control accumulator Z2232 (left side):** 70 bar [16, 17].
If pre-charge pressures are too low, the accumulators must be recharged with nitrogen [18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you resolve an "Engine start signal short to ground" (Middle 103) or "short to external voltage" (Middle 105) alarm?
questions.answer: This indicates a short circuit in the engine start output [4]. Remove the Middle module connector pin XM1.16 [4]. Check whether the alarm stops when you force the output in the I/O Forcing window [4, 5]. If the alarm stops, the fault lies in the wire harness as a short circuit to earth or operating voltage, and the harness must be repaired [4, 5]. If this action does not correct the malfunction, replace the Middle module [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the part numbers and functions of the main hydraulic pumps on the LH517i loader?
questions.answer:
The loader utilizes several main hydraulic pumps driven by the torque converter or engine:
*   **Steering pump (P3111):** A variable displacement pump that provides oil flow and pressure for the steering hydraulics [1].
*   **Boom and bucket pump (P3211):** A variable displacement pump that delivers oil flow and pressure for the boom and bucket hydraulics [2, 3].
*   **Engine blower pump (P3311):** Provides oil flow and pressure to run the hydraulic motor of the engine cooler [4, 5]. 
*   **Cooling and brake flushing pump (P4513):** A variable displacement axial piston pump that provides oil flow to run the hydraulic cooler fans and to flush and cool the axle brakes [4, 6].
*   **Brake charging pump (P3513):** A constant pressure axial piston variable pump that supplies oil flow and pressure for the machine's brake hydraulics [2, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What triggers the "Door latch alarm" or "Seat belt alarm", and how does the system warn the operator?
questions.answer: These alarms are triggered when the **door latch or seat belt is left open while the machine is moving above a parameter-defined speed limit** [15, 16]. A seat belt or door latch indicator on the display will illuminate a constant red whenever they are open, but will **blink red and sound an audible alarm buzzer** once the machine's speed exceeds the safety limit [15, 16]. The operator must **securely close the cabin door or fasten their seat belt** to clear the alarm [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the four most common causes of hydraulic system failures on the Sandvik LH517i loader?
questions.answer: The four main causes of hydraulic system failures are dirt, heat, water, and cavitation, with dirt being the worst of the four [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the part numbers and functions of the hydraulic accumulators used in the loader?
questions.answer:
The loader relies on several accumulators to store hydraulic pressure and dampen movements:
*   **Pilot pressure accumulator (Z3131):** Stores pilot pressure for the steering, boom, and bucket valves [19].
*   **Ride control accumulators (Z2231 and Z2232):** Two 6-liter piston type accumulators (Z2231 on the right, Z2232 on the left) that suspend the boom to improve driving comfort and reduce stress on the frame [20, 21].
*   **Brake system pressure accumulator (Z3531):** A parallel double piston accumulator that stores hydraulic oil to serve as an alternative supply for the brake system [22, 23]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the displacement, maximum pressure, and maximum flow rate specifications for the main hydraulic pumps?
questions.answer: The steering pump (P3111) has a displacement of 71 cm³/rev, a maximum pressure of 280 bar, and a maximum flow of 154 L/min at 2170 rpm [1-3]. The boom and bucket pump (P3211) has a displacement of 110 cm³/rev, a maximum pressure of 295 bar, and a maximum flow of 238 L/min at 2170 rpm [2-4]. Additionally, the cooling and brake flushing pump (P4513) has a displacement of 45 cm³/rev, a maximum pressure of 210 bar, and a maximum flow of 97 L/min at 2170 rpm [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can excessive air and cavitation in the hydraulic system be recognized and diagnosed?
questions.answer: Excessive air can usually be recognized by sluggish, erratic, and uneven operation of the hydraulic system, which causes the oil to cavitate and overheat [4, 5]. Cavitation can be diagnosed by checking for a low oil level in the tank, leaks in the pump suction line joints, incorrect hydraulic fluid types, water or contamination in the circuit, or very low oil temperatures [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which sensors are used to monitor the machine's steering angle and boom/bucket positions, and what are their part numbers?
questions.answer:
The loader's articulation and implement positions are monitored by the following sensors:
*   **B3030**: A CAN steering angle sensor located on the upper middle hinge joint, used to measure the machine's steering angle for automated steering and end-cushioning [9].
*   **B2032**: A CAN boom position sensor located at the right side lift arm pin, used to monitor the boom's height [10].
*   **B2065**: A 4-20mA linear bucket position sensor located inside the tilt cylinder to monitor the bucket's tilt angle [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components make up the emergency hydraulic power supplies for steering and braking?
questions.answer:
In case of a main system failure, the loader uses these emergency backup components:
*   **Emergency steering hydraulic power pack (A3141):** Contains an electric motor (**M3020**) and pressure relief valve (**V3181**) to provide alternative oil flow for steering if the main steering pump fails or the engine shuts down [24].
*   **Brake release pump (A3542):** An electric pump powered by motor **M3018** that is used to charge the brake accumulators so the park/emergency brake can be released when the main converter-mounted pump cannot be used [22, 25]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure setpoints for the steering pump (P3111) and how are they checked?
questions.answer: The steering pump's maximum pressure should be 280 ± 8 bar [5]. This is checked by connecting a gauge to MP101 and pulling the bucket backwards against the end stops [5]. The steering pump's differential (stand-by/dp) pressure should be 25 ± 2 bar [5, 6]. This is measured at engine idle by checking the pressure difference between measuring points MP101 and MP102 [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps for a "No data received in SAE J 1939 from ECM" (Chair 64) alarm?
questions.answer: This alarm signifies a contact failure between the J1939 and the CAN bus [3]. First, with the machine's power on and the ignition key in position 1, disconnect connectors XC4.7 and XC4.8 and measure their voltages against earth; the voltage should be approximately 2-3 V [4]. Next, turn the ignition key to 0 and measure the resistance between pins XC4.7 and XC4.8, which should be around 55-65 Ohms [4]. If the resistance differs, check the terminal resistor and wire harness [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the electrical system monitor the fluid levels and temperatures of the hydraulic circuits?
questions.answer:
The system uses several specific sensors and limit switches to track fluid conditions and trigger VCM warnings or alarms:
*   **Main Hydraulics:** Temperature is monitored by sensor **B3001** [11]. The oil level triggers a warning via limit switch **S3012** and an alarm (which shuts down the machine) via limit switch **S3056** [11].
*   **Brake Hydraulics:** Temperature is monitored by sensor **B3068** [11]. The oil level triggers a warning via limit switch **S3014** and an alarm via limit switch **S3013** [11].
*   **Fuel System:** The fuel level in the tank is monitored by an analog 4-20mA sensor, **B3011** [12]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for troubleshooting an "E-stop circuit supply voltage short to ground" (Chair 24) or "short to external voltage" (Chair 25) alarm?
questions.answer: These alarms point to a short circuit in the emergency stop output [6]. Detach the Chair module connector pin XC2.2 and check whether the alarm stops when you force the corresponding output in the I/O Forcing window [7]. If the alarm stops, there is a short circuit to earth or operating voltage in the wire harness, which requires repair [7]. If repairing the wire harness does not clear the malfunction, the Chair module is broken and must be replaced [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the diagnostic steps if an I/O module is missing from the CAN bus?
questions.answer: Check the AMP8-connector for current flow to ensure the pins carry the machine's operating voltage (approximately 24-27 V), measure the ground pins to ensure there is no resistance, and verify the CAN-bus resistance reads between 55-65 Ohms with the main power switched off [7-9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot an "I/O module missing from the CAN bus" error on the display?
questions.answer: If a module stops communicating with the CAN bus, check the module's power supply, CAN connectors, and current supply [3]. Use a multimeter to measure the missing I/O module's X_4 connector to ensure there is 24V power at pin X_4.4 (where "_" is the module identifier F, M, R, or C) [3]. Additionally, verify the module's ground by checking the AMP8 connector (for example, pins XM4.1 and XM4.3); there should be no resistance between these connector pins and the machine's ground [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the hydraulic oil filtration managed, and what are the key filter part numbers?
questions.answer:
Filtration is managed by multiple return and pressure filters:
*   **Main hydraulic return filter (Z3421):** Filters particles from the hydraulic oil returning to the main tank and features a clogging indicator (**S3076**) [11, 12].
*   **Brake hydraulic return filter (Z3521):** Filters particles from oil returning to the brake hydraulic tank and features a clogging indicator (**S3077**) [12, 13].
*   **Brake pressure filter (Z3511):** Located in the brake hydraulic circuit to separate particles from the oil before it reaches the parking brake block, equipped with a clogging indicator (**S3078**) [14].
*   Additionally, the tanks have breather filters **Z3441** (main tank) and **Z3442** (brake tank) to clean air entering the reservoirs [11, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which sensors on the loader utilize CAN bus communication to monitor machine articulation and boom position, and what are their part numbers?
questions.answer: The machine relies on a CAN steering angle sensor (**B3030**) located on the upper middle hinge joint to measure the steering angle for automated steering and cylinder end-cushioning [6, 7]. Additionally, a CAN boom position sensor (**B2032**) is located at the right side lift arm pin to monitor the boom's height [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the system respond to a low engine oil pressure alarm, and what actions are required?
questions.answer: The system will display a **"The engine will be shut down!"** pop-up, alerting the operator that a critically low engine oil pressure has been detected [10]. A counter on the screen will show the **remaining time until the engine is automatically stopped** [10]. The required response is to immediately **check the engine oil level**, ensure the oil filters are not blocked, and verify that the oil pressure sensor is functioning properly [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the "PROXIMITY STOP" and "Proximity detection, Speed retarding" alarms mean?
questions.answer: These are generated by the optional Proximity Detection System [17]. A "Speed retarding" warning appears when the **machine enters a caution zone**, alerting the operator that the machine's speed is being automatically reduced [18]. A "PROXIMITY STOP" alarm is triggered when an **obstacle or tagged personnel is detected in the critical danger zone**, forcing the machine to halt [17]. The operator must wait for the area to clear or safely navigate the obstacle, as the pop-up will disappear once the sensor inputs return to a normal safe state [17, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the defined circuit pressure settings for the steering and the boom and bucket systems?
questions.answer: The steering pump's maximum pressure is set to 280 ± 8 bar with a differential (stand-by/dp) pressure of 25 ± 2 bar [6]. The boom and bucket pump's maximum pressure is set to 295 ± 10 bar with a stand-by pressure of 35 ± 2 bar [7]. Furthermore, the main relief valve in the priority block limits the circuit's overall maximum pressure to 330 bar [8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you measure the CAN bus resistance if a "Control system module missing" (Chair 26) alarm occurs?
questions.answer: Ensure the machine's main power is switched off, then measure the CAN bus resistance from the AMP8 connector between pins XM4.2 and XM4.6 using a multimeter; the reading should be 55-65 Ohms [5]. Additionally, measure the CAN bus from the AMP8 connector to the display module's X1 connector (e.g., from XM4.2 to X1.2, and XM4.6 to X1.6) [6]. If the 55-65 Ohm resistance differs or if any resistance is detected on the lines to the display, the CAN bus wire harness must be repaired [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you adjust the stand-by pressure for the boom and bucket pump (P3211)?
questions.answer: First, ensure the steering pump differential pressure is at least 25 bar [12]. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point MP201, start the engine, and operate at idle [12]. The stand-by pressure should read 35 ± 2 bar [12]. If an adjustment is required, shut down the engine, turn pump adjustment screw 1, restart the engine, and re-check the pressure [13]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a hydraulic pump that is operating noisily?
questions.answer: A noisy pump is typically caused by air in the system, cavitation, or a worn pump. Diagnosis involves checking the complete system for air leaks, inspecting for restrictions on the intake side (such as a clogged intake line, a plugged air vent in the reservoir, or excessively high oil viscosity), and checking the pump for wear [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the causes and responses for tire-related warnings from the TPMS (e.g., "Tire over temperature" or "Tire extreme under pressure")?
questions.answer: A "Tire over temperature" alarm means the **tire temperature is too high**, and the operator should respond by **decreasing the machine's tramming speed** [12]. An "under pressure" alarm indicates the **tire pressure is too low**, requiring the operator to inspect the tire and valve for damage and **add more air if necessary** [13]. For "over pressure" alarms, the operator must check the pressure level to safely regulate it [14]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the VCM system communicate with the engine ECM to control and monitor engine speed?
questions.answer: The VCM system communicates with the engine ECM via the SAE J1939 CAN bus network [9]. The request for the engine revolution count (from the throttle pedal) is sent to the ECM through the J1939 bus, and the actual engine revolution data is returned to the VCM system over the same bus [9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary control modules that communicate over the CAN bus in the VCM system?
questions.answer: The Vehicle Control and Management (VCM) system is distributed across five main control modules that communicate via the CAN bus: the Chair module (XC), Dashboard module (XD), Front module (XF), Middle module (XM), and Rear module (XR) [1-5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot faults with the yellow warning or red alarm indicator lamps on the instrument panel?
questions.answer: Remove the lamp bulb and measure the voltage at the connector (XM2.21 for the yellow lamp, XM2.18 for the red lamp); the voltage should be 0 V to confirm no short circuit to external voltage exists, or it should match the machine's operating voltage to confirm the supply voltage is not missing [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What component is used to log machine data via the CAN bus, and what is its part number?
questions.answer: The machine can be equipped with an EPEC Data Collection Unit (DCU), part number **A3077** [12]. This module connects to the CAN bus to support data logging, system monitoring, and transmitting diagnostic information for features like the Proximity Interface [12-14]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for troubleshooting an uncontrolled hydraulic oil cooler fan pump signal causing a "Hydraulic cooling control short to external voltage" (Rear 181) alarm?
questions.answer: First, verify in the IO measurement window whether there is a current value for the coil [5]. If the value is zero, detach the Rear module connector pin XR2.4 and measure the current between the wire and earth (mA) using a multimeter [5]. If there is current without any active control, the fault lies in the wire harness [5]. Next, check the impedance of the coil; the resistance between the connector pins should be approximately 12-24 ohms [5]. If the resistance is incorrect, the valve is broken and must be changed [5]. If all these checks pass but the malfunction persists, replace the Rear module [5]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a short circuit to ground or external voltage in a control module's voltage supply (e.g., Dashboard 30/31 or Middle 110/111)?
questions.answer: To troubleshoot a "Module supply pin short to ground" or "short to external voltage" alarm (such as Dashboard 30 or 31 for pin XD1.1), detach the specific connector pin that caused the alarm from the module [2, 3]. Turn off the system's operating voltage and turn it back on [2, 3]. If the alarm is not repeated, the fault is a short circuit to ground in the wire harness [2]. If the alarm stops immediately upon detachment, the fault is a short circuit to the supply voltage [3]. If repairing the wire harness does not correct the malfunction, the module is broken and must be changed [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which hydraulic coolers are used on the machine and what do they cool?
questions.answer:
The machine utilizes three primary coolers operated by hydraulic fan motors:
*   **Hydraulic oil cooler (A3562):** A split-cell cooler that cools both the main hydraulic oil and the brake hydraulic oil [15, 16].
*   **Transmission oil cooler (A3561):** Cools the transmission oil [16, 17].
*   **Engine cooler (A3361):** Uses a hydraulic fan motor driven by the engine blower pump to cool engine coolant and charge air [5, 18]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the key pressure and output settings for the brake hydraulic circuit?
questions.answer: The brake charging pump (P3513) operates at a pressure of 170 ± 10 bar and has a displacement of 18 cm³/rev [7, 10]. Within the brake system, the brake valve pressure is 112 bar, the brake release pressure is 107–135 bar, and the brake disc pressure is 79–89 bar [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the cabin control joysticks calibrated?
questions.answer: In the Calibration menu, select the window for the specific movement: X-JOY (boom), Y-JOY (bucket), or Steering [25-28]. To calibrate, move the joystick to its extreme full positions (e.g., full left/right or full up/down), and then return it to the zero/middle position [25, 28]. The new voltage values will automatically update in the window [25, 28]. Press 'Calib' to save [25, 28]. Note that calibration is only permitted if the actual input voltage differs from the middle position by more than the specified "Dead band" percentage [25, 28]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot "Forwards working light relays signal short to ground" (Dashboard 56) or "short to external voltage" (Dashboard 57) alarms?
questions.answer: These alarms signify a short circuit in the output of the lights connected to the Dashboard module [8]. Detach the specific connector pin from the Dashboard module that caused the alarm, such as pin XD1.7 for the front cabin corner lights [9]. Check if the alarm stops when you force the output on in the I/O Forcing window [9]. If the alarm stops, repair the wire harness as it has a short circuit to ground or operating voltage [9, 10]. If this does not correct the malfunction, change the Dashboard module [9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you calibrate the steering, boom, and bucket position sensors using the VCM?
questions.answer:
You must navigate to the Service menu's Calibration window and select "More..." [20, 21].
*   **Steering sensor:** Select "Steering sensor". Set the machine completely straight and press OK [20, 22]. Turn the machine fully to the left and press OK [20, 22]. Turn the machine fully to the right and press 'Calib' [22, 23].
*   **Boom sensor:** Select "Boom sensor". Lift the boom fully up and press OK [21]. Lower the boom fully down and press 'Calib' [21].
*   **Bucket sensor:** Select "Bucket sensor". Tilt the bucket fully up and press OK [21]. Tilt the bucket fully down and press 'Calib' [24]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot the electrical system if the machine does not power up after turning on the main switch?
questions.answer: First, check that the main switch is in the ON position [1]. Next, inspect the main circuit breakers F3035 and F3064 located in the rear frame box X3056 to make sure they are not tripped [1]. Finally, check the control system voltage on the VCM display, which should be approximately 24–27 V [1]. If the operating voltage is below normal, check the battery connections [1]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is an "I/O module missing from the CAN bus" fault diagnosed on the LH517i loader?
questions.answer: If a module stops communicating with the CAN bus, you must check the module's power supply, CAN connectors, and current supply [1]. Use a multimeter to measure the missing I/O module's X_4 connector to ensure there is 24V power at pin X_4.4 and verify the ground connection at pins X_4.1 and X_4.3 [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the VCM system distinguish between warnings and alarms, and what is the general operator response?
questions.answer: The machine uses a **yellow indicator light for warnings and a red indicator light for alarms** [1-3]. Whenever an abnormal condition is detected, a pop-up window will appear on the display showing the reason for the alarm, the set limit, and the current measured value [4, 5]. If any active warning or alarm appears on the display, the operator **must not operate the loader** until the cause has been determined and the fault has been repaired by service personnel [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What troubleshooting steps should be taken if there is no pressure in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: To diagnose a lack of pressure, you should check the system from the reservoir to the pump to ensure filters, strainers, and the intake are not clogged. Additionally, check the oil level, inspect the intake side for air leaks, verify that the oil viscosity is not too high, and determine if the pump itself is faulty [2]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for measuring CAN bus resistance if a module communication fault is suspected?
questions.answer: First, ensure the machine's main power is switched off [4]. Measure the CAN bus resistance from the AMP8 connector using a multimeter, specifically between pins XM4.2 and XM4.6 [4]. The resistance should be 55-65 Ohm [4]. If the resistance is incorrect, repair the CAN bus wiring [4]. Furthermore, measure the CAN bus from the AMP8 connector to the X1 connector of the display module (for example, between XM4.2 and X1.2, and between XM4.6 and X1.6) [4]. If any resistance is detected during this measurement, repair the CAN bus wire harness [4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should be checked if the system gives a "Steering pump pressure sensor (B3026) high error" (Rear 28) alarm?
questions.answer: Measure the voltage from sensor pole A, which must match the machine's operating voltage [6]. If it does not, there is a fault in the wire harness or Rear module connector pin XR2.23 [6]. Next, measure the connection from sensor pole B to ground (GND), which connects to Rear module connector pin XR3.11 [6]. Finally, detach the cable for Rear module connector pin XR3.6 and measure the current to earth; with a 0-bar pressure, it should read approximately 4 mA [6]. If these actions do not clear the malfunction, change the Rear module [7]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for diagnosing a "CAN Communication Backbone 1 Net" (U001088) Bus Off alarm?
questions.answer: The U001088 alarm indicates missing CAN communication on the BB1 network [10]. This fault will prevent the engine from starting, or if the engine is running, it can only be stopped using the aux-stop [10, 11]. To diagnose this, check all wiring connected to CAN backbone 1 for open or short circuits, specifically inspecting connectors B:14 and B:10 [11]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary control valves in the steering and boom/bucket circuits, and what do they do?
questions.answer:
The primary control valves include:
*   **Steering valve (V3102):** Controls the directional movement of the machine's steering cylinders and generates the necessary pilot pressure for both the steering and the boom/bucket valves [1, 3, 8, 9].
*   **Boom and bucket main valve (V2201):** A hydraulically controlled valve that directs oil flow to the boom and bucket cylinders [3].
*   **Priorization valve (Y2137):** A valve located in the inlet block that prevents bucket movements when the boom is being used, prioritizing hydraulic power to the boom [10]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the main components that supply and protect power in the LH517i electrical system, and what are their part numbers?
questions.answer: The machine features a +24VDC electrical system powered by two batteries (**G3004**) and charged by the alternator (**G4005**) [1]. A transformer (**G0003**) is used to step down the voltage from 24 VDC to 12 VDC for certain components [1]. The main power supply is protected by two primary circuit breakers: **F3035** (400 A) and **F3064** (200 A), both of which are located in the rear frame electrical box **X3056** [2-4]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are external and internal hydraulic leaks diagnosed?
questions.answer: External leaks on the pressure side are visually easy to locate due to the presence of hydraulic fluid, whereas external leaks on the intake side are more difficult to detect [8]. Internal leaks generally become evident as the system components wear out and overheat, and they can typically be diagnosed by performing by-pass or draw tests [6, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot a "No data received in SAE J 1939 from ECM" (Chair 64) alarm?
questions.answer: The Chair 64 alarm indicates a contact failure between the J1939 and the CAN bus [8]. With the machine's power on and the ignition key turned to position 1, disconnect connectors XC4.7 and XC4.8 and measure their voltages against earth; the voltage should be approximately 2-3 V [9]. Next, turn the ignition key to position 0 and measure the resistance between connector pins XC4.7 and XC4.8, which should be around 55-65 Ohms [9]. If the resistance differs from these values, check the terminal resistor and wire harness [9]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a short circuit to ground or external voltage in a control module's voltage supply?
questions.answer: Detach the module connector pin associated with the alarm, turn off the system's operating voltage, and turn it back on; if the alarm is not repeated, there is a short circuit to earth in the wire harness, but if the alarm stops upon detachment, there is a short circuit to the supply voltage [3-6]. (Ref: Sandvik LH517 Technical Manual)

questions.question: When diagnosing a failure to reach the maximum pressure of 320 (±8) bar on main hydraulic Pump 1 (P3111) at test port MP100, which specific adjustment screw should be calibrated?
questions.answer:
To adjust the maximum pressure for main hydraulic Pump 1 (P3111) at test port MP100 to the target of **320 (±8) bar**, you must calibrate **adjustment screw 101** [1]. 

According to **Section 5.7.6: Main hydraulic pumps pressures check** (found in the Maintenance Manual on pages 256–257), the step-by-step procedure to check and adjust this pressure is as follows:

1. **Prepare the machine for inspection:** Park on a level surface, shut down the machine, install the frame articulation locking device, lower the boom to rest on the bottom limits, and turn the bucket lip to rest on the ground [2].
2. Connect a pressure gauge to test port **MP100** (for Pump 1) [3].
3. Turn the 24 V disconnect switch to the ON position [3].
4. Turn the machine on to driving mode by turning the ignition switch to position 1 and pressing the start button [3]. *(Ensure the battery level is more than 50% and water temperature is less than 50ºC).*
5. Let the pressure rise [3].
6. Use the VCM (Vehicle Control and Management) display to activate Pump 1 for checking [1].
7. Release the brakes [1].
8. Pull the bucket back against the stop [1].
9. Check the pressure for Pump 1. During this check, the Pump 2 value must be **0 bar**, and the correct pressure for Pump 1 is **320 (±8) bar** [1].
10. If the pressure is out of specification, turn off the machine and adjust the pressure using **adjustment screw 101** [1]. 

*(Note: Adjusting the maximum pressure influences the stand-by pressure, which is set to **35 (±2) bar** using adjustment screw 102. It is necessary to check and adjust both pressures several times during adjustment operations [4, 5].)*

questions.question: A technician finds that the Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) has lost power, but the MCU, PDU logic, and fire suppression system remain operational; which specific manually resettable circuit breaker in the main fuse block (+U2) needs to be checked?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided manuals, if the Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) loses power but the other systems remain operational, the technician needs to check the manually resettable circuit breaker **CF04** (which has a capacity of **10A**) located in the **main fuse +U2** block [1-4].
