questions.answer: First, check circuit breaker **F0140** in the instrument panel [8]. Disconnect pins **XD4.7** and **XD4.8**, turn the ignition key to position 1, and measure the voltage between each pin and ground to ensure it reads **2-3 volts** [8]. Next, turn the ignition key to 0, switch off the main switch, and measure the CAN bus resistance between pins **XD4.7** and **XD4.8**, which should be **55-65 ohms** [9]. If the resistance is incorrect, inspect the terminal resistor and related wiring [9]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Identify the function of the brake charging and cooling pump unit (P2521).
questions.answer: The brake pump unit (P2521) is a double piston pump with two pumps mounted on the same shaft [5]. Pump 1 produces constant hydraulic pressure and flow for the machine's coolers and brake flushing circuit, while Pump 2 produces constant pressure and flow for the brake charging system [5]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What CAN protocols does the Volvo Engine Management System (EMS 2) use to communicate with the machine's control units?
questions.answer: The Volvo EMS 2 uses a fast **J1939 CAN link** (operating at 250 Kbit/s) for all primary communication between the engine control unit and the Control Interface Unit (CIU) or Display Control Unit (DCU) [8, 9]. It also uses a slower **J1708/J1587 link** specifically for diagnostic information, flashing codes, and communication with the VODIA diagnostic tool [9]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the emergency steering system function, and what specific components drive it?
questions.answer: If the engine stops abnormally during operation, the emergency steering system is activated automatically to allow the operator to steer the machine to safety [13]. An electric motor (M2020) powers the emergency pump unit (A2141), which provides hydraulic oil flow directly to the steering valve (V2104) [14, 15]. A pressure relief valve (V2161) limits this emergency pump's maximum pressure to 160 bar [15]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a "Supply voltage low" or "Supply voltage high" (e.g., Chair 196.12290.0 / 196.12291.0) alert on the TH551i?
questions.answer: These alerts indicate that the battery voltage is outside of the allowed operating limits [1]. To diagnose, use a multimeter to **check the battery voltage when the machine engine is stopped and running; the voltage should be between 22 and 30 Volts** [2]. If the reading falls outside this range, inspect the condition of the battery and the alternator, and verify the power supply wiring [1]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the three main causes of hydraulic system failures on the Sandvik TH551i?
questions.answer: The three main causes of hydraulic system failures are dirt, heat, and cavitation [1, 2]. They are generally diagnosed by checking the time it takes the hydraulic system to complete a cycle (to identify sluggishness) and checking if the pressure output is normal to pinpoint the faulty component [3]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the Volvo Engine Management System (EMS) classify its engine-specific malfunction messages and what responses are advised?
questions.answer: The EMS classifies messages into three color-coded types on the display: a Red "ALARM" indicates a serious fault requiring the operator to immediately contact a qualified workshop; a Yellow "WARNING" indicates a fault where a workshop should be contacted as soon as possible; and a Blue "MESSAGE" provides non-critical engine information for the operator [7]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the role of the directional control valve (V2118) in the hydraulic circuit?
questions.answer: The directional control valve (V2118) acts as a prioritization valve that ensures the steering circuit always has the highest priority over other hydraulic functions [6]. Additionally, when the onboard jacking system is activated, valve V2118 adjusts the steering and tipping pump (P2112) to output its maximum pressure [7]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the displacements and maximum pressures defined for the brake hydraulic pumps?
questions.answer: The brake charging pump (P2521) has a specified displacement of 18 cm³/rev and a maximum pressure of 190 bar. The brake flushing pump has a displacement of 45 cm³/rev and a maximum pressure of 60 bar [1]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the combination switch (S1154) and what does it control?
questions.answer: The combination switch (S1154), located in the cabin, allows the operator to control the front window wipers, the low/high beam lights, the left/right blinkers, the window washer, and the horn [1]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose a "Supply voltage low" or "Supply voltage high" alert?
questions.answer: These alerts indicate that the machine's battery voltage has fallen below or exceeded the allowed operating limits [5, 6]. To diagnose this, first check the battery voltage with a multimeter when the engine is stopped and running (normal operating voltage is typically **24-27 V** up to 30 V) [7, 8]. Next, inspect the condition of the battery to see if it needs charging, check the alternator's condition, and inspect the power supply wiring [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the default pressure settings for the steering and dump box (tipping) circuits?
questions.answer: For the steering circuit, the maximum steering pump pressure is 290 bar (±10 bar) and the stand-by pressure is 35 bar (±2 bar) [3, 4]. For the dump box circuit, the box up pressure is 280 bar (±5 bar) and the box down pressure is 100 bar (±5 bar) [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the reversing buzzer (H3002) activated during operation?
questions.answer: The reversing buzzer (H3002) is controlled by the VCM system and the gear shift button [2]. When the operator selects a reverse gear, relay **K2008** becomes energized, which activates the buzzer. Once a forward gear is selected, relay **K2008** is deactivated and the buzzer stops [2]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How should a "Transmission messages missing" (Chair 180.4105.1) CAN bus fault be diagnosed?
questions.answer: This fault indicates a connection failure between the Chair module and the transmission control unit [7]. First, check **circuit breaker F0139** in the instrument panel [7]. Next, disconnect **pins XC4.7 and XC4.8**. With the machine's power on and the ignition key in position 1, use a multimeter to measure the voltage between each pin and ground; both should read **2-3 volts** [7]. Turn the key to 0, switch off the main power, and measure the CAN bus resistance between pins XC4.7 and XC4.8, which should be **55-65 ohms** [8]. Repair the wiring or terminal resistor if the values are incorrect [8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What components are protected by the circuit breakers in Box X2021, and what are their specific fuse IDs?
questions.answer:
Box X2021, located on the left side of the articulation area, protects several electrical items from short circuits and overloads [3-5]. Key fuses include:
*   **F2062 (100 A):** Supplies the brake release pump (**M2018**) [4, 5].
*   **F2050 (25 A):** Supplies the hydraulic oil filling pump (**M2019**) [4, 5].
*   **F2144 (25 A):** Supplies the fuel transfer pump (**M2057**) [4, 5].
*   **F2141 (10 A):** Controls the pilot pressure valve for the emergency steering pump (**M2020**) and the brake release pump (**M2018**) [4, 5]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What do the pressure filters Z2111 and Z2511 do in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: The pressure filter Z2111 separates particles from the oil in the dump box and steering hydraulic circuits [16]. The pressure filter Z2511 separates particles from the oil in the brake hydraulic circuit [17]. Both filter units feature an electric indicator that triggers an alert on the VCM display if the pressure loss indicates a blockage [18, 19]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the calibration procedures for the gearbox, suspension, and proximity brakes using the VCM?
questions.answer:
These calibrations are accessed through the VCM display's Maintenance menu:
*   **Gearbox Calibration:** Navigate to Maintenance\Calibration\Gear Box. Calibration requires adequate transmission oil temperature; if the oil is too cold, a "Heating mode" will automatically control the engine to idle in neutral to warm the oil before calibration begins [17, 18].
*   **Suspension Calibration:** Navigate to Maintenance\Calibration\Sensors\Axle Suspension to run the "Suspension Minimum Current Calibration." This automated test establishes the minimum currents required for the suspension up and down movements [19-21].
*   **Proximity Brake Calibration:** Navigate to Maintenance\Calibration\Proximity Brake, where you can select to calibrate either the Proximity Brake Valve or the Proximity Brake Zero by following the on-screen instructions [22]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you troubleshoot an alert indicating "Voltage in uncontrolled output" or leaking voltage?
questions.answer: This fault indicates a short circuit to the supply voltage. Diagnose it by detaching the connector pin from the module, turning the system's main power off, and then turning it back on again [15, 16]. If the alert clears, the fault is located in the wire harness (a short circuit to the operating voltage), and the wiring must be repaired [15, 16]. If the alert remains active, the module is likely faulty and requires replacement [15, 16]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the brake relay valves (V2504 and V2505)?
questions.answer: The brake relay valves (V2504 and V2505) control the actual brake pressure applied to the front and rear axles [24]. They use supply pressure from the brake accumulators to keep the front and rear axle brake pressures 2-3 bar lower than the pilot pressure supplied by the brake pedal valve (V1501) [24, 25]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I test and adjust the pressure of the steering and tipping pump (P2112)?
questions.answer: To check the pressure, connect a **400-bar pressure gauge to the steering pump measuring point MP101** [1, 2]. Start the engine, let it idle, and monitor the gauge or the VCM display by navigating to Maintenance\Testing\Steering Pump Test [2, 3]. The **correct pressure is 290 bar (±10 bar)** [3]. If the reading is incorrect, turn off the engine, adjust the maximum pressure using **adjustment screw 101**, and then restart the engine to repeat the pressure check [3]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the CAN bus facilitate transmission control, and which component IDs are involved?
questions.answer: The operator controls the gears using a shift lever that communicates with the Dashboard module over the SAE J1939 CAN bus through pins **XD4.7** (CAN high) and **XD4.8** (CAN low) [5]. The VCM system transfers this shift lever position data via the Chair module to the transmission control unit (TCM) using the SAE J1939 protocol, which then physically controls the transmission [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What causes an orange "Blocked" pop-up to display and how can it be cleared?
questions.answer: The "Blocked" pop-up appears when the control system prohibits an action that could cause personal injury or machine damage, such as attempting to tram while the cabin door is open [3, 4]. The operator must resolve the cause of the error (for example, by closing the door), and the pop-up will disappear automatically [3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the correct procedure for bleeding air from the main hydraulic valve (V2205)?
questions.answer: Bleeding the main hydraulic valve requires two people: one to operate the VCM in the cabin and one to handle the bleeding points [8]. Make sure **bleeding nipple 205 is closed**, and never lower the suspension when it is open [9]. **Open bleeding nipple 206**, then lower the suspension using the VCM window [9]. Allow the oil to bleed from the nipple until no air bubbles appear, then **close bleeding nipple 206** [9]. **Never raise the suspension when bleeding nipple 206 is open** [9]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What antenna connections are located on the Sandvik Knowledge Box used for data management?
questions.answer: For machines equipped with onboard monitoring and data management, the Sandvik Knowledge Box features specific connections for wireless communication: **X9** connects to the GPS/GLONASS antenna, **X8** connects to the WLAN antenna, and **X7** connects to the GSM/UMTS antenna [14]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you diagnose and identify the causes of excessive heat in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: Excessive heat damages packings and seals, leading to leaks [6]. It is diagnosed by checking for incorrect oil viscosity, inspecting hoses to ensure they are properly sized, routed away from heat sources, and free of sharp bends, looking for worn components causing internal leakage, and checking for exterior dirt build-up that insulates the system and prevents cooling [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What CAN bus diagnostic connectors are available directly on the cabin instrument panel?
questions.answer: The instrument panel provides two direct bus diagnostic connectors for maintenance personnel: connector **26** provides access to the **CAN-Open** bus (supplying VCM system information), and connector **27** provides access to the **J1939** bus [18-21]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is a "Short circuit to ground in output" (such as in device supply or lights) diagnosed?
questions.answer: To isolate the fault, first detach the specific connector pin from the affected module [13, 14]. Next, use the VCM system's forcing functions to force the output into the **ON** state [13, 14]. If the alert is no longer active after doing this, the fault is a short circuit to ground within the wire harness, which must be repaired [13, 14]. If the alert persists after repairing the wiring and cycling the power, the control module itself is likely broken and must be changed [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specific flow rates defined for the transmission hydraulic circuit?
questions.answer: The transmission hydraulic system utilizes two pump outputs with variable flow rates depending on engine speed. The first produces a minimum of 95 l/min at 850 rpm and a maximum of 242 l/min at 2075 rpm. The second produces a minimum of 102 l/min at 850 rpm and a maximum of 264 l/min at 2075 rpm [2]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the hydraulic pressure specifications for the engine cooler pump?
questions.answer: The engine cooling fan pump's minimum stand-by pressure is 55 bar (±5 bar) at engine idle, and its maximum pressure is 200 bar (±10 bar) when the engine is at full speed [3, 9, 10]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure and rpm setpoints for the engine cooler pump (P2311) and how are they adjusted?
questions.answer: Connect a pressure gauge to measuring point MP301 and a speed sensor to the engine cooler blowers. Using the VCM's "Engine Cooling Fan Pump Test", check the minimum stand-by pressure, which should yield **900 rpm (±100 rpm)** at **50 bar (Mesabi coolers) or 55 bar (Nissens coolers)**. This is adjusted using **adjustment screw (A)**. At maximum pressure, the blowers should rotate at **1800 rpm at 255 bar (Mesabi)** or **1600 rpm at 200 bar (Nissens)**, which is adjusted using **adjustment screw (B)** [5-8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I diagnose a "Gear selector malfunction" (Dash 181.4098.1) alert?
questions.answer: Check **circuit breaker F0140** in the instrument panel [9]. Disconnect **pins XD4.7 and XD4.8** on the Dash module, turn the ignition key to position 1, and ensure the voltage between each pin and ground measures **2-3 volts** [9]. Turn the key to 0, switch off the main switch, and measure the CAN bus resistance between pins XD4.7 and XD4.8, which should be **55-65 ohms** [10]. If readings are incorrect, inspect the terminal resistor and related wiring; if all readings are correct, replace the gear selector [10]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the starter isolation switch?
questions.answer: The starter isolation switch disables the engine starting circuit while keeping the battery's current to the machine's electrical system turned ON [8]. It is specifically used during maintenance situations to prevent accidental engine startups [8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the pressure settings for the brake charging and cooling pump unit (P2521) and how are they adjusted?
questions.answer: The brake charging pump maximum pressure should be **190 bar (±10 bar)**, measured at MP501 at engine idle and adjusted using **adjustment screw (A)**. The brake cooling pump maximum pressure should be **60 bar (±10 bar)** producing a blower speed of **2400 rpm (±100 rpm)**, measured at MP536 at maximum engine rpm, and adjusted using **adjustment screw (B)** [9-12]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I verify the pressure setting of the brake charging pump (P2521)?
questions.answer: Connect a **400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point MP501** to monitor the brake pump pressure [10, 11]. Start the engine, let it idle, and check the pressure reading on the gauge, which **should be 190 bar (±10 bar)** [10]. If the pressure does not match this specification, turn off the engine, make adjustments using **adjustment screw (A)**, and then restart the engine to verify the new pressure reading [10]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for diagnosing a missing control system module (e.g., "Chair Module Missing" or "Dash Module Missing")?
questions.answer: First, turn the system's main power off and then back on [9]. If the module is still missing, check the wiring harness by measuring the voltage to ensure the module is receiving the machine's operating voltage [10]. Use a multimeter to measure the resistance between the module's ground pins and the machine's ground (it should read **0 ohms**) [11]. Finally, with the main power off, measure the CAN bus resistance across pins **4.2** and **4.6** (or equivalent CAN pins), which must be between **55-65 ohms** [12]. If these readings are correct, the module itself may need replacement [9, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the manual fault tracing procedure for the SAE J1939 CAN bus cables between the Volvo EMS 2 and the DCU/CIU?
questions.answer: Turn off the main switch and disconnect the 8-pin Deutsch connector at the DCU/CIU [6]. Connect a break-out box (**9998699**) and cable (**88890016**) between the engine control unit and the DCU [6]. Measure the resistance across pins **16** and **17** to verify the two 120-ohm termination resistors; the reading should be approximately **60 ohms** [6]. To check the voltage, turn on the power and measure between pin **16 (CAN-H)** and pin **18 (0V power supply)**, and between pin **17 (CAN-L)** and pin **18**; both measurements should read between **2.3 V and 2.7 V** [7]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the filtration ratings and requirements for the main and brake hydraulic return filters?
questions.answer: The main hydraulic oil return filter (Z2421) has a filtering capacity rating of β10 > 200 and is equipped with magnetic filtration [7]. The brake hydraulic oil return filter (Z2521) has a filtration rating of β20 > 200 [8]. Both systems require the filters to be equipped with a by-pass valve and a limit switch that triggers a warning on the VCM display if the pressure loss across the element reaches a critical clogging limit (0.3 bar for the brake filter) [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a red "Alarm" pop-up indicate and how must the operator respond?
questions.answer: A red "Alarm" pop-up indicates that the machine control system has detected a major problem [1, 2]. The operator must take immediate action to prevent damage to machine components, and the control system may automatically stop some or all machine operations during this time [1, 2]. The operator must stop using the machine until the cause of the alarm is identified and corrected [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot a "Transmission messages missing" alert indicating a connection failure between the Chair module and the transmission control unit?
questions.answer: First, check the condition of circuit breaker **F0139** in the instrument panel [1, 2]. Next, disconnect pins **XC4.7** and **XC4.8** [2]. With the machine's power on and the ignition key in position 1, use a multimeter to measure the voltage between pin **XC4.7** and ground, and **XC4.8** and ground; both should read **2-3 volts** [2]. Finally, turn the ignition key to 0, switch off the main switch, and measure the resistance between pins **XC4.7** and **XC4.8**, which should be **55-65 ohms** [3]. If readings are incorrect, check the wiring or terminal resistor [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the main modules and networks that make up the Vehicle Control and Management (VCM) system architecture on the TH551i?
questions.answer: The VCM system uses a CAN bus network (utilizing CANOpen and SAE J1939 protocols) to connect various modules and manage vehicle operations [1, 2]. The primary components on this network include the Front module, Middle module, Rear module, Dash module, Chair module, Display module, Engine Control Module (ECM), and Transmission Control Module (TCM) [2-4]. It also networks with the TPMS receiver, integrated scale, and jacking controller [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are the stand-by and maximum pressures checked and adjusted on the steering and tipping pump (P2112)?
questions.answer: Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point MP101 and use the VCM window (Maintenance\Testing\Steering Pump Test) with the engine running. To adjust the **stand-by pressure** to the correct setpoint of **35 bar (±2 bar)**, turn off the engine and use **adjustment screw 102**. To adjust the **maximum pressure** to the correct setpoint of **290 bar (±10 bar)**, use **adjustment screw 101** [1-4]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 400 A main fuse (F2035) located in Box X2056?
questions.answer: The 400 A main fuse (**F2035**), housed in Box X2056 on the left side of the front frame, protects the main switch (**S2001**), the battery (**G2004**), and the jump start circuit [6, 7]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: When does a yellow "Notice" pop-up appear and what is the required response?
questions.answer: A yellow "Notice" pop-up is displayed when the system detects a medium-severity problem [1, 2]. It does not require immediate action from the operator; however, if the alert persists or occurs repeatedly, the underlying cause must be investigated and corrected [1, 2]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot a "Transmission messages missing" (Chair 180.4105.1) alert?
questions.answer: This indicates a connection failure between the Chair module and the transmission control unit [4], [5]. Check circuit breaker F0139, then disconnect pins XC4.7 and XC4.8 [5]. With the machine's power on and the ignition key turned to position 1, use a multimeter to measure the voltage between each pin and ground; it should read 2-3 volts [5]. Next, turn the ignition key to 0, switch off the main switch, and measure the CAN bus resistance between pins XC4.7 and XC4.8 [5], [6]. It should be 55-65 ohms; if not, check the terminal resistor and wiring related to it [6]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I check and adjust the pre-charge pressure of the pilot-system pressure accumulator?
questions.answer: With the machine parked on a level surface and the engine off, **connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point MP405** [6]. Start the engine and verify that the **pressure reads 35 bar (±10 bar)** [6]. Next, turn off the engine, immediately turn the power on and off repeatedly, and monitor the pressure drop at MP405; the **pressure collapse point should be 15 bar (±2 bar)** [6, 7]. If the pre-charge pressure is too low or too high, use a separate filling device on **measuring point MP125** to recharge or discharge nitrogen as needed [7]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What does a repeatedly tripping circuit breaker indicate and how is it diagnosed?
questions.answer: A circuit breaker that cannot be reset and trips immediately upon trying to close it usually indicates a complete short-circuit, a connection to earth, or a faulty component [1-3]. It is diagnosed by first attempting to reset the breaker once a fault is resolved; if it trips again immediately, you must stop trying to force it closed and instead systematically examine the electrical wiring and related components for shorts or earth faults [1, 3, 4]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot a CAN bus error on the OptiMine/Monitoring data management unit (e.g., Cross Core XA AI)?
questions.answer: Verify that the status LED is green and the CAN bus is properly plugged into the **CAN 1** connector [10, 11]. Check that a **120-ohm terminal resistor** is connected to the CAN 1 output [11]. Because the monitoring kit replaces one of the machine's existing terminal resistors, ensure there are exactly two terminal resistors on the machine's CAN bus [11]. With the power isolated, measure the resistance across the CAN H and CAN L lines; the total resistance should read **60 ohms** [11]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the designations and functions of the primary hydraulic cylinders on the machine?
questions.answer: The steering cylinders (A3121) steer the machine and are cross-connected so they operate together [20, 21]. The tipping cylinders (A3223) are used to raise and lower the dump box [2]. The suspension cylinders (A2425 and A2426) are attached to the front axle and are used to adjust and level the height of the machine [22, 23]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the CAN bus connections on the Cross Core XA AI data management unit used for monitoring, and how is it terminated?
questions.answer: The **Cross Core XA AI** unit features several communication connectors, specifically **X8** (CAN 1 in), **X9** (CAN 1 out), **X10** (CAN 2 in), and **X11** (CAN 2 out) [15, 16]. When connecting this monitoring unit to the machine's CAN bus via CAN 1, a **120-ohm terminal resistor** must be connected to the CAN 1 output [17]. Because this replaces one of the machine's existing terminal resistors, technicians must verify that the total bus resistance remains at 60 ohms [17]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for diagnosing a "Short circuit in front lights high beam" (Front 166.9078.1) alert?
questions.answer: This indicates a short circuit to ground in the output [9]. First, detach connector pin **XF2.6** from the Front module [9, 10]. Use the VCM's forcing functions to force the output to the ON state [9]. If the alert is no longer active, the fault is a short circuit to ground in the wire harness [9]. After repairing the wiring, turn the system main power off and then back on [9]. If the alert persists, the Front module may be broken and requires replacement [9]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which components are used to filter returning hydraulic oil, and what are their component IDs?
questions.answer: The main hydraulic oil return filter (Z2421) cleans hydraulic oil returning to the main hydraulic tank [8, 9]. The brake hydraulic oil return filter (Z2521) cleans the oil returning from the brake flushing circuit to the separate brake hydraulic oil tank [10-12]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I investigate a "Service brake control coil resistance invalid" (Dash 181.4099.1) alert?
questions.answer: This alert indicates that the coil resistance is out of the allowed difference range [11]. Use a multimeter to measure the impedance of the service brake control valve coil between connector pins **XD1.6** and **XD1.7** on the Dashboard module [11, 12]. The correct value is approximately **22 ohms** (which varies slightly according to temperature) [12, 13]. If the measured value differs significantly from 22 ohms, replace the coil [12, 13]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the function of the Navigation Sensor Unit (NSU) in the AutoMine system, and how does it connect to the vehicle?
questions.answer: The Navigation Sensor Unit (NSU) manages the odometer interface, the integrated or external gyroscope interface, mode light control, and three spare digital outputs [10, 11]. It bridges communication by featuring an Ethernet interface that connects to the AutoMine InfraFREE computer, and a CAN bus interface that connects directly to the machine's VCM control system [10, 11]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot a "Force sensor out of range" alert on the integrated scale system?
questions.answer: Check the alert log to identify the missing sensor and turn off the system's main power [5, 6]. Verify that the sensor is receiving the machine's operating voltage of approximately **24-27 V** [5, 6]. Measure the resistance between the sensor's ground pins and the machine's ground, which should be **0 ohms** [5, 6]. Finally, with the main power off, measure the resistance of the CAN bus between connector pins **XR4.7** and **XR4.8**; it should be **55-65 ohms** [7, 8]. If any values differ, repair the wire harness [5-8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the primary modules that make up the Vehicle Control and Management (VCM) system?
questions.answer: The VCM system's architecture consists of several interconnected modules that manage the vehicle's functions [9]. The typical system includes the Front module, Middle module, Rear module, Dash module, Chair module, Display module, the Engine Control Module (ECM), and the Transmission Control Module (TCM) [10-13]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: What steps are taken to troubleshoot a "Short circuit to ground in output" alert (e.g., Front 166.9028.1 for steering wheel lock)?
questions.answer: Detach the specific connector pin (e.g., **XF1.2**) from the affected module [11]. Use the VCM system's **forcing functions to force the output to the ON state** [11]. If the alert clears, there is a short circuit to ground in the wire harness that must be repaired [11, 12]. After repairing the wiring, turn the main power off and then back on; if the alert remains, the module is broken and must be replaced [12]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you resolve a "Voltage in uncontrolled output" alert, which indicates a short circuit to the supply voltage?
questions.answer: Detach the affected connector pin from the module, **turn off the system's main power, and then turn it back on again** [13]. If the alert is no longer active, the fault is a short circuit to the operating voltage within the wire harness, which needs to be repaired [13, 14]. If the alert persists after the reset, the module itself is likely faulty and requires replacement [14]. (Ref: Sandvik TH551 Technical Manual)

questions.question: When performing a steering pump test via the VCM on the P2112 pump, you record a maximum pressure of 275 bar at measuring point MP101 instead of the specified 290 ± 10 bar. Which specific adjustment screw must you turn to correct this, and which two solenoids must be disconnected prior to the test to prevent unwanted axle movements?
questions.answer:
To correct the maximum pressure on the steering and tipping pump (P2112), you must turn **adjustment screw 101** [1, 2]. 

Prior to beginning the test, you must disconnect the electric connectors from solenoids **Y2087 and Y2088** [3]. Disconnecting these prevents unwanted axle movements while the system is being pressurized during testing [3].

According to the **Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 10.10.2 ("Checking and adjusting the box/steering pump pressures", pages 636-638)**, the complete step-by-step sequence for testing and adjusting the maximum pressure is as follows:

1. Disconnect the electric connectors from the solenoids **Y2087** and **Y2088** [3]. 
2. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the measuring point **MP101** [3].
3. Start the engine and let it idle [1].
4. Make the pump produce maximum pressure by operating the VCM window (Navigation route: **Maintenance\Testing\Steering Pump Test**) [1].
5. Check the pressure from the gauge. The correct maximum pressure is **290 bar (±10 bar)** [1].
6. Because your reading (275 bar) does not match the specification, turn off the engine and adjust the maximum pressure with **adjustment screw 101** [1, 2].
7. Start the engine and repeat the pressure checking procedure [1].
8. If needed, turn off the engine and readjust [1].
9. Once the correct pressure is achieved, exit the “Steering pump test” window [2].

questions.question: After depressurizing the suspension circuit via discharge valve V2421 to check the accumulators, what specific pre-charge pressure readings should you expect when connecting a gauge to measuring points MP451 (low-side) versus MP452 (high-side) for front suspension accumulator 1?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, here are the specific pre-charge pressure readings and the step-by-step procedure for checking the front suspension accumulators.

**Expected Pressure Readings**
According to the "Technical Specifications, section Default pressure settings", the expected nitrogen pre-charge pressures for front suspension accumulator 1 are:
*   **MP451 (low-side):** 40 ± 3 bar [1]
*   **MP452 (high-side):** 80 ± 3 bar [1, 2]

**Step-by-Step Sequence**
The procedure is detailed in Section 5.7.19, "Checking the precharge pressure of the suspension system pressure accumulators" [3]. Before performing these checks, ensure the hydraulic oil temperature is between 60°C and 80°C and the engine is not running [3]. 

1. **Depressurize the suspension circuit:** Open the discharge valve **V2421** [3, 4]. 
   *   *WARNING:* The front frame will lower down when the valve is opened, so ensure nobody is in the hazard zone [3, 4]. 
   *   Leave the valve **V2421** open during maintenance [4].
2. **Depressurize the hydraulic oil tank:** Push the pressure relief button and check the gauge to ensure all pressure is relieved [4].
3. **Disable engine starting** [4].
4. **Verify depressurization:** Connect a pressure gauge to measuring point **MP418** to confirm that the suspension circuit is completely non-pressurized [4].
5. **Check the accumulators:** Detach the protection caps from the measurement points and connect your gauge to the high-side (**MP452**) and low-side (**MP451**) measuring points to check the pre-charge pressures [1, 4, 5].
6. **Recharge if necessary:** If the pre-charge pressure is too low, the accumulators must be recharged with nitrogen [5]. 
7. **Finalize:** Refit the protection caps and close the suspension discharge valve **V2421** [5].

questions.question: You are diagnosing a "Transmission messages missing" alert (Chair 180.4105.1) and have switched off the main power to measure the CAN bus terminal resistor across the Chair module connector pins XC4.7 and XC4.8. If your multimeter reads 120 ohms instead of the target 55-65 ohms, what specific CAN bus wiring fault does this resistance value indicate?
questions.answer:
If your multimeter reads 120 ohms across the Chair module connector pins **XC4.7 (CAN high)** and **XC4.8 (CAN low)** instead of the target 55-65 ohms, it indicates that **only one of the two required terminating resistors is connected to the circuit**. 

According to the system specifications, a complete CAN bus network must have exactly two **120 Ω terminating resistances** connected to the bus, which together provide a nominal parallel resistance of approximately **60 Ω** (or 55-65 ohms) across the CAN H and CAN L connections when the system power is isolated [1, 2]. A reading of exactly 120 ohms means there is a **missing or failed terminal resistor**, or an **open circuit (broken wire)** in the CAN bus harness that has disconnected one of the resistors from the network [1-3].

**Step-by-Step Diagnostic Sequence (Service and Repair Manual TH663i, pages 488-489):**
When diagnosing the **Chair 180.4105.1 "Transmission messages missing"** alert, the procedure requires checking both the voltages and the terminal resistor [3-5]:

**Action 1 & 2: Circuit Breaker and Voltage Check**
1. Check the condition of circuit breaker **F0139** in the instrument panel [5].
2. Disconnect pins **XC4.7 and XC4.8** [5].
3. Make sure the machine’s power is on and the ignition key is turned to **position 1** [5].
4. Measure the voltage between pin XC4.7 and ground, and between pin XC4.8 and ground. Each should measure between **2-3 volts**. If not, check for short circuits or loose connections [5].

**Action 3: Terminal Resistor Check** (where your reading occurred)
1. Turn the ignition key to **position 0** [3].
2. Switch **off** the main switch [3].
3. Measure the resistance between pins **XC4.7 and XC4.8** with a multimeter [3]. 
4. If the resistance is not between **55-65 ohms** (such as your 120-ohm reading), you must check the terminal resistor and the wiring related to it for faults [3]. 

If the wiring and resistors are confirmed to be intact after repairing any faults but the issue persists, the Chair module itself may be broken and must be replaced [3].

questions.question: During a steering cylinder rod side bypass test, you connect a capillary test hose to measuring points A and B to release pressure, disconnect the piston side hoses, cap them, and then start the engine and move the steering wheel to pressurize the rod side. If oil flows steadily from the disconnected piston side cylinder port, what specific internal component failure does this confirm?
questions.answer:
If oil flows steadily from the disconnected piston side cylinder port during this procedure, it confirms that the **piston seals** (item **17**) are bypassing (failing) in the rod-to-piston side direction [1, 2]. This indicates that the bypassing cylinder needs to be replaced or overhauled [2]. 

According to the **Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 11.8.1 "Steering cylinder bypass test" (pages 696–698)**, this specific procedure is known as the **Piston Side Bypass Test** [3]. The complete step-by-step sequence for this test is as follows:

1. Perform the preparatory safety steps: Install the frame articulation locking device, depressurize the suspension circuit by opening the discharge valve, depressurize the hydraulic oil tank by pushing the pressure relief button, and disable the engine starting [3, 4].
2. Release the hydraulic pressure of the steering circuit by connecting a capillary test hose to the steering cylinder pressure measuring points **A** and **B**, gradually screwing the quick connects on to release the pressure into a suitable container [3, 5].
3. Disconnect the piston side hydraulic lines of the cylinders to be tested from the manifold, and plug the manifold to eliminate any high-pressure oil injection hazard [5].
4. Allow the cylinder piston side oil to drain into a container via the disconnected hoses until all oil flow has stopped, securing the hoses to the container [2].
5. With a second person observing the container and piston side hose ends from a safe position, start the engine and move the steering wheel to pressurize the rod side hydraulic circuit of the cylinder [2].
6. Observe the cylinder; if oil is coming from the cylinder, the piston seals are bypassing in this direction, confirming the component failure [2].
7. Shut down the engine [6].
8. Release the hydraulic pressure of the steering circuit again using the capillary test hose at measuring points **A** and **B** [6].
9. Remove the plugs in the manifold, reconnect the piston side cylinder hoses, and replace the O-rings [6, 7].
10. Check the hydraulic oil level, which should be between the sight glasses when the dump box is lowered, and refill if necessary [7].
11. Remove the frame articulation locking device, start the engine, and operate the steering hydraulics through its full cycle a few times until the steering functions smoothly [7].
12. Stop the engine and check the steering system for any leaks [7].

questions.question: You receive a "Fuel level left tank sensor low alarm" (Middle 183.4163.0) and decide to test the sensor's analog output. After detaching the cable from the Middle module connector pin XM3.6 and measuring the current to ground, what exact milliamp (mA) reading at 0-bar pressure will confirm the sensor is functioning within its normal baseline range?
questions.answer:
Based on the Service and Repair Manual TH663i, if you are diagnosing the **Middle 183.4163.0 "Fuel level left tank sensor low"** alert and proceed to test the sensor's analog output, a reading of approximately **4 mA** at 0-bar pressure will confirm the sensor is functioning within its normal baseline range [1, 2].

According to the troubleshooting procedures for Fuel Transfer Pump Control (Middle module alerts), the specific step-by-step diagnostic sequence is as follows [1-3]:

*   **Action 1: Wire harness**
    1. Measure the voltage from the sensor. The voltage must be the same as the machine’s operating voltage.
    2. A fault may exist in the wire harness or Middle module connector pin XM2.23.
*   **Action 2: Wire harness**
    1. Measure the ground (GND) from the sensor.
*   **Action 3: Sensor** (This specific test)
    1. Detach the cable from the Middle module connector pin **XM3.6**.
    2. Measure the current to ground using a multimeter.
    3. At 0-bar pressure, the current should be approximately **4 mA**.
*   **Action 4: Module**
    1. If Actions 1 through 3 do not correct the malfunction, the Middle module itself may be broken and must be changed.

questions.question: When performing a steering pump test at measuring point MP101, what is the specified maximum pressure setting, and which specific adjustment screw should be turned if the reading is outside of the 290 ± 10 bar range?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, the specified maximum pressure setting for the steering and tipping pump (P2112) is **290 bar (±10 bar)** [1, 2]. If the reading falls outside of this range, you must turn **adjustment screw 101** to correct the maximum pressure [2, 3]. 

According to the **Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 10.10.2 "Checking and adjusting the box/steering pump pressures" (pages 636–638)**, the complete step-by-step sequence for this procedure is as follows:

1. Disconnect the electric connectors from the solenoids **Y2087** and **Y2088** to prevent unwanted axle movements during the checking and adjusting procedure [4].
2. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the measuring point **MP101** [4].
3. Start the engine and let it idle [2].
4. Make the pump produce maximum pressure by operating the VCM window (Navigation route: **Maintenance\Testing\Steering Pump Test**) [2].
5. Check the pressure from the gauge. The correct maximum pressure is **290 bar (±10 bar)** [2].
6. If the reading doesn’t match the specification, turn off the engine and adjust the maximum pressure with **adjustment screw 101** [2, 3].
7. Start the engine and repeat the pressure checking procedure [2].
8. If needed, turn off the engine and readjust [2].
9. Once the correct pressure is achieved, exit the "Steering pump test" window [3].

questions.question: When checking the tailgate load holding valve with a pressure gauge installed at MP210 and the hydraulics non-pressurized from MP209, what is the exact ± 5 bar tolerance range the pressure must fall within before utilizing adjustment screw 1?
questions.answer:
When checking the tailgate load holding valve, the pressure must fall within the exact tolerance range of **175 ± 5 bar** [1-3]. 

According to the **Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 12.7.7 "Adjusting the tailgate load holding valve" (page 779)** [3-5], the complete step-by-step procedure is as follows:

1. Install a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point **MP210 (2)** [3]. *(Note: The system default pressure settings specify that the hydraulics must be non-pressurized from measuring point **MP209** during this check [1, 2]).*
2. Start the engine and let it idle [3].
3. Drive the tailgate to the open and to the closed position a few times, and leave it in the closed position [3, 5].
4. Check the pressure from the pressure gauge. The pressure should be **175 bar ± 5 bar** [5].
5. If the pressure falls outside of this range, adjust the pressure using **adjustment screw (1)** [5].

questions.question: During the box hinge bearing dial gauge measurement, what specific axial play tolerance range (in millimeters) must be maintained, and what three thicknesses of shim plates can be used on the lower flange to achieve this specification?
questions.answer:
Based on the source material, the dial gauge measurement procedure that utilizes shim plates on a lower flange actually applies to the **center articulation / middle hinge joint**, rather than the dump box hinge. 

**Axial Play Tolerance and Shim Specifications:**
*   **Axial Play Tolerance Range:** The required axial play for the hinge bearing is **0.05 - 0.2 mm** (the factory setting is 0 - 0.1 mm) [1, 2].
*   **Shim Plate Thicknesses:** The three available thicknesses for the shim plates are **0.1 mm, 0.2 mm, and 0.5 mm** [3, 4]. Each shim group must have the exact same thickness [4].

**Step-by-Step Adjustment Sequence:**
According to the *Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 4.2.5 ("Adjusting the middle hinge joint clearance", page 170)*, if your dial gauge readings are outside the allowed 0.05 - 0.2 mm tolerance, you must perform the following steps:

1. **Tighten the flange:** First, tighten the **lower flange (1)** bolts to a torque of **660 Nm** [4]. These bolts can be accessed via holes in the front frame [4]. Once tightened, perform the dial gauge measurement again [4]. 
2. **Adjust the shims:** If tightening the bolts does not correct the clearance, add or remove the **shim plates (2)** using the 0.1 mm, 0.2 mm, or 0.5 mm sizes as needed [4]. 
3. **Re-tighten and measure:** Tighten the lower flange again to **660 Nm** and perform the dial gauge measurement a third time [4].
4. **Replace if necessary:** If the clearance still falls outside the tolerance after shim adjustment, the middle hinge bearings must be replaced [4].

questions.question: What is the target pressure specification for the brake flushing pump when measured at MP536 with the engine at full rpm, and what is the expected brake flushing pressure at MP511 with the engine at idle?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, here are the target pressure specifications and testing procedures for the brake flushing pump:

**Target Pressure Specifications**
*   **Brake flushing pump pressure (MP536):** According to the "Default pressure settings" tables, the target pressure measured at measuring point **MP536** with the engine running at full rpm is **60 ± 5 bar** [1, 2]. 
*   **Brake flushing pressure (MP511):** The expected brake flushing pressure measured at measuring point **MP511** with the engine running at idle is **0.5 - 2.5 bar** [1, 2].

**Step-by-Step Procedure for MP536 (Brake cooling/flushing pump maximum pressure)**
According to the *Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 10.10.4 "Checking and adjusting the brake pumps pressures"* [3, 4]:
1. Disconnect the electric wiring from the solenoids **Y2087** and **Y2088** to prevent unwanted axle movements during the checking and adjusting procedure [4].
2. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the measuring point **MP536** [5].
3. Attach a reflector as near the hub as possible to the oil cooler blower located in the right corner box [5].
4. Start the engine and set maximum engine rpm with the throttle [6].
5. Check the pressure from the gauge and measure the blower rpm with a speed sensor. The cooler should rotate at **2400 rpm (±100 rpm)**, and the pressure should be **60 bar (±10 bar)** [6]. *(Note: The manual specifies that the rotation speed of the blower is the most important factor when adjusting the blower pump pressure, and the pressure reading is just a guideline [6]).*
6. If the readings do not match the specifications, turn off the engine, adjust the pressure using **adjustment screw B**, and then start the engine to repeat the pressure checking procedure [7].

**Step-by-Step Procedure for MP511 (Brake flushing pressure check)**
According to the *Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 13.12.3 "Brake flushing pressure check"* [8]:
1. Park the machine on a level surface and shut down the engine. Prevent machine movement with wheel chocks [8].
2. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the measuring point **MP511** [8].
3. Start the engine and let it idle [8].
4. Check the gauge reading. The correct pressure is **0.5 - 2.5 bar** [8].
5. Stop the engine [8].
6. Disconnect the pressure gauge [8].

questions.question: Within the tipping section of the hydraulic main valve (V2205), the port relief valves with anti-cavitation function are designed to limit the pressure to what specific values for the box "up" movement versus the box "down" movement?
questions.answer:
Within the tipping section of the hydraulic main valve (**V2205**), the port relief valves (item **4**) with anti-cavitation function are designed to limit the pressure to the following specific values [1, 2]:

*   **Box "up" movement (rising the box):** Limited to **300 bar** [2, 3].
*   **Box "down" movement (lowering the box):** Limited to **125 bar** [2, 3].

These valves are designed to protect the tipping valve and cylinders from pressure peaks [2, 3]. The integrated anti-cavitation function prevents cavitation by allowing oil to flow from the tank side to the service port side if under-pressure occurs in the cylinder lines [2, 3]. 

*(Note: While the port relief valves limit the absolute maximum pressure to 300 bar / 125 bar to prevent damage, the standard operating pressures tested at measuring points **MP203** (Box up) and **MP204** (Box down) are governed by the feed reducer valves, which limit the working port pressures to **280 bar** and **100 bar**, respectively [2, 3].)*

**Manual References:**
This information is detailed in the *Service and Repair Manual TH663i*:
*   **Section 10.11** "Hydraulic main valve" - Tipping section (Page 654) [2].
*   **Section 12.7.4** "Functional description of components" - Tipping section (Page 764) [3].

questions.question: What are the exact machine dimensions, including the total length, maximum width, and overall height of the Sandvik TH663i?
questions.answer:
Based on the "Machine specification" sections found in the Technical Specifications of the Maintenance Manual (Sections 3.1 and 6.1) and the Operator's Manual (Sections 3.1 and 8.1), the exact machine dimensions for the Sandvik TH663i are:

questions.question: What are the specifications for the standard Volvo TAD1643VE-B engine powerpack regarding power output, maximum torque, and displacement?
questions.answer:
According to the machine specifications found in the Operator's Manual (Section 8.5, page 299), the Maintenance Manual (Section 6.5, page 385), and the Service and Repair Manual (Section 8.2.1, page 380), the standard Volvo TAD1643VE-B engine powerpack has the following specifications:

*   **Power Output (Output capacity):** 565 kW (758 hp) @ 1900 RPM [1-3].
*   **Maximum Torque:** 3261 Nm (2404 lb.-ft.) @ 1300 RPM [2-4].
*   **Displacement:** 16.1 liters (982 cubic inches) [2-4].

Additional relevant specifications for this engine include:

*   **Cooling System:** Liquid cooled [4, 5].
*   **Weight (wet):** 1440 kg (3175 lb) [3, 7, 8].

questions.question: Based on the main component locations guide, where are the powerpack, center hinge, and operator's compartment situated on the machine?
questions.answer:
According to Section 3.3 "Main component locations" (page 130 of the Maintenance and Operator's Manuals), these parts are identified by the following component numbers on the machine diagram:

*   **Powerpack:** Component number **3** [1, 2].
*   **Center hinge:** Component number **5** [1, 2].
*   **Operator's compartment:** Component number **6** [1, 2].

Based on the machine orientation guidelines in Section 3.4, the operator's compartment is situated on the front left side of the machine, the powerpack is located at the front (engine end) of the unit, and the center hinge is located between the front frame (1) and the rear frame (2) [1, 3]

questions.question: When verifying the service brake circuit, what specific pressure should be measured at points MP505 (front axle) and MP506 (rear axle) when the brake pedal is released, and what is the target default pressure for the brake charging pump (P2521) at measuring point MP501 when the engine is idling?
questions.answer:
According to the "Default pressure settings" specifications (Section 6.6 / 8.6), the required pressure for the service brake circuit when the brake pedal is released is **110 ± 5 bar** at both measuring point **MP505** (front axle) and **MP506** (rear axle) [1-3].

For the brake charging pump (**P2521**), the "Default pressure settings" table lists the target default pressure at measuring point **MP501** with the engine running at idle as **170 ± 10 bar** [1, 4]. 

However, when performing the specific procedure to check and adjust this pump (Section 10.10.4, "Checking and adjusting the brake pumps pressures"), the manual specifies the maximum pressure target as **190 ± 10 bar** [5, 6]. 

The step-by-step sequence for checking and adjusting the brake charging pump pressure at **MP501** is as follows:
1. Disconnect the electric wiring from the solenoids **Y2087** and **Y2088** to prevent unwanted axle movements during the checking and adjusting procedure [6].
2. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the measuring point **MP501** [6].
3. Check the brake charging pump maximum pressure by starting the engine and letting it idle [6].
4. Check the pressure from the gauge, which should read **190 bar (±10 bar)** [6].
5. If the reading doesn't match the specification, turn off the engine and adjust the pressure using **adjustment screw A** [7].
6. Start the engine and repeat the pressure checking procedure [7].

questions.question: If you are diagnosing a "Short circuit in retarder cylinder out" (Alert Middle 167.9033.1) at connector pin XM1.4, how does the VCM's automatic over-rev protection override normal operations if the engine exceeds the standard retarder working range of 700 - 1400 rpm?
questions.answer:
When diagnosing the **Middle 167.9033.1 "Short circuit in retarder cylinder out"** alert at connector pin **XM1.4**, the system indicates that a short circuit to the supply voltage has occurred [1]. The required diagnostic action is to check the wire harness and connections, and then try to control the function again to ensure it works properly [1].

While the standard hydraulic retarder operates within the **700 - 1400 rpm** range [2], the VCM features an automatic over-rev (overspeed) protection system designed to prevent damage to the engine and transmission [2]. If the engine exceeds the allowed limits, the VCM overrides normal operations through the following sequence (Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 9.5.2 "Auxiliary braking control"):

*   **Automatic 100% Activation:** The VCM automatically engages the retarder to 100% capacity, regardless of the control panel switch setting or the accelerator pedal's position [2, 3].
*   **Throttle Override:** Normal operator inputs are ignored; pressing the throttle pedal will *not* deactivate the retarder during an overspeeding-related activation [3].
*   **Forced Upshift:** Because transmission protection is given top priority, if the 100% retarder effect is insufficient to counter the overspeeding condition, the system will automatically force the transmission to upshift [3].
*   **Safety Disengagement:** Once upshifts are no longer possible (for example, if the transmission is already in its highest gear), the VCM will automatically disengage both the torque converter lock-up and the retarder to protect the system [3].

questions.question: When checking the steering and tipping pump (P2112) at measuring point MP101, which specific adjustment screws on the pump must be turned if the stand-by pressure falls outside the 35 ± 2 bar range or the maximum pressure falls outside the 290 ± 10 bar range?
questions.answer:
If the pressures for the steering and tipping pump (**P2112**) fall outside the target ranges at measuring point **MP101**, you must use the following specific adjustment screws:
*   Use **adjustment screw 102** if the **stand-by pressure** falls outside the **35 ± 2 bar** range [1, 2].
*   Use **adjustment screw 101** if the **maximum pressure** falls outside the **290 ± 10 bar** range [2, 3].

According to the Service and Repair Manual TH663i, Section 10.10.2 "Checking and adjusting the box/steering pump pressures" (pages 636–638), the complete step-by-step sequence is as follows [1, 3, 4]:

**Preparations:**
1. Disconnect the electric connectors from the solenoids **Y2087** and **Y2088** to prevent unwanted axle movements during the procedure [1]. 
2. Connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to the measuring point **MP101** [1].

**Check the stand-by pressure:**
3. Start the engine [1].
4. Make the pump produce stand-by pressure by operating the VCM window (Navigation route: **Maintenance\Testing\Steering Pump Test**) [1].
5. Record the gauge reading, which should be **35 bar (±2 bar)** [1].
6. If the reading doesn’t match the specification, **turn off the engine and adjust the stand-by pressure with adjustment screw 102** [1]. 
7. Start the engine, repeat the pressure checking procedure, and readjust with the engine off if needed [1]. 
8. Turn off the engine [3].

**Check the maximum pressure:**
9. Start the engine and let it idle [3].
10. Make the pump produce maximum pressure by operating the VCM window (Navigation route: **Maintenance\Testing\Steering Pump Test**) [3].
11. Check the pressure from the gauge, which should be **290 bar (±10 bar)** [3].
12. If the reading doesn’t match the specification, **turn off the engine and adjust the maximum pressure with adjustment screw 101** [3]. 
13. Start the engine, repeat the pressure checking procedure, and readjust with the engine off if needed [3].
14. Exit the "Steering pump test" window when the correct pressures are achieved [2].

questions.question: To troubleshoot a "Transmission oil pressure sensor low" alert (Rear 184.4141.0), what supply voltage must be verified at the sensor, and what specific ground connector pin on the Rear module should be checked for continuity?
questions.answer:
Based on the provided source material, here is the troubleshooting information for the **Rear 184.4141.0 "Transmission oil pressure sensor low"** alert:

**1. General Instructions for Alert 184.4141.0**
According to the manual's specific entry for this alert (Section 17.6, Rear module alerts), the required action is to: *"Check the condition of the sensor and wire harness. Measure the sensor's supply voltage, GND and pin connections."*

**2. Supply Voltage Verification**
While the specific entry for 184.4141.0 does not detail the exact voltage, the standard diagnostic procedure for identical 4-20 mA pressure sensors wired to the Rear module (such as the Engine cooler pump pressure sensor or Steering pump pressure sensor) states:
*   The supply voltage must be the same as the **machine’s operating voltage** (approximately 24–27 V).
*   This supply voltage is provided by the Rear module "SENSOR & SWITCH SUPPLY" at connector pin **XR2.23**.

**3. Sensor Signal Pin**
The inputs table lists the Transmission oil pressure sensor as a 4-20 mA sensor connected to pin **XR3.6**. *(Note: The manual's table lists the module as "Chair" for this specific entry, but the "XR" prefix indicates it is a Rear module connector pin).*

**4. Specific Ground Connector Pin**
The provided source material **does not specify** an exact ground connector pin number on the Rear module for this specific sensor. Following the standard diagnostic sequences for other Rear module sensors, the manual only provides the general instruction to *"Measure the GND from the sensor."*

questions.question: If the VCM generates a "Box lever safety analog value high" alert (Chair 180.4109.1), which specific connector pin on the Chair module must be detached to measure the changing voltage with a multimeter during lever movement?
questions.answer:
When diagnosing a "Box lever safety analog value high" alert (**Chair 180.4109.1**), you must detach connector pin **XC3.13** on the Chair module to measure the voltage with a multimeter [1]. 

According to the troubleshooting procedures for the Chair module, the complete step-by-step diagnostic sequence is as follows [1-3]:

**Action 1: Box lever connection**
1. Check from the diagnostics windows of the lever if the voltage value changes with movement [1].
2. If the value does not change, detach the connector pin **XC3.13** [1]. Use a multimeter to measure if the voltage changes when the lever is moved [1].
3. If the voltage value stays at 5 V, the error is in the GND connector pin **XC3.4** of the Chair module. Check the connection to this connector pin [2].
4. If the voltage value stays at 0 V, the error is in the +5 V REF voltage feed of connector pin **XC3.2** of the Chair module. Check the connection to this connector pin [2].
5. If the voltage does not change, check the lever and the wire harness [2].

**Action 2: Calibration of the lever**
1. Check the calibration values from the Y direction calibration window by moving the lever from side to side and returning it to the middle position [2].
2. If the calibration values differ from the lever voltages, calibrate the lever [2].

**Action 3: Module**
1. If Actions 1 or 2 do not correct the malfunction, the Chair module is broken and must be replaced [3].

questions.question: What should be checked if the control system reports a missing module (e.g., Alert Chair 247.2.0) causing the E-stop to activate?
questions.answer: When a module is missing from the bus, switch off the system's main power and measure the resistance of the CAN bus between the missing module's **connector pins 4.2 and 4.6** [4]. The resistance should read **55 - 65 Ohms** [4]. If the value differs, the CAN bus wiring must be repaired [5]. Additionally, verify the module is receiving operating voltage (**24-27 V**) across **pins 4.4 and 4.5** [6]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How can I diagnose the cause of a noisy hydraulic pump?
questions.answer: A noisy pump is typically caused by **air in the system, cavitation, or a worn pump** [4]. To diagnose, check the entire system for air leaks [4]. If cavitation is the cause (a vacuum on the intake side), check the intake line for restrictions, ensure the pump and reservoir air vent are not clogged, and verify that the oil viscosity is not too high [4]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: Which sensors monitor the hydraulic and brake oil levels, and how do they function within the VCM system?
questions.answer: The hydraulic oil level is monitored by sensor **S2012** (which triggers a warning) and sensor **S2056** (which triggers an alarm) [11, 12]. The brake oil level is monitored by sensor **S2103** (warning) and sensor **S2104** (alarm) [11, 12]. These sensors send their signals to the Middle module (**XM1.19 through XM1.23**), which processes the data to display alerts if fluid levels drop too low [11, 12]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I measure the CAN bus resistance if a sensor or the Rear module is reporting as missing?
questions.answer: First, ensure the **system main power of the machine is switched off** [2, 3]. Using a multimeter, measure the resistance between the Rear module CAN **connector pins XR4.7 and XR4.8** [2, 3]. The resistance of the CAN bus between these pins should read **55 - 65 Ohms** [2, 3]. If the resistance differs from this value, the CAN bus wiring must be repaired [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should I do if the control system module is missing, causing the E-stop to activate (Alert Chair 247.2.0)?
questions.answer: Measure the resistance between the machine's ground and the missing module’s **connector pins 4.1 and 4.3** using a multimeter; there should be **no resistance** [1]. Next, with the system main power switched off, measure the CAN bus resistance between the missing module's **connector pins 4.2 and 4.6**, which should be **55 - 65 Ohm** [1]. If the resistance differs from these values, repair the CAN bus wiring [2]. If the wiring is intact, replace the missing module [2]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How does the Data management unit (Monitoring/OptiMine) integrate into the CAN bus, and what are its connection points?
questions.answer: The Data management unit connects to the existing machine CAN bus to provide and structure measurement data [18]. On the Cross Core XA AI Data management unit, connectors **X8** and **X9** are designated for CAN 1, while connectors **X10** and **X11** are designated for CAN 2 [19]. When the OptiMine kit is fitted via the CAN 1 connection, its built-in resistor replaces one of the machine's existing termination resistances; technicians must ensure there are only two terminating resistances on the bus (measuring 60Ω across CAN H and CAN L) and that the bus speed is configured to 250kb/s [20]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What should I check if there is no pressure in the hydraulic system?
questions.answer: A complete lack of pressure can be caused by a **clogged intake, low oil level, air leaks in the intake, excessive oil viscosity, or a faulty pump** [4]. Diagnose this by checking the oil level, inspecting the system from the reservoir to the pump, and ensuring that filters and strainers are not clogged [4]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are SAE J1939 data link communication faults (MID 128 / 144, SID 231) on the engine control unit diagnosed?
questions.answer: This fault can be caused by **CAN H and CAN L short-circuiting** to each other, to battery negative (pin 3), or to the power supply (pin 4) [9]. Diagnosis involves using a break-out box and multimeter to measure the resistance towards the EMS 2 between **pins 16 and 17**, which should be approximately **60 Ω** [10, 11]. You should also measure the voltage between **CAN-H (pin 16) and 0V (pin 18)**, and **CAN-L (pin 17) and 0V (pin 18)**; both should read **2.3 V – 2.7 V** [12]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I diagnose the "Transmission messages missing" alert (Chair 180.4105.1)?
questions.answer: First, check the condition of circuit breaker F0139 in the instrument panel [1], [2]. Next, disconnect pins XC4.7 and XC4.8 [2]. With the machine’s power on and the ignition key turned to position 1, measure the voltage between pin XC4.7 and ground, and between pin XC4.8 and ground; each should measure 2-3 volts [2]. Then, turn the ignition key to position 0, switch off the main switch, and measure the resistance between pins XC4.7 and XC4.8 using a multimeter, which should read 55-65 ohms [3]. If the values are incorrect, check for short circuits, loose connections, or terminal resistor faults [2], [3]. If the wiring is intact, replace the Chair module or transmission ECU [3], [4]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you calibrate the suspension control valves?
questions.answer: On the VCM, navigate to **Maintenance > Calibration > Suspension Minimum Current Calibration** (or Sensors > Axle Suspension) [11, 12]. A warning will indicate that the machine will move during the test, so clear the surroundings [12]. The system will automatically step through the calibration to find the **"Suspension up minimum current"** and **"Suspension down minimum current"** [12, 13]. Once the automated adjustments finish, the system will prompt you to press "OK" to save the successfully calibrated values [13, 14]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What functions are controlled by the combination switch (S1154) in the cabin?
questions.answer: The combination switch (**S1154**) is located on the steering column [7]. It allows the operator to control the front window wipers, the low and high beam lights, the left and right directional blinkers, the horn, and the window washer [7, 8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I perform a rod side bypass test on the steering cylinders?
questions.answer: Install the frame articulation locking device, depressurize the suspension circuit by opening the discharge valve, and depressurize the hydraulic oil tank via the pressure relief button [7]. Release the steering circuit pressure by connecting a capillary test hose to pressure measuring points (A) and (B) [8]. Disconnect the piston side hydraulic hoses from the cylinder, cap the hoses, and secure a drain container under the cylinder [9, 10]. Start the engine and move the steering wheel to pressurize the rod side hydraulic circuit [10]. If oil leaks from the disconnected piston side of the cylinder, the piston seals are bypassing (from rod to piston side), and the cylinder must be replaced or overhauled [10]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the displacements (output capacities) of the main hydraulic pumps?
questions.answer: The steering and tipping pump (P2112) has a displacement of 145 cm³/rev [1]. In the brake system, the brake flushing pump has a displacement of 45 cm³/rev, and the brake charging pump has a displacement of 18 cm³/rev [2]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are "Supply Voltage low" (164.9010.1) or "Supply Voltage high" (164.9011.1) alerts diagnosed?
questions.answer: These alerts indicate that the battery supply voltage is not within the allowed limits [8], [9]. To diagnose, check the condition of the battery and charge it if needed [8]. Additionally, check the condition of the alternator and inspect the power supply wiring for any faults [8], [9]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the specified circuit pressures for the brake system?
questions.answer: The brake charging pump pressure should be 170 ± 10 bar, and the brake flushing pump pressure is 60 ± 5 bar [6]. The brake pedal pressure when the brakes are released is 110 ± 5 bar [6]. The brake flushing pressure at idle should be between 0.5 - 2.5 bar [6], and the maximum pressure for the electric brake release pump is 140 ± 5 bar [7]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What tire-related warnings are generated by the TPMS (Tyre Pressure Measurement System), and what actions should the operator take?
questions.answer: The TPMS generates alerts for **tire leaks** (sudden pressure drops), high or low **tire pressures**, and **high tire temperatures** [22-27]. If a tire leak is detected on any wheel, the operator must **check the tire and valve for leakages** [22, 25, 26]. If a high tire temperature alert appears, the required action is to **decrease the tramming speed** [23]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I check the terminal resistor on the CAN bus for the Chair module?
questions.answer: Turn the ignition key to position 0 and **switch off the main switch** [1]. Use a multimeter to measure the resistance between the Chair module's **connector pins XC4.7 and XC4.8** [1]. The resistance should be **55-65 ohms** [1]. If the resistance is not within this range, check the terminal resistor and the wiring related to it [1]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the correct maximum pressure and RPM values when testing the engine cooler pump (P2311), and where do I measure them?
questions.answer: Disconnect solenoids Y2087 and Y2088, attach a reflector to the engine cooler blowers, and connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point MP301 [3]. Using the VCM "Engine Cooling Fan Pump Test" function, check the maximum pressure and RPM [4, 5]. For Mesabi coolers, the blowers should rotate at 1800 rpm (±100 rpm) with a pressure of 255 bar (±10 bar) [5]. For Nissens coolers, the blowers should rotate at 1600 rpm (±100 rpm) with a pressure of 200 bar (±10 bar) [5]. If the reading does not match the specification, turn off the engine and adjust the maximum pressure with adjustment screw A [5, 6]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What are the functions and part numbers of the primary pressure filters in the steering/box and brake hydraulic circuits?
questions.answer: The pressure filter **Z2111** separates particles from the oil in the box and steering hydraulic circuits, while the pressure filter **Z2511** filters the brake hydraulic circuit [5, 6]. Both filter units feature an electric indicator that triggers an alert on the VCM display if pressure loss exceeds 4 bar (indicating blockage), and a spring-loaded non-return valve that allows oil to bypass the filter if pressure loss exceeds 5 bar [5-8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How is the steering and box pump (P2112) pressure tested and adjusted?
questions.answer:
First, disconnect the electric connectors from solenoids Y2087 and Y2088 to prevent unwanted axle movements, and connect a 400-bar pressure gauge to measuring point **MP101** [1]. Start the engine and use the VCM (Navigation: Maintenance\Testing\Steering Pump Test) [1]. 
*   For **stand-by pressure**, the target is **35 ± 2 bar**. If it is out of specification, turn off the engine and adjust using **adjustment screw 102** [1].
*   For **maximum pressure**, let the engine idle and use the VCM to make the pump produce maximum pressure. The target is **290 ± 10 bar**. If incorrect, turn off the engine and adjust using **adjustment screw 101** [2]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I diagnose a "Transmission messages missing" (Chair 180.4105.1) or "Engine Messages Missing" (Chair 180.4106.1) alert?
questions.answer: To diagnose this fault, first check the condition of **circuit breaker F0139** in the instrument panel [1]. Next, turn the ignition key to position 1 and use a multimeter to measure the voltage between both **pins XC4.7 and ground, and XC4.8 and ground**; each should measure **2-3 volts** [1]. Then, turn off the main switch and measure the resistance of the CAN bus terminal resistor between **pins XC4.7 and XC4.8**, which should be **55-65 ohms** (or approximately **60 ohms**) [2, 3]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I resolve a cabin door switch error where both contacts are open (Alert Chair 180.4097.1)?
questions.answer: Test the wire harness while the door is open. Use a multimeter to verify that the voltage of **connector pin XC3.19 measures 24 V**, and the voltage of **connector pin XC3.20 measures 0 V** [5]. If these voltage measurements are incorrect, repair the wire harness of the door switch [5]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot a short circuit to ground in the alarm buzzer output (Alert Chair 164.9096.1)?
questions.answer: Detach **connector pin XC2.17** from the Chair module [8]. Use the system's forcing functions to force the output to the **ON state** [8]. If the alert is no longer active, the fault is a short circuit to ground within the wire harness [8]. After repairing the wiring harness, turn off the system main power and then turn it back on again to reset it [8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do you verify the CAN bus communication if a sensor, like the Force sensor or Inclinometer, is reported missing from the bus?
questions.answer: Turn off the main power of the machine and use a multimeter to measure the resistance between the Rear module CAN **connector pins XR4.7 and XR4.8** [7]. The resistance between these pins should be **55 - 65 Ohms** [7]. If it falls outside this range, you must repair the wiring of the CAN bus [8]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: What is the procedure for calibrating the transmission?
questions.answer: Transmission calibration is accessed via the VCM under **Maintenance > Calibration > Gear Box** [3, 4]. The transmission oil must be at an adequate temperature to proceed; if it is too cold, you can run the **"Heating mode"** which automatically cycles the transmission through Stall, Stabilization, and Idle phases until the proper temperature is reached [4, 5]. During the calibration process, the system automatically calibrates valves 1 through 6, followed by the clutches (starts with a pre-phase and then calibrates 7 clutches) [6-9]. Once the sequence finishes, you must **switch the ignition key to the zero position** [10]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How do I troubleshoot a short circuit to ground or supply voltage in the machine's lighting outputs, such as the front cabin corner light (Dash 165.9046.1 or 165.9047.1)?
questions.answer: For a short circuit to ground, detach the connector pin (e.g., XD1.15) from the module and use the system's forcing functions to force the output to the ON state [10]. If the alert clears, the fault is a short to ground in the wire harness [10]. For a short circuit to supply voltage, detach the pin, turn off the system main power, and then turn it back on [10], [11]. If the alert is no longer active, the fault is a short circuit to the operating voltage in the wire harness [11]. If the alert remains active in either test, the module itself may be broken and must be replaced [10], [11]. (Ref: Sandvik TH663i Technical Manual)

questions.question: How are short circuits to ground or to supply voltage diagnosed in the VCM module outputs?
